title: Shimmer
content:
Shimmer is a shiny, lavender-colored, pearlescent liquid. It can be found at any point in the game in the Aether, a mini-biome that generates once per world in the Underground or Cavern layers, and always on the same half of the world as the Jungle. After the Moon Lord has been defeated, it can be obtained limitlessly by using the Bottomless Shimmer Bucket.
Shimmer has the unique function of transforming ("transmuting") certain dropped items and entities submerged in it:

Most crafted items are transformed back ("decrafted") into their crafting materials.
Certain items are transformed into other items. A few items can only be obtained via this transformation, such as Ambrosia. Some item transformations only work under certain conditions.
The sprite of town NPCs is changed, which is purely a visual change.
Certain enemies are transformed into other enemies.
Most critters are transformed into Faelings or into an item.
Items will float upwards after transformation until they leave the liquid, then linger in midair and produce vibrant lights until a player picks them up, similarly to souls. Items that cannot be transformed will follow normal gravity and sink to the bottom of the Shimmer.
In addition to its transforming effect, Shimmer also has an effect on other things that enter it:

When a player's head is submerged in the liquid, or the bobber of a player's fishing pole touches the liquid, they will be afflicted with the Shimmering debuff. This causes them to fall slowly while phasing through all blocks until they reach an opening.
Certain projectiles will bounce upwards upon contact with a Shimmer pool, such as a falling Fallen Star from a Star Cloak or Star Wrath.
When enemies that have no special transmutations and are not immune to the Shimmering debuff (e.g. the Werewolf) enter Shimmer, they will slowly become more transparent, eventually turning completely invisible. Then they will slowly become more and more opaque. Attacking the enemy will cause it to become opaque faster.
Unlike other liquids, the player cannot fish or use items in Shimmer, nor can it be picked up with an Empty Bucket. Shimmer also does not have a liquid bomb variant. It can still be moved by pumps, however.
Upon contact with any other liquid, Shimmer will form Aetherium Blocks.


== Item transmutations ==
Below is a list of special item transmutations. The common decrafting transmutations are not included.


== Decrafting exceptions ==
Apart from normal decrafting, many recipes have special decrafting results and rules. They are referred to as "decrafting exceptions" on this wiki.


=== Multiple recipes ===
Items which have multiple recipes are only decrafted into one specific set of ingredients.
For example, the Avenger Emblem can be crafted with any of the four basic emblems, but it will always decraft into a Warrior Emblem.
All items affected by this decrafting exception are listed below. Crafted items that already have a special item transmutation are not included, as that transmutation takes precedence over decrafting.


=== Alternate ingredients ===
Some items have "one" recipe that can take alternative crafting ingredients. These always yield the first item of their respective group, regardless of what alternatives (and combination thereof) was used for crafting.
For example, the Balloon Chair can be crafted with 4 of Silly Green Balloons, Silly Pink Balloons, or Silly Purple Balloons ("Any Balloon"), in any combination. It will always be decrafted into 4 Silly Green Balloons, because the Silly Green Balloon is the first of the "Any Balloon" items, as listed at Any Balloon.
All relevant alternative crafting ingredients and their decrafting results are listed below.


=== Evil biome-dependent ===
Certain items that have recipes with crafting ingredients pertaining to the evil biomes are decrafted based on the current world's evil biome. In worlds with the special world seed Drunk enabled, the decrafting result follows the evil biome of the current day.
For example, in a Corruption world a Monster Lasagna is always decrafted into Rotten Chunks (the Corruption-exclusive ingredient), whereas in a Crimson world it is always decrafted into Vertebrae (the Crimson-exclusive ingredient) instead.
All items affected by this decrafting exception are listed below. Crafted items that already have a special item transmutation are not included, as that transmutation takes precedence over decrafting.


=== Unique decrafting ===
A few items are decrafted into a specific set of items that do not directly comprise any of their recipes.
For example, the Copper Pickaxe is decrafted into Wood and Copper Ore, even though Copper Ore is not part of its crafting recipe.
All items affected by this decrafting exception are listed below.


=== Potions ===
Items that can be crafted at a Placed Bottle, Alchemy Table, or Alchemy Flask are decrafted into a random subset of their ingredients. Although said items might be acquirable in other ways apart from crafting (e.g. many potions being found as loot throughout the world), this rule still applies regardless of obtainment method.
The randomness is achieved by making every individual item in the decrafting result have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to disappear, including items within the same stack of ingredients. Consequently, decrafting items craftable at a Placed Bottle, Alchemy Table, or Alchemy Flask only yields 2/3 (66.67%) of the ingredients on average. This matches the Alchemy Table's and Alchemy Flask's 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ingredients when crafting.
All items affected by this decrafting exception are listed below. Crafted items that already have a special item transmutation are not included, as that transmutation takes precedence over decrafting.


=== Post-Skeletron ===
Items that can be crafted with Bones cannot be decrafted until Skeletron is defeated. Although said items might be acquirable in other ways apart from crafting (e.g. Pianos being found generated throughout the world), this rule still applies regardless of obtainment method.
All items affected by this decrafting exception are listed below. Crafted items that already have a special item transmutation are not included, as that transmutation takes precedence over decrafting.


=== Post-Golem ===
Items that can be crafted with Lihzahrd Bricks cannot be decrafted until Golem is defeated. Although said items might be acquirable in other ways apart from crafting (e.g. Lihzahrd furniture being found in the Jungle Temple), this rule still applies regardless of obtainment method.
All items affected by this decrafting exception are listed below. Crafted items that already have a special item transmutation are not included, as that transmutation takes precedence over decrafting.


=== Non-decraftable ===
Certain items cannot be decrafted at all in order to prevent exploits or certain unfortunate implications.
For example, decrafting the Blizzard in a Bottle (which can be found in Frozen Chests and Frozen/Boreal Crates) would allow obtaining Frost Cores without defeating Ice Golems, and decrafting a Bunny Stew would mean bringing a dead, cooked Bunny back to life.
All non-decraftable items are listed below.


== Critter and enemy transmutations ==
Below is a list of critter and enemy transmutations. Any critter or enemy not listed here will not transmute into anything, and will turn temporarily invisible instead.
These transmutations do not only occur when the respective enemy or critter is submerged in Shimmer, but also when spraying it with the Shimmer Gun.


== NPC transmutations ==
Below is a list of the NPCs' alternative sprites. Transmuting them again returns them to their classic looks.
These transmutations do not only occur when the respective NPC is submerged in Shimmer, but also when spraying them with the Shimmer Gun.


== Notes ==
Projectiles that are reflected upon touching the Shimmer will only be reflected when they reach the Shimmer pool's upper surface. Shooting them at the sides or the bottom of the Shimmer pool (by using Bubbles) will instantly destroy the projectile.
Statue-spawned creatures will not be transformed in Shimmer, despawning instead.
Enemies made invisible by the Shimmer can be seen with a Hunter Potion.
Despite both being designed for use with water, the Super Absorbant Sponge can also soak up Shimmer, as well the Liquid Sensor (Water) being able to detect Shimmer.
When decrafting items whose crafting recipe produces a stack (e.g. Crystal Bullets), the same amount of said item need to be thrown into Shimmer for decrafting. Any excess items will remain untransmuted.
Fallen Stars produced from decrafting will not disappear at daytime. However, if they failed to be picked up by the player (e.g. if they are attracted towards the player, but are not picked up by the player eventually), they will still disappear.
While the Chromatic Cloak is equipped to prevent Shimmering, being submerged in Shimmer is comparable to being submerged in water: the player's horizontal and vertical movement speed are slowed by the same amount, the Shimmer can be swam in using accessories such as Flippers, and the player will transform into Merfolk if wearing the Neptune's Shell or its upgrades. However, the player cannot drown in the Shimmer; the breath meter does not appear.
Entering Shimmer removes and provides immunity to the same debuffs as water (such as On Fire!).
In Expert Mode, touching Shimmer while in the Snow or Ice biome will inflict the player with the Chilled debuff.
Despite the weapons' stats being swapped, shimmering an Ice Boomerang in Remix worlds will not turn it into an Ice Bow and will instead just transmute it into a Snowball Cannon like normal.
This can be used to get a Hardmode ranged weapon very early on in pre-Hardmode.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

The decrafting properties of Shimmer can be utilized in several ways:
One can Shimmer reforge crafted gear for desired modifiers by repeatedly crafting and decrafting the gear.
Extra or outclassed gear can be decrafted to get the materials back.
Items found throughout the world can be looted, then decrafted. Some examples include Underground Cabin furniture and Magic Mirrors.
In multiplayer, excess Recall Potions can be decrafted to potentially get Specular Fish. The Specular Fish can then be crafted into Wormhole Potions.
Similarly, in singleplayer, any Wormhole Potions that may be obtained can be decrafted to potentially get Specular Fish.
Furthermore, most potions can be decrafted two at a time to get Bottles, then Glass, and finally Sand Blocks. Albeit slow, this is one of the ways to make Sand renewable.
Items can be bought from NPCs, then decrafted to get resources.
An Iron Anvil can be bought from the Merchant for 50 Silver and then decrafted into five Iron Bars.
A Furnace can be bought from the Merchant when spoken to in a Jungle for 3 Silver and then decrafted into 20 Stone, four Wood, and three Torches.
Easy ways to teleport to a Shimmer pool include the Aether Pylon (though it requires the actual Aether biome) or Teleporters (which can require more setup).
Covering a Shimmer pool with Aetherium Platforms will prevent the player from accidentally falling in while still letting dropped items through.
Relocating the Shimmer can be done in several ways:
Using pumps, craftable post-Skeletron.
Using the Bottomless Shimmer Bucket, available post-Moon Lord.
The Super Absorbant Sponge, Ultra Absorbant Sponge, Dry Bombs, and Dry Rockets remove Shimmer.
If a lot of certain ore is needed, a kind of higher tier ore can be transmuted down into what is needed. This can be helpful for getting Iron/Lead Ore which is used in a lot of recipes, or obtaining the materials for the Drill Containment Unit.
Shimmer makes it far easier to obtain some items with the most complex crafting recipes by swapping their components, which means that one only needs to obtain a sufficient number of any of them instead of one of each.
Fish Finder
Angler Tackle Bag
Ankh Shield components:
Reflective Shades
Armor Bracing
Medicated Bandage
Countercurse Mantra
The Plan
Greedy Ring
Similarly, Shimmer makes it easier to complete a set of Mining armor or Gladiator armor, or to get a certain emblem dropped by the Wall of Flesh.


== Trivia ==
Shimmer may be a reference to several substances or locations in media that have similar properties:
In the 2018 science fiction horror film Annihilation, an amorphous phenomenon called "the Shimmer" has the power to transform and mutate living things.
In the 1991 action-adventure game The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, areas called Mysterious Ponds allow the player to throw in items and receive a stronger item in return.
In the science fiction television series Doctor Who, a cloaking device called a "shimmer" allows its owner to change their appearance as well as that of others.


== See also ==
Chlorophyte Extractinator(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which can also transmute and exchange items.


== History ==

title: Glowing Mushroom biome
content:
A Glowing Mushroom biome, also known as Glowing Mushroom Fields, is a biome characterized by Mushroom grass, Glowing Mushrooms, and Giant Glowing Mushrooms growing on Mud Blocks. The grasses and plants in a Glowing Mushroom biome emit a vibrant blue glow, along with many of its unique enemies. The Truffle NPC requires a house in a Surface (above-ground) Glowing Mushroom biome and sells mushroom-themed items.

Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes are Glowing Mushroom biomes below 0 depth. They can be found naturally, randomly generating on world creation. The background of an Underground Glowing Mushroom biome depicts numerous small mushrooms. Several mushroom-themed versions of normal Cavern enemies spawn here in pre-Hardmode, and some completely unique enemies will spawn in Hardmode. Giant Glowing Mushrooms will grow if there is enough vertical space. Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes are large, layered caverns which feature Mushroom vines hanging from the ceiling and surface-style Giant Glowing Mushrooms. They generate with set features, including a span of flat ground (for Giant Glowing Mushrooms to grow on), or possibly a wide lake for fishing purposes. These long spans of flat ground are conducive to the spawning of Gold Chests, statues, and other objects which generate underground but rely on having a certain amount of level terrain like Life Crystals, making these biomes attractive when hunting for such things.
Surface Glowing Mushroom biomes are Glowing Mushroom biomes above 0 depth. They do not generate naturally and must instead be created by the player, unless using the Toadstool secret seed. After placing 100 mushroom-related tiles, the biome background will appear, which depicts towering mushrooms. When the biome reaches a size of 160 mushroom-related tiles, the sky will be darkened. There are several exclusive enemies, some of which can also be encountered in Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes.
A Glowing Mushroom biome can be created manually by planting Mushroom Grass Seeds on Mud Blocks, or spraying the Jungle with the Clentaminator using Dark Blue Solution. To be considered Glowing Mushroom biome, an area needs to contain 100 mushroom-related tiles. These include Mushroom grass, naturally grown Glowing Mushrooms, Underground Giant Glowing Mushrooms, and Mushroom vines. However, in the Underground layer and below, the Glowing Mushroom background will only be displayed when there are at least 161 mushroom-related tiles.
The Truffle Worm, a critter used to summon Duke Fishron, can only spawn in an underground Glowing Mushroom biome.


== Contents ==


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
Mushroom grass is immune to being converted by an evil biome.
Use of the Clentaminator with Green Solution on a Glowing Mushroom biome converts it to a Jungle biome. However, attempting to use Purification Powder to convert a Glowing Mushroom biome to a Jungle biome will fail.
Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes do not generate within the Ice biome and the Underground Desert.
In Underground layer and below, while the area functionally changes to a Glowing Mushroom biome at 100 related blocks, the background of a Glowing Mushroom biome will not appear until 161 Glowing Mushroom biome blocks are present.
The Funkytown achievement requires 200 Glowing Mushroom biome blocks nearby the player.
The Funkytown achievement can sometimes be obtained by using a Magic Mirror, Ice Mirror, Cell Phone, or Shellphone while in an Underground Glowing Mushroom biome. This is likely a bug caused by lag.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

An efficient way to create an artificial Glowing Mushroom biome is to put Mud Blocks in such a fashion that they form a grid of 1×1 empty cells. This way, the Mushroom grass has more blocks it can spread to, greatly accelerating the process of creating the biome. Plants and Glowing Mushrooms can grow inside these gaps.
Caution should be taken when creating a Surface Glowing Mushroom biome in pre-Hardmode, as the enemies that spawn there are much more powerful than other pre-Hardmode enemies.
It is a wise idea to make two NPC houses in pre-Hardmode in a surface Glowing Mushroom biome in preparation for the Truffle and a companion NPC such as the Dryad. This will also address the issue listed above, as having NPCs in the biome will drastically reduce enemy spawn rates.
Either Surface or Underground Mushroom biomes will allow obtaining a Mushroom pylon, by building two or more houses and placing chosen NPCs there; it is not necessary to wait for Hardmode and Truffle's appearance.
On the surface, it is easiest to produce the biome in the Jungle due to the prevalence of mud; this can provide a second pylon for the Jungle area. Alternatively, mud can simply be placed as needed. When choosing a location, consider that the Mushroom biome background will appear up to about a screen's width away from the mushroom-related tiles.
A Floating Island can make a good option for a Surface Mushroom biome. This keeps the Mushroom biome and its enveloping darkness out of the way of most surface activities, and will also put it out of the way of biome spread.
Alternatively, the natural Mushroom biomes will mostly appear at great depths, and these can be "colonized" to provide a convenient way-station to the Underworld. Naturally, the NPCs should be fully sealed away from the dangerous local enemies; even so, the spores of Fungi Bulbs and Giant Fungi Bulbs may be troublesome in Hardmode.
Note that NPCs placed in an Underground Mushroom biome will probably qualify as a "Cavern Town", and spawn gem critters in the vicinity. These will look quite odd (and nearly indistinguishable) by the biome's natural lighting, but supplying some brighter lighting will show their various colors.


== Trivia ==

A sample from the 1990 side-scrolling platform game Super Mario World is used in the background music for the Glowing Mushroom biome.
Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes will glow brighter if the player is near the "center" of the biome.
When entering or leaving a Surface Glowing Mushroom biome, there is a noticeable delay as the sunlight fades to darkness, and especially when it returns.

Painting only one Mud Block then using one Mushroom Grass Seed on it and letting it spread to adjacent Mud Blocks will allow to create a whole colored Glowing Mushroom biome. Normal paints will only be visible with a light source while deep paints will always be visible.


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===
Glowing Mushroom backgrounds are combined with the current forest background.

		
		
		
		
		


==== Underground layer ====

		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Mushroom Chests are now guaranteed to have one of their exclusive drops, with the Shroom Minecart and Mushroom Vanity each having a 50% chance.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: The Truffle NPC now likes living in the surface Glowing Mushroom biome.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Added three new backgrounds for the Surface Glowing Mushroom biome.
Mushroom Chests in Underground Cabins now have a 1/2 (50%) chance of containing the Shroom Minecart and a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of containing the Mushroom vanity set. These will spawn as secondary loot alongside the loot from ordinary Gold Chests.
Mushroom Grass Seeds now have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped from destroyed Glowing Mushrooms.
Spore Bats and Spore Skeletons now spawn in the Underground Glowing Mushroom biome at all stages of the game. The former has a 1/100 (1%) chance of dropping the new Mushroom-themed Shroomerang, while the latter drops all of the same loot as other types of Skeletons, including the new Carton of Milk.
The Mushroom Pylon is now sold by any happy NPC in the Glowing Mushroom biome.
Underground Glowing Mushroom biome is now larger and redesigned, with hanging mushroom vines, large lakes for fishing, new backgrounds, and surface biome trees. They also spawn much larger and in a layered formation.
Desktop 1.3.0.3: Fixed a bug where the Truffle Worm would not spawn.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Truffle Worms can now be killed by enemies.
Underground Glowing Mushroom cabins, which spawn with their respective Mushroom furniture and have corresponding loot from Underground Gold Chests, now spawn.
Desktop 1.2.4: The very rare Truffle Worm critter, which is fished as bait to spawn the new Duke Fishron boss, now spawns in the Underground Glowing Mushroom biome in Hardmode.
Desktop 1.2.3: The uncommon Glowing Snail critter will now spawn in the Glowing Mushroom biome.
Desktop 1.2: 
Can now be spread with the Clentaminator using Dark Blue Solution on mud.
Glowing Mushrooms now have their own biome with exclusive backgrounds, enemies, and music:
5 new enemies spawn in the Surface Mushroom biome: Anomura Fungus, Fungi Bulb, Mushi Ladybug, Mushroom Zombie, and Spore Zombie.
In addition, the Anomura Fungus, Fungi Bulb, Fungo Fish, Giant Fungi Bulb, and Mushi Ladybug all spawn in the Underground Glowing Mushroom biome in Hardmode.
Now can be cultivated as a Surface Mushroom biome on the surface:
The new, Surface Mushroom biome-exclusive Truffle NPC will now move into any valid NPC house in a Surface Mushroom biome in Hardmode.
The Dryad will now sell Mushroom Grass Seeds when in the Glowing Mushroom biome.
Desktop-Release: Introduced.

Console 1.0.933.1: Underground Glowing Mushroom cabins and furniture added. ()
Console 1.0.750.0: Underground Glowing Mushroom cabins and furniture added. ()
Console 1.02: Glowing Mushrooms given their own biome (music, background, spawns, etc.) and added the ability to cultivate one on the Surface.

title: Fish (item)
content:
The Fish is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Penguin that follows the player. When the player is flying or is far enough away, the Baby Penguin will use a jetpack to catch up. The Fish has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being obtained from Frozen Chests and a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped from Frozen and Boreal Crates.


== Trivia ==
The Baby Penguin looks similar to the penguin inside the Penguin Cage.
The penguin appears to wear goggles while flying.
The penguin using a jetpack may be a reference to the Learn to Fly video game series.

title: Exotic Chew Toy
content:
The Exotic Chew Toy is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Fennec Fox that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Fennec Fox pet will fly by flapping its ears like wings to catch up to them. The Exotic Chew Toy can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum.


== Trivia ==
The buff tooltip is a reference to the 2013 electronic dance novelty song "The Fox (What Does the Fox Say?)" by Norwegian comedy duo Ylvis, and to the fact that fennec foxes have very large ears.
The item tooltip refers to the fact that fennec foxes are known for being able to produce very high-pitched barks.
The word fennec means fox in Arabic, originating from the Persian fanak. Thus, fennec fox essentially means fox fox.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

title: Party
content:
A Party is an event that can occur randomly, or be activated manually using a Party Center. Parties are mainly visual, having little functional effect on gameplay, with the exception of some exclusive vanity and novelty items available from the Clothier and Party Girl. A Party lasts until dusk (7:30 PM), and if spawned randomly, begins at dawn (4:30 AM).
A Party has a random 1/10 (10%) chance (or 1/7 (14.29%) chance in Celebration Mk 10 worlds) of occurring at any particular dawn ("thrown" by one to three NPCs), without the need for a placed Party Center. See below for the detailed conditions. When NPCs throw a Party, any placed Party Center activates, a burst of confetti appears on each NPC, and a pink status message displays: “Looks like <NPC name>, <NPC name>, and <NPC name> are throwing a party”. At its conclusion, the Party automatically deactivates with a puff of smoke on all NPCs and another pink status message: “Party time's over!”. A Party can still be reinitiated manually afterward.
During a Party, the following effects are active:

All NPCs (including town pets and the Traveling Merchant) except the Old Man, Skeleton Merchant, Tax Collector, and Zoologist wear Party Hats.
NPCs (except for town pets) will also occasionally throw confetti at nearby players.
Balloons continually rise in the background.
Regular Bunnies have a 2/3 (66.67%) chance to be replaced with Party Bunnies, which appear as Bunnies wearing Party Hats, but still only drop regular Bunnies when caught with a Bug Net.
This only applies to naturally spawned Bunnies.
The Clothier and Party Girl sell additional Party-exclusive novelty and vanity items.
Most NPCs display unique quotes when spoken to.
If the Party had occurred naturally:
The Party Girl will give the player a Slice of Cake when spoken to. She will only give this item once per Party, even in multiplayer.
The Cool Slime town pet will move in.


== Contents ==


=== NPC quotes ===
Most NPCs display unique quotes during Parties when spoken to:


== Notes ==
Parties thrown randomly by NPCs can only occur under the following conditions:
The last random party was thrown more than 5–10 days ago (the actual cooldown period is chosen at random when a random Party initiates).
The Party Girl is present.
There are at least five eligible town NPCs present, i.e. those who can throw a Party. Eligible NPCs include the Traveling Merchant, but not town pets, the Old Man, and the Skeleton Merchant.
A Party Center can be used to initiate a Party at any time, regardless of the criteria above (e.g. even if there are no NPCs in the world at all).
The names of the NPCs as well as the number of NPCs who throw a Party are determined randomly:
With 13 or more eligible town NPCs present, there is a 1/5 (20%) chance for three NPCs, a 4/15 (26.67%) chance for two NPCs, and a 8/15 (53.33%) chance for one NPC to throw the Party.
With fewer than 13 town NPCs present, the chances are 1/3 (33.33%) for two NPCs and 2/3 (66.67%) for one NPC. It is impossible for three NPCs to throw the Party in this case.
The status messages if one and two NPCs throw a Party are as follows:
“Looks like <NPC name> is throwing a party”
“Looks like <NPC name> & <NPC name> are throwing a party”
A Party will immediately start in a Celebration Mk 10 world upon world creation.
Worlds with both For the Worthy and Celebrationmk10 seed enabled (e.g. a Zenith world) will instantly kill all town NPCs except the Traveling Merchant, Old Man, and Skeleton Merchant once the first party ends.
Parties affect all NPCs (except the Tax Collector, Old Man, and Skeleton Merchant), regardless of their location in the world.
The background balloons effect will disappear if no NPC is within a 240×135-tile rectangle centered on the player, and there is no Party Center within a 170×125-tile rectangle centered on the player.
A Party will not end even if all NPCs are killed.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
The event was introduced to celebrate Terraria's 5th birthday, May 16, 2016.
Even though the Tax Collector does not wear a Party Hat or say anything related to Parties, he can still throw a Party.
Parties are the only event that allow seeing the hair of some NPCs, most noticeably the Dye Trader.
The Goblin Tinkerer's quote references "pin the tail on the donkey", a party game.
Even though the Pirate's quote is on eating so much cake his beard is white, his beard in his sprite is the same color as always.
The Truffle's quote is a joke on the words mushroom and much room.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
The Merchant now sells Rainbow Glowsticks during a Party.
The Zoologist now sells the Swarm Grenade during a Party.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Zenith worlds' first Party now instantly kills most Town NPCs after it ends.
The Cool Slime can move in during a natural Party.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
The Party Girl now gives a Slice of Cake to the first player that talks to her during the Party.
Parties can now only occur naturally if the Party Girl is present.
Bunnies spawned from Bunny Statues now also wear Party Hats.
Desktop 1.3.2.1: Fixed NPC-started parties occurring only for 1 player in the server at random.
Desktop 1.3.2: Introduced.

Console 1.17: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.1096.2: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.3.2.1 to 1.4.0.1.

title: Pyramid
content:
The Pyramid is a Desert structure composed of Sandstone Bricks. The bulk of it is buried underground, with its tip sometimes visible from the Desert surface. It contains a single zigzagging tunnel leading downwards, with a treasure room in its center. The room contains unique loot and is furnished with unique decorative banners and a variety of Pots and Coin Stashes.
Pyramids are rare structures and will not appear in every world. They are slightly more common in worlds with the special world seed Drunk, while worlds with the Celebration Mk 10 seed always feature a Pyramid as the entrance to the Underground Desert. Pyramids are much more common in worlds with the secret world seed Sandy britches.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
The Pots that generate in Pyramids have the highest chance to spawn a Coin Portal out of every other Pot in the game, with a 1/125 (0.8%) chance of spawning one.
The lowest possible altitude of the tip of a Pyramid is 4' (on the Depth Meter).
The tip of a Pyramid is normally buried 13–19 blocks in the sand, although it can be lower or higher than that if the main Desert with the Underground Desert or an Oasis happens to be generated in the vicinity of a Pyramid. In certain cases, it is even possible for the Pyramid to slightly protrude from the sand.


=== Generation ===
Below are the details about the creation of Pyramids during world generation.
Pyramids can only be generated in Dunes biomes, smaller patches of Desert that do not feature the Underground Desert. The chance that a Pyramid generation attempt occurs in a Dunes biome is 4/5 (80%), but since the attempt may fail (see below), the actual chance of a Dunes biome containing a Pyramid is lower. Only one Pyramid can be generated in a Dunes biome at most, and as the number of Dunes in a world is limited (depending on world size), the maximum possible number of Pyramids is limited accordingly:

The main Desert (with the Underground Desert) is generated after the Dunes biomes but before the Pyramids. As a result, it is possible that the main Desert and Underground Desert are placed in the same location as an existing Dunes biome ("overwriting" it), in which case a Pyramid may be generated in the main Desert and possibly the Underground Desert. The same applies to Oases, which are generated after the Pyramids.


==== Secret world seeds ====
In drunk worlds, the generation chance per Dunes biome is increased to 100%. Again, this does not mean that every Dunes biome is guaranteed to contain a Pyramid, as the generation attempt may fail.
In worlds with Celebration Mk 10 seed active, an additional Pyramid will always be generated in the main Desert, acting as the entrance to the Underground Desert. This Pyramid does not count into the maximum numbers above.


==== Technical details ====
While a Dunes biome is being generated, a potential location for the basis for the tip of a Pyramid is being determined (provided the 4/5 (80%) roll succeeds). The horizontal coordinate of the location is randomly chosen within 200 tiles of the center of the Dunes biome, and the vertical coordinate is 20 tiles below the topmost solid block at the selected horizontal coordinate (checking from the top true world border to the bottom of the world).
After the Dunes biomes and the main Desert have been generated, the previously determined locations are evaluated for the validity of a Pyramid placement.
Each determined potential location must meet the criteria below. Otherwise, the Pyramid will not be generated there.

It must be more than 300 tiles away from the left or right true world borders.
This area is normally occupied by the Ocean, where Dunes biomes cannot be generated anyway.
It must not be located in the short stretch between the Dungeon and the Ocean (i.e., between the Dungeon and the Ocean that is on the same side of the world as the Dungeon), and also has to be at least 630 (small worlds) / 960 (medium) / 1260 (large) tiles horizontally away from the Dungeon.
For example, if the Dungeon is on the left side of the world, Pyramids can only generate at the right side of the Dungeon, and have to be at least 630 / 960 / 1260 tiles away.
In Celebration Mk 10 worlds, the location must not intersect with the Underground Desert.
It must be at least 220 tiles (110 tiles in drunk worlds) horizontally away from any Pyramids that have been generated before, i.e. this restriction does not apply to the first Pyramid that is generated in the world.
It must be above the surface line.
If the tile at the potential location is open air, then the spot is moved downward to the first solid block. As before, this block must be above the surface line, and it must also be a pure Sand Block. If so, the tip of the Pyramid will be one to seven tiles above this Sand Block and the rest of it will be generated going down from there. Otherwise, the Pyramid will not be generated.
It can be seen that the constraints of this process make Pyramids significantly rarer than the seemingly high rate of 80% of Dunes biomes. The initially selected random location oftentimes does not fulfill the criteria, causing the generation attempt to fail, and there are no re-rolls for repeated attempts.


== Tips ==
Pyramids are relatively rare and is not guranteed to generate. There are several ways to search for potential Pyramids in world:
The housing query shows a visual indicator about the "house" at the cursor. By querying areas below the surface Sand, Pyramids can be identified by its zigzagging tunnel.
 Tiles will be briefly displayed at greater brightness when switching lighting mode from White to Retro. This may help locate underground Pyramids.
Since Pyramids are made out of Sandstone Bricks which cannot be corrupted, they can be helpful in blocking the spread of evil biomes or The Hallow.


== Trivia ==
While the Pyramids' real-life counterparts are located in Egypt, the Cactus plants that grow in the nearby Desert are based on the saguaro, a species native to the Sonoran Desert, a desert spanning large areas of Mexico and the United States of America.
An experiment generating one hundred small worlds in 1.2.0.3.1 showed an 83% chance of having no Pyramids, a 15% chance of having one Pyramid, and a 2% chance of having two Pyramids. Another experiment generating one hundred small, medium, and large worlds in 1.3.5 showed a 16% chance in small worlds, 42% chance in medium worlds, and 39% chance in large worlds of having one or multiple Pyramids.
Since then, Pyramids were made more common.

title: Cursed Piper Flute
content:
The Cursed Piper Flute is a transformation mount item that turns the player into a Rat. While in this form, the player has a small hitbox and can fit in 1-tile gaps, but loses their ability to use items; using items will result in the player dismounting and returning to normal. The rat form also grants the player the ability to stick to the sides of blocks by moving in the direction of them, while slowly sliding down. The player can also climb up blocks by holding ▲ Up, and slide down blocks quicker by holding ▼ Down. The rat forms replaces player's hurt sound with a rat's squeak.
The Cursed Piper Flute can be found in Ivy Chests within the Underground Jungle.


== Notes ==
Sticking to blocks refreshes the rat form's jump, allowing the player to perform wall jumps.
The rat form has a top horizontal speed of 38 mph and a jump reach of 8.07 tiles.
The rat slides down blocks at a speed of 5 mph when sticking to them. When holding ▲ Up, it climbs up blocks with a top speed of 8 mph, and when holding ▼ Down, it slides down blocks more quickly with a top speed of 23 mph.
Using a Featherfall Potion or equipping Djinn's Curse reduces the base sliding speed to 3 mph, but does not affect sliding speed when holding ▼ Down. It also increases the climbing speed when holding ▲ Up to 10 mph.
Equipping Climbing Claws or Shoe Spikes or any of their upgrades allows the player to fully stick to blocks without sliding down, unless ▼ Down is held. It also increases the climbing speed when holding ▲ Up to 13 mph.
When both of the above effects are combined, the player can fully stick to blocks without sliding down unless ▼ Down is held, and the climbing speed when holding ▲ Up is increased to 15 mph.
The rat form reduces fall damage by 90%.
While in rat form, the player takes up less space, being only 0.875 tiles wide and tall.
Like other transformation mounts that reduce the player's size, if the player attempts to dismount in a place where they cannot fit, the dismount will fail. On the third attempt, the player will be teleported to the nearest open space and dismount. If there is no valid location within 25 tiles to the top and left of the player's feet and 24 tiles to the bottom and right of the player's feet, the player will instead be teleported to the world spawn point.


== Tips ==
Since the rat can be transformed in and out of in combat, players may use it to reduce their hitbox size when dodging large numbers of projectiles.


== Trivia ==
The Cursed Piper Flute is a reference to the medieval German folk tale of the Pied Piper of Hamelin. According to the legend, the piper was a rat catcher hired by the town of Hamelin, which was suffering from a rat infestation, to lure the rats away with his magic pipe.
Using Reflective Gold Dye on this mount gives a close imitation of a Gold Mouse.

title: Swiftness Potion
content:
The Swiftness Potion is a buff potion which grants the Swiftness buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's maximum movement speed by 25%, but does not stack with sprinting accessories (such as Hermes Boots), nor does it affect the speed of mounts. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Swiftness Potions can be found in pots, chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Though the Swiftness buff alone will not boost the player's top running speed when they have a sprinting accessory equipped, it will boost top speed further when running on Asphalt Blocks, and also increases horizontal air speed by an extremely small amount.
The Swiftness buff stacks with the effects of the Slice of Cake.
The Swiftness Potion can also be used with Sunflowers and other movement accessories to increase the player's top speed even further.

title: Toy Tank
content:
The Toy Tank is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Santank Mount that grants mounted players an extra jump and has two auto-targeting weapons attached: A front-facing machine gun and a homing rocket launcher. The Toy Tank is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 6.25–25% chance depending on the current wave.
The maximum movement speed of the mount is 41 mph, and it takes about 1.5 seconds to reach top speed. The maximum jump height is 12 tiles without a double jump, or 26 tiles with the double jump when timed right. The double jump can be stacked with other extra jump accessories. The Santank is 2 tiles wide and 3 tiles tall, meaning that it does not change the player's height and makes it easier to travel through narrower corridors than with larger mounts such as the Unicorn Mount and Pirate Ship Mount.
The Santank's two attached weapons only fire if there are enemies in front of the player. The machine gun's bullets deal 100 base damage and are fired in a spread of 22.9°, making the weapon somewhat inaccurate. The homing rockets are initially fired directly upwards, deal 120 base damage, and seek the closest target after being fired, including targets that are outside the mount's initial detection range (e.g. enemies behind the player). The damage of the projectiles does not scale with any damage bonuses the player has, but their critical strike chance is affected by the player's ranged critical strike chance. The machine gun fires a bullet every 0.17 seconds (i.e. 6 shots per second), while the rocket launcher fires a rocket every 0.67 seconds.


== Notes ==

The Santank Mount's detection range is a cone-shaped area of 120° in front of the player (60° above the horizontal axis and 60° below) which extends up to 53.125 tiles from the player (highlighted in red in the image on the right).
This is merely the mount's target detection area. It can hit enemies that are outside (the machine gun's bullets can hit enemies that are more than 53.125 tiles away and the homing rockets can hit enemies virtually anywhere), but neither weapon will fire if there are no enemies with a direct line of sight to the player in this detection area.
The player can use items or other weapons while the tank attacks.
It cancels fall damage.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Although the mount has decent DPS and is reasonably fast, it limits the player to double jump accessories. This behavior is typically detrimental to survival since wings are preferable most of the time, but it has some use cases, namely for the Solar Pillar as Crawltipedes only attack players in the air, and the Old One's Army as outside of Betsy in the final wave of the Post-Golem tier, the enemies for the event have poor mobility and will generally target the Eternia Crystal over the player.
The Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons pairs well with the mount's built-in double jump.


== Trivia ==
Its tooltip, 'For the REALLY naughty ones.', is a reference to Santa Claus' nice and naughty list. The buff tooltip, "Crossing off the naughty list...", references the same story.
The name of the Santank Mount itself is a reference to the name of the Santa-NK1 while it was in development.

title: Water Walking Potion
content:
The Water Walking Potion is a buff potion which grants the Water Walking buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to walk on the surface of all liquids (water, lava, honey, and Shimmer), and prevents fall damage when falling onto liquid surfaces. The player can sink into liquids by pressing ▼ Down. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Water Walking Potions can be found in pots and chests.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Tips ==
Despite the description, players are also able to walk on lava without taking damage and without the need for the Obsidian Skin Potion. This makes it a viable alternative to Obsidian Skin Potions when traversing the Underworld, as the ingredients required are generally safer to obtain (though more time-consuming to gather in bulk). Players should still take care when dropping long distances onto lava, as they may find themselves partially submerged and take damage from the lava.
This potion can be used to make the Ocean into a makeshift arena, for fights against the Dreadnautilus or Duke Fishron, for instance.
While Lava Waders (and their upgrade, the Terraspark Boots) partially combine the functionalities of this potion and the Obsidian Skin Potion, they require an additional accessory slot.


== Trivia ==
The buff icon appears to depict the Guide.

title: Fuzzy Carrot
content:
The Fuzzy Carrot is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bunny Mount. It has a top speed of 40 mph. The Fuzzy Carrot is obtained from the Angler as a reward for completing his 5th fishing quest.


== Notes ==
The Bundle of Balloons stacks for higher jumps, and the Lava Waders will allow walking on water, honey, and lava.
Having the Cloud in a Bottle or any double-jump accessory equipped gives the player the ability to jump twice while riding the bunny.
Riding the Bunny negates fall damage.
When using a weapon with autoswing (such as the Terra Blade), while moving away from the fire direction, the Bunny Mount will appear to moonwalk.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Summoning or de-summoning emits a significant amount of light particles with the same velocity as the character that last about 2 seconds, fading in both brightness and speed over the duration. This can be useful in cave exploration, as by pressing Quick Mount when grappled to a wall, the particles will reveal an area behind it.
This mount is quite a bit easier to obtain than the others since it does not need any bosses to be beaten, does not cost any coins, and can be obtained quickly and reliably. Even if one has no interest in fishing it may be worth taking the time to do five Angler quests for the early game mobility boost.


== Trivia ==
It is the only fishing quest reward not related to water or fishing in any way.
However, there is a Bunnyfish quest fish.
The Fuzzy Carrot, along with most (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) / all  other pre-Hardmode mounts, is one of the few pre-Hardmode items with a rarity of .

title: Acid Venom
content:
Acid Venom is a Hardmode debuff that prevents health regeneration and causes the afflicted entity to take damage each second for the duration of the debuff. Enemies lose 30 health per second (15 damage displayed every 0.5 seconds), while players lose 15 health per second (1 damage displayed every 0.07 seconds).
Its damage can be increased by Accelerated Afflictions.
Certain sources of Acid Venom additionally inflict Potent Acid alongside it. The combination of the two debuffs is referred to as Potent Venom in item tooltips.

title: Jungle Temple
content:
The Jungle Temple (also known as the Lihzahrd Temple or simply The Temple) is a large, enclosed structure constructed out of Lihzahrd Bricks and located in the Underground Jungle. It is always present in any generated world, but can only be properly entered after Plantera has been defeated. The Jungle Temple contains unique Lihzahrd-themed enemies, traps, and furniture. The Lihzahrd Furnace, a crafting station for further Lihzahrd-themed furniture, can be found in its Chests. The Lihzahrd Altar found in the Temple's final chamber is used to summon the Golem boss. Defeating Golem triggers the spawning of Cultists, used to summon the Lunar Events.
The Temple is entered via the Lihzahrd Door located at one of its two top corners. The door is initially locked, requiring a Temple Key to open, which is dropped by Plantera. Unlocking the door consumes one Temple Key from the player's inventory, and the door remains permanently unlocked for all players in the world. It is generally impossible to enter the Temple via any other conventional means since Lihzahrd Bricks can only be mined with at least the Picksaw dropped by Golem, and Lihzahrd Brick Walls impose numerous restrictions, e.g. on Teleporter use. There are, however, several methods to enter the temple prior to defeating Plantera.
The Temple's entrance leads to a long corridor that winds downward through several chambers, ending in a large room at the bottom containing the Lihzahrd Altar. The Altar can be used to summon Golem at the cost of one Lihzahrd Power Cell. Lihzahrd Power Cells are guaranteed to be found in the Temple's Lihzahrd Chests and are also dropped randomly by the Temple's Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes.
The entire Temple is filled with several types of traps, including Flame, Spear, Spiky Ball, and Super Dart Traps. Traps occur much more frequently in the Temple than in the Dungeon and are far more dangerous and damaging. They are activated by Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, which only respond to players (enemies walk on them freely without triggering them). As in the Dungeon, all Temple traps, pressure plates, and wires can be looted by the player for use in player-built mechanisms.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
Even during pre-Hardmode, Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes can spawn outside the Jungle Temple, if the player is standing directly in front of a Lihzahrd Brick Wall (in the Temple's entrance, for example). They pose a very high threat to players with early-game equipment.
Before defeating Plantera, the Lihzahrd Brick Walls will prevent the teleport of following items. The player will not be teleported if the destination is in front of a Lihzahrd Brick Wall.
Teleporters, the Rod of Discord, and the Rod of Harmony will simply not teleport the player.
Pylons will show the status message "Ancient forces prevent you from accessing this location..." when used, and the player will not be teleported.
The player cannot remove any traps other than the Wooden Spikes without a Picksaw or a better pickaxe. It is also impossible to see, cut, or place wires in front of Lihzahrd Brick Walls before defeating the Golem. However, Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are still mineable.
In extremely rare cases, it is possible for the Jungle Temple to generate almost entirely outside of the Underground Jungle, with only a small portion of the edge still touching it. This can happen in worlds even without secret seed world generation modifications to the Jungle Temple. If the player is having trouble looking for the Jungle Temple inside the Jungle, it may be best to check the edges of neighboring biomes.
In a For the Worthy world, the Jungle Temple is 3× bigger than in a normal world. This often means that finding the temple is trivial as it more often than not extends down into the Underworld. Great caution needs to be made, however, as despite being considered in the temple, the Altar in its natural position causes Golem to enter its enraged state due to being in the Underworld. This can also happen in a drunk world.
In a Remix or Zenith world, the Jungle Temple will generate on the surface.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

The Jungle Temple is densely wired. Collecting all wires in the Temple (using the Wire Cutter or The Grand Design) can net a player over 1000 wires.
The Dangersense Potion is useful for avoiding traps, as the buff also highlights Wooden Spikes in addition to traps and pressure plates.
If the player is overwhelmed by Lihzahrds, a way to disable the traps is to shoot at them with some Rocket IV / Mini Nuke II, removing the Pressure Plates and the Wooden Spikes.
The traps can be disarmed by directly removing the wires connecting them to Pressure Plates. The Grand Design can be helpful for doing this.
This can only be done after defeating the Golem.
The Lihzahrd Furnace can be sold for 2 Gold and since every chest inside the temple contains one, selling excess ones is an effective way of making money.
If the player is having trouble locating the temple, consider using the Clentaminator's spray to light up the surrounding environment to highlight the Jungle Temple on the map.


== Trivia ==
The colors of Wires in the Jungle Temple appear to be based on the horizontal position of the pressure plate they originate from.
Life Crystals can generate in the Jungle Temple, although it is extremely rare.

title: Dark Mage's Tome
content:
The Dark Mage's Tome is a mount-summoning item that places the player on a Book Mount which grants limited flight. The Dark Mage's Tome has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Dark Mage in Master Mode.
The mount allows a player to hover and glide at a fixed height of 8 tiles high in mid-air for 5 seconds following a jump or walking off a ledge. It otherwise glides along the ground, and automatically climbs ledges that are no more than 1-tile-high. Whether on the ground or hovering, its top speed is 41 mph. The Book Mount also cancels fall damage.
Extra jump accessories can be used during hover, increasing the max hover height. The height is also adjustable in the down direction by pressing ▼ Down.


== Achievements ==


== Notes ==
Hovering is triggered when the player leaves the ground while mounted. Mounting in midair will not trigger hovering.
This mount has unusual interactions with platforms, flat-surface items, and other non-block surfaces:
While mounted, the player can move onto platforms and flat-surface items from adjacent blocks that are flush with the surface, but will pass through them if airborne in any way, including jumping, falling, hovering, or upon taking knockback.
The player cannot use stairs while mounted. They will pass through ascending stairs and hover above descending stairs.
Water Walking Boots and its upgrades have no effect. As with ledges, the mount will glide for 5 seconds, then fall into the liquid.


== Tips ==
The hover time will not be consumed when gliding on the ground, meaning that the player can glide infinitely as long as they are on the ground. This can be used for quicker traveling, as the top speed of the mount is higher than that of the Lightning Boots or its upgrades (41 mph vs. 34 mph).
For a pre-Hardmode arena, it would be better to use other mounts like Fuzzy Carrot, Golf Cart Keys, Saddles for horizontal mobility or Slimy Saddle for vertical mobility.


== See also ==
Other pre-Hardmode items that allow limited hover:

Bee Mount(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions)
Flying Carpet

title: Fishing
content:
Fishing is an activity accomplished by using a fishing pole at a body of liquid (water, honey, or lava) while having bait in the player's inventory. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button will cast a fishing line along with the bobber, which only functions when the bobber is thrown into liquid. Pressing the button again when the bobber moves up and down will reel in the line and often an item will come up with the line. The Angler NPC provides daily fishing quests and rewards their completion with an assortment of equipment, paintings, coins, potions, and vanity items.
Fishing provides an assortment of game resources: Crafting materials for potions and food, a variety of very useful accessories such as mobility improvements like the Frog Leg or Balloon Pufferfish, and even pets such as the Zephyr Fish. Some fish can even be used as tools or weapons. Through crates, fishing also provides an alternative source for ores, coins, many chest items, and some exclusive specialties such as the Falcon Blade, Sailfish Boots, Tsunami in a Bottle, and Enchanted Sundial.
While fishing is not strictly necessary for game progression, some of the Angler's quest rewards (the Fish Finder components) are required to complete the Shellphone. Fishing is also required to summon and fight Duke Fishron.
For pre-Hardmode players, fishing can be a good way of obtaining money and equipment; by mid-Hardmode, it is less competitive with other money-making options, enemy drops, and advancing equipment.


== Requirements ==

75 connected tiles of liquid are required (1,001 for Oceans, 50 for honey) in order for fishing to work, and 300 or more tiles to be optimal (1,001 for Oceans, 200 for honey). The width of the top row of continuous liquid tiles (the row where the fishing bobber sits) determines the calculated pond width, and then the depth directly below those is counted. If the pond becomes wider at lower depths, that additional width is not counted. The player may successfully fish in a 1-tile-wide pond, as long as it is 75 tiles deep. The distance of the bobber to the shoreline does not matter. These tile requirements (75 required, 300 optimal) are identical for lava fishing.
It is possible to fish while partially submerged in liquid, as long as the player's arms are above the bobber.
Fishing can, however, be done while moving, flying, while grappled to blocks, sitting on a chair, while floating on liquid with the Slime Mount, or while standing on top of the surface of the liquid, e.g. using Water Walking Boots.
Fishing can be done in lava, but will only work with the Hotline Fishing Hook, the Lavaproof Fishing Hook (or its upgrades), or by using a Magma Snail, Lavafly, or Hell Butterfly as bait. It can take much longer to get a bite in lava due to the smaller drop table, but the chances increase with at least two of these sources, and increase further with all three; see the Catch frequency section below for details.
Fishing in Shimmer is impossible. As soon as the fishing pole's bobber touches the liquid, the player is inflicted with the Shimmering debuff and fishing is instantly canceled.


== Fishing quests ==

Catching a quest fish for the Angler NPC requires fishing in the proper biome and height for the day's current quest, which can be determined by talking to the Angler. The Angler gives out special rewards when the correct quest fish is turned in. Quest fish cannot be caught if the player already has that particular quest fish in their inventory, if the quest fish was already turned in that day, or if the Angler is not alive. However, if the player puts the quest fish in a storage item, the trash slot, or simply drop it on the ground, then they may catch another quest fish to store it for later. This saves time and effort, in case the same quest is repeated afterwards. The Angler changes his quest every day at dawn (4:30 AM). Although there is no other way of knowing where the quest fish is, the player does not need to speak with him beforehand to be able to catch it.


== Factors ==
Given the prerequisites for fishing are fulfilled, some factors influence the quality/rarity of the caught item. There is a variety of relevant equipment:

Certain accessories and items. They can stack with each other, and most of them are rewarded from Angler quests. (Lavaproof Tackle Bag, Angler Tackle Bag, and Angler Earring stack with each other for a combined total of +30 Fishing Power).
Buffs from certain potions help with fishing, all of which can be crafted or rewarded by the Angler.
Fishing poles can be crafted, received as Angler rewards, bought from other NPCs, or found in chests.
Bait comes from multiple sources: captured critters, Angler rewards, crates, and even crafting.
Chum Buckets can be dropped by enemies spawned by Blood Moon fishing.
The Gummy Worm gives a permanent boost of 3 to Fishing Power.
Sitting on any chair or toilet increases Fishing Power by 5.
All the factors are combined into a total Fishing Power that determines the chances of higher-quality catches. Fishing Power is calculated by starting with adding these three basic factors:

The Fishing Power of the fishing pole used.
The bait power of the bait used.
Effects from items and potions.
After the above three kinds of factors are added, bonuses (or penalties) are applied, as follows:

The time the player is fishing, as a multiplicative factor applied to the previous factors. These factors are listed in the "time" table below and stacked multiplicatively (e.g. when fishing during Full Moon and between 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM, the factor would be 1.3×1.1=1.43).
The number of Chum Buckets used on the liquid's surface, as a flat bonus.
The size of the lake. Lakes with fewer than 300 tiles (200 for honey) incur a Fishing Power penalty, as a multiplicative percentage applied to the previous factors.
When fishing without the High Test Fishing Line, Lavaproof Tackle Bag, or Angler Tackle Bag, there is always a 1/7 (14.29%) chance that the fishing line will break on reel-in, forfeiting the caught item. Chances of consuming bait remain the same even if the line breaks. With one of the three accessories equipped, the line never breaks.
The exact stats of factors that increase or decrease Fishing Power are listed in the tables below. Because some of the bonus factors are multiplicative, the Fishing Power amounts given by any of the three basic factors can seem to vary depending on, e.g., time of day or weather (For example, when fishing during rain, the Angler Earring can appear to provide more than just +10 Fishing Power).


=== Luck ===
The player's luck statistic affects their Fishing Power. This effect is hidden, i.e. it never affects the numbers displayed in the UI by the Fisherman's Pocket Guide or related accessories.
If the player has bad (negative) luck, there is a chance (determined once every catch attempt) that their Fishing Power will be reduced. Similarly, good (positive) luck gives a chance of increasing their Fishing Power.

If a player has total luck less than zero, then there is a (−100 × luck)% chance per catch attempt that the player's Fishing Power will be reduced by −10% to −40%.
If a player has total luck greater than zero, then there is a (100 × luck)% chance per catch attempt that the player's Fishing Power will be increased by +10% to +40%.
Actual fishing catches are not influenced by luck beyond Fishing Power.
The chance of catching crates is not affected by luck, although which kind of crate is caught is affected. This is because crates have a flat percentage chance of being caught, which is not affected by Fishing Power or luck, but if a crate is caught, the kind of crate is determined by Fishing Power. See the Crate mechanics section below for further details.


== Fishing poles ==
Fishing poles are used with bait for fishing. Some are craftable, while others are either sold by NPCs, found in chests, or are awarded by the Angler.


== Bait ==
Baits are required to obtain fishing catches. They are mostly caught critters, and can also be obtained from crates or rewarded by the Angler NPC.


== Catches ==


=== Items ===

A large variety of items can be fished up. They generally cannot be obtained in any other way, save for a few exceptions. Most items can only be caught in a certain biome or layer (see Mechanics below for details).
Fishing catches can be roughly grouped into the following categories:

Crafting materials, primarily used for crafting potions (including food)
Quest fish, which are used for fishing quests
Usable items – weapons, tools, accessories, and others
Crates, grab bags that contain various random loot
Junk items, which have a chance to replace all other water catches when the player's fishing power is less than 49 and the pond has less than 300 tiles of liquid.


=== Enemies ===
When fishing in water during a Blood Moon event, several Blood Moon-themed enemies can bite the line. These enemies are:

There is a 1/6 (16.67%) chance for one of these enemies to bite the line instead of a fish. (1/3 (33.33%) chance with the Chum Caster.) Note that Fishing Power has no effect on this chance, nor does the use of Chum Buckets. The type of enemy is determined after this chance.
In pre-Hardmode, Zombie Mermen and Wandering Eye Fish each have 1/2 (50%) chance to bite. In Hardmode, the Dreadnautilus has 1/10 (10%) chance to bite and the other four enemies each have 9/40 (22.5%) chance to bite.
If the player is using a Sonar Potion, the enemy's name will be shown in red. Reeling the line spawns the enemy at the bobber's location.


=== Town pet ===
During a Blood Moon event, fishing in water can also spawn an exclusive town pet: the Surly Slime.
If the Surly Slime is not obtained in the world, upon retracting the line during a Blood Moon, there is a 1/5 (20%) chance for each fishing enemy spawn to be replaced with the Surly Slime. Note that Fishing Power has no effect on this mechanic, nor does the use of Chum Buckets.
Once the Surly Slime is fished up, it will respawn naturally if killed, without the need to fish up another, and fishing during Blood Moon will not produce new Surly Slimes.


=== Visible catches ===

When fishing, possible catches are randomly displayed in the pond near the bobber. Only item catches are visible, while enemy and NPC catches are not.


== Mechanics ==


=== Catch frequency ===
When fishing, there is a hidden catch counter which tracks the player's progress toward making a catch. The counter normally starts at 0 and increases over time. When it exceeds 660, there is a [math]\displaystyle{ \frac{75+\text{Fishing Power}}{2}\times100\% }[/math] chance that a fish will bite (capping out at 123 Fishing Power, a 100% chance). The counter then resets to 0, regardless of whether or not there was a bite.
When fishing in lava with at least two/three of the following item kinds in use, the counter resets to 240/480 instead (if there was no bite): lava bait, a Hotline Fishing Hook, and/or a lava-proof accessory (Lavaproof Fishing Hook or its upgrades).
The catch counter increases every tick according to these factors:

Therefore, a formula for the average catch rate would look like this:
[math]\displaystyle{ {\frac{660\times\frac{points}{bite}}{\left(1.5+1+\frac{\text{Fishing Power}}{30}+1.5\times\frac{\text{Fishing Power}}{300}\right)\times\frac{points}{tick}}\div60\times\frac{ticks}{second}} }[/math]
or simply:
[math]\displaystyle{ {\frac{11}{2.5+\frac{23}{600}\times\text{Fishing Power}}\times\frac{seconds}{bite}} }[/math]
Accounting for the chances of failed bites, the average catch rates below and above 123 Fishing Power look like the following:

It is also important to note that below 123 Fishing Power, the maximum time required for a fish to actually bite is unbounded. Should the bite check consistently fail, catch times can potentially become arbitrarily long. At a Fishing Power of 25, multiple failures for a given cast of the fishing rod are quite plausible. If the bite check fails the first four attempts but succeeds on the fifth, the total time for the catch will become approximately 15.9 seconds. This outcome can potentially occur 1/16 (6.25%) of the time when fishing with 25 Fishing Power.


==== Reel in time ====
Whenever a bite occurs, the bobber will move up and down for a short duration, and reeling in the line during this period will yield a fishing catch. The reel in time is affected by Fishing Power: measured in ticks, it equals to the player's Fishing Power, plus a random value in 91–240 (inclusive). Each tick, this time is reduced by a random value in 1–4 (inclusive). If the player did not reel in the line during this time, the bite expires, and the catch counter resets.


=== Biomes ===

When fishing in lava or honey, the player can only get fishing catches from that specific liquid, regardless of the location of the lake.
When fishing in water, a player can be eligible for catching fish from multiple biomes at once if they are in a hybrid biome. However, certain biomes take priority over others. The priority order is listed in the following table.
If a player is in multiple biomes but the higher priority biome does not generate a fish, the game will proceed to check for fish in subsequent biomes. Desert and Ocean will block all catches from lower priority biomes due to having plentiful catches.
Specially, when fishing in the Ocean, the game checks for the bobber's location instead of the player's location. The bobber has to be located in the Ocean biome and above surface to yield Ocean catches.
Items that can only be caught in "pure" biomes (Forest biome in all layers, from top of the world to bottom they are: Space/Sky, regular surface Forest, pure Underground, pure Cavern) would require the biome not overlapping with any other biomes. Otherwise, the player can only get fishing catches from the overlapping biomes.
Worlds with Remix special world seed have some special rules about "pure" biomes, see Notes section below for details.


==== Notes ====
The background and music playing have a different priority order, and will not necessarily match which biome is used for generating fish; for example, if Glowing Mushroom music is playing but there is enough Ebonstone nearby, the player will not be able to find Glowing Mushroom quest fish and will get Corruption catches instead.
In Not the Bees worlds, there is a 1/2 (50%) chance for a fishing attempt not to be considered as a Jungle attempt and a 1/2 (50%) chance for fishing attempts in honey to be considered as in water instead. The latter also applies to Zenith worlds.
In Remix worlds:
When fishing in the Cavern layer (see below for details about layers), if the fishing attempt yields surface crates, there is a 1/2 (50%) chance for it to be changed to yield Ocean crates. If the fishing attempt yields other surface catches, there is a 1/3 (33.33%) chance for it to be changed to yield Ocean catches.
When fishing in the Space layer, the player is never considered in the Corruption or Crimson.


=== Layers ===

The height requirement (Space/Surface/Underground/Cavern) refers to the position of the fishing bobber, not the player. Thus, setting up two pools at different altitudes around the border of two layers allows fishing in either layer while standing in the same spot.
The five layers in fishing are roughly the same as the layers of the world:


==== Notes ====
In worlds with the special world seed Remix enabled, the Underground and Cavern layers are swapped when fishing: Catches normally exclusive to the Underground layer can only be caught in the Cavern layer in those worlds and vice versa. Furthermore, in those worlds there is a random chance that a fishing attempt in the Cavern layer is treated as if it were in a different area:
1/6 (16.67%) chance for the bobber to be considered to be in a surface Ocean biome.
1/3 (33.33%) chance for the bobber to be considered to be in the surface layer, but not in an Ocean biome.
With the remaining chance of 1/2 (50%), no change occurs and the bobber is considered to be in the Cavern layer as normal.


=== Catch quality ===

There are 6 different catch quality slots for catches, each with its own associated chance:

The denominators are rounded down. A Fishing Power of 85, for example, would have a [math]\displaystyle{ \frac{1}{\left\lfloor\frac{4500}{85}\right\rfloor}= }[/math] 1/52 (1.92%) chance of an Extremely Rare catch.
When a new fish is generated, each different catch quality is checked for success, separately from one another. For example, the Uncommon, Rare, and Very Rare rolls might all succeed, while the Common and Extremely Rare rolls fail. Then, depending on which roll(s) succeed as well as factors such as height and biome, the game will generate a fish.
With some exceptions, the highest catch quality roll that succeeded will take priority over lower catch quality slots in determining which fish a player receives. However, not every catch quality slot will contain a fish that can be caught; in that case, the game will move on to checking lower catch qualities. Success at the higher catch quality roll will not carry down to lower quality slots. For example, if the Rare roll succeeded but there is no Rare fish available to be caught, the game will move on to checking whether or not the Uncommon roll succeeded; if the Uncommon roll failed, it will move on to checking Common.
Each biome has a list of available biome-specific fish that can be caught there, based on the catch quality rolls and other factors. If no biome-specific fish is generated, the game will move on to checking subsequent, lower priority biomes. Many of the fish available in catch quality slots vary based on randomness, so succeeding at a catch quality roll in a specific biome does not guarantee that the player will get a specific fish of that quality or any fish of that quality at all. If no fish is selected for the slot, the game will proceed to check more common slots instead and move on to subsequent biomes if and only if none of those slots contain fish either.
When fishing in the water, a successful Extremely Rare roll will always check for a special catch first (Advanced Combat Techniques, Dread of the Red Sea, Frog Leg, Balloon Pufferfish, and Zephyr Fish, in that order). If none of these checks succeed, the game will then check for biome-specific fish.
All quest fish occupy the Uncommon slot.
There are only four Plentiful fish: Bass, Trout, Flounder, and Rock Lobster. If all other checks fail and the player is fishing in the water, they will catch one of these by default: Trout if fishing in the Ocean, Flounder or Rock Lobster if fishing in the Desert or Oasis on (with Rock Lobster being half as common as Flounder), and Bass otherwise.


=== Crate mechanics ===
There is a separate roll to determine if a crate is caught, defaulting to 10% (or 25% with a Crate Potion active). A Rare catch will generate a biome crate if available; if no biome crate is available or no biome is present, an Extremely Rare or Very Rare catch will generate a Golden Crate, a Rare or Uncommoncatch will generate an Iron Crate, and a Wooden Crate otherwise. In Hardmode, the crate will be the Hardmode-equivalent crate.
Fishing in honey will never generate a crate. Fishing in lava can generate crates, but those crates will be either Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates.


=== Stack sizes ===

Stackable fish (i.e., Bomb Fish and Frost Daggerfish) generate in stacks that vary based on the player's Fishing Power. These can vary significantly, with higher Fishing Power levels generating higher minimum stack sizes as well as significantly higher maximum stack sizes.


== Notes ==
There are a total of 16 different fishing locations that can yield distinct catches.
The number of completed quests is tied to the character, rather than the world. The minimum number required for a particular reward can be accrued by completing quests in multiple worlds. The number of completed quests for the purposes of achievements is instead a running total for all characters in all worlds, so multiple characters can contribute to earning achievements.
There is no overlap between "fishable" fish and critters or enemies: The player may fish up a Golden Carp or Tropical Barracuda, but never a Goldfish or Piranha. Even if the player can see a Goldfish in the water, they need a Bug Net rather than a fishing pole to capture it.
The bobber will move two or three times per bite, after which the fish will go away, but the line will remain cast. As long as the reel-in occurs before this animation ends, the timing of the click does not affect the quality of the catch.
It is possible to catch a day's quest fish without having asked the Angler about it.
Time must pass naturally from 4:29 AM to 4:30 AM (the start of a new day) before another quest begins.
Sleeping will make time accelerate. This will make completing more quests easier.
With an Enchanted Sundial, the player can get a new quest immediately.
Ocean-only catches, including quest fish, cannot be caught from a Hallowed or Corrupted/Crimson Ocean. They may be catchable further out towards the map edge, where biome Sand Blocks are farther from the water surface. When the Ocean biome music plays, Ocean fish can be caught.
The minimum height for Sky fishing in all world sizes is higher than that for generating floating lakes. Because of this, a floating lake can be generated too low to be counted as Sky, and will only yield surface fish and crates.
Fishing can be done on reverse gravity (using the Gravitation Potion or the Gravity Globe); the bobber would fall "upwards" into the water, and fish can be caught as usual.
Weapons and accessories obtained through fishing will never have any modifiers.
Despite being used in the crafting recipe, the Angler Earring's Fishing Power bonus stacks with the Angler Tackle Bag, which again stacks with the Lavaproof Tackle Bag.
