title: Guide:Blood Moon strategies
content:
A Blood Moon is a common randomly occurring event that takes place over the course of an entire night; however, a Blood Moon can also be initiated when the player uses a Bloody Tear(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Blood Moons are signaled by the message "The Blood Moon is rising..." in the lower left corner of the screen (or the top middle of the screen on  Mobile).
A Blood Moon will only occur if at least one player in the world has more than 120 health, and only on nights when a moon is present (any night except a new moon). Given those criteria, a Blood Moon has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance of occurring. It will also not spawn if another event is currently taking place, such as Lantern Night(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Slime Rain(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Weather-related occurrences (like Windy Days(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Thunderstorms(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) do not count as events, so there can be crossovers.


== Contents ==


=== NPC quotes ===
Some NPCs display unique quotes during a Blood Moon when spoken to:


== Effects ==
While a Blood Moon is active, multiple effects can happen:
=== Enemies ===

The spawn rate of enemies on the surface increases. Not only do they spawn faster, but more are spawned than can normally exist on-screen at once.
This works no matter the environment, so for example Corruption and Crimson enemies can swarm more than they normally would.
It only affects spawn rates above the surface. Spawn rates below the surface remain the same.
Enemies can spawn near towns, even though those normally suppress enemy spawns.
Zombies and their counterparts become able to open Doors.
Goldfish, Bunnies, and Penguins turn into Corrupt Goldfish, Corrupt Bunnies and Corrupt Penguins in Corruption worlds, or Vicious Goldfish, Vicious Bunnies, and Vicious Penguins in Crimson worlds.
Those spawned from Statues will also become Corrupt/Vicious, and do not revert to their regular forms after the Blood Moon is over. If it is raining during the event, transformed Goldfish will flop around on the ground, instead of walking.


=== Fishing ===
When fishing in water during a Blood Moon event, several Blood Moon-themed enemies can bite the line. These enemies are:

There is a 1/6 (16.67%) chance for one of these enemies to bite the line instead of a fish. (1/3 (33.33%) chance with the Chum Caster.) Note that Fishing Power has no effect on this chance, nor does the use of Chum Buckets. The type of enemy is determined after this chance.
In pre-Hardmode, Zombie Mermen and Wandering Eye Fish each have 1/2 (50%) chance to bite. In Hardmode, the Dreadnautilus has 1/10 (10%) chance to bite and the other four enemies each have 9/40 (22.5%) chance to bite.
If the player is using a Sonar Potion, the enemy's name will be shown in red. Reeling the line spawns the enemy at the bobber's location.


=== Visual effects ===

A red filter will be applied to the screen, shifting the colors of all entities and light towards red and purple shades. Some of the unique effects of this filter are listed below:
The filter will also alter the projectile colors of many weapons.
Placed Living Cursed Fire Blocks turn yellow, creating a unique effect.
The Glowing Mushroom Biome, which is normally blue, will appear pink-purple because of the red shader.
Almost all water will turn red, including rain.


=== Other effects ===
Deathweed blooms during a Blood Moon.
The Zoologist NPC will transform into her werefox form.


== Preparation ==


=== General tips ===


=== Arena ===
Due to town NPCs being vulnerable to enemies during this event, it is recommended that you make your base above ground level at the beginning. If you have already made a base, a simple barricade of a block or some kind of furniture (such as a Work Bench) behind a door will prevent most enemies from getting in. The increased enemy spawn rate will result in more Wraiths spawning in Hardmode, which can be a nuisance; however, they can only move upward if they're inside a block, and hover or move downward otherwise.
A simple ditch around or below your base can take care of most ground level mobs, including Clowns. Even better, line the bottom of the ditch with lava and it will kill them for you. You will want to place a thin layer of lava in the ditch -- about a single Lava Bucket -- enough to damage enemies but not burn the coins and items they drop. As mentioned above, traps can make the arena even deadlier when used correctly. Keep in mind that Dripplers and similar, unrelated enemies (such as Demon Eyes) can hover and fly above your defenses.
If you do not want to build an arena (or are simply unprepared), you can also stay safe in your house while using weapons that attack through blocks (like the Vilethorn in pre-Hardmode or Crystal Vile Shard in Hardmode), or minions and sentries to attack incoming mobs.
Fished-up enemies may need more preparation, as they will often run away if unable to reach the player (outside of the Blood Eel and Dreadnautilus). In pre-Hardmode, fishing can be done in an enclosed area (to prevent other enemies from hitting you or the enemies from running away) and near a house with a door to run in and close once the enemy has been summoned. In Hardmode, an arena consisting of rows of platforms over the ocean can be helpful to provide room to manuever).


=== Gearing Up ===


==== Pre-Hardmode ====


===== Armor =====
Silver or Tungsten armor should be used at the bare minimum. Gold or Platinum armor provide more defense, but are harder to obtain.
If the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu have been defeated, Shadow or Crimson armor are both good options because they provide a mobility increase and increased regeneration, respectively.
Molten armor is a good option for Melee users, but it requires a visit to the Underworld after the evil biome boss has been defeated.
Rangers can use Fossil armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), although they need to stop by the Underground Desert for it.
Meteor armor and Jungle armor are useful for Mages.
A Mage can also use the Wizard set with Meteor Leggings or Jungle Pants.
Summoners can use the Flinx Fur Coat(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) if no bosses have been defeated.
If the player has defeated the Queen Bee, Bee armor(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) can also be used to increase minion slots.
Obsidian armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is another alternative that gives boosts to whip speed and range. However, it has the same requirements as Molten armor.


===== Weapons =====
For Melee users:

The Enchanted Sword is useful as it has high damage for its obtainment method and shoots a projectile. If it is unavailable, the Blade of Grass, Volcano or Light's Bane/Blood Butcherer can also be used.
The Hive-Five(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is useful for dealing damage while under cover. If it has not been obtained, the Code 1(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Amazon(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are good backups.
As enemies come in mass hordes, the Storm Spear(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or The Rotted Fork can be used to pierce multiple enemies.
The Ball O' Hurt or The Meatball can be used to disrupt enemy lines.
For Rangers:

The best bows available in the early game are the Demon Bow and the Tendon Bow, both of which should be used with Jester's Arrows. However, if Queen Bee has been defeated, The Bee's Knees(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is an excellent option that should be used with Wooden Arrows.
While all guns available at this point lack any pierce, the Minishark has a rapid rate of fire. The Boomstick and the Quad-Barrel Shotgun(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used against crowds from above due to their bullet spread.
Despite its ammunition being tedious to gather in large quantities, the Star Cannon is a strong weapon due to its high damage.
Consumable ranged weapons are still viable at this stage. The strongest piercing consumable weapons include Bone Throwing Knife(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Frost Daggerfish(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
For Mages:

The Ruby Staff and the Diamond Staff are the best gem staves available.
A strong alternative is the Thunder Zapper(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Vilethorn is useful for piercing damage. In Crimson worlds, the Crimson Rod can be used to deal chip damage to enemies from inside your base, although the cloud cannot pass through blocks.
The Space Gun has a rapid rate of fire. It also costs no mana when paired with full Meteor armor.
The Demon Scythe is dropped by Demons and Voodoo Demons, but a powerful option for crowd control.
For Summoners:

The Snapthorn(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a strong whip option that can inflict crowds with the Poisoned debuff. The Slime Whip(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Leather Whip(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are weaker options, but are safer to obtain.
Any minion can be used to attack from shelter, but some good options include the Finch Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Flinx Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Imp Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), although the Imp requires a dangerous trip to the Underworld.
Sentries are also useful for the purpose mentioned above. The Ballista Rod(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a powerful option, but the Lightning Aura Rod(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be used to inflict chip damage.
Keep in mind that you will need to defeat the Old One's Army event at least once to gain the ability to use the Tavernkeep sentries outside the event, however.


===== Accessories =====
Any extra jump bottle, such as the Cloud in a Bottle or the Sandstorm in a Bottle, is great for mobility. If you can, combine them with a Shiny Red Balloon, then further with a Lucky Horseshoe if fall damage is a problem.
Running boots, like the Hermes Boots or the Flurry Boots, are a great accessory to have, allowing you to more easily get away from crowds of enemies. Hooks are also useful for this purpose.
Once you have the Goblin Tinkerer, you can combine your running boots with Rocket Boots to make Spectre Boots, then further with an Anklet of the Wind and an Aglet to make Lightning Boots. You can also see this guide on how to further upgrade them into Terraspark Boots.
Unlike other running boots, the Sailfish Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be combined with the Frog Leg to create Amphibian Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a viable alternative to Terraspark Boots.
If you are playing on Expert Mode or higher difficulties, the Shield of Cthulhu(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can help with quick evasion and extra damage.
The Worm Scarf(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Brain of Confusion(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are also great survivability accessories.
Once you've gotten your hands on it, the Shark Tooth Necklace(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a good increase to DPS, especially on higher difficulties.
Feral Claws can be used by both Melee users and Summoners.
If a Mage does not mind the Mana Sickness(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) debuff, a Mana Flower will allow them to continuously use weapons for as long as they have mana-restoring potions.
In Corruption worlds, the Magic Cuffs are a good alternative otherwise.
Summoners should use the Pygmy Necklace as it provides a valuable extra minion slot. This requires defeating Queen Bee, however.


===== Potions =====
This applies to both pre-Hardmode and Hardmode.

Food items will grant the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Exquisitely Stuffed(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) buffs, which give helpful stat boosts.
Ironskin Potions, Endurance Potions and Regeneration Potions will help tremendously with survivability.
Swiftness Potions will aid in your dodging.
Ammo Reservation Potions and Archery Potions are good for Rangers.
Magic Power Potions and Mana Regeneration Potions are must have for Mages.
If you already have a minion, a Summoning Potion lets you bring an extra one to the fight.
Rage Potions or Wrath Potions are useful for almost all classes. The Rage Potion does not affect minions and sentries, however.


==== Hardmode ====


===== Armor =====
Most of the early Hardmode ore armor sets, with the corresponding head piece, are fairly effective for dealing with this event:
Palladium armor provides good regeneration, useful when retreating back to your base at low health.
Mythril armor is stronger than Adamantite armor for Melee users, despite having lower defense.
Orichalcum armor is a good option for crowd control.
Adamantite armor grants good offensive bonuses.
Titanium armor gives a similar amount of defense to Adamantite armor, with a more defensive set bonus in comparison.
If one does not mind hybrid sets, Warriors and Rangers should use the Frost Breastplate, Spider Greaves(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), and their corresponding Adamantite Head piece.
A mage can use a combination of the Adamantite Headgear, Mystic Robe(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), and Forbidden Treads(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to maximize magic DPS. However, this is very frail.
A summoner should use Spider armor(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) for extra minions. However, if one desires extra range and speed for whips, Obsidian Armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used.
If you have beaten Queen Slime, Crystal Assassin armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used by all classes and its set bonus will allow you to free up an accessory slot that would normally be taken by the Shield of Cthulhu at this point.
Once at least one mechanical boss has been defeated, Hallowed armor with the corresponding head piece can be used for its solid set bonus.


===== Weapons =====
For Melee users:

Despite being a pre-Hardmode weapon, the Night's Edge is still solid as it has high damage. The Ice Sickle can also be used.
Flint(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) has high pierce and damage and can attack through ceilings.
The Amarok(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Frostbrand are both useful due to the Frostbite(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) debuff.
If at least one mechanical boss has been defeated, the Gungnir and the Mushroom Spear are good piercing weapons.
The Flying Knife(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be controlled, allowing you to use it while inside shelter.
The Dao of Pow can be used to disrupt enemy lines and inflict the Confused debuff (although some enemies are immune).
The Shadowflame Knife(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) inflicts the Shadowflame(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) debuff and can ricochet up to two times.
For Rangers:

The Daedalus Stormbow(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (with Ichor or Holy Arrows), Marrow and Ice Bow are all good bows. Even the Hellwing Bow(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is still useful due to its infinite pierce.
The Adamantite Repeater and Titanium Repeater (with Jester's Arrows) can be used if one has not obtained them.
The Clockwork Assault Rifle (with Crystal Bullets or Cursed/Ichor Bullets), the Onyx Blaster(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (with Cursed/Ichor Bullets), the Phoenix Blaster, and the Uzi are all excellent choices. The Megashark is even better if you've beaten The Destroyer.
The Dart Rifle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Dart Pistol(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are great for debuffs. Use Ichor Darts(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for the Dreadnautilus and Hemogoblin Shark, and Cursed Darts(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Crystal Darts(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for crowds and the Blood Eel.
The Flamethrower excels at dealing with crowds if one has beaten Skeletron Prime.
The Toxikarp(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) has a rapid fire rate and inflicts the Poisoned debuff. It must be fished up in the Corruption, but is a good option if you want to get a new weapon as fast as possible.
The Star Cannon is still a solid option, but can be upgraded into the Super Star Shooter(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) after any mechanical boss has been defeated.
For Mages:

The Flower of Frost and Frost Staff can both inflict the Frostbite debuff. The Flower of Fire is a weaker version of the former.
The Life Drain(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is great against crowds.
For passive damage, the Nimbus Rod and Clinger Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used.
The Crystal Vile Shard(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is useful for attacking mobs from shelter.
The Golden Shower and Cursed Flames are good for debuffs.
The Killing Deck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can pierce through crowds if the cards are allowed to fly beyond them a bit before being recalled.
The Crystal Storm and Unholy Trident have a rapid fire rate, but the latter is dropped by deadly Red Devils.
The Sky Fracture(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) deals good damage against single targets, but does not pierce.
The Crystal Serpent(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is good against crowds.
The Spirit Flame(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is very strong against the Dreadnautilus.
For Summoners:

Few options are available for whips in early Hardmode, but the Cool Whip(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a solid choice. The Durendal(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be used after at least one mechanical boss has been defeated.
Alternatively, the Firecracker(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used with Abigail's Flower(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which gets a buff in Hardmode. Abigail will have a hard time catching up with the Blood Eel and Dreadnautilus during its spinning attack, however.
The Spider Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) is available early, and a decent improvement over the Pre-Hardmode options, especially with the spiders' ability to latch onto enemies and inflict the Acid Venom debuff. Putting walls behind your arena can make the spiders more mobile.
If Queen Slime has been defeated, the Blade Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a good option especially when paired with whips, and will ignore the defense of any Blood Squids that Dreadnautilus summons.
For sentries, the Queen Spider Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) and Barnacle Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are the easiest to obtain. If you are willing to take on the Tier 2 Old One's Army (or farmed Defender Medals beforehand), the tier 2 Tavernkeep sentries can also be used (like the Ballista Cane(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Lightning Aura Cane(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)).


===== Accessories =====
Wings are always useful to have in Hardmode.
The class-based Emblems dropped by the Wall of Flesh (Warrior, Ranger, Sorcerer, Summoner(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) will help with the higher defense of Hardmode enemies.
To avoid being knocked back by enemies during important fights, the Cobalt Shield (or its upgrades) is extremely useful.
Warriors and Summoners can combine their Feral Claws with a Titan Glove to create the Power Glove, which can then be upgraded into the Mechanical Glove for the former or the Berserker's Glove(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for the latter.
Warriors should also use the Yoyo Bag(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) if they plan on using yoyos.
A Ranger can use the Magic Quiver if they prefer bows over guns.
Mages can also use the Magnet Flower(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Mana Cloak(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Celestial Cuffs(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions).


== Blood Moon Fishing ==
Unprepared players may want to avoid fishing during a Blood Moon because of the exclusive enemies that can be fished up -- these are the Zombie Merman(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Wandering Eye Fish(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in pre-Hardmode, while the Hemogoblin Shark(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Blood Eel(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Dreadnautilus(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be hooked in Hardmode. It is strongly recommended to at least bring Sonar Potions if you plan on fishing at this time, as it will warn you with red text when you're about to hook up an enemy -- Although this detail also applies to the Surly Slime(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a harmless town pet that moves in shortly after being fished up. The extremely rare Advanced Combat Techniques(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a permanent booster, and Dread of the Red Sea(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a painting, are also available and are the only catches that are not highlighted with red text.
If you do wish to intentionally hook them up for their drops, you can also use the Chum Caster(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) dropped by the Zombie Merman and Wandering Eye Fish, as well as throw any Chum Buckets(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) that you get from fished up Blood Moon enemies into the water to further speed up the process.
Be sure to prepare a proper arena with an open space before fighting them for their drops, like mentioned in the General tips section. Keep your surroundings in mind as well, and get rid of any dangerous enemies or mobs that are starting to get too big whenever you see them, as they can easily make a important fight take a turn for the worse -- So for example, a Dreadnautilus fight can very quickly be ruined by a random Clown.


=== Specific Strategies ===


==== Indoor Pool ====
Rather than using an arena exposed to other enemies, a walled-off arena can be built with a sizable pool of water on the bottom. For enemies that cannot pierce through walls, the player can include a house with a door to hide in before attacking with weapons like the Crystal Vile Shard(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Flint(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) that can do damage through walls.
For enemies that can pierce through walls, specifically the Blood Eel and Dreadnautilus, several rows of platforms for dodging can be helpful. The Chillet(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) mount can be used to dash through enemies and attacks. 
Be careful not to make an arena so large that Blood Moon enemies spawn inside. Using player-made walls can prevent spawns and give the Spider Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) something to attach to.

title: Town
content:
A town is a player-created mini-biome which is created when three or more NPCs are in close proximity (including the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets, but excluding the Skeleton Merchant). Towns have the greatest effect on reducing the spawn of enemies, though the enemy spawn reduction effect is weaker in the Underworld, and will not have effect when some events are occurring. See effect of friendly town NPCs on spawn rates for details.
The Shadow Candle, when placed and activated or when held, prevents the creation of a town mini-biome, even if enough NPCs are present. 


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
Only NPCs that are within a 240×135-tile rectangle centered on the player are considered inhabitants of the town.
Despite a town having to include at least 3 NPCs, pylons only require two NPCs (including the Old Man and town pets, but excluding the Skeleton Merchant and the Traveling Merchant) to function.

title: Eater's Bone
content:
The Eater's Bone is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Eater that follows the player. The Baby Eater will not teleport to the player when it is far away, unlike most other pets. The Eater's Bone has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Eater of Worlds.


== Trivia ==
This item was not available between the versions  1.2.0.3 and  1.2.1 due to a bug where the Eater of Worlds dropped a Blend-O-Matic in its place.

title: Water Candle
content:
The Water Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light, and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants the Water Candle debuff to the player.
The Water Candle debuff increases all enemy and critter spawn rates by 33%, and increases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50%. The debuff is applied to any players holding or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Water Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Multiple candles will not stack with each other, even if one is placed and the other held.
Several Water Candles are found commonly on the shelves of the Dungeon. They can also be crafted at a Crystal Ball.
Placed Water Candles can be shut off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them, and will toggle when activated via wiring. Water Candles that are turned off will not activate the Water Candle debuff.
The Water Candle's effect is the opposite of the Peace Candle, which decreases enemy spawn rates. If a Peace Candle and a Water Candle are active at the same time, neither have any effect on spawn rates. Conversely, the Water Candle's effect stacks with that of the Battle Potion.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Water Candle can be placed or held underwater. It will give off light underwater if placed or held. It will increase enemy spawn rates underwater, whether placed or held.
Water Candles cannot be used to increase the spawn rates and max spawns of certain events such as the Goblin Army, Frost Legion, Pirate Invasion, Martian Madness, Pumpkin Moon, Frost Moon, Lunar Events, and Old One's Army, although the increase still applies to the Blood Moon and Solar Eclipse.
Placing or holding a Water Candle in Space causes its effects to be much more prominent, increasing the effective spawn rate from +33% to +167%. This is the only situation in which the Peace Candle does not fully cancel out the Water Candle, but rather reduces its effect to a spawn rate increase of +100%, although the 50% increase to maximum amount of simultaneous on-screen enemies will still get canceled out.
In addition to its general spawn rate increasing effect, the Water Candle also specifically increases spawn chance of a few enemies. It multiplies spawn chance of Unicorns and Wyverns by 1.9×, and multiplies spawn chance of Martian Probes by 4.16× before defeating Martian Madness or by 5.71× after defeating the event, making it even more potent when it comes to farming these enemies.


== Tips ==
It may help to collect (or turn off) all Water Candles found in the Dungeon, as doing so will lower enemy spawn rates in the area.
If the player enjoys fishing, it can often be useful to place Water Candles around their town, as it increases the spawn rate of bait critters like Fireflies and Worms. The NPC presence still prevents the spawn of hostile enemies.
Water Candles can be useful for farming enemies for rare items, since the increased spawn rate provides more enemies from which to acquire drops.
To collect a few Water Candles in the early game, the player can enter the Dungeon before defeating Skeletron, and look for Water Candles in the early part of the Dungeon before the Dungeon Guardian kills the player. One can also use beds to set their spawn point near the Dungeon for quick retries if they fail to pick up the Water Candle.

title: Slasher's Mysterious Skull
content:
Slasher's Mysterious Skull is a transformation mount item that transforms the user into a Velociraptor. While in this form, wings can be used, which differs from other mounts. It will show a Pterosaur carrying the Velociraptor (the player) when flying. However, the player cannot dash while using the mount. The player can still swing weapons, drink potions, and use Hooks and items as normal, with unique visual animations for each action. The player's hurt sound is also replaced with a growl.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
It has a top speed of 38 mph when running or when flying horizontally, 46 mph when flying vertically, and 60 mph when flying diagonally.
It does not benefit from movement speed boosts.
As long as any wings are equipped, the player in Velociraptor form can always fly at maximum speed and can fly horizontally, regardless of whether the wings themselves have the ability to do either.
Its base jump height is 7.5 tiles high.
It reduces fall damage by 90%.
The mount is 3 tiles tall and 2 tiles wide, like the player, allowing it to pass through doorways normally.
When used, it plays a low growl sound and emits a white puff of smoke.
Some items will not be shown when held by the Velociraptor, such as the Sergeant United Shield.
Some items put in the helmet vanity slot or social accessory slot still display on the Velociraptor's head, including all headgear that does not hide the player's hair.
Some may only have a part of the helmet vanity shown (e.g. Heroicis' Hat only shows the hat).
Some may not display at all.

The nest from the Finch Staff also persists on top of the Velociraptor's head.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Due to these buffs and the relative ease in acquiring it, the skull can be an effective early game battle mount.
Since this mount allows any pair of equipped wings to fly at the mount's maximum speed, it is very effectively combined with the pre-Hardmode Fledgling Wings, making them surpass the speed of early Hardmode wings (which also benefit from this mount).
However, the Skull seems to not benefit from the increased flight time of the Rocket Boots (or their upgrades), or any bonuses to jump speed. With enough supporting accessories, Fledgling Wings grant comparable mobility with or without this mount.


== Trivia ==
Slasher's Mysterious Skull is one of only two mount-summoning items that are crafted, the other being the Drill Containment Unit.
The mount more closely resembles velociraptors in Jurassic Park than modern reconstructions of velociraptors.
The tooltip references the 1975 British comedy film Monty Python and the Holy Grail with the phrase "with nasty, big, pointy teeth!" referring to Tim the Enchanter’s depiction of the Rabbit of Caerbannog.
The mount's use of a pterosaur to fly is very similar to the one used by the Amber Mosquito pet.

title: Cosmic Car Key
content:
The Cosmic Car Key is a Hardmode, post-Golem mount-summoning item. When used, it summons a rideable UFO Mount that allows the player to fly and hover indefinitely. The Cosmic Car Key has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event.


== Notes ==
The UFO mount does not work in liquids. When attempting to fly through them, the player will automatically be dismounted.
The mount has a top speed of 41 mph when flying up/down or east/west. When flying diagonally, however, it can reach 58 mph max.
Because of this, one can fly at the same speed as, if not faster, than the Dungeon Guardian (41 mph consistently).
When ascending the UFO, it can travel upwards through a one block gap while also moving east or west.
The UFO cannot fly downwards through "bottom" platforms (that is, hammered to the lower half of the block), and will instead bounce off them. Other platforms can be passed downward with only a slight delay.
Falling from maximum speed and mounting the UFO allows it to fly at 51 mph.
Similarly, it is possible to fall from a height at max speed and then mount the UFO and fly diagonally. This reaches a speed of 66 mph.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
When using this mount, it may be useful to replace other mobility accessories such as any wings or boots with damage or defense-based accessories.
Wings with hovering abilities in tandem with Lightning/Frostspark/Terraspark Boots can provide more speed and mobility than the UFO mount at the cost of infinite flight (unless Soaring Insignia is equipped).
Using wings with a fast ascent speed such as Jetpack, it is possible to fly upwards with the wings, deploy the mount and maintain the speed of the wings beyond the duration of the wings.
Using the Rod of Discord can be a great way to travel while using this mount, as it allows the player to teleport through tight areas rather than dismounting the UFO.
It is possible to give this mount to another player while mounted and still keep using the UFO.
The mobility of this mount and the ability to use items while riding it make it a good mount for construction.
If one needs to have an infinite flight mount underwater, the Cute Fishron Mount or the Witch's Broom are good replacements for the UFO.
This mount may not be the best to use in an arena for intense boss fights (such as the Empress of Light and Moon Lord), as its infinite flight time is overshadowed by its rather slow speed, lack of dashing ability, and slow turning speed. It may be preferable to use the Cute Fishron with Honey and Water bubbles (which has a very fast speed along with boosting damage by 15% when in and shortly after leaving liquids) or to not use mounts at all and instead have the Soaring Insignia, the Expert Mode-exclusive drop from the Empress of Light, which provides infinite flight time.


== Trivia ==
The buff tooltip is a reference to the film Independence Day, in which a Macintosh computer is used against an alien spaceship.
The name of the item might be a reference to a line in a rant about the insanity of everyday life by Eric T. Duckman from season 3, episode 6 "A Room with a Bellevue" from the American adult animated sitcom Duckman. The line goes, "...knowing when it's time to flash the cosmic car key at those Pearly Gates, I won't be in the coffin anyway...".


== History ==

Increased drop rate.
Worms and teleporting enemies will no longer spawn if the player stays still in the UFO for 5 or more seconds.

Fixed 'allow mounting' check not taking player's velocity into account (mounting into ceiling exploit)
Fixed issue where Shroomite armor and Psycho Knife stealth would work on mounts.

title: Lifeforce Potion
content:
The  Lifeforce Potion is a buff potion that grants the Lifeforce buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's health capacity by up to 20% (see below for details). This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
Maximum health granted by the Lifeforce buff will not be counted by health conditions of certain game mechanics (e.g. the spawning of Nurse, Eye of Cthulhu, and Goblin Army, etc.). The player have to increase their permanent maximum health (with permanent boosters) to fulfill these conditions.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Lifeforce Potions can sometimes be found in Shadow Chests and in Gold Chests that spawn within 250 blocks of the bottom of the world, making it possible to obtain them in pre-Hardmode.
If the player has used a total of 15 Life Crystals and 20 Life Fruits to upgrade their health capacity to the 500 point maximum, the Lifeforce Potion will temporarily boost the player's health capacity by +100, to a total of 600, the highest amount of health one can legitimately reach.
The Lifeforce Potion does not always increase the player's maximum health by exactly 20%. Instead, it grants +20 HP for every 100 HP of the player's maximum health. For example, a player with 425 maximum health will be granted 505 maximum health rather than 510.

As the player's natural health regeneration rate is related to the maximum health, it will also slightly increase the player's regeneration rate.


== Tips ==
The Prismite can only be acquired by fishing in The Hallow. Though it can be caught at any depth, the player will have a greater chance to catch the Prismite if they fish on the surface, because only two special fish can be caught within the surface Hallow (the Prismite and the Princess Fish).
Using the Lifeforce Potion can greatly increase a player's chances of winning any major boss battle, especially in Expert Mode and Master Mode, since the player needs all the buffs and health they can get.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Stack limit increased from 30 to 9999.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Duration increased from 5 to 8 minutes.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Sprite updated.
Desktop 1.2.4: Introduced.

title: Stylist
content:
The Stylist is an NPC vendor who can change the player's hairstyle and hair color. She also sells a variety of Hair Dyes, which apply dynamic effects to the player's hair. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
Rescuing her as the Webbed Stylist, who can be encountered randomly in Spider Nests in the Cavern layer. Interacting with her in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free her. If the Webbed Stylist is killed, she will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Stylist NPC is killed, she will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.
Selecting the “Hair Style” option in the Stylist's dialog opens a window where the player can choose a new hairstyle and color. The changes are immediately visible on the character for preview. Permanently applying the changes incurs a fee: switching to a different hairstyle costs 10 Gold; changing hair color costs 2 Gold. Hairstyle and color can be changed repeatedly and at any time.
Like with all other vendors, the Stylist's prices can vary depending on her happiness; this also affects her prices for hairstyle and color changes, as follows: The combined cost of changing hairstyle and color is multiplied by her happiness-based price multiplier, and then rounded to the nearest multiple of 1 Gold. Thus, the cost of changing hairstyles can be 8–15 Gold Coin, changing hair colors can cost 2–3 Gold Coin, and changing both hairstyle and hair color at once can range from 10 Gold to 18 Gold.
The Stylist will defend herself against nearby enemies with her Stylish Scissors. She deals 10 / 15 / 17 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Stylist also has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping the Stylish Scissors upon death.
The Webbed Stylist is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Stylist will transform into her Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. She can be returned to her classic look by submerging her in Shimmer again or spraying her with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==

Infested Spider Walls can be used to create an artificial Spider Nest, which will allow the Webbed Stylist to spawn. Regular Spider Walls cannot be used, as they are considered safe walls and therefore do not qualify.
Unlike other spawns in a Spider Nest, the Webbed Stylist has the following spawning requirements:
She requires an unsafe Spider Wall to be behind (not above) an eligible spawning block.
She cannot spawn on blocks covered by water that is more than 1 tile deep.
She can only spawn in the Cavern layer, with the exception of the following special and secret world seeds:
In worlds with The Constant enabled, she spawns in any layer above The Underworld.
In worlds with Dual Dungeons enabled and The Constant disabled, she spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers.
In worlds with Remix enabled and The Constant and Dual Dungeons disabled, she spawns in the Underground layer.


== Tips ==
Using a Battle Potion and/or Water Candle and running in and out of the Spider Nest will give the Webbed Stylist a better chance of spawning.
As with all similar NPCs, she spawns the same as enemies – positioning oneself with a Spider Nest just off-screen and then checking it once in a while for the spawn is an easy way to find her.
A Webbed Stylist can be damaged and killed by spiders (Wall Creeper in pre-Hardmode and Black Recluse in Hardmode). Finding her is therefore made simpler by looking for red damage numbers.
Due to how difficult it can be to deal with Black Recluses in early Hardmode, it is recommended to find the Stylist in pre-Hardmode.
Once obtained, the Stylist is one of the easiest NPCs to make happy. By placing her in the Ocean, a relatively safe biome to build in once reached; alongside the Dye Trader, an easily-obtainable NPC; items can be sold to her for 126% of their usual value.


== Names ==
The Stylist may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
The Stylist was created as a result of an official NPC design contest, being a heavily modified version of the Salonist. The original poster, TerrariaOnline poster bwdy (aka avarisc, Ripsand), is credited and thanked in the 1.2.3 changelog, as well as poster Omnir for contributing several of the hairstyles.
Spider Nests were introduced in 1.2. When the Stylist was introduced only months later, in 1.2.3, it was impossible to obtain her in worlds created prior to 1.2, as they do not feature any Spider Nests. Until the ability for players to create an artificial Spider Nest was introduced in 1.4.4 (via Infested Spider Walls), third-party tools were the only option to encounter the Stylist in pre-1.2 worlds.
Her line “Don't go exploring with scissors, they said. You won't get trapped in a spider's web, they said!” is a case of the Laundry Room Viking meme.
Despite her saying this, she will attack enemies with her Stylish Scissors as soon as she is freed.
The phrase "X they said, it would be Y they said" derives from the 1959 French comic book series Asterix. One of the catchphrases is translated into English as "Join up, they said! It's a man's life, they said!".
The Stylist, alongside the Princess, is depicted in the painting Princess Style.
In one of her quotes, she refers to the Dye Trader as the "Dye Master".
Despite saying “Tea? Coffee? Or is it just orange juice again?”, she does not sell tea nor coffee. Also, orange juice does not exist in any version of the game.
The Stylist seems to be attracted to the Dye Trader, according to her happiness quote “<name of Dye Trader> is quite the looker... so exotic... I think I'm in love...”. However, he has no similar quote so the feeling does not appear to be mutual.
Her quote “I'm staying inside! The Einstein look is NOT in fashion.” is a reference to the fact that the physicist Albert Einstein is often portrayed as having electrified hair. This is further evidenced since the quote only happens during storms.
As evidenced by her quote “Am I hearing spiders? Oh, just noisy neighbors, I don't like that.” the Stylist is implied to have some lingering trauma from being trapped in the Spider Nest. Despite this, she does not dislike living in the Underground biome.

In the game files, the Stylist has separate "gore" images for her head and hair.

Judging by the happiness quote about the Goblin Tinkerer, the Stylist hates goblins for their lack of hair, but not bald people such as the Painter and the Demolitionist, and even the Cyborg.
 The Bestiary entry for the Stylist: "The Stylist loves style, gossip, and hair. Aside from performing a miracle makeover, she sells some hair product as well."

title: Striking Moment
content:
Striking Moment is a buff granted for 5 seconds when an enemy attack is specially blocked; an enemy attack can be blocked in this way right before damage is taken by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate while holding a Brand of the Inferno or Sergeant United Shield, with a shield accessory equipped. If a Sergeant United Shield is not being thrown, the equipped shield accessory is unnecessary. Striking an enemy with a melee weapon when the buff is active deals 500% (five times) the usual damage, after which the buff will be removed. This bonus can be used with any melee weapon.


== Notes ==
For melee weapons that can deal a "melee hit" (see List of items that deal melee hits for the full list), if any entities are hit by the item itself during the use animation, the damage bonus will be applied to all of them. If the item can also create projectiles on hit (this includes the Muramasa and Volcano), the projectiles created also inherit the damage bonus.
For melee weapons that deal damage via a projectile, only the first entity hit by the projectile receives the damage bonus. This also includes attacking with melee weapons that perform both a "melee hit" and fire a projectile, but when no entity is hit by the weapon itself during its animation.
The following projectiles will not be affected by this buff, to prevent lingering projectiles triggering the bonus repeatedly.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.2.1: Fixed tooltip incorrectly stating 500% increased damage, now correctly states 400% increased damage (500% total).
Desktop 1.4.0.1: No longer quintuples the damage of The Horseman's Blade's projectiles and other projectiles that spawn on hit.
Desktop 1.3.4.1: Changed tooltip; used to incorrectly state 300% increased damage, now incorrectly states 500%.

Console 1.17: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.3.4.1.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.3.4.1 to Desktop 1.4.0.1.

title: Frost Moon
content:
The Frost Moon is a Hardmode, post-Plantera, Christmas-themed event summoned with the Naughty Present any time at night, ending at dawn (4:30 AM). It can be summoned any time of year and does not require the actual Christmas season. During the event, unique and highly difficult enemies spawn at high rates and attack the player. It is similar to the Pumpkin Moon event, but is more difficult. Visually, the moon turns into a snowman, though remaining in its current phase.
The entire event consists of 20 waves. Waves progress as the player reaches certain kill scores. After a wave's required score is met, the next wave begins, and the kill score is reset to 0. Status messages will indicate when the wave has advanced, and which wave has been achieved. See the table below for the points awarded for each enemy and the score required for each wave. Expert Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) worlds will gain a 2× point multiplier and Master Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) worlds will gain a 2.5× multiplier. When the event is over, the total score will be displayed by a status message: “The Frost Moon has passed! (Score: <total score>)”
The Frost Moon event always ends at 4:30 AM. The goal of the event is to progress through all 20 waves before the event ends, although the achievement for the event is awarded at wave 15.
The Naughty Present, which summons the Frost Moon, requires materials only available in Hardmode worlds where the player has already defeated Plantera (although it can still be summoned in pre-Hardmode worlds). As such, it is intended to present a challenge even to players with mid-to-late Hardmode equipment. In the final waves, multiple boss-level enemies are fought at once.
Frost Moon enemies drop powerful weapons and accessories, as well as pet and vanity items. Most drop with extreme rarity, and even players who manage to complete the event will find they need to do so several times before obtaining them. Drop chances for items dropped by bosses increase as waves are completed. In the final wave, the Everscream, Santa-NK1, and Ice Queen are all guaranteed to drop their respective trophies.
Reaching the 15th wave before 4:30 AM will display the status message “The spirit of Christmas spreads cheer...” at dawn (4:30 AM). For the entire day and night, all special effects of the Christmas season will occur. At 4:30 AM of the next day, the status message “The spirit of Christmas fades...” will appear and all Christmas effects will no longer occur until the Christmas season begins again or the player reaches the 15th wave of the Frost Moon again.


== Contents ==


== Waves ==

Total points required to reach wave 15: 3410, wave 20: 10160
Present Mimics may spawn at any wave, instead of wave-appropriate enemies, if there are currently less than four Present Mimics around.
The maximum number of bosses at once depends on the wave. While this number is reached (or possibly exceeded, for example if the player manages to somehow reach wave 9 without killing two Everscreams from wave 6), no more of this type of boss will spawn.


=== Loot ===
All of the boss-type enemies (Ice Queen, Santa-NK1 and Everscream) have increased chances to drop loot in later waves. This chance starts at 11.11% (20%) in wave 4 (when these enemies first spawn) and grows at a nonlinear rate up to 33.33% by wave 19 (100% by wave 14). The formula is as follows (with [math]\displaystyle{ w }[/math] being the wave number in question):

This chance is affected by the luck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) of the player closest to the enemy upon its death.

Trophies have their own, separate chance to drop (which also applies alongside the general drop chance explained above). Starting at wave 15, there is a chance each Ice Queen, Santa-NK1 and Everscream killed will drop its respective trophy. This chance increases at wave 17 and again at wave 19, as shown below. Luck does not affect this chance.

The table below displays the drop rates of all items affected by the loot drop factor explained above.


== Notes ==

The Frost Moon event will sometimes end after leaving and then reentering the world.
Water Candles, Peace Candle, Battle Potions and Calming Potions have no effect during the invasion, as the same with some other events.
If the player is killed during the event, the event is not canceled. The player will keep re-spawning and can continue fighting its enemies as the event continues until dawn. In single-player games, exiting the world and reloading it will cancel the event, but it will also delete the items from the ground.
The Frost Moon does not stack with the Blood Moon. Summoning the Frost Moon while a Blood Moon is active will result in a regular Frost Moon.
Summoning a Pirate Invasion during a Frost Moon will cancel it.
Any boss enemies that are still on a player's screen by the time dawn breaks will begin to move rapidly in a single direction, rushing off-screen to despawn. It is still possible to pursue or even kill some bosses while this is occurring.
Lingering enemies beaten after the event is over will never drop any rare items.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Because spawn rates for areas where Frost Moon enemies cannot spawn are also increased, a Frost Moon can be used to farm for other items, e.g., Pirate Maps at the Ocean, while completely avoiding the Frost Moon enemies.
The Frost Moon enemies are susceptible to the Ichor debuff, which makes a Flask of Ichor, Ichor Arrows or Bullets, or the Golden Shower very effective.
Players should kill the enemies as soon as they spawn to ensure that more enemies can spawn continuously in order to increase the chances of reaching later waves.
The Frost Moon can be a great way to obtain a large amount of coins quickly.
A good potion to use is the Warmth Potion as it decreases damage significantly from enemies in the event.
Players focused on obtaining summoning weapons and gear can skip the Frost Moon altogether. Instead, the enemies of the Pumpkin Moon drop several summoning-related items, as well as mobility items of equal strength compared to those from the Frost Moon.


== History ==

Frost Moon's "Expert drop bonus" modifier has been reduced slightly, with the base drop rates being increased by the same amount, and the end result being that Classic Mode drops are slightly more generous, while Expert drop rates stay the same.
Frost Moon now receives a 2.5× point multiplier when playing in Master mode. Previously, it received a 2× multiplier in Expert, but no additional gain in Master.
Frost Moon will now display the total score when the event is over.

title: Paladin's Shield
content:
The Paladin's Shield is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shield that has a 1/10 (10%) / 19/100 (19%) chance of being dropped by Paladins in the Hardmode Dungeon. While equipped, it grants the following effects:

+6 defense
Immunity to knockback
While the wearer's health is above 25%, it grants all nearby players on their team (excluding themselves) the Paladin's Shield buff, which provides 25% damage reduction and redirects that damage to the wearer.


== Crafting ==


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
The range of the Paladin's Shield is 50 tiles. Players that are more than 50 tiles away, even if they are on the same team, are not affected.
If two or more players on the same party equip the Paladin's Shield, only the one closest to the damaged party member will take the split damage. If multiple other players with Paladin's Shield are equally far away from the damaged player, the player who joined the server later will take the split damage.
Players with the Paladin's Shield equipped will not take split damage from other party members also using the Paladin's Shield, but will still reduce the damage the party member takes as if the damage was being split. Wearers will only take split damage if the party member does not have a Paladin's Shield equipped. This means that if all party members are wearing the Paladin's Shield and are within 50 tiles from each other, they will gain a 25% damage reduction at no cost.
Damage taken will first be reduced by the damaged player's defense and damage reduction effects, then be split by the Paladin's Shield. The damaged player takes 75% of this reduced damage, and the wearer of the Paladin's Shield takes 25% of this reduced damage.
Damage given to the wearer of the Paladin's Shield will be reduced again by the wearer's defense and damage reduction effects.
The wearer will always take at least 1 damage from a teammate being hit.
The teammate can receive 0 damage if said teammate takes 1 damage from an attack, and the damage gets split.
Receiving shared damage will cause the wearer to react as if they had been hit. This means that:
The wearer's invincibility frames will trigger, which is affected by the Cross Necklace.
Accessories that trigger when damaged, such as the Star Cloak and Honey Comb, will activate. Dodging effects (e.g. Black Belt, Brain of Confusion(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) can also activate.
Despite not activating the Turtle armor's set bonus, shared damage will use the (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Hallowed armor's Holy Protection buff / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Titanium armor's Shadow Dodge buff, and will affect the damage reduction of the Beetle Shell's Beetle Endurance buff.
Even though the Paladin's Shield only absorbs damage when the wearer is above 25% health, any split damage exceeding 25% of the wearer's health will kill them if the wearer is at 27% health, for example.
When the player is killed by the Paladin's Shield's damage redirection, a unique death message ("<Name of player> died for the team.") will be displayed.
In Expert Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Paladin has a chance of 49/11250 (0.44%) to drop two Paladin's Shields at a time, and a chance of 7/1125 (0.62%) to drop both a Paladin's Shield and a Paladin's Hammer. Note that both of these chances are already included in the 19/100 (19%) stated at the top.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The Paladin's Shield can synergize with the Brand of the Inferno(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to block attacks, granting the Striking Moment buff.
The chance of obtaining a Paladin's Shield after killing n Paladins can be calculated with the following formula:
Classic Mode: [math]\displaystyle{ 100\%\times\left(1-(1-0.0933)^n\right) }[/math]
Expert Mode: [math]\displaystyle{ 100\%\times\left(1-(1-0.1356)^n\right) }[/math]
See this plot for Classic Mode and this plot for Expert Mode.


== Trivia ==
The icon of the buff that is received from the Paladin's Shield portrays the old sprite of the item.
The function of the Paladin's Shield may be a reference to the Cover ability of Cecil Harvey from Final Fantasy IV, which allows him to absorb damage dealt to a party member in a similar fashion.


== History ==

Self damage can no longer be dodged.
Self damage now inflicts an individual type of invincibility frames.
Will now only proc every 0.67 seconds.
Getting killed by the Paladin's Shield now displays a unique death message.

title: Stardust armor
content:
Stardust armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord armor set consisting of the Stardust Helmet, Stardust Plate, and Stardust Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Stardust Fragments.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

+38 defense
+66% summon damage
+5 minion slots
+1 sentry slot
+30% whip range
Summons a Stardust Guardian minion that floats behind the player. It is passive until an enemy is within a 30-tile radius from the player. It will then quickly charge through blocks towards the enemy, striking rapidly with punches that each deal 50 base summon damage. The Stardust Guardian will return behind the player once no enemies are within range.
The Stardust Guardian is affected by summon damage bonuses, including those from whips.


== Set ==


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Stardust Guardian's base damage is 30. The 66% summon damage bonus from the full set increases it to 50.
The Stardust Guardian applies 5 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hit.
The Stardust Guardian can be dyed via the pet slot in the player's equipment menu.
Like all armors made from Luminite, equipping Stardust armor makes the player give off light, in this case white. Unlike other Luminite sets, equipping just one piece of the set gives off the full amount of light.
Light given out from the armor does not stack with Shine Potion, and the brightness is exactly the same as Shine Potion.


== Tips ==
Using Stardust armor, accessories, and buffs, it is possible to have 11 minion slots.
When compared to Valhalla Knight armor, Stardust armor grants a difference of +6% summon damage, +5 minion slots, +30% whip range, and the Stardust Guardian, whereas Valhalla Knight armor grants a difference of +30 defense, +2 sentry slots, +20% movement speed, +4 HP/second health regeneration, and buffs to melee weapons and Ballista sentry summons.
Valhalla Knight armor boasts significantly more survivability than Stardust armor, at the cost of offensive attributes.
Depending on the situation it may be worth replacing solely the Stardust Plate with the Valhalla Knight's Breastplate. This results in +8 defense, +8% summon damage, and +4 HP/second health regeneration, at the cost of +2 minion slots, +15% whip range, and the Stardust Guardian.
As the Guardian can move through blocks, the player is able to wall themselves in and depend on the Stardust Guardian for defense or to farm enemies while inactive.


== Trivia ==

Stardust armor has the lowest defense of the four Luminite armors.
The Stardust Helmet is the only piece of non-Tavernkeep armor that increases sentry slots.
The Stardust Guardian was originally created as a reference to Algalon the Observer from the massively multiplayer online role-playing game World of Warcraft. However, due to the community's enthusiasm in comparing the Stardust Guardian to Star Platinum from Stardust Crusaders, the third story arc of the Japanese manga series JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, lead programmer Yoraiz0r has acknowledged the resemblance and said the armor can be a reference. The similarities have become more apparent with the rework of the Star Guardian's attack style in 1.4.0.1: Its flurry of punches resembles Star Platinum's primary method of attack, "Ora Ora Rush".


== Gallery ==

		
		


== See also ==

Vortex armor
Nebula armor


== History ==

Tooltips of summon-related items now say "summon damage" instead of "minion damage".
Stardust Helmet now gives +1 sentry slot.
Stardust Chestplate and Leggings now give +15% whip range each.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Reworked the Stardust Guardian's functionality, now automatically attacks enemies within range with a barrage of punches. Previously, it was passive until activated by double-tapping the ▼ Down key, which placed it on the nearest block beneath the cursor position. Once placed, the Guardian became a sentry-style minion that could chase enemies for very short distances before returning to its original position. It periodically triggered explosions that dealt 20 damage and caused enemies in the blast radius to target the Guardian instead of the player. It was deactivated by holding the ▼ Down key, which caused it to return to following the player passively.
Increased sell value from no value to 31 Gold 50 Silver.

title: Town Dog
content:
The Dog is a town pet. It arrives at dawn (4:30 AM) the day after the player uses the Dog License, which is purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. The Dog does not count towards the NPCs' "crowded" limit and hence will not affect NPC happiness, although it does count as a regular town NPC for the purpose of the Pylon network. There are six breeds of Dog, with one randomly being chosen when it arrives. Only one Dog can be present at a time.
Just like any other town NPC, the Dog requires a valid house and can be manually assigned to one via its NPC flag. The Dog can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). It may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for its home tile (standing point).
The Dog can be talked to with the ⚷ Open / Activate button, like any other town NPC. It offers a “Pet” option, which places the player directly in front of the Dog when selected, and displays an animation of them petting the Dog, an effect that is purely visual. It only works if there are at least two flat tiles on the same level as the Dog in front of it. Using any item, taking damage, or closing the dialogue window terminates the animation.
Like with the Angler, the status message displayed when the Dog is killed is “<Name of Dog> has left!”. It will respawn within the next days, and may respawn as a different breed. Furthermore, using a Dog License while a Dog is already present causes the Dog to disappear and be "exchanged", releasing a puff of smoke and rerolling its breed and name immediately.


== Notes ==
Status messages about usage of the Dog License:
First use: “The license teleports away to the dog delivery service...”
Subsequent uses when the Town Dog does not exist: “Wait for your pet to move in before exchanging it!”
Subsequent uses when the Town Dog exists: “Pet Exchange: Successful!”


== Achievements ==


== Names ==
The Town Dog may have any of the following names:


=== Corgi ===


=== Labrador ===


=== Beagle ===


=== Dalmatian ===


=== Pit Bull ===


=== Husky ===


== Quotes ==
“Woof!”
“Bark!”
“Woof woof!”


== Trivia ==
The Bestiary page for the Town Dog depicts the Labrador dog breed by default.
Many names are references:

"Lucky" is a reference to Sigma's pet dog of the same name in real life.
"Marshall" is a reference to the character from PAW Patrol, and a reference to the widespread use of dalmatians by fire departments in the United States.
"Balto" is a reference to the real-life sled dog Balto, who played a large part in saving countless children in Nome, Alaska from diphtheria in 1925.
"Indiana" is a reference to the Indiana Jones franchise as "Indiana" was of Indiana Jones's childhood dog, an Alaskan Malamute (similar to the husky breed).
"Hachiko" is a reference to the real-life Akita Hachikō, remembered for his remarkable loyalty to his master. Both Huskies and Akitas belong to the Spitz type.
"Sparky" is in remembrance of Redigit's deceased pet dog, Sparky.
The name was originally going to be for the "Husky" breed instead of the "Labrador" when town pets were revealed.
"Sven" is a reference to popular YouTuber "PewDiePie", as he named his wolf in Minecraft "Sven".
"Navi" and "Zelda" are references to characters from The Legend of Zelda franchise and also the names of Redigit & Cenx's current dogs.
"Shino" is a reference to Terraria YouTuber and beta tester "Khaios", as his Shiba's name is Shino.
"Kona" is also a reference to Khaios, he had to leave this dog with his parents when he moved to Japan.
"Odie" is a reference to the dog of the same name in the famous comic strip and TV series Garfield.
"Pebbles" was added in remembrance to Reddit user GoldKat1234's Labrador.
"Spike" is a reference to Tom and Jerry, which features a bulldog named Spike.
 The Bestiary entry for the Town Dog: "A loyal companion to many. Excitable and always ready for action."

title: Princess
content:
The Princess is a Hardmode, post-Plantera NPC vendor who sells royal-themed vanity items and furniture, and is typically the final town NPC that the player encounters. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.Verify
All other town NPCs (not including Santa Claus or town pets) are present, meaning that she can only move in after defeating Plantera (as the Cyborg, the second-to-last NPC unlocked by game progression, can only spawn after defeating her).
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Princess is killed, she will automatically respawn after some time.
The Princess will attack nearby enemies with the Resonance Scepter, for which she has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping upon death if the current world is in Hardmode.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
The Princess is unique in that she does not have any biome or neighbor preferences. She loves up to three NPCs that live nearby and is liked by all NPCs around her.
She also hates being lonely and her unhappiness is maxed to 150% if she is not surrounded by at least two other NPCs within 25 tiles, or two other NPCs that are between 25 and 120 tiles away.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Princess will transform into her Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. She can be returned to her classic look by submerging her in Shimmer again or spraying her with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
The Princess is one of the starting NPCs in Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds, always named Yorai.


== Names ==
The Princess may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
Five of the Princess's names are Japanese, each of which have different meanings:
Ai translates to "love" (愛).
Hikari translates to "light" (光).
Hime translates to "princess" (姫).
Momo translates to "peach" (桃). Based on the translation, the name "Princess Momo" means "Princess Peach".
Yuuki translates to "courage" or "bravery" (勇気).
Some of the Princess's names are references to characters from popular culture:
Alice from the 1865 novel Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
Ariel from the 1989 American animated musical fantasy movie The Little Mermaid.
Belle from the 1991 American animated musical romantic fantasy movie Beauty and the Beast.
Charlotte from the Japanese seinen manga series Berserk.
Emilia from the 2014 Japanese light novel series Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World.
(Cure) Flora from the 2015 Japanese magical girl anime series Go! Princess PreCure.
Peach (Momo; see above) and Rosetta (the Japanese name of Rosalina) from the Japanese media franchise Mario.
Rosetta could also reference the 2008 American computer animated movie Tinker Bell.
Sofia from the 2013 American animated children's television series Sofia the First.
The Princess has the chance to share the name Faye with the Dryad.
One of the Princess' possible names is Yorai, named after Yoraiz0r, one of the lead developers of Terraria.
She is depicted in the paintings Painting of a Lass and Princess Style.
The Princess is a child, similar to the Angler. She has a shorter sprite compared to most other NPCs' sprites.
While most NPCs die via the usual death animation, the Princess simply vanishes in a puff of smoke. She also has a unique death message: Instead of “<Name of Princess> was slain...”, the message reads “<Name of Princess> has left!”. This is likely due to rating concerns, as depictions of children being killed tend to result in an "Adults Only" rating from the ESRB, which might have limited the game's distribution.
“Like my dress? Gee, thanks! Just sewed it.” is a reference to a similar lyric from the song “7 Rings” by Ariana Grande.
The Princess has a happiness quote for herself: “<Name of Princess> is a little unsettling to be around, but terribly cute!”. This quote cannot be legitimately seen in-game, since it requires two copies of the same NPC to be alive at once.
Her quote calling the Truffle a "fun guy" plays on the homophone for fungi.
The quote, “The stars at night remind me of glitter on a beautiful, black dress. I shall soon have one made!” could be a reference to her Shimmered form which was added after she was introduced.
Along with the Traveling Merchant, Zoologist, Steampunker, and Cyborg, she is among a small group of NPCs who sell a new item post-Moon Lord. The Princess's item is a Music Box (which requires the player to defeat the Moon Lord during Hardmode).
The Princess is the only NPC who likes and is liked by all other NPCs.
 The Bestiary entry for the Princess: "Shy and innocent, this happy young lady sees the positive in everything, and everybody. She appreciates all of her subjects, from all walks of life."

title: The Tongue
content:
The Tongue is a debuff inflicted by the Wall of Flesh when the player has the Horrified debuff and one of the following happens:

The player gets behind the Wall of Flesh.
The player attempts to leave the Underworld.
When afflicted with this debuff, the Wall of Flesh draws in the player with a tendril at a base speed of 56 mph, ignoring blocks in the way. In Expert Mode, the debuff also causes the player to lose 50 health per second (5 damage displayed every 0.1 seconds). If the euclidean distance between the player and Wall of Flesh is more than 187.5 tiles when the debuff is inflicted, the player will die instantly instead of being drawn to the Wall of Flesh.

=== From enemy ===

title: Mushroom Staff
content:
The Mushroom Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Mushroom Boi minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, dealing contact damage. If the nearest target is too far away, the Mushroom Boi will dive towards it, creating a red explosion on impact that deals 133% of the weapon's damage (10 base damage) and 300% of its knockback (base knockback of 6 (Average)), and then teleport back to the player.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Mushroom Boi inflicts 18 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hit, meaning it can hit for up to 3.33 times per second.
The Mushroom Boi can target enemies within a 50-tile distance.
The dive happens whenever any of following conditions are fulfilled:
The Mushroom Boi is trying to reach an enemy that is more than 10 tiles above it.
The Mushroom Boi is trying to return towards the player due to being too far away. It can enter this returning mode if its vertical distance from the player is more than 18.75 tiles or if its total distance is more than 31.25 tiles, and only when it does not have a valid target. If the Mushroom Boi reaches the player while they are airborne, it will continue to stay in the returning mode until the player lands.
The dive has a cooldown of 2.25 seconds after the impact.


== Tips ==
Unlike most pre-Hardmode minions which use static invincibility, the Mushroom Bois use local invincibility frames, meaning that their damage output will linearly scale with how many Mushroom Bois are summoned. As a result, Mushroom Bois remain efficient even when the player uses all or most of their minion slots on them.
Due to both how the Mushroom Bois AI operates and how linear damage scaling of the minions works, a whip with high tag damage like the Spinal Tap or Snapthorn is required to be used almost constantly for them to be useful.
Therefore, despite Bee armor providing an additional minion slot, Obsidian armor tends to be slightly better, if not even, with the Mushroom Staff, due to its buffs to whips.
Its linear scaling which incentivizes gear that provides more minion slots, combined with its strong need for whips, makes this minion not very effective if used by non-summoners.
If obtained, Cattiva can be substituted in place of a Mushroom Boi even when the player has dedicated all of their minion slots to the Mushroom Staff for max damage, as it provides higher DPS than a single Mushroom Boi. Cattiva also benefits from using the same high tag damage whips mentioned above.
If using this minion to fight the Wall of Flesh, the player should build a hellbridge rather than using a Water Walking Potion, as Mushroom Bois handle platforms well.
The Shark Tooth Necklace is highly effective at boosting the Mushroom Staff's low base damage.


== Trivia ==
This item is part of a crossover with the game Dead Cells.
There are two unused sounds in the game files related with the Mushroom Boi: "Deadcells mushroom jump" and "Deadcells mushroom land"
Its tooltip is a reference to get fixed boi, the code that activates the Zenith special seed.

title: Regal Delicacy
content:
The Regal Delicacy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Slime Princess that follows the player. The pet resembles a miniature Queen Slime with blush, small dotted eyes, and a tiny mouth. The Regal Delicacy has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime in Master Mode.


== Crafting ==


=== Used in ===


== Trivia ==
The pet is the female counterpart of the Slime Prince, spawned with the Royal Delight.
The buff tooltip, "She is the higher authority", is connected to the Slime Prince buff's tooltip, "He answers to a higher authority".
When the player is far enough away, the Slime Princess will fly to the player with her wings, similar to Queen Slime.
Following community suggestions, developers toyed with the idea that the Royal Delight and Regal Delicacy could be crafted together into one pet-summoning item. However, this was not implemented until 1.4.4.
