title: Legacy:Guide:King Slime strategies
content:
King Slime is an optional Pre-Hardmode boss. Due to its low stats and predictable attacks, it is considered the easiest boss in the game by most players.


== Spawn Condition ==
King Slime has a 1 in 300 chance of spawning in place of another slime if the following conditions are met:

The player is located in the two outer third of the map (the far left or far right).
Depth is above zero. It may spawn slightly underground, though, as the average ground level is higher than that.
There must be standard, green grass. Forest is not enough as for standard slimes.
Goblin Scouts spawn in the same locations as the King Slime, so you'll know if you're in the right place if you encounter any. A Water Candle and/or the Battle Potion can speed up the process of encountering it.
It is important to note that contrary to other biome requirement, in this case grass must be precisely on the surface where he spawns, and not somewhere random on screen. In this case, grass does not determine biome (as purity is the absence of other biomes, and not a biome in itself), but spawn types. So, simply putting grass on screen to create an artificial biome does not work. Grass must be slightly off screen, as it is where enemies spawn , and not enclosed in a room with player placed walls. See NPC spawning for more info.
He can also be summoned using Slime Crown.
As with almost all bosses, it despawns if every player involved are dead.


== The Fight ==
King Slime is very similar to a normal Slime: it moves by hopping to the player and attempts to make contact, which deals damage. The pattern of his jumps is predictable and repeatedly: two normal, one small, and one high. King Slime can be eternally stuck in small to medium-sized enclosures if it spawns there. Aside from this, it's mostly the same.
King Slime becomes smaller and faster the lower his health is, which makes him harder to hit. He will also summon Blue Slimes as he gets damaged to harass the player. These can draw the player's attention towards the Blue Slimes and waste ammo and time on them instead of King Slime, so the use of piercing weapons or ammo is important.


== General Strategies ==


=== Terrain Preparation ===
Due to the fact this boss cannot pass through blocks, there are some arena options:

A pit or a wall with height of 20 blocks. The highest jump height of King Slime is 17 blocks, and therefore the boss cannot pass through something higher than that.
The player can add traps to this pit, which would make the fight even easier or.
A flat area with small room below it with Platforms as roof for the player. The king slime cannot enter small rooms and thus cannot touch the players in this room.
Arena made up of platforms and Ropes for both horizontal and vertical movement.
It is also recommended to close any caves near the summoning spot, since the boss might spawn inside and get stuck.

Or just make a small 2*4 pit cover the top with wooden platforms and shoot upwards.
The player can also climb up a rope and attack from above.


=== Gearing Up ===


==== Armor ====
Armor is not very important in this fight; however, some suggestions are below. 

For all classes, Silver Armor or Tungsten Armor can increase survivability significantly in Expert or Master Mode. Platinum Armor is even better but is made from a rarer ore.
Pumpkin Armor is also cheap and more powerful than Cactus armor due to its set bonus. It's especially easy to obtain during Halloween, but can also be obtained by throwing cactus in the shimmer.
Wizard set or Jungle armor is best for Mages.


==== Weapons ====
Most weapons can be used to fight this boss without difficulties, except for weak, close-ranged melee weapons like the Umbrella. Piercing weapons may be preferred, to hit both the Blue Slimes and the King Slime himself.

For Melee users

The Thorn Chakram is a good option to keep the boss at range, but can struggle against the hordes of slimes.
The Rotted Fork has high. It requires you to destroy multiple Crimson Hearts.
The Chain Knife can give the player plenty of range.
Projectile swords such as the Enchanted Sword and Starfury can help the player avoid King Slime's heavy contact damage.
The Ice Blade is a weaker option that is easier to obtain.
For Ranged users

A cheap and powerful option is a Bow, such as the Gold, Platinum, or even the Tendon/Demon Bow
Frostburn Arrows or Jester's Arrows are the preferred ammo types, due to the high single target damage of the former and the piercing effect of the latter.
The Snowball Cannon is another strong ranged weapon.
All guns are very effective against King Slime, although they are harder to obtain than the other ranged weapons.
The Musket or The Undertaker are the easiest to obtain out of all guns, only requiring a single Shadow Orb/Crimson Heart.
The prefered ammo type is Musket Balls, as Silver Bullets are too expensive and/or tedious to amass in the early game.
For Magic users

Gem staves are the most common magic weapons in this part of the game. The Emerald staff and all stronger staves do well against King Slime.
The Crimson Rod can be helpful in this fight, found in the Crimson, respectively. The Vilethorn is not as strong but is similarly available in the Corruption.
For throwers
Grenades, Shuriken or Throwing Knives can be effective.


==== Accessories ====
Like weapons, most accessories can help, but accessories obtained in chests are usually enough to defeat King Slime. It is unlikely that players will have access to the Tinkerer's Workshop at this stage of the game, so combined accessories are not listed below.

Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots or the Panic Necklace can assist with horizontal mobility.
The Flying Carpet is also a very good accessory since its ability to hover can make the King Slime unable to reach the player.
Any double jump accessories such as the Cloud in a Bottle greatly increases vertical mobility.
A Band of Regeneration boosts health regeneration, increasing survivability.
Feral Claws are great for warriors and summoners, but requires exploring the underground jungle.


==== Potions ====
Ironskin Potions and Regeneration Potions greatly increase survivability.
Any food that grants the Well Fed or better should be used.
Swiftness Potions increase mobility.
Ale provides useful melee buffs
Archery Potions increase the effectiveness of bows.
Mana Regeneration Potions are very important for mages, as it allows for very quick mana regeneration.
Magic Power Potions make magic weapons more potent.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Lava Pit Strategy ===
Because King Slime can be harmed by Lava, a good strategy is to use a Lava Bucket to make a long strip of land with a small amount of lava (shallow enough so items don't burn) and then make some widely placed platforms. The player can jump, use Rocket Boots, or employ a Grappling Hook to move between platforms. Just be careful to not jump in the lava if you don't plan to use Obsidian Skin Potions. This strategy works with his teleports, and the minions will all die from falling in the lava. The player doesn't have to focus on fighting, because the lava will dish out major damage. The player can also skip the platforms and use a Obsidian Skin Potion, and just evade by running under King Slime, or use Rocket Boots to fly over.


=== Ocean strategy ===
King Slime is very slow in liquids. If the player can find a way to move quickly in water, they can easily outmaneuver this boss. The best options for moving in the water are the Flipper  or the Trident.


=== Death Box Strategy ===
Upon the player's death, the King Slime will attempt to travel off-screen in order to despawn. However, the King Slime cannot travel through solid blocks, so he can easily be trapped in a small area until death.

A solid box must be constructed. The box should be large enough to hold the King Slime, yet not so large that he can still wander off-screen.
A bed should be placed within the box. In order to make the bed usable, it may be easiest to build a small cubicle within the box to hold the bed.
Before the King Slime spawns, the player should be inside the box with his spawn set on the bed. Once the King Slime awakens, he will teleport within the box to attack the player. The player should deal any damage he can to the King Slime at this time. The King Slime should inevitably kill the player and attempt to hop off screen. However, he will find himself trapped in the box and will not be able to leave. The player will respawn at the bed and is free to deal any additional damage to the King Slime before his next death. Repeat this process until the King Slime is defeated.
Weapons and traps that can deal damage to the King Slime during a player's death will greatly speed up the battle, such as the Crimson Rod, Dart Traps, or a thin layer of lava.
Since this strategy revolves around the player's death, Hardcore players should avoid implementing this strategy.

title: Config.json settings
content:
Config.json is a file created by Terraria that primarily stores settings that were chosen via Terraria's settings menu.
Config.json resides in one of the following locations by default:

Windows: %USERPROFILE%\Documents\My Games\Terraria
Mac: ~/Library/Application support/Terraria
Linux: $HOME/.local/share/Terraria
Android: /sdcard/Android/data/com.and.games505.TerrariaPaid or /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/com.and.games505.TerrariaPaid
iOS: Browse > On My (device) > Terraria


== Hidden settings ==

In addition to storing the in-game menu settings, config.json allows players to set certain game options that have not yet been added to the menu. In order to set these options, quit Terraria completely, open the config.json file, edit the desired settings, then save the config.json file and start Terraria.


=== Gameplay ===


=== Visuals ===


=== Other ===


== Notes ==
One may want to backup the config.json file if they are launching different versions of the game on a single device, as the file is shared among Terraria instances and the settings inside may get overridden.

title: Stardust Cell Staff
content:
The Stardust Cell Staff is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist summon weapon that summons a Stardust Cell minion. It hovers near enemies, firing a homing mini-cell that attaches itself to the target, inflicting the Celled debuff to deal 20 damage per second (20 damage displayed every 1 second). A maximum of 10 mini-cells can be attached to one target at a time, for a total of 200 damage per second (200 damage displayed every 1 second). The Stardust Cell will teleport to enemies out of range.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Stardust Cell Shots are fired at a rate of once every 0.6 seconds on average.
In addition to their normal fire rate, Stardust Cells have a 50% chance to fire an extra shot at an enemy that is currently being hit by the player. The extra shot deals 33.33% damage (20 base damage), and once it is fired there is an average cooldown of 0.75 seconds before it can be fired again.
This extra shot cannot be triggered by other Stardust Cell Shots, by secondary slash projectiles created by the Super Star Shooter or Muramasa, or by projectiles created by the set bonuses of Chlorophyte armor, Titanium armor, or Orichalcum armor.
The Stardust Cells can target enemies up to 125 tiles away from the player.
This detection range is boosted to 187.5 tiles for enemies that are targeted by the player.
The Stardust Cells will attempt to return to the player's side if their distance from the player is 84.4 tiles or more, which can interrupt their attacks.
The Stardust Cells can teleport to targets that are between 28.75 tiles to 53.75 tiles away.
After teleporting to an enemy, a Stardust Cell will also instantly fire a mini-cell.
The Stardust Cells need to be within 31.25 tiles of their target to fire shots.
The Stardust Cell Shots cannot be reflected.
Any number of Stardust Cells can damage a target at a time; they have no invincibility frames between each other's hits.
Stardust Cell Shots can continue homing in on their target for 5 seconds before disappearing, making them very unlikely to miss.
The Stardust Cell Shots have a top speed of 72 mph when chasing a target.
Damage ticking from mini-cells retains its original pace regardless of when additional mini-cells were added.
Even though the Celled debuff is inflicted for 15 seconds, it does not deal any damage if no mini-cells are attached to the enemy, and the mini-cell projectiles only have a total lifespan of 5 seconds.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Tips ==
The Stardust Cell Staff can be considered to be an indirect upgrade to the Xeno Staff. Unlike the Xeno Staff's UFOs, however, the Stardust Cells do not re-target instantly after an enemy has been defeated. This increased targeting speed can bring the Xeno Staff on par with the Stardust Cell Staff under certain circumstances, such as against larger groups of enemies.
Because Stardust Cells possess excellent homing and teleportation abilities, they perform exceptionally well and consistently against most bosses, such as fighting the Empress of Light during daytime.
However, the Stardust Cell Staff's performance against the Moon Lord is rather inconsistent. When his eyes are closed, the homing Stardust Cell Shot currently in pursuit will immediately dissipate, causing some damage to be lost.
Stardust Cells have a solid synergy with Stardust Dragon Staff and Constellation, because they easily trigger the extra shot.


== Trivia ==
The Celled debuff's tooltip, "being eaten by cells", is the only tooltip that does not begin with an uppercase letter.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Damage display from Celled changed from 10 damage displayed per 0.5 seconds to 20 damage displayed per second for every stack of mini-cell.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: Removed mana cost (cost 10 mana previously).

title: Truffle Worm
content:
The Truffle Worm is a rare Hardmode critter and boss-summoning item that spawns in the underground Glowing Mushroom biome. It summons Duke Fishron when used as bait. It can only be used in the Ocean, at any time. It emits a small amount of light.
The Truffle Worm can be caught with a Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net and Golden Bug Net, however, it is more difficult to catch than other critters, as it burrows away when a player comes too close. It must be approached quickly in order to successfully catch it. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Truffle Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Truffle Worm cannot be released again unless decrafted via Shimmer.


== Crafting ==


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Truffle Worms do not take damage from enemies.
Despite having a bait power of 666%, the Truffle Worm cannot be used for ordinary fishing, and can only be used to summon Duke Fishron by fishing in the Ocean. When attempting to use it as bait elsewhere, the bobber will simply sit in the water indefinitely.
The Truffle Worm will always be consumed upon summoning Duke Fishron. Items that reduce the chance of bait consumption such as the Tackle Box or its upgrades will have no effect.
When a Truffle Worm is the first bait to be used, the Fisherman's Pocket Guide and its upgrades simply display "Warning!" instead of listing Fishing Power.
100 tiles of Mushroom blocks are not necessary for Truffle Worms to spawn. Mushroom enemies and Truffle Worms will spawn wherever there is Mushroom grass, without requiring that the area is actually considered a Glowing Mushroom biome.
On Mushroom grass, each enemy spawn has a 2/3 chance of being a mushroom-themed enemy or critter. Each time this happens, there is a 1/5 (20%) chance that the mushroom-themed character is a Truffle Worm. Considering the maximum spawn rate (1/60 per tick), the approximately of maximum expected Truffle Worm spawns is 480 per hour.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==


=== Spawning ===
Unlike other critters, NPCs cannot be used to increase the spawn rate of Truffle Worm.
Each existing enemy may reduce the spawn rate of the next. Getting rid of excess enemies will give the Truffle Worm more opportunities to spawn.
Water Candles and/or Battle Potions will increase its spawn rate.
One way to increase the chances of finding Truffle Worms is to convert a large section of the Underground Jungle into an Underground Glowing Mushroom biome, using the Clentaminator with Dark Blue Solution. A slower alternative would be to use Mushroom Grass Seeds on plain Mud Blocks.
A simple (but perhaps slow) way to farm them is to move away from and back to a Glowing Mushroom biome repeatedly, causing new enemies to spawn and potentially a Truffle Worm.
Teleporters (with hoiks) or the Portal Gun can be used to make an infinite falling loop. If it is high enough, going in can cause other enemies to despawn, allowing the Truffle Worm to have more chances to spawn.


=== Catching ===
Truffle Worms will burrow themselves (eventually despawning) if the player is near them for about 1 second, so the use of a speed-enhancing item is suggested. Hooks, wings, or Lightning Boots grant speed improvements; Tabi, Master Ninja Gear, a full set of Crystal Assassin armor, or Shield of Cthulhu (though this item deals damage and thus may be less suitable) allow dashing.
If a Truffle Worm is let free by a player, it will also burrow, and despawn almost immediately if approached or stood near for more than a few seconds.
It should be noted that, if the Truffle Worm burrows offscreen, it will despawn as soon as it is offscreen. If it falls, however, like a normal enemy and the same way a Worm would, it will follow normal NPC despawning rules, and can be followed for more distance.
Dashing and using a Bug Net with autoswing makes it trivial to opportunistically catch Truffle Worms when exploring the Mushroom biome in early hardmode unless enemies are in the way.
The Truffle Worm can be caught even while burrowing.  If the Truffle Worm is in a small pit where it is impossible or very difficult to catch from above, and there is a cave below it, a player can jump up directly under it and swing the Bug Net to catch it as it tries to burrow downward.
Summoned minions do not directly target the Truffle Worm but can inadvertently kill it; using the Guide to Critter Companionship can prevent this.
A Rod of Discord makes catching Truffle Worms easier, since it greatly facilitates getting near them.
A Golden Bug Net has a longer reach and swings faster than a regular Bug Net, making the catch easier.
Since the Lifeform Analyzer can announce the presence of a Truffle Worm, it is highly recommended to carry it.
Furthermore, since enemies despawn further than the Lifeform Analyzer's reach, one can estimate the location of the Truffle Worm and accelerate the process of hunting it.


== Trivia ==
The number 666 in the Truffle Worm's "666% bait power" is a reference to the number of the beast, commonly associated with Satan. This alludes to its ability to spawn Duke Fishron.
The combination of truffle and worm represented by the Truffle Worm ties in with the combined pig-and-fish-like nature of Duke Fishron.
Traditionally, pigs have been utilized for the extraction of edible truffles, a highly prized food.
This is also referenced by the Truffle's quote, "You haven't seen any pigs around here have you? My brother lost his leg to one.", as well as how the Pigron and Cute Fishron mounts' summoning items are both Truffles.
The Windy Balloon, Lunatic Devotee, Truffle Worm, and Prismatic Lacewing are the only entities classified as an "enemy" that otherwise deal absolutely no damage to the player.
 The Bestiary entry for the Truffle Worm: "An extremely rare, difficult to catch glowworm. A specific, powerful sea creature is insatiably attracted to these."


== See also ==
Prismatic Lacewings, another critter that is used for boss summoning.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4.8: Now grants the "Like a Boss" achievement.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Stack limit increased from 999 to 9999.
Spawn rates are now impacted by Luck.
Desktop 1.4.3.1: Truffle Worms no longer take damage from hostile NPCs or projectiles.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Now used to craft Truffle Worm Cages.
Desktop 1.3.0.3: Fixed Truffle Worm not spawning.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Truffle Worms can now be killed by enemies.
Desktop 1.2.4.1: Fixed a bug where trying to use multiple Truffle Worms while the line is pulled would make numerous Duke Fishrons appear. Fixed issues where the Truffle Worm would be consumed without summoning Duke Fishron.

title: Regeneration Potion
content:
The Regeneration Potion is a buff potion which grants the Regeneration buff when consumed. The buff provides health regeneration by restoring an additional 2 health per second, for a total of 960 health. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Regeneration Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Regeneration buff's effect is stackable with the Band of Regeneration. The buff is hypothetically equivalent to equipping 2 Bands of Regeneration.


== Tips ==
The Regeneration Potion is very useful when planning to fight for an extended period of time, such as when dealing with a Goblin Army, Pirate Invasion, or during boss fights. In addition to multiplying the healing potential of a Mushroom, it uses ingredients that are fairly common and easy to find, making it convenient to produce.

title: Ancient Horn
content:
The Ancient Horn is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Basilisk Mount that grants mounted players an extra jump and can charge through and damage enemies. The Ancient Horn has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Basilisks.
The Basilisk mount provides accelerated land speed at 41 mph and provides increased jump height (14 tiles/28 feet), though is still hindered by water as usual. While mounted on the Basilisk, the player is immune to knockback and only takes 20% fall damage.
If the Basilisk is moving at a speed of least 21 mph, running through enemies inflicts 90 base damage, not counting enemy defense. This damage is considered summon damage, meaning that minion-enhancing items will improve it. Enemies that are damaged by this attack do not inflict contact damage on the player, but the player will suffer contact damage from enemies that survive it, if the hitbox of the player gets hit.
The mount emits a faint red glow from 27' underground downwards. This light does not grow stronger as the player descends, and its color is unaffected by dyes.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Compared to the Unicorn Mount, the Basilisk is much slower, but has much more acceleration and lower height, making it more suitable for underground exploration. It can also be better for battle depending on the player's gear, as it trades the Unicorn's invulnerability for a lower charge delay and higher damage.
When used with the Neptune's Shell, the Basilisk Mount is capable of extreme mobility underwater, competing with that of the Turtle Mount and even Cute Fishron (in the air).
Using an Umbrella, Djinn's Curse, or Featherfall Potion with this mount will cause the player to glide through the air at significant speeds, allowing the player to move long distances quickly when jumping from a high ledge.
The Basilisk is capable of charging through the segments of The Destroyer (and the Eater of Worlds) with minimal damage to the player. When running along the Destroyer's body, the Basilisk can achieve very high DPS due to summon damage bypassing the Destroyer's high defense.
Both the Basilisk and Unicorn Mount's charge abilities operate the same way sprinting accessories do in terms of momentum. This means that mounting while sprinting, dashing with the Shield of Cthulhu or Tabi, or moving quickly through the use of a canceled grapple will immediately cause the Basilisk to begin charging, even if the distance covered would normally not be enough to trigger it.
Due to the Basilisk already not receiving knockback, the player can save an accessory slot on the Cobalt Shield (or its derivatives).
The Cloud in a Bottle and its upgrades, but not wings, work while on the Basilisk mount.

title: Marble Cave
content:
The Marble Cave is a mini-biome found in the Cavern layer. It is made entirely out of Marble Blocks and Marble Walls, and contains several Pots of a design unique to the area. It normally generates as a long, singular horizontal passage, but the shape can be affected by overlapping cave systems. Marble Caves can also be generated with appropriately themed Underground Cabins built with Smooth Marble Blocks, housing Marble Chests with ordinary underground treasure.
Marble Caves can prove to be one of the most dangerous areas in the game, even for endgame characters. While Hoplites are ranged enemies that deal respectable damage to pre-Hardmode characters, the Hardmode enemy Medusa inflicts the Stoned debuff, one of the most deadly debuffs in the entire game, capable of completely immobilizing the player from great distances, dealing significantly inflated fall damage, and leaving them vulnerable for several seconds if they survive. Even well-prepared characters should take caution when in the vicinity of a Marble Cave, as even being near one can cause these unique enemies to spawn in ordinary underground spaces.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
Since it is only a mini-biome, the usual NPC spawning rules do not apply to the Marble Cave. Instead, Hoplites and Medusa require one Marble Block on which they can spawn, inside the player's spawn range; or any Marble Block between 30 and 60 tiles away from the player. A single Marble Block is sufficient (although the chance increases with the number of Marble Blocks) and Marble Walls do not have any impact. However, if the player is standing on a Marble Block, the chance for Hoplites and Medusa to spawn gets a significant boost. In that case, no further Marble Blocks in the vicinity are required.
In worlds with the special world seed Drunk enabled, the generation structure of Marble Caves is swapped with Granite Caves.
In worlds with the special world seed The Constant enabled, Marble Caves can generate on the surface, though Hoplites and Medusa will not.


== Tips ==
If it generates at a low enough depth, the cave can be flooded with lava. This can be a double-edged sword; while the lava takes care of deadly enemies like Hoplites and Medusa, the lava itself is quite easy to fall into. Filling the spaces between the spiky formations with lava can be an effective defense, and if done right, can allow for the complete elimination of threats.


== Trivia ==
The pot designs, the look of the marble, and the enemies all are references to ancient Greece and ancient Rome.


== See also ==
Underground

title: Guide:Getting started with Hardmode
content:
Hardmode is the second half of the game, initiated in a world when the Wall of Flesh is defeated for the first time. New, more powerful enemies spawn with new loot, increasing the power level of both enemies and the player dramatically, and The Corruption/Crimson begin to spread and infect nearby blocks. Once started, Hardmode cannot be turned off through normal gameplay.
The beginning of Hardmode is very dangerous due to the new threats, and can easily catch newer players off guard. This guide focuses on helping new players recognize and deal with the threats posed in early Hardmode.


== Preparations ==

Once Hardmode starts, the more threatening enemies can make a lot of normal actions and travel more difficult. However, you can mitigate this by improving your gear and safety and mitigating risks. Use Pylons or other movement infrastructure to move to and from distant parts of the world quickly and safely. Especially notable is having a Cavern Pylon or Hellevator for rapid and efficient access to the cavern layer.
Make sure you have a good supply of herbs and potions, ideally by farming herbs. Several easy-to-get potions are massive advantages both for speed and safety, such as Spelunker Potions, Hunter Potions, Featherfall Potions, and Mining Potions. Being able to have these potions constantly active during early Hardmode makes early exploration much faster and safer.
Progressing smoothly at the start of Hardmode will require the Pwnhammer and the Molten Pickaxe; you will get the prior from killing the Wall of Flesh, but you should craft the latter in advance if possible. If you are not able to mine Hellstone for the pickaxe, then once Hardmode starts, you will be able to blow it up with Dynamite and collect it that way. Other early Hardmode gear will generally be whatever gear you kill the Wall of Flesh with, but the Emblem that the Wall of Flesh drops is a great addition for extra damage output. If the Night's Edge was crafted in pre-Hardmode, it serves as a reliable weapon for regular enemies, given its decent damage, knockback, and excellent coverage around the player. Other weapons that can function well in early Hardmode includes the Demon Scythe, which can deal damage comperable to several early Hardmode weapons, the Starcrash, making a servicavle substitute for the Firecracker if the Wall of Flesh didn’t drop the latter, and the Pheonix Blaster when paired with Hardmode ammo types. On Expert Mode and above, the Demon Heart that the Wall of Flesh drops also gives an extra accessory slot. The weapons dropped by the wall itself also can be used to get through the beginning of hardmode, the Clockwork Assault Rifles low bass damage is offset by its rapid three-shot bursts which only conusme a single bullet, the Laser Rifle is good at long range and also costs no mana with full Meteor armor, the Firecracker pairs well with minions that have high base damage, and while the Breaker Blade is outclassed as a main weapon by the aforementioned Night’s Edge, it’s high knockback can make it a decent way to fend off enemies that are chasing you.
When Hardmode begins, the evil biome of your world and then new Hallow biome will generate in large strips in your world, fanning out in a V. These strips are very important for early Hardmode progression, but the evil strip can corrupt housing and disrupt Pylons. If you want to prevent this risk in advance, you can plant a large number of Sunflowers near pylons, but this is easier to do after the start of Hardmode as most Pylons will be safe with no intervention.
These strips and the chasms in pre-Hardmode will spread their biomes to nearby blocks, quickly on the surface and slowly underground. Surrounding patches of evil biome with 2 Sunflowers at each end, or a 3 block wide vertical tunnel, will contain their spread.
In  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, evil biomes infecting the Jungle poses a threat as they would permanently convert Jungle mud into dirt, making it much harder to purify the Jungle and undo the damage once it is infected. Evil biome spread is also harder to contain in these versions in general, due to random stone blocks in the cavern layer having a chance of being infected when a Demon Altar/Crimson Altar is smashed.

If you have not found it yet, consider looking for the Aether. Shimmer becomes much more useful in Hardmode, allowing you to cycle the Emblem the Wall of Flesh drops and avoid reforge costs on some expensive new Hardmode gear by crafting and decrafting it repeatedly. You can look for the Aether in Hardmode, and it will be faster with faster mining speed, but more dangerous due to the enemies.


== The First Steps ==
Now Wall of Flesh is dead and the world is in Hardmode. Make sure to collect the items the Wall of Flesh drops - the Wall of Flesh will place a square of Demonite or Crimtane Bricks to prevent its items from falling into lava below, but if your inventory fills up before you collect all the drops, the other items may fall down into lava pools below. Make sure you get the Pwnhammer, and the weapons and Emblems the boss gives are also useful.
The first goal is to get better gear, and the biggest improvement is mining the new Hardmode ores. The new Pwnhammer you got will let you smash Altars, and this is how you spawn Hardmode ores. Each of the first three Altars you smash will generate a new type of ore - Cobalt or Palladium, Mythril or Orichalcum, then Adamantite or Titanium. After that, the cycle repeats and smashing more Altars generates more of these same ore types. The third altar of each cycle generates the most powerful ore, so smashing 9 or 12 Altars is a good benchmark to aim for, but there is no downside to smashing more.
The first Altar smashed will allow the mechanical bosses and Pirate Invasions to spawn naturally. An inopportune Pirate Invasion can be a major setback early on, but there are ways to mitigate this risk, such as digging a small pit. You can test to see if your pit is effective by trying to jump across it without any movement bonuses/jump height bonuses, and by pouring lava at the bottom of the pit, the pirates will automatically die and count towards the kill total. Natural mechanical boss spawns can be avoided by staying underground all night or exiting and reentering the game. It is possible to do early Hardmode progression without smashing any Altars, but it's not recommended.
If you feel that you need a better weapon before mining for Hardmode ores, the Arms Dealer sells Empty Bullets now, which along with Explosive Powder from the Demolitionist, can craft Exploding Bullets for crowd control. These are best used with a fast and consistent gun like the Phoenix Blaster, but the Shotgun is a new buyable alternative. For summoners, it may be worth it to farm Black Recluses in spider nests for Spider Fangs, as this is their major gear upgrade; however, other weapons crafted from Hardmode ores can make this process much easier.


=== Hardmode ore mining ===
You will need a Molten Pickaxe to mine the first tier of Hardmode ores, then need to use this ore to craft a stronger mining tool that can mine the next tier of Hardmode ore. Hardmode ores can be used to craft Pickaxes or Drills - Drills have faster base speeds, but less range and do not benefit from mining speed bonuses or speed-increasing modifiers. However, it is very easy for Pickaxes to outspeed Drills due to this - a Light or Quick Pickaxe will always outspeed its Drill counterpart when supported with a Mining Potion and food buff, in addition to having better range. Pickaxes are almost always the better option to craft.
Use Mining Potions and Spelunker Potions to quickly spot and mine to new ore deposits. If you see ore you cannot mine, make a note of it and look for other ore types you can mine. At this point, it is best to mine in pure caverns, as this area has the least dangerous enemies and is the easiest to mine through. Other biomes do not give enough extra value for the extra threat they pose at this point, and the Underground Jungle and Underground Desert especially are extremely lethal now.
Most enemies at this point are very dangerous relative to the rewards they give, but if you spot a chest out in the open, especially if it hangs off an edge, try shooting it from a safe distance. These may be Mimics, which offer a massive amount of gold and useful accessories when killed. They deal high damage, but cannot go through blocks or fall through platforms, and it is well worth killing these.
You need 45 Cobalt Ore or 54 Palladium Ore for the first Hardmode Pickaxe, and 100 Mythril Ore or 120 Orichalcum Ore to get a new Hardmode Anvil + new Pickaxe. Because these new Pickaxes let you mine the next tier of ore, once you have enough ore to make the next Pickaxe, consider teleporting home and crafting it immediately. The tier 3 ore Pickaxes do not let you mine any new blocks, and in general can be skipped; however, the Titanium Pickaxe with maximum mining speed buffs can reach the maximum mining speed in the game, so it can be worth crafting that. In this case, you need 110 Titanium Ore to craft a Titanium Forge and Pickaxe. Another option is to mine some Cobalt/Palladium, craft the Power Bombs, and just use them to blow up the more advanced ores. This method has higher efficiency than crafting pickaxes/drills, but is also more dangerous to use, especially at the lava layer.
How much ore you mine will depend on what gear you want to work with, but 300 or so Adamantite Ore or Titanium Ore is enough to get a full armor set and a good weapon. Pure summoners do not get much value out of Hardmode ore mining after getting a Hardmode Anvil, but getting a good ore weapon can help them in getting the gear they want; additionally, one may wish to craft a Titanium Mask/Adamantite Helmet if they intend to play tank summoner.


==== Fishing for Hardmode ores ====
Hardmode versions of Crates can give Hardmode ores as well, but this is very slow compared to mining for them. The main reasons to fish for Hardmode ores are if you want to avoid the risk of a natural Pirate Invasion or if you want a Titanium Pickaxe in a world that has Adamantite instead.
For fishing up Hardmode ores, fishing in the Hallow or Underground Hallow is the fastest by a wide margin. Divine Crates drop Hardmode ores twice as often as any other Biome Crate, Prismite are useful for Lifeforce Potions, and the Crystal Serpent is a strong early Hardmode weapon. Make sure to use Crate Potions and stack as much fishing power as you can.
Hellstone Crates from lava fishing does guarantee that all crates reeled in can have tier 3 Hardmode ores, but Hellstone Crates only have a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of generating on a given crate roll, making them actually more rare than other Biome Crates with good fishing power.


=== Gearing up ===
Hardmode ores and a new Hardmode Anvil allow for much stronger gear than in pre-Hardmode. Repeaters especially are very strong yet easily obtainable weapons, and Unholy Arrows can be bought from the Arms Dealer at any time now, with fantastic crowd control, consistency, and range. Swords and Spears lack in range, but are powerful get-off-me tools and strong options for melee players. Mages benefit from Hardmode ore armors, but need to get a new weapon from elsewhere, such as a Crystal Serpent. The new Wizard NPC also sells the Crystal Ball, which gives a free buff to magic weapons, and Greater Mana Potions, which are enough to fully sustain the mana costs of most magic weapons.
The alternate versions of Hardmode ores produce slightly stronger weapons, but cost more bars to craft. Titanium weapons are better than Adamantite weapons, but Adamantite armor is better than Titanium armor, giving better damage and defense while also being cheaper to craft. Titanium armor's set bonus is difficult and dangerous to use if you are not constantly taking hits. If your world has Titanium, you can shimmer Titanium Ore down into Adamantite Ore to craft that armor set. Lower tier ore armor is also usable, but generally weaker than Adamantite armor. 
Summoners want Spider armor and a Spider Staff and Queen Spider Staff, which requires killing Black Recluses in spider nests. You need 52 Spider Fangs(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) for the armor and minion, and an extra 24 for the sentry. Black Recluses deal huge damage, have projectile spit, and are heavily resistant to knockback, making them difficult to face at this point, but they cannot move through blocks while minions can be summoned on the other side of blocks, which makes this a bit easier.


== Souls and enemies to farm ==
With better weapons and armor, it is time to focus on getting new and powerful loot from all the new enemies. These are important for further weapon upgrades, a wide variety of accessories, and being able to manually summon the mechanical bosses, which are the next required bosses in progression.


=== Wings ===
Wings are the main staple of Hardmode movement, granting a high level of vertical mobility control and reach alongside immunity to fall damage. To craft any given pair of wings, you need 20 Souls of Flight and another item depending on the pair you want. To get Souls of Flight, go to space and kill Wyverns. Wyverns spawn far more frequently when you are near a Water Candle taken from the Dungeon. During the night, higher spawn rates mean more Wyvern spawns, but they can be hard to see, so you should consider a Hunter Potion in this case. They are fast flying worm enemies that circle away from you then rush towards you, with a limited turn radius. You can dodge them by running under them to abuse their turn radius, or fall away from them and shoot along their length using a Featherfall Potion to adjust fall speed. Piercing weapons like Unholy Arrows or an Aqua Scepter are excellent at killing Wyverns quickly. You will generally need to kill 3-4/2 Wyverns to get enough Souls for a pair of wings.
There are many options for the other crafting ingredient for a pair of Wings. The quickest options to obtain are Angel and Demon Wings, which require 10 Feathers and 15 Souls of Light or Night. However, Fairy Wings, Frozen Wings, and Harpy Wings are better, requiring 99 Pixie Dust, an Ice Feather, and Giant Harpy Feather respectively. Fairy Wings are the most reliable wings to farm for in most scenarios, as Pixie Dust is a common resource from a common enemy. However, if one chooses to farm Ice Golems for Frost Armor, an Ice Feather can be obtained while collecting Frost Cores. Additionally, the Giant Harpy Feather, albeit rare, can be obtained from Harpies in pre-Hardmode.
As you progress through Hardmode, new and stronger Wings become available, and each requires 20 Souls of Flight. Besides killing Wyverns, you can also decraft your old Wings via Shimmer to get back Souls of Flight that way. It is helpful to check for new wing options as you beat bosses.
Wings also get huge benefits from a Shiny Red Balloon, a Frog Leg, or their upgrades. It is well worth using one of these options alongside wings for a major mobility boost. Featherfall Potions also provide a huge boost to the vertical control that Wings offer, and are easy to craft with the Feathers gathered from killing Harpies while waiting for Wyverns or farming a Giant Harpy Feather.


=== Underground evil and Hallow ===
With the V generated at the start of Hardmode, there are now evil and Hallow biomes in the cavern layer. Enemies killed here have a chance of dropping a Soul of Night or Soul of Light respectively, and each biome has its own useful crafting material. Underground Corruption has Cursed Flames that drop from Clingers and World Feeders, Underground Crimson has Ichor that drops from Ichor Stickers, and the Underground Hallow has Crystal Shards that grow on the sides of Pearlstone and other Hallowed blocks and can be mined to collect them.
For mages, 20 of the unique crafting material, 15 of their respective Soul, and a Spell Tome from the Wizard can be used to craft spell book weapons, the Golden Shower, Cursed Flames, and Crystal Storm. On the ranged side of things, the new crafting materials can be used to craft new Arrows, Bullets, and Darts - Ichor Arrows and Crystal Bullets are especially useful, while all of the new dart types are useful. Flasks of Ichor are also very useful for players using minions, as Ichor provides a defense penetration buff that gives more damage the more hits the player can deal. Crystal Shards can also be used to craft Super Mana Potions(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), which restore so much mana that they minimize Mana Sickness durations even on the most expensive magic weapons.
These biomes can also spawn Biome Mimics, big, powerful, and aggressive Mimic variants that are almost immune to knockback and can pass through blocks to kill you. With their fast movement and random actions, it can be hard to deal with them without a lot of empty space; it may be best to leave them alone for now. However, if you can kill them, they offer fantastic weapons, accessories, and extra healing potions. You can also craft Keys of Night(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)/Light(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to spawn these Biome Mimics on the surface, where you have far more space to deal with them, so you should not feel obligated to kill them here.
Almost all Biome Mimic drops are useful, but the Flesh Knuckles(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is especially notable due to its value to tank builds, as the Mechanical bosses have many attacks that are hard to dodge but have relatively low damage. While only one evil spawns with a given world, the other evil's respective seeds can be bought from the Dryad in a Graveyard now. This is useful to have both Cursed Flame and Ichor in one world. In Expert Mode or above, having both Worm Scarf and Brain of Confusion equipped is also very beneficial against Hardmode Bosses. The Putrid Scent(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be shimmered into Flesh Knuckles and vice versa, so waiting for the other evil Biome Mimics to naturally spawn is not needed if you want both of these.
Mummy variants can spawn on infected variants of Sand Blocks on the surface. Dark and Blood Mummies(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can drop Dark Shards while Light Mummies can drop Light Shards. These items can also be gathered in infected versions of the Underground Desert, but are far easier, safer, and faster to farm on the surface. These Shards are used to craft the Onyx Blaster(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Dao of Pow, and Sky Fracture(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), along with their respective Soul type.


=== Events ===
There are a number of events, such as Sandstorms or the powered-up Goblin Army, that can give more powerful weapons and gear now.

While raining, Ice Golems can spawn in the Snow biome, which drop Frost Cores(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) for Frost armor, Cool Whip(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Blizzard in a Bottle and Ice Feathers for Frozen Wings. Angry Nimbuses can also drop the Nimbus Rod as a useful magic weapon.
Frost armor is most useful for ranged weapons, but can benefit melee weapons as well, especially if a Catalyst Band(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is equipped. Cool Whip is a strong new whip for summoners, especially for low-damage minions, most notably the Blade Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Ice Golem will fire lasers rapidly at you, and being frozen by these can easily lead to death. Try to block it in to prevent it from moving and whittle it down while avoiding its head.
Sandstorms now spawn Sand Elementals(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which drop Forbidden Fragments(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for Forbidden armor and the Spirit Flame(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), as well for crafting a Sandstorm in a Bottle.
Forbidden armor is useful as a magic-summon hybrid, but requires using weapon of both classes to stand out against single-classed sets. The Spirit Flame is a great magic weapon against upcoming bosses, while a Sandstorm in a Bottle is otherwise hard to get and using it to craft a Bundle of Balloons can allow for skipping Wings entirely.
Try to stay high off the ground, as Dune Splicers will tear you to shreds otherwise, and shoot down the elemental from a distance.
The Goblin Army now spawns Goblin Warlocks, which drop a useful weapon for every class besides summoner.
See Guide:Goblin Army strategies for more info on dealing with Goblin Warlocks.
A Pirate Invasion gives a huge amount of money, both from direct drops and sold furniture. Very rarely, it can also give the Coin Gun.
See Guide:Pirate Invasion strategies for more info on how to deal with this event.
Queen Slime can be summoned using a Gelatin Crystal(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and can drop the Blade Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as a powerful new minion or the Gelatinous Pillion(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as a mobile all-round mount with high fall speed.
See Guide:Queen Slime strategies for more info on how to deal with Queen Slime.
Blood Moons now spawn Clowns that can be killed for Bananarangs and new fishing enemies that can drop the Drippler Crippler(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Sanguine Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which are very strong options for their respective classes at this point.
However, fished Blood Moon enemies in Hardmode are very dangerous, especially when paired with all the other enemies around them. It is best to fish up these enemies near your spawn point to prevent them from despawning after you die, most notably the Dreadnautilus. See Guide:Blood Moon strategies for help on dealing with these enemies.


=== Other gear of note ===
Mimics are rare, but offer powerful defensive utility in Cross Necklace, Star Veil, and Philosopher's Stone, a good hook in Dual Hook, and the Titan Glove. These can all be crafted into powerful and useful accessories.
Wolves and Basilisks(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can drop the Lilith's Necklace(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Ancient Horn(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) respectively, which can replace Wings entirely when coupled with extra jumps and Featherfall Potion support.
Pixie Dust and Crystal Shards can be used to craft Greater Healing Potions, helping give more HP back in a pinch.


== Moving forward ==
The next bosses to defeat are the mechanical bosses, which allude to major pre-Hardmode bosses and are a major step up in stats and difficulty. You will need answers to their fast movement and high damage, and you need to deal enough damage to kill them in a single night, or they will despawn (or enrage in the case of Skeletron Prime).
These bosses can spawn randomly during the night if an Altar has been smashed, with an accompanying status message at the start of the night. They can also be spawned manually with their mechanical summon items, which require Iron/Lead Bars and Souls of Night/Light to craft, along with a material associated with the boss' pre-Hardmode counterpart: Lenses for the Twins, Rotten Chunks or Vertebrae for the Destroyer, and Bones for Skeletron Prime. You can buy and shimmer Iron Anvils from the Merchant to get more Iron Bars if need be, while a good enemy farm can make gathering the other materials for these summons much faster and easier.
If you are struggling with the mechanical bosses, consider seeing what Potions you could make use of for the fights, and how you could improve your mobility to avoid attacks. A good pair of Wings loves the extra speed of a Balloon and the extra vertical control of Featherfall or Gravitation Potions. Food buffs from Pumpkin Pies and the speed buff from Swiftness Potions can greatly assist in horizontal acceleration, and a shield that can prevent stray hits from ruining your movement with knockback. Ironskin and Regeneration Potions are massive survivability buffs that are easy to craft as well. Lifeforce and Endurance Potions are harder to craft, but still very good to have.
For more help with the Mechanical bosses, see Guide:The Destroyer strategies, Guide:The Twins strategies and Guide:Skeletron Prime strategies.

title: Jewel of Light
content:
The Jewel of Light is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a Fairy Princess that provides pink-colored light. It is fast and will always position itself slightly elevated behind the player. The Jewel of Light has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light in Master Mode. While equipped, not only does the pet produce light, but the player as well.


== Notes ==
Despite being exclusive to Master Mode, the Fairy Princess does not possess any unique abilities, such as the Wisp in a Bottle's manual repositioning or the Suspicious Looking Tentacle's treasure sensing. This, combined with the fact that it still has the same brightness as those items (120%) might render its usefulness rather limited.
However, one might prefer the fairy for its lighting color and static positioning behind the player's back.


== Trivia ==
The pet that is summoned is very similar to the Ice Queen summoned by the Frozen Crown and has the same flight patterns.

title: Magic Lantern
content:
The Magic Lantern is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a small glowing Magic Lantern which hovers above the player, emitting dim yellow light. The lantern will also highlight all treasures within a 17-tile radius from the lantern's location, overlaying small yellow sparkles over them. The Magic Lantern can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 10 Gold during the night of a full moon.
The lantern will always try to maintain a position just forward of and above the player, passing through blocks as needed. If the player is far enough away or in midair, the lantern will propel itself with a rocket exhaust in order to catch up to them. The lantern's position can block objects of interest at ceiling height, but if the player just turns around, the lantern will move to their other side.


== Notes ==
The Magic Lantern highlights the same tiles as the buff from the Spelunker Potion:


== Tips ==
The Magic Lantern can be farmed by creating a new world, getting to the Cavern layer, and looking for the Skeleton Merchant until the morning after the first night (the first night after creating a new world will always be a full moon), then creating a new world. This way the player can make sure that when they find the Skeleton Merchant he has the Magic Lantern.
Alternatively, a slower but very reliable method is to wait for the full moon when the player finds the Skeleton Merchant. This can be done by trapping him on screen (and sleeping in a bed to accelerate time) until a full moon occurs. This option is better pursued when the player has a Sextant or its upgrades.

title: Dark Mage
content:
The Dark Mage is a mini-boss that spawns during the Old One's Army event, during wave 5 in Tier 1, and waves 4 and 6 in Tier 3. 


== Behavior ==
The Dark Mage hovers slightly above the ground and randomly chooses between three attacks:

The Dark Mage summons an orb of Dark Energy and then hurls it directly at the player, dealing 80 / 160 / 240 damage.
The Dark Mage summons a large rune on the ground, which then generates a large area of light that heals most enemies within its 62.5-tile range, restoring up to 500 health. The rune cannot affect itself or other Dark Mages and only heals enemies who have more than 30 maximum health and deal at least 1 damage.
The Dark Mage begins chanting as a Dark Sigil appears above it, creating several clouds of purple particles on solid tiles within an approximately 30-tile range in its immediate vicinity. After a short moment, Old One's Skeletons will appear from these clouds, which can also damage the player as they are being summoned. This attack cannot be done if there are more than 200 NPCs in the world.


== Variants ==


== Notes ==
The Dark Mage will continue to respawn until Wave 5 reaches 99% in Tier 1. This allows it to be farmed by players with late pre-Hardmode and higher gear.
It is advised that players should keep an additional world they desire to grind Tier 1 raids, since defeating the mechanical bosses or the Golem will bring higher tier raids.
Like other members of the Old One's Army, the Dark Mage is immune to Teleporters and lava and will take half damage from traps.
The Dark Mage is restricted to hovering a bit above the ground. It cannot fly upwards, though the skeletons it summons can.
Two pet eggs, the Gato Egg and Dragon Egg drop from the Dark Mage; however, the Creeper Egg light pet drops from the Ogre.


== Trivia ==
The Dark Mage has an Expert Mode-exclusive Treasure Bag in the game files, but it is currently unobtainable, as it never actually drops it.
The pet drops from the Dark Mage in Tier 1 are one of the highest drop chances for any pet items from enemies, beaten out only by the Bone Key, a guaranteed drop from the Dungeon Guardian.
The War Table, War Table Banner, Dragon Egg, and Gato Egg are not affected by luck, unlike most uncommon loot drops. Thus, they will always drop at their listed drop rates.
The Dark Mage cannot heal itself, other Dark Mages, or the Moon Lord.
If a boss reaches its second phase and is then fully healed by the Dark Mage, the boss will still maintain its current phase (with the exceptions of Santa-NK1, Plantera, and Queen Slime, as this will cause them to revert into the first form after being fully healed).
Although Dark Mage is a mini-boss in Terraria, in Dungeon Defenders 2 they exist as standard enemies.
A mini-boss variant of Dark Mage does exist in Dungeon Defenders 2, but with the name “Malthius”.
 The Bestiary entry for the Dark Mage: "A small, levitating sorcerer from Etheria who wields dark magic and can even raise fresh minions for the Old One's Army."

title: Full Moon Squeaky Toy
content:
The Full Moon Squeaky Toy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Werewolf that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Werewolf flies after them by flapping its arms, mimicking a bird-like creature. The Full Moon Squeaky Toy can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Hardmode Blood Moon for 30 Gold. 


== Trivia ==
The Baby Werewolf pet may be an homage to the now-removed Werewolf pet from the  Old-gen console and 3DS versions of Terraria.
The Baby Werewolf appears to have a tail, unlike the Werewolf enemy it is based on.

title: Mana Regeneration Potion
content:
The Mana Regeneration Potion is a buff potion which grants the Mana Regeneration buff when consumed. The buff increases the rate at which the player's mana regenerates. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Mana Regeneration Potions can be found in Pots and Shadow Chests in The Underworld.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
This potion's buff grants the user the same speed of mana regeneration as a player who is standing completely still. This allows the user to be more mobile, and lowers any downtime for mana-consuming items.

title: Abigail's Flower
content:
Abigail's Flower is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Abigail minion. She floats towards enemies and inflicts continuous contact damage, as well as pausing to emit damaging flashes of light.
When Abigail's Flower is used more than once, multiple Abigails do not spawn; instead, the existing Abigail becomes stronger and faster for each additional summon. Abigail has a visual indicator for the number of times she is summoned, with the flower on her head changing shape and hue for each stage. In Hardmode, the boost from multiple summons is much greater.
Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. It spawns more frequently in The Constant and Zenith worlds.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Used by tools ==
Abigail's Flower can be used by the Rubblemaker to put themselves back in a placed state:


== Notes ==

Abigail's damage starts at 6 and will increase each time she is summoned thereafter. It will increase by 3–4 damage (55% of the weapon's listed damage)  in pre-Hardmode and by 7–8 damage (130% of the weapon's listed damage) in Hardmode. For example, using Abigail's Flower five times will cause Abigail to deal 19 base damage in pre-Hardmode and 37 base damage in Hardmode.
Initially, Abigail can damage a maximum of 3 enemies at once. This number will increase by 1 every two summons. For example, using Abigail's Flower three or four times will allow Abigail to damage 4 enemies at once, using it five or six times will allow her to damage 5 enemies at once, and so on.
Abigail also increases in movement speed and acceleration with each summon.
Although Abigail has an attack animation, she will continue to deal damage upon contact, rather than dealing damage when she attacks.
Abigail applies 20 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hitting an enemy, meaning she can hit up to three times per second.
Abigail can target enemies up to 43.75 tiles away.
This detection range is boosted to 131.25 tiles for enemies that are targeted by the player using a whip or summon staff.
Abigail will attempt to return to the player's side if her distance from the player is more than 62.5 tiles.
In regular worlds, Abigail's Flower can only grow on the surface layer and above. In Remix and Zenith worlds, it can grow in any layer.
The flower breaks in one hit when mined, making a grassy sound effect.
When a tombstone is selected for a tile update, there is a 1/30 (3.33%) chance that a random point within a 20×20-tile area is chosen. If the tile directly below that point is grass, an Abigail's Flower is placed at that point.
If the Constant seed is active, a second random point is chosen and the check is repeated once if the first attempt fails.
Abigail's Flower grows on most types of grass (see below), and can replace existing plants. It cannot grow within a 240×240-tile rectangle centered on another Abigail's Flower (i.e., multiple flowers need at least 120 tiles horizontally or vertically between them).


== Tips ==
It may help to make a large area of Tombstones evenly spaced out in large areas while trying to obtain this item.
It is best to be used with another item that can counter an enemy's movement, as Abigail cannot move while attacking.
Despite being a pre-Hardmode summon weapon, Abigail's Flower can work well during Hardmode, due to the substantial damage boost it gains. It is especially effective paired with the Firecracker.
Chaos Balls will detonate on impact with Abigail, making her a passive shield against these attacks.
Abigail positions herself behind the player when idle; one can take advantage of this when enemies are behind blocks by facing the opposite direction, allowing Abigail to phase through the barrier.


== Trivia ==
The flavor text of the item is a reference to Wilson's examination quote for Abigail's Flower in Don't Starve Together.
Abigail's Flower is the only weapon to gain a damage boost with game progression.
Abigail will occasionally make the sound of a laughing Pipspook, an entity in Don't Starve Together.
This also makes Abigail the only summoned minion who has idle sound effects.

The flower on Abigail's head has three different shapes which she will cycle through when summoned repeatedly. The color of the flower changes every cycle. For example, Abigail first has a small red flower, then a medium red flower, then a large red flower. Summoning her a fourth time will result in a small purple flower, then a medium purple flower, then a large purple flower, and so on.
The colors are represented in the HSL format. Saturation (S) and lightness (L) levels are always fixed at 100% and 60%, respectively. The hue (H) is calculated with the following formula, with [math]\displaystyle{ n }[/math] being the number of summons:
[math]\displaystyle{ H = \left ( -46.8 * \left\lfloor \frac{n - 1}{3} \right\rfloor + 360 \right ) \bmod{360} }[/math]
The only exception is the second cycle, which has its own HSL values, separate from this formula.
The colors for the first 21 summonings are listed below. Further summonings continue to use the formula but this cannot be seen in-game without third-party software like mods, due to the limited number of minion slots.

Internally, a modified version of the Medusa Head's rays is used for Abigail's attack animation.
Despite being a plant, Abigail's Flower cannot be grown by walking over grass blocks with Flower Boots equipped.
Abigail's Flower is one of the very few weapons that can be acquired as physical objects in the game's world, the others being the Enchanted Sword, the Terragrim, and the Water Bolt.
The three summon weapons with this special summoning mechanic are Abigail's Flower, Desert Tiger Staff, and Stardust Dragon Staff.


== See also ==
Abigail's Flower at the Don't Starve Wiki


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Now deals knockback.
Removed mana cost (cost 10 mana previously).
Now placeable with the Rubblemaker.
Desktop 1.4.4.5: Can now grow on Mushroom and Ash grass.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Now breaks in one hit when mined, and makes a grassy sound when doing so.
Can no longer grow on Jungle grass.
Desktop 1.4.3.2: 
Increased base speed by 33%.
Decreased speed growth per minion from 1.5 to 1.4 (ends at exactly the same value at 11-minion).
Improved base acceleration by 10%.
Decreased acceleration growth from 2 to 1.75 (maxes out at the same minion count).
Fixed (again) Abigail's Flower growth not appearing on servers, requiring players to log in again to see it.
Desktop 1.4.3.1: 
Increased spawnrate by 33%.
Abigail can now only hit up to 3 enemies at once per "attack". This cap increases with additional summons.
Fixed an issue where Abigail's Flower would not visually sync on servers when it grew (rendering it invisible until the player rejoined).

title: Ammo Box
content:
The Ammo Box is a furniture item. It can be purchased from the Arms Dealer for 10 Gold in Hardmode.
Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Ammo Box grants the Ammo Box buff, which provides ranged weapons with a 1/5 (20%) chance per shot not to consume ammunition. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world. The buff can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
Unlike equipment buff items, the Ammo Box must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.


== Notes ==
The Ammo Box can be activated limitlessly with no cooldown period. It is never consumed, and all players may use it to give themselves the buff.
The increased ammo conservation chance from the Ammo Box buff has no effect on consumable ranged weapons.


== See also ==
Ammo Reservation Potion, a potion with a similar effect.

Is now sold by the Arms Dealer in Hardmode, instead of by the Traveling Merchant at any time.
Buy price and sell value decreased from 15 Gold / 3 Gold to 10 Gold / 2 Gold.
Buff duration of 10 minutes removed. The buff now lasts until the player dies or leaves the world.

title: Dangersense Potion
content:
The Dangersense Potion is a buff potion which grants the Dangersense buff when consumed. The buff reveals hazardous traps, blocks, and objects that can potentially harm or impede the player by highlighting them in red, even in complete darkness. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Dangersense Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.


== List of hazards ==
The Dangersense buff highlights the blocks and objects listed below. Some of these will not be highlighted if the player affected by the buff has equipment that prevents harm from them.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Dead Man's Chests are not highlighted by the Dangersense buff, but the traps surrounding them are.


== Tips ==
The ability to locate Cobwebs makes finding Spider Nests much easier.
In addition to Spider Nests, Dangersense Potions can also be used to find caverns by following patches of Cobweb.
The ability to see traps, including pressure plates, makes traversing the Dungeon and Jungle Temple much easier.
For avoiding mechanism-based traps, having the Mechanical Lens (including its upgrade, The Grand Design) with oneself, or holding out certain mechanisms will reveal their wiring, effectively exposing their structure and allowing the player to disassemble or dodge them.
Dangersense Potions make it much easier to also collect traps for the player's own purposes, such as Jungle Temple traps, or Geyser in caverns.
Dangersense Potions can highlight Cracked Dungeon Bricks in the Dungeon, making finding hidden passages trivial.
When using a boss arena with traps such as Boulders, this potion can be useful for dodging them while still being able to concentrate on the fight.
Traps coated with Echo Coating can still be spotted with Dangersense, as the buff also causes objects to emit red particles.


== Trivia ==
The Dangersense Potion is named TrapsightPotion internally.


== See also ==
Hunter Potion, a similar consumable which highlights entities.

Now highlights Hellstone even if the player has fire block immunity (on account of creating lava when mined).

title: Flinx Staff
content:
The Flinx Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Flinx minion. It runs towards enemies, bouncing upwards upon contact before attempting to hit its target again. Its rapid attack rate also allows its bouncing to keep it airborne atop slow flying enemies.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Flinx cannot pass through blocks and will stay in place if summoned inside blocks until having to chase the player when out of range.
The Flinx minion applies 10 ticks of static invincibility frames upon hitting an enemy, meaning it can hit up to six times per second.
The Flinx, as well as the Vampire Frog and the Pirates, are the only minions capable of swimming in all liquids whilst pursuing enemies.


== Tips ==
The Flinx Staff is a reliable alternative to other early-game minion-summoning weapons such as the Finch Staff and Slime Staff. Unlike them, it can be crafted using relatively common ingredients and does not require luck to obtain, although the player has to kill Snow Flinx to obtain it.
Like other early-game minion-summoning weapons, rapidly resummoning Flinx onto an enemy can deal damage faster.
On top of being easy to obtain, it tracks grounded enemies very well, and scales well with summon tag damage.


== Trivia ==
The Flinx minions appear to be purple-colored Snow Flinx with a bun of fur behind their heads.
Prior to 1.4.5.0, minion-summoning weapons used to consume mana when used. The Flinx Staff was the only minion-summoning weapon to consume 5 mana instead of 10.

Flinx Fur Coat
