title: Guide:King Slime strategies
content:
King Slime is an optional pre-Hardmode boss. Due to its low health and very predictable attacks, it is considered the easiest boss in the game by most players. However, some may think the Eye of Cthulhu is easier because King Slime has relatively high contact damage.


== Spawn Condition ==
King Slime can be spawned by fulfilling any of these conditions:

Rarely in the outer lateral sixths of the map, during daytime, and only on grass, replacing a normal Slime's spawning.
150 slimes are defeated during the Slime Rain event (or 75 if King Slime was already slain in the world at least once).
Using the Slime Crown.
As with almost all bosses, it despawns if every player involved is dead.


== The Fight ==
King Slime is very similar to a normal Slime: it moves by hopping to the player and attempts to make contact, which deals damage. The pattern of his jumps is predictable and repeatedly: two normal, one small, and one high. After the high jump, the King Slime can teleport to the player. With his huge size and predictable movement, King Slime is easy to hit.
Getting too far away from King Slime will make it teleport to the player, meaning that the player cannot escape by simply running offscreen.
King Slime becomes smaller and faster the lower his health is, which makes him harder to hit. He will also summon Blue Slimes as he gets damaged to harass the player. These can draw the player's attention towards the Blue Slimes and waste ammo and time on them instead of King Slime, so the use of piercing weapons or ammo is important.


=== Expert Mode ===
There are not many changes to the King Slime itself besides its higher damage and health. However, when damaged it will spawn Spiked Slimes in addition to regular Blue Slimes. Those can throw volleys of spikes at a short distance, so having a weapon that can pierce multiple targets and attack from a range will be necessary to avoid being bombarded to death.


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===
King Slime is one of the few bosses in the game that lack the ability to go through blocks. He also will drop off platforms when the player does. This can be exploited as follows:

Make one or two long rows of platforms above the ground; King Slime will eventually teleport to ground level and the player can easily hit him from the platforms. If he moves to the upper platforms, falling down for a brief time before jumping back up will cause him to fall down as well.
Since King Slime spawns Blue Slimes, a Blue Slime Banner is a good idea to provide offensive and defensive buffs.


=== Gearing Up ===


==== Armor ====
Armor is not very important in this fight; however, some suggestions are below.

For all classes, Silver armor or Tungsten armor can increase survivability significantly in Expert or Master Mode. Platinum armor is even better but is made from a rarer ore. If the player is looking for defense but does not have platinum in their world, Jungle armor provides more defense than Gold armor.
Cactus armor is a cheap option, as it is easy to obtain and provides a useful thorns effect dealing damage to any slimes that run into the player. In Expert or Master Mode, better armor is recommended due to King Slime's buffed HP and attack power.
Pumpkin armor is also cheap and more powerful than Cactus armor due to its set bonus. It's especially easy to obtain during Halloween, but can also be obtained by throwing Cactus in the Shimmer.
If the player has difficulty using lower-tier armors, one of these more advanced armors can be obtained:

Gladiator armor is extremely powerful for melee users due to its set bonus, but are rare drops from Hoplites. Ancient Shadow armor is similarly powerful, but are also very rare drops from Eaters of Souls and thus are Corruption only.
Fossil armor with a Gi optimizes for ranged damage, and is fairly easy to obtain.
Wizard set or Jungle armor is best for mages.
Different Gem Robes have different interactions with Gem staves. Specific recommendations are given in the Magic Weapons section below.
Flinx Fur Coat is the best choice for summoners paired with any high-defense helmet and leggings, ideally Jungle armor.


==== Weapons ====
Due to King Slime's high contact damage, using a long-range weapon that can keep a safe distance from him is recommended. Piercing weapons may be preferred, to hit both the Blue Slimes and the King Slime himself. 

For Melee users

The Thorn Chakram is a good option to keep the boss at range, but can struggle against the hordes of slimes. The Trimarang is more rare, but performs similarly to the Thorn Chakram.
The Storm Spear can penetrate the hordes of slimes and damage the boss from range with its projectile, but is difficult to obtain due to it only being found deep in the Underground Desert, or through fishing.
The Rotted Fork has higher damage than the Storm Spear, but lacks the projectile and requires you to destroy multiple Crimson Hearts.
Flails such as the Ball O' Hurt, Flaming Mace, and Chain Knife can give the player plenty of range, with the first two being able to pierce through minions as well.
The Mandible Blade can be thrown rapidly from a safe distance.
Projectile swords such as the Enchanted Sword, Starfury, and Blade of Grass can help the player avoid King Slime's heavy contact damage, though they are difficult to obtain at the point where you would likely fight King Slime. They do higher damage when the blade is used as well, at the cost of somewhat greater risk.
The Ice Blade is a weaker option that is easier to obtain.
The Amazon is the best yoyo available, but is difficult to obtain for the same reasons as the Blade of Grass.
The Malaise or Artery are easier to get, but perform worse.
For Ranged users

A cheap and powerful option is a bow, such as the Gold, Platinum, or even the Tendon/Demon Bow.
Frostburn Arrows or Jester's Arrows are the preferred ammo types, due to the high single target damage of the former and the piercing effect of the latter.
The Blood Rain Bow is the strongest bow available, however it can be tiresome to obtain.
The Snowball Cannon is another strong ranged weapon.
Molotov Cocktails have a large area of effect, do high damage and inflict On Fire!.
If the player has done some fishing, Frost Daggerfish are strong and can pierce.
If the player has explored the Underground Desert, Bone Javelins are very effective on the boss itself. Similarly, Bone Throwing Knives are good for clearing the slime minions.
All guns are very effective against King Slime, although they are harder to obtain than the other ranged weapons.
The Musket or The Undertaker are the easiest to obtain out of all guns, only requiring a single Shadow Orb/Crimson Heart.
The preferred ammo type is Musket Balls, as Silver Bullets and Tungsten Bullets are too expensive and/or tedious to amass in the early game.
For Magic users

Gem staves are the most common magic weapons in this part of the game. The Emerald Staff and all stronger staves do well against King Slime. Gem staves gain additional powers when paired with Gem Robes.
In general, given enough gems to make both a robe and a staff of different gems, the higher-tier gems should be used for the staff. Pairing a staff with a matching robe is almost always a good combination.
The Amethyst Robe pairs well with piercing staves, as it allows multiple hits.
The Emerald Robe can be used to great advantage by targeting King Slime from above (such as a platform) and leaving projectiles embedded in the ground for him to run into. This does not work well with the Amber Staff, which bounces off the ground.
The Sapphire Robe increases total damage by 20% but splits the projectile into two weaker ones. With King Slime's defense of 10, this means that the Sapphire Robe makes weapons below 25 damage worse and above 25 damage better (counting damage from the tooltip). If using the Shark Tooth Necklace, it is useful for all gem staves. It also has special interactions with the Sapphire Staff and especially the Ruby Staff that causes them to do much higher damage.
The Wand of Frosting is an easily obtained magic weapon that does well in this fight. The Daybloom Staff is a weaker alternative.
The Thunder Zapper and Crimson Rod can be helpful in this fight, although they require exploring the Underground Desert or Crimson, respectively. The Vilethorn is not as strong but is similarly available in the Corruption.
For Summoners
The Snapthorn is the best whip available, it will deal a significant amount of damage. However, getting it requires Underground Jungle materials.
The Soulscourge and Vasculash are weaker yet easier to obtain alternatives, only requiring mining Demonite or Crimtane.
While rare, a Foxparks summon works well in this fight, switching between the flamethrower attack for minions and the normal attack (combined with whips) when attacking the boss himself. Foxparks can only be summoned in one slot, so any additional slots must be filled with other minions.
The best multiple-use summon weapons at this part of the game are the Flinx Staff and the Vampire Frog Staff.
The Finch Staff is serviceable if anything stronger hasn't been obtained.
Abigail's Flower, is a weak choice, yet efficient if there are no other summon weapons available.


==== Accessories ====
Like weapons, most accessories can help, but accessories obtained in chests are usually enough to defeat King Slime. It is unlikely that players will have access to the Tinkerer's Workshop at this stage of the game, so combined accessories are not listed below.

Hermes Boots, Dunerider Boots, Flurry Boots, or the Sailfish Boots can assist with horizontal mobility.
If obtained, Fledgling Wings are amazing for extra mobility in the air.
Any double jump accessories such as the Cloud in a Bottle greatly increases vertical mobility.
A Band of Regeneration boosts health regeneration, increasing survivability.
Feral Claws are great for warriors and summoners, but requires exploring the Underground Jungle.
The Snapping Stone is useful for increasing ranger damage. Similarly, the Poison Barb will add damage through the Poisoned debuff.
While usually not useful in combat, the White String is cheap enough to craft that it can be crafted over and over again to get a Warding or Menacing modifier. Similarly, Zombies can be farmed for a Shackle with good modifiers.


==== Potions ====
Ironskin Potions and Regeneration Potions greatly increase survivability.
Any food that grants the Well Fed or better should be used.
Swiftness Potions increase mobility.
Ale or Sake provide useful melee buffs.
Archery Potions increase the effectiveness of bows.
Mana Regeneration Potions are very important for mages, as it allows for very quick mana regeneration.
Magic Power Potions make magic weapons more potent.
Summoning Potions give summoners an extra minion, but are more difficult to obtain than the potions listed above.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Platform/Minecart strategy ===
Create one or two rows of platform about 18–20 blocks off the ground and at least 35–50 blocks long. Walk back and forth along the platform, firing at King Slime. If he or his slimes reach the platform, drop down temporarily and use hooks or double-jumps to return; this will cause King Slime and his minions to drop down as well, following you.
While it takes more work, making a minecart track instead of platforms can give you an even greater speed advantage, and can be useful for further fights in the game. If you can't make a very long track, put bumpers on the end. King Slime will have a hard time trying to teleport to the player because of the speed attained on a Minecart.


=== Lava Pit Strategy ===
Because King Slime can be harmed by lava, a good strategy is to use a Lava Bucket to make a long strip of land with a small amount of lava (shallow enough so items don't burn) and then make some widely placed platforms. The player can jump, use Rocket Boots, or employ a Grappling Hook to move between platforms. Just be careful to not jump in the lava if you don't plan to use Obsidian Skin Potions. This strategy works with his teleports, and the minions will all die from falling in the lava. The player doesn't have to focus on fighting, because the lava will dish out major damage. The player can also skip the platforms and use a Obsidian Skin Potion, and just evade by running under King Slime, or use Rocket Boots to fly over.


=== Ocean strategy ===
King Slime is very slow in liquids. If the player can find a way to move quickly in water, they can easily outmaneuver this boss. The best option for moving in the water is the Hardy Saddle, obtained by fishing, but other options include the Flipper, Flipper Potion, or the Trident.


=== Tunnel strategy ===
Since King Slime can't jump freely in narrow corridors, make a tunnel (3 blocks high), block off the sides, and make a 1 block hole in any wall, then on the neighbouring blocks don't do anything, then mine the neighbouring blocks of the neighbouring blocks, and repeat this pattern until the tunnel has holes to attack from (like with any guns), then summon King Slime and him and his minions won't be able to go through the gaps, while you can safely attack him from the gaps that you have just made. Though you still have to move from time to time to avoid his teleportation.

title: Flask of Cursed Flames
content:
The Flask of Cursed Flames is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips to inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff on hit for 3–6 seconds, which deals 24 damage per second and increases knockback on targets. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Cursed Flames cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Tips ==
The Flask of Cursed Flames can prove to be very useful when mining, as it gives more light than torches, and both pickaxes and drills are affected by the buff.

Flask of Ichor, the Crimson counterpart

title: Finch Staff
content:
The Finch Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Baby Finch minion. It flies towards enemies to deal contact damage. The Finch Staff has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being found in Living Wood Chests within Living Trees. Newly created Journey Mode characters spawn with a Finch Staff.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Notes ==
The Baby Finch will always be summoned at the player's cursor; it will have to fly to the player's head before nesting. However, the nest sprite appears instantly when the first Baby Finch is summoned.
Having at least one summoned Baby Finch and the Finch Staff in the inventory automatically summons one Baby Finch when the player joins a world.
Newly created Journey Mode characters spawn with one Baby Finch summoned.
Baby Finches do not target enemies without a clear line-of-sight, even if they are targeted with ⚷ Open / Activate.
The Baby Finch minion applies 15 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hitting an enemy.
The Baby Finch minion can target enemies up to 50 tiles away from the player, and will automatically return to the player's side if its current target gets more than 50 tiles away from the player.
While the Baby Finch buff is active, a nest appears on the player's head, in which the Baby Finch will rest when not attacking. When multiple Baby Finches are summoned, they will all be visible and stacked on top of each other on the player's head.


== Tips ==
Compared to other early-game summons, it is much easier to get than Slime Staff and has piercing, unlike Flinx Staff.
Unlike most pre-Hardmode minions which use static invincibility frames, the Baby Finch minion uses local invincibility, meaning that its damage output will scale with how many Baby Finches are summoned.
Rapidly resummoning Baby Finches onto an enemy deals damage faster.
Cornering an enemy with a Baby Finch will result in very high DPS.


== Trivia ==
The Baby Finch's sprite is most likely based on a common chaffinch.


== Gallery ==

		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Removed mana cost (cost 10 mana previously).
Now automatically summons one Baby Finch upon spawn if the player previously summoned a Baby Finch, not when the Finch Staff is just held in the inventory. Newly created Journey Mode characters spawn with one Baby Finch summoned.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Reworked to be more reliable with hitting its targets.
Enemies knocked back by the Baby Finches are knocked away from the player now, regardless of the angle of the Baby Finch.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: Fixed an issue where Baby Finches were unable to descend through platforms.

title: Hardy Saddle
content:
The Hardy Saddle is a mount-summoning item that summons a Turtle Mount that can swim and has increased movement speed in liquids (51 mph maximum), but reduced movement speed (26 mph maximum) and jump reach (3.53 tiles maximum) on land. It also allows the player to breathe underwater.
The Hardy Saddle has a 7/80 (8.75%) chance of being obtained from Golden Crates and a 133/1600 (8.31%) chance of being obtained from Titanium Crates.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The Lava Shark Mount is another preferable alternative for underwater travel, because it is much faster and its summoning item is slightly more common.
This mount is exceptionally useful in worlds with the secret world seed Waterpark enabled, as early-game underwater mobility (and infinite air) is much more useful in a flooded world.


== Trivia ==
The buff tooltip is a reference to a verse from the poem "Paul Revere's Ride" (1860) by American poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow: "One if by land, Two if by sea".
The player can travel upwards indefinitely using the Turtle Mount and the Bottomless Water Bucket by constantly placing water above the player and swimming upward.

title: Campfires
content:
Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration.
The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers.
Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details).
Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Used to craft ===


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Notes ==

Blocks and walls do not obstruct campfires from granting the Cozy Fire buff.
Campfires do not provide the Cozy Fire buff to NPCs.
Despite providing light, campfires do not count as light sources for NPC housing.
Most campfires are dislodged by liquids, but Cursed Campfire(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Ichor Campfire(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Coral Campfire(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) function in every liquid except lava. They also stay lit during rain in The Constant special world seed.


== Tips ==
Fireplaces are similar to campfires, but are not a strict upgrade (see their page for details). Since both items provide the same Cozy Fire buff, campfires and Fireplaces do not stack with each other.
Campfires and Heart Lanterns provide different health regeneration buffs that stack with each other. Together, they grant 10% increased innate health regeneration and 1.5 HP/s constant regeneration.
Campfires (or Fireplaces) and Heart Lanterns are widely useful throughout the game:
In bases: To recover faster after retreating to the safety of the base, or after dying and respawning.
In arenas: To improve health regeneration during lengthy bossfights and events.
While exploring: They can be kept in the hotbar and placed on the fly in dangerous areas.
Place campfires every 340' as measured by the Compass (or its upgrades) to maximize their coverage and minimize overlap.
Campfire crafting recipes are also available at Cooking Pots, the Furnace, and the Furnace's upgrades.


== Trivia ==

Campfires have a few environment interactions that are purely visual:
Their smoke particles are affected by wind speed and direction.
They emit extra smoke in rain.
In the presence of the Moon Lord, campfire flames turn black.
Normal Campfires can sometimes be found in a Campsite, along with some placed Silver or Gold Coins.
The Rainbow Campfire appears to be made out of Crystal Blocks, but their component Rainbow Torches are instead made from Rainbow Bricks.
The Campfire has seven upgrades, the most out of any crafting station.
They are as follows: Cooking Pot/Cauldron, Furnace, Glass Kiln, Hellforge, and Adamantite Forge/Titanium Forge.
Ice Torches and Frozen Campfires are the only corresponding Torch and Campfire pair that do not have a matching descriptor.
 The Bone Campfire's tooltip incorrectly displays the Shadowflame Bow's information.

title: Guide:Pumpkin Moon strategies
content:
The Pumpkin Moon is a post-Plantera Hardmode event triggered by activating the Pumpkin Moon Medallion. The event is very rewarding if you can successfully keep pace, providing a large amounts of money and good weapons by the end of the night.
However, the event is also difficult and requires a lot of preparation.


== The Event ==

The event consists of 20 waves, with the final wave lasting until the end of the night. As the event goes on, stronger enemies and unique bosses will appear.
During the first few waves, a large number of Scarecrows, Hellhounds and Splinterlings will appear. These enemies only have average stats, so a weapon with good crowd control abilities will clear the first waves fairly fast.
On wave 4, Poltergeists will start appearing. And on wave 5, Headless Horsemen will start appearing. These are weaker than the Boss enemies, but much stronger than the average ones. Even if they are not a threat by themselves, they can be very dangerous combined with the minibosses.
The first miniboss, the Mourning Wood will start appearing on wave 6. This enemy will walk towards the player, and then shoot Flaming Wood when it stops moving. It can also leave Greek Fire on the ground. While it can prove to be rather easy to kill, on later waves many of them will spawn, so one can easily get overwhelmed by their projectiles.
On wave 10, the main Boss of the Event will appear, the Pumpking. It behaves similarly to Skeletron; attempting to stay above the player and attacking with the blades on its arms. The most dangerous attack it has are its Flame Scythes: a large, highly damaging projectile that speeds up over time, similar to Demon Scythes. It's rather slow for a boss enemy, so it can be easily outran and dodged by moving in wide circles.
The further the player has progressed, the more boss enemies will be able to spawn at once, and their chance to drop an item will also increase. On the final wave, up to seven of each boss can appear, and they will always drop an item and their respective trophy.


== Preparation ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===

The Pumpkin and Frost Moons are much easier to handle with the proper arena.
A flat surface about 168 blocks wide (see NPC spawning) will focus all spawns on the arena. Above it there should be a long platform of the same width, high above the ground in order to keep grounded enemies out of reach.
Since the player will mostly focus on the Bosses on the later waves, Lava pit and Traps may be helpful to take out the weaker enemies more easily. However, on higher difficulties the Traps' low damage is practically useless against the higher-health enemies, making them almost a liability due to the invincibility frames they provide and the risk of being hit by them and taking massive damage in the process.
It's also a good idea to make a room with a Bed near the Arena, so in case of death you can quickly get back to it.


=== Gearing up ===
The event can be summoned at any time post-Plantera, but is intended to be done soon after Golem.


==== Armor ====
For melee, DPS is maximized with the Chlorophyte Mask, Monk's Shirt, and Squire's Greaves/Valhalla Knight's Greaves.
Beetle armor with Scale Mail can also be used, but is ideal only when using the Terra Blade.
Rangers should use Shroomite armor with the headpiece that suits their weapon.
Shroomite armor's set bonus becomes useless in later waves, so the Shroomite Leggings can be replaced with Tiki Pants for an extra minion or Red Riding Leggings for a 3% advantage in critical strike chance and 25% summon damage.
For a mage, the highest DPS is attained by using Spectre armor with Hallowed Headgear in the head slot, using the Spectre Hood only when at low health.
Dark Artist's Leggings can be used along with Hallowed Headgear in place of Spectre Pants, but does not facilitate armor switching.
Summoners should use Tiki armor. They can also switch to the Squire's Great Helm after summoning, losing two minions to gain constant regeneration greater than that provided by Palladium armor.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users

The Flairon is a very strong weapon for both crowd control and single targets. Scourge of the Corruptor works similarly.
The Terra Blade, Influx Waver and Seedler are very reliable swords for both single targets and crowds. However, the Flying Dragon is an immensely devastating option, that, although requires beating the post-Golem Old One's Army, contends well with all of the Frost Moon's enemies with the right gear.
The Sky Dragon's Fury is excellent against both bosses and crowds. The Sky Dragon's Fury should use the alternate attack against bosses.
The Kraken is the strongest yoyo at this stage, and can be used with the Magic Yoyo Bag to either throw piercing yoyos or do heavy single-target damage.
The Keybrand can be thrown into the ground, doing high damage to small enemies and to the Mourning Wood if it stays in that location.
The Paladin's Hammer is very good for crowds and decent against bosses, especially for reducing defense.
Possessed Hatchet is fast and deals decent damage, but it becomes ineffective in the later waves, as there will be too many boss enemies for it to handle. It also inflicts the powerful Hemorrhage debuff.
The Psycho Knife deals extreme damage to Mourning Woods and other grounded enemies.
If the Empress of Light has been defeated, the Starlight would be a better choice.
Vampire Knives can be used to quickly heal in critical situations, but have lower DPS than most other options.
A Flask of Ichor significantly boosts damage output the most by applying the Ichor debuff. Flask of Nanites, while not being particularly useful for damage output, inflicts the Confused debuff, which can help make your life easier when dealing with regular enemies.
For Ranged users

Tsunami and Eventide are of the best weapons to use. With Ichor or Holy Arrows, they can deal massive damage to all enemies. Chlorophyte Arrows have less damage but have homing bounces that can spread out over a wide area. Eventide can also use the Magic Quiver to take advantage of its high pierce.
The Aerial Bane is well-suited to this event, as it can deal extra damage to Pumpkings and Poltergeists while raining attacks onto the enemies below.
The Electrosphere Launcher, Snowman Cannon, Stynger or Pulse Bow are very effective for crowd control.
The Xenopopper paired with Crystal Bullets is very strong against the bosses. The Chain Gun is also a good option. Chlorophyte Bullets and Nano Bullets can be used to increase accuracy, with the latter one being more useful in crowd control.
The Tactical Shotgun and Sniper Rifle with Chlorophyte Bullets can be useful for mini-bosses, though being weaker than the former two guns.
The Nail Gun can be useful against bosses if few post-Golem weapons have been obtained.
For Magic users

The Razorblade Typhoon excels against both enemies and bosses. The Charged Blaster Cannon is another weapon with high pierce and high damage against all targets.
The Arc Surge can obliterate this event very quickly, though being a very rare drop from Martian Saucer.
The Nightglow provides a nice balance between crowd control and single target damage.
The Bubble Gun, Laser Machinegun or Inferno Fork are good against the bosses. The Heat Ray is a weaker alternative.
The Staff of Earth can be effective against grounded enemies.
Betsy's Wrath, Magnet Sphere, Rainbow Gun, and Nimbus Rod are all very good secondary weapons. Betsy's Wrath can also work well as a primary weapon with its wide, gravity-affected area of effect and high damage.
The Razorpine and Blizzard Staff are very effective weapons for this event, if the player has done the Frost Moon beforehand.
For Summoners

The Kaleidoscope and Electric Eel are the best whips at this point in the game. They can serve specific scenarios and summoning-based playstyles. The Morning Star is weaker but easier to obtain.
The Morning Star and Kaleidoscope are relatively interchangeable whips that provide large summon tag damage boosts to minions and sentries.
The Electric Eel deals damage to multiple enemies through special debuffs.
The Xeno Staff is an extremely powerful and competent minion with consistent DPS. It is much more suited to taking down single targets, however.
Tempest Staff has slightly lower DPS and a much less competent AI, but is still viable against crowds of enemies. The Deadly Sphere Staff is a weaker alternative.
The Terraprisma is an extremely powerful and useful minion that can clear waves of enemies and weaker minibosses alike. However, it can be difficult to obtain, due to it being dropped after defeating the daytime Empress of Light.
Summon weapons that enhance only a single minion at one time, such as the Desert Tiger Staff, can do high damage but risk leaving the player open to attack if it gets distracted.
The Ballista Staff, Flameburst Staff, and Explosive Trap Staff are reliable damage-dealing sentries that can be even further enhanced by wearing Tavernkeep armors.
The Staff of the Frost Hydra is the best sentry available if you don't want to fight the Old One's Army. Its projectiles inflict Frostbite and deal relatively high damage.


==== Accessories ====
Wings, particularly those with hovering abilities such as Betsy's Wings or the Hoverboard are helpful. However, it's much better to use Mounts instead, as they save accessory slots that would be used for mobility items.
Worm Scarf is useful in this event as it gives a 17% damage reduction. The Master Ninja Gear can be used to dash, and grants a chance to dodge attacks.
The Frozen Shield is great for survivability.
For melee users:
The Fire Gauntlet is the best accessory to have at this stage, due to its useful Hellfire debuff, boosts to melee damage, and the ability to grant autoswing to all melee weapons.
For magic users:
The Celestial Emblem, Mana Cloak, and/or Magnet Flower are the best magic-focused accessories at this stage and suit many different playstyles.
For ranged users:
The Magic Quiver and/or Sniper Scope should be equipped to maximize damage dealt by the player's arrows and bullets, repectively. The Magic Quiver can be upgraded into the Molten Quiver, the Stalker's Quiver and Phoenix Quiver, while the Sniper Scope can be upgraded into the Recon Scope. However, most of these upgrades add relatively few advantages to their precursors. The Phoenix Quiver is more useful though, being able to redirect missed arrows.
The Chaos Cylinder can be used to cycle through different types of ammo.
For summoners:
The Pygmy Necklace can be obtained relatively easily from the Witch Doctor.
Whip stacking accessories such as the Ouroboros Ring and Twilight Grasp give you the ability to cycle through more whips to apply tag damage or other buffs, and can increase the damage output significantly.
Generally, most damage-increasing accessories such as Class-specific emblems, Avenger Emblem Destroyer Emblem, Celestial Shell, and/or the Celestial Stone are extremely important to progress in the events.


==== Mounts ====
The use of mounts can save accessory slots that would've been used for mobility.

The Brain Scrambler is very helpful, as the Scutlix has very high movement speed, a very high jump and extra laser attacks. The Master Mode-exclusive Toy Tank can also be used if the player has already fought the Frost Moon.
The Shrimpy Truffle or Cosmic Car Key provide permanent but slower flight.


==== Potions ====
Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, Lifeforce Potion, and Ironskin Potion will greatly increase survivability.
Any food item that provides the Well Fed buff is good.
Heartreach Potion is incredibly useful when picking up the hearts dropped by Mourning Woods or Pumpkings.
Mana Regeneration Potion is a must for mages.
Swiftness Potion will increase mobility.
Rage Potion and Wrath Potion will improve DPS.
Magic Power Potion, Archery Potion, Ale or Sake and Summoning Potion will further improve it for Mages, Rangers, Melee, and Summoner users respectively.


== Specific strategies ==
A very good way to go through waves, until any Pumpkings arrive at wave 10, and even kill some if aiming correctly, is to use a Cannon at a platform 37 blocks high from the ground (where the enemies are) as each Cannonball deals 300 damage, which is devastating for the early waves even for Mourning Woods. In addition, most attacks cannot hit the player.
Using Dynamite with an explosion-proof arena causes splash damage that can demolish early waves.
With the Cosmic Car Key, an effective technique against Pumpking is to move in a diamond formation around him while targeting him. This is especially effective if you place sentries such as the Frost Hydra or Queen Spider to deal with enemies below.
Both Pumpkings and Mourning Wood drop some hearts upon being defeated. In later waves (especially the final one), when you're swarmed by several of these monsters at once, a player with a Cross Necklace, Heartreach Potion, high Defense and a damaging weapon can potentially heal from killing them faster than they can damage you.

title: Shadow Orb (item)
content:
The Shadow Orb is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a slow-moving Shadow Orb which follows the player around and emits dim, purple light. The orb can move through solid objects and liquids unhindered, but moves very slowly, causing it to fall behind when the player is moving quickly. If it falls far enough behind, it will teleport to the player's location. The Shadow Orb has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Shadow Orbs, but it also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being acquired from Corrupt Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which are obtained by fishing in The Corruption.
The Crimson counterpart to the Shadow Orb is the Crimson Heart.


== Notes ==
The orb's position can be somewhat controlled using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down keys, allowing the player to reorient the orb directly above or below them respectively.
This will cause the orb to catch up slightly faster, if it is lagging behind.
The orb will emit purple light even if dyed.


== Tips ==
When paired with Acid Dye of any color, the orb will have stripes in the color but it will be buggy, as parts of, or even the whole orb itself, can disappear.
It can be paired with Reflective Gold Dye to make the Shadow Orb appear similarly to how it looked prior to 1.2.
Twilight Dye can render the orb almost completely invisible.

title: Parallax
content:
Parallax is an option which controls how much the underground backgrounds scroll relative to foreground objects such as walls, blocks, and NPCs.
Settings from 0 – 100 (inclusive) are available;

A setting of 0, the default setting, will make the background "stationary", causing it to follow player's movement, just as foreground objects do.
A setting of 100 will make the background scroll with the player's movement at a relatively high speed.

title: Guide:Jump height comparison
content:
Jump height can be boosted in various ways, and this page lists different jump heights under various conditions. Because some other factors may also interfere with jump height, the results on this page are calculated under the following assumptions:

The player is not in liquids.
Gravity not change during a jump.
The player does not step on a Honey Block.
The heights of flight (Rocket Boots, wings, and certain mounts) are not listed here. Compared to jump, flight is more flexible in vertical movement, so a single height cannot represent their ability.


== Jump heights of the player ==
Jump boosts can increase the player's own jump height by increasing their jump speed and/or jump duration. Extra jumps also benefit from them.


== Jump heights of mounts ==
Mounts have their own jump speed and jump duration, which can enhance extra jumps as well. Neither mounts' own jumps nor the extra jumps enhanced by mounts benefit from jump boosts.
Only normal mounts are included. Mounts that fly, swim, cannot use items are not listed here.
Painted Horse Mount / Majestic Horse Mount / Dark Horse Mount, Chillet / Chillet Ignis, Trusty Chillet / Trusty Chillet Ignis are three groups mounts with identical stats, so each group only lists one. Chillet and Trusty Chillet have the same sprite, where Chillet is in §Pre-Hardmode, while Trusty Chillet in §Hardmode.

title: Underground
content:
The Underground is the first layer below the surface. It fills the area between the Surface and Cavern layers, beginning at a depth of 0ft and extending downward.
Its distinctive background can recognize the Underground, which no longer contains naturally-placed Dirt Walls like surface terrain, but instead displays a unique, often brown, backdrop with no naturally-placed walls. Players cannot remove this backdrop using a Hammer, nor can they place blocks in midair, as no wall generally exists here (though players can place their walls, just as they can above surface terrain). Natural Underground blocks are generally similar to those in the surface, with Dirt and Stone making up the majority of the biome. Clay, Silt, and lower-tier gems and ores can also be found in small pockets here. Some miscellaneous treasures can be found here, including Gem Trees (which drop Gemcorns, Stone, and occasionally their respective gems when chopped down); dye plants including Green Mushrooms, Orange Bloodroot, and Teal Mushrooms; and the Blinkroot herb.
The Underground is home to more aggressive enemies than the surface. More powerful Red and Yellow Slimes will spawn down here (alongside the rare Pinky), while Blue Jellyfish spawn in the water and Giant Worms are found burrowing through the ground. In Hardmode, more powerful counterparts of these enemies will spawn, with the Digger, Green Jellyfish, and Toxic Sludge mostly replacing Giant Worms, Blue Jellyfish, and regular slimes respectively.
Traps will also begin appearing in this layer. Underground Cabins, though not as common as in the Caverns, will frequently appear with handy loot such as the Cloud in a Bottle, Hermes Boots, and Magic Mirror.
In general, not much time is spent here, but instead in the Cavern layer, which holds many more enemies, spawns treasures, and unique drops. Therefore, it is a wise idea almost entirely to ignore this layer in favor of exploring the Caverns.
Occasionally, the Mouse and Snail critters will be found scurrying around. Fairies have a rare chance of randomly showing up and guiding the player to a random treasure (such as chests, Life Crystals, or ores) nearby.
True underground versions of biomes, such as the Ice biome or Underground Corruption, do not begin in this layer, but in the Cavern layer (except for the Underground Desert, which begins in Surface terrain and extends through the Underground and a portion of the Cavern). In Hardmode, some blocks in the Underground can be converted into Hallow, Corruption, or Crimson.


== Contents ==


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
A pure Underground biome is required for fishing in Underground, otherwise no Underground-exclusive fishing catches can be obtained.


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===

title: Hunter Potion
content:
The Hunter Potion is a buff potion which grants the Hunter buff when consumed. The buff shows the location of enemies, critters, and NPCs on the screen by highlighting them in red (enemies) or green (critters and NPCs). Although these affected entities glow, they do not emit any light to the surrounding area. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Hunter Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Tips ==
Hunter Potions are very useful for locating rare enemies such as Mimics, Nymphs, and Cyan Beetles, or critters such as Truffle Worms and Mice.
Bound NPCs like the Goblin Tinkerer and the Tavernkeep and neutral ones such as the Skeleton Merchant will be highlighted green under the effect of this potion, making locating them much easier as well.
The Lifeform Analyzer informs the player of the presence of nearby rare creatures. This helps determine when a Hunter Potion is worth consuming.
The Hunter Potion has great utility when fighting enemies that move through blocks, such as burrowing worm enemies like the Eater of Worlds, or Man Eaters and Angry Trappers. It makes it possible to see them when they would otherwise be hardly visible, and anticipate their attacks.
Hunter Potions can also be used to locate pocket caves underground by revealing enemies that spawn inside them.
Certain enemies  such as Wraiths will not be made any more visible by this potion.
The Hunter Potion allows distinguishing fake Lunatic Cultists from real ones.
Hunter Potions can be quite difficult to craft, as a Shark Fin is needed for each one. Shark Statues can make this an easier process.

title: Cyborg
content:
The Cyborg is a Hardmode, post-Plantera NPC vendor who sells several "high-tech" items, most notably rocket ammunition for launcher weapons. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
Plantera has been defeated.
The Cyborg will defend himself against nearby enemies with three different kinds of explosives: grenades, rockets, and proximity mines, which are identical in behavior to the Grenade Launcher, Rocket Launcher, and Proximity Mine Launcher respectively. The Cyborg's proximity mines will also deal triple their usual damage when stationary.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Cyborg will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Names ==
The Cyborg may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
A cyborg is a being with both organic and biomechatronic body parts. Skin can be seen on the Cyborg NPC's hands and face, which is easier to notice in his old sprite.
Although most of his body seems to be coated or replaced with metal, the Cyborg has the regular NPC hit sound effect instead of a mechanical hit sound effect.
Along with the Traveling Merchant, the Zoologist, and the Princess, the Cyborg is one of the only NPCs that sells a post-Moon Lord item (the Portal Gun Station).
Unlike the other examples, the post-Moon Lord requirement can be circumvented by bringing a Portal Gun or Portal Gun Station from another world.
Almost all of the Cyborg's names are letters in the Greek alphabet. Naming robots and cyborgs with Greek letters is common in science fiction.
The names Syn-x and A.N.D.Y. are likely references to Re-Logic lead developers Whitney "Cenx" Spinks and Andrew "Redigit" Spinks.
The name T-3E0 is most likely a reference to C-3PO, a humanoid robot character from the American epic space opera media franchise Star Wars.
The name Niner-7 may be a reference to the character Seven of Nine from the American science fiction television series Star Trek: Voyager.
In the source files of the game, it can be found that the Cyborg's light on his head is off when he is wearing a Party Hat: 
His quote “My expedition efficiency was critically reduced when a projectile impacted my locomotive actuator.” is a reference to the "Arrow in the Knee" quote from the action role-playing video game The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, where a guard tells the player: "I used to be an adventurer like you, then I took an arrow in the knee."
The Zoologist shares a similar quote to the reference above: “I collected critters like you once, then I took a cursed fox bite to the knee!”
His quote “I built myself a taste mechanism, so I can drink some ale!” might be a reference to the movie Bicentennial Man.
The quote “This sentence is false, or is it?” references a common logical paradox often associated with robots.
His quote “<Name of Tavernkeep> said I reminded him of a certain "EV2". Perhaps I should meet her.” is a reference to the character EV2 in Dungeon Defenders 2.
His quote “So that 'punk' lookin' chick is an inventor, eh? I think I could show her a thing or two!” might suggest that he has some interest in the Steampunker.
Because this quote suggests he does not know the Steampunker already, it conflicts with a piece of lore, since the Cyborg's Bestiary entry states that he was created by the Mechanic and the Steampunker.
However, the Cyborg does not directly say that he knows the Mechanic either, meaning that there may be no memories of the event for him.
 The Bestiary entry for the Cyborg: "The Cyborg was built with the combined efforts of the Mechanic and the Steampunker to aid in rocket science and world defense."

title: The Crimson
content:
The Crimson is an evil biome with a fleshy infection, red gore theme, in contrast to the dark purple wasteland theme of its counterpart, The Corruption. Every world will contain one of the two generated randomly except for special seeds (each with a 50% chance of occurring) or chosen by the player upon world creation. Both contain similar hazards and feature their own unique enemies, items, and blocks. The tools, weapons, and armor obtained via Crimson material generally have minor advantages over those obtained via Corruption materials; however, Corruption tools are slightly faster. Crimson-themed enemies also tend to have slightly higher stats, such as health, defense, and damage.
The Crimson surface contains red Crimson grass, Crimson Trees, and Vicious Mushrooms. Red thorny bushes grow on the grass and will damage the player when touched. Water in the Crimson is also red. The Crimson also contains multiple chasms, extensions of the biome into the underground. Every chasm has an entrance on the surface and leads to a large, circular cavity, then branches off into small "fingers" which end with a Crimson Heart. Crimson Altars generally line the chasm's passages, appearing inside and around it. Chasms consist of Crimstone, which can be blown up by explosives, mined with a Nightmare/Deathbringer Pickaxe or higher, or purified to Stone by using Purification Powder.
The Crimson spreads, meaning it slowly converts adjacent tiles to their Crimson variants. See below for details. Chasms, Crimson Altars, and Crimson Hearts will only appear upon world generation, and will not spawn in a Crimson area that has formed through spreading. If enough Crimson manages to take over a new area, then that area will eventually adopt the Crimson's theme music, background, and water color. For an area to be considered a Crimson biome, at least 300 tiles of Crimson grass or Crimson blocks must be present.


== Contents ==


== Spread ==

The Crimson spreads itself, similar to The Corruption and The Hallow. This means that it slowly converts certain susceptible tiles that are in the vicinity of existing Crimson blocks. While its spreading capabilities are very limited during pre-Hardmode, it spreads much faster and more aggressively after defeating the Wall of Flesh. Defeating Plantera for the first time reduces the speed of the Crimson's spread by 1/2 (50%).


== Crimson Desert ==

In Hardmode, Crimson spreads through Deserts, transforming them into Crimson Deserts. A Crimson Desert is fairly similar to a regular Crimson biome: The theme music and enemies are the same, with the addition of:

Surface Desert:
Blood Mummies
Underground Desert:
Dark Lamias
Tainted Ghouls
Desert Spirits
During a Sandstorm:
Flesh Reavers
Sand is replaced by Crimsand. Cacti drop ordinary cactus when cut, even though they have a different color. Waterleaf is not able to grow in Crimson Deserts. If a Crimson biome overlaps a Desert biome during world generation, Sand will be converted to Crimsand, but it will not spread until Hardmode.


== Crimson Snow ==

Like the Crimson desert, Crimson Snow biomes are created when Crimson spreads into a Snow biome during Hardmode. Snow Blocks are not convertible, but Ice Blocks can be converted into Red Ice Blocks. Red Ice can be created during generation if a Crimson biome overlaps a Snow biome, but it will not spread until Hardmode.


== Notes ==

During world generation, the left half of the progress bar frame is red. Additionally, the main progress bar will be yellow. The step in the world generation process in which the Crimson is created is called “Making the world bloody”. Also, the world's tree icon in the world selection has one red-colored side.
Crimson can be created or spread artificially using Crimson Seeds, Vicious Powder, Blood Water, and either the Clentaminator or the Terraformer with Red Solution, obtainable from the Steampunker during a Blood Moon in Crimson worlds (she sells Purple Solution in a Corruption world instead).
After the Moon Lord has been defeated, Red and Purple Solutions can be Shimmered into each other.
It is possible to create an artificial Corrupt biome in a Crimson world without the use of another world. To do so, one must buy Corrupt Seeds in Hardmode from the Dryad while in a Graveyard.
Artificially creating a new Crimson biome requires at least 300 Crimson tiles. Although Corruption might replace Crimson at world generation, it does not prevent Crimson from being artificially created in a Corruption world (and vice versa), nor does it prevent the Crimson biome's spread.
During Hardmode, any enemy in the Crimson or Underground Crimson has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance to drop a Crimson Key.
The Steampunker will only sell the Flesh Cloning Vat and Red Solution in a world that is naturally generated with Crimson. Artificially creating a Crimson biome in a Corruption world will not cause her to sell these items.
A Drunk world will generate both Corruption and Crimson biomes.


== Tips ==

If a world generated with a random world evil chosen to be Crimson, one of the Guide's tips will tell the player to break a Crimson Heart.


== Trivia ==

Occasionally, multiple chasms might overlap, causing a sort of "cross" or "X" pattern, as seen in the two images to the right.
Because of the large circular cavity, its out-warding branches, and the entrance tunnel cutting at sharp angles, the chasm has many interpretations when combined with the Crimson's gore-related theme:
A cartoonish hand with its fingers outstretched.
A heart connected to veins, because of its red theme.
These chasms could represent the body of a neuron, a cell in the brain, evidenced by its associated boss, the Brain of Cthulhu, while the Corruption chasms resemble worm tunnels and has a worm-like boss, the Eater of Worlds.
The entrance of the chasm has teeth-like stalactites and stalagmites, and could be interpreted as the entrance being the mouth of a beast.
Many Crimson enemies have deformed features or blisters that resemble cancerous growths. This contrasts with the rotten bodies of many Corruption enemies, sometimes with green pus dripping out of them.
During a Blood Moon, three critters turn Vicious (Vicious Bunny, Vicious Goldfish, and Vicious Penguin), a reference to the Crimson. They can also manually be turned Vicious with Vicious Powder.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, the Crimson is a living being who wants to balance the world, and the creatures who come from it used to worship the Crimson. It acts like a hive mind connected to all worlds. The being itself is unseen.
Based on this, it appears likely that Crimstone is this massive being's flesh. This is supported by its appearance, as well as the fact that the item used to craft items with it is called the Meat Grinder.
The progress bar color during world generation being yellow for Crimson worlds might be based on the fact that the Crimson biome features the Ichor as its exclusive material.
Crimeras can sometimes appear as ambient entities in the background in the surface Crimson biome.

title: Darkness
content:
Darkness is a debuff that decreases the player's light vision, which functions much like a reverse Night Owl buff, dimming rather than amplifying provided light.
Visually, the debuff causes the player to gain a blue tint, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and their eyes will appear to close for the debuff's duration.

title: Cattiva
content:
Cattiva is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Cattiva minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, dealing contact damage. When Cattiva is falling and its target is more than 6.25 tiles above it, it can also perform a double jump with visuals similar to the Cloud in a Bottle to reach its target. Unlike the double jumps used by the player, Cattiva does not need to land on the ground to refresh its double jump and can use it endlessly while mid-air.
Cattiva can also mine alongside the player with a pickaxe power equivalent to 41% (approximately that of the Iron Pickaxe) and mining speed of 16. It will continue to mine even after the player stops, as long as the player is still nearby. Cattiva will also cut down trees and cacti alongside the player, either cutting the same tree/cactus or another one nearby. It has an axe power of 171% when cutting trees and an axe power of 57% when cutting cacti, as well as a chopping speed of 16 in both cases. Only one copy of Cattiva can be summoned at a time; additional uses of the summon weapon do not summon additional minions, nor do they improve the existing minion. Like other Pals, Cattiva can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate.
Cattiva has a rare chance to spawn on Grass, Jungle grass, Snow, or Ice blocks above surface during daytime if the player is not in a Graveyard biome, but it cannot spawn in the center 1/4 of the world. It is initially spawned as the distressed Cattiva, with two Goblin Archers spawned around it. After killing both Goblin Archers (or making them despawn), Cattiva will turn into its item form when the player is within 6.25 tiles from it.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Trusty Cattiva ==

Trusty Cattiva is an upgraded version of Cattiva obtained by crafting Cattiva with a Kinship Peach. Compared to Cattiva, it has a higher base damage and increased movement speed and acceleration. It also sticks to enemies when attacking them, letting it deal damage much more consistently than Cattiva, which instead tends to move through enemies when attacking them. It otherwise acts identically to Cattiva. The player cannot summon both Cattiva and Trusty Cattiva at the same time, as they will replace each other when summoned.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==


=== Distressed Cattiva ===
Cattiva cannot spawn if there is already a distressed Cattiva or a distressed Foxparks present in the world.
When attempting to spawn a distressed Pal, the game first checks the player's inventory for Cattiva and Foxparks items (not including the "Trusty" variants). If the player already has one of them in their inventory but not the other one, the game will spawn the one the player does not have. If the player has both items or neither of them, then there is a 40% chance to spawn distressed Foxparks and 60% chance to spawn distressed Cattiva. The 40% chance for Foxparks is affected by luck and is checked for first, meaning positive luck reduces spawn chance of distressed Cattiva and negative luck increases it.
Assuming the distressed Cattiva being located at (x, y), it will search for two applicable solid tiles (including platforms and Planter Boxes) located within (x-6, y-5) to (x-6, y+11) and (x+6, y-5) to (x+6, y+11) (two 17-tile high vertical columns 6 tiles to the left and right from it). For the tile to be applicable, the 3×3-tile area directly above it has to be empty (except for the two tiles at bottom left and right, i.e. (x-1, y-1) and (x+1, y-1)). The associated Goblin Archers will be spawned at these tiles.
The distressed Cattiva will immediately despawn if it cannot find two applicable tiles.
The distressed Cattiva's AI may sometimes detect its associated Goblin Archers improperly, preventing it from turning into an item. In this case, walking away from it (but not letting it despawn) then reapproaching it and killing all nearby enemies may fix the issue.
The distressed Cattiva can take damage from enemies, but all hits only deal 5 damage to it, regardless of the enemy's actual damage. This damage value is then reduced by distressed Cattiva's 15 defense, meaning it will only take 1 damage per hit in practice.
Internally, the game checks if horizontal distance of Cattiva's spawning location from the world spawn is greater than 1/8th of the world width (525 / 800 / 1050 tiles in small / medium / large worlds, respectively). In normal world this prevents it from spawning in central 1/4th of the map, but the spawning area can be different in special or secret world seeds that change the world spawn point, such as Celebration Mk 10 and How did I get here.


=== Cattiva & Trusty Cattiva ===
The Cattiva minion can target enemies within a 50-tile range, and non-boss targets that are not marked with a summon weapon must located within a 120×75 tiles rectangular area centered around the player.
When Cattiva is on the ground, or while falling in liquid, it will jump upwards if its vertical distance from the target's Y coordinate is greater than 1.875 tiles (or 1 tile when it mine alongside the player and its target is a block).
The Cattiva minion only deals damage during its claw swipe animation, which happens when they are less than 1.25 tiles from the target position and lasts for 0.27 seconds.
This means that if Cattiva on the ground are below the target buttom by less than 1.875 tiles but more than 1.25 tiles, they will neither attack nor jump, and will instead keep following the target.
The Cattiva minion will use a double jump approach its target when the following conditions are met:
It is falling, with a falling speed greater than 5 mph.
It is not in liquid.
It is below the target, with its bottom more than 6.25 tiles away from the target's Y coordinate.
When Trusty Cattiva sticks to enemy, its maximum speed is 102 mph, but its maximum descent speed is still 51 mph.
The Cattiva minion applies 9 ticks of local invincibility frames on hit, meaning it can hit for up to 6.67 times per second.
When the For the Worthy seed is active, Cattiva takes half as many hits (rounded up) to break blocks, trees and cacti.
The Traveling Merchant sells the Pal Metal set if the player has Cattiva, Foxparks, Chillet, Chillet Ignis, Digtoise, or their "Trusty" variants in the inventory or in any portable storage item when speaking to him.


== Tips ==

To increase the chances of finding Cattiva or Foxparks, the player may construct a long row of Snow or Ice Blocks for them to spawn on. The player can also use a Water Candle and Battle Potion, and create an artificial Jungle biome (see Guide:Artificial biomes) nearby to increase spawn rates. Luck will increase the chance to spawn Foxparks instead of Cattiva, meaning items that decrease luck, such as the Raven Feather, Wilted Clover, or Pretty Mirror can also help with spawning of Cattiva, as can being under the Stinky debuff. Note that they only spawn during daytime on Surface.
Grass or Jungle grass may also be used for the spawning platform, but they are less ideal, as grass may result in unwanted King Slime spawns while in the outer sixths of world, and Jungle grass reduces the spawn chance of Pals due to Jungle enemies spawning on it.
It can be helpful to construct this farm directly above the Ocean, since the Ocean naturally provides a large empty area, meaning the player will not have to worry about enemies spawning in unwanted spots and reducing the efficiency of the farm.
Additionally, enemies can spawn on-screen while the player is near the world border, making it easier to notice the Pals after they spawn.
Luck can be completely disregarded after obtaining one of them, as the one not owned by the player is guaranteed to spawn.
While the Goblin Archers that spawn alongside it are alive, the music will change to the Goblin Army theme. This makes it easier to know when a Pal is nearby, even if one lacks the Lifeform Analyzer.
Whether the Goblin Army has been defeated has no bearing on the spawning of the distressed Cattiva. It can spawn prior to defeating the event and continues to do so afterward.
Cattiva acts similar to a pre-Hardmode version of the Blade Staff, in that both weapons have an incredibly fast rate of attacking. Thus, it tends to work well with whips that have high tag damage such as the Spinal Tap, or when the player has increased armor penetration when using the Shark Tooth Necklace.
Cattiva's mining ability can be detrimental in certain scenarios, namely when trying to dig near lava or building.


== Trivia ==

While the player is wearing Sunglasses, Cattiva will appear to wear them as well.
This pair of Sunglasses is achieved by stacking two sprites of player-equipped Sunglasses: .
The way to obtain Cattiva is a reference to camps guarded by hostile NPCs in Palworld, where Pals are locked in cages, waiting to be rescued.
When attacking or mining, Cattiva will create visual sparkle effects.


== See also ==
Cattiva at the Palworld Wiki


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: 
The distressed Pal event now guarantees the pal the player have yet to obtain.
The distressed Pal event is now 25% more common.
Distressed Cattiva now takes 5 damage from all hits, and should have a fair chance to be saved in higher difficulties.
Can now be upgraded into its "Trusty" variant using a Kinship Peach, from crafting.
Increased damage from 9 to 11.
Invincibility frames between attacks increased from 8 to 9 ticks.
Can now jump in mid-air.
Cattiva now refuses to sit on the shoulders of players that are rotating.
Desktop 1.4.5.3: 
Improved spawn rates from 1/300 (0.33%) to 1/200 (0.5%).
Balanced the ratio from 70% Cattiva and 30% Foxparks to 60% Cattiva and 40% Foxparks.

Console 1.4.5: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.5: Introduced.

title: Dye Trader
content:
The Dye Trader is an NPC vendor who sells the Dye Vat and other dye-related items. He will move in when the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
The player has a dye, dye plant, Strange Plant, or Dye Vat in their inventory, and at least four other town NPCs are in the world. Note that while the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Dye Trader is killed, he will automatically respawn after some time.
Once Hardmode has been reached, players may trade Strange Plants with the Dye Trader for uncraftable and unpurchasable animated dyes. These dyes are given at random in sets of 6 for each exchanged Strange Plant.
The Dye Trader will defend himself against nearby enemies with his Exotic Scimitar. He deals 11 / 16 / 19 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Dye Trader also has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping the Exotic Scimitar upon death.


== Items sold ==


== Strange Plant quests ==
Speaking to the Dye Trader in Hardmode will show the "Strange Plants" quest, in which the Dye Trader asks players to fetch him rare plants. In return, he rewards players with 6 vials of a special dye that mostly cannot be obtained otherwise. More of these dyes become available as the game progresses.


=== Rewards ===


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Dye Trader will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Names ==
The Dye Trader may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
Ahirom, Abdosir, Hiram, and Batnoam are the names of ancient Phoenician kings and queens. Phoenicia was an east Mediterranean empire that became wealthy from the purple dye extracted from coastal snails, and Sea Snails drop the ingredient for Purple Dye.
Hanno is the name of a Carthaginian explorer from the 5th century BC, who is known for his naval exploration of the western coast of Africa.
One of his quotes mentions that he sells "the richest colors"; however, he only sells 7 dyes, one of them only on multiplayer.
The Dye Trader's sprite was created by former Re-Logic artist Waffles. In 1.3.0.1, it was updated by Lazure.
The Dye Trader's comments about Rich Mahogany have been confirmed by Cenx to be a reference to the Anchorman film series.
Even if the player is wearing the Dye Trader's own attire, he still criticizes their clothes.

Despite it being hidden under his turban, the Dye Trader's hair is observed to be black, which can be seen when it is removed during a Party in favor of a party hat.
His persona is heavily inspired by stereotypes of early Middle Eastern and North African culture, as seen by his clothing (turban), his drops (Exotic Scimitar), and references to a sultan in his quotes.
As seen in his quotes, he is greedy and looks down on monotone robes.
 The Bestiary entry for the Dye Trader: "Eccentric and rather snobby to a fault, the Dye Trader has expensive tastes. He is passionate about the materials used in the dyes he sells."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Now sells Easter Blocks.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Now rewards 6 vials of the quest reward dye after turning in a Strange Plant instead of 3.
NPCs who die will now respawn freely, ignoring the original unique conditions which were required to spawn in the first place.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
The option to exchange Strange Plants for dyes now requires Hardmode.
Defeating pre-Hardmode bosses is no longer part of the spawn requirements. Now instead always requires at least four other town NPCs (in addition to having a dye, dye plant, Strange Plant, or Dye Vat in the inventory).
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Added the Strange Plants quest.
Having a Strange Plant in the inventory now fulfills the spawn requirement. Otherwise, if the player has no Strange Plant in the inventory but has a dye, dye plant, or Dye Vat, there is now an additional spawn requirement: Any of the major pre-Hardmode bosses (Eye of Cthulhu, Skeletron, or Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu) must have been defeated.
Now defends himself with an Exotic Scimitar.
Now sells Dye Trader's Turban, Shadow Dye, Negative Dye, and Brown Dye.
Sprite updated.

title: Birdie Rattle
content:
The Birdie Rattle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Lil' Harpy that follows the player. It will never land and can fly through blocks. The Birdie Rattle can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Gold.

title: Prismatic Lacewing
content:
The Prismatic Lacewing is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera flying critter and boss-summoning item that spawns on the surface Hallow after Plantera has been defeated. Prismatic Lacewings disappear almost instantaneously when spawned in any other biome, and only spawn in the Hallow between dusk (7:30 PM) and midnight (12:00 AM). When killed by a player, it summons the Empress of Light; death from non-player sources will generally not result in summoning. Only one Prismatic Lacewing can be naturally spawned at a time.
The Prismatic Lacewing can be caught with Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, and Golden Bug Net. Releasing it from the inventory (with ⚒ Use / Attack) and killing it will still summon the Empress of Light.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.


== Crafting ==


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
Unlike other critters, the Prismatic Lacewing cannot regenerate health when damaged, nor will it take damage from other enemies.
While the Empress of Light is alive, killing more than one Prismatic Lacewing at once will not summon additional copies of the boss.
The Prismatic Lacewing will despawn almost immediately if released outside of the Hallow, but can still be killed to summon the Empress of Light if done fast enough or if placed directly onto a damaging projectile, such as with the Spiky Ball, Clinger Staff, Rainbow Gun, or a Phaseblade/Phasesaber.
Prismatic Lacewings will only spawn on Hallowed grass (not including its mowed variant), Pearlstone Blocks, Pearlsand Blocks, and Pink Ice Blocks.
A Prismatic Lacewing can only be damaged by a player if they are close enough; it will appear translucent if the player is far away. This is likely done to prevent accidentally summoning the Empress of Light while the Prismatic Lacewing is off-screen.
If the Prismatic Lacewing takes damage from a player but is killed by another projectile (e.g. from a trap), the Empress of Light will still spawn.
Fallen Stars count as player damage for this purpose, hence the boss will be summoned if the Prismatic Lacewing is hit by a Fallen Star.
If the Prismatic Lacewing only takes damage from non-player sources, the boss will not be summoned.
In Remix worlds, the Prismatic Lacewing can spawn at any time of day.
The Prismatic Lacewing emits light.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Using a Bug Net, it can be kept in the player's inventory to later release it at a more appropriate time, such as to fight the Empress of Light when better prepared.
The Guide to Critter Companionship (or its upgrade, the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence) can be helpful to prevent accidentally summoning the Empress of Light.
It is recommended that the player remember to deactivate the Guide to Critter Companionship before attempting to summon the boss.
Using a Battle Potion and Water Candle increases its spawn rate, like enemies.
Similarly, because it is considered an enemy, its spawn rate is increased during the Blood Moon event and can be easily farmed using a Bloody Tear.
Building a platform roughly 35 tiles above a Hallow biome while under the influence of a Water Candle, the player can expect 3–8 Lacewings to spawn, provided they are there from 7:30 PM to 12:00 AM.
If the player does not have a surface Hallowed biome in their world, Holy Water or a Clentaminator with Blue Solution can be used to create one.
Spreading out sentry weapons and using summons with long range such as the Sanguine Staff can quickly clear the mob cap to allow more Prismatic Lacewings to spawn.


== Trivia ==
The Windy Balloon(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Lunatic Devotee, Truffle Worm, and Prismatic Lacewing are the only entities classified as an "enemy" that otherwise deal absolutely no damage to the player.
Contrary to their behavior as butterflies in-game, real-life lacewings are not butterflies, but are more genetically similar to mantisflies and antlions.
 The Bestiary entry for the Prismatic Lacewing: "Should one of these luminescent beings perish in the chaos of night, a sleeping tyrant is rumored to violently awaken."


== See also ==
Butterflies
Truffle Worms, another critter that is used for boss summoning.

Stack limit increased from 999 to 9999.
Spawn rates are now impacted by Luck.
