title: Legacy:Guide:The Twins strategies
content:
The Twins are the Hardmode version of the Eye of Cthulhu. They are the mid-boss of the hardmode bosses, stronger than The Destroyer but weaker than Skeletron Prime.


== Terrain preparation ==
The sky is a must when battling the Twins, as they must be dodged often.

A very long Sky Bridge (if possible made out of Asphalt or Frozen Slime Blocks) is optimal. Continuously running with Spectre/Lightning Boots causes both of the Twins to miss you with their projectiles very often, and keeps each Twin at a stationary horizontal position most of the time, allowing you to fire backward continuously at it. Wings will help dodge each of the Twins' second phases. When one Twin enters its second phase, defeat it before activating the other Twin's second phase. Using Asphalt can negate the need for Lightning Boots. Using Asphalt with Lightning or Frostspark Boots can allow you to avoid taking damage completely.
The standard Boss arena of several layers of wood platforms may be of use, though a skybridge would be preferred, as it allows firing and maneuvering in any direction. A solid ceiling just above your top platform will block Retinazer's beam attacks, as Retinazer always flanks from above.
If your arena is relatively small, hook up any heart statues and star statues you might have, with a 1 or 5 second timer. A minimum of three should be enough to keep you alive until the end of the fight. Bring mana/health potions to be safe.
Also, a wall on both sides of a small area can block Spazmatism's cursed fire, but be careful not to run out of time from covering behind the wall. It is helpful to have a one block hole one block up to shoot through. This is more useful if you want to try tanking the boss with the above tip of heart statues. If you can tank the hits with the help of heart statues, you can gun down Retinazer while Spazmatism is only able to charge at you.
If you have access to Gravitation Potions, this can easily eliminate the need for an arena, although the player's view flips instead of the player character (as of 1.2), this may make the battle very confusing.


== Gearing up ==


=== Armor ===
Adamantite armor or Titanium armor should be used (or Hallowed armor from another mechanical boss). The defensive set bonus should generally be used, though those confident in their dodging ability may opt for the ranged bonus for extra damage. The frost set can be used it provides good defense and inflicts the frostburn debuff


=== Weapons ===
By this time you should have a reasonable amount of money, so you may want to invest some of it into modifiers for your weapons.

The Adamantite Repeater with Cursed Arrows or Frostburn Arrows is the optimal weapon for players who have yet to beat any Hardmode boss.
If you have beaten The Destroyer or have gotten lucky with Angry Trappers and in a Crimson world, the Megashark or Uzi with Ichor Bullets or Cursed Bullets are very highly effective ways to beat the twins if you're good at aiming.
The Sharanga with Wooden Arrows will be very useful as well, as it turns Wooden Arrow into Spectral Arrow, severely hurting the eyes.
The Megashark with Crystal Bullets is optimal if The Destroyer has already been defeated. Many of the Crystal Bullets' secondary shards will hit The Twins, causing much quicker damage than any other projectile.
Other weapons that work quite well are the Clockwork Assault Rifle with Crystal Bullets, because it has reasonable damage and a good range, and the Star Cannon, if you have enough ammo saved up. Even the Phoenix Blaster with Meteor Shot can be a viable weapon, provided that armors with ranged bonuses are being used, and the player is reasonably accurate.
The Clockwork Assault Rifle or the Gatligator can be reasonably useful with Exploding Bullets. Just keep your distance. Crystal bullets work well as well.
For magic users, the Laser Rifle is an effective magic weapon due to its fast firing speed, if you are lucky enough for it to drop from the Wall of Flesh. Cursed Flames is also a good idea because both Twins are vulnerable to Cursed Inferno. The Frost Staff is even better. Alternatively the Crystal Storm is an effective magic weapon that can be crafted before challenging any of the Hardmode bosses. Another good weapon for your first time facing the twins is the Unholy Trident . If you have crimson, a good idea is the get the Golden Shower , because The Twins are vulnerable to the Ichor.
For melee users, the Ice Sickle and the Death Sickle could also be used, as Spazmatism will spend most of the time behind you, so shooting constantly backwards with the piercing projectile will hit him multiple times and deal quite reasonable damage. Retinazer can then be taken down with the Light Discs or the Ice Sickle while he is behind the player, charging.


=== Accessories ===
Accessories that improve mobility are a must, since the Twins use quick attacks. 

The Spectre Boots and Wings are a must, especially for the Sky Bridge method. They allow the player to dodge, and also allow the player to flee temporarily if health is running low.
The Obsidian Shield, the Cobalt Shield and Ankh Shield will prevent knockback.
The Charm of Myths is more helpful than you might think, as it provides a good health regeneration and reduced cooldown of healing potions, greatly increasing your healing potential.
The Cross Necklace or Star Veil is another good choice, as the Twins' frequent ramming moves deal a lot of rapid damage, and the extra period of invulnerability mitigates a significant portion of this damage.
The Moon Charm is very helpful if melee is to be used, as it will give a minor boost to all stats, raising your defense and therefore survivability, and also giving higher damage, so the fight can be completed faster.
If possible, reforge all Accessories for damage or defense bonuses. If money is no object (see Guide:Making Money#Useful Glitches), having all Accessories reforged to Warding or Menacing provides an extra 20 defense or 20% damage.


=== Potions ===
At least seven Greater Healing Potions. Ten to be safe; this will be more than enough for any Twins fight.
Regeneration Potion and Ironskin Potion will help prevent fatal damage. Two of each will likely cover the entire night.
One Pumpkin Pie will likely last the entire fight, and it's easy to craft.
Gravitation Potion can be especially useful, as it eliminates the need for any arena and may free up an accessory slot (keep in mind you will need to prevent fall damage yourself when the potion wears off, if you unequip the Wings). Three of these will last the entire fight.
Swiftness Potion helps you evade the twins. Two should last the entire fight.
If you have access to a Crystal Ball, activate it just before the fight. It will likely last the entire fight.
If you have access to a world with Corruption on PC, a Wrath Potion is a good bonus, but not necessary.
For magic users, a Magic Power Potion is also a good substitute for Wrath Potions.
Because the Twins are vulnerable to many debuffs, melee players can take great advantage of Flasks. The Flask of Ichor greatly increases the damage output of melee weapons, and the Flasks of Poison, Fire, and Cursed Flames will tack on even more damage.


== The Battle ==
The Twins, as the name suggest, are two separate monsters, both of which must be defeated. They have a combined health of 43,000, shared between them. Retinazer, distinguished by its red iris, fires lasers. Spazmatism, distinguished by its green iris, fires cursed flames. When reduced to less than half health, they will transform, gaining a slight boost in offense and defense. They will not both transform at the same time; both must be reduced to half health for each to transform. When one is destroyed, the other will continue attacking in the same pattern. It is a great idea to take them out one at a time, because if they both end up in their second forms at the same time it can be very difficult to defeat them.


=== Retinazer ===
In its first form, Retinazer will fire lasers at the player at a steady but somewhat slow rate. This is occasionally interrupted by charging attacks, which mirror that of its partner. Retinazer does slightly less damage than Spazmatism, but this is offset by its higher accuracy thanks to the speed of the lasers. When not charging, Retinazer will always be aligned vertically with the player, positioned above them, which makes its shots easy to block with a solid ceiling.
When it changes into its second form, Retinazer will no longer engage in charge attacks. Instead, its lasers will fire with increasing frequency as it loses health. This is occasionally supplemented by a weaker but much more rapid laser attack that tracks extremely well. To avoid this, try to fall as fast as you can (Preferably without fall damage), and you can be left unscratched. With wings it is possible to "zig-zag" up and down to dodge the lasers. This is made trickier as the fight goes on, with Retinazer using more rapid and fast lasers that are therefore harder to dodge.


=== Spazmatism ===
Spazmatism, like Retinazer, varies between firing cursed flames from a distance and engaging in charging attacks. The flames do more damage than the lasers, but aren't as fast and thus easier to dodge. Spazmatism is always aligned horizontally with the player. The Spazmatizm would continuously shoot cursed flames at the player every second for about 8 seconds before slowly firing to 10-15 seconds per shot.
Spazmatism's second form changes his attack pattern dramatically compared to Retinazer. Its cursed flame attack becomes a constant stream of flame, which will last for several seconds. However, it doesn't chase the player quite as quickly as it does in its first form, making avoiding the attack somewhat easier. Once it stops spewing flame, it will charge with greatly increased speed, which also does a lot more damage. Dodging these charges is quite difficult. Much like Retinazer, fall as fast as you can while he is charging, and you should be okay. Misdirecting Spazmatism's charges is easier than it sounds; if you jump as he slows down, he will charge over you. This causes Spazmatism to charge at you from either above or below, making him easier to dodge if you just run.
Another tactic if in multiplayer is to have one player fly around him, distracting him while another fires arrows or bullets at him. (More effective once Retinazer is defeated)


=== Which to Defeat First ===
Defeating Retinazer first:
Pros:
Retinazer has a ranged attack, and defeating this Twin first will assist players who are bad at dodging, afraid of lasers, or have a relatively low movement speed.
Cons:
Retinazer has many, many lasers to dodge, and, in addition, if you are a slow player, can be the more deadly of the two Twins to fight.
Defeating Spazmatism first: 
Pros:
Damage from Cursed Inferno can easily add up, so if you defeat him first, you won't have to deal with that for as long.
Cons:
If you are a melee player (unless you have a melee weapon that shoots a beam such as the True Night's Edge), or slow, dodging the flamethrower vomit is potentially deadly.


== Tips ==
Both Eyes, while not charging attack the player, stay in specific position relative to the player. And weapons such as Nimbus Rod are very useful, if combined with good tanking armor. The positions  are:
Retinazer's first form will stay in either diagonally to the East or West  from the player while not charging attack.
Retinazer's second form will stay directly above the player while normal attack.
Retinazer's second form rapid attack will stay at the east/west to the player, slightly moving vertically.
Spazmatism, in both forms will stay horizontally to the east or west of the player at normal attack.

title: Queen Slime
content:
Queen Slime is an early-Hardmode, Hallow-themed boss. Fighting Queen Slime is not required for game progression – much like her pre-Hardmode counterpart, King Slime – but her defeat may reward the player with useful items.
While Queen Slime is alive, her exclusive music Queen Slime will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning ==
Queen Slime is summoned by using a Gelatin Crystal in The Hallow or Underground Hallow, at any time.


== Behavior ==
The Queen Slime fight consists of two phases. In the first phase she behaves somewhat similarly to King Slime, hopping towards the player to deal contact damage (albeitmore quickly than King Slime) and teleporting to the player's location when unable to reach them. However, she also has two new attacks, where she tries to crush the player with a Queenly Smash, or fires a spread of bouncy Regal Gel projectiles. Additionally, she summons slime minions to aid her in the fight. Upon reaching 50% of her maximum health (9,000 / 14,400 / 18,360), she grows large wings and begins flying above the player while passing through blocks. She can still summon slime minions in this phase and use her Queenly Smash and Regal Gel attacks, albeit in a different manner, but will no longer teleport.
If the player dies or if the horizontal distance of the player from Queen Slime is greater than 500 tiles, she begins moving away from the player (by jumping in first phase or flying in second phase) and despawns in 0.17 seconds once she is off-screen.


=== First phase ===


==== Main attacks ====
Queen Slime has three main attacks which are chosen randomly, meaning she may use the same attack several times in a row or alternate between different attacks. After finishing each attack, she stays still for 1 second before starting her next attack.

Quick Jumps: Queen Slime performs a series of four quick jumps towards the player with varying heights. She stays on ground for 0.17 seconds after the first, second and third jumps, however this is reduced to 0.08 seconds when she is below 66% of her maximum health (11,880 / 19,008 / 24,235). Queen Slime performs these jumps in a set pattern:
Performs a normal jump, reaching a maximum height of 6.42 tiles.
Performs another normal jump.
Performs a low jump, reaching a maximum height of 3.56 tiles.
Performs a high jump, reaching a maximum height of 17.2 tiles.
Regal Gel: Queen Slime stays still and charges energy within her crystal for 1 second, before firing a spread of six Regal Gel projectiles that are affected by gravity, and can bounce off solid blocks once before dissipating. The first projectile is fired directly to right of the Queen Slime, and the next ones are each rotated 36° counter clockwise.
Queenly Smash: Queen Slime stays still for 0.5 seconds, then leaps toward the player while passing through blocks and attempts to position herself above them, with the exact height and orientation of the leap varying based on her distance to the player. 0.5 seconds after her leap, she briefly pauses midair for another 0.5 seconds, and then slams directly downwards, creating a shockwave upon contact with solid blocks that deals damage within a 30×30-tile square area centered on the point of impact.


==== Teleporting ====
Queen Slime can teleport to the player under the following two circumstances:

The line of sight between Queen Slime and the player is obstructed by solid blocks.
The player's feet are more than 20 tiles below or above the top of Queen Slime's hitbox.
As soon as either of these conditions is met, a counter begins increasing at a rate of 1.5 per second, starting from 0. If neither of the two conditions is met, the counter will instead decrease at a rate of 1 per second (down to a minimum of 0). When the counter reaches 500, Queen Slime teleports to the player's location. If it reaches 0 while Queen Slime is jumping, the teleportation is delayed until she lands on the ground. Afterwards, the counter resets back to 0.
In order to teleport to the player, Queen Slime tries to find a suitable target location with the following steps:

If the total distance between Queen Slime and the player is greater than 125 tiles, she will teleport directly on top of the player, even if they are midair.
Otherwise, she tries to find a valid block to teleport on that is 7–10 tiles (Chebyshev distance) away from the player's center.
A block is considered valid for teleporting if it is an unactuated solid block (including platforms, but not planter boxes), does not contain lava, and if the tile above it is not occupied by any unactuated, unsloped solid blocks (including platforms and planter boxes). Additionally, Queen Slime is required to have an unobstructed line of sight to the player after teleporting there.
If the previous step fails, then she tries to find a valid block to teleport on that is 2–6 tiles (Chebyshev distance) away from the player's center.
If all of the previous steps fail, then she will teleport directly on top of the player, even if they are midair.
Once the target location is chosen, Queen Slime stays still, disappears over the course of 1 second, and then reappears at the target location over the course of 0.5 seconds. She immediately starts a random main attack after teleporting.


==== Spawning slimes ====
Queen Slime can spawn 1–2 slime minions from her body upon taking damage, with the type of each slime being randomly selected out of the following 3 options:

Crystal Slimes, which fire one / three gravity-affected crystal spike projectiles at the player every 0.83 seconds / 0.67 seconds. However, its Expert Mode fire rate is used only if there are fewer than 4 other Crystal Slimes alive. In Classic Mode the crystal spikes are aimed at the player, while in Expert Mode they are shot in tall, vertical arcs above the Crystal Slime with lower horizontal range compared to those fired by Spiked Ice Slimes, Spiked Jungle Slimes, and Spiked Slimes.
Bouncy Slimes, which fire pink bouncy gel projectiles at the player once every 0.67 seconds / 0.5 seconds that can bounce off blocks twice before dissipating.
Heavenly Slimes, which fly towards the player in an attempt to deal contact damage, similarly to a Slimer.
At the beginning of the fight, Queen Slime can spawn slimes upon taking any hit that brings her below 98% health. Afterwards, she needs to lose at least 2% of her maximum health (360 / 576 / 734 health) compared to her health at the last time she spawned slimes before she can spawn them again, with this process repeating. For example, bringing her to exactly 17,639 / 28,223 / 35,984 (98%) health causes her to spawn slimes for the first time, after which she will not spawn new slimes until brought to below 17,279 / 27,647 / 35,250 (96%) health.
As a result, Queen Slime has a maximum of 24 opportunities to spawn slimes in her first phase, meaning 24-48 slimes in total, or 36 slimes on average. This number will be lower if any of Queen Slime's slime-spawning opportunities are skipped by reducing her health by more than 2% of her maximum health in a single hit.


=== Second phase ===


==== Main attacks ====
When Queen Slime reaches 50% of her maximum health (9,000 / 14,400 / 18,360), she grows a pair of large wings and begins to fly. She attempts to stay 15 tiles above the player, and gains the ability to pass through blocks. Queen Slime can no longer jump or teleport in this phase, but can still use her Regal Gel and Queenly Smash attacks in a different manner, which are chosen randomly. After finishing each attack, she waits for 2 seconds before starting her next attack.

Regal Gel: Queen Slime charges energy within her crystal for 1 second, before firing a spread of ten Regal Gel projectiles that are affected by gravity, and can bounce off solid blocks once before dissipating. The first projectile is fired directly to right of the Queen Slime, and the next ones are each rotated 36° counter clockwise.
Queenly Smash: Queen Slime pauses in place for 0.17 seconds, then slams directly downwards, creating a shockwave upon contact with solid blocks that deals damage within a 30×30-tile square area centered on the point of impact. If she falls for more than 2 seconds without hitting solid blocks, she will cancel the attack early. This attack can be only performed if she is above the player and the horizontal distance between player's center and Queen Slime's center is less than 15.625 tiles, otherwise she defaults back to the Regal Gel attack.


==== Spawning slimes ====
Similar to the first phase, Queen Slime can spawn 1-2 slime minions from her body upon taking damage, which can be either Crystal Slimes, Bouncy Slimes, or Heavenly Slimes. However, she only needs to lose 1.5% of her maximum health (270 / 432 / 550 health) compared to her health at the last time she summoned slimes before she can spawn them again.
As a result, Queen Slime has a maximum of 33 opportunities to spawn slimes in her second phase, meaning 33-66 slimes in total, or 49 slimes on average. This number will be lower if any of Queen Slime's slime-spawning opportunities are skipped by reducing her health by more than 1.5% of her maximum health in a single hit.


== Aftermath ==
If King Slime has already been defeated, the Princess will begin selling Royal Romance.
The Queen Slime emote  is unlocked.


== Notes ==
The Royal Gel does not make players immune to the slimes she summons.
Despite being a Hardmode boss, developer items cannot be obtained from Queen Slime's Treasure Bag.
While the boss needs to be summoned in The Hallow, the fight can take place anywhere, and she does not enrage outside of the biome. This means the player can go into a different biome once the fight starts and the fight will continue as normal.
Unlike King Slime, the Queen Slime requires leaving the screen to despawn after killing all players in the world. She may not be able to despawn during her first form if solid blocks prevent her from leaving the screen, and when this happens the fight can be continued after a player respawns.
Queen Slime herself and Regal Gel projectiles are slowed down by liquids. In the Queen's second phase, she is no longer affected by liquids unless she is trying to stomp the player.
The Bouncy Slimes and Crystal Slimes will not fire projectiles while they are floating on liquids, like most other slimes.
In worlds with the For the Worthy seed active, the Queen Slime receives the following AI changes:
Her horizontal speed during low and normal jumps is increased, allowing her to cover more distance with jumps (low jumps: 23 mph → 37 mph, normal jumps: 20 mph → 37 mph).
She fires 15 Regal Gel projectiles in her second phase instead of 10. Additionally, the spacing between projectiles in both phases is reduced from 36° to 24°.
She no longer pauses for a short time before slamming down during her Queenly Smash attack.
When slamming down during her Queenly Smash attack, her acceleration is increased by 100% and her top falling speed is increased by 14.2%.
Defeating Queen Slime is not required for the Slayer of Worlds achievement.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

The Dart Pistol or Dart Rifle combined with Crystal Darts can make quick work of her minions as well as damage her multiple times per dart.
Palladium armor can be useful due to the Rapid Healing buff it provides.
Queen Slime herself has a relatively simple attack pattern. Half the threat comes from the minions she spawns, which can fill the screen with projectiles and quickly overwhelm the player. Killing or avoiding these should be a top priority.
Stay in the air using wings or mounts during her first phase, as many of her attacks cannot reach the player there. During her second phase, the player should stay closer to the ground while occasionally luring her back up, as they can avoid many of her projectiles and minions due to their slow and predictable movement patterns.
In Master Mode, The Black Spot mount allows the player to hover above all attacks in the first phase.
Fight Queen Slime in daylight, since her attacks may be hard to see at night.
Queen Slime can be killed easily before any other Hardmode bosses, and even before destroying Demon or Crimson Altars. The Crystal Assassin armor she drops will help the player survive in early Hardmode.
Like most bosses, she is immune to lava, but her minions are not. An arena made of lava paired with Lava Waders or Terraspark Boots can make the fight significantly easier.
Another effective strategy against her minions is to try to inflict multiple damaging debuffs at once. A good example of this is using the Shadowflame Knife paired with Frost armor and a Flask of Cursed Flames, as the three debuffs are often enough to finish off any of the slimes, even if only one knife hits.
For magic users, the Life Drain is a very good choice for this fight. Because it deals continuous damage around the cursor, this allows the player to consistently damage the boss while focusing on dodging. Since the minions spawn from the center of the boss, it will deal some damage to them right as they spawn. In addition, the player gains a boost to their life regeneration while damaging an enemy.
Use several disconnected platforms, which can allow her minions to fall down and away from the fight.
Any wings paired with flight-boosting accessories and the Shield of Cthulhu (for its dash ability) makes dodging most of her attacks easy (but does not take care of her minions).
The Daedalus Stormbow paired with Holy Arrows and summoned minions can take care of her minions.
When fighting her in higher difficulties, never remain directly above multiple Crystal Slimes. Their spikes can kill the player in seconds.
Invisibility Potions can be used to decrease spawn rates of other enemies and prevent the Heavenly Slimes from chasing after the player. Note that taking any damage will instantly cancel the buff, however.


== Trivia ==
Queen Slime's AI was created entirely by developer Grox The Great, while the visual effect was created by Yoraiz0r.Verify
The feather covered in pink slime on her trophy resembles the sword covered in slime from King Slime's trophy.
Queen Slime was one of the two bosses added in the 1.4 update, along with the Empress of Light. Both are Hallow-themed.
The Queen is centered on the Hallow's crystal theme while the Empress composes the Hallow's rainbow theme, as seen by the colors of their summon items, their attacks, and the exclusive items they drop.
Queen Slime is one of the three bosses whose map icon does not change upon entering their second form, the others being the Brain of Cthulhu and the Santa-NK1.
Most of Queen Slime's drops are upgraded versions of King Slime's drops. Both the Ninja armor and Crystal Assassin armor are feudal Japanese-themed sets that do not favor a specific class. Each boss also drops a mount-summoning item (Slimy Saddle and Gelatinous Pillion), a hook (Slime Hook and Hook of Dissonance), and a novelty weapon (Slime Gun and Sparkle Slime Balloon).
Unlike most boss loot drops, the Hook of Dissonance's drop chance is not affected by luck, and so will always drop with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance. This might be because the Hook of Dissonance is Queen Slime's counterpart to King Slime's Slime Hook: The latter is also unaffected by luck, because if the Slime Hook does not drop, the Slime Gun will drop.
The Volatile Gelatin also shares a resemblance to the Royal Gel, both being the Expert Mode drops for Queen Slime and King Slime respectively and being crowns similar to that of the respective bosses covered in gel. However, this is purely an aesthetic difference and the two have completely different uses.
The wings of her second form resemble an oversized pair of Angel Wings.
The Queen Slime's crown gore that appears upon her death is different from the King Slime's crown gore. While the King's crown appears when Blood and Gore is on, the Queen's does not.
This is likely because not only does her crown drop on death, but her wings also drop.
 The Bestiary entry for  Queen Slime: "Hallowed slimes consolidated into a haughty, crushing force adorned in dazzling crystals. She is rumored to grow wings."


== Gallery ==

		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Can now teleport to platforms.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Maximum flight speed and acceleration in Phase 2 have been reduced by about 15%.
Now takes up more enemy slots, reducing or outright eliminating additional enemy spawns during her fight (not including her own minions).
Desktop 1.4.1: Now drops the Blade Staff.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: Fixed an NPC smoothing issue.
Desktop 1.4.0.3: Fixed bug where more than one could be summoned at once.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

title: Tiki Totem
content:
The Tiki Totem is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiki Spirit that floats and spins above the player's head. Unlike most pets, it will not teleport to the player when the player moves too quickly for it to keep up; it will simply float straight towards the player. The Tiki Totem can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 2 Platinum when he is spoken to in the Jungle biome during Hardmode.


== Notes ==
If it is equipped alongside the Wisp in a Bottle, both pets overlap each other while the player is not moving.


== Trivia ==
The Tiki Spirit is likely a reference to the character Aku Aku from the Crash Bandicoot video game franchise.

title: Guide:Deerclops strategies
content:
Deerclops is a pre-Hardmode boss. It is not required to be killed to progress the game, but it drops several Don't Starve-themed items, such as the useful pet item Eye Bone or the Houndius Shootius sentry-summoning weapon.


== Spawning ==
Deerclops can be spawned using the Deer Thing in the Snow biome, crafted from 3 Flinx Fur, 5 Demonite or Crimtane Ore, and a Lens, or found in Frozen Chests. Deerclops also naturally spawns at exactly midnight during a Blizzard in the Snow biome if one player has either 9 defense or 200 health. Despite being summoned or being naturally spawned in the Snow Biome, it can be fought at any biome after being summoned. While the boss can spawn at any point, it is not recommended to fight it until the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu has been defeated.


== The Fight ==
Deerclops has four attacks:
If it is close to the player, Deerclops will smash the ground, summoning a wave of Ice Spikes that quickly travels towards the player. Every third consecutive wave does not go as far, instead spreading in both directions. Ice Spikes freeze the player briefly.
If it is not close enough to its target to use the Ice Spikes attack, Deerclops will "scoop" and then throw numerous chunks of Debris into the air that fall back down. These chunks can pass through blocks.
Deerclops will occasionally stand in place and roar, inflicting the Slow debuff on all players within 50 tiles for 12 / 24 / 30 seconds, unless they are already affected by the debuff.
If the player is above Deerclops for enough time, five Shadow Hands will be summoned around the player.
Deerclops cannot pass through solid blocks, but if the player is above it, far enough away, and Deerclops cannot reach them, it will quickly rise through the blocks to reach the player.
If the player is more than 30 tiles away, Deerclops will turn a dark shade of purple, two reddish, semi-transparent images of Deerclops will begin spinning around it, and it becomes immune to all damage.
If all players are dead or there are none nearby, Deerclops will wander around instead of immediately despawning. This will happen until a player gets close to the boss, at which point the fight will resume as normal. Once one in-game day (24 real-world minutes) has passed since Deerclops's spawn, it will despawn as soon as no players are near. Leaving and re-entering the world will also cause it to despawn.


=== Expert Mode ===
Deerclops now has a fifth attack:

Shadow Hands will be periodically summoned that either move forwards slowly, move forwards quickly and curve, or spin in place. Shadow Hands are summoned more frequently as Deerclops's life gets lower. Shadow Hands predict the player's movements.


== General strategies ==


=== General tips ===


=== Terrain preparation ===
It is recommended to clear a large flat area in the Snow biome.
One or two layers of platforms is enough since Deerclops follows the player if they are 30 blocks away, passing through blocks and being immune to attacks. 


== Gearing up ==
It's recommended to have at least 260–280 health before you attempt to fight Deerclops. If using magic weapons, having the max amount of mana is recommended.


=== Armor ===
A full set of at least Gold or Platinum armor should be acquired, but better armor is always an option. Other armor sets with set bonuses can be effective as well.
Fossil armor is the best set available for rangers, the Gi can be used in place of the chestplate if ammo conservation is not a concern.
Crimson armor is good for tanking hits due to the high defense and increased regeneration.
Shadow armor gives a boost to mobility and a increased crit chance for all weapons.
The Wizard set, with magic-boosting or defense-boosting leg armor, provides the most damage for magic users. If defense is preferred, Jungle armor or Meteor armor can be used.
Meteor armor's set bonus can make the Space Gun and Gray Zapinator much more effective against Deerclops since it reduces Space Gun's and Gray Zapinator's mana usage to 0.
Obsidian armor is the best summoner armor set at this point in the game which focuses on whip bonuses.
Bee armor is an alternative set if Queen Bee has been defeated and focuses on minion bonuses.
Molten armor is the best pre-Hardmode armor set for melee classes, although it requires a visit to the Underworld and a pickaxe that can mine Hellstone.


=== Weapons ===
For melee users:

For swords, a solid choice would be the Blade of Grass or Bee Keeper.
The Volcano  deals high damage, and inflicts On Fire!, making it the ideal sword for this fight.
The Terragrim performs excellently if acquired, especially if you stand under Deerclops and swing up towards his torso.
The Starfury does high damage at a range with its falling stars.
The Flamarang can deal very high damage to Deerclops at a safer distance than most swords.
The Hive-Five's ability to release bees when it hits an enemy makes it the best yoyo for this fight.
For ranged users:

The Molten Fury and The Bee's Knees are the best bows for the fight available at this stage.
The Demon or Tendon Bow can be used for players who find it hard to obtain other weapons.
The Blood Rain Bow is an effective choice but requires more precise aiming to be used properly. It works best with Shimmer Arrows as they have high base damage and are easy to obtain.
The Musket or The Undertaker are decent and the Minishark can also be used. The Boomstick is also a very powerful choice.
The Star Cannon is incredible for this fight, but the ammo is extremely tedious to obtain and is better used on later bosses.
Silver/  Tungsten Bullets are the preferred bullets to use with the guns mentioned above. Meteor Shots can also work with the former two, but the piercing is not helpful for this fight and they do slightly less damage. Musket Balls can also be used.
Poison Darts (with the Blowpipe or Blowgun) can be used intermittently to keep the boss constantly Poisoned.  Redundant with the Poison Barb or any other source of the debuff.
For magic users:

The Demon Scythe is the best option for this fight, but can be annoying to obtain since farming Demons is required.
The Space Gun is a good weapon, especially when combined with Meteor armor.
The Gray Zapinator is also an excellent weapon, thanks to its high damage output, especially with Meteor armor.
The Mystic Bloom is a pre-Boss weapon whose short-range homing petals can easily target the boss.
Crimson worlds will benefit from having the Crimson Rod, as you can fire it once and then switch to another weapon, increasing damage output.
The Thunder Zapper does high damage at the cost of heavy mana usage.
The Ruby Staff paired with the Sapphire Robe, the Amber or Emerald Staff paired with the Amethyst Robe, or the Diamond Staff paired with any robe are solid combinations for this boss.
The Bee Gun performs well, but requires defeating the Queen Bee.
The Vilethorn is a solid choice, especially due to Deerclops's low defense.
For summon users:

If a set of Bee armor has been obtained, then two uses of the Flinx Staff and two uses of the Vampire Frog Staff does the most damage.
If the Queen Bee hasn't been defeated, than two Flinx and one Vampire Frog does the most damage
If the player doesn't want to mix minions, the Mushroom Staff's use of local frames scales better with minion count than most other minions.
The Snapthorn is the best whip when using most minions against Deerclops. The Starcrash is stronger when using high-damage summon weapons, including Abigail's Flower, the Imp Staff, and Ballista Rod. If neither can be obtained, the Soulscourge and Vasculash are good alternatives.
Sentry weapons like the Ballista Rod and Explosive Trap Rod are more viable on Deerclops than other bosses due to it slow speed and large body. These pair well with the Starcrash, which can more than double their damage. By using the War Table and one of the Old One's Army accessories, three sentries can be summoned for maximum damage.


=== Accessories ===
Anything that increases your vertical mobility is a godsend. The Cloud in a Bottle is good, but better choices would be the Blizzard in a Bottle, Fart in a Jar, or Sandstorm in a Bottle and its upgrades, especially the Bundle of Balloons. You can also use the Rocket Boots and its upgrades or Fledgling Wings for flight, and if Rocket Boots are upgraded, speed.
Combining both Rocket Boots and its upgrades and Fledgling Wings is viable, as it increases flight time, and if Rocket Boots have been upgraded, speed.
Since Deerclops' ice spike attacks are clearly telegraphed, you can use the Slimy Saddle mount to jump above the ice spikes while remaining in close quarters, if you only had time to make a flat area to fight Deerclops in with no platforms.
The Shark Tooth Necklace is a very good increase to DPS.
If Queen Bee has been defeated, the Stinger Necklace is an upgrade to the Shark Tooth Necklace, increasing both on survivability and damage.
The Harpy Charm provides a small boost to ranged damage.
If going melee, the Magma Stone and its upgrades or the Feral Claws are useful, increasing DPS and enabling autoswing respectively.
The Feral Claws works for whips too, enabling autoswing for whips.
The Snapping Stone and its upgrades provide a good DPS boost for rangers.
If Queen Bee has been defeated, the Pygmy Necklace is an exceptionally good accessory for summoners.
The Squire's Shield/Apprentice's Scarf are great choices for summoners, although they don't stack.
Anything that reduces damage is very helpful, including the Expert Mode-exclusive Worm Scarf and defensive reforges on accessories.
The Expert Mode-exclusive Brain of Confusion increases critical strike chance for 3 seconds and chance to dodge on being attacked makes it a useful accessory against Deerclops.
If the Hand Warmer has been obtained, use it, since Deerclops inflicts the Chilled and Frozen debuff. Being immune to these effects makes manuevering around considerably easier.
In Expert Mode, Shield of Cthulhu's dash is essential and makes the fight considerably easier.


=== Potions ===
Ironskin Potions, Endurance Potions, Warmth Potions, and Regeneration Potions will help tremendously with survivability.
Warmth Potions will reduce Deerclop's damage by 30% and reduce the duration of the inflicted Frozen and Chilled debuffs, using one will greatly increase survivability.
A food item that provides Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied, or Exquisitely Stuffed is very useful.
Swiftness Potions will aid in dodging.
Ammo Reservation Potions and Archery Potions are good for rangers, and Archery Potions specifically for bow users.
Magic Power Potions and Mana Regeneration Potions are a must have for mages.
If you already have a minion, a Summoning Potion lets you bring an extra to the fight.
Rage Potions or Wrath Potions are useful for almost all classes.
Honeyfins heal more than the average Healing Potion and can prove valuable.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Legs Strategy ===
Once Deerclops is spawned, stand on his legs, underneath his torso. In this area, most of Deerclop's attacks cannot hit you, like the Ice Spike attack. The only attacks that are especially worrying are the Shadow Hands and third Ice Spike combo hit, but those should be easy to avoid with basic movement accessories. One way to enhance this method is to build a row of platforms 2–3 blocks off the ground in a flat area, and the player may move on 2 layers instead of one to avoid attacks easier.


=== Short Skybridge ===
Build a skybridge 20–30 blocks off the ground and spanning 100 or so blocks long, with a flat area underneath. Deerclops will stand beneath the platforms and follow the player's motion, but will not use his Ice Spikes attack. Instead, he will only summon Shadow Hands (if the player is above him) or throw debris if the player is off to one side. He can be easily handled by slowly walking just ahead of him until he begins to throw debris, then jumping in the opposite direction to avoid the ice chunks. Keep walking the other way until he throws debris again. 
The main risk is the Expert Mode Shadow Hands that can knock the player the wrong direction, knocking them into debris or causing Deerclops to summon many Shadow Hands. This can be avoided by jumping over the Hand or using the Cobalt Shield or Gladiator armor to avoid knockback.


=== Respawn Strategy ===
Set up a spawn point with a Bed in the arena where you will fight Deerclops. Because Deerclops won't despawn as long as a player was near within a certain period of time, the player will be able to die an infinite amount of times during the fight. This method may take a long time with lower-tier gear, but eventually defeating Deerclops is nearly guaranteed, as long as the player can deal some damage each time they respawn.

title: Underground Hallow
content:
The Underground Hallow is a dangerous Hardmode biome, being one of the biomes that spawns when the Wall of Flesh is defeated. It is the underground version of the surface-level Hallow, and appears in the Cavern layer. It operates similarly to the surface Hallow, being comprised of Pearlstone and Pearlsand; though it spawns different enemies, along with Crystal Shards, a common Hardmode crafting material. Gelatin Crystals can also be found to summon Queen Slime. The Underground Hallow spreads just like its surface counterpart, The Hallow, and similarly will conflict with Corruption and Crimson, as well as their underground variants.
Underground Hallow does not suppress the spawn of other underground and cavern enemies.
All enemies killed in the Underground Hallow have a 1/5 (20%) chance to drop a Soul of Light.
Note: Most characteristics of the surface Hallow apply to the Underground Hallow, with the exception of the enemies that spawn. See The Hallow for more extensive information.

title: Inferno Potion
content:
The Inferno Potion is a buff potion that grants the Inferno buff when consumed. The buff casts a spinning ring of fire around the player that deals 20 damage per second and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 2 seconds to all enemies inside of it while also giving off light. Critters and other passive NPCs are unaffected. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Inferno Potions can be found in Shadow Chests.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Enemies that are immune to the Hellfire debuff are also immune to damage from the Inferno Potion's ring of fire.
Crafting this potion requires a Hotline Fishing Hook, a Lavaproof Fishing Hook, or lava critters, as its two fish ingredients can only be caught in lava.


== Tips ==
While the ring deals minimal damage to most Hardmode enemies, it is very useful against enemies that throw destructible projectiles, as these are easily destroyed by the ring. Examples include Duke Fishron with his Detonating Bubbles and Plantera with her Spores.


== Trivia ==
If a player dies from the Inferno buff's ring of fire while PvP is active, the following unique death message will be displayed: "<Player name> was consumed by the inferno."

title: Lizard Egg
content:
The Lizard Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Lizard that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pet Lizard will sprout wings like those of a Flying Snake to catch up with the player. The Lizard Egg has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance of being dropped by Flying Snakes and Lihzahrds in the Jungle Temple.


== Trivia ==
Despite the fact that the egg hatches into a Lizard, it is still dropped by Flying Snakes.
The name being spelled as "Lizard" (like the real-world creature) could be referencing the strange spelling of "Lihzahrd".
The Pet Lizard's buff tooltip, "Chillin' like a reptilian", could be a combination of references to the phrase "chillin' like a villain" and the fact that lizards are reptiles.
The Pet Lizard appears to resemble a green iguana, a large, real-world lizard that is often kept as a pet due to its docile nature (see green iguana in captivity).

title: Imp Staff
content:
The Imp Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Flying Imp minion. It hovers near enemies, shooting fireballs that inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3–6 seconds and can pierce up to 4 times, dissipating on the 5th hit.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Imp attacks with an average rate of fire of once every 1.13 seconds. The delay between attacks can range between 0.75 seconds and 1.5 seconds.
The Imp Fireball applies 6 ticks of static invincibility frames upon hitting an enemy, which means that multiple Imps will interfere with each other's attacks.
While the Imp can fly through water, its fireball projectiles cannot travel through water. Regardless, the Imp will still attempt to fire at underwater enemies.
The Imp minions can target enemies up to 125 blocks away from the player.
This detection range is boosted to 187.5 tiles away from the player for enemies that are targeted by the player.
If the Imp minions are more than 62.5 tiles away from the player, they attempt to return to the player's side before resuming their attacks.
The Imp Fireballs move at a speed of 113 mph, and will disappear after 2.5 seconds if they do not hit an enemy or block.

title: Character styles
content:
Styles are chosen during character creation and determine the character's base clothing style, which is displayed when no armor or vanity items are equipped, or when the player is wearing Familiar clothes. This style of a character can be changed at any time at a dresser, and a character's gender can be changed at any time with the Gender Change Potion.


== Styles ==
There are 5 different styles to choose from:


=== Poses and animations ===


== Notes ==

Styles are purely cosmetic and do not affect gameplay in any form outside of visually. For example, a female character with style 1 will not have any less defense than another statistically identical female character with style 4, despite having exposed legs, nor will females with style 1 equipped be hindered by being in a Snow biome. NPCs will also not give different dialogue to players depending on their character style. However, NPCs will have varying dialogue between female and male characters, for example, the Stylist.
Familiar outfit pieces bought by a player in a specific style will not preserve said style when equipped on another player who uses a different style; a Familiar Shirt bought by a player with style 2 will not appear as a style 2 shirt if equipped on a player with style 1. In short, the Familiar outfit will only ever show the style of its current wearer.
Some animations seem to "detach" an arm from the character as to angle it in a usually impossible way. For example, firing a ranged weapon will change the entire character sprite to rotate the arm, while playing an instrument or petting a town pet will rotate the arm as its own object.

title: Ruinous Staff
content:
The Ruinous Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon crafted using desert and light/dark materials. It summons a Forbidden Ruin minion that hovers above the player. Upon finding a target, the Forbidden Ruin aggressively chases it and tries to stay at a short fixed distance to its target, while firing high-velocity Forbidden Bolt projectiles towards it which gradually slow down. The Forbidden Bolts do not pierce and explode upon dissipating, dealing their full damage and knockback to other nearby enemies, but not to the enemy directly hit by them. When multiple Forbidden Ruins are summoned, they form a spinning orbital formation while firing in rapid succession.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Forbidden Ruin has a random cooldown ranging from 1.75 seconds to 1.92 seconds between firing Forbidden Bolts, meaning it fires once every 1.83 seconds on average.
The Forbidden Ruin can target enemies within a 50-tile range.
The Forbidden Ruin tries to stay within 12.5 tiles of its target while firing Forbidden Bolts.
The Forbidden Ruin continuously adjusts its position to stay along the line segment between the player and its target, moving dynamically whenever either entity shifts position. If the distance between the player and the enemy drops below 12.5 tiles, it reverts to hovering directly above the player.
The Forbidden Bolt applies 30 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hit.
Upon exploding, the Forbidden Bolt deals damage within a 7×7-tile square area.
The Forbidden Bolt automatically dissipates after 0.62 seconds.


== Tips ==
Because of its high base damage and slower fire rate, it synergizes exceptionally well with the damage multiplier of Firecracker's explosions.


== Trivia ==

The Forbidden Ruin minion behaves similarly to the Xeno Staff minion, sticking closely to a single target and firing fast-moving projectiles.
The ring of Forbidden Ruin minions behind the player when idle forms differently if the user is wearing a full set of Forbidden armor.
The top of Ruinous Staff resembles an Ankh, the ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic symbol most commonly used in writing and in art to represent the word for "life" and, by extension, as a symbol of life itself.
This symbol also appears on the Ankh Charm and Ankh Shield.
This is one of a small "set" of weapons made with two shards apiece, the other members being the Onyx Blaster, the Sky Fracture, and the Dao of Pow. Their recipes, names and appearances link the weapons to themes of Darkness, Light, and Balance, with the Ruinous Staff and Dao of Pow both representing Balance. The set also includes one weapon for each of the four damage types, where the Ruinous Staff is the summon weapon.

title: Old One's Army
content:
The Old One's Army is a unique Dungeon Defenders 2 crossover event that can be triggered by placing an Eternia Crystal on an Eternia Crystal Stand. Waves of enemies begin spawning from portals on both sides of the crystal, seeking to destroy it. The objective is to protect the Eternia Crystal until all waves are cleared – if the crystal is destroyed, the event automatically ends.
There are three different versions, or "tiers", of the event: 

After defeating the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu, the Old One's Army is unlocked in its first tier with an initial maximum of five waves.
After defeating any mechanical boss, the event receives a substantial increase in difficulty in its second tier and gains two more waves, totaling a maximum of seven.
After defeating Golem, the event reaches its third, final tier of difficulty, with the full range of enemies and mini-bosses present in some way during the seven waves.
Clearing later waves rewards the player with Defender Medals, a unique currency that can be used to purchase special weapons, armor, and the Defender's Forge from the Tavernkeep NPC. This gear is specifically suited for the event, due to its exceptional level of difficulty, and stronger equipment is unlocked with each progressed tier. Not only are its enemies extraordinarily resistant, but it also employs numerous anti-cheat/exploit mechanisms, such as preventing the player from placing or removing blocks or liquids for the event's duration.


== Summoning ==
To initiate the Old One's Army event, an Eternia Crystal Stand must be placed first. An Eternia Crystal must then be placed on it by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on the stand. Both the crystal and its stand are purchased from the Tavernkeep for coins. The Tavernkeep can be found randomly in a world as the Unconscious Man after the Eater of Worlds or the Brain of Cthulhu has been defeated.


=== Terrain requirements ===
Summoning this event has some unique requirements for the terrain around the summon area. If they are not fulfilled, the Eternia Crystal cannot be placed successfully, and a status message appears informing the player that the surface is inadequate.

A minimum clearing of 60 tiles horizontally is required on each side of the Eternia Crystal Stand, measured from the center of the stand (a 121-tile clearing in total, with the stand at the center tile). The enemy portals will spawn farther away if given the space, however: up to 120 tiles away from the center of the stand on each side.
A minimum clearing of 10 tiles vertically is required (i.e., between the "floor" and the "ceiling", if there is one).
Additionally, tiles above the floor may not be immediately next to the Eternia Crystal Stand.
The floor may not have holes wider than 1 block.
The player can build up to a height of three tiles before blocks are considered obstructing the necessary space. Platforms and inactive blocks do not count as part of a flat floor, and will count against the three-tile height allowance; but floor blocks with Actuators on them that are solid when the crystal is placed will count as flat, and can be successfully actuated after the event has started. In addition, closed Trap Doors are considered flat, and can be successfully opened and/or reclosed after the event has started.


== Waves ==
The event consists of a set number of waves, with each wave becoming progressively more difficult. The player has to kill a certain amount of enemies to finish a wave. Each enemy (including mini-bosses) counts as 1 kill in Classic Mode, or 2 kills in Expert Mode and above. See wave chart for details.
At the end of each wave, there is a 30-second countdown to the next wave, signified by a timer appearing over the Eternia Crystal. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Eternia Crystal Stand during this time will allow the player to skip the countdown and immediately start the next wave. The Eternia Crystal Stand's tooltip and the completion message of the first wave also indicate this fact.
The event comes in three possible tiers, depending on game progression when the event is triggered. In addition to the difference in bosses, the common event enemies also differ between Tiers, with stronger stats and a more menacing appearance in higher tiers.

Tier 1 consists of five waves, with one or more Dark Mages serving as mini-bosses in the final wave. Tier 1 is triggered when the event is summoned before any mechanical bosses have been defeated. The final wave will only end after at least one Dark Mage is killed. Completing Tier 1 awards 5 Defender Medals in total.
Tier 2 consists of seven waves, with one or more Ogres serving as mini-bosses in the final wave. Dark Mages will not appear in this tier. Tier 2 is triggered when the event is summoned in a Hardmode world after at least one mechanical boss has been defeated. The final wave only ends after at least one Ogre is killed. Completing Tier 2 awards 25 Defender Medals in total.
Tier 3 consists of seven waves, with the boss Betsy spawning in the final wave. The Dark Mage and Ogre will also spawn during the previous three waves. Tier 3 is triggered when the event is summoned after Golem has been defeated. The final wave only ends once Betsy is defeated. Completing Tier 3 awards 100 Defender Medals in total. In Expert Mode worlds, an additional bonus of 30–49 Defender Medals is dropped by Betsy's Treasure Bag. Furthermore, in Master Mode worlds, the boss relics will only drop during this tier.


== Defender Medals and sentries ==
The completion of each wave, beginning with the third, awards the player Defender Medals, a special currency used to purchase items from the Tavernkeep NPC that can help players complete future attempts of the Old One's Army. Among them are special sentry summon weapons, which are fueled by Etherian Mana, a resource that drops only during this event. Etherian Mana allows multiple sentry minions to remain placed simultaneously and permanently until the event is over, with more Etherian Mana allowing more sentries to be placed. All Etherian Mana disappears once the event is over, whether uncollected or within the player's inventory.
At the beginning of the event, the player will receive 10 Etherian Mana, allowing them to place one sentry. Note that sentries not obtained from the Tavernkeep (such as the Queen Spider Staff) do not and cannot use Etherian Mana, but can be summoned separately.
Each sentry type available from the Tavernkeep (Flameburst, Explosive Trap, Lightning Aura, Ballista) comes in three different tiers: Rod, Cane, and Staff, from least to most powerful and expensive.
Once the event is completed successfully in a world, the weapons can then be used outside the event with normal summoning rules.


== Drops ==
Each mini-boss in the event can drop a trophy (1/10 (10%) chance) and a mask (1/7 (14.29%) chance). Betsy also always has a 100% chance of dropping a Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Mini-bosses can also drop pets, vanity items, and powerful weapons and accessories. All enemy banners dropped during this event are functional, although they provide the player a weaker buff compared to that of other enemy banners, only granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken and most often require higher kill counts before they will be dropped.
Enemies will not drop biome-specific drops, such as Biome Keys, or coins, even with effects like Midas or with the Lucky Coin or its derivatives. They also do not drop Presents during Christmas, nor Goodie Bags during Halloween. 


== Contents ==


== Anti-cheat mechanisms ==
The Creative Shock debuff prevents placing or mining blocks during the event. It also prevents using Buckets to spill or collect any liquids.
All blocks: Blocks cannot be used to completely prevent event enemies from advancing. Old One's Army enemies are able to go to enter a "ghostly" state where they can move through blocks. They initially spawn in this state, then re-enter it whenever there is no clear path between them and the player. For example, if the player enters a tunnel below the arena, enemies will fall through the blocks to enter the tunnel.
Teleporter: Event enemies are not affected by Teleporters, rendering them useless for the event. However, players are still able to use them.
Lava: Event enemies take no damage from lava, rendering it useless for the event.
Water, Honey, and Honey Blocks do not slow down the enemies.
Traps: While traps will damage event enemies normally, they are less efficient than sentries; Traps can additionally make sentries less effective, since trap attacks cause invincibility frames in the enemies they hit, while sentries do not. Traps may still be useful in areas out of the reach of sentries.


=== Oversights ===
Actuators can be used to transform the arena after the event has started. Keep in mind that walls can result in the enemies simply moving through, and dropping them below the Eternia Crystal's level will cause them to float up to it.
Ice Rod can place temporary ice blocks.
Dirt Rod can be used to move Dirt Blocks in the area.
Weapons and tools that create placed blocks are usable and will produce blocks. However, these blocks cannot be removed with tools until the event is over.
Sandgun will still produce placed Sand Blocks when fired.
Dirt Bombs and Sticky Dirt Bombs can be used, and will produce placed Dirt Blocks.
Proximity Mine Launcher and explosives can destroy blocks that are not explosion-proof.
Conveyor Belts can be used to move Etherian Mana towards the player. Note that neither sentries nor the event enemies are moved by conveyors.
Etherian Mana can be placed in a storage item (e.g. a Chest or Piggy Bank) left unopened between events, allowing it to be reused for future events.
It is possible to open a storage item with Autopause enabled to stop it from disappearing in between events.
Minecart Tracks are allowed in the arena, allowing the player to use Minecarts to run over enemies.
Block-Swapped platform hoiks can be used to block enemies, as many of the anti-cheat systems only apply to solid blocks and ignore platforms.


== Wave chart ==


== Equipment chart ==
The Old One's Army event brings associated equipment. The armor and sentry weapons are available from the Tavernkeep in exchange for Defender Medals, while other weapons and accessories are dropped by event enemies. Though all of the equipment is coordinated with other equipment of the same class, the only specific benefit from this coordination is the buffs granted to each sentry by the corresponding armor set bonus; neither the weapons nor the accessories are involved in any additional unique bonuses, and so can be used with any other armor or exchanged for any other weapon at the player's preference.
Tier 2 items become available after one mechanical boss is defeated, and Tier 3 items become available after Golem is defeated.


== Status messages ==
All unique status messages associated with the Old One's Army event are listed below.
When the Eternia Crystal is destroyed:

"The old one's army proves victorious..."
When the first wave is completed:

"Wave Complete! Interact with the Crystal to rush next wave!"
When a wave is completed:

"Wave Complete!"
When the Eternia Crystal Stand is placed at an inadequate location:

"The eternia crystal rejects this area and pops away instantly, the Tavernkeep mentioned it should rest in a large flat open area..."


== Notes ==
The Eternia Crystal regenerates its health very slowly when not taking damage.
The Eternia Crystal has 2× as much health in Expert Mode and 3× as much health in Master Mode.
All enemies in the event will scale their health in multiplayer.
Bringing a mechanical boss's summoning item to a pre-Hardmode world and defeating one will still only produce Tier 1 Old One's Army.
Traps like Spiky Ball Traps or Super Dart Traps can do a small amount of damage to the Eternia Crystal.
If Tavernkeep's sentries have been summoned using regular mana before summoning Old One's Army, they will vanish at the beginning of the event. Regular sentries will not vanish.
The "cleared" status of the event is indicated by white light surrounding the Eternia Crystal, as well as a change in music, by which point the event is considered won even if enemies then proceed to touch the Eternia Crystal or the player dies. The event can even be won posthumously if the remaining sentries finish off the last boss.
For Tiers 1 and 2, one can still progress through the last wave by killing enemies but must defeat at least one of its respective final bosses in order to clear the event.
For Tier 3, the event is considered cleared once Betsy is defeated, regardless of how many enemies are left at that point.
Betsy will spawn off-screen on the ground instead of from the Mysterious Portals.
The four sentry-boosting accessories have identical effects and do not stack with each other. They differ only in appearance, each matching one of the Tier 2 armor sets.
If the player kills the boss while the Eternia Crystal is broken, the game will still count it as a failure and the player will not get Defender Medals nor the victory message. However, bosses defeated this way will still drop their unique loot.
While dialogue claims the Eternia Crystal "pops away instantly" when the arena is rejected, the Eternia Crystal item is not dropped from the inventory or consumed.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Because of the Creative Shock debuff, any building work to prepare the arena must be completed beforehand. It is not possible to place or remove blocks or furniture while the event is happening, not even between waves.
During the event, players can combine two different kinds of sentries with different limits:
Regular sentries (Houndius Shootius, Queen Spider Staff, etc.) work as normal. By default, the player can only have one non-Tavernkeep sentry summoned, but Tavernkeep armor and other gear will let them summon more.
During the event, the Tavernkeep sentries are summoned using 10 Etherian Mana. The Etherian Mana supply is the only limit to how many the player can summon, and they will last until the event ends. Outside the event, they work like any other sentry.
In general, players will likely struggle to finish the Old One's Army without a Tavernkeep sentry for the tier; for later tiers having a set of Tavernkeep armor will also help. The player gets a Tier 1 sentry for free; saving up 15 Defender Medals will let them buy a Tier 2 sentry before facing the Tier 2 army. If they can save up a full 45 Defender Medals, they will also be able to buy Tier 2 armor up front. During Tier 2, they should focus on collecting at least 60 Defender Medals for a Tier 3 sentry – another 150 Defender Medals in addition will let them get the armor as well. Note that both the sentries and the armor are also quite useful for regular gameplay.
If the player is in a Hardmode, non-Expert Mode world, but has yet to defeat a mechanical boss, they can easily farm the event with a Blessed Apple or Ancient Horn mount by simply running back and forth. The damage the mounts deal while charging will oneshot all enemies besides the Dark Mage.


== Trivia ==
Due to rounding, it is possible to finish Tier 3 Old One's Army when Betsy has very low health but is not defeated yet.
The Eternia Crystal slowly develops cracks as it gets more damaged.
In the Bestiary, the entries of many enemies depict their Tier 3 variant, including their statistics, before ever reaching the tier.
In the game files, an unused NPC called DD2AttackerTest can be found. It looks identical to the Angry Tumbler enemy.

title: Achievements
content:
Achievements are earned by performing various tasks in Terraria.


== Achievements introduced in 1.3.0.1 ==
88 achievements were introduced in 1.3.0.1.

The  Xbox One version,  version,  iOS and   Google Play versions still have achievements in addition to the in-game ones from the  Old-gen console version, GameCenter and Google Play respectively, but these achievements are deprecated.


== Achievement introduced in 1.4.0.1 ==
One achievement was introduced in 1.4.0.1. Counting previously existing achievements, there are a total of 89 achievements.


== Achievements introduced in 1.4.1 ==
15 achievements were introduced in 1.4.1. Counting previously existing achievements, there are a total of 104 achievements.


== Achievements introduced in 1.4.4 ==
11 achievements were introduced in 1.4.4. Counting previously existing achievements, there are a total of 115 achievements.


== Achievements introduced in 1.4.5.0 ==
22 achievements were introduced in 1.4.5.0. Counting previously existing achievements, there are a total of 137 achievements.


== Tips ==
If the player has no intention to keep the Minishark, they can purchase it and sell it back for the full price, so long as they do not close the Arms Dealer's shop window. The Completely Awesome achievement will still be unlocked.


== Trivia ==
There is one enemy capable of completing five achievements at once when slain: King Slime (Slippery Shinobi, Slayer of Worlds, Sticky Situation, Vehicular Manslaughter, and Gelatin World Tour)
There are three enemies capable of completing four achievements at once when slain:
Any mechanical boss (Buckets of Bolts, Slayer of Worlds, Mecha Mayhem, and Vehicular Manslaughter)
There is one enemy capable of completing three achievements at once when slain:
Pinky (Gelatin World Tour, Vehicular Manslaughter, and Pretty in Pink)
As of version 1.4.5.5, there are six unimplemented achievements in the game code:
Behind The Mask – Slay the Insane Cultist, a mad magician with powerful spells.
Behind The Mask was left unused due to a similar achievement already being available.
Davy Jones' Locker – Defeat the Flying Dutchman, the sails of the plunderin' skies.
Winterhearted – Defeat the Ice Queen, wicked witch of the coldest nights.
Pumpkin Smasher – Defeat the Pumpking, the spooky lord of hallow's eve.
Pumpkin Smasher is a reference to the American alternative rock band The Smashing Pumpkins.
Independence Day – Defeat a Mothership, overminds of the martian invaders.
Independence Day is a reference to the 1996 American science fiction action movie Independence Day, where the military fights attacking aliens.
Hex Education – Defeat a Goblin Warlock, conjurers of the darkest flames.
Hex Education is a pun on "sex education" and the Goblin Warlock's hex related powers (such as the Shadowflame Hex Doll and Shadowflame Knife it drops).

title: Betsy
content:
Betsy is a Hardmode, post-Golem mini-boss that spawns once during the seventh and final wave of Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. Like all enemies in the Old One's Army, she will despawn upon completion or failure of the event. Defeating Betsy is the only way to complete the final wave of the event successfully.


== Behavior ==
Upon being summoned, Betsy cycles through the following attacks in the following order. If within close enough proximity to the player, she will target them instead of the Eternia Crystal.

Betsy charges at the target twice in succession.
Betsy positions herself to the left or right of her target before flying horizontally in a straight line. During this time, she spews a fiery stream of Betsy's Breath from her mouth downward, damaging the target and inflicting the player with the On Fire! debuff for 7–10 / 14–20 / 17.5–25 seconds.
Then, Betsy charges at the target once.
Betsy flies forward a short distance while shooting six small Betsy's Fireballs that are affected by gravity, exploding upon contact with the player, the Eternia Crystal, or solid blocks.
Betsy then flies around in a large loop, similar to Duke Fishron's Detonating Bubble attack during his second phase.
Afterwards, Betsy performs her fire breath attack again.
Finally, Betsy hovers in place and roars, spawning three Tier 3 Etherian Wyverns that appear around her, while also spawning an additional three from both Mysterious Portals.
This attack will not summon Etherian Wyverns if there are already at least five Etherian Wyverns currently existing in the world.


== Notes ==
Regardless of the world's current point of progression, Betsy always spawns Tier 3 Etherian Wyverns, which can be seen if she is spawned via mods or other external programs.
Betsy can only spawn a maximum of six Etherian Wyverns from Mysterious Portals. The cap is shared between all Mysterious Portals if more than two are summoned with the use of mods.
Betsy's attack pattern may randomly skip some of her attacks depending on the player's attacks or movements. However, the first four attacks and the final summoning attack are always performed consistently.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

The On Fire! debuff is a major source of damage. Note that it negates life regen from Nebula armor's set bonus – hence, if the player is unable to avoid Betsy's flame breath attack, it might make the armor ineffective.
The Obsidian Skin Potion can prevent the debuff.
A floating pool of water (utilizing Bubbles) can be used to cancel the On Fire! debuff. Honey will also cancel the debuff and also give extra life regeneration, but slows down the player's movement while submerged in it unless they are using Flipper Potions.
This does not apply to life-stealing effects such as the Spectre armor Hood set bonus or the Vampire Knives. It does not affect the Life Drain's health regen boost either.


== Trivia ==
Betsy is a boss originating from Dungeon Defenders 2, as the 1.3.4 update brought a crossover event between the two games.
Betsy's Treasure Bag is the only obtainable Treasure Bag that does not contain Expert Mode-exclusive items, and the only Treasure Bag capable of being dropped by an event-exclusive mini-boss.
Betsy's attack behavior of flying and launching projectiles is fairly similar to Duke Fishron's. Unlike Duke Fishron, however, she does not have additional phases as a boss.
Betsy, and by extension the Etherian Wyvern, are different from Terraria's long, segmented Wyverns and do not possess the Worm AI. This is because Betsy and the Etherian Wyvern resemble archetypal wyverns, whereas Terrarian Wyverns resemble Chinese dragons.
Betsy's four weapon drops are the same as those dropped after defeating her in "The Wyvern's Den" map in Dungeon Defenders 2, with each one capable of being equipped exclusively by one of the four base characters:
Flying Dragon, a sword for the Squire;
Betsy's Wrath, a staff for the Apprentice;
Aerial Bane, a bow for the Huntress;
and Sky Dragon's Fury, a polearm for the Monk.
 The Bestiary entry for  Betsy: "A vicious Etherian dragon who leads the minions of the Old One's Army that found their way to this world."

title: Ichor (debuff)
content:
Ichor is a Hardmode debuff that lowers the afflicted player's defense by 15, or adds 15 armor penetration when calculating damage against afflicted enemies. It is inflicted by the ranged attacks of Ichor Stickers in the Underground Crimson or by Tainted Ghouls found in Crimson Underground Deserts. It can also be inflicted by weapons and ammo crafted with Ichor.


== Causes ==


=== From player ===


=== From enemy ===


== Immune NPCs ==


== Notes ==
Enemies and players afflicted with Ichor are highlighted in a golden color. They will be visible in the dark but do not emit light.


== Tips ==
Because of its effect, Ichor is useful even in the late game, since very few enemies are resistant to it. It is especially useful against enemies with high defense (e.g. Skeletron Prime (especially during its spin attack), Duke Fishron, etc.)
A common tactic is to use an Ichor-inflicting weapon on an enemy, and then finish it off with the player's main weapon.


== Trivia ==
The damage increase from Ichor on the player changes depending on the world difficulty (Expert/Master Mode), due to how the effectiveness of defense changes with the difficulty.
This does not apply to PvP combat. In those scenarios, defense is always as effective as in Classic Mode, regardless of the actual world difficulty.
Ichor as a debuff may be a reference to Jarate from the 2007 multiplayer first-person shooter game Team Fortress 2, as both are yellow liquids that cause those afflicted to take more damage, along with both being implied to be urine.


== See also ==
Betsy's Curse, another debuff that lowers defense.
Cursed Inferno, its Corruption counterpart.

title: Love Potion
content:
The Love Potion is a Hardmode thrown potion that functions similarly to Thrown Water. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Lovestruck debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles, causing them to emit red hearts for 30 seconds. It also increases affected NPCs' happiness by 10% for the duration of the effect.
Its counterpart is the Stink Potion.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Lovestruck debuff cannot increase a NPC's happiness beyond 75%, or increase a homeless NPC's happiness (which is always set to 150%).
The Lovestruck debuff's happiness boost stacks multiplicatively with other happiness infuences.
For example, if a NPC is housed in a liked biome (94% buy price modifier), is near a loved NPC (88% buy price modifier), and has the solitude bonus (95% buy price modifier) while being affected by the Lovestruck debuff (90% buy price modifier), the total buy price modifier will be equal to: 94% × 88% × 95% × 90% = 70.73%, capped at 75%.
The Lovestruck debuff can increase happiness of NPCs when the Remix seed is enabled, which will still affect their prices, despite happiness being otherwise disabled in this seed.
It can be created and used in pre-Hardmode worlds if an artificial Hallowed sea or lake is created for fishing – or if either Princess Fish or the Love Potion itself is transferred to the world by a Hardmode player.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Tips ==
Since the Princess Fish (25 Silver) sells for more than the Love Potion (40 Copper), it is more profitable to sell the fish than it is to sell the potions.


== Trivia ==
Lovestruck is considered a debuff because it cannot be terminated manually and the Nurse charges money for removing it, similar to other debuffs. Despite this, the debuff icon has a blue background, which usually indicates a buff.
This might be because the Love Potion is used to "make someone fall in love", which could imply that the target is unable to remove the effect.
The red hearts that the Love Potion releases upon collision and debuff emits are fully bright in the dark.
