title: Sandstorm
content:
The Sandstorm is an event that occurs in the Desert at high wind speeds. The Mighty Wind debuff, active for the entire duration of the event, continuously pushes the player in the direction of the wind. Certain enemies normally only found in the Underground Desert will spawn on the surface during a Sandstorm, as well as several new and dangerous enemies. Sandstorms always take place in all Desert biomes of the world at the same time, and the Weather Radio and its upgrades indicate the event by switching between “Sandstorm” and their standard display.
Vision is limited during a Sandstorm due to the large number of sand particles flying across the screen. The color of these particles depends on whether the Desert is pure, Corrupt, Crimson, or Hallowed. While the effects are amplified in the Color and White lighting modes, which may be resource-intensive on some devices, using the Retro or Trippy modes will remove much of the effects.


== Details ==
In order for a Sandstorm to occur, the wind speed must exceed 30 mph. Once this criterion is met, there is a chance of 1/64,800 (0.0015%) every tick that a Sandstorm begins. This means that when the wind speed reaches (and stays above) 30 mph, it takes on average 12 minutes 28.59 seconds until a Sandstorm occurs. Sandstorms are 50% more common in Hardmode: The chance each tick is increased to 1/43,200 (0.0023%), resulting in an average duration of 8 minutes 19.06 seconds until the beginning of a Sandstorm.
A Sandstorm lasts anywhere between 8 minutes and 24 minutes. The duration is random and is determined when the Sandstorm starts.
If the wind speed drops below 30 mph during a Sandstorm, the remaining time of the Sandstorm will be divided by 15. For example, if a Sandstorm has 15 minutes remaining, the wind speed drops below 30 mph and does not reach 30 mph again, then the Sandstorm will stop 1 minute later.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==

Sandstorm enemies require Sand Blocks (including their infected variants) to spawn on, much like surface Antlions. Furthermore, they also require at least 40 fully interconnected Sand Blocks of any variant (10 in Remix and Zenith worlds) within a 9×9-tile square, with the selected Sand Block at the top-center. Which means that they need at least 5 layers of sand (2 in Remix and Zenith worlds) to reliably spawn. See the image on the right for a visualization.
Sandstorms can never be initiated manually.
No status messages are displayed when a Sandstorm starts and ends, so if one wants to experience it from start to finish, the Desert will have to be checked frequently. Alternatively, the player can use the Weather Radio and its upgrades to see if there is a Sandstorm currently happening.
In Remix and Zenith worlds, Sandstorm happens below Cavern layer and at least 350 tiles above the bottom true world edge (about 310 tiles above the visible world edge).


== Tips ==
Since the Sandstorm only occurs in the Desert biome and on the surface layer, one can simply fly over the biome or go underground to avoid it.
One way to dodge attacks from enemies like the Angry Tumbler is to use movement accessories, e.g. Dunerider Boots or Lightning Boots.
Grapple the ground (or a tree) with a (Squirrel)-Hook will also stop the player from being pushed away from the wind.
All 4 pre-Hardmode Roller Skates completely suppress the Mighty Wind debuff while rolling fast, coasting or even when standing still.
The Basilisk Mount or similar high-speed mounts are resistant to the Mighty Wind debuff when the player is in motion. This can ease the player's task of crossing the Desert during this event. However, the Mighty Wind will still push the player around when standing still.
Placing background walls in the middle tile of where the player walks will stop the Mighty Wind debuff, making movement normal.
The effects of the Mighty Wind can lead to the player falling and getting stuck in one of the entrances to the Underground Desert. This can be avoided by blocking off all entrances, e.g. with platforms.


== Trivia ==
The Sandstorm is similar to the Blizzard event in that it reduces visibility and spawns new enemies, however unlike the Blizzard (and some real-life sandstorms), it is not tied to rain in any way. It is also similar in that it happens simultaneously with another event – in this case, the Windy Day.
The wind direction is related with the pushing direction of the Mighty Wind debuff.
When the Weather Radio indicates that the wind is moving at 0 mph, the Sandstorm pushes the player west (left).
The player squints their eyes while they are in a Sandstorm.


== History ==

Sandstorms only occur when wind speed is above 30 mph.

title: Amulet of the Night
content:
The Amulet of the Night is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Bat. While in bat form, the player has infinite flight and their hurt sound is replaced with a squeak. The bat form has a top movement speed of 23 mph when moving in the cardinal directions, and a top movement speed of 33 mph pixels when moving diagonally. If the player has any dashes equipped, they can also perform a dash with a special animation by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled. The player will be pulled out of the form when any of the following occurs:

The player uses or places any item, including weapons.
The player is submerged in liquids or is inflicted with the Wet debuff.
The Amulet of the Night is dropped by Vampires during a Solar Eclipse and can be found in naturally generated chests in the Vampirism secret world seed.


== Notes ==
The bat form's dash inherits the velocity, length, and unique effects of the player's equipped dash.
While in the bat form, the player takes up less space, only being 1.25 tiles wide and 1.125 tiles tall.
Like other transformation mounts that reduce the player's size, if the player attempts to dismount in a place where they cannot fit, the dismount will fail. On the third attempt, the player will be teleported to the nearest open space and dismount. If there is no valid location within 25 tiles to the top and left of the player's feet and 24 tiles to the bottom and right of the player's feet, the player will instead be teleported to their world spawn point.
The player is also teleported to their world spawn if the target location is valid but would place the player inside of the Jungle Temple before Plantera is defeated.
Using the mount in a world other than the Vampirism seed does not cause the player to burn in sunlight, and the mount itself causes no vulnerability to the sun.
The bat form's eye is fully visible in the dark.


== Tips ==
Despite being obtainable in early pre-Hardmode in the Vampirism secret world seed, the Amulet of the Night has infinite flight time, making it the only method of gaining infinite flight in pre-Hardmode.
Their abundance in chests in this seed and high sell price makes it an effective source of early-game coins.
The bat form is only two tiles tall rather than three, allowing the shapeshifted player to easily fit in spaces too small for many enemies while still being able to use doors. Placing a passage two tiles high in front of a door effectively prevents every mob capable of opening doors from reaching the door. This can be most simply achieved by placing a single block on the upper third of a door (or the bottom third if the door is on the ceiling) interposing that block between the door and enemy spawns. Houses and fortifications designed around this can easily be made impenetrable to almost every mob in the game while allowing players with the Amulet of the Night, Enchanted Pixie Dust, or Cursed Piper Flute to pass easily; this eliminates the need to barracade doors during invasions.
This strategy is most relevant during eclipses and when building in the Cavern layer at the start of a vampirism game, which are also the two possible opportunities for a player to obtain an Amulet of the Night.
This can also contain NPCs to their rooms without sealing the door entirely, allowing players to enter by double tapping the mount button. Visually, this appears to be the player becoming an intangible mist to pass through the opening which is thematically consistent with the vampires in Dracula.
The Amulet of the Night can be used to immediately activate the Hermes Boots sprint by double tapping the mount button, allowing the player to quickly reach the maximum run speed which is often faster than the bat form itself. This makes the Amulet of the Night competitive with dash items, with the Amulet using a mount slot rather than an accessory slot to activate the sprint.


== Trivia ==
Despite the Stake Launcher having a bonus damage against Vampire enemies in both humanoid and bat form, this effect does not apply to players transformed with this mount in PvP.

title: Drill Containment Unit
content:
The Drill Containment Unit (sometimes abbreviated to DCU) is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord mount-summoning item that summons a Drill Mount, a rideable, flying vehicle that mines tiles extremely quickly via a stream of blue lasers. It can fly and hover indefinitely and has a mining range of 15 tiles.
The Drill Mount is one of the fastest controllable ways to mine in Terraria, but it has a number of special characteristics:

Unlike other mounts, players cannot use any tools or weapons while riding the Drill Mount.
Unlike most other mounts, players can fly through liquids while riding the Drill Mount, though they can still drown.
Unlike other mining tools, the Drill Mount does not inflict damage on enemies. It also cannot mine blocks behind other blocks, rather always drilling tunnels through all blocks directly ahead of the player.
Mining speed bonuses do not affect Drill Mount's mining speed.
The Drill Mount flies at 41 mph vertically, 31 mph horizontally, and 51 mph diagonally. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack makes the Drill Mount mine all mineable blocks, including furniture, objects, trees, Lihzahrd Bricks, Altars (during Hardmode), and Shadow Orbs / Crimson Hearts, among others. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate makes the Drill Mount mine background walls. Holding ⚷ Open / Activate and ⚒ Use / Attack simultaneously will mine both blocks and walls.
Crafting the Drill Containment Unit requires a total of 160 Luminite (thus requiring defeating the Moon Lord at least twice), 600 Chlorophyte Ore, 600 Glowing Mushrooms, 20 Ectoplasm, 120 each of Hellstone and Meteorite ores, and 40 Obsidian. This also requires four different crafting stations: a Hardmode Forge for the Chlorophyte and Spectre Bars, an Autohammer for the Shroomite Bars, an Ancient Manipulator for the Luminite Bars, and a Hardmode Anvil for the Drill Containment Unit itself.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Crafting tree ===


== Notes ==

The Drill Mount has 210% pickaxe power, axe power, and hammer power, allowing it to destroy every block and destroy trees in one hit. Its tool speed is 1.
The Drill Mount leaves surrounding blocks hammered into slopes.
Due to the Drill Mount's ability to destroy Altars with its hammer coding, if brought to a pre-Hardmode world, trying to mine them or the blocks underneath them will result in the usual health penalty per hit.
Using dyes will change the color of both the Drill Mount and the lasers fired from it.
Similar to a chainsaw, the mount's lasers will cease functioning after 1 minute of continuous use.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Holding a light source like a Glowstick or Torch can improve visibility while mining.
The player can use a Spelunker Potion with a Torch or other light source to more easily find ores. The Spelunker Glowstick can be used to create a weaker glow effect with the benefit of being an inexhaustible option.
Like all mounts, using it will not remove minions. Summoners can take advantage of this to defend themselves when mining.
A yoyo, chainsaw, or drill can be used when riding the Drill Mount. This works when the item is already in use and the player activates the mount afterward. However, it is purposeless as the mount will be unable to mine blocks this way. In most cases, getting off the mount is a better option to deal with enemies.
The Drill mount is significantly slower underwater, so equipping items which increase its speed underwater, like the Neptune's Shell, should be used.
When the Drill Mount is operating underwater, items that prevent drowning should be used.
Because of the automatic sloping, it can be useful for underground terraforming or making caves in maps.


== Trivia ==
It has the highest monetary value of materials of any craftable item in the game, pricing at 1 Platinum 85 Gold 60 Silver from the bars or 1 Platinum 54 Gold from the base material (Obsidian does not have any sell value).
Despite this, it still only sells for 5 Gold.
The Drill Mount has the longest digging range of any digging tool, matched only by the Laser Drill.
Re-Logic's trailer video for 1.3.0.1 shows a player using a Laser Machinegun while riding in the Drill Mount, although this feature is not available in-game.
The Drill Containment Unit is one of only two mount-summoning items that are crafted, the other being Slasher's Mysterious Skull.

The Drill Mount was originally designed to be a ground-based mount that would dig through and slope the terrain (likely in a similar fashion to the Digging Molecart, which was later introduced). Because the implementation of this concept was prone to bugs and not satisfying to use, it was changed to a flying mount.
The sprite for that previous iteration of the mount remains in the game as Mount_Drill.png. The buff icon resembled this design until 1.4.5.0.
The mount appears to be made of Martian Plating, despite not requiring drops from the Martian Madness event to craft.
Despite being a post-Moon Lord item and requiring Luminite Bars, it is not crafted at the Ancient Manipulator.

title: Pygmy Staff
content:
The Pygmy Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Pygmy minion. It fires a spear towards nearby enemies that inflicts the Acid Venom debuff for 5–10 seconds, but does not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The Pygmy Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Plantera.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Notes ==
The Pygmy minions fire spears every 0.5 seconds.
The Pygmy minions can target enemies within a 50-tile range, and will automatically return to the player's side if their distance from the player is greater than 62.5 tiles.
The Pygmy minions try to aim ahead of their target, by predicting where the target will be 0.33 seconds later using its current position and velocity.
They can only fire spears at their target if the target's future position is within 28.125 tiles of them horizontally.
The Pygmy spears are launched at the speed of 113 mph and can travel for 0.33 seconds before being affected by gravity.


== Trivia ==
Each time a Pygmy is summoned, it randomly has one of four possible sprites. However, they are all functionally identical.
The Pygmy catches up to fast-moving players by flying through the air while standing, sitting, or hanging onto its spear.
In real life, the anthropological term for pygmy peoples refers to ethnic groups whose average height is relatively short. It is primarily associated with the African Pygmies, hunter-gatherer tribes originating from the Congo Basin.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Removed mana cost once more (cost 10 mana previously).
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Pygmy damage increased from 34 to 40.
Pygmy spears are now slightly faster.
Pygmies will now attempt to predictively aim at moving targets.
Pygmy spears now always inflict Acid Venom, and no longer inflict Poisoned.
Pygmies now move faster when returning to the player.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Projectile speed increased by 50%.
Detection range increased by 40%.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Reduced the duration of Venom from 10–20 seconds to 5–10 seconds.
Item and minion sprites updated.
Minion spear sprite updated.
Minion spear no longer pierces.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Pygmies now have a chance to inflict Poisoned and Venom.
Pygmies now have a larger range and the first projectile thrown will always pierce rather than getting stuck.
Desktop 1.2.4.1: Now requires 10 mana again.
Desktop 1.2.4: 
Mana cost reduced from 10 to 0.
Damage increased from 29 to 34.

title: Roller Skates
content:
Roller Skates are pre-Hardmode mount-summoning items that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant or Skeleton Merchant. There are four different color variants with identical functionalities. Unlike other mounts that override the player's movement stats with their own stats, Roller Skates only increase the player's movement stats by a flat amount, meaning the player will still benefit from various movement speed boosts when mounting Roller Skates. These stat increases are detailed below:

Increased maximum movement speed by 5 mph.
Increased acceleration by 0.375 tiles/second².
These bonuses are applied after most movement speed calculations, therefore they are not affected by most movement speed multipliers.
The only exception to this is the additional movement speed multiplier gained from running on Asphalt Blocks, see Notes for details.
Increased jump speed by 1.
Increased jump duration by 2.
These bonuses are applied after all positive jump height calculations, but before all of the negative, therefore they are not affected by positive multipliers (e.g. Frog Leg), but are affected by negative multipliers (e.g. Oozed).
Additionally, they also grant the following effects:

Velocity is not lost when moving.
Allows the player to move on Minecart Tracks.
Their minimum speed (or coasting speed) matches the player's current block placement speed. By default, this is 8 mph. Because tile placement speed is capped to 300%, the theoretical maximum coasting speed is 27 mph.


== Types ==


=== From Traveling Merchant ===


=== From Skeleton Merchant ===


== Notes ==
The coasting speed can be increased by the High Spirits buff, Builder Potion buff, Brick Layer (or its upgrades), or by having used the Ambrosia item.
The Brick Layer and its upgrades do not stack with each other to increase coasting speed.
Note that the placement speed from the Brick Layer will only apply while holding a non-Torch block. This behavior also means that there is no bonus without holding a block.
The coasting speed is increased when holding any variants of Minecart Tracks or Ropes, due to them having a lower use time than other blocks.
Players cannot grab and travel along ropes while using Roller Skates, however.
Unlike with most mounts, it can be used with hooks, wings, and a dash.
Unlike with most mounts, a player mounted with Roller Skates remains 3 tiles tall, allowing them to enter doors.
The Cloud in a Bottle and its variants can be used with Roller Skates.
Since Roller Skates increase the player's movement speed by a flat amount, the player will still benefit from the top running speed granted by sprinting accessories like Hermes Boots.
The player cannot fly with Rocket Boots (or its upgrades) while using Roller Skates, and having them equipped will not increase the player's flight time with wings.
Running on Asphalt Blocks further multiplies the top running speed by 2.25× and the deceleration rate by 1.6×.
For top running speed, this does not result in an effective multiplier of 7.875×. This is because after applying the initial 3.5×, the game then adds 5 mph granted by the mount and multiplies the result by 2.25×.
The resulting top running speed is roughly 7.875× of the base running speed + 12 mph.
For deceleration rate, this results in an effective multiplier of 3.2×.


== Tips ==
Roller Skates can make building a Wall of Flesh arena easier, as they can ride on Minecart Tracks and allow more free movement than the Digging Molecart.
They can make building with Conveyor Belts easier, as they counteract conveyor's motion. Brick Layer (or its upgrades) and holding a typical block (to activate Brick Layer) raises Roller Skates' minimum speed to 14 mph, while conveyors move at 13 mph. Adding Ambrosia does not change this, seemingly due to rounding.
Roller Skates synergize with most wings that can hover, potentially doubling their flight time. Lazure's Barrier Platform, Hoverboard, Betsy's Wings, Nebula Mantle, Vortex Booster, and Celestial Starboard consume their flight time at half rate while hovering not pressing directional input, and Roller Skates let them maintain horizontal movement without holding directional input.
Despite not formally granting immunity, Roller Skates suppress the effects of slowing debuffs such as Chilled and Mighty Wind.


== Trivia ==
Roller Skates were first seen in the March 2024 State of the Game blog.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.8: Fixed Roller Skates preventing wings from appearing under certain circumstances.
Desktop 1.4.5.7: 
Reworked to scale with the player's movement stats.
Now grants movement speed, acceleration speed, and jump height.
Preserves momentum when airborne at high speed.
Moving at block placement speed unchanged.
Fixed Roller Skates slowing down the Celestial Starboard.
Desktop 1.4.5.4: Fixed Roller Skates erroneously preventing fire blocks from inflicting Burning.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: Introduced.

Console 1.4.5: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.5: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.5: Introduced.

title: Enchanted Pixie Dust
content:
The Enchanted Pixie Dust is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Pixie. While in this form, the player will emit a dim light in a 15-block radius and gain infinite flight. Additionally, the player will be able to fit through 1-tile gaps and their hurt sound is replaced with a twinkling sound. If the player has any dashes equipped, they can also perform a dash by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled. The player loses their ability to use other items, and doing so will result in the player dismounting and returning to normal. It is dropped by Pixies with a 1/200 (0.5%) chance after defeating any mechanical boss.


== Notes ==
The pixie will move at a maximum speed of 23 mph in the cardinal directions and 33 mph diagonally. The speed is reduced to 50% in water and lava, and to 25% in honey.
The pixie form's dash inherits the velocity, length, and unique effects of the player's equipped dash.
While in the pixie form, the player takes up less space, only being 0.5 tiles wide and 0.875 tiles tall.
Like other transformation mounts that reduce the player's size, if the player attempts to dismount in a place where they cannot fit, the dismount will fail. On the third attempt, the player will be teleported to the nearest open space and dismount. If there is no valid location within 25 tiles to the top and left of the player's feet and 24 tiles to the bottom and right of the player's feet, the player will instead be teleported to their world spawn point.


== Tips ==
Using a swimming buff, such as the Neptune's Shell, will restore the movement speed to its maximum while in water. However, only the Flipper Potion or Fishron Wings will restore it to its maximum in all liquids.


== Trivia ==
If the player is named "Khaios", the color will change to black with green particles.
The mount resembles a Fairy instead of a Pixie.

title: Guide:Surviving in the Jungle Temple
content:
The Jungle Temple, also known as the Lihzahrd Temple, is a big structure that is located in the Underground Jungle, with no surface entrance.
It can only be accessed after defeating Plantera in the hardmode Underground Jungle, and exploring it is mandatory to progress to the Lunar Events.
The place is usually explored to obtain the materials needed for Solar Tablets(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and to obtain the drops from the boss of the area, the Golem. Even with post-Plantera gear, surviving in the place can be challenging, due to the very strong enemies and the considerably high amount of traps.


== Recommended Gear ==


=== Armor ===
Hallowed has great defensive abilities from its set bonus, and works with all four classes.
Chlorophyte armor is the best for Melee players. Turtle armor has more defense, but smaller offensive bonuses.
Shroomite armor is the best choice for Ranged users.
Spectre armor is the strongest armor available for Mage characters.
Spooky armor is the best for summoners. Tiki armor is a comparable alternative.


=== Weapons ===
For Melee users:

Terra Blade or Seedler(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are the best Swords available.
The Eye of Cthulhu(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is the strongest Yoyo.
Vampire Knives are a good choice because of their high DPS and lifesteal.
Paladin's Hammer is a strong weapon, especially against crowds.
Using a Death Sickle is recommended due to it being able to shoot through walls.
The Scourge of the Corruptor is useful due to the tiny eaters being able to chase enemies.
Shadowflame Knife(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Light Discs are still decent weapons.
If used correctly, the Fetid Baghnakhs(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can deal an extreme amount of damage to all enemies.
For Ranged users:

The Megashark or Sniper Rifle with Crystal Bullets are two of the best guns available.
The Tactical Shotgun with Chlorophyte Bullets is also a solid choice.
The Tsunami is the strongest bow available.
The Chlorophyte Shotbow and the Pulse Bow(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) are also powerful bows to be obtained without defeating other bosses.
Holy Arrows, Chlorophyte Arrows, and Venom Arrows are excellent arrows to use with diverse abilities. Venom Arrows are the best for the Pulse Bow, as said bow negates any special effects from custom arrows.
The Dart Rifle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Pistol(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) with Cursed Darts(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Crystal Darts(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are good for crowds.
The Nail Gun(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is decent as well.
For Magic users:

The Nightglow(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Stellar Tune(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Razorblade Typhoon, and Bubble Gun are the best weapons for raiding the temple, capable of easily destroying the crowds. However, they are often difficult to obtain.
The Inferno Fork is good for both crowds and single targets.
The Spirit Flame(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Crystal Serpent(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are still solid weapons.
The Shadowbeam Staff and Magical Harp make full use of their bouncing, piercing projectiles due to the enclosed nature of the Temple.
Several secondary items can massively help with the horde of enemies in the Jungle Temple:
The Magnet Sphere synergies well with most other weapons.
Using Rainbow Gun can easily lock down tight hallways with its lingering projectile.
Using a Nimbus Rod to cover a vertical drop from layer to layer allows for a good crowd control of enemies.
A Clinger Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can keep almost all enemies at bay with its wall of Cursed Flames, however, the Lihzahrds' second phase can sometimes push through it with its speed.
A Golden Shower helps applying Ichor to enemies, making other weapons more effective against them.
For Summoners:

The Raven Staff are the best for crowd control, while the Desert Tiger Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is better for single targets.
The Sanguine Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Blade Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are still decent, despite being obtained much earlier in the game. The latter may need specialized optimizations, though.
The Tempest Staff is great against the slower enemies in the temple.
In terms of whips, the best few are the Dark Harvest(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Morning Star(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Kaleidoscope(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Morning Star and even a Durendal(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) might be preferred due to the difficulty of obtaining the others.
The Firecracker(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) specially synergizes with the Desert Tiger Staff.
The Staff of the Frost Hydra or any of the Tavernkeep's Sentries are also good to have.


=== Accessories ===
Wings are almost mandatory at this point.
Mobility accessories such as the Shield of Cthulhu(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Tabi are always good. The Master Ninja Gear is a helpful upgrade of the Tabi.
Good damage increasing accessories include:
The Class Emblems
The Fire Gauntlet (In Nintendo 3DS version, the Mechanical Gloves) for melee users
The Stalker's Quiver(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Molten Quiver(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Magic Quiver for bows, the Sniper Scope and Recon Scope(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for firearms
The Celestial Emblem(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) for mages
The Papyrus Scarab and Necromantic Scroll for summoners
An upgrade of the Mana Flower, such as the Magnet Flower(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Mana Cloak(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is very helpful for sustained usage of magic weapons.
The Magic Cuffs or Celestial Cuffs(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) are pretty good for quickly regaining mana as a mage.
The Frozen Shield(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) greatly increases survivability and grants knockback resistance. The Charm of Myths also increases survivability by allowing quicker healing.


=== Potions ===
Hunter Potion is useful for detecting enemies in the next room or layers.
A Dangersense Potion(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) is extremely useful as it will highlight the traps all over the temple.
Any items that grant Exquisitely Stuffed(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is useful in most situations, including in the Jungle Temple.


=== Other ===
A Grappling Hook is useful to stand out of the Lihzahrds' reach.
Having an abundance of lightings is greatly recommended for exploring the temple.
It's also good to use the bonuses of a Sharpening Station(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Ammo Box(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), Crystal Ball, War Table(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Bewitching Table(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), depending on class.
A Slice of Cake(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) grants a general mobility buff, which is useful for all classes.


== Exploration ==
There are two main enemies in the Jungle Temple:

Lihzahrds have two forms: they'll first walk on two legs, and then when they get to half Health, they'll become quadrupeds, becoming much faster and immune to knockback.
Flying Snakes possess the ability to fly and do considerably higher damage, however they are significantly more vulnerable to knockback and have less health.
Additionally, Mimics occasionally spawns in the Jungle Temple. All Golden Chests in the temple are to be treated as such.
The enemies are not the only threat found, the Jungle Temple is notorious for its large amount of Traps, such as:

Super Dart Traps, which will launch high-speed poisonous darts;
Flame Traps, which will deal very large amounts of damage with a short range;
Spiky Ball Traps, which drops spiky balls that bounce and linger around for a long time;
Spear Traps, that jab you from above with high-speed spears;
Wooden Spikes, which will deal damage to you when touched.
One should move slowly and carefully, and pay attention to the floor. If you can't seem to spot pressure plates very well, you can stick to traversing across the ceiling or you can hold (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Wire Cutter to enable you to see the wires leading to some of the traps. Cutting them will disable the traps and allow you to pass safely. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Additionally, traps can also be mined with a Pickaxe. Explosives can also be used to easily remove Wooden Spikes.
At the end of the Temple lies a wide, expansive area where a single Lihzahrd Altar can be found. The Lihzahrd Power Cells found in chests and dropped by local enemies can be used to activate it and summon the boss of the area, the Golem.

title: Life Booster
content:
The Life Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Life Nebula buff which immediately increases the player's health regeneration rate by 3 health per second for 8 seconds. When a Life Booster is picked up while the Life Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Life Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Life Booster expires, and the Life Nebula buff decreases by one level. All levels of Life Booster nullify the effects of damaging debuffs, such as from Poisoned or On Fire!, with the exception of Hunger.
Life Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.


== Tiers ==


== Notes ==
Despite being such a powerful buff, debuffs that temporarily negate natural health regeneration, such as On Fire!, Poisoned, and Acid Venom completely invalidate any extra life regeneration it may provide.
In multiplayer, any player can pick up Life Boosters and benefit from the Life Nebula buff, even if they are not wearing Nebula armor. Additionally, picking up a Life Booster will grant all nearby players (within a 43.75-tile radius) one instance of Life Nebula. If the player acquiring the Life Booster is on a team, only nearby players within that team will obtain the buff.


== See also ==
Damage Booster
Mana Booster


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Reduced healing per Life Booster stack from 5 HP/second to 3 HP/second.
If a Life Booster is placed into the player's inventory using an inventory editor, it will no longer appear as its frames of animation, and will instead be properly animated.

title: The Hallow
content:
The Hallow is a Hardmode surface biome characterized by pastel-colored fairytale graphics, with cyan-colored grass, multicolored trees, and a large rainbow in the background, as well as similarly whimsical-looking (though quite dangerous) enemies. The Underground Hallow biome can be found directly beneath a naturally-generated Hallow biome.
The Hallow does not exist in newly generated worlds, with the exception of select special or secret world seeds. When the Wall of Flesh is defeated for the first time and the world converts to Hardmode, a diagonal stripe of the Hallow biome extending from the surface to the bottom of the world will be generated, converting all applicable tiles to their Hallowed variant. This initial conversion can replace preexisting sections of the world's "evil biome" (Corruption or Crimson). If areas of the Jungle or Glowing Mushroom biome are included in the conversion area, Stone will be converted, but grass on Mud Blocks will be unaffected.
Once generated, the Hallow spreads in a manner similar to the evil biomes; Pearlstone, Pearlsand, and dirt blocks growing Hallowed grass will spread Hallow to neighboring blocks, causing Hallow enemies to spawn over ever-larger areas. Hallow can also be seeded in new areas via Hallowed Seeds, Holy Water, or Blue Solution. See below or the Biome spread page for more details.
The Hallow, unlike Crimson and Corruption, cannot spread through mud areas such as those found in Jungles or Glowing Mushroom biomes, and Sunflowers can stop its surface spreading like they would stop the spread of evil biomes in pre-hardmode.
The Dryad can tell the player the percentage of Hallow and Corruption/Crimson in the world.


== Contents ==


== Spread ==

The Hallow spreads itself, similar to the evil biomes. This means that it slowly converts certain susceptible tiles that are in the vicinity of existing Hallowed blocks. Defeating Plantera for the first time in the world reduces the speed of the Hallow's spread by 1/2 (50%). If the Hallow is introduced into a pre-Hardmode world, its spread will be very limited, similarly to the evil biomes.


== Hallowed Desert ==

When the Hallow spreads into the Desert, it becomes a Hallowed Desert. It is very similar to the Hallow: the music theme is the same, the enemies are the same (except for the Light Mummy and Crystal Thresher), and the background becomes slightly different.
The sand is also replaced by pearlsand. Although their color is different, Cacti still drop Cactus when cut, and Waterleaf plants are also able to grow.


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
An artificial Hallow biome requires at least 125 Hallowed blocks, such as Hallowed grass, Pearlstone, Pearlsand, or Pink Ice.
In Hardmode, all enemies in the Hallow have a chance of dropping a Hallowed Key.
Making an artificial Hallow biome in a pre-Hardmode world (for example via Blue Solution) will change the background and music, though no Hallow enemies will spawn.
However, oddly, Lightning Bugs will still spawn at night.
The Corruption or Crimson is unable to overlap the Hallow.
The Hallow can spread to Grass and Flower Walls.
Based on the source code, the Dryad considers the Hallow to be "good", as opposed to the Corruption or Crimson, which she considers "bad." However, she does not consider the world to be "pure" until all three are eradicated.
Again, on beginning Hardmode the Hallow can overlay the Jungle, and this will convert stone but not Jungle grass. Due to the Jungle being mostly Mud, this can lead to there not being enough Hallow blocks present to consistently spawn the biome's enemies. However, the Pearlstone present can still produce small fragments of Hallow biome, which can cause water to be colored pink.


== Trivia ==

The Hallow does not have an alternate version, unlike The Corruption (which has The Crimson). Originally, a candy-land themed alternate for the Hallow was planned, but the idea was scrapped before development.
The verb to hallow means to make holy, indicating that the name Hallow likely means holy land.
In Celebration Mk 10 worlds, Hallowed grass will spawn on Floating Islands at world generation, allowing for the creation of a Hallow biome pre-Hardmode.
In a similar way, the secret seeds Does that sparkle and Too easy cause worlds to automatically generate with a Hallow biome, although the latter starts the player off in Hardmode.
On occasion, winged unicorns and swarms of Pixies and Gastropods can be seen in the background of the surface Hallow as ambience.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, the Hallow was created by the Ancient Spirit of Light once the world's guardian (the Wall of Flesh) is defeated. It is an extreme overcompensation of purity that exists to cure threats to the critical balance of life and serves to counterbalance the methods of the evil biomes.


== Gallery ==
Every Hallow background has a rainbow in it.

		
		
		
		
		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Lady Of The Lake can now be obtained through fishing.

Added Prismatic Lacewing and Gelatin Crystal, which summon the two Hallowed bosses, the Queen Slime and Empress of Light.
Added three new backgrounds.
Added Otherworldly Hallow track from the canceled Terraria: Otherworld.
Biome block requirement changed from 100 to 125.
Desktop 1.2.1: The Crimson and Hallow can now counteract each other.
Desktop 1.2.0.3: Hardmode Crimson, Corruption, and Hallow spread is now slowed after killing Plantera instead of any mechanical boss.
Desktop 1.1: Introduced.

The Crimson and Hallow can now counteract each other.

title: Guide:Dungeon Guardian strategies
content:
The Dungeon Guardian is statistically the strongest enemy in Terraria (if not counting invincible enemies), and only spawns when you move below -3 (underground) depth in the Dungeon before defeating Skeletron. Once Skeletron is defeated, Dungeon Guardians will no longer spawn. The only reason to fight it is for the Bone Key it drops.


== Terrain Preparation ==

You need to be in a world where Skeletron has not been defeated. Otherwise, it will not spawn. As it will instantly kill you when it touches you, the only way to defeat it is to outrun it. Therefore you have five good options for terrain:

The first option is simply use the whole map, by using Gravitation Potions to move around. You will fall faster than it and you can move diagonally to go even faster.
The second option is a very long Skybridge. You will be equally fast as the Dungeon Guardian when running horizontally and jumping with wings. If you want to outrun it make a diagonal skybridge or build the skybridge out of Asphalt.
The third option is to simply use a good pair of Wings or a flying mount such as the Cosmic Car Key, Witch's Broom (Expert Mode only) or Shrimpy Truffle (Also Expert Mode only) with a clear, open space.
The fourth option requires a rail system that goes in a circle, using a fast Minecart (Using a boosted Minecart is more useful) or Booster Tracks. This can also be automated with Traps, such as Spike Ball or Spear Traps within the rail circle of with summons and a Star Wrath.
The fifth option is to set up a Hoik loop. As the Dungeon Guardian spawns, use a recall potion to get to a spawn point set up near the Hoik loop, and mount it. If timed correctly, you will loop around fast enough to make the Dungeon Guardian constantly change direction, and, as a result, it will simply spin in tight circles in the center of the Hoik loop.
To reliably "summon" the Dungeon Guardian, it is recommended to dig a shaft straight down from outside the dungeon. The Depth Meter or any of its upgrades are recommended for this.
If the player has access to the Mechanic ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)and Steampunker) it is possible to build a Teleporter arena (example). This can make the fight dramatically easier, especially if the Teleporters are automated with Timers. As the Mechanic is found in the Dungeon, it is required for the player to bring materials from a world where Skeletron has already been defeated.


== Gearing Up ==


=== Armor ===
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Frost armor is a great choice, as the Dungeon Guardian is not immune against the Frostburn debuff, greatly increasing damage dealt. It also provides a good critical strike chance bonus.
If using magic weapons, the Spectre Armor(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) with the Spectre Mask will release extra projectiles which will deal even more damage to the Guardian.
Another option is to use Beetle Armor with the shell along with defensive accessories and an Endurance Potion and Lifeforce Potion to give you a fairly good chance of surviving a hit from the Dungeon Guardian should it happen to hit you. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions)Titanium armor's set bonus allows the player to survive a hit every 30 seconds.
You can also use Tiki Armor if you want to use Minions.


=== Weapons ===
Because of its massive defense, no weapon will deal more than 1 damage (2 with a critical hit), so it is much better to use weapons with a very high rate of fire or multiple projectiles. It is recommended to use any prefix that increases critical hit chance or firing speed.

For Melee users

The Flairon releases many bubbles when used, which can deal rapid damage to the Guardian.
The Vampire Knives, the Scourge of the Corruptor and Seedler(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are useful due to their multiple projectiles and fast rate of fire.
Solar Eruption(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) has great reach and hits many times when used.
Though very late into the Game, the Zenith(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) provides a long range attack, whilst each sword deals hits, allowing for consistent, rapid damage to the Guardian
For Ranged users

The best guns are the Chain Gun, S.D.M.G(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Vortex Beater(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Megashark, Gatligator(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), Minishark, or Uzi, listed in decreasing order of effectiveness. Combine them with Crystal Bullets for additional damage from the released fragments.
The best bow is the Phantasm(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), with the Tsunami and Eventide(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as passable alternatives. Combine them with Holy Arrows or Luminite Arrows for more damage.
The Piranha Gun is very easy to use and deals damage at a decent rate.
(3DS version) A bow with Heart Arrows stuns the Dungeon Guardian, making the fight a lot easier.
For Magic users

Some of the fastest magic weapons include the Razorpine, Laser Machinegun(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Bat Scepter or Blizzard Staff. Out of these, the Razorpine is the most effective if used correctly.
The Lunar Flare(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) has a very high fire rate, along with a high critical strike chance, making it another useful weapon.
The Nebula Arcanum(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can hit a lot of times if used correctly.
The Last Prism(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be used effectively, however you might need to use a Mana Flower and a large quantity of super mana potions.
For Summoners

The Stardust Dragon Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Xeno Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and the Terraprisma(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) deal damage at a fast rate. The Blade Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), performs the best due to its very fast attack speed.


=== Accessories ===
As the Dungeon Guardian will instantly kill you, your defense is entirely irrelevant. For this reason, it is recommended that you use mobility accessories rather than defensive ones (it's possible to survive up to 3 hits with enough defense, damage reduction and a lifeforce potion, this however comes at the cost of damage output and mobility, making it unlikely to succeed without the use of teleporters, minecarts or some other mobility method). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Note that any equipment that gives a chance to dodge an attack is ignored by the Dungeon Guardian. As with weapons, prefixes that boost your critical strike chance or movement speed will be much more valuable than damage or defense.

The best Wings to use are Fishron, Solar or Stardust Wings. The Hoverboard, Celestial Starboard, Betsy Wings, Vortex Booster, and Nebula Mantle have the ability to hover, which is very good as well. With any type of wings, the Frog Leg is very useful because it provides 50% increased flight speed.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)If you are in Expert Mode, the Soaring Insignia grants infinite flight time, which is invaluable during this fight.
Master Ninja Gear gives you the ability to dash, (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) as well as a chance to dodge a hit.
The Destroyer Emblem and Eye of the Golem increase critical strike chance.
The Pygmy Necklace, Necromantic Scroll and Papyrus Scarab increase the maximum number of minions.
If you use a Skybridge, a Cobalt Shield or better will prevent enemies from knocking you into the Dungeon Guardian.


==== Mounts ====
The Cosmic Car Key and Shrimpy Truffle are both strong choices. The Witch's Broom, while being Expert Mode only, also boasts a greater horizontal speed than that of the Dungeon Guardian
The Blessed Apple is good if using a sky bridge.
Another trick is to use a looping minecart track and use the Mechanical Cart as its lasers can increase dps.
The Black Spot is a suitable choice due to its infinite flight, but it moves slower than the Dungeon Guardian horizontally and only matches its speed verically. It will, however, move faster when travelling diagonally.


==== Other ====
The Rod of Discord allows you to teleport away from the Guardian. In combination with a sufficiently fast mount, such as the Blessed Apple or Ancient Horn, the Rod of Discord has the ability to render the fight extremely simple, so long as the player does not accidentally teleport into the Dungeon Guardian or wait too long to teleport away from it.


=== Potions ===
Gravitation Potions, in case you use that method.
Swiftness Potions and something to give you the Well Fed buff to increase your movement speed.
Any Mana Potions if you use magic weapons.
Rage Potions increase critical strike chance for all classes. An Ale or Crystal Ball will increase it further for Melee and Magic weapons respectively.
Potions that provide light, such as Hunter Potion, Night Owl Potion and Shine Potion allow you to see better at night.
A Summoning Potion can be used for an extra minion.
An Ammo Reservation Potion is great for saving bullets.


== Specific strategies ==


=== Boosted Cart Method ===

If you have killed the three Mechanical Bosses in Expert Mode, you will have access to the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It upgrades all minecarts to a speed which is faster than the Dungeon Guardian, but this means that you may end up despawning it. You should control your speed to allow it to keep up.
Therefore, you can make a long, flat minecart track to traverse across with a boosted minecart to combat the Dungeon Guardian at a distance.

When you are riding a Minecart on a track that's directly over a Teleporter and it is activated at that moment, it can teleport you and the Minecart you're riding to another rail that's on top of another Teleporter, keeping your momentum in the process. The branching rail on top is set to a passive state (you pass through it on the bottom line without switching on to it). The bottom Teleporter has a Pressure Plate Track over the Teleporter to trigger it, but the top one does not. The top rail has a bumper at the end of the line to make you turn around to the other direction without losing speed.
Lastly, this only works if you are moving slowly enough such that the Dungeon Guardian is lured in between the two Teleporters upon teleporting. Otherwise, you'll simply run straight into him in the same manner of if you just had a bumper at the end of the rail.


=== Hoik method ===
With the use of Hoiks, the Dungeon Guardians won't be able to reach you, so the fight will be a lot safer. The Hoik should be the size of the first room in the Dungeon, anything bigger is unnecessary. After that, all you need to do is shoot at it or kill it with Minions such as the Stardust Dragon.


=== UFO Method ===
If you have the Cosmic Car Key, you can take advantage of the fact that the UFO mount's horizontal speed is the same as the Dungeon Guardian's at 41 mph. This means, that if you travel in a horizontal direction, the Dungeon Guardian is unable to catch you and will maintain a constant distance, allowing you to attack freely until it dies. However, the vertical speed of the Cosmic Car Key is less than 41 mph, if you travel upwards, the Dungeon Guardian can catch and kill you, so caution is required when changing direction. Because the Cosmic Car Key travels at 58 mph diagonally, you can increase the distance by travelling diagonally for a while. Reducing the distance can be done by releasing the left/right keys for a short time.
It is also recommended that you use a high rate of fire gun or projectile shooting sword, like the Terra Blade, Influx Waver, or the Vortex Beater.


=== Bee Mount Method ===
If you have obtained the Honeyed Goggles from the Queen Bee, the Bee Mount can be used to outrun the Dungeon Guardian by moving up and down in a large sine wave, as its Diagonal Speed of 51 mph is enough to outrun the Dungeon Guardian. Pairing this with any long-ranged weapon, you can stay consistently not very far ahead of the Dungeon Guardian, whilst launching continuous damage at it. With this, you could defeat the Dungeon Guardian without even meeting the Wall of Flesh, and without any extreme prep time (outside of fighting several Queen Bees).
Make sure to hold ▼ Downbefore the bee gets too tired after an ascent!


=== Shadow Jousting Lance method ===
The damage that a Shadow Jousting Lance(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (or any lance) gets from momentum doesn't have a limit, therefore it can be paired with the Mollusk Whistle or the Inner Tube and a very deep pool of water to gain ridiculous amounts of momentum, and, in turn, damage, by surfacing from the bottom to the top of the pool of water. This damage appears to be able to one-shot the Dungeon Guardian with the right setup. See this demonstration of the strategy on YouTube.

title: Blue Chicken Egg
content:
The Blue Chicken Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Blue Chicken that follows the player. The Blue Chicken Egg can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 25 Gold.


== Trivia ==
This item is a reference to the 2016 farm life simulation role-playing game Stardew Valley, in which the Blue Chicken is a rare variant of normal Chickens.
The buff tooltip is a reference to the fact that in Stardew Valley, Blue Chickens are only available after the player has earned enough friendship with Shane, an NPC in the game.
In Stardew Valley, blue chickens actually hatch from white eggs, and there are no blue eggs.

title: Blade Staff
content:
The Blade Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons an Enchanted Dagger minion. It flies towards enemies and slashes through them repeatedly at a fast pace. It also has 25 armor penetration. Enchanted Daggers arrange themselves along a carousel above the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Blade Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime.
Its best modifier is generally Focused, but in some cases Ballistic or Worthy (see below for details), as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it. Although the Eager modifier is recognized in-game as its best modifier, it can be considered excessive as the majority of enemies do not have enough defense for the extra armor penetration to provide a greater benefit.


== Notes ==
The Enchanted Dagger applies 10 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hitting enemies, meaning it can hit up to 6 times per second.
In practice, when Enchanted Daggers are attacking they will not be colliding with enemies for the whole time, and their actual hit rate will be closer to 4 times per second.
The Enchanted Dagger can target enemies that are up to 50 tiles away, and will automatically return to the player's side if it is more than 56.25 tiles away.
Tag damage bonuses that come from whips and modifiers are reduced to 66.9% for the Enchanted Dagger, rounded down. The extra damage from Durendal's enchanted energy and Electric Eel's electric energy tag do not count as tag damage, and these fixed damages will not be reduced.


== Tips ==
In most cases, Focused is the modifier that provides the highest damage; however, depending on damage bonuses and the target's defense, the highest-damage modifier may vary:
A Ballistic Blade Staff (+5 tag damage) will only match or exceed a Focused one (+3 tag damage) when both of the following are true: the player's total summon damage bonuses are less than 86% and the whip's tag damage modulo 3 equals 1. Otherwise (i.e. when either condition is not met), Ballistic provides less damage than Focused.
If the armor penetration from Worthy adds exactly 2 damage, then Worthy deals the same damage as Focused. If it adds more than 2 damage, then Worthy's damage is greater; if it adds less, Focused is superior.
Eager deals more damage than Worthy if one of the following conditions is met:
Eager's armor penetration provides 6 damage and the player's summon damage bonus is below 86%.
Eager's armor penetration provides 7 damage and the summon damage bonus is below 186%.
Eager's armor penetration provides 8 damage.
Equivalently, Eager is the best modifier when the enemy's defense is at least 36 (or 52 with the Ichor debuff) and the player's summon damage bonus is below 86%; when the enemy's defense is at least 38 (or 54 with the Ichor debuff) and the summon damage bonus is below 186%; or when the enemy's defense is at least 40 (or 56 with the Ichor debuff).
The Enchanted Dagger benefits massively from whip tag damage and whip stacking. Most whips can more than double the minion's DPS due to its low base damage but high attack rate.
For example, the daggers synergize very well with the Reaping mechanic of the Dark Harvest, dealing high DPS against multiple targets. The daggers also synergize well with the Kaleidoscope, which has high summon tag damage.
On the other hand, the low base damage makes the Enchanted Daggers scale poorly with percentage-based damage bonuses, such as the Firecracker's explosion.
Although the Blade Staff has no base knockback, it can gain knockback from accessories like the Papyrus Scarab or buffs like Well Fed. This drastically increases its effectiveness against enemies that are affected by knockback, as several daggers can lock an enemy in place.
Like the Sanguine Staff and Terraprisma, the Blade Staff's precise movement, tracking, and fixed idle position make it an ideal choice against fast bosses and for crowd control.
Due to its rapid attack rate, it is an effective minion for killing a Dungeon Guardian.
The Blade Staff can also be a decent choice for melee users, who can passively increase their damage output with a Flask of Ichor.


== Trivia ==
The internal name of the Blade Staff is Smolstar.
Along with the Stardust Dragon Staff, Desert Tiger Staff, and Raven Staff, the Blade Staff is one of four summon weapons whose buff description is not “<name of minion> will fight for you”, instead being Death by a thousand cuts.
“Death by a thousand cuts”, or lingchi, was a torture and execution method used in China from roughly 900 CE until it was banned in 1905.
The Enchanted Dagger's behavior of hovering above the player's head could be a reference to the ancient Greek story of Damocles, a courtier of Dionysius I who was allowed to have his king's position of authority and fortune for one day. However, this came at the cost of having a sword hung above his throne, symbolizing the looming, omnipresent peril faced by people in positions of power.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Now has a tag damage penalty of 33%, which only applies to flat tag damage, and does not affect tag critical strike chance.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Removed the 25% tag damage penalty.
Removed mana cost (cost 10 mana previously).
Blade Staff tooltip now properly mentions that it ignores some enemy defense (functionality unchanged).
Desktop 1.4.4: Now has a tag damage penalty of 25%.
Desktop 1.4.1: No longer drops from Enchanted Swords, and now drops from Queen Slime.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.

title: Nurse
content:
The Nurse is an NPC who will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
The player's maximum health is greater than 100.
The Merchant is present.
The Nurse will fully restore the player's health and cure them of any active debuffs at the cost of coins (there are exceptions, see Notes and History).
Healing costs are 1 Copper per health restored, plus an additional 1 Silver per active debuff on the player, all multiplied by the Nurse's current Happiness price adjustment, and then doubled if playing on Expert Mode. Also, the Nurse charges increasing amounts of money for healing as the game progresses; these specific increases are listed below. Thus, at the start of the game, the cost of restoring 100 health can range from 75 Copper / 1 Silver 50 Copper (with maximum happiness) to 1 Silver 50 Copper / 3 Silver (with maximum unhappiness), while by endgame it can range from 1 Gold 50 Silver / 3 Gold up to 3 Gold / 6 Gold.
The Nurse will defend herself against nearby enemies by throwing green syringes that damage and poison enemies for 3–5 seconds. She can also throw red syringes to heal herself and other nearby NPCs for 20 health, which can also home in on targets. She deals 8 / 12 / 14 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.


== Price increases ==
The cost of healing changes based on three factors: The Nurse's current Happiness, game progression, and Expert Mode. Happiness affects the Nurse's price by raising or lowering it to within a range of 75% to 150% of its base (in the same way that other NPCs' prices are affected by their happiness). Playing in Expert (or Master) mode further affects prices by permanently doubling them. Progression-based price increases are based on which bosses have been defeated in the current world. These increases are listed in the table below; only the single highest applicable increase is chosen and applied.


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Nurse will transform into her Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. She can be returned to her classic look by submerging her in Shimmer again or spraying her with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
If the player has an active debuff and is at full health, the heal option will also be available.
If planning on healing and drinking Ale, make sure to drink the Ale after healing, as Tipsy is technically a debuff and will be cured by the Nurse.
The Nurse cannot remove Potion Sickness, Water Candle, and Creative Shock, nor does she charge extra for them.
Like with all NPCs' attacks, the Nurse cannot heal NPCs or herself when the player is talking to her. Additionally, she cannot heal NPCs when drowning.
The Nurse can throw one healing syringe per 10–19 ticks, and the cooldown between throws is 5–14 ticks. As a result, her healing per second is 50 health on average.
If a healing syringe thrown by the Nurse does not hit her target, it will begin homing in on them.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The Nurse can be used as a "healing station" when at low health during a boss fight, by teleporting to the spawn point (using a Magic/Ice Mirror or one of its upgrades) where the Nurse is present. Autopause can be used to grant more time.


== Names ==
The Nurse may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
There appears to be conflict between the Nurse and the Mechanic during a Blood Moon. During this time, the Merchant has a chance of saying, “Oh, great. I can hear <name of Mechanic> and <name of Nurse> arguing from here.”
The Arms Dealer seemingly has romantic interest in her according to his quotes when the Nurse is present. This is also reflected in the Nurse's quote “Hey, has <name of Arms Dealer> mentioned needing to go to the doctor for any reason? Just wondering.” The Nurse, through other NPC dialogue, is implied to already be in a romantic relationship with the Arms Dealer as noted by the Stylist in her quote, “Mhmm, I heard from <name of Party Girl> that <name of Mechanic>'s friend <name of Nurse> spent her boyfriend's last paycheck on shoes.”
The Nurse is depicted in a painting called Nurse Lisa, a reference to the famous portrait painting Mona Lisa by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci.
When talking to the Nurse while in a crowded area, she will say, “Hey, I dislike the lack of social distancing here.” This is a reference to the COVID-19 pandemic that was ongoing at the time of Journey's End's launch, when the quote was introduced, and the “social distancing” practice people were encouraged to follow by staying six feet or two meters away from one another in public.
During a Party, when the Nurse dons a party hat, her hairstyle is different. She wears it down instead of up in a ponytail; this makes sense as wearing a party hat while having hair in a ponytail would be cumbersome.

The Nurse's quote, “I don't give happy endings.” is a reference to happy endings, the practice of masseuses offering sexual favors to their clients at the end of a massage for additional payment.
The Nurse will not use this quote if the Blood and Gore setting is turned off.
Although the Zoologist is registered as hated by the Nurse, she does not seem to actually hate her. The dialogue indicates that the Nurse hates the Zoologist's unique anatomy more than the Zoologist herself: “Oh, I hate treating <name of Zoologist>, so difficult!”
However, such a phrase is also often used to describe someone who is being difficult, such as refusing to be still while being given a shot.
Her quote “I need to have a serious talk with <name of Guide>. How many times a week can you come in with severe lava burns?” most likely refers to the Guide Voodoo Doll being sacrificed in lava or being carried around by Voodoo Demons near pools of lava in the Underworld.
Her interaction phrase “The monsters of <world name> have slain you <number of non-PvP deaths> times already? I wonder which one picked up your banner...”, said when the player was slain between 25 and 99 times inclusive, refers to the fact that the player can obtain most enemies' respective banners when that enemy is slain every 50th time, and a few rarer ones give their banners if slain every 25th time.
One of the Nurse's possible names is Allison, which may be a reference to Allison Cameron, a specialist from the medical drama television series House.
 The Bestiary entry for the Nurse: "The Nurse's snarky attitude and poor bedside manner may be scary, but for a price, she will cure all that ails a wounded Terrarian."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
The Discount Card now also applies to the Nurse's healing service.
The Nurse can no longer remove Brain of Confusion's Cerebral Mindtrick buff.
Desktop 1.4.4: The Nurse can now comment on how often the player has been dying in her random dialogue.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Now charges increasing amounts of money for healing as the game progresses.
Fixed a bug where the condition for the quote about the Guide was that a Demon Eye (rather than the Guide) is present.
The Nurse can no longer heal NPCs when drowning.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Sprite updated.
Desktop 1.2.3: Nurse no longer charges for or removes Heart Lantern and Campfire buffs. This also applies to the Potion Sickness and Water Candle debuffs.
Desktop 1.1: Now has random name given to her on spawn. Her deaths will be reported with this name. Also other NPCs will use it in their quotes. No longer spawns a second Nurse in multiplayer.
Desktop-Release: Introduced.

title: Key of Light
content:
The Key of Light is a craftable item which spawns a Hallowed Mimic when placed in any slot of any empty Chest. The world must be in Hardmode and the only item inside the Chest must be a single Key of Light.
The Hallowed Mimic is spawned as soon as the Chest is closed, consuming both the Key of Light and the Chest.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
If utilizing Autopause, the Hallowed Mimic will not spawn until the game is unfrozen again. On  Console, the Hallowed Mimic will not spawn unless Autopause is disabled.
Placing a Key of Light in a storage item other than a Chest (such as a Barrel) will not spawn the Mimic.
The Hallowed Mimic does not have to be spawned in The Hallow; it can be summoned anywhere.
Placing a Key of Light in a Chest without closing it and directly opening another inventory interface (which is only possible if Autopause is disabled), such as that of another Chest, will not spawn the Mimic.
A Key of Light pulled into a chest by Wiring will not spawn the Mimic.

title: Creative Shock
content:
Creative Shock is a debuff inflicted during the Old One's Army event. Affected players can neither place nor remove blocks. The debuff will be canceled as soon as the player defeats the Old One's Army, the Eternia Crystal is destroyed, or they move outside of the debuff's area. The debuff area is calculated from the positions of the Mysterious Portals and the Eternia Crystal (see Notes for details). The debuff will be re-inflicted if the player moves back into the affected area.


== Causes ==


=== From environment ===


== Notes ==
Usually, the debuff area will comprise all of the space between the two Mysterious Portals, and will also extend 50 tiles from the portals' edges outwards in all directions.
More precisely, the game draws a rectangle around both Mysterious Portals and the Eternia Crystal. This rectangle is the smallest possible rectangle that still fully contains all three entities. The rectangle is then extended by 50 tiles in all four directions, and constitutes the debuff area. This means that the position of the Eternia Crystal may increase the size of the debuff area, e.g. if it is moved (via a Teleporter and/or hoik) outside of the space between the two portals.
Though Torches cannot be freed using pickaxes or drills under the debuff, they may be freed with ⚷ Open / Activate.
Cobwebs can be removed via tools or the player touching them, but they cannot be placed.
Explosives will destroy susceptible blocks.
Buckets cannot be used to add or remove liquids.
Wire and Actuators can still be placed.


== Trivia ==
Creative Shock rhymes with and is likely a reference to creator's block, a temporary psychological inhibition that prevents a writer, artist, or other creative individual from proceeding with their work.


== History ==

Desktop 1.3.4.2: Fixed bug where Drill Containment Unit was usable while Creative Shock was active.
Desktop 1.3.4: Introduced.

Console 1.17: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.1096.2: Introduced.

title: Bee Hive (biome)
content:
A Bee Hive is a mini-biome located in the Underground Jungle. The hive itself is made from Hive blocks; on the interior, it contains pools of honey and typically one Larva. Destroying the Larva summons the Queen Bee. Any projectile, tool, weapon, or enemy will destroy the Larva with a single hit, so caution should be taken around the Larva if the player is not ready to fight the Queen Bee.
The number of Bee Hives per world is dependent on world size: there are usually 6–8 hives in Small or Medium worlds, and 11–16 hives in Large worlds.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
In Drunk worlds, Bee Hives are significantly larger, have irregular outlines, and often contain multiple Larvae. Because of this, the amount of Bee Hives per world are typically less than normal.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Honey and Honey Blocks naturally spawn in small amounts in the Underground Jungle, however, contrary to popular belief, this is not a sign that a Bee Hive is nearby.
The bottom of the hive will be filled with honey. Standing in the honey provides a regeneration buff, but greatly slows the player's movement, which makes dodging difficult. If a player is stuck in the honey pool when they accidentally spawn Queen Bee, they will be acutely vulnerable and likely take many hits before they can escape. Placing platforms can help avoid falling into the honey pool. Care should be taken not to place platforms or anything else on a Larva, as that will break it.
A Larva can be hidden under the surface of the honey. If a hive seems not to have a visible Larva (or a large hive has only one) the player should be very cautious about using weapons in the honey or shooting into it, lest they face a surprise attack from the Queen Bee.
Any water poured onto the honey will create Honey Blocks. If a Larva is partly submerged or just under the surface, the forming blocks will break the Larva, summoning Queen Bee as usual.
If a hive is large enough, it can be made into a decent arena by (optionally) clearing the walls of the hive and adding platforms. This is not only useful for the Queen Bee fight, but also for the Plantera fight.
Wearing Chlorophyte armor or Orichalcum armor in the Underground Jungle is risky; either set bonus can accidentally break a Larva somewhere in the distance, setting off an unexpected Queen Bee fight. At this point the player should be fairly well equipped with Hardmode gear, but even so, a player can be caught off-guard.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Should the player be staying in a Bee Hive for extended periods of time, such as when building arenas for future battles against the Queen Bee, it may prove difficult or even life-threatening to survive due to the large numbers of Hornets that frequently accumulate within Bee Hives. For dealing with multiple Hornets, ranged weapons such as the Musket, The Undertaker, or gem staves can be useful for eliminating them quickly, as well as equipping a Bezoar, submerging in honey to get its regeneration buff, and placing Hornet Banners around the hive. The player should also try to place blocks around the Larvae to avoid accidentally awakening the Queen Bee by firing arrows or bullets at them. Weapons that can pierce enemies or travel through blocks such as whips, the Vilethorn, and the Gray Zapinator should be avoided or used extremely carefully within the hive's enclosed spaces.


== Trivia ==
Bee Hives usually have one Larva, but larger hives can contain two Larvae, and smaller hives have a low chance of not containing any Larva.
Very rarely, two Bee Hives can overlap, making one giant Bee Hive.
Larva can be painted like any other block.
In Not the Bees worlds, larva can spawn on any blocks. That means you can replace the blocks under the larva and it will not break. It will not break even with unique blocks, such as spikes from the Dungeon.

title: RGB
content:
Terraria features built-in RGB lighting effects for supported Razer, Logitech, Corsair and SteelSeries peripherals.
The vendor's respective lighting software must be installed for these effects to function (e.g. Razer Synapse/Razer Chroma, Logitech G Hub, Corsair iCUE or SteelSeries Engine).


== List of effects ==


=== Backgrounds ===
Most background effects have two versions; one for "high detail" peripherals such as keyboards, and one for "low detail" peripherals such as mice, headphones and keypads.
Effects listed lower on the following table will take priority. While multiple effects can be active at any time, those that are not transparent will block out any previous effects. For example, the Rain effect will display on top of most effects due to it being transparent, but the Blizzard effect (which is listed lower and is not transparent) will override it.


== SteelSeries Engine events ==
Terraria also features integration with SteelSeries Engine, adding events for the player's life, mana and breath percentage.


== Hidden settings ==
Config.json contains a few hidden RGB-related settings:

UseRazerRGB, UseLogitechRGB, UseCorsairRGB and UseSteelSeriesRGB can be used to enable/disable support for a specific vendor's peripherals.
RGBUpdatesPerSecond determines how many times per second a device will be sent new lighting information. Defaults to 45.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Added background effects for Deerclops and the Aether.
Desktop 1.4.2.2: Fixed an issue where SteelSeries support was following the UseLogitechRGB setting instead of UseSteelSeriesRGB.
Desktop 1.4.1: Added support for SteelSeries peripherals and SteelSeries Engine events.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: RGB-related error log entries now properly indicate that they are normal messages, and not errors. They also include a message indicating that RGB can be disabled.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

title: Kites
content:
Kites are miscellaneous items that can be held by the player. A kite can be flown during Windy Days or if the player runs fast enough while holding it. It can be raised higher with ⚒ Use / Attack and lowered with ⚷ Open / Activate. Lowering a kite back to the player will make them put it away. As long as the kite is above the player's head, the player will get the High Spirits buff which will increase in duration until it maxes out at 12 minutes and 1 second. The buff has the following effects:

+15% movement speed
+10% mining speed
+15% placement speed when placing blocks and walls
Up to +0.1 luck, depending on the remaining buff duration:
+0.1 with at least 9 minutes remaining
+0.067 with less than 9 minutes but at least 6 minutes remaining
+0.033 with less than 6 minutes but at least 3 minutes remaining
0 with less than 3 minutes remaining
A kite can be placed on the ground from the hotbar with ⚷ Open / Activate if the player is not currently flying the kite. The kite initially has some upwards momentum that carries it several blocks above the stake into the air, even on a calm day. 


== Types ==
There are 24 different types of kites, either dropped by certain enemies or purchased from NPCs.
Some kites are obtained by killing a slime that spawns attached to a Windy Balloon during the Windy Day event. Every other kite obtained from enemies can be dropped when the wind speed ≥ 20 mph, which sometimes overlaps with the Windy Day event as well. The Windy Day event does not guarantee that the other enemies mentioned will drop their kites.


== Notes ==
Kites can pass through solid blocks.
Kites can be used on non-Windy Days if the user maintains enough speed, but are more difficult to keep afloat.
Kites can be used while riding a mount, or while flying. However, the player will appear backwards while the kite is in use.
The color of the Pigron Kite is picked randomly each time it is used.
Kites can be used in reversed gravity, but will retain their normal orientation.
If a player fulfills the following conditions ("AFK") for more than 1 minute and has a kite in their inventory, their character will automatically equip and use the kite:
The player does not move.
The player is not using any item (except kites).
None of the following control keys are pressed: ▲ Up, ▼ Down, ◀ Left, ▶ Right, ↷ Jump, and Auto Select.
Failing to fulfill any of the conditions resets the timer.
The Koi Kite is normally always available for purchase, since the Zoologist does not appear before the Bestiary has been filled to at least 10%. The only exception is the secret world seed Vampirism, where she is the starting NPC.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
The three Hardmode jellyfish (Green Jellyfish, Blood Jelly, and Fungo Fish) do not have kite variants, unlike the pre-Hardmode Blue and Pink Jellyfish.


== Gallery ==

		
		
		
		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: 
Fixed leashed kites not flying or sometimes spawning into floors.
High Spirits buff changed:
Now only obtains duration when the kite is above its player's head.
Mining speed bonus reduced from 15% to 10%
Movement speed bonus reduced from 25% to 15%.
Desktop 1.4.5.6: Improved stability of newly appearing anchored kites.
Desktop 1.4.5.4: Leashed kites no longer break if they lack an anchor.

Can now be placed in the world as persistent background objects.
Kites are automatically taken out when the player is AFK for more than 1 minute.

Added a reel sound to kites.
Renamed "Crimson Bunny Kite" to "Vicious Bunny Kite" to match the NPC.

Increased drop rates for the Goldfish and Bunny Kites as well as the plain colored kites (kites that drop from slimes that spawn attached to a Windy Balloon) from 1/260 (0.38%) to 1/72 (1.39%) each.
Increased drop rate for the Bone Serpent Kite from 1/25 (4%) to 1/15 (6.67%).
