title: Battle Potion
content:
The Battle Potion is a buff potion which grants the Battle buff when consumed. The buff increases the spawn rate and maximum number of enemies and critters that can be on-screen at once by 100%, effectively doubling these rates. This lasts for 7 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The effect stacks with those of other items which allows a manual alteration of spawn rates, such as Water Candles. Similarly, items like Sunflowers or Calming Potions moderate the effect. For example, having both a Battle and a Calming Potion active will result in a spawn rate increase of only 54% (instead of 100%, due to the -23% of the Calming Potion) and an increase in the maximum number of enemies on-screen of only 40% (instead of 100%, due to the -30% of the Calming Potion).
Spawn rate effects like Battle Potions (and Water Candles) can be used to increase the spawn rates of events that do not have a set spawn rate, like the Blood Moon and Solar Eclipse.
Battle Potions and Water Candles cannot be used to increase the spawn rates of events like the Pumpkin and Frost Moon. The spawn rates of these events override spawn rate effects.
The Calming Potion has the opposite effect of the Battle Potion but as they are both potions, they are both considered buffs and as such can be canceled early. In contrast, the Water Candle effect is classified as a debuff.
The Battle Potion increases the spawn rates of NPCs, such as the Skeleton Merchant and bound Goblin Tinkerer, bound Mechanic, and bound Wizard.
The effect stacks between players because each player spawns their own NPCs. It also increases the maximum amount of enemies that can be spawned, allowing multiple players to drink them and spawn enemies at a much faster than intended rate.
The evil crafting material dropped from decrafting Battle Potions into Shimmer is dependent on the world evil; it will drop Rotten Chunks in Corruption worlds and Vertebra in Crimson worlds.
In Drunk worlds, the two world evils switch every in-game day, meaning Battle Potions will alternate between both materials each day.


== Tips ==
When using Battle Potions, beware when entering Dungeons, and even more so Hardmode Dungeons. Spawn rates can get out of control and difficult to handle even for the best equipped players.
Battle Potions can be used to farm affected events for rare drops, such as the Money Trough from the Blood Moon, Broken Hero Swords from the Solar Eclipse, and many items from the Pirate Invasion.
The Battle Potion is useful for increasing the chances of certain rare enemies and critters to spawn, such as the Martian Probe, Truffle Worm and Prismatic Lacewing.
Battle Potions should not be used during boss fights, as a significantly increased amount of enemies, or many instances of rare but extremely dangerous or annoying enemies spawning can easily overwhelm players while a boss is alive.

title: Golden Seaweed
content:
The Golden Seaweed was used to summon a pet Golden Turtle. It lasted until the player manually canceled the buff by using the Golden Seaweed again. It was obtained from Chests, but only on the  Amazon Fire TV. It was obtainable on other mobile devices via trading. 
This item was removed alongside all other mobile exclusive content in the Mobile 1.3.0.7 update.
Players on  Windows Phone who acquired the Golden Seaweed via trading continue to have access to it.


== Trivia ==
Despite the name of the item, its color was a reddish orange rather than gold (though the summoned Turtle was gold).
The turtle's flying animation may have been a reference to Gamera, a Japanese turtle monster similar to Godzilla that could fly, breathe fire, and was a friend to a child who loved turtles.

title: Legacy:Guide:Lepus strategies
content:
Lepus is a 3DS-exclusive boss spawned by the Suspicious Looking Egg. This page contains strategies to defeat the boss.


== Summoning ==
You must kill Corrupt Bunnies or Diseaster Bunnies during Easter, or disaster bunnies (not spawned by Lepus) when they will drop Suspicious Looking Eggs, which you must hold in your hand and use to summon Lepus. Try summoning him near your base or anywhere there is a small house made of strong materials. If you leave the area, Lepus will despawn.


== The Fight ==
Once you have spawned Lepus, he will be far from the player's current position and once you encounter him he will use jumping attacks and continually leap over the player, like the King Slime. He will occasionally lay small eggs which spawn Diseaster Bunnies or larger ones which spawn weaker Lepuses. Remember to destroy them if you are not confident as they may spawn more weaker Lepuses and overpower you.

One strategy for beginning players who do not have access to lava is to use Grenades, sold by the Demolitionist. First, make a platform above Lepus and wall him in. Then, throw the grenades down at him. This usually destroys his eggs when grenades are constantly thrown. Eventually, usually after 3 stacks of grenades, Lepus is defeated. To make sure that grenades are constantly thrown at Lepus, having another player pass you grenades as you throw them makes this strategy very easy.
Lepus is vulnerable to lava. Make a house with a layer of thin lava so the drops don't burn. Be sure to put the thin layer of lava on top of the house and near the sides. You may want lava protection to collect the drops. Because you can summon multiple Lepuses, this is a good way to make money. See Guide:Making Money
Build a wall out of any material and create an opening in it. After spawning the Lepus, attack it from the other side of the wall through the opening. Most weapons will do, such as swords, bows, and guns, but for his big hit box, it's easier to use a spear (early-game players may want to use the Trident for the best result.) If you want to weaken him first, use a Thorn Chakram in close range.
In multiplayer, one player can attack the Lepus through the opening while another player focuses on destroying Lepus Eggs as they can hatch into Diseaster Bunnies or even additional, weaker versions of the Lepus.
The Water Bolt is a good weapon of choice if you enclose Lepus In a small area and place a layer of platforms, just out of his reach. Since the Water Bolt’s attacks bounce off walls, you can place a thin layer of lava at the bottom and use water bolts to bounce of the walls of the enclosed area, and make Lepus unable to hatch eggs.
If you want to get the battle done early, then you may want to buy dynamite instead of grenades. However, there is a downside to using dynamite, since it destroys more blocks. If you use dynamite, then you will want to be away from your town.


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===

Boss battles can be won or lost before the battle ever starts.  Choose your equipment and have it ready; find and/or make potions and placed buffs; use the highest-tier food you have available; set up an arena appropriate to the boss; learn the strategies for the boss you're facing.
Prepare your Boss-fighting arena with adequate lighting, and Campfires and Heart Lanterns for health regeneration.
Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.  Depending on the game stage, this can include items such as Lesser Healing Potions or Honeyfins. On the  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile versions, Restoration Potions and Eggnogs(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) are healing potions with a shorter cooldown and the same net healing per second considering Potion Sickness.
Due to the shorter cooldown, they can be used earlier than Honeyfins without overhealing, which can lead to a higher amount of healing over the course of the whole fight.
Likewise, carry mana potions if you use Magic weapons.
The Strange Brew(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is also an option, which yields very similar healing abilities to Healing Potion with added chances to trigger periods of invulnerability upon consumption.
On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, Restoration Potions can save a slot, but will likewise trigger both cooldowns.
It is suggested to build houses for the Nurse NPC in your arena. The Nurse can heal and remove debuffs instantly, at the cost of some money.
Bosses are displayed on the Minimap: Follow the boss's icon to track it when you're struggling to find it. You can identify the boss icons by checking their respective wiki pages.
Once you have freed the Mechanic in the Dungeon, you can use Wire to enhance your arena with Traps and helpful Heart and Star Statues. The former helps to damage the enemies, though be careful to set them up correctly in order not to hurt yourself during the battle. The latter will spawn heart and star pickups, respectively. Connect these devices to timers to activate them infinitely.
Don't avoid using summon weapons or sentry-summoning weapons on non-summoner builds since those are always a damage increase, especially with the aforementioned buffs.
It may be useful to summon and kill the Eye of Cthulhu or King Slime before summoning any harder boss in order to spawn an extra one-use pool of Hearts. Note that this will take up a big chunk of the spawnable healing Hearts, which will cause Heart Statues to not spawn as many/any Hearts.


=== Terrain preparation ===


=== Gearing up ===
Depending on where you're at in the game, many weapons can be used. Choose the ones available to you.


==== Armor ====
At the very least, you should have a full set of Silver Armor.
Gold/Platinum Armor is a great defensive choice.
If the Brain of Cthulhu has been beaten, the Crimson armor is a solid all-class option.
If the world evil boss has been defeated, the Molten armor is the best set for Warriors.
The Necro armor offers great boosts to rangers, although it requires a decent grind.
The Meteor armor offers the best boosts to mages, and has great synergy with the Space Gun.
Summoners have no specific armor at this point, and should use the Crimson armor or Pumpkin armor.


===== Weapons =====
For Melee users

The Starfury or the Enchanted Sword can deal good damage at range. Use these to keep distance from Lepus.
An Enchanted Boomerang or stronger can do good damage to Lepus.
The Bladed Glove, if obtained, can easily take out the Lepus Eggs.
The Blade of Grass is a great option if you're willing to get close to Lepus.
The Fiery Greatsword is a great weapon if you've taken out the Brain of Cthulhu or Eater of Worlds.
A Flail such as the Ball O' Hurt or The Meatball can take out the Diseaster Bunnies and Lepus Eggs with ease.
For Ranged users

A Gold or Platinum Bow or better will do great damage to Lepus. Jester's Arrows can pierce through Lepus and his minions, while Frostburn Arrows, can do good damage while inflicting the Frostburn debuff.
The Minishark will do phenomenal damage, while having great range.
The Sharanga(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) is by far the best bow available if the player has defeated the Brain of Cthulhu or Eater of Worlds.
The Boomstick is a great weapon, although it requires getting in closer range than other options require.
The Snowball Cannon will do fair damage, while having cheap ammunition.
The Star Cannon is the best weapon available, although its ammo is very tedious to grind.
Heart Arrows(3DS version) are extremely powerful, and can allow you to effortlessly beat Lepus with any kind of bow that doesn't change ammo.
For Magic users

Gem Staves deal decent damage, have low mana usage, and can pierce through some enemies.
The Roman candle is a good weapon, but has a heavy mana cost.
The Water Bolt is a great weapon, if you're lucky enough to find one.
The Crimson Rod is effectively free damage, and can be used by any class to great effect.
For Summoners

The Slime Staff is the only weapon available.


==== Accessories ====
A Sweetheart Necklace and/or Magic Cuffs are very useful if you are constantly getting hit.
The Magma Stone is great for maximizing damage output.
The Feral Claws are great for attacking with a sword.
The Mana Flower is great for mages.
Reforging accessories to Menacing is preferred, but Warding will also work for a safer fight.


=== Potions ===
Archery Potions are great for players using a bow.
Endurance Potions are fantastic to minimize damage taken.
Ironskin Potions are cheaper alternatives to Endurance Potions, but are more useful if you don't have much defense. They also stack well with Endurance Potions.
Magic Power Potions and Mana Regeneration Potions are must haves for mages.
Summoning Potions are good for any class, because every class can do with an extra minion to fight for you.
Swiftness Potions will help with dodging.
Thorns Potions are great to go along with a sweetheart necklace.
Wrath Potions and Rage Potions will help increase DPS.
Any food Item that provides the Well Fed buff is very useful. Sashimi is easy to get in bulk by fishing
A Flask of Poison or a Flask of Fire are useful potions for melee players if they have killed Queen Bee.
Ale is also useful for melee players if you can deal with the reduced Defense.
A Ammo Reservation Potions will make sure you don't run out of ammo.
Honeyfins will provide 120 health, which is better than Healing potions.

title: Chlorophyte armor
content:
Chlorophyte armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses armor set consisting of the Chlorophyte Plate Mail and Chlorophyte Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Chlorophyte Mask, Chlorophyte Helmet, Chlorophyte Headgear, and Chlorophyte Visor, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, magic and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Chlorophyte Bars (450 Chlorophyte Ore).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:

Summons a Leaf Crystal minion above the player. It periodically fires green, laser-like bolts of energy that instantly hit the target and deals 100 base damage and 10 (Extremely strong) knockback.


== Set ==


=== Helmet variants ===


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Leaf Crystal is capable of firing two separate simultaneous volleys of projectiles. It is possible for both volleys to target the same enemy.
One volley targets the nearest enemy within 43.75 tiles on its own. It requires a clear line-of-sight, but can still travel through blocks if it misses or if the player hides behind cover right before the volley is shot. This volley has a cooldown of 0.67 seconds.
A second volley activates when an enemy (only within 135 tiles) takes damage from other sources first (e.g. from a player attack, or from lava, a minion, a trap, etc). This volley will target enemies through blocks, and the projectile will travel through blocks to reach the target. This volley has a cooldown of 0.83 seconds.
The Leaf Crystal has the following properties:
When firing, it launches a projectile moving in a straight line and does not home in or track targets.
In PvP, only the second volley will target players (i.e., they need to take damage from another source first for the Leaf Crystal to target them).
The Leaf Crystal emits a small amount of green light.
It does not benefit from damage-increasing bonuses (e.g. accessories) and cannot deal critical hits.
It does not target critters directly but can still damage them if they happen to be in its path.
The Leaf Crystal is not affected by Critter Shampoo, despite behaving similarly to other set bonus summons such as the Stardust Guardian.
If a full set of Chlorophyte armor is equipped, it will display a dark pulsating effect. This only occurs if no vanity is covering it or it is equipped as vanity itself.


== Tips ==
The Leaf Crystal can be very useful for farming certain enemies while inactive, for example in search of rare drops and Biome Keys.
Chlorophyte armor has unusually high classless offensive bonuses, second only to Crystal Assassin armor, making it highly useful in mixed-class setups.
The Chlorophyte Mask enables defensive options for ranged and magic loadouts, having the benefit of offering far better survivability than other pre-Plantera ranged and magic armors.
The Chlorophyte Visor is an offensive alternative that trades survivability for DPS, and can be used in hybrid summoner loadouts.
Despite Chlorophyte armor's upsides, it may be advantageous to avoid upgrading from whatever previous armor the player was using, for a multitude of reasons:
Hallowed armor proves to be a superior option in case a more defensive playstyle is preferred, as Chlorophyte armor's set bonus is more offensive in comparison. The Hallowed armor enacts the Holy Protection buff which grants the player immunity to the next attack from enemies whereas Chlorophyte's set bonus acts as a sentry tower to fight for them.
Players focusing on summon weapons in particular might find the Holy Protection buff from Hallowed armor more useful than the +6 defense and +4% summon damage boosts gained by upgrading to Chlorophyte armor. Hallowed armor also grants a higher movement speed boost by +3%. Chlorophyte armor's higher increase to critical strike chance does not matter if the player exclusively uses summon weapons, as they cannot critically strike at all.
In case the player did not use Hallowed armor, it might be advantageous to stick to Adamantite armor if they focus on magic weapons, and Frost armor if they prefer ranged or melee weapons. The former's mana cost reduction bonus might prove more useful than the Leaf Crystal's extra damage depending on the weapon chosen; meanwhile, other stat bonuses of the sets are almost the same. Frost armor's Frostbite can prove to be a more reliable source of extra damage than the Leaf Crystal's shots, while also able to spread across multiple enemies. In addition, Frost armor offers a higher increase to damage and provides a bonus to melee attack speed.
Players focusing on melee weapons have the option to go straight for Turtle armor, which serves as a defensive alternative to the more offensive-oriented Chlorophyte set.
Chlorophyte armor can later be de-crafted via Shimmer into the Chlorophyte Bars needed for the Spectre, Shroomite, and Turtle armor sets.


== Trivia ==
The Chlorophyte armor offers the highest universal critical strike chance bonus of any armor set in the game.
Hallowed and Chlorophyte armor are the only armor sets that have variations for all four classes.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: 
The Leaf Crystal no longer fires a bolt when hitting villagers.
Fixed the Chlorophyte armor's set bonus sometimes shooting bolts from Leaf Crystals that no longer exist.
Desktop 1.4.5.6: Fixed Chlorophyte Visor's tooltip incorrectly showing that it gives 12% summon damage, when it gave 16%.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: Added Chlorophyte Visor.
Desktop 1.4.4.8: Fixed an issue where the fire cooldown time of the Leaf Crystal's first volley was inadvertently reset when swapping between armor.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
The Leaf Crystal's projectile is now an instantaneous bolt of energy, dramatically reducing its likelihood of missing.
Now has a distance limit for how far it will fire when triggered by hitting an NPC (previously it could be significantly off screen).
Desktop 1.4.1: Decreased the cooldown of the Leaf Crystal's first volley from 0.83 seconds to 0.67 seconds.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Chlorophyte Mask defense decreased from 25 to 20.
Chlorophyte set bonus now gives an additional 5% damage reduction if the player is wearing the Chlorophyte Mask.
The Chlorophyte Helmet's 20% ammo conservation effect now stacks with the 20% ammo conservation effect of the Shroomite Breastplate.
Leaf Crystal sprites updated. Old sprite: .

Desktop 1.2.3: Decreased the cooldown of both of the Leaf Crystal's volleys from 1 second to 0.83 seconds. Increased its damage from 40 to 50.
Desktop 1.2.1: Graphics variant for female characters added.

title: Legacy:Guide:Queen Bee strategies
content:
The Queen Bee is a pre-Hardmode boss that can be summoned either by breaking a Larva in a Bee Hive, or by using an Abeemination anywhere in the Jungle.


== Terrain Preparation ==
The Queen Bee is very fast as she charges horizontally at you, so vertical mobility is a must.

Prepare a fairly large area to fight in, as the Queen Bee is about as tall as you can jump. Have wooden platforms extending from one side of the hive to the next, so you can jump to evade its charge attacks.
Have a small pool of honey below the platforms in case you need a regeneration buff, and cover all other sources with blocks or platforms, so they don't slow you down during battle. A campfire or a heart lamp would greatly reduce the need for potions, as well.
If fighting the Queen Bee on the surface using an Abeemination, similar preparations are recommended. You will have the advantage of open space, so if you have a flight or double jump Accessory, you may not need a layer of platforms.


== Gearing Up ==


=== Potions ===
Bring at least 5 Healing Potions. If you want to be safe, bring more, as any boss fight can take an unexpected turn. If you can get them, bring Greater Healing Potions instead.
Ironskin Potions are required, as the extra 8 defense can block a significant amount of the Queen Bee's charges.
A Regeneration Potion is recommended, but not necessary as Honey increases life regen.
Swiftness Potions can allow more agility in dodging her main attacks, however, a running accessory such as Spectre Boots may negate the need for a swiftness buff.


=== Accessories ===
A running accessory, such as Hermes Boots, can allow more adept dodging.
Spectre Boots or a double jump Accessory are necessary for mobility and evasiveness.
If you have managed to obtain one, a Bezoar can be effective at removing the poison debuff.


=== Armor ===
A full set of at least Gold armor should be acquired.
Shadow armor is good too, providing boosts to movement and melee speed.
Any accessory reforged to have a Modifier that increases defense is highly useful.
When it comes to HP, 300 Health is recommended, but lower amounts can be offset by better armor.


=== Weapons ===


==== Melee ====
For swords, the best sword would be the Blade of Grass, Fiery Greatsword, or Night's Edge.
For boomerangs, a Thorn Chakram or Flamarang are excellent.
When it comes to flails, they are not recommended, as they have slow use time. However, a Blue Moon or Sunfury can do a relatively significant amount of damage.


==== Ranged ====
Ranged weapons are usually a better option than melee weapons, as when the Queen Bee is not charging, it spends most of it's time holding still.

If you plan on using bows, you should use at least a Gold Bow with Jester's Arrows/Unholy Arrows.
If you are using guns, A Musket or Undertaker would suffice, but if you want raw damage or speed, a Boomstick or Minishark are the way you should go. If you are using a slower weapon, 400 bullets should be enough. If you are using the Minishark, a full stack of 999 is best.
When using a gun, the best ammunition is Meteor Shot, as it has higher base damage and can bounce, hurting her twice.
Oddly, Heart Arrows(3DS version) perform their initial stopping ability, then permanently slow the queen, making them a great way to kill her, assuming the Valentine Event is happening.


==== Magic ====
If you're going to use magic weapons a Crimson Rod is always effective. Summon it at the top of the hive and use another weapon with it.
Meteor armor w/ Space Gun is also an extremely effective way to kill her, but stay in honey to avoid dying. Also, Water Bolt is good to have due to it's ability to bounce around the hive and damage her multiple times.
The Water Bolt is a fantastic weapon if you're fighting inside of the Hive, due to how many times it can ricochet off walls. Additionally, it can be helpful for taking out bees due to how many times it can pierce.
With practice the Demon Scythe becomes an effective weapon as it does high damage and pierces though the timing is hard to get correct.
The Aqua Scepter is also a great weapon, but you'll run out of mana quickly. However, if you set up a Star Statue, this can be negated.


==== Summoning ====
Summoners have very few options to use against Queen Bee, as most summoning gear drops from her.

The earliest minion Summoning weapon is the Slime Staff. The slime staff is extremely rare, and this weapon is very weak.
You could try to mine in The Underworld for Hellstone to get the Imp Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions). This is effectively the only viable option.


== Summoning Queen Bee ==
You can either destroy the Crystallized Larva (found within hives in the Underground Jungle) or craft an Abeemination to summon her. This only works on the jungle surface or the underground jungle. Any other location and she simply won't spawn, like most other bosses. However, she can leave the Jungle once summoned.


== The Fight ==
The Queen Bee has 3 distinct attack patterns. 1. She will try to level height with you and charge at you from left-right or right-left three times. 2. She will hover near you and spawn small bee minions which will then attempt to attack you by contact damage. 3. She will behave like a normal hornet and fly around, shooting stingers which have a chance to poison you.

When she charges you, use platforms, a flight Accessory, or a double jump accessory to dodge upwards. Attack downwards with a spear or flail for extra damage.
When she summons her bees, it is effective to use a Melee Weapon or Magic Weapon that hits a large area (example: Any sword, and a Water Bolt would probably be effective due to it's ricochet. Another good way to deal with that phase it to use a high rate-of-fire weapon such as the Minishark. This will kill the bees instantly at she spawns them.
If she is using the stinger-shooting phase, keep moving back and forth. A Swiftness Potion and/or a running Accessory can give you the upper edge in this stage. Use a ranged weapon, and try to track her movement.
You could also head to the surface Jungle after you have defeated her once and use an Abeemination. With a Minishark, this fight might take about 2-3 minutes, with you being in no real danger.

title: Underground Jungle
content:
The Underground Jungle is a dense network of small caverns, composed primarily of Mud, pools of Water, Thorny bushes, and Bee Hive traps. It is located below the surface of the Jungle biome, in the same side as the Underground Desert and opposite to the Dungeon and Snow biome, and extends through the entire Cavern layer until stopping at The Underworld.
The Underground Jungle always contains the Jungle Temple and three to seven Bee Hive mini-biomes (depending on world size).
Common treasure rooms are Jungle Shrines, Underground Cabins, and Living Mahogany Trees.
In addition to its own unique enemies, Underground Jungle also spawns all of the Underground and Cavern enemies in itself as well.
In Hardmode, all enemies have a chance of dropping a Jungle Key.
Furthermore, the Underground Jungle undergoes several minor changes throughout the course of Hardmode:

Upon entering Hardmode, it becomes prone to being converted by the Evil biome and starts spawning Chlorophyte Ore.
After defeating one mechanical boss, Life Fruit begin spawning.
Once all three mechanical bosses have been defeated, Plantera's Bulbs begin spawning.


== Contents ==


== Location ==
The Underground Jungle can be found directly underneath the surface Jungle biome. It starts around the middle of the Underground layer, at these depths:


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===

		
		


==== Underground Jungle (Cavern) ====

		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Changed music track from Jungle to a new track exclusive to the biome, Underground Jungle.
Added alternative music track, Jungle (Otherworldly).
Desktop 1.3.1: 
Bee Hive background objects now spawn which, when hit, will fall to the ground spawning Bee enemies.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Honey and Honey Blocks spawn naturally in small amounts in the vicinity of a Bee Hive.
Living Mahogany Trees are now generated in the Underground Jungle.
Desktop 1.2.4: 
Added Variegated Lardfish (used in Summoning Potion).
Desktop 1.2: 
Added bosses Queen Bee and Hardmode Plantera and Golem.
Added Bee Hive and Jungle Temple (accessible after defeating Plantera).
Added Life Fruit (Hardmode), each permanently increases the player's health capacity by 5.
Added drops Bezoar and Hardmode Adhesive Bandage.
Hornets and Man Eaters can now drop Ancient Cobalt armor pieces.
Added Lac Beetle (Violet Husk), Spiked Jungle Slime, and Hardmode Jungle Creeper, Moss Hornet (Tattered Bee Wing), and Moth (Butterfly Dust).
Added Rich Mahogany, Sky Blue Flower, and Hardmode Angry Trapper (Uzi), Arapaima, and Giant Tortoise (Turtle Shell) to Jungle and Underground Jungle.
Desktop 1.0.6: 
More gems spawn in the Underground Jungle.
Thorny bushes growing from Jungle grass are now destroyed on contact with the player.
Underground Jungle now has Mud Background to avoid spawning Underground/Cavern layer enemies.
Added Jungle Spores.

Hornets and Man Eaters no longer drop Jungle armor.
Doctor Bones now exclusive to Jungle and Underground Jungle.
Added Moonglow to Jungle and Underground Jungle.

Now found directly under the surface Jungle biome.
Jungle plants now grow underwater.
Added Jungle Bat and Piranha to Jungle and Underground Jungle.

title: Golf Cart Keys
content:
The Golf Cart Keys are a post-Skeletron mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Golf Cart which emits light, can charge through and damage enemies, and damages enemies that it lands upon. The Golf Cart Keys can be purchased from the Golfer for 50 Gold after Skeletron has been defeated, and a golf score greater than 2000 is earned by the player.


== Notes ==
The Golf Cart emits a radial light that, unusually, is placed about 15 tiles in front of the mount to emulate headlights. With a radius of about 25 tiles, it illuminates roughly 40 tiles in front and 10 tiles behind the Golf Cart.
The Golf Cart's top horizontal speed is 41 mph. When surpassing 20 mph, it will start dealing 40 base summon damage and a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to enemies and critters it runs into, while also applying 30 ticks of global invincibility frames to them.
While falling, the Golf Cart deals 40 classless damage and a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to enemies and critters it runs into, while also applying 12 ticks of global invincibility frames to them.
Dealing damage to enemies with the Golf Cart grants the player 0.2 seconds worth of invincibility frames.
It reduces fall damage taken by 80%, jumps higher than normal (14.51 tiles), and its jump height will stack with extra-jump accessories like the Cloud in a Bottle.
The Golf Cart increases the player's height to 3.625 tiles.
The Golf Cart works within water but moves slower. Like most mounts, it does not affect breath, so the player can still drown.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The Golf Cart can achieve surprisingly high jumps when the Cloud in a Bottle, Fart in a Jar, Blizzard in a Bottle, Tsunami in a Bottle, and Sandstorm in a Bottle (or any of their variants) are all equipped at the same time.
The Golf Cart is a fantastic choice against the Wall of Flesh due to consistently outspeeding it even on Expert Mode and above.


== Trivia ==
The Golf Cart Keys appear to have a Bunny pendant.
The internal name for the Golf Cart mount is GolfCartSomebodySaveMe.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.

title: Eater of Worlds
content:
The Eater of Worlds is a pre-Hardmode Corruption-themed worm boss. It is not a single target, but a string of segments with individual health. When any inner body segment is destroyed, it splits into multiple smaller worms, each with their own head and tail. Each section of the Eater of Worlds must be killed in order to defeat the entire boss. The Eater of Worlds is immune to lava, like all enemies that pass through blocks.
Fighting the Eater of Worlds is the only way to obtain Shadow Scales, and it is one of the only ways to obtain usable quantities of Demonite Ore. Individual segments drop some of these when killed, with a larger amount of them being dropped upon defeating the entire boss.
The Eater of Worlds is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Brain of Cthulhu. The Hardmode mechanical boss equivalent to the Eater of Worlds is The Destroyer.
While the Eater of Worlds is alive, its exclusive music Eater of Worlds will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning and spawning ==
The Eater of Worlds spawns upon destroying every third Shadow Orb in a Corruption world.
It can also be summoned manually by using a Worm Food in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.


== Segments ==
The Eater of Worlds consists of 67 / 72 segments in total.


== Behavior ==
The Eater of Worlds initially spawns with all of its segments coiled in place, and then gradually uncoils while releasing visual purple particles from its body. Although its segments are invisible before moving from their spawning position, they can still take damage in this state.
The Eater of Worlds attacks the player by lunging towards them in an attempt to deal contact damage. While midair, it gradually becomes affected by gravity and is eventually forced to fall down, needing to "burrow" through solid blocks (including platforms and Planter Boxes, as well as the top portion of furniture that can be stood on, such as tables) or liquids before it can lunge towards the player again. While burrowing, it gradually builds up speed in the direction of the player, up to a limit. Upon burrowing out of tiles at full speed, it can reach a maximum height of approximately 31 tiles before being forced to fall down.
The Eater of Worlds consists of a string of body and tail segments that are connected to a head segment and follow the movement of that head segment. However, unlike other worm enemies, the Eater of Worlds' segments do not share a health bar – each segment has its own health pool and all segments need to be killed separately to fully defeat the boss. Killing a middle segment causes the worm to split into two smaller worms that behave similarly to the original boss. Segments adjacent to the defeated one may be converted into a different segment type:

When a head or tail segment is killed, its adjacent body segment will be converted to a new head or tail segment, respectively.
When a body segment is killed, its adjacent body segments will be converted to either a new head segment or a new tail segment, depending on which segment type the newly split worm would be missing.
Lone segments	that are not connected to any other segments cannot survive on their own. They die instantly and drop loot as normal.
For instance, killing the body segment of a three-segment worm (one head, body, and tail segment each) will kill the other two segments along with it, as no other connected segments remain.
As a result, the smallest possible worm is one that is made of two segments in total: a head segment and a tail segment.
Newly created head segments lose all of their momentum and immediately become affected by gravity, needing to fall down and burrow before they can attack the player.
If the head segment of one of the worms is more than 62.5 tiles horizontally or vertically away from the player's center, that worm becomes able to freely fly through the air similar to a Wyvern and is no longer affected by gravity. The worm will resume its normal behavior upon returning into range.
If the player dies or is in neither the Corruption nor the Crimson, all of the worms begin fleeing by moving downwards. Once a fleeing worm's head segment is in the bottom half of the Cavern layer, that worm will instantly despawn, even if it is still on-screen. This behavior can be canceled if the player enters one of the evil biomes again before the worms despawn, causing them to target the player again.
Like most enemies in the game, the worms can also despawn if they are consistently off-screen for 12.5 seconds. The worms may despawn separately from each other, which will still reduce the total health of the boss.


=== Expert Mode ===
In Expert Mode, the Eater of Worlds has 5 extra body segments, and all of its segments are 20% larger in size and have 2 extra defense. It also has 20% increased maximum speed and accelerates over twice as fast.
The increased speed allows it to reach a maximum height of approximately 44 tiles when burrowing out of tiles at full speed, before falling down.
The Eater of Worlds will randomly shoot Vile Spit from its head and body segments, as long as the segments have an unobstructed line of sight to the player. The Vile Spit projectiles can be destroyed by the player in a single hit from any attack or projectile.
Body segments have a 1/900 (0.11%) chance per tick (average of once every 15 seconds) to shoot Vile Spit. They also can only shoot when they are above the surface and are not in front of any background wall.
Head segments shoot more frequently as their individual health decreases. The chance for them to shoot Vile Spit linearly increases from 1/390 (0.26%) per tick (average of once every 6.5 seconds) at full health to 1/90 (1.11%) per tick (average of once every 1.5 seconds) just before dying. Unlike body segments, they can shoot regardless of altitude and background walls.
The Eater of Worlds takes 80% less damage from the following projectiles and explosives (this damage reduction is applied before defense):

For example, the Grenade's normal base damage of 60 is reduced to 12 against the Eater of Worlds.


== Aftermath ==
The Tavernkeep will begin to spawn as the Unconscious Man.
Meteorites will be able to land.
The Dryad will be able to move in if she could not already.
The Merchant will begin selling the Drum Set and Drumstick if he was not already.
The Arms Dealer will begin selling Unholy Arrows at night if he was not already.
The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
The Traveling Merchant will be able to sell the Gray Zapinator if he could not already.
The Eater of Worlds  and Brain of Cthulhu  emotes are unlocked.
The Brain of Cthulhu cloud can now spawn in the background if the world was generated with Crimson.


== Notes ==
Trying to summon the Eater of Worlds with Worm Food while another is still alive will not work and the item will not be consumed.
Fully defeating the entirety of the Eater of Worlds is not completely necessary to progress, as a certain amount of segments may drop the needed amount of materials.
However, defeating the Eater of Worlds is the only way to gain access to the Tavernkeep and Meteorites.
The different segments of the Eater of Worlds are not equivalent in stats: the head segment will deal significantly more damage than the body or tail, but also has the least defense.
The reverse is true for its tail; it has more defense than the body or head, but also deals the least damage.
The Eater of Worlds only takes 65% of the usual damage from the fire projectiles of the Molotov Cocktail and Obsidian Swordfish, and the projectiles will pierce 1 less target.
When the Skyblock tile threshold is not exceeded, the Eater of Worlds gains the ability to freely fly through the air at all times regardless of its distance to the player, without being affected by gravity or needing to burrow through tiles.
In worlds where the special world seed For the Worthy seed is enabled, the Eater of Worlds receives the following changes:
All segments have 2 extra defense.
Head segments are 35% larger, while body and tail segments are 40% larger.
This stacks multiplicatively with the Expert Mode size increase.
Maximum speed is increased by 40% compared to Classic Mode and by 33.33% compared to Expert Mode.
This allows it to reach a maximum height of approximately 77 tiles in Expert Mode when burrowing out of tiles at full speed, before falling down.
Acceleration is increased by 71.4% compared to Classic Mode and by 33.33% compared to Expert Mode.
The chance for body segments to shoot Vile Spit in Expert Mode is increased to 1/450 (0.22%) per tick (average of once every 7.5 seconds). They can also shoot Vile Spit at any altitude, like head segments, but still cannot shoot when in front of background walls.
Additionally, Vile Spit is 42.9% faster and cannot be destroyed while above the surface.
Killing a head segment spawns a Big Eater of Souls.
While the Eater of Worlds is alive, all Eaters of Souls gain 50% increased health and can shoot Vile Spit at the player at a rate of once per second. The Vile Spit fired by them is identical to the one fired by the Eater of Worlds and receives the same boosts mentioned above. In Expert Mode, Eaters of Souls also gain 2 extra defense but do not benefit from the Hardmode stat scaling.
The damage of Vile Spit is not increased in Legendary Mode compared to Master Mode, despite technically being an enemy.
In worlds where the special world seed Celebration Mk 10 is enabled and the For the Worthy seed is disabled, the Eater of Worlds' segments are 50% smaller.
This stacks multiplicatively with the Expert Mode size increase.
 The conditions of whether Dungeon Bricks and Dungeon Brick Walls (in a set of bricks and all three variations of walls with matching color. The color of both are chosen randomly) can be dropped is checked upon entering the world, or occasionally during gameplay. If no Dungeon Bricks and no Dungeon Brick Walls of any kind were found (i.e. no walls with ID 7, 8, 9, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98 nor 99 and no tiles with ID 41, 43, nor 44), Eater of Worlds will drop Dungeon building materials upon its defeat and reset the drop condition (i.e. it cannot drop them again until another check is performed and passed).


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

If the player manages to quickly find the initial spawning location of the Eater of Worlds, they can attack it with a piercing weapon while it is still in its coiled state, which will damage many of its segments at once and can potentially kill it in seconds.
Effective weapons against the Eater of Worlds include piercing or area-of-effect weapons, such as the Vilethorn, Spiky Balls, whips, and fast melee weapons like the Falcon Blade and the Terragrim.
In Classic Mode, Grenades are an effective weapon against the Eater. That is not true in higher difficulties, since the Eater gains resistance to explosives.
Like other worm enemies, once the Eater's head passes a given point, every body segment must follow. This allows the player to stand next to the body, attacking every segment as it goes by. The player should be wary of the head looping back around.
To avoid getting overwhelmed by many worms at once, it may be helpful to only aim for the head or tail of the worm, as these segments will not cause the boss to split further when killed.
The cramped spaces of the chasms can quickly lead to being surrounded, which is a potentially lethal situation, especially in higher difficulties. It may be preferable to hollow out an area in advance, in order to gain more space for maneuvering. A quick way to escape is to have a Bed to teleport to (using Recall Potions or a Magic or Ice Mirror) on the surface of the Corruption.
Farming the Eater of Worlds is particularly profitable, being one of the most effective ways of making money prior to Hardmode.
Converting the Demonite Ore to bars and selling its drops will yield an average of 19 Gold per kill.
If Vile Mushrooms (for crafting the Vile Powder needed for Worm Food) run short, Vile Powder can also be purchased directly from the Dryad during a Blood Moon.
Since each segment can drop loot when killed, it can be a good source of Presents during Christmas, and Goodie Bags, Bloody Machetes, and Bladed Gloves during Halloween.
In Hardmode, it can provide other items as well:
It is a good way to farm for a Corruption Key, as every segment has a chance of dropping one.
In a Corrupt Snow biome, it can drop Amaroks, with each selling for a base value of 4 Gold.
In a Corrupt Ocean, it can drop Pirate Maps.
The Eater of Worlds will start to flee underground if the player leaves the Corruption biome, but will not immediately despawn. Players can utilize this mechanic to keep the Eater of Worlds away from themselves without despawning it by moving in and out of the Corruption, watching for the boss's icon on the minimap to make sure it does not leave.
Using a flail will block any Vile Spit from hitting the player when the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held down. Alternatively, a whip can sweep a large area clean of Vile Spit in a single strike.


== Trivia ==

The Eater of Worlds and Skeletron are the only bosses that do not have their own unique AI.
Skeletron only shares its AI with the Dungeon Guardian.
The Eater of Worlds might spawn outside of the world border on rare occasions when breaking Shadow Orbs.Verify
The Eater of Worlds is sometimes abbreviated as "EoW".
With five eyes on the body segments and three eyes on the head and tail segments each, the Eater of Worlds has 331 / 356 eyes in total.
The Eater of Worlds measures roughly 195 / 209 tiles.
Because the Compass and Depth Meter reveal each tile to be 2 feet in length, the Eater of Worlds would be about 130 yards (142.17 m) long in real life, or 139.33 yards (152.38 m) long in Expert Mode.
The Eater of Worlds has the highest health of all pre-Hardmode bosses.
Oddly enough, but most likely intentionally, it is not required to actually completely defeat the Eater of Worlds to get progression-locked items such as the Nightmare Pickaxe or Shadow armor, since each separate segment drops Shadow Scales.
Because the Eater of Worlds has no more unique drops than the mask, trophy, and the Eater's Bone in Classic Mode, this can prove beneficial for players who are not strong enough to fight it yet but want better gear.
However, in Expert Mode and above, defeating it does reward the player with the Worm Scarf.
The ability to drop progression-locked materials is a trait shared with the Brain of Cthulhu, the Crimson counterpart to this boss.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, the Destroyer is a simulacrum of Cthulhu's spine. Despite the Destroyer taking heavy influence from it, the Eater of Worlds has no connection to Cthulhu and is not mentioned to be a former body part, unlike other pre-mech forms.
According to Redigit, the Eater of Worlds is named Edward. This statement was most likely a joke and is not considered official lore.
The Steam Workshop page appears to show the Eater of Words with centipede-like legs rather than its usual worm-like depiction.
Contrary to its name, the Eater of Worlds does not "consume" or destroy any blocks.
According to the Angler, a severed piece of the Eater of Worlds fell into the water and mutated into a corrupt fish, creating the Eater of Plankton.
 The Bestiary entry for the Eater of Worlds: "Conceived from the bottomless malice of the Corruption, this mighty abyssal worm tunnels wildly to devour all in its path."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Digging sound changed from "Roar 1" to "Eow dig".
Changed music track from Boss 1 to a new track exclusive to the boss fight, Eater of Worlds.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Restructured how Demonite Ore/Shadow Scale drops are handled in Expert and Master. Overall, the quantity of drops from segment kills has been reduced, while the amount of drops from Treasure Bags has been increased.
In Expert Mode, the total quantity of drops is split roughly evenly, with 50% of the ore/scales coming from the partial kills and 50% coming from Treasure Bags.
In Master Mode, the total quantity of drops is weighted heavily toward the Treasure Bag, with only 25% of the rewards coming from partial kills, and 75% coming from the Treasure Bags.
Classic Mode drop rates and weighting has been left entirely untouched by all of these changes.
Desktop 1.4.2: Vile Spit fired by the Eater of Worlds in Expert Mode no longer inflicts the Weak debuff.
Desktop 1.4.0.2: Defeating the Eater of Worlds now allows Meteorites to fall rather than breaking a Shadow Orb, and defeating it more often will increase the chance of a Meteorite falling the following night.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Added Eater of Worlds Relic, a Master Mode-only, trophy-like item.
Added Writhing Remains, a Master Mode-only pet item that summons a miniature Eater of Worlds. It has a 25% chance of dropping upon the Eater of Worlds' death.
Now has more segments, even more so in Expert Mode.
Desktop 1.3.5.3: Fixed despawning in rare situations in multiplayer.
Desktop 1.3.5: Sprite updated. Old sprite was .
Desktop 1.3.0.5: Reduced damage of the Vile Spit attack.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
New AI in Expert Mode, now shoots Vile Spit at players.
Now drops a Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Desktop 1.2.3: Now has a chance of dropping the Eater Mask.
Desktop 1.2.1: Now has a chance of dropping the Eater's Bone instead of the Blend-O-Matic, as the drop chance is now fixed.
Desktop 1.2.0.3: Now has a chance of dropping a Blend-O-Matic. This is meant to be the Eater's Bone drop, but it is bugged.
Desktop 1.2: Now has a chance of dropping the Eater of Worlds Trophy.
Desktop 1.1.2: The Eater of Worlds can now spawn when a third Shadow Orb is broken within the Hallow, but will still flee due to not being in the Corruption.
Desktop 1.0.6: 
No longer counts as defeated when it flees.
Head health reduced from 80 to 65, damage reduced from 43 to 22.
Body health reduced from 210 to 150, damage reduced from 18 to 13, defense reduced from 7 to 4.
Tail health reduced from 300 to 220, damage reduced from 15 to 11, defense reduced from 10 to 8.
Desktop 1.0.5: 
No longer drops Shadow armor.
Can no longer follow players out of the Corruption.
Head health reduced from 140 to 80, damage reduced from 50 to 43.
Body health reduced from 230 to 210, damage reduced from 25 to 18.
Tail health reduced from 350 to 300.
Desktop 1.0.4: 
Fixed a bug where simply selecting Worm Food in the hotbar summoned the Eater of Worlds.
Head health increased from 120 to 140, damage increased from 40 to 50, defense increased from 0 to 2.
Body health increased from 200 to 230, damage increased from 10 to 25, defense increased from 4 to 7.
Tail health increased from 300 to 350, damage increased from 10 to 15, defense increased from 8 to 10.
Desktop-Release: Introduced.

Console-Release: Introduced.

Mobile-Release: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.
