title: Remix
content:
Remix, also known as Don't dig up (or simply DDU), is a special world seed. It flips usual progression upside-down, with players starting in the Underworld and working their way up.


== World generation changes ==


=== Layers ===
The mechanics for the layers in this world are reversed, meaning that the player will encounter Cavern layer content in the Underground layer (e.g. Cavern quest fish can be caught in the underground layer; NPCs usually encountered in the Cavern layer can instead be found in the Underground layer; the Jungle Temple appears in the Surface layer).
The heights of the borders between layers are also changed: as shown by the Depth Meter, starting from the top of the world, the border between the Surface and Underground layers is located at about 30% height of the world, and the border between the Underground and Cavern layers is located at 50%–60% height of the world.
Starting from the top of the world, players will encounter the following layers:


==== Space ====
The Floating Islands are themed after the evil biome of the world, with structures built of Lesion or Flesh Blocks and a Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountain placed on the island. Skyware Chests are replaced by Lesion or Flesh Chests but contain their normal loot.
The player can leave the top world border if they travel high enough. Doing so will kill the player and display one of the following unique death messages:
“<Player name> became an astronaut.”
“<Player name> is now space debris.”
“<Player name> left orbit.”
“<Player name> has ascended.”
“<Player name> departed <world name>.”


==== Surface ====
The surface is completely covered in the evil biome of the world, with very high spawn rates. Evil Snow biomes and Desert biomes also exist in their usual places.
The surface is constantly dark as the sun never rises, and the biome backgrounds are replaced with a space-like starry sky.
Gravity is weaker, as if the player were under the effects of a Featherfall Potion, including not taking damage from falls.
The Jungle Temple is on the surface, painted red in a Crimson world and purple in a Corruption world. The Dungeon is painted the same color.
Living Trees generate without leaves and in larger groups.
Living Wood Chests are replaced with Ebonwood or Shadewood Chests, depending on the world evil.
Both vertical and horizontal tunnels are longer and more frequent, and they tend to connect to other living trees more often.


==== Underground ====
This layer is considered Cavern layer when spawning enemies, fishing, and dropping souls.
It includes biomes such as the Underground Jungle, Underground Desert, and Ice biome.
Lava replaces water in most places in this layer. Unlike regular worlds, the Ice Biome will also contain lava, while lava will not be present in the Underground Desert.
The Underground Desert only generates with background walls in this layer.


==== Cavern ====
This layer simulates the surface layer of a regular world, containing plants and features found in the surface world such as trees, Mushrooms, and water, and can have weather events. It contains most surface biomes, including the Desert and Snow biomes, and their respective features and enemies, such as Oasis locations.
The bottom of the "oval" the Underground Desert generates in is still here, but contains water rather than lava and lacks background walls.
This layer is considered as the Ocean 50% of the time when spawning NPCs. This means all the enemies, critters, and the Angler that originally only spawned in the Ocean will be able to spawn there, but their natural spawn rate is reduced by 50%.
See below for detailed Ocean biome condition.
Fireflies can spawn between 4:30 AM and 7:30 PM.


===== Glowing Mushroom layer =====
This "layer" is located in the Cavern layer, above the Underworld.
This layer is completely occupied by the Glowing Mushroom biome. Aside from Glowing Mushroom tiles, it also contains Stone Blocks and early ores. Surface enemies such as Demon Eyes and Zombies replace normal enemies for that area.


==== Underworld ====
The player spawns on an island in the center of the Underworld at the beginning of the game. The island is fully covered by an ash forest and contains no Hellstone.
Lava bait critters cannot spawn in the Underworld within the lateral center 22% of the world.
Spawns attempted between maxTilesX*0.39-34 and maxTilesX*0.61+84 will not allow Hellbats, Demons, Voodoo Demons, Lava Bats, or Red Devils. Tiles outside this range will allow these spawns, regardless of the player's position.
Area thresholds are 992'/1476'/1916' West and 1092'/1576'/2016' East for Small/Medium/Large worlds, respectively.
The regular Underworld generation, enemies, etc. spawns again when leaving the central area.
Pots in the Underworld contain Rope and Fallen Stars.
Ash trees in the Underworld have a 3.55% chance to drop 20–40 Ropes when shaken.


=== Other ===
The Ocean biome will be overridden by evil biomes for the purpose of spawning NPCs, meaning the original Ocean structure on each side of the world surface no longer acts as the Ocean if they are not purified.
For the purposes of spawning NPCs, the Ocean biome can also be found around the Cavern layer (except for the innermost 14% of the world: 7% to each side from the center of the world). The exact vertical range: the top border is 200 tiles below the border between the Underground and Cavern layers, the bottom border is 200 tiles above the bottom of the world. This area is treated as the Ocean with a 50% chance, while the remaining 50% chance as the surface.
See Fishing section below about Ocean biome condition for fishing purposes.
The generation chance for ocean cave increased from 1/3 (33.33%) to 1/2 (50%).
Minecart tracks are 50% more common.
The Marble Cave, Granite Cave, Glowing Mushroom biomes, and Spider Nest generate in the Underground layer.
The Ice biome extends to the top of the Glowing Mushroom layer, while the Underground Desert extends into the Cavern layer.
The Underground Jungle will extend into and replace the Glowing Mushroom layer.
The Meteorite biome will still generate on the surface.


=== Evil biomes ===
The entire surface is converted into evil tiles, down to 3 tiles below surface at most.
The evil biome chasms will extend below this.
The evil biome will cover approximately 1/7 of the world on each side.


=== Hardmode conversion ===
Once the Wall of Flesh is defeated, instead of the usual "V" pattern conversion, the following conversions will be done:

The Hallow will replace one of the sections of evil on the sides of the world, always on the opposite side of the Dungeon (i.e. the same side as the Jungle).
The upper border is the border between the surface and underground layer (0 feet). For each column of tiles, the height of the border will be randomly changed by -1, 0, or +1 tile.
The lower border of the area is 10 tiles above the bottom true world border.
The conversion is divided into two parts, based on horizontal range:
The width of the first part is 1/7 of the world. Within this range, all tiles that can be converted will be converted into their Hallowed counterpart.
The width of the second part is 1/14 of the world, extended from the first part towards the center of the world. Within this range, only Corruption/Crimson tiles will be converted into their Hallowed counterpart.
Corrupt/Crimson Jungle grass and Mushroom grass will not be converted.
No new evil biome is generated.
The usual wall replacement will be performed after tile conversion.
Below is a table of the conversion zone's border in different world sizes, with the Dungeon at different sides.


==== Converted tiles ====
Below is a list of converted tiles during Hardmode conversion.


== Other changes ==


=== Weapon progression ===
A variety of weapons have switched places in game progression with each other. This means that they will have their obtain method swapped, and their stats are changed to match the current game progression.
This mechanic only changes the weapons' stats according to world seed (i.e. weapons obtained in this seed will not change to the corresponding weapon when brought to normal worlds, only their stats will revert to normal).

Magic Dagger, Wand of Sparking, and Wand of Frosting
The Magic Dagger is found in Chests, or sold by the Skeleton Merchant for 50 Silver during Third Quarter.
Damage decreased from 30 to 14.
Use time increased from 8 to 15.
Mana cost decreased from 6 to 5.
Can no longer autofire.
Rarity decreased from  to .
Sell value decreased from 5 Gold to 10 Silver.
The Wand of Sparking is dropped by Mimics during Hardmode.
Damage increased from 14 to 40.
Use time decreased from 26 to 10.
Mana cost increased from 2 to 6.
Velocity increased from 7 to 12.
Inflicts Hellfire instead of On Fire!.
Can autofire.
Rarity increased from  to .
Sell value increased from 20 Silver to 5 Gold.
This also affects the Wand of Frosting, as it is crafted from Wand of Sparking:
Damage increased from 15 to 42.
Use time decreased from 26 to 10.
Mana cost increased from 2 to 6.
Velocity increased from 7 to 12.
Inflicts Frostbite instead of Frostburn.
Can autofire.
Rarity increased from  to .
Sell value increased from 15 Silver to 5 Gold 5 Silver.
KO Cannon and Chain Knife
The KO Cannon is dropped by Cave Bats.
Damage decreased from 40 to 18.
Use time decreased from 28 to 25.
Knockback decreased from 6.5 to 5.
Can no longer autofire.
The Chain Knife is dropped by Clowns.
Damage increased from 12 to 60.
Use time decreased from 20 to 15.
Can autofire.
Maximum range doubled from 9.4 tiles to 18.8 tiles.
Rarity increased from  to .
Sell value increased from 25 Silver to 3 Gold 50 Silver.
Ice Bow and Snowball Cannon

The Ice Bow is found in Frozen Chests and Frozen/Boreal Crates, or dropped by Ice Mimics during pre-Hardmode.
Damage decreased from 39 to 8.
Use time increased from 14 to 17.
Rarity decreased from  to .
Sell value decreased from 5 Gold to 2 Gold.
The Snowball Cannon is dropped by Ice Mimics during Hardmode.
Damage increased from 10 to 22.
Use time decreased from 19 to 6.
Has 50% chance to save ammo.
Rarity increased from  to .
Sell value increased from 2 Gold to 5 Gold.
Bubble Gun and Aqua Scepter
The Bubble Gun is found in Locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon and Golden Lock Boxes.
Damage decreased from 70 to 5.
Has 20 armor penetration.
Rarity decreased from  to .
Sell value decreased from 5 Gold to 1 Gold 75 Silver.
The Aqua Scepter is dropped by Duke Fishron.
Damage increased from 27 to 90.
Use time decreased from 16 to 10.
Now uses local immunity frames and applies 12 local immunity frames per hit.
Rarity increased from  to .
Sell value increased from 1 Gold 75 Silver to 5 Gold.
Unholy Trident and Flower of Fire
The Unholy Trident is found in Shadow Chests and Obsidian Lock Boxes.
Damage decreased from 150 to 42.
Mana cost decreased from 19 to 9.
Rarity decreased from  to .
Sell value decreased from 10 Gold to 2 Gold 50 Silver.
The Flower of Fire is dropped by Red Devils.
Damage increased from 48 to 85.
Use time decreased from 16 to 12.
Inflicts Hellfire instead of On Fire!.
Rarity increased from  to .
Sell value increased from 2 Gold 50 Silver to 10 Gold.


=== Environment ===
The sun no longer rises, causing the surface of the world to be in constant darkness.
Spawns in the Cavern layer are split 50-50 between day and night enemies/critters.
Activities that follow the day and night cycle still happen on "day" and "night" according to time, if not stated otherwise. For example:
NPCs walk and talk around their town during the daytime and stay in their house during the night.
A new fishing quest is given at dawn by the Angler.
Random boss spawns and events occur following the day and night cycle regularly. Manual event summoning also follows the day and night cycle.
On the surface, during the day the map still shows map exploration as if it were normal day.
Lava now does 200 base contact damage to players, and the duration of the On Fire! debuff is increased to 10.5 / 21 / 26.25 seconds. Additionally, enemies will not take direct contact damage from lava, and will only suffer from the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds.
Flesh Block and Lesion Block now count as blocks for creating their respective evil biome. They are also now visible with Biome Sight Potions.
Lihzahrd Bricks no longer count towards creating a Jungle Biome.
Note that despite this, as long as the player is in front of unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Walls, Golem will not enrage.
Dropped Fallen Star items no longer disappear during the day.
Fallen Stars which fall from the sky can hurt players and NPCs and no longer drop as an item upon impact. They will deal 2,000 / 4,000 / 6,000 damage to players, and 1,000 damage to NPCs regardless of difficulty.
All tiles below surface update 66% faster, and overground updates in normal worlds can also happen below surface (see Plants § Growth). Grass can also spread naturally at any height.
Effects like Rain, Sandstorm, Snowstorm and similar happen below Cavern layer and at least 350 tiles above the bottom true world edge (about 310 tiles above the visible world edge), same requirements as for the Forest Pylon. This should be accounted for when looking for enemies that spawn in these environments, like Sand Elemental or Angry Nimbus.


=== Fishing ===
When fishing in Space, the player is never considered in Corruption and Crimson biomes.
The Underground layer will work as the Cavern layer when fishing.
The Cavern layer, on the other hand, acts as the Underground layer.
When fishing in this layer, there is a 1/2 (50%) chance for a fishing attempt to be considered a surface attempt.
If the attempt is considered a surface attempt, there is a 1/3 (33.33%) chance for it to be considered in Ocean.
Note that due to biome priority, evil biome fishing catches will take priority over Ocean catches (this is the same as worlds without Remix seed).


=== Events ===
The Slime Rain cannot occur.
The Solar Eclipse can still occur, displaying the status message “The horrors have arrived!” when it starts.
The event only affects the Cavern layer and the entire Underworld. It does not affect the surface.


=== Enemies ===

Surface enemies spawn 20 tiles below the Underground-Cavern border and at least 190 tiles above the true bottom world border (around 150 tiles above the visible bottom world borer). During Blood Moon or Solar Eclipse, surface enemies can also spawn at least 20 tiles below the Cavern layer in the lateral center 30% of the world.

Slimes
Have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance for their bonus drop to be replaced by a Fallen Star.
Will sometimes come out of Pots upon breaking them. Such slimes will always carry a Fallen Star.
Have a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of spawning King Slime when killed when the following conditions are met:
The King Slime has not been defeated in the current world yet, and there is no King Slime alive.
The player has dealt damage to it.
At least one player in the world has more than 140 health and 8 defense.
Lava Slime
Does not release lava upon death.
Drops Gel.
Drops Slime Staff at 1/8000 (0.01%) / 1/5600 (0.02%) chance.
Damage decreased from 15 to 7.
Defense decreased from 10 to 2.
Max health decreased from 50 to 25.
Coins drop decreased from 1 Silver 20 Copper to 25 Copper.
Behaves like most surface slimes.
Mimics (pre-Hardmode)
Drops the Band of Regeneration, Magic Mirror, Cloud in a Bottle, Hermes Boots, Mace, Shoe Spikes, Flare Gun, and Extractinator.
Damage decreased from 80 to 30.
Defense decreased from 30 to 12.
Max health decreased from 500 to 300.
Coins drop decreased from 10 Gold to 2 Gold.
Ice Mimic (pre-Hardmode)
Drops the Ice Boomerang, Ice Blade, Ice Skates, Ice Bow, Glacier Fang, Blizzard in a Bottle, Flurry Boots, Toy Sled, and Extractinator.
Additionally, the pre-Hardmode Ice Mimic is still able to drop the Heavy Sling, meaning it is not Hardmode exclusive in Remix worlds.
Same stat changes as Mimics in pre-Hardmode.
Eater of Souls, Devourer, and Crimera
Size, damage, defense, max health, and coins drop increased by 30%.
Eaters of Souls and Crimeras have increased movement speed, constantly rushing into the player.
Wraith
Size, damage, defense, max health, and coins drop increased by 20%.
Face Monster
Size, damage, defense, max health, and coins drop increased by 10%.
Movement speed increased.
Pixie, Unicorn, Gastropod, and Rainbow Slime
Can spawn during pre-Hardmode (provided Pearlstone, Hallowed Grass, Pink Ice, or Hallowed grass is available), and at any height.
Despite this, they still spawn twice as often in the Cavern layer during Hardmode.
Prismatic Lacewing
Can spawn at any time of day in Hallow biomes in the Cavern layer. They will not despawn if released outside of the Hallow.
Martian Probe
Has a rare chance to spawn in the Cavern layer. Martian Probes can still spawn in the Space Layer.


=== Bosses ===
Bosses that can only be summoned at night can be summoned at any time and never despawn or become enraged due to the time being daytime. For example, Skeletron may be summoned at any time, and does not enrage between 4:30 AM and 7:30 PM.
In addition, bosses that can randomly spawn at night (The Eye of Cthulhu and mechanical bosses) no longer require the player to be in the Surface or Space layers to spawn, meaning being underground will not prevent the bosses from naturally spawning.
Deerclops
It can only naturally spawn in Snow biomes at the surface layer, and will not spawn in Snow biomes at the Cavern layer, where the Blizzard visual effect is displayed.
Empress of Light
She is not affected by the day and night cycle, and will not be enraged as long as she is below Surface.
However, she immediately enrages when she reaches the surface.
Once enraged, she follows her normal behavior, despawning at night time if she was not damaged when not enraged.
Thus, summoning the Empress of Light on the surface during the night results in her instantly despawning.


=== Armor ===
Ash Wood armor
Each set piece only has 1 defense (total of 3).
The armor's set bonus reduces lava damage by 64% (reduced from 200 to 72), instead of 50%.


=== NPCs ===
The Tax Collector replaces the Guide as the starting NPC.
The NPC Happiness system is disabled. Price modifiers will always be 100%, and the “Happiness” option in the dialogue window is removed.
However, Love Potion can still increase happiness of NPCs and affect their price modifiers.
Dryad no longer sells any of the Thrown Powders.
It is still possible to craft Vicious or Vile Powder through its respective Mushroom, and Purification Powder through Shimmer Transmutations.
Steampunker no longer sells the Clentaminator, or any of the solutions.
It is still possible to bring them from another world.
Truffle no longer sells the Dark Blue Solution. He still requires his house in a surface Glowing Mushroom biome.


=== Items ===
Several biome pylons have their biome requirements changed:
Instead of being at or above the surface, the Forest Pylon has to be below Cavern layer and at least 350 tiles above the bottom true world edge (about 310 tiles above the visible world edge).
The Mushroom Pylon has an additional requirement: has to be 200 tiles above the bottom true world edge (i.e. not in the Underworld).
The Ocean Pylon can be at anywhere as long as the following conditions are fulfilled:
Not in Space (below 65% altitude).
Not in the underground layer.
Not in the center 14% of the world.
At least 350 tiles above the bottom true world edge (about 310 tiles above the visible world edge).
Ash Wood Bow
Damage decreased from 10 to 6.
Use time increased from 25 to 29.
Ash Wood Hammer
Damage decreased from 9 to 4.
Hammer power decreased from 45% to 35%.
Ash Wood Sword
Damage decreased from 13 to 8.
Use time increased from 17 to 23.


== While generating ==
The Terraria logo rotates and flips upside down.
The background turns into the starry sky background of Space.
The Corruption music will be played, regardless of world evil.


== Tips ==

Quickly take advantage of Pylons and the overlapping biomes to bring spares in advance of setting up a new town. Doing so near natural Minecart Track is recommended.
The NPC Happiness system being disabled means no need to keep track of preferred biomes and neighbors.
Keep in mind that the Forest Pylon cannot be bought on the surface, and does not work there (neither purifying the location nor building away from the evil biome will work). It does, however, work at the Cavern layer.
Either a Teleporter, a Magic Conch, an Ocean Pylon placed on the surface (either in a town well above the world evil or with a sufficient number of Sunflowers to counteract the world evil), or a town on an artificial biome island like a Glowing Mushroom biome will be required to teleport to the surface directly. Due to how the Ocean Pylon check works in this seed, it can function anywhere on the surface outside center 14% of the world; however, the pylon will not be sold over most of the surface, requiring the pylon to be brought up from elsewhere.
Rope will be far more useful to hold onto, both for setting up an "Up-a-vator" to the surface or for developing quick-access "deeper" up into biomes from Pylons.
Be extra careful when digging tunnels upwards; the layer just below the surface has a lot of lava and Lava Traps. One misstep can rain lava down the tunnel to eventually end up at the bottom of said tunnel. Also, be wary of Silt, Sand, and similar blocks. If the solid block holding them up is mined, they will fall and similarly rain down large pools of lava. Always keep the surrounding areas well-lit and pay attention to the tile the player is digging.
A Grappling Hook, Gladiator armor set, or Cobalt Shield is highly recommended if attempting to reach the Floating Islands; getting knocked back from taking hits causes the player to rise into the air faster than almost non-existent gravity pulls them down which will lead to the player getting "juggled" up to the top of the world and then subsequently dying. This is exacerbated by the sheer numbers of Harpies spawning.
Due to the low surface gravity, extra jump accessories and Shield of Cthulhu can be used to "skim" the surface for very early traversal, before the enemies can be survived. This can help map out world generation to aid in exploration. Adding Rocket Boots or Featherfall Potion makes this process semi-trivial.
As the entire surface is covered in Corruption/Crimson, the world can quickly become engulfed by said biomes as soon as Hardmode starts.
It may be a good idea to protect housing and pylons by surrounding them in 3×3 tunnels to prevent NPCs from being forced to move out.
However, several factors make spread prevention easier, even before Hardmode.
Aside from any limited pre-Hardmode spread over underground grass and unusually deep evil biome chasms, the pure area of the world is essentially a rectangle. This makes digging tunnels to prevent spread easier, as this can be done axis-aligned without compromising much on the protected area, as opposed to the usual diagonal stripes.
The Digging Molecart is effective for digging a horizontal tunnel just underneath the surface. This can be done twice, the second time just above the first to allow the placed minecart tracks to block vines (there should be no corruptible blocks in between the tracks, only at least one block of air to create a gap at least three blocks wide including the tracks).
After digging vertical tunnels on the sides of the world, ropes can be placed down the sides of the tunnel as a cheap and easy way to block thorny bushes.
Upon the start of the Hardmode, the Hallow replaces a strip on the side of the world that is already entirely Corrupt/Crimson, and no new area is immediately infected with the evil biome.
This does not immediately decrease the overall purity of the world.
The Hallow always appears on the same side as the Jungle, which the Hallow cannot spread through.
The location of the infectious biomes is completely predictable even in pre-Hardmode, unlike in normal worlds, meaning that it is easy to prepare tunnels in pre-Hardmode simply by blocking off the existing Corruption/Crimson.
Due to starting the world in a portion of Underworld with weaker enemy spawns, setting up a town to convert those spawns to critters is relatively simple. The Underworld-specific critters cannot be caught until the player has at least beaten an evil biome boss (to be able to craft the Lavaproof Bug Net), but gem critters also spawn with considerable regularity, making for a decent early game coin farm. Once access to Hellstone has been secured, the various Underworld critters will also serve as a handy source of decent fishing bait.
Alternatively, one may obtain the Golden Bug Net to skip the process of beating bosses at a 1/80 (1.25%) chance per quest completed.
The Aether biome has a pure stone ring despite its surroundings being infected. This can aid in locating the biome in pre-Hardmode.
Once located, a Magic Conch combined with a Teleporter will allow quick travel to here. A Cavern Pylon or Ocean Pylon (if in the cavern layer) can also facilitate travel there as the pure stone ring is wide enough to allow housing NPCs within, but as evil biomes prevent NPCs from selling pylons, the pylon will need to be bought ahead of time.
Of the weapons with progression switch, Unholy Trident and Aqua Scepter are exceptionally strong for their tier.

title: Moon phase
content:
The moon in Terraria moves through a cycle of eight different phases, with the next phase in the cycle appearing each night. The current phase is indicated by the amount of the moon that is visible during the night. The phase of the moon primarily affects the shop inventory of certain NPCs; other effects influenced by the moon include the spawn rates of certain enemies and critters, and the player's Fishing Power.
It takes eight in-game nights for the moon to move through all of its phases. The cycle begins with the full moon upon world creation, where the entire circular moon is visible, and four nights later, after three waning phases, reaches the new moon, where no moon is visible. Another four nights later, after three waxing phases, the cycle ends with the return of the full moon.
Each moon phase starts at dawn (4:30 AM) and lasts until the next dawn. Therefore, a moon phase also encompasses the day preceding the night of that moon phase. This is important because most phase-dependent content and effects are not limited to nighttime.
The current moon phase is reported by the Sextant, an informational accessory which can be obtained from the Angler NPC as a fishing quest reward, or any of its upgrades.
A Blood Moon can occur during any moon phase except for a new moon. A Pumpkin Moon or Frost Moon can be summoned by the player on any night.


== Phase-dependent content ==
The following tables detail items and occurrences that depend on particular moon phases. They refer to both the day and the night of the stated moon phase, unless not applicable or noted otherwise.


=== General effects ===


=== Items for sale ===


== Notes ==

There are nine different standard styles of the moon. When a world is generated, one random standard moon style is assigned to it. It can be changed with a Moon Globe.
During a Frost or Pumpkin Moon event, the moon takes on a special, themed appearance. As with the regular moon styles, its sprite is cut to match the size of the current moon phase.
In worlds with the special world seed Drunk enabled, the moon appears as a smiley face.
It is possible to summon a Blood Moon during a New Moon by using a Bloody Tear, which will immediately advance the moon phase to a Waxing Crescent.
The moon will cycle through phases on the title screen. This is easiest to see by dragging it.


== Tips ==
If the player does not have access to a Sextant, they can determine the current moon quarter by inspecting the shop inventory of the Painter, Golfer (provided a sufficiently high golf score), or Dryad. In Hardmode, the exact moon phase is revealed by which set of clothes the Clothier has for sale.


== Trivia ==
The phases shown suggest that the Terraria world is set on its planet's northern hemisphere: The intermediate phases have their circular side on the right for waxing phases, and the left for waning phases.

title: Legacy:Guide:Crafting a Terra Blade
content:
This guide describes the necessary steps involved with crafting the Terra Blade.


== Ingredients ==
The following materials are required to craft the sword:

40 Demonite Ore / Crimtane Ore
12 Jungle Spores
15 Stinger
1 Muramasa
60 Hellstone
20 Obsidian
12 Hallowed Bar
3 Broken Hero Sword


== Overview ==


== Light's Bane / Blood Butcherer ==
Either the Light's Bane or Blood Butcherer will be needed to craft a Terra Blade. The Light's Bane requires materials specific to a world with The Corruption, while the Blood Butcherer requires materials specific to a world with The Crimson.
The Light's Bane is crafted using 10 Demonite Bars at an Iron Anvil or Lead Anvil. The Demonite Ore needed to craft these bars can be found randomly throughout the world, with increased frequency in corrupt chasms. Large amounts can also be harvested by defeating the Eye of Cthulhu or Eater of Worlds.
The Blood Butcherer is crafted using 10 Crimtane Bars at an Iron Anvil or Lead Anvil. The Crimtane Ore needed to craft these bars can be found randomly throughout the world. Large amounts can also be harvested by defeating the Eye of Cthulhu or Brain of Cthulhu.


== Blade of Grass ==
The Blade of Grass requires materials from the Underground Jungle. It is crafted using 12 Jungle Spores and 15 Stingers at an Iron Anvil or Lead Anvil. Stingers are dropped by Hornets and Spiked Jungle Slimes. Jungle Spores are harvested from small glowing plants scattered around the Underground Jungle: . These plants can be broken by any tool or weapon. Vines are dropped by Man Eaters.


== Muramasa ==
The Muramasa cannot be crafted, but rather must be obtained from Gold Chests found in the Dungeon. Defeating Skeletron is required in order to fully access the Dungeon. Skeletron can be summoned at night, by speaking to the Old Man near the entrance of the Dungeon.
Golden Keys are needed to open any Gold Chest found in the Dungeon. These keys can be found by defeating Dungeon Slimes, looting chests, or breaking pots. Most enemies in the Dungeon also have a rare chance of dropping Golden Keys. It's possible that none of the chests in the Dungeon will contain the Muramasa, in which case a new world must be made to find more Gold Chests.


== Fiery Greatsword ==
The Fiery Greatsword requires Hellstone, a material only found in the Underworld. The sword can be crafted using 20 Hellstone Bars at an Iron Anvil or Lead Anvil. A Nightmare Pickaxe, Deathbringer Pickaxe, or a Reaver Shark is needed to mine Hellstone. An Obsidian Skull and Lava Waders are useful accessories when mining this ore, as it will release Lava when broken.
Alternatively an Obsidian Skin Potion can be used which will make it much easier to mine as you'll be immune to the burning and lava and will allow you to reach otherwise dangerous pockets of ore.
Unlike other bars, Hellstone can only be smelted into Hellstone Bars by combining it with Obsidian at a Hellforge. Obsidian is formed when Water contacts Lava, and Hellforges can be found randomly throughout The Underworld.


== Night's Edge ==
The Night's Edge is crafted by combining the Light's Bane or Blood Butcherer, Blade of Grass, Muramasa, and Volcano at an Altar. Demon Altars can be found randomly near The Corruption, while Crimson Altars can be found randomly near The Crimson.
The Night's Edge is the last material of the Terra Blade able to be crafted pre-Hardmode. To complete the crafting process, materials from Hardmode are required.


== Excalibur ==
Crafting the Excalibur requires Hallowed Bars, which are dropped from any of the mechanical bosses. It is crafted using 12 Hallowed Bars at a Mythril Anvil or Orichalcum Anvil.


== True Blades ==
Crafting the True Night's Edge requires the Night's Edge and a Broken Hero Sword, and crafting the True Excalibur requires the Excalibur and another Broken Hero Sword. The two Broken Hero Swords are dropped by Swamp Things and Frankensteins during a Solar Eclipse. It is not guaranteed that every Solar Eclipse will yield a Broken Hero Sword, but a Water Candle and/or a Battle Potion can be used to increase the chances of enemies that can drop it to spawn.


== Terra Blade ==
The Terra Blade is crafted using the True Night's Edge, the True Excalibur and a third Broken Hero Sword at a Mythril Anvil or Orichalcum Anvil.

title: Mud Bud
content:
The Mud Bud is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns Plantero, a miniature version of Plantera, that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Plantero flies towards them in a manner similar to Plantera's second form while emitting a trail of falling leaves that are affected by wind. The Mud Bud can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after defeating Plantera.


== Trivia ==
The Mud Bud is stated to be Redigit's favorite pet item in the game.
The pet was introduced following a suggestion by a player.
The pet appears similar to both of Plantera's map icons.
The name Plantero could be a portmanteau of Plantera and sombrero, referencing the pet's hat. Alternatively, it could be seen as a masculine equivalent of Plantera, given that the vowel at the end of a word usually indicates its grammatical gender in languages such as Italian or Spanish.

title: The Aether
content:
The Aether is a mini-biome that can be found in the outer fifth of the world in the Underground or Cavern layers. It is generated once upon world creation and is always located on the same side of the world as the Jungle biome. The biome features a large pool of Shimmer in its center that is surrounded by a few Gem Trees. Faelings occasionally fly above the pool.
Players can also create artificial Aether biomes by placing Shimmer in the Underground or Cavern layers. An Aether biome requires at least 300 tiles of Shimmer.
While in the Aether, a unique background effect shows the star-filled sky of Space, with multicolored stars, blackening the entire background but the stars. This effect will also display over tiles that are in complete darkness.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
The player is only considered to be in an Aether mini-biome if they are at least 50 tiles below the surface layer and at least 430 tiles above the true bottom world edge (i.e. most parts of the underground and cavern layers), as well as in the vicinity of at least 300 tiles of Shimmer.
Since a Terraria world is not dynamically updated, worlds generated pre-1.4.4 will always lack an Aether mini-biome.
Before defeating the Moon Lord, the Aether is the only source of Shimmer, meaning it is finite and cannot be replenished.
However, once defeated, the Bottomless Shimmer Bucket becomes available and can be used to create unlimited Shimmer.
The Aether Monolith can be used to suppress the background effect of the Aether, as well as replicate it outside of the mini-biome.
For the purposes of the Aether Pylon, the Aether biome will be counted even if it is on the Surface or Underworld layers, where Aether biomes normally cannot exist.
Rain particles (including those from the Eyebrella) will not appear in the Aether.
The music of the Underground Corruption, Underground Crimson, and Underground Hallow will not override the Aether's music or its visual effects.
The Dungeon will suppress the Aether's visual effects.


=== Generation ===

The Aether always generates on the same side of the world as the Jungle.
The game will generate the Aether by randomly selecting a tile in a zone (see below for technical info about this zone's size and the number of generation attempts in the zone); then check a 211×211 to 249×249 (size is determined randomly) rectangular area centered on the chosen tile for the following:

The borders of the area must be at least 50 tiles away from the world borders.
The area must have no Ebonstone or Crimstone Blocks (unless in a Remix / Zenith world).
Note that this is only a generation restriction. The Aether biome still retains all of its functionalities in hybrid biomes that include the Corruption/Crimson.
If the area passes the check, then the tile is considered valid, and the Aether biome will be generated centered on the tile. Otherwise, continue the process of selecting and checking random tiles. Internally, the Aether biome will be considered a 200×200 rectangular area centered on the valid tile (the bottom-right tile of the four center tiles is the center), and no other structures will overlap with it.


==== Zones ====
To better describe the size of the zone, we first set a coordinate system to describe tile location in a world: (all values below are in tiles)

The coordinates of the top-left tile in the world is (0,0), while the coordinates of the bottom-right tile is (mX,mY), where mX is the world width and mY is the world height (i.e. the positive direction of X and Y axis is "left to right" and "top to bottom", respectively).
The height of the border between Surface and Underground layers is S (Y = S).
Similarly, the height of the border between Underground and Cavern layers is C (Y = C).
When selecting a random tile (X,Y), the respective coordinate will be a random number between these values: X = [X1, X2); Y = [Y1, Y2)
The size of the first zone is determined as following:

Zone A
Y axis:
Minimum depth is Y1 = (S + C) ÷ 2 + 50, and the maximum depth is Y2 = [(mY - 250) × 2 + C] ÷ 3.
If Y2 is more than mY - 460, then Y2 is set to mY - 460.
If Y2 ≤ Y1, then Y2 is set to Y1 + 50.
X axis:
The range is X1 = 200, X2 = mX × 0.11; or X1 = mX × 0.89, X2 = mX - 200, depending on the side of the world.
This effectively makes the selected tile in the outer 11% of the world, and at least 200 tiles away from the world borders.
Then, randomly select a tile inside Zone A. If it failed to pass the check mentioned above, then the game will try 20000 times to find a valid tile inside another zone (Zone B):

Zone B
Y axis:
Y1 is set to (S + C) ÷ 2 + 20. Y2 is unchanged.
X axis:
X1 and X2 are unchanged.
If those attempts all failed, then the game will continue to select random tiles in another zone (Zone C), until a valid tile is found:

Zone C
Y axis:
Y1 is set to S + 120. Y2 is unchanged.
X axis:
Range is set to X1 = 200, X2 = mX × 0.2; or X1 = mX × 0.8, X2 = mX - 200, depending on the side of the world.
Celebration Mk 10 Zones
In Celebration Mk 10 worlds, the first scanning zone is different from other worlds. Also, in addition to the Aether biome, most water pools in this zone are replaced with Shimmer pools.
The size of the first zone (Zone A) in a Celebrationmk10 world is determined as following:

Y axis:
Minimum depth is Y1 = S + 150, and the maximum depth is Y2 = (C + S + 200) ÷ 2.
If Y2 ≤ Y1, then Y2 is set to Y1 + 50.
X axis:
Same as the range of Zone A in other worlds.
Process generation
After determining the zones, the game will first try 10,000 times in Zone A.
If no valid tile is found, then try another 10,000 times in Zone B.
If still no valid tile found, then continue to select random tiles in Zone C.


== Tips ==

The Guide's name can be used to find the Aether's horizontal location upon world creation.
Note that this method may not always work, as it only calculates the position of the first generation zone (Zone A). Since the Aether cannot overlap with Ebonstone or Crimstone Blocks in regular worlds, if it fails to generate in Zone A, it will generate in another zone, rendering this method invalid.
If the original Guide has died, a world with the same World Seed can be created to find the original Guide's name.
This will never work on For the Worthy worlds, even when using the correct name order of the Demolitionist instead. 
First, find the number (n) corresponding to the Guide's name (the numbers are in the table below).
Then, substitute n into the equation in the table below to calculate the horizontal location of the Aether biome shown on the Compass (in feet, 1 tile = 2 feet). Note that the Aether is always on the same side of the world as the Jungle.

The completed list of possible Aether's horizontal locations in the table below.

Building a town in the Aether can prove worthwhile to passively collect gems in moderate amounts. Gem critters spawn aplenty near town NPCs in the Cavern layer and are transmuted into gems when they walk into the Shimmer. A Water Candle and Battle Potion can help increase critter spawn rates.


== Trivia ==
In Greek mythology, Aether is the personification of the bright upper sky.
The Aether's name uses the archaic spelling of the word æther, with the Latin letter æ separated. In modern English, aether is normally spelled ether.


== History ==

The Aether's visual effects are now suppressed when in the Dungeon.
Gem Trees now generate in the Aether biome.

title: Guide:True Zenith
content:
True Zenith is a colloquial name for an exceptionally difficult secret seed combination that includes all secret world seeds and special world seeds (except for Skyblock). This seed can be considered the highest world difficulty possible in Terraria, previously held by the Zenith seed.


== Before starting a True Zenith world ==


=== General tips ===
Because the world starts in Hardmode, it is relatively easy to skip progression and get Hardmode weapons without needing to build up through pre-Hardmode progression. This is best achieved by special enemy drops that can be manipulated and slowly chipped down, such as the Poison Staff, Wand of Sparking, or Snowball Cannon (due to remixed weapon progression). If the spawn of the player is undesirable, the effects of Royale with cheese (which also works in singleplayer) gives the player five extra spawn points, which not only let them find potential base site alternatives and loot, but can let them traverse the map considerably faster. However, any spawn point (including the original one) has a chance to be located on top or inside lava and/or spikes, which early in the game will instantly kill you. Naturally-generated Teleporters (from the Beam me up secret seed) can also teleport you inside spikes.
Due to the sweeping changes made by this seed regarding increased difficulty, both enemies and exploration in general becomes significantly tougher. The higher the difficulty mode the player selected when playing True Zenith, the more this becomes the case. If playing on Legendary Mode on this seed, it is recommended for the player to use armor and accessories that let the player in general take more hits.


=== Seed effects ===
The What a horrible night to have a curse (Vampirism) secret seed makes On Fire! deal 50 damage per second, instead of 4. This causes enemies like Skeleton Archers to become much more dangerous. In general, it is recommended to carry Water Buckets or a Bottomless Water Bucket to mitigate this. As an alternative, the Nurse can also immediately remove the debuff.
Due to the effects of the Celebration special seed, the Rod of Discord now has a significantly improved drop rate of 1%. This makes it a much more viable item to farm for if the player is struggling with bosses.
Celebration also gives the Wizard Hat an extra minion slot. In general, this armor piece can be useful for its offensive bonuses, providing the player finds and kills Tim early on.
As a result of the effects of the Double daring dangers secret seed, biomes behave very differently than usual. In short, the next biome-associated tile below the player determines the player's biome (e.g. relevant for obtaining Souls of Night), while enemy spawns depend only on the tile they are spawned on (or the ones below). Walls behind the tile can be of relevance. This makes it incredibly easy to manipulate enemy spawns and loot for most biomes.
This information is also relevant if trying to do biome-specific fishing quests. Furthermore, as the Cavern and Underground layers are swapped due to the effects of Remix, fish caught in the "Underground" layer can actually be caught in the Caverns layer, and vice versa.
The large rooms near each dungeon biome transition also provide a good area to expand into an enemy farm.
Underground Cabins from the I am error secret seed can sometimes generate with Bone Blocks or Bone Platforms, which makes it possible to get Necro armor and the Spinal Tap early. (Note that the Dungeon biome section of Double daring dangers would already have been accessible as the player starts in Hardmode, so the ability to access Bones from this method does not break progression anyway.)
Planetoids' effect on the seed also causes the entire map to have big gaps between circle-shaped landmasses, making it easy to make perimeters with Dynamites, which are useful for both boss arenas and mob farms. It also makes it relatively easy to explore with infinite flight, which itself can be easily obtained with the use of Amulet of the Night, a common item found in chests across the map.
All traps are coated in Echo Coating, making them largely impossible to avoid during the game. This makes Spectre Goggles, which reveals echo-coated blocks and which can be found in chests, incredibly helpful. These come with the downside of taking up an accessory slot, however. This is not the case for the Echo Chamber, which can be equipped in a vanity slot and still function. Echo Chambers require Echo Blocks, wire, and Gray Bricks to craft. Echo blocks can make up the walls of underground cabins and gray bricks are easily craftable, however wire is traditionally post-Skeletron. This can be circumvented by collecting (placeable) explosives, which can be Shimmered with the Shimmer bubbles randomly dotted around the map. If the player cannot find either of those, they can buy a Paint Scraper from the Painter for 1 Gold, allowing you to remove echo coating from tiles in a small distance around you.
NPC happiness is disabled due to the effects of Remix, so you can place NPC houses as close together as you want without having to worry about prices.
Due to the effects of Bring a towel, it will perpetually rain, allowing enemies like Flying Fish and Angry Nimbus to spawn always (no matter where you are in the world). This also means that NPCs will immediately move in to a home that is selected for them, once the player has moved far enough away.


=== World generation ===
The evil biomes are split between the two sides of the world, one side generates crimson while the other side generates corruption.
The Underworld generates the same way as on the Zenith seed.
However, due to the huge amount of lava generating in the upper layers and the strong settling potential of the planetoids seed, it is typically almost filled to the top with lava.
The other layers consist of planetoids and mini-biomes, as well as the Dual Dungeons.
The Aether does not generate.
Shimmer can still be found in the gray brick layer of the Dual Dungeons or in small bubbles around the world.
The caverns layer, like on the Remix seed, behaves like a surface / underground hybrid layer.
In the bottom half of it, all blocks are replaced with their evil variants. The top half is purified.
In a strip above the Underworld, blocks are instead replaced by the Jungle (and stone blocks with crispy honey blocks).
This strip does not grow with the world size, causing it to replace more of the evil biomes on smaller worlds.
In the outer parts of the world, all stone in the entire caverns layer is replaced with its evil variants. This also replaces the crispy honey blocks near the underworld, but does not affect pure grass blocks in the upper half or jungle grass near the underworld.
The underground layer, like on the Remix seed, behaves like the caverns layer. However, all blocks are replaced by their ice biome counterparts.
The upper half of this layer uses pink ice blocks.
Mushroom patches become Jungle patches.
Sky islands are infected and their chests are locked (Zenith seed).
The top of the world generates a strip of painted glowing mushroom grass and hive blocks. Below that, a strip of crispy honey blocks is generated.
This does not stretch into the outer parts of the world.
The Dual Dungeons generate normally, however are subject to the following of the above elaborated changes:
Infected stone replaces other stone variants in the outer parts of the world.
Pink ice replaces ice in the upper half of the underground layer.
Crispy honey blocks replace blocks near the top. Walls are converted to infested spider walls.
The ice biome replaces what would usually be the evil biome or Hallow above the caverns layer.
The Hallow is purified / infected in the cavern layer and converted to ice in the underground layer.
The Temple and Dungeon are painted.
Most of the jungle is replaced by glowing mushroom grass, this is an interaction with the toadstool and mole people seed.
Interestingly, the desert remains completely unaffected.
Several meteorites land across the world during generation.


== Pre-Bosses ==


=== Immediate survival ===
(Unfinished)

In almost all cases, every single chest (or trash can and barrel) as well as just about every Life Crystal and Mana Crystal is surrounded by a large amount of spikes, and should be approached carefully. The optimal way to handle these, especially without a way to reveal the spikes, is by mining from below and using Block Swap to ensure you don't get hurt by the spikes.
It is highly recommended to set up boxes around all 6 spawn points (neutral + all 5 teams' spawn points) with player-placed background walls and no exits besides doors blocked on the inside with any non-block object. This will make respawning and teleporting between them via team changing significantly safer by preventing enemies from entering the spawn boxes or spawning inside them.
As most enemies will kill you in 1-2 hits before you gear up and get life crystals, it's a good idea to build Horizontal one-way walls to shoot at enemies through, and if you box in enemies on the other side of one, you can easily chip them down. Place platforms vertically along the wall and hammer them into stairs so you can shoot through them.


=== Settling in ===
Establishing a base near one of your available spawn points is encouraged early, as the player's inventory can quickly become filled. Lead and iron ore, while definitely being outclassed in regards to what gear they can craft, are still largely useful for managing your storage effectively.
The pure Ice biome is particularly great for this, as it's the only biome without any burrowing enemies, and all of its hardmode enemies have chance to drop some kind of weapon, in addition to all enemies there having a 1/300 chance to drop an Amarok. If you are in the Ice biome, Snowballs can be crafted in bulk easily, and are a much safer way to chip down the health of a tanky enemy such as a Mimic than to use your Copper Shortsword. If you have the materials or money, using a Wooden Bow and a couple thousand Wooden Arrows is a viable alternative.


==== NPCs ====
Establishing NPC housing early is incredibly useful. Particularly useful NPCs for this stage of the game include:

Arms Dealer: Sells the Shotgun for 25 Gold gold, which is helpful if you haven't had any luck with Hardmode weapon drops. Break pots until you get Silver Bullets to get him to move in.
Demolitionist: Provides explosives, which are useful for the quick gathering of resources. You will need blocks for traversing dangerous gaps caused by the effects of Planetoids. Additionally, grenades are a serviceable weapon to use on enemies, and are cheaper (and more immediately available) than the Shotgun.
Merchant: Sells the Piggy Bank to let you stash your coins between inevitable deaths, the Bug Net to catch critters for food/fishing bait, and the Mining Helmet to provide constant light to avoid dying in darkness.
Tax Collector: Safe and passive income. Also has a chance to drop a Classy Cane, which is serviceable (if very short range) and is virtually free as you'll only need boulders (or a house with wired traps) to kill the Tax Collector consistently.
Painter: Sells the Paint Scraper for 1 Gold, giving you a cheap (if low distance) method of detecting traps and spikes until you find the Spectre Goggles.
Wizard: Sells the Ice Rod, which is a decent early weapon option, as well as Spell Tomes which can be crafted alongside basic Hardmode ingredients into solid earlygame weapons like the Crystal Storm, Golden Shower, or Cursed Flames.
Additionally, establishing a town also enables the Traveling Merchant to visit. He becomes more useful on this seed, as seeds with Zenith enabled increase the amount of items he can sell by 2. He can sell useful weapons like the Orange Zapinator or Sergeant United Shield. The Extendo Grip is also very helpful for mining, blocking off enemies with placed blocks, and disarming all types of traps.
You can force the Angler to spawn by going to either edge of the world (until the Underground Ocean background appears) and making a small pool with sand as the base.


=== Gearing up ===
(Unfinished)
Banners, which now utilize their own menu, are incredibly useful in higher difficulties where enemies normally have significantly inflated amounts of health and contact damage. They prove especially useful if the player is farming for items in the early game, and consistently runs into the same enemies.

Obtaining a Cross Necklace from a Mimic can be incredibly useful to sustain more hits from enemies before inevitably dying.
Meteor armor may be useful if the player finds one of their spawns to be near a naturally-generated meteorite, as the armor set provides some defense (over none), and allows the player to spam the Space Gun to chip down enemies' health.
It's possible to find a naturally-generated Chlorophyte Extractinator in Underground Cabins due to the effect of I am error seed, though they seem to be rare. Shimmering it into Chlorophyte Bars and crafting a Chlorophyte Pickaxe can help unlock progression past Mechanical Bosses without defeating Mechdusa, making the fight with her much easier.


=== Herbs ===
Due to the effects of the Mole people seed, herb sprouts can only generate during world generation, and will not naturally generate afterwards. This can make access to herbs for potions crafting challenging. There are a few solutions for each herb:

Some herbs can  generate during world generation and are easy to find because of large amounts of suitable soil for them, usually it's Daybloom, Blinkroot, Deathweed and Shiverthorn. Moonglow, Waterleaf and Fireblossom are more rare and might be impossible to find without an aid of map editor.
It's possible to obtain Herb Bag or Can Of Worms from chests in the Dungeon, because of the effects of Double daring dangers which causes surface chest loot to generate in dungeon chests, or in sky island generated due to the effect of I am error seed. It's recommended to shimmer all Can Of Worms into Herb Bags until you obtain seeds for all herbs.
Because of the constant rain and the effect of Remix seed, for Fireblossom to bloom it needs to be at least 350 tiles above the bottom true world edge (about 310 tiles above the visible world edge). Which means that all naturally generated Fireblossom in the Underworld will not bloom. It's still possible to find blooming Fireblossom due to the effect of I am error seed, which can relocate ash blocks higher in the world.


== Expanded exploration and preparation for combat ==


=== General tips ===
Since both traps and Statues are more common on this seed, you can use it to your advantage to find heart statues and use the wiring from naturally-generated traps to place them. Then you can build a boss/event arena around that for extra healing during those fights, even before fighting Skeletron.
As statues can spawn clustered together and wired up to Red Pressure Plates, it's very important to destroy any enemy-spawning statues on sight to prevent being overwhelmed by constant spawns, especially from flying/wall phasing enemies. Use explosives to destroy them from a distance if you can't get close enough to mine them with a pickaxe.
The evil biomes in this seed are detected by the usual proximity method along with checking if there is any evil biome tile within 300 tiles below the player. While Sunflowers can help negating the former evil biome proximity, they do not work with the latter, leading to cases where standing on a given block can switch the biome to the evil one and moving a single block to the sides can switch it back to normal. To fix that, stand where the evil biome is applied and dig down up to 300 blocks and destroy all evil biome tiles on the way.
Because the Underworld is mostly flooded in lava, a strategy to make it useful is to make a town as soon as you get there and fish a Superheated Blood (lava shark mount) which grants immunity to lava along with extremely high horizontal mobility when mounting it. This is also viable to use when fighting the Wall of Flesh, although is by no means required.
Fishing becomes considerably more useful for a variety of reasons on this seed. Due to several changes in both world generation and enemy contact damage, once the player reaches max health exploration tends to be less rewarded. As the player starts in Hardmode, fishing can allow quicker access to Hardmode ores (albeit being a tedious process) as well as a variety of useful accessories such as the Frog Leg, Tsunami in a Bottle, or Balloon Pufferfish.
Combat-wise, the Anchor (which can be obtained by fishing) is a solid weapon to use against enemies. Similarly, if fishing in specific biomes, the Crystal Serpent or Toxikarp may also prove useful as early weapons.


=== Combat ===


==== Specific enemies ====


===== Biome Mimics =====
Biome Mimics may be easy to summon once the player is able to find locations to farm Souls of Light or Night, but they are brutally hard to take on due to their highly erratic movement and health, making it both lengthy and frankly irritating for the player to attempt to fight one, making such a fight a battle of attrition. The player should absolutely not attempt to fight one until they have built an arena (preferably near NPCs for lowered enemy spawn rates), obtained at least a few Hardmode weapons, and have some movement accessories equipped; however, if the player can successfully take one of these, they can obtain particularly powerful drops.
Once you have access to the Mechanic, you can set up two teleporters spread away horizontally with switches on top of them. Then, you can summon the mimic, run to a teleporter, and attack the mimic with any ranged weapon. Use Smart Cursor to automatically use the switch and teleport to the other side of the arena when the mimic gets close to you. If the teleporters are spread away far enough, the mimic will always be in the air dashing towards your direction, being unable to perform any other attacks, making it predictable and easy to kill.
In regards to Biome Mimic drops, the Life Drain, Clinger Staff, and Daedalus Stormbow can be effective in killing The Destroyer segment of Mechdusa (the latter also being good against Mechdusa as a whole), while the Flesh Knuckles and Putrid Scent are both powerful combat accessories. Additionally, the hooks dropped by these mimics can uniquely be useful on this seed, if the player has not acquired one yet, and also makes fighting them in the future considerably easier. If manually summoning Biome Mimics, note that due to the effects of Drunk what the world deems to be the "current" world evil swaps every day at 4:30 AM. If you would like to be a bit more precise in obtaining weapon drops from a specific world evil mimic (e.g. preferring Chain Guillotines over Fetid Baghnakhs) you can use the dialogue from the Dryad ("You must cleanse the world of this corruption." vs "You must cleanse the world of this crimson.") to determine the world evil currently selected, before consuming a Key of Night.


===== Ice Golems =====
Ice Golems can spawn during Blizzards. It is recommended to either use hoiks and/or minions to kill them, as on this seed the laser produced by this enemy can deal a large amount of damage at once, and becomes much harder to dodge if the player is lacking in mobility. The Frost Cores they drop can be useful, if you wish to craft Frost armor and/or the Cool Whip, which is likely to be the first Hardmode whip that summon damage users can use on this seed.


===== Sand Elementals =====
Sand Elementals can spawn during Sandstorms. Their Forbidden Fragments are useful for crafting Forbidden armor, which is a valuable offensive but low defense hybrid armor set. This armor set (because of its set bonus), when combined with a piercing magic weapon like the Life Drain, is perhaps the most effective setup against the Destroyer segment of Mechdusa.


==== Pre-Hardmode bosses and events ====
Although not required by any means, these bosses can often provide useful drops.


===== Eye of Cthulhu, King Slime, and Deerclops =====
These bosses can be spawned fairly easily. The Suspicious Looking Eye and Deer Thing can be found in naturally-generated chests, while the Slime Crown is relatively inexpensive to craft. All three can be fought in the same arena. They are also not particularly difficult, as the player has access to Hardmode weapons.

Eye of Cthulhu will drop the Shield of Cthulhu, a remarkably useful accessory which provides the player with a dash, greatly improving the player's mobility in the early game. Additionally, as is the case in normal worlds, repeatedly summoning and killing the Eye of Cthulhu can also provide a source of early-game money.
Most of Deerclops' drops are irrelevant, but Chester can be useful for storage, while Houndius Shootius and/or the Bone Helm may prove useful when performing idle tasks such as fishing.
If your arena is not in an Ice biome, you can easily create one by putting ice blocks below the player.
King Slime's most relevant drop is the Slimy Saddle, which is useful for greatly increasing vertical mobility. Occasionally, Royal Gel can also prove useful at times, depending on the circumstance.


===== Eater of Worlds and Brain of Cthulhu =====
Even considering the high difficulty of this seed, the Eater of Worlds and Brain of Cthulhu are not too hard to kill, as the player has access to Hardmode weapons. Killing one of them gives access to the Worm Scarf and Brain of Confusion and also enables the Tavernkeep to spawn, which can open up more options for the player. Realistically the player should manually summon these bosses in their respective biomes using the respective boss summoning items, as due to the effects of Double daring dangers, Shadow Orbs and Crimson Hearts become much more inacessible to reach.

Note that being able to stack the Worm Scarf and Brain of Confusion on any given world is made much more easily on this seed, as both world evils are available from the start. In general, equipping both will improve your chance to survive during boss fights overall, and will be far more impactful than offensive accessories.


===== Skeletron =====
If the player wishes to fight Skeletron at any time, the Dungeon point is located in a single Dungeon room in the top outer corner of the map on the side that has the Skeletron Dungeon. Defeating Skeletron is useful as it enables access to the Mechanic, and also enables a few accesories such as the Obsidian Shield to now become available.


===== Queen Bee =====
(Unfinished)
Queen Bee's drops on their own are irrelevant and have been outclassed by this point, but defeating her will grant access to the Witch Doctor, who sells some useful items, such as the Imbuing Station to craft Flasks of Ichor with, Leaf Wings, and the Pygmy Necklace for Summoners.


===== Tier 1 Old One's Army =====
By this point, the player will have access to Hardmode weapons, so this tier of the Old One's Army will not generally provide a significant challenge to the player. However, the Apprentice's Scarf or Squire's Shield may prove useful if the player does the event in the future and has the Barnacle Staff or Queen Spider Staff. It is recommended to do this event repeatedly until the player has enough medals to afford a full tier 2 Tavernkeep armor set.


===== Wall of Flesh =====
While the Wall of Flesh can be skipped, the Demon Heart and emblems that it drops can be very helpful for further progression, and summoners can benefit from the Firecracker. Note that fighting the Wall of Flesh does not outright require terrain preparations: an easy method for fighting this boss is repeatedly attempting the fight while using an Orange Zapinator and riding a fast mount like the Unicorn, Basilisk, or Golf Cart on a platform just above the lava, to eventually roll a high damage shot and finish the boss off. Obsidian Skin Potions are also recommended when fighting the Wall of Flesh, as projectiles from the Imps can light the player on fire, easily rendering the fight unbeatable. If not using them, have Water Buckets ready.


==== Potential loadouts at this stage ====


===== Survivability =====
For armor, the Titanium Mask, Frost Breastplate, and Adamantite Leggings are best.
For accessories, reforging them to Warding (Armored and Guarding will also suffice) will help. Flesh Knuckles, Berserker's Glove (which are crafted from Flesh Knuckles), and Obsidian Shield are the easiest defense-increasing accessories that are available. The Ankh Shield is also technically available at this stage too, but can be tedious to acquire. Similarly, the Moon Charm boosts your defense, but unless you got it from a lucky drop early, it is locked behind farming Werewolves. On top of these, as stated earlier, using the Worm Scarf and/or Brain of Confusion can boost your survivability significantly.
For buffs, the Ironskin Potion and Endurance Potion, both of which are easy to obtain, can help even further.
If factoring in health regeneration, the Honey buff, Heart Lanterns, Campfires and Regeneration Potion are easy sources of it.
Well Fed and its medium tier upgrade are easy to obtain, and they boost the player's offensive and survival capabilities multilaterally.
Note that on Legendary Mode, even though enemy contact damage is adjusted to over five times that of the Classic Mode value, enemy projectile damage is the same as it is on Master Mode. If you are fighting a boss with large amounts of projectiles (e.g, Queen Slime) but you are able to dodge the boss itself well, you should consider specializing in defense, if not already. On this seed, doing so will make a greater difference than killing a boss slightly faster would.
Additionally, note that life regeneration becomes more potent the higher defense the player has; less damage directly taken from attacks will reduce the amount of time needed to heal the player to full health, which therefore reduces the chances of the player getting killed in a very short amount of time if they get hit multiple times in a row. 


===== Offense =====
Using a Wizard Hat combined with the Mystic Robe and Meteor Leggings, can be a very powerful (albeit fragile) armor set, providing damage bonuses comparable to that of traditional early Hardmode armor sets. Note that numerous magic weapons are readily available in early Hardmode (arguably more than any other phase of progression), including but not limited to the Frost Staff, Orange Zapinator, Life Drain, Wand of Sparking (on seeds with Remix enabled), Crystal Serpent, and Golden Shower.
If you are looking for extra DPS, the most readily-available minions from this stage are the Imp Staff and Spider Staff, although the latter requires Hardmode fishing to obtain the Mythril Bars or Orichalcum Bars necessary to craft a Hardmode Anvil.
As a whole, it is not recommended to be fully specialized into summoner loadouts this early on, as even with Spider armor available, good options are not easily obtained. On this seed, consider temporarily using a loadout for a different damage type until you have obtained a Bewitching Table, a way to consistently craft more Summoning Potions when you need them, and have the Witch Doctor moved in to sell the Pygmy Necklace.
On higher difficulties, a fight the player walks away from is equivalent to a fight won, especially on Hardcore. For this reason, it is worth using weapons that can stunlock enemies quickly if said enemy can quickly accelerate towards the player and kill them quickly (e.g. Mimics or Giant Tortoises).
The Snowball Cannon in particular is very good at this, as due to the effects of Remix it gains a much higher firerate, not to mention higher damage too.
The Blade Staff is dropped by Queen Slime is available not much later in progression by this point. Disregarding its damage entirely, the homing capabilities of Enchanted Daggers paired with their ability to rapidly stunlock enemies make them invaluable when exploring the world.


===== Mobility =====
As stated earlier, the Shield of Cthulhu is an easy-to-obtain accessory which can provide the player with a dash.
Roller Skates  are both very powerful and very easy to obtain. The Skeleton Merchant who sells them spawns much more frequently on this seed, as the player will be in the Caverns biome more often.
Regarding flight, Fin Wings are the only wings that are available before fighting Mechdusa (and killing at least one of the bosses) that do not require Souls of Flight. Note that they can be harder to obtain on this particular seed, as happiness being disabled means the Angler's reward rates cannot be improved by using that system.
As an alternative, the Sharkron Balloon is serviceable in regards to vertical mobility (especially if combined with a Frog Leg and hook) and is considerably easier to obtain than Fin Wings. You can also craft a Blizzard in a Bottle and/or Sandstorm in a Bottle using Frost Cores and Forbidden Fragments and a Crystal Ball, which can further improve player mobility for the time being at the cost of an accessory slot.
Once the player has defeated any of the bosses in Mechdusa, the Steampunker Jetpack or wings from a Developer set (i.e, Red's Wings) become available.

=== Events ===


==== Hardmode Blood Moon ====
If you want access to Hardmode ores without fishing, you can break Altars without having to kill any boss with the Haemorrhaxe, which can be obtained by farming Hemogoblin Sharks during a Blood Moon. They can be trapped by having a 3-block gap above the water pool and a 3-block thick ceiling above it to prevent them from clipping through it. Setting up a spawn point nearby the pool and enclosing the whole pool in a room will prevent them from despawning even when you get killed, as they will never get off-screen. Since fishing during a Blood Moon can be dangerous because of Blood Eels and Dreadnautilus, you can also set up portals with the Portal Gun (which can appear in Chests across the map with a 1/7 (14.29%) chance because of the We don't even test for that secret seed) with enough distance to despawn them before they can attack you. Additionally, you can also use a Sonar Potion to tell what Blood Moon enemy is fished up.
Once you're considerably more geared up, other Blood Moon enemies can be challenged. The Bananarang (which is dropped by Clowns) is a good melee weapon with some range, while the Sanguine Staff is a solid minion that can be used up to the Plantera phase.

=== Queen Slime ===

Her drops are not particularly substantial in this seed, but can be useful nonetheless. Crystal Assassin armor's damage buffs are too weak (and the armor does not have great defense), not to mention its dash tends to not be relevant as the Shield of Cthulhu is available. The Blade Staff is fine for all classes, and can be useful in some circumstances as a way to stunlock enemies from their knockback. Their knockback effect can be intensified by equipping a Moon Stone and/or consuming food buffs. Furthermore, the Hook of Dissonance can provide the player with a hook if they do not have one already, and the Gelatinous Pillion becomes useful as Wings are much harder to come by before defeating any of the three bosses in Mechdusa.


=== Mechdusa ===

Even though Mechdusa appears to be all three mechanical bosses at once, defeating one of the three bosses will still be counted towards the game's progression. Defeating one allows the second tier of the Old One's Army to be available, allows Life Fruit to begin to spawn in the Jungle, and allows the Steampunker to move in. Within the context of this seed's difficulty and numerous changes, the Destroyer is probably both the easiest and most strategically advantageous boss to kill first within Mechdusa; both advantageous within the own boss fight, and also for unlocking new options for the player after the fight is over (regardless if they won against the two other bosses). If timed correctly, weapons like the Life Drain can kill the Destroyer segment when coiled up in a matter of seconds, even on Legendary Mode. Killing the Destroyer also gives the player much more breathing room and space, as Skeletron Prime and The Twins function much more like traditional bosses. From there, it is generally recommended to focus on Skeletron Prime first, as it is a lot easier to dodge Prime's attacks during the first phase of the Twins than it is to dodge the second phases of the Twins' attacks while fighting Prime too. In general, sure to not accidentally let one of the Twins reach their second phase until you are ready, as it can make the fight significantly harder.


=== Tier 2 Old One's Army ===
As stated previously, the first tier of the Old One's Army can be repeatedly grinded for Defender Medals until the player has defeated any of the three bosses in Mechdusa, at which point second tier sentries and armor sets become available. These armor sets are powerful in both damage increases and versatility as well as being relatively inexpensive to obtain. In particular, Squire armor is likely the most helpful out of these sets on this seed, due to its high defense and the life regeneration properties of its headpiece. Also, keep in mind that damage taken at any point while having Squire armor equipped will also double the speed of your Ballista sentries for 5 seconds.
Regarding sentries, using Ballista Canes and Explosive Trap Canes alongside the Barnacle or Queen Spider staves can help your odds in completing this event successfully. Piercing weapons like the Golden Shower, Life Drain, and the Flint are not difficult to acquire and perform excellently against this tier. 
Most Tier 2 weapons dropped by the Ogre tend to be irrelevant; the Ghastly Glaive, Sleepy Octopod, and Brand of the Inferno are generally too close-range to be safe, as contact damage is incredibly high on this seed, and melee damage users playing on this seed should build towards melee weapons with range built in (like the Shadowflame Knife or Bananarang). For ranged damage users, the Phantom Phoenix is adequate, but is not particularly strong against Mechdusa due to lack of consistent piercing damage. Additionally, the Phantom Phoenix is rivalled by the Chlorophyte Shotbow (which is also easier to obtain). However, the Tome of Infinite Wisdom can prove useful to magic damage users with its secondary attack also being effective against the Destroyer. 
If doing this tier mainly for its gear, the player should do it as soon as available, as they will need all the help available. If doing this tier repeatedly to farm Defender Medals for when the third tier is available, note that it becomes easier to do so once you beat Mechdusa and Plantera.

Not much is different about her in this seed combination (besides her For the Worthy changes), although she can enrage more easily, thereby making the fight considerably harder due to the effects of Double daring dangers on biomes. Note that she will not enrage if the floor of the arena you fight her on is lined with Jungle grass.

=== Lunatic Cultist ===

(Unfinished)


=== Celestial Pillars ===
(Unfinished)


=== Moon Lord ===

The Moon Lord can be fought in the Underworld with some preparations. If you plan to use the lava shark, you can further flood the Underworld with lava and blow up/level the terrain so you can use all of it, or big portions of it, as a huge passageway that works as the arena. You will want to build another ceiling right where the lava ends, so that when he spawns his Moon Boulders, those spawn above the ceiling and cannot reach you. You will also need a Rod of Discord to easily dodge his Phantasmal Deathray, as both the lava shark's vertical mobility and the Underworld's (and, therefore, the arena's) vertical space are limited. Otherwise, you can easily outrun him and his True Eyes of Cthulhu and use ranged attacks from far away.


==== After Moon Lord ====
Congratulations on beating the hardest seed combination in Terraria!


=== Duke Fishron ===
Since the world has no surface, Duke Fishron is always enraged in True Zenith making him possibly the hardest boss out of all on this seed. One of the ways to fight him can be using full Summoner build with post-Moon Lord sentries while dodging his dashes with Rod of Harmony.
