title: Guide:Skeletron strategies
content:
Skeletron is a pre-Hardmode boss protecting the Dungeon. It's typically the last boss players will fight before the Wall of Flesh. Like any other boss fight in Terraria, defeating it is helped by preparing armor, buffs, and an arena. After this are some hints, tips, and strategies to help other players to do so.


== Spawn Condition ==
Skeletron can be spawned by fulfilling one of these conditions:

Talk with the Old Man at night. He can be found at the Dungeon entrance;
Kill the Clothier at night, with Clothier Voodoo Doll equipped.
It must then be defeated before all the involved players die.


== The Fight ==
Skeletron is a large skeleton, composed of a head and 2 hands. In order to defeat it, the head must be killed.
It attacks the player by swiping its hands. This attack is quite easy to predict, as it prepares them by pulling them back, so you can prepare to dodge them. However, the main issue is their erratic trajectory. The player can dodge them by either jumping or running around. It can use both hands to have different timings and trajectories, so the player might get caught off-guard by trying to dodge its other hand.
Timing is key in order to defend from the hands: after dodging them, use piercing weapons to deal damage to both arms (and Skeletron's skull, if it happens to align with them). The arms don't have much health, so they can be dispatched fairly easily.
After some time, Skeletron will use its spinning attack. Skeletron moves slowly, but they constantly follow the player. During this attack, Skeletron's defense is lowered to zero, but gains more attack. The player should use the fastest weapon at their disposal to deal a lot of damage. However, make sure to constantly move; if the player gets hit by it, they might get stunlocked and take a lot of damage.
During the spin attack, the hands will stay fixed in a uphanded position while Skeletron moves. This time can also used to deal damage to them, but keep in mind that their defense isn't reduced.
Failing to defeat it before 4:30 AM in-game will cause Skeletron to enrage. When enraged Skeletron acts just like the Dungeon Guardian; gaining extreme amounts of damage and defense, instantly killing players while only taking 1 or 2 damage from all attacks.


=== Expert Mode ===


==== Target Priorities ====
Skeletron's head has 60 defense until one of its hands go down. This means that almost every weapon at that point will not do more than 1 damage without a critical hit. As such, players are forced to defeat the arms first in order to progress. Moreover, the hands can inflict the Slow debuff, and its spin attack is much faster than in Classic Mode. After one of the arms goes down, Skeletron gains the ability to shoot skulls with a small homing effect when it's not spinning. The frequency of this attack increases as its health goes down and when the other arm falls. Skeletron's head also inflicts the Bleeding debuff, disabling natural health regeneration.
It is recommended to kill both hands at the same time, to minimize the amount of time Skeletron spends attacking with homing skulls alongside its remaining hand.


==== Mobility ====
Because of the player's lack of knockback immunity, getting hit by the spin attack can result on a death even at full health due to its massive damage and speed, so the player needs high mobility to avoid it at all costs.
A Blue Horseshoe Balloon or its equivalents together with Lightning Boots can provide that mobility, together with the Shield of Cthulhu, or a Featherfall Potion.
It's easier to dodge the skulls of the second stage while Skeletron remains above the player, since they can be dodged like Queen Bee's stingers with a little curve. However, this could make the spin attack connect more easily if the player isn't careful, as the head will stand closer to them.
The most effective way to dodge the skull attacks while remaining under the head of Skeletron is to run/dash left and right in quick and alternating succession.
While Skeletron is spinning, running in a straight line with Boots isn't recommended as it starts firing the skulls as soon as the attack is completed, so the player will most likely get hit by one of them. Because of this, moving in circles using the hover effect and/or double jumps is much safer. Featherfall Potions will allow players to stay in the air for much longer, making the circling much easier. On the other hand, if a straight line is prepared and health isn't a concern, it can be easy to inflict a lot of damage with a medium-ranged weapon like a yoyo with a string or a bow while backing away down the line, as the player can land many shots in succession without needing to aim.


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===

Warning: Don't make significant edits to the Dungeon floor. Doing so can stop the Endgame Cultists from spawning, potentially blocking progression. It is generally more convenient to plan the arena above the Dungeon roof or to the side of the Dungeon.
The entrance area to most Dungeons can often be modified into a more desirable arena if needed. Most important is that there is enough room to dodge the hands, as well as enough vertical space to avoid getting trapped when Skeletron's head begins to spin. 


=== Gearing up ===
Even though 300 health is considered enough by the Old Man, it's recommended to fight Skeletron with 400 health (and 200 mana for magic users). On Expert Mode or higher difficulties, 400 health is almost mandatory.


==== Armor ====
A full set of at least Shadow armor or Crimson armor should be acquired as the player should have killed their evil boss, but armor for the player's weapon class is always an option.
The Gladiator armor's knockback immunity provides significant advantages against Skeletron, especially in high difficulties.
TheMolten armor is the best pre-Hardmode armor set for melee classes, although it requires a visit to the Underworld and a pickaxe that can mine Hellstone. It is also possible to use this set as a ranger.
The Fossil armor is the only armor set available for rangers before the dungeon.
The Wizard set, with magic-boosting or defense-boosting leg armor, provides the most damage for magic users. If defense is preferred, Jungle armor or Meteor armor can be used.
If using the Diamond Staff, a Gem robe such as the Amethyst Robe can be useful for its homing effect.
Meteor armor's set bonus can make the Space Gun and Gray Zapinator much more effective against Skeletron since it reduces Space Gun's and Gray Zapinator's mana usage to 0.
The Obsidian armor is the best summoner armor set at this point in the game which focuses on whip bonuses.
The Bee armor is an alternative set if the Queen Bee has been defeated that focuses on minion bonuses. It is also possible to use this set as a ranger or a melee user, in case the evil boss was skipped, and defense isn't a concern.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users:

Yoyos such as Amazon are excellent against Skeletron, as they can deal high damage from a distance. Eliminating the hands first can be done very rapidly as the hands tend to push yoyos around, making additional contact and dealing more damage.
The Hive-Five far outperforms the Code 1 and Amazon, but requires killing the Queen Bee.
The Volcano is a strong choice if the player has mined Hellstone. It isn't as risky as other broadswords due to its greater reach, has great damage output, and inflicts a debuff that may increase visibility as well as damage.
The Starfury does excellent damage with the star projectile, as well as regular melee damage vs the hands.
A Phaseblade can be thrown, piercing through multiple parts of Skeletron at once. It can be used as a standard broadsword as well for riskier but higher damage, giving it some flexibility.
The Blade of Grass might not dish out as much damage as some of the other swords around this point in progression, but because of its projectiles it's somewhat safer to use.
Both the Bee Keeper and Lucy the Axe do more damage than any sword besides the Volcano, but both require defeating a difficult boss and require close combat.
Boomerangs like the Thorn Chakram work well but they are more effective when thrown past the Skull.
The Flamarang is also available if the player has mined Hellstone, and is one of the best boomerangs available before Hardmode.
Flails can work due to their long range and ability to hit both the arms and head with a single attack. The only viable flails available at this point are the Ball O' Hurt and The Meatball.
For Ranged users:

The Bee's Knees is a great choice as the Bees can deal massive damage, especially during Skeletron's spinning attack.
The Pew-matic Horn is one of the strongest guns available in pre-Hardmode, and works well vs Skeletron.
The Demon and Tendon Bow are the most accessible bows at this stage. Use them with Frostburn Arrows and Jester's Arrows.
The Molten Fury and Hellfire Arrows are very strong if the player has already gotten Hellstone.
The Blood Rain Bow can be used in some arena setups to deal damage while protected from flying skulls in Expert Mode, but otherwise deals relatively low damage.
The Minishark, Musket, and Boomstick are very effective against Skeletron.
The Minishark may prove ineffective without a Shark Tooth Necklace as Skeletron's defense when it isn't spinning renders the Minishark almost useless.
Bone Javelins are very effective due to their high damage and firing speed.
Molotov Cocktails can be used to deal large amounts of damage to Skeletron.
Beenades can be used to deal damage without needing to aim.
The Star Cannon is the most powerful weapon in pre-Hardmode, but requires some preparation to build up enough ammunition.
However, in worlds with For the Worthy active, Skeletron will deflect projectiles from the Star Cannon, rendering it useless.
For Magic users:

The strongest weapon at this stage is Demon Scythe, obtained from as a rare drop from Demons in the Underworld.
The Gray Zapinator is stronger than the Space Gun, and benefits from the Meteor armor's set bonus as well. Its only downside is its limited availability from the Traveling Merchant.
The Bee Gun, dropped by the Queen Bee, does steady damage, especially with the Hive Pack equipped. Its main attraction is that it requires no aiming at all, allowing the player to focus on dodging.
While weaker than the above items, the Thunder Zapper, Space Gun, Mystic Bloom are convenient to obtain and make the fight relatively straightforward.
Gem staves are weaker options for this fight but can be obtained easily, though the Wizard set provides insignificant defense and the staves' damage is not good enough to finish off the boss quickly.
Amethyst's homing ability is very helpful in this fight, being able to track the boss while the player focuses on dodging.
The strongest combinations are generally, Emerald Staff with Amethyst Robe, and Diamond Staff with Ruby Robe. If any of the ores are not present in the world, the reversed combination between staff and robe can also be used, though being weaker.
Other gem staves are all viable, but way weaker than the combinations above, for this specific fight.
The Crimson Rod is also a very effective method of damaging Skeletron, even allowing it to be used in combination with other weapons. If carefully placed, the cloud created by the Rod can cause 100 damage per second. However it will only be available in a Crimson world.
The Weather Pain, dropped by Deerclops, is a powerful homing magic weapon that can make short work of the hands in the first phase. Because it makes one lingering projectile at a time, it can be used in conjunction with other weapons.
For Summoners:

The Snapthorn is generally the best whip available. The Starcrash can do more damage when paired with high-damage minions like the Imp Staff, but its meteors can miss Skeletron due to the boss's high speed if the player is not careful.
The Vampire Frog Staff, from the Blood Moon, and Imp Staff, from the Underworld, are the strongest minions available. The Frogs deal high damage but may require additional platforms to reach Skeletron, while the imps can fly and aim well but may occasionally interfere with each other due to i-frames.
The Hornet Staff, dropped by the Queen Bee, can do well when paired with whips and the Hive Pack, but have difficulty overcoming Skeletron's defense on their own.
The strongest sentry available is Houndius Shootius. The Ballista Rod or Flameburst Rod are also helpful alternatives.


==== Accessories ====
Spectre Boots, Lightning Boots, Frostspark Boots, or Terraspark Boots are very useful for their hover effect and running speed.
The Cloud in a Bottle or any of its upgrades and their counterparts are recommended, especially on Expert mode. Fledgling Wings, rarely found in Skyware Chests or Sky Crates, may serve as a replacement.
The Amber Horseshoe Balloon behaves similarly to Fledgling Wings, with the added benefit of receiving the Honey buff whenever the player is struck as well as helpful Bees.
The Sweet Barb has similar honey and bee effects when struck, while providing additional bees when arrows hit the boss.
The Snapping Stone can provide a steady damage boost for ranged players. Similarly, the Harpy Charm can buff critical strike chance for all ranged weapons and guide arrows to the boss.
The Pyroclastic Stone is a significant upgrade to the Snapping Stone that buffs both melee and ranged weapons.
The Shield of Cthulhu is extremely useful for the Expert Mode fight, as the dash makes dodging the skulls and the spin attack much easier.
The Shark Tooth Necklace and/or Stinger Necklace can significantly increase damage output, especially when using weapons with high attack speed.
If the Queen Bee has been defeated, the Pygmy Necklace is an exceptionally good accessory for summoners.
The Squire's Shield/Apprentice's Scarf are great choices for summoners, although they don't stack.
The Hive Pack gives a boost to the damage and velocity of some of the bees spawned by the Queen Bee's drops.
The Worm Scarf and Brain of Confusion reduce damage taken, making them invaluable for Expert and Master Mode.


==== Potions ====
Ironskin Potions, Endurance Potions, and Regeneration Potions will make the job easier for any player and are highly recommended. Two potions will last for the entire night, provided the player stays alive the entire time.
The Inferno Potion is a good idea for melee players.
The Swiftness Potion helps for outrunning the spinning attack.
Mana Regeneration Potion is mandatory for magic users. Magic Power Potions are also helpful.
If using a melee weapon, Ale/Sake provides a decent boost.
Any food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed/Plenty Satisfied buff is very helpful, especially on Expert Mode since it will bring regeneration back to normal.
An Archery Potion gives a very good damage and velocity bonus to bows.
Wrath Potions and Rage Potions also increase damage output.
Featherfall Potions can aid with air mobility and give basic flying abilities.
Summoners should use Summoning Potions.


==== Others ====
The Slimy Saddle helps with dodging and can also be used to escape the spin attack. The Honeyed Goggles can be used for a similar purpose with its flight.
A good Grappling Hook is also useful for enabling sudden bursts of movement.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Minecart Strategy ===

An alternative to high-maneuverability armor or accessories, which can even work against Expert Mode Skeletron, is to craft a Minecart for the extra speed and build a large, diamond-shaped Minecart Track, such as one having in the middle on each side three Minecart Tracks with a Bumper on the outer end, and the inner end connects using a switch track to two diagonal tracks, with both connected and the preferred direction up on one side and down on the other, and with a total width of roughly 90-100 blocks. After the Skeletron battle begins, mount the Minecart and accelerate to maximum Minecart speed. While collisions can occasionally occur, they should be uncommon enough that healing will not be a problem. Using attacks at range is highly preferred, though unlike a hoik system, a Minecart might not move fast enough to allow a boomerang to do all of the work as in some Dungeon Guardian strategies. If using pre-Hardmode weapons, the Molten Fury with Frostburn Arrows is highly recommended.
If using the Minecart strategy and for whatever reason the battle lasts until dawn, the Dungeon Guardian A.I. will actually cause the Skeletron head to follow you at such a slow and steady pace that it should never catch up. In such a case, however, you will take fatal damage from contact and deal 1 damage with every landed attack, or 2 from critical hits, causing fast attacks at range to become essential (such as the Space Gun with the full set of Meteor armor); thus, having a set of accessories with critical chance modifiers becomes far more important than damage, defense, or mobility, should it come to this.


=== Circle Strategy (Expert/Master) ===
Mobility and damage matter the most in these modes.
Near the Dungeon, make two or three long rows of platforms, about one screen high and two screens wide. Use a horseshoe balloon and Spectre Boots or Lightning Boots, a combination that is essentially like wings in pre-Hardmode. Featherfall Potion is also a plus. The Shield of Cthulhu is the last essential accessory. An optional item is the Umbrella if you can obtain it.
During the fight, use your platforms to move in circles around Skeletron, flying over and around him and running underneath. The Shield of Cthulhu will allow you to dash away from the skull and accelerate instantly.
The Bee's Knees and Bee Gun with the Hive Pack are especially effective weapons, as accuracy is not as important with these weapons. The Space Gun is another effective alternative.
Using this method, just keep circling and attacking the hands; once the skulls start shooting, you will still be circling and dodging will still be easy.

title: Shrub Star
content:
The Shrub Star is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns an Everscream Sapling to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Everscream Sapling flies toward them, tucking its legs together and emitting fire from its legs like a rocket. The Shrub Star is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 5–25% chance depending on the current wave.


== Trivia ==
The tooltip is a reference to the English lullaby "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star".

title: Mana Sickness
content:
Mana Sickness is a debuff that reduces the player's magic damage after they consume any mana-restoring item. Automatically drinking Mana Potions with the Mana Flower will also cause the debuff. Whenever a mana-restoring item is consumed, the player is inflicted with 5 seconds of Mana Sickness. The percentage of magic damage reduction is proportional to the remaining debuff duration (see Notes for formula), reducing by 1% every 1/5 second; at 5 seconds remaining, the damage reduction is 25%. All mana-restoring items inflict the same length of the debuff; for example, a Lesser Mana Potion induces the same duration of Mana Sickness as a Greater Mana Potion.
If the player consumes additional mana-restoring items while the debuff is active, the duration will be increased by 5 seconds for each item consumed, up to a maximum of 10 seconds (50% damage reduction).
The magic damage reduction is multiplicative rather than additive, and is applied after all damage multipliers. For example, if the player has +100% damage from buffs and items, the total damage with the debuff at 5 seconds left comes to 150% (200% × (1 - 25%); -25% comes from Mana Sickness).


== Causes ==


=== From item ===


== Notes ==
The magic damage reduction is calculated by the following formula, with the remaining debuff duration measured in ticks.
[math]\displaystyle{ \text{Reduction multiplier}=0.25\times\frac{\text{Debuff duration}}{300} }[/math]


== See also ==
Potion Sickness, debuff that is also triggered by drinking potions
Mana Surge, a buff with similar mechanics but results in the opposite effect


== History ==

title: Xeno Staff
content:
The Xeno Staff is a Hardmode, post-Golem summon weapon that summons a UFO minion. It hovers above enemies, firing blue lasers that hit the target instantaneously. If an enemy is 18.75 to 50 tiles away, it will instantly teleport above it. The Xeno Staff has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Notes ==
The UFO's lasers are fired instantaneously at a rate of once every 0.45 seconds on average.
UFO minions can target enemies up to 125 tiles away from the player, and will automatically return to the player's side if their distance from the player is more than 125 tiles.
If an enemy is targeted by the player, UFO minions can continue attacking it until their distance from the player is more than 187.5 tiles, at which point the minion targeting circle disappears and aggro range of UFO minions returns to normal, causing them to teleport to the player's side.


== Tips ==
The Xeno Staff's fast movement speed and perfect accuracy make it an excellent choice against faster bosses such as Duke Fishron and the Empress of Light.


== Trivia ==
The prefix xeno- means foreign, different in origin, and often relates to aliens.
Prior to the 1.3.5 update, the Xeno Staff had an extremely low sell value (at only 20 Silver), making reforging it to a desired modifier very cheap.
The Xeno Staff has the lowest item ID of all items added in the 1.3.0.1 update.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Removed mana cost (cost 10 mana previously).

title: Space
content:
Space is the layer making up the top of the world, above the Surface. Gravity is decreased in Space, which means the player can jump higher and will fall slower, similar to the Featherfall effect. The sky is dark and stars are visible, even when the sun is still up. There are no naturally occurring blocks or objects in Space, although Floating Island or Living Tree parts may extend into it.
Despite being at such high altitudes, players that enter Space do not experience any consequences. They will neither incur the Suffocation debuff nor will the breath meter appear.
Fallen Stars spawn in Space and can appear inside structures made at high altitudes. Harpies and, in Hardmode, Wyverns spawn in Space. Additionally, Martian Probes are more likely to spawn in Space and common enemies such as slimes and Zombies can also appear in Space, given a viable area to spawn on.
The Forest Pylon can be used in Space.


== Contents ==


== Altitude thresholds ==
There is no definite border between the Surface and Space. The transition is smooth; there are different altitude thresholds for the biome's features listed in the table below. These thresholds are based on the area between the surface line and the top of the world. Since the distance between the two differs from world to world due to the randomized world generation, the thresholds can be expressed more accurately in percentages of said area.

Concrete, absolute altitudes for a given world can be displayed in the table above by moving a character to the very top of said world (the head must touch the visible world border) and entering the readout of the Depth Meter (or its upgrades) here:


== Notes ==
A pure Space biome is required for fishing in Space, otherwise no Space-exclusive fishing catches can be obtained.
During pre-Hardmode, Space enemies cannot spawn in the central 10% of the world (horizontally).
For example, in a small world (which is 4200 tiles wide), Space enemies in pre-Hardmode can only spawn more than 210 tiles (5%) laterally away from the world's center. They cannot spawn within those central 420 tiles.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
There are numerous ways to reach Space:
Build a pillar of blocks or any type of Rope.
Consume a Gravitation Potion or use a Gravity Globe.
Equip wings, Rocket Boots or their upgrades, or other jump-boosting accessories to reach higher altitudes, especially when used from a Floating Island or other tall structures.
Use an Ice Rod as a mode of ascension, or to use as a way to reset wings' flight time midair.
Fly up while being a ghost from a deceased Hardcore character.
Note that this does not grant the Into Orbit achievement.
Construct a railroad that ascends upwards.
Use a mount that flies, like the Bee or UFO Mount.


== Trivia ==
The Space music of the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version used to be exclusive to only those versions, but has since been implemented into the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version as the Space Day theme.


== History ==

title: Everscream
content:
The Everscream is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Frost Moon event. It is the Frost Moon equivalent of the Mourning Wood, which behaves in an almost identical way to the Everscream.
Defeating the Everscream during the Frost Moon event will add 50 / 100 / 125 points to the final score.


== Behavior ==
The Everscream alternates between two attacks:

Fires a volley of Pine Needles at the player. This is somewhat similar to Mourning Wood's Flaming Wood attack, but the Pine Needles are fired more rapidly, deal less damage, are less accurate, do not pass through blocks, and are affected by gravity.
Releases several bouncing Ornaments, which are affected by gravity and shatter after 5 seconds in a manner similar to Crystal Bullets, in that their shrapnel also deals damage. These are fired in a similar but slower manner to the Mourning Wood's Greek Fire.


== Notes ==
The Everscream begins spawning during the Frost Moon event at wave 4.
The Everscream may hover through blocks in order to reach far-away players.
The Everscream has a higher chance of dropping loot in later waves. See Frost Moon § Loot for more details.
When the Frost Moon event ends, all enemies will flee, including the Everscream. Unlike other event mini-bosses such as Mothron, who are invincible when the Solar Eclipse event ends, Everscreams can still be harmed and killed after the event is over, showing little to no retaliation. This allows the player to easily defeat the Everscream if they are fast enough. This trait is shared by the Mourning Wood.


== Tips ==
Most of the Everscream's attacks can easily be avoided by staying on platforms high enough above the ground, as the attacks have limited range. Attacking with any ranged or long-range melee weapon from there trivializes the fight.
The Everscream is one of the few mini-bosses whose attacks can be shielded, as its Ornament and Pine Needle attacks do not go through blocks.
Unlike Mourning Wood, the Everscream's attacks do not deal increased damage after its health drops past 25%.


== Trivia ==
The Everscream's Pine Needle attack is similar to the Razorpine that it drops.
Everscream is a portmanteau of evergreen and scream.
The Everscream and the Dark Mage(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are the only event bosses that cannot drop a ranged weapon.
 The Bestiary entry for the Everscream: "If trees could scream, this evil evergreen would do so constantly. Deadly are the ornaments hurled from its branches."

title: Banners (enemy)
content:
Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks, platforms, and Planter Boxes. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters.

When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken.
Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon.
There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

== Banners with non-default kill count ==
By default, a banner is obtained upon defeating a specific enemy 50 times (or for every 50 afterward). For the following banners, this kill count requirement is different:


== Unobtainable ==


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Banner effect calculation ==

When dealing damage to enemies, banners apply their damage increase on base damage, before being reduced by defense and doubled by critical strike. When taking damage from enemies, banners also apply their damage reduce on base damage before being reduced by defense and damage reduction effects. As a result, the effect of banners is usually more significant than other damage increase/decrease effects, especially in Expert Mode where banners are more effective.
The following table shows some examples about banner effect.


== Notes ==
Bosses do not have banners, but trophies instead. These do not grant any buffs, however.
If an NPC lands the killing blow on an enemy that would have dropped a banner, the last player to hit the enemy receives the banner.
The effective range of the buffs from banners is based on the center of the player's view, not where the player is positioned. This can be proven by using Binoculars or a gun equipped with the Sniper Scope or its upgrades.
Enemies spawned from Statues count towards the kill count as usual. Because of this, banners for some Hardmode enemies, such as Wraith banners, can be obtained in pre-Hardmode using their respective statues.


== Tips ==
Banners can be suspended under Smoke Blocks and Living Fire Blocks hammered to half blocks or to flat-bottomed slopes. This may be preferred over blocks, platforms, or Planter Boxes, as nothing can collide with Smoke and Living Fire Blocks.
However, the War Table Banner immediately breaks when placed.
The blocks can be painted with Echo Coating to suspend banners invisibly and with no collision. Likewise, the banners can be painted to provide their buffs invisibly.
Living Fire Blocks emit light, while Smoke Blocks do not.


== Trivia ==
Each banner may be placed in a right- or left-facing orientation, but this is decided by which tile column in the world the banner is placed. Placing it one block to the left or right will flip the orientation.
The left half of the Nymph Banner depicts the Lost Girl, while the right half is the actual Nymph enemy.
The Nymph Banner's internal name is misspelled as NypmhBanner.
Diggers share the same banner and kill count with their pre-Hardmode counterparts, the Giant Worms.
The Tortured Soul does not have a banner.
The Maggot Zombie does not have its own banner; however, the Zombie Banner does offer a buff against it.
The Hoplite and Medusa Banners are the only banners that do not show a picture of the enemy. Instead, each resembles dark green banners with golden Greek patterns, with the Hoplite and Medusa Banners having a picture of a helm and snake on them respectively.
The Bunny, Bird, Goldfish, and Penguin are the only four critters that have banners of themselves. The four banners still give a buff on attack and defense against the aforementioned critters, even though they cannot actually harm the player.
While the player has no banner, the Nurse will muse about a hypothetical "player banner" if spoken to while the player has died at least 25 and less than 100 times (outside of PvP): "The monsters of <world name> have slain you <number of non-PvP deaths> times already? I wonder which one picked up your banner..."
This line of dialogue is slightly deprecated as of the 1.4.5.0 update, as enemies no longer drop banners by themselves.
The dedicated window for banners located beside the crafting menu was first seen in the March 2024 State of the Game blog.

title: Pumpking
content:
The Pumpking is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Pumpkin Moon event. He is the event's final enemy and can move freely through blocks. He is the equivalent to the Ice Queen from the Frost Moon, being the Pumpkin Moon's most powerful enemy, coming in at the last waves of the event, and being the event's only flying boss.
Defeating the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event will add 150 / 300 / 375 points to the final score, giving the most number of points for any enemy in the event.
Like the Mourning Wood, the later the Pumpkin Moon wave in which the Pumpking is killed in, the more likely he is to drop items. A Pumpking defeated during wave 15 has a guaranteed chance to drop at least one item from his standard drop table.


== Behavior ==

The Pumpking has two arms, called Pumpking Blades, which behave much like Skeletron's hands by swiping towards the player to inflict contact damage, but unlike Skeletron's hands, the Pumpking Blades are entirely immune to damage. The Pumpking repeatedly switches between three different attack patterns at random, with his current attack mode indicated by his facial expression. When transitioning to his next mode, his head rotates to reveal a different expression.

Mode 1: The Pumpking's face resembles a typical jack-o-lantern, with a sinister-looking grin. He attempts to hover directly above the player and performs aggressive melee swipes with his Pumpking Blade arms. About five seconds into this stage, he will rapidly accelerate towards the player at a high speed for the rest of the time he remains in this stage.
Mode 2: The Pumpking's mouth is partially open, with a grimacing expression. The Pumpking Blades periodically fire large yellow scythe-shaped projectiles called Flaming Scythes. Similar to the Demon Scythe's projectiles, the Flaming Scythes are motionless for a few seconds before gradually beginning to spin and accelerate toward the player with increasing speed, dealing massive amounts of damage per hit.
Mode 3: The Pumpking's face appears surprised, with his mouth agape in an "O" shape. While following the player from a greater distance, he spits out several yellow Greek Fire projectiles from his mouth, similar to the Mourning Wood, which fall to the ground before lingering on solid tiles for a short while, inflicting immense damage upon contact.


== Notes ==
The Pumpking begins to spawn during the Pumpkin Moon event at wave 10.
If not defeated before dawn (4:30 AM) or all players present in the current world are dead while the event is active, all active Pumpkings will retreat straight down through the ground and despawn. This trait is also shared by the Mourning Wood.
Stray Flaming Scythes thrown by a Pumpking can travel far outside enemy spawn boundaries, able to kill town NPCs in their houses.


== Tips ==

The Flairon can be very effective against the Pumpking, who tends to float right above players (well within the range of the Flairon and its homing bubbles), causing very high damage per hit.
The Pumpking's contact damage is relatively lower than the damage inflicted by his projectiles, especially his Flaming Scythes. Using wings and other flight-based accessories like the Soaring Insignia to fly closer towards his head while tanking his contact damage with high defense may help the player avoid taking excessive amounts of damage, especially in cases when they are being attacked by multiple Pumpkings at once.
High-mobility items, such as the Anti-Gravity Hook, the Tabi and its upgrades, or the Shield of Cthulhu, allow for easier handling of the Pumpking.


== Trivia ==

Pumpking is a portmanteau of pumpkin and king.
The Pumpking's NPC ID image only contains his head, which is the only part of his main body that can take and deal damage. The cloak that is attached to the Pumpking head's sprite is stored separately as a harmless, non-damageable entity by the name of PumpkingCloak.xnb.
Despite its name, The Horseman's Blade drops from the Pumpking and not from the Headless Horseman.
The Pumpking and the Poltergeist are the only two Pumpkin Moon enemies whose main bodies consistently travel through blocks.
The Pumpking Blades have health and defense values even though they cannot be damaged.
A cloud in the shape of the Pumpking can occasionally be seen in the background.
 The Bestiary entry for the Pumpking: "A pumpkin has many faces. A pumpkin will murder all with many sharp blades. A pumpkin is king of the harvest."

title: Town Bunny
content:
The Bunny is a town pet. It arrives at dawn (4:30 AM) the day after the player uses the Bunny License, which is purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. The Bunny does not count towards the NPCs' "crowded" limit and hence will not affect NPC happiness, although it does count as a regular town NPC for the purpose of the Pylon network. There are six breeds of Bunny, with one randomly being chosen when it arrives. Only one Bunny can be present at a time.

Just like any other town NPC, the Bunny requires a valid house and can be manually assigned to one via its NPC flag. The Bunny can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). It may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for its home tile (standing point).
The Bunny can be talked to with the ⚷ Open / Activate button, like any other town NPC. It offers a “Pet” option, which places the player directly in front of the Bunny when selected, and displays an animation of them petting the Bunny, an effect that is purely visual. It only works if there are at least two flat tiles on the same level as the Bunny in front of it. Using any item, taking damage, or closing the dialogue window terminates the animation.
Like with the Angler and the Princess, the status message displayed when the Bunny is killed is “<Name of Bunny> has left!”. It will respawn within the next days, and may respawn as a different breed. Furthermore, using a Bunny License while a Bunny is already present causes the Bunny to be "exchanged", releasing a puff of smoke and rerolling its breed and name immediately.


== Notes ==
Status messages about usage of the Bunny License:
First use: “The license teleports away to the bunny delivery service...”
Subsequent uses when the Town Bunny does not exist: “Wait for your pet to move in before exchanging it!”
Subsequent uses when the Town Bunny exists: “Pet Exchange: Successful!”


== Achievements ==


== Names ==
The Town Bunny may have any of the following names:


=== Lop ===


=== White ===


=== Silver ===


=== Angora ===


=== Flemish ===


=== Dutch ===


== Quotes ==
*Rabbit noises*
*Bunny noises*


== Trivia ==
The Bestiary page for the Town Bunny depicts the Angora bunny breed by default.
The Bunny's quotes reference the lack of popular onomatopoeia for bunny noises in written English (unlike "Meow" or "Woof" for cats and dogs, respectively).
Despite the real-life Flemish breed of rabbit being one of the giant breeds, the sprite is the same size as the others.
The "White" variant is a reference to the real-life Florida White breed of rabbit, with red eyes and an albino fur pattern to match.
The "Silver" variant is a reference to the real-life Standard Chinchilla rabbit breed, named after their resemblance to a chinchilla.
Many names are references:

"Alice" may be a reference to the white rabbit in Alice in Wonderland.
"Bugz" may be a reference to Bugs Bunny, one of the main characters from the show Looney Tunes.
"Bunbun" is a reference to a mini-lop character from webcomic Sluggy Freelance.
"Bunnicula" is a reference to a children's book series and animated TV series by that name.
"Bunstar" may be a reference to the manga Beastars, where one of the characters, Haru, is an anthropomorphic rabbit.
"Buster" and "Babs" are a reference to two characters of the same name from Tiny Toon Adventures.
"Caerbannog" is a reference to the killer rabbit from Monty Python and the Holy Grail.
In a similar way, the "White" bunny appearance has red eyes, possibly referencing the very same rabbit.
"Daisy" is a reference to Doomguy's pet bunny of the same name.
"Donnie" may be a reference to Donnie Schenck from AMC's Preacher, where he was known as the "Bunny Man" for the noise he would make upon having his wrist fractured.
"Dustbunny" may be a reference to the phrase dust bunny.
"Flappie" is a very common name for pet rabbits in the Netherlands, and may be a reference to the song with the same name by Dutch comedian Youp van 't Hek.
"Flops" may be a reference to King Bumi's pet goat-gorilla Flopsie from Avatar: The Last Airbender.
"Hazel" may be a reference to the protagonist of the book Watership Down, a rabbit named Hazel.
"Inaba" is a reference to the Hare of Inaba from Japanese mythology.
"Jazz" is likely a reference to Jazz Jackrabbit, the titular character in a series of platformer-style computer games of the same name from 1994.
"Joshua" is likely a reference to the character of the same name from the role-playing video game series Trails. Furthermore, both "Renne" and "Estelle" are possible names for the Cat and Dog, respectively, likely referencing the names of two other characters from the same series.
"Kaguya" may be a reference to the Rabbit Goddess Kaguya Ōtsutsuki from Naruto.
The name Kaguya itself usually refers to the main character of The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter (also known as The Tale of Princess Kaguya), Nayotake no Kaguya-hime. Also, in Japanese culture, there's an association between rabbits and moon.
"Lola" is a reference to Lola Bunny, a character from the movie Space Jam.
"Max" is a reference to the "hyperkinetic rabbity thing" from Sam & Max. It could also be a reference to the children's show Max & Ruby.
"Oreo" is a reference to the popular cookie brand of the same name, of which the breed, Dutch, is the same color.
"Peter" may be a reference to Peter Rabbit, the titular character in the books by Beatrix Potter.
"Presto" is a reference to the Pixar short of the same name.
"Roger" is a reference to the title character in Who Framed Roger Rabbit.
"Thumper" is a reference to the rabbit character from Bambi.
"Yin" and "Yang" is a reference to the ancient Chinese philosophy concept of Yin and yang, which also inspires many common names for black and white pets such as the Dutch species.
"Mochi" may be a reference to the character of the same name from the Lonely Wolf Treat series by NomnomNami.
 The Bestiary entry for the Town Bunny: "Guaranteed to keep the vegetable supplies in check. Might possibly become a hat."
This refers to the Rabbit Perch, a vanity item sold by the Zoologist.

title: Cobwhip
content:
The Cobwhip is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 60% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

3 tag damage
Releases a small spider that lasts for 3 seconds, which repeatedly deals 2 damage on contact and has 30 armor penetration, but does not inflict knockback. The spider also applies the Cobwhip's tag damage to enemies it hits, like the whip itself. If a spider already exists, Cobwhip hits will refresh its duration instead of releasing a new one.
Its best modifier is Legendary.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The spider applies 20 ticks of local invincibility frames on hit, meaning it can hit for up to 3 times per second.
The spider does not benefit from whip tag effects and ignores the player's prioritized target.
The spider can target enemies within a 28.125-tile distance.


== Tips ==
The Cobwhip can also be crafted with a Living Loom, making Living Trees convenient for summon users as the Finch Staff can also be found in its chests.


== Trivia ==
Unlike the Spider Staff's minions, the Cobwhip spider cannot climb background or latch into enemies.

title: Flight
content:
Flight allows players to move freely in the air. Rocket Boots, Wings, and certain Mounts allow flight with varying duration and maneuverability.
The Soaring Insignia grants infinite flight time with items that normally have a duration.
Some flight items allow the player to "hover". Activating this varies by item. For example, the Drill Containment Unit hovers automatically, the Flying Carpet hovers while holding ↷ Jump, and the Hoverboard hovers while holding ↷ Jump + ▼ Down.
Some flight items, like the Jetpack and Bee Mount, allow faster ascent while holding ▲ Up or faster descent while holding ▼ Down.


== Rocket Boots ==
Rocket Boots are pre-Hardmode accessories which offer early access to limited flight. All variants provide 1.17 seconds of flight time with a 1.5 times multiplier to jump speed Verify. Rocket flight will only activate after all extra jumps (e.g. from Sandstorm in a Bottle) are used.
When paired with wings, rocket flight is disabled to give wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time.


== Mounts ==


== Wings ==


== Other flight accessories ==


== Notes ==
While wings and mounts automatically cancel fall damage, Rocket Boots do not.
After wing's flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide, slowing descent speed by 66.67%.
All flying mounts have 50% increased vertical speed during flight, except for the Winged Slime Mount with 25% decreased speed instead.


== Tips ==
Although not true flight, an alternative to long range flight can be achieved using the gravity switching affects of Gravitation Potions or the Gravity Globe accessory. When using these, gravity can be flipped using the ▲ Up key, causing the player to suddenly lift off the ground and fall in the opposite direction. This can be useful to quickly find Floating Islands.
An Ice Rod can be used to lay blocks of ice to land in midair, making it possible to remain in the air indefinitely.

title: Guide:Setting up Steam Multiplayer
content:
This guide explains the process needed to be taken in order to set up multiplayer using the Steam interface.


== Hosting a world ==

Follow the method below if you want to allow friends to play on your local world.


=== Setting up the server ===

From the title screen, go to "Multiplayer" > "Host & Play".
Select a character to play as, or create a new one.
Select a world to play on, or create a new one.
You will then be prompted to choose a Steam multiplayer mode. If you want friends to be able to freely join, select "Friends Only", or if you only want select friends to join, select "Invite Only".
You will then be prompted to enter a password. Enter a password or leave blank if you do not want the server to be password protected.
It will then start the server, and join the selected world.


=== Inviting friends ===

NOTE: These steps are only required if the " Invite Only" mode was selected in the server setup.

Open up your inventory.
Go to "Settings" in the lower right corner.
Click on the "Invite Friends" button in the middle of the menu. This will open up the Steam overlay with a dialog showing your online friends.
Click the invite button on the right of all the friends you want to invite. They will then receive a notification with the invite.
Click the "Return to Game" button on the lower left of the dialog to return to Terraria.


== Joining a world ==
Follow the method below if you want to join a friends world or if you have received an invite.
NOTE: You may only join a friend's world using this method if they have set it up with the above steps.


=== Joining a "Friends Only" World ===
From the title screen, go to "Multiplayer" > "Join via Steam". This will open the Steam overlay to the "Friends" dialog.
Find the friend that you wish to play with in the list. Click the triangle drop-down menu beside their name and click "Join Game". If this option is grayed out or not available, but they are running a server via Steam, then it is most likely to be on "Invite Only" mode. Ask them to send you an invite and follow the steps in the next section.
Select a character to play as, or create a new one.
You may be prompted to enter a password. If you do not know the password, ask your friend for it to continue.
It will then join you onto your friends world at the default spawn point, giving the status message “[Player] has joined.”


=== Joining an "Invite Only" World ===
If you have been invited to play on a friend's world, you should see a notification saying "[Steam Name] has invited you to play Terraria".
Go to the main title screen, and click on this notification. If the notification has expired, open the Steam overlay manually using the default key combination "Shift+Tab". You should see an open chat window with the invite. If you do not see this invite, or you have accidentally canceled it, ask your friend to send you a new one.
Click "Join Game".
Do not press the Esc key to close the Steam window, instead close it by clicking in the middle up closing tab; pressing Esc would send you back to Terraria's main menu.
Select a character to play as, or create a new one.
You may be prompted to enter a password. If you do not know the password, ask your friend for it to continue.
It will then join you onto your friends world at the default spawn point, giving the status message “[Player] has joined.”


== Notes ==
You are allowed to set up an invite only server or a friend only server, and can disable the ability of those joined to be able to allow anyone else to join (disabling friends of friends joining / disabling friends sending invites to others).
These methods will not allow you to set up a dedicated or LAN server but rather use Steam's servers to broadcast your world. If you want to create a dedicated server see Guide:Setting up a Terraria server.
Steam Multiplayer for Terraria was introduced in 1.3.0.1, and will not work for older versions.

title: Life Fruit
content:
The Life Fruit is a Hardmode plant and permanent booster item that grows on Jungle grass in any area within the Underground layer or below, and only after any mechanical boss has been defeated. Life Fruit grow 25% faster on average in Expert Mode.
When used, a Life Fruit permanently increases the player's health capacity by 5 and restores the player's health by 5, turning one unit in the player's health bar golden. Life Fruit can only be used once a player has reached the 400 health cap from consuming Life Crystals. A total of 20 Life Fruit is required to reach the maximum 500 health capacity. Once this is reached, the player's health cannot be increased beyond 500, with the exception of the Lifeforce buff.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Used by tools ==
Life Fruits can be used by the Rubblemaker to turn back into their placed states:


== Notes ==

Life Fruit can spawn on any block of Jungle grass (including player-placed ones) below the Surface; the spawning tile does not have to be in an Underground Jungle biome, nor does it have to be off-screen. However, they will never spawn within a 122×122 (102×102) tile area (centered on the Life Fruit) of each other, i.e. they will be spaced 60 (50) tiles apart at maximum concentration.
Like other plants, Life Fruit can be harvested with any weapon or tool; a pickaxe is not required, and any attack can uproot them. They will also be uprooted if the Jungle grass beneath them is replaced.
Since they are classified as plants, Life Fruit are also affected by the Guide to Environmental Preservation and its upgrade, the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence.
Life Fruit are highlighted by the Spelunker buff or Spelunker Glowsticks by a yellow glimmer, like ores and treasures.
Life Fruit has the highest Metal Detector value. This can make searching for ores or other valuables more difficult once full health has been reached as any errant Life Fruit will be prioritized over everything else in the area.
On the minimap, Life Fruit are 2×2 squares and are a slightly lighter color of green than the rest of the foliage around it. When hovered over, they are labeled as "Life Fruit".


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The first Life Fruit obtained should ideally be turned into an Aegis Fruit, as 4 defense provides a greater survivability boost than 5 max health, or into a Kinship Peach as both Trusty Cattiva and Trusty Foxparks are extremely powerful.
A Lifeforce Potion can be used to temporarily increase health capacity beyond 500, to a maximum of 600.
In order to obtain maximum health, 20 Life Fruit are required. After the player reaches it, the excess Life Fruits may be used to brew Jungle Juice.
Farms can be made by making long platforms of Jungle grass underground. Jungle grass spreads with Jungle Grass Seeds.
Life Fruit can replace all forms of wild Jungle plants that grow on Jungle grass, including Jungle Spores and the common 3-block-wide bushes, so clearing plants to encourage growth is not required. The same is true of Jungle vines and thorns. However, Life Fruit do not replace Bee Hives, so placing a row of platforms beneath each row of Jungle grass may be worthwhile to prevent them from appearing.
Life Fruit can grow in front of background walls.
Fairies can often lead the player to Life Fruit.
If the player has explored a large area of the Underground Jungle before defeating a mechanical boss, they can use the Metal Detector in conjunction with the map to find Life Fruit very effectively.
Between defeating the first and the third mechanical boss, a quick and easy way to find Life Fruit is to use the Clentaminator with Dark Blue Solution specifically, as this will break the Life Fruit and leave them on the ground, illuminated by the glowing mushroom grass for the player to see. After the player is done gathering, the biome may be easily switched back to the jungle via Green Solution. However, this method becomes much more dangerous after Plantera's Bulbs begin to spawn, because the conversion will break them and summon Plantera.


== Trivia ==
The small golden heart on the Life Fruit represents the golden heart obtained when the fruit is consumed.
This item's name might be a reference to the Epic of Gilgamesh and the fruit of life Gilgamesh finds at the bottom of the sea.

title: Eye Bone
content:
The Eye Bone is a pet-summoning item that spawns Chester, a mobile Piggy Bank, to follow the player. Chester, being a pet, is essentially an upgrade to the Money Trough as it follows the player and does not require repeated summons. The Eye Bone has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.


== Tips ==
Using a Void Bag with Chester will result in the player possessing three inventories simultaneously instead of the usual one.
The Eye Bone and the Money Trough are both portable versions of the Piggy Bank, but the Eye Bone is arguably better because it can be placed in the pet slot to conserve inventory space.
Unlike the Money Trough, Chester is permanently out and follows the player, allowing for quick and easy item and coin transfer by simply using the "Quick Stack to Nearby Chests" inventory function.
Chester can cause problems for  Console players, however. It is typically close enough that the ⚷ Open / Activate button defaults to opening it; and with default controller layouts, this button is also the Grapple button. Chester can thus interfere with Console players' hooks.


== Trivia ==
Chester and Cenaxe are the only pets in the game with a practical function other than lighting.
The Eye Bone's tooltip is a reference to Wendy's examination quote for the Eye Bone in Don't Starve.
Chester's buff tooltip is a reference to Wilson's examination quote for Chester in Don't Starve.
Chester resembles The Luggage from the comic fantasy novel series Discworld.
The sound of Chester opening and closing is very similar to the sound made when the player's inventory is opened () and closed ().


== See also ==
Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester
Eye Bone at the Don't Starve Wiki
Chester at the Don't Starve Wiki

title: Legacy:Guide:Beating the Tutorial
content:
This guide is a guide which walks the player through “beating” the Tutorial.


== Getting Started ==
Once you've followed the initial directions to complete the start of the Tutorial, the real fun begins. Gather some decent weapons and Armor so you are prepared for whatever it is that you come across while exploring, building, or even just crafting.


== The Crimson or Corruption Boss Preparation ==
When you start to explore, you will find either The Crimson or The Corruption in your world. These biomes have big Chasms to avoid and enemies to fight.
Don't fight anything in the crimson or corruption yet, but destroy the grass to get either crimson seeds or corrupt seeds so you can safely farm Vile Mushrooms (in the Corruption) or Vicious Mushrooms (in the Crimson).
After you have at least 20 Vile Powder or Vicious Powder, the easy part is done. After you have finished this step, go back to the crimson/corruption and kill as many enemies as you can.
You will get Vertebrae from the Crimson or Rotten Chunks in the Corruption.
After you have completed the first two steps, you should go mining in order to get better Armor (such as Iron armor).
Once the Corruption or Crimson has spread sufficiently, the farming can begin. Kill as many Eaters of Souls or Crimera as possible in order to get Rotten Chunks or Vertebrae, and farm Vile Mushrooms or Vicious Mushrooms and craft them into Vile Powder or Vicious Powder. Keep farming until you have 15 Rotten Chunks/Vertebrae and 30 Vile/Vicious Powder. Once you have the required materials, make your way back to an Altar. When you get there, craft Worm Food or Bloody Spine.
Now you should be able to fight the Eater of Worlds or the Brain of Cthulhu.


== The Eater of Worlds or The Brain of Cthulhu ==
This next step involves defeating the Eater of Worlds for the corruption or the Brain of Cthulhu for the crimson.
These two bosses will help you get better armor, such as Demonite armor or Crimtane armor.
First, however, you must be prepared:

Craft a Light's Bane and a Campfire. The Campfire will heal you, and the Light's Bane will be your weapon.
If you made your Corruption or Crimson farm away from the spawn area, make an arena and be prepared with decent armor.
Once you have defeated the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu, you will have collected plenty of Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples, which can be used to craft Shadow armor or Crimson armor.
It is recommended to keep farming the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu in order to obtain the Nightmare Pickaxe or the Deathbringer Pickaxe so you can mine better ores for better armor.


== The Dungeon ==
This step is completely optional, but highly recommended. The true dungeon is located on the far right of the world, beyond the island. In order to enter The Dungeon, Skeletron must be defeated. By this point, you should have Shadow armor or Crimson armor. If you don't, you may want at least Gold or Silver armor. Proper armor should make the Skeletron fight far easier. For strategies, see the Skeletron Guide.
Now The Dungeon is unlocked! Besides the occasional Cursed Skull, the Dungeon should be relatively easy with your current gear. Try to destroy any Water Candles you see, as they increase the spawn rate of enemies in the area. Open all chests you come across, specifically looking for helpful key items:

Cobalt Shield
Shadow Key


== The Wall of Flesh ==
Now to face the final threat: the Wall of Flesh, the only thing keeping you from Hardmode! With your newly acquired Nightmare Pickaxe, you should be able to mine through Obsidian, which means you can make a hellevator to get to the underground. Be prepared for a long fall; you may die from fall damage, so it's a good idea to have either a Lucky Horseshoe or many blocks to build a staircase. It's also a good idea to store your items in a Piggy Bank or Safe (you'll need the Merchant to move in to buy these).
At this point, you'll need to farm Voodoo Demons in order to get the Guide Voodoo Doll. Once you get one, save it, because you'll need to throw the Doll into the lava to summon the Wall of Flesh. Take caution in killing Voodoo Demons, because if the Guide Voodoo Doll drops into lava, the Wall of Flesh may be summoned before you are fully prepared for the fight.


== If You Made it ==
Kudos to you, you managed to get the world into Hardmode! Your first goal: Destroy your world's Demon/Crimson Altar. Doing this will spawn one of two different ores:

Cobalt Ore
Palladium Ore
Once you have full palladium or cobalt gear, you can either skip to and fight Ocram now if you can do enough damage to defeat him before the night ends, or gather more gear.


== Twins ==

This is the real tricky part. It's almost impossible to make any ‘fast' progress now, but there is a way. You'll need to keep killing the Wall of Flesh until you obtain a Laser Rifle. Once you've got that, you'll need to stock up on Mana Potions, which can now be bought from the Merchant.
Your next goal will be to fight The Twins. They are an easy source of Hallowed Bars, and their Souls of Sight will allow you to get by without Cobalt, Palladium, Mythril, Orchalcum, Adamantite, or Titanium. The biggest concern for this battle is defeating both of them within the end of the night, so they don't run away. A Cursed Flames spell tome or Clockwork Assault Rifle can also help immensely in the battle.
Once you've got the Hallowed Bars, there's not much you can do now. You could place them or sell them, but you can't craft them because there's no Hardmode Anvil. You could try glitching the one Demon Altar to break it twice, or maybe find a second one (also via a World Generation glitch). If you do happen to get the second Hardmode Ore, make sure to search around the world and mine them asap, because they'll allow you to make Hallowed weapons.


== The Age of Chlorophyte ==
All people should follow the next step. Of course, that is if you were very, very lucky and got adamantite into your world.
If you managed to get Adamantite, your first goal will be to craft an Adamantite Forge. That will allow you to craft Chlorophyte weapons and armor. You'll need to first create an artificial Jungle and craft a Drax, however.

For melee players, Turtle armor or Chlorophyte armor with the Chlorophyte Mask is recommended. The Chlorophyte Claymore and Chlorophyte Partisan are both good melee weapons.
For rangers, Chlorophyte armor with the Chlorophyte Helmet is recommended (Note that, due to Plantera not being defeated yet, Shroomite armor is impossible to get). The Chlorophyte Shotbow and Chlorophyte Arrows are a good combo for ranged weapons.
For mages, Chlorophyte armor with the Chlorophyte Headgear is recommended. Again, note that Spectre armor is currently inaccessible to the player because Plantera has not yet been defeated.
Once you're all geared up, proceed to the next step.


== Side Quest: Plantera ==
This is a completely optional side-quest. If you only have Hallowed armor, you'll need an arena. Even if you have Chlorophyte armor, an arena is still recommended. If needed, you can create an artificial Jungle within the spawn area (for invincibility) for an easy battle. Plantera can drop:

the Flower Pow, a flail weapon. Good for melee fighters.
the Venus Magnum or Grenade Launcher and Rockets. Good for rangers.
the Leaf Blower, Wasp Gun, or Nettle Burst. All of these are good for mages.
the Pygmy Staff. Good for summoners. It will also cause the Witch Doctor to sell more items if the player has it in their inventory.
The Axe. This is the best Hamaxe in the game.


== Ocram ==
Now for Ocram. With your new gear and spawn area invincibility, the only remaining problem is dealing damage. The Venus Magnum (if you farmed Plantera) or Megashark (from farming in the ocean) can deal massive amounts of damage, especially if you use Chlorophyte Bullets.


== Endgame ==
Once you've farmed Ocram enough, you should be able to craft Dragon armor, Titan armor, and/or Spectral armor, the endgame armors of a glitched Tutorial. After this, you can take a few screenshots and show off to your friends, but it's highly recommended that you start a real world. It's much easier than beating the Tutorial. And... this was all pointless because you cannot save your tutorial world.

title: Bewitching Table
content:
The Bewitching Table is a furniture item found naturally placed in the Dungeon and can be obtained by fishing in the Dungeon. In Hardmode, it is also sold by the Witch Doctor for 10 Gold if the Wizard is present. It emits light when placed. It fulfills a house's table requirement.
Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Bewitching Table grants the Bewitched buff, which increases the player's minion slots by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
Unlike equipment buff items, the Bewitching Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 3×3 tiles being available.


== Crafting ==


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Notes ==
The Bewitching Table can be activated limitlessly with no cooldown period. It is never consumed, and all players may use it to give themselves the buff.
It can be placed on flat-surface furniture.
The Bewitching Table does not have an effect on sentry capacity. The latter can be increased by the War Table.
The Bewitching Table is sometimes obtainable from the Dungeon pre-Skeletron in Drunk worlds.


== Trivia ==
The staff on the buff icon could be a Raven Staff due to the apparent feather-like purple spikes on the top, however the shape of the shaft much more closely resembles the Slime Staff sprite with what appears to be purple slime dripping off of it. Due to the fact that the buff was added after both the Raven and Slime Staves (1.3.0.1 vs. 1.2.1 and 1.2) it is likely that the icon is supposed to depict an amalgamation of multiple summon weapons and was purposely meant to be left ambiguous.


== History ==

Now available as a drop when fishing in the Dungeon.
Now has Shimmer transmutation loop with Alchemy Table and Alchemy Flask.
Item and placed sprites updated.

title: Lilith's Necklace
content:
Lilith's Necklace is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Wolf. Some vanity items are visible when transformed, but certain accessories cannot be used, such as wings. The player can still swing weapons, drink potions, and use items as normal, with unique visual animations for each action. The player's hurt sound is also replaced with a wolf's bark. Lilith's Necklace has a 1/30 (3.33%) / 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Wolves.
Newly created Journey Mode characters named Wolfpet or Wolf Pet (case-insensitive) will have Lilith's Necklace equipped in the mount slot.


== Notes ==
Although the Wolf cannot use most movement accessories, such as wings, boots, or the Flying Carpet, the Wolf can use any accessories that grant extra jumps. Items that grant increased acceleration, like the Magiluminescence, also increase the deceleration speed while using this mount.
The Wolf has a running speed of 48 mph, with a short acceleration time. This mount is also smaller than some land mounts, only requiring 3-tile tall gaps, compared to the Unicorn Mount's 5-tile tall requirement.
After transforming into the Wolf, using a whip shifts the attack range slightly. This is because the whip swings from the Wolf's head position rather than the player's original hand position after transformation, shifting the whip's attack range outward slightly.
It reduces fall damage by 90%.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
Lilith's Necklace refers to the name of Redigit and Cenx's daughter, Lilith. The item was added because Lilith was "obsessed with wolves".


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Fixed Fishing Rod lines not being offset correctly when using Lilith's Necklace.

Use sound updated.
The required names for Journey Mode characters are no longer case-sensitive.
Desktop 1.4.4.1: Reduced max speed (10 to 9.5), acceleration (0.25 to 0.18), and jump speed (10.01 to 9.01).

title: Desert
content:
The Desert is a biome which consists predominantly of Sand Blocks and cacti. Every world contains a main Desert area (which houses the Underground Desert biome beneath it) and, possibly, additional small Desert patches called Dunes (which only contain layers of Sand Blocks on the surface and do not have underground parts). Pyramids and small pools of water can rarely appear in Dunes. Objects in the Desert appear slightly hazy due to heat distortion, and  water has a unique turquoise color. A Desert can also be generated with an Oasis mini-biome, featuring Palm trees and a large pool of water in the center.
An area is considered a Desert biome if there are at least 1500 Sand Blocks, Hardened Sand Blocks or Sandstone Blocks, causing the water and background to change. Cacti and Desert enemies can spawn on even a single block of sand, however. Deserts are overridden by most other biomes, including the Ocean. Rain will occur in Deserts just as in any other surface biome. A Sandstorm may occur when wind speed is over 30 mph, which causes special enemies to spawn and pushes the player in the direction of the wind.
The Desert can be infected by the Corruption, the Crimson, or The Hallow. Corruption/Crimson Deserts may already spawn upon world creation. The enemies from the main biome (the evil biome or the Hallow) can spawn in an infected Desert alongside the normal Desert enemies (except for Mummies and Sand Sharks, which have special biome-specific variants), and the music from the main biome is played. The sand in an infected Desert is replaced by Ebonsand, Crimsand, or Pearlsand Blocks, respectively. Although their color will change, cacti still drop Cactus when cut, and Waterleaf are also able to grow in a Hallowed Desert.


== Contents ==


== Entrances to the Underground Desert ==
There is a 1/2 (50%) chance that the main Desert will generate with one of four types of structures that lead towards the Underground Desert. These are called chambers, pit, anthill, and larva hole.

The chambers consist of a zigzagging downward tunnel with one or two small rooms connected to the corners.
Pits are large funnels generated at the center of the Desert.
Anthills are upward cones with narrow downward holes in the center. 2–3 anthills will generate across the surface of the main Desert.
Larva holes are downward funnels with narrow holes in the center. 2–3 larva holes will generate across the surface of the main Desert.

		
		


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
In Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds, a Pyramid is always generated at the center of the main Desert, replacing the original entrance to the Underground Desert.


== Tips ==
The main Desert/Underground Desert pair will be on the same side as the Jungle/Underground Jungle, and opposite to the Snow biome and the Dungeon.


== Trivia ==
The Desert is the least popular biome for housing (discounting invalid housing biomes like the Corruption and the Crimson). A total of five NPCs either hate or dislike living in it, more than any other biome.
The Desert and the Glowing Mushroom biome are the only surface biomes without a biome-exclusive boss.
According to the Bestiary entry for the Sand Shark, a saltwater river ran through the Desert in ancient times.


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===

title: Living Mahogany Tree
content:
Living Mahogany Trees are large tree-shaped structures generated at world creation in the Underground Jungle. The trunk of a Living Mahogany Tree is hollow, and (unlike Living Trees) always contains an Ivy Chest at its base. Interestingly, the inside of it uses safe Living Wood Walls which can be collected.


== Loot ==
Each Ivy Chest will always contain one primary item, and can potentially contain multiple secondary items, or none at all. Besides one of the items listed here, they will also contain common items depending on the height they were found: Underground or Caverns.


== Notes ==
Living Mahogany Trees can spawn in all parts of the Cavern layer instead of only Underground Jungle in Drunk worlds.
When mined (with a Pickaxe or Drill), the blocks drop Rich Mahogany, while Mahogany Leaf Blocks are destroyed without dropping items.
A Living Mahogany Tree may spawn over a Jungle Temple, replacing some Lihzahrd Bricks with Living Mahogany, allowing early access in some cases.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.1: Fixed Living Mahogany trees not considering Jungle Grass as Jungle when generating, significantly limiting their numbers.
