title: Wisp in a Bottle
content:
The Wisp in a Bottle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a light-providing Wisp that follows the player around. While active, it is similar to the Flickerwick. The Wisp emits cyan light and is brighter and keeps better pace with the player than other light pets, except the Suspicious Looking Tentacle and Jewel of Light(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) which have the same light radius. It moves in accordance with the direction keys the player is pressing, although it is oriented above the player's head by default. The Wisp's movement range appears to be about 7 tiles to the left, right, and below the player's hitbox and 7 tiles above the Wisp's normal starting position. The Wisp in a Bottle has a 1/400 (0.25%) / 799/160,000 (0.4994%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones.


== Notes ==
The Wisp will often remain deep within the blocks ahead, causing the immediate area around your character to remain dark. To negate this effect, stand still and the Wisp should return.
Jumping will not direct the Wisp upward, and falling will not direct it downward. Instead, the up or down buttons must be used, respectively.
When the player is far ahead, the Wisp will spin to catch up to the player, giving off less light.
The Wisp moves at 26 mph when not spinning, and 61 mph when spinning. The latter is equal to the Unicorn Mount's top speed.
If the player's speed exceeds 61 mph, the wisp will teleport to the player when too far away.
On the  Console version and  Mobile version, the Wisp is controlled with the right joystick and left joystick, respectively.
Dye applied to the Wisp does not change the amount or color of light emitted, even if the Wisp is made invisible.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Grappling a block will allow the player to freely direct the Wisp.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Applying Twilight Dye, Living Ocean Dye or Living Flame Dye seemingly turns the Wisp completely invisible while still providing light, should players wish for such a thing for cosmetic reasons or when fighting Dungeon Spirits. Some other dyes can achieve this effect as well, such as Shadow Dye, Grim Dye, and Reflective Metal Dye, although to a lesser degree.
When directing the Wisp into a Cloud Block, it will glow significantly brighter, unlike most light sources.


== Trivia ==
The Wisp appears to be a flaming skull.
Wisp refers to Will-o'-the-wisps, mythological ghost lights reported to lead travelers to their death in swamps.

title: Ironskin Potion
content:
The Ironskin Potion is a buff potion that grants the Ironskin buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's defense by 8, thus reducing damage by 4 / 6 / 8. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Ironskin Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Tips ==
The Ironskin Potion is more effective than the Endurance Potion against attacks that deal less than 40 / 60 / 80 damage; however, it is most effective to use both at the same time.
The Ironskin Potion is a very useful asset during the game as it requires very cheap and easily farmable items, making it easy to craft a large number of them.


== Trivia ==
Although it can be made with Lead Ore, it still has Iron in the name.
Lead in real life is generally toxic when inhaled or orally ingested.

title: Legacy:Guide:The Destroyer strategies
content:
The Destroyer is one of the bosses unlocked when the game enters Hardmode. It is extremely strong, dealing very high damage to the player even when the player has very high-tier armor. It is generally recommended as the first boss to fight following the Wall of Flesh.


== Terrain Preparation ==
The type of preparation you'll be making depends on your approach.  If you are using melee, The Destroyer is best fought on an arena consisting of tall walls with multiple layers of Wood Platforms. This will allow players to move around the arena freely, and to keep a good watch on where the boss is.  If you are using ranged, pick a wide, open, flat area, with plenty of clear space for flying and dodging. The Destroyer can clear a lot of vertical space. Like any other burrowing enemy, it can only control its movements in tiles/blocks. 
Another method of defeating The Destroyer utilizes a Nimbus Rod,  ropes, and Platforms. Build a platform up high enough so that the Destroyer can just barely reach the player, but not so high as to despawn the Destroyer when standing atop it, and make a rope up. Place Nimbus Clouds, and then use the mechanical worm. The clouds will damage the destroyer while you fight off the probes. You may need to replace the clouds mid-fight. If you wish to do additional damage fire down at him with a Poison Staff, preferably at an angle as to do damage to multiple segments per shot. 
It may be useful to summon and kill Eye of Cthulhu (he will die in a matter of seconds when engaged with hardmode weapons) before summoning the destroyer in order to spawn an extra one-use pool of Hearts. You can also choose to add a few Heart Statues wired to a Timer to supply you with some additional health. Another great help is building a few small pools of Honey and building Campfires and Heart Lanterns around the arena. Last of all you can move the Nurse in a nearby house (not too close!) or your spawn point, as the destroyer will never despawn if you use your Magic Mirror allowing you to momentarily escape the fight to heal.
A tricky alternative way of building an arena is by creating a small box, wire up a few Heart Statues around it and some honey inside it. Combine this with high defense, a Cross Necklace and a Charm of Myths. The Destroyer himself will only deal relatively low damage, less than your healing potential, making the fight very easy. Another way is to build a horizontal platform very high in the sky (200 to 300 blocks), with 1 block replaced by a Wood Platform. The Destroyer will be unable to reach you, allowing you to easily kill him with ranged weapons. Although those two ways may make the fight a lot easier, they might also make the fight somewhat boring.


== Gearing Up ==


=== Armor ===
This boss is actually quite easy, in spite of the massive amount of health it has. The minimum for armor would be a full set of Molten Armor. At this point you should have a full set. If you don't, Obsidian Skin Potions can be used to mine loads of Hellstone. But always remember that it's always good to fight bosses [The Destroyer,etc.] with friends/other players. Titanium armor is also incredibly effective against the destroyer, because of the invincibility after hitting an enemy. However, the player will need to take a lot more time gathering resources to make a full set of titanium armor. A last great option is Orichalcum armor, because of its set bonus. Flower petals frequently multi-hit The Destroyer upon flying across the screen, and can sometimes (if angled correctly) hit most of its segments length wise.


=== Weapons ===
Different weapons can have different usefulness against this boss. However due to his high health and multiple segments piercing weapons are recommended. Aside from choosing the right weapon it may be worth your time to earn some money and get a good modifier for your weapon as well.


==== Melee ====
The Destroyer is the easiest of the 3 mechanical bosses for a melee character, considering his movement in the air is limited.

The weakest form of the destroyer is when he attacks vertically, if he does so, it is best to use an effective sword and swing at it multiple times. This takes out a lot of its health and if he keeps attacking you vertically, it will take a short amount of time to defeat it.
Right from the start, Night's Edge can be very useful, seeing that if you spent enough time farming the materials, (which you should have done by now) the damage count, with the right Modifiers can make the boss fight last about 2 and a half minutes.
If just coming out into Hardmode, after you have already defeated a Hardmode boss, Gungnir is very effective.
The Dao of Pow can do significant damage across multiple body parts.
An Ice would also be able to deal significant damage, while allowing you to maintain some distance from The Destroyer.
A large sword would be reasonably effective, or used as a backup for defeating the Probes. Good choices include; Phasesaber, Titanium Sword, Cutlass and if you have already defeated a Hardmode boss, Excalibur.
If you are a hardmode starter, consider using a Mythril Halberd or if possible, an Adamantite Glaive with a godly reforge.
After defeating another Mechanical Boss, the Mushroom Spear sold from the Truffle NPC will obliterate him.


==== Magic ====
For magic users, the destroyer can be defeated with ease depending on the weapons used.  

Various other piercing magic weapons could obliterate this boss in no time. Most notably the Rainbow Gun, the Poison Staff, or the Golden Shower, due to their piercing ability, though of those options, only the Golden Shower is obtainable before The Destroyer has been defeated. However if you are unable to obtain any of those you can settle for a Frost Staff or a godly Magic Dagger as well.
If you were using a Skybridge made with platforms as an arena, using the Nimbus Rod will enable you to eliminate The Destroyer very quickly, just place the clouds over the platforms near you. when he passes by, he'll receive ridiculously high damages in just one leap. However, note that the platforms must be at least 200-300 blocks high.
If you happen to obtain a Queen Spider Staff, this would be a major advantage, being able to summon the Queen Spider once and then switching to another weapon, while the Queen Spider supports you with additional damage and the killing of Probes.


==== Ranged ====
As with most bosses, ranged weapons would be easier to use than melee weapons. And even while this is one of the easier bosses for melee, a ranged weapon with enough piercing can simply hit so many parts at once that it outdamages melee weapons by a great amount.

The Daedalus Stormbow coupled with holy arrows obliterate The Destroyer in a matter of seconds, and is obtainable right after defeating the wall of flesh.
An Adamantite Repeater or Titanium Repeater, combined with Jester's/Holy Arrows or Unholy/Hellfire Arrows would deal quite reasonable damage. Any of these arrows would be good choices, and if Jester's arrows are too difficult to obtain, Unholy arrows do very well in this fight and are the easiest of these arrows to procure.
Uzi will work.  Combined with Meteor Shot or Crystal Bullets this can do nicely.
If you already defeated one of the other mechanical bosses you may consider using a Flamethrower or Magical Harp, the latter of which is the perfect weapon against the destroyer, due to its infinite piercing ability and lingering projectiles.
Another interesting weapon is the Cannon, which should be placed instead. It can deal high damage and pierce through multiple parts, giving great damage potential, however, it may be hard to get in a good shot, aside from aiming up and simply waiting for The Destroyer to charge through you.
The Gatligator with Exploding Bullets is fairly good against the destroyer, as the large amount of segments is very easy to hit even with the Gatligator's inaccuracy and the Exploding Bullets can cause splash damage possibly hitting multiple segments.
A good ammo against all the bosses especially the destroyer is Exploding Bullets (though Crystal Bullets also perform admirably), as they will deal damage from the bullet and the explosion so they deal double. also sometimes you will hit on the connection of two segments and deal triple damage due to the explosion hitting both segments. this combined with the Clockwork Assault Rifle can deal a good amount of damage.
Another method is to use a Star Cannon with at least the deadly modifier and begin shooting the destroyer. It's going to most likely kill it due to the star cannon's high damage and piercing ability.


=== Accessories ===
There are many great accessories available at this point. Especially (Frozen/Leaf) Wings would be of great help, as well as Lightning Boots. Harpy Wings are also a good choice. Those two accessories would allow you to move almost freely through the air and on the ground, making it a lot easier to evade The Destroyer and his lasers. A must have for melee users, as well as being useful for ranged users, would be the Obsidian Shield, preventing you from being knocked around by the lasers, both from The Destroyer and the Probes. The Mana Flower is less useful during this fight, as the Probes you kill will almost always supply you with enough mana and drinking a mana potion once during the fight isn't a great deal either. Even though this boss is immune to all debuffs, the probes that it releases are not, so items like the Magma Stone or other items that inflict debuffs are useful.
For the remaining accessories the Cross Necklace (or Star Veil) are extremely useful due to their ability to lengthen the time delay until you take more damage. The Charm of Myths will also help you survive longer because of its regeneration and potion sickness decreasing effect. If you rather go for more damage an Emblem (or Mechanical Glove/Celestial Emblem for melee/magic users respectively) would supply you with additional damage. If you do go for a mechanical glove, using a Magma Stone (dropped from Hellbats) will help in dispatching probes, as well as making it useful thoughout Hardmode, as fire damage from all melee weapons and light from pickaxes and drills is a great asset.  As with all boss fights it is best to reforge your accessories with damage, critical strike chance or defense increasing modifiers.


=== Potions ===
As with all boss fights a good supply of Healing Potions or even Greater Healing Potions would help you survive longer and a supply of Mana Potions in case you are going to use magic weapons.
One of the most useful potions would be the Ironskin Potion, helping you survive longer. Regeneration Potions also help for this.
A Bowl of Soup, Pumpkin Pie or Cooked Marshmallow can never hurt and are quite easy to make.
A Hunter Potion could be useful, so you can see where The Destroyer is going to surface and a Swiftness Potion to evade him.
In case you are going to use a repeater the Archery Potion is a must have and since they last four minutes you should make 2-3 of them.
If you prefer magic weapons instead a Magic Power Potion, Mana Regeneration Potion should be used instead. Also the buff from the Crystal Ball would give you some advantage.
If you are going to use melee the Thorns Potion could come in handy, but avoid using flasks, because The Destroyer is immune to all debuffs.
Shine Potions and Night Owl Potions are helpful, but not really essential. They just make sighting other mobs and the terrain easier.
Featherfall Potions and Gravitation Potions are also useful if you want more control while in the air or have limited access to the flight accessories.


== The Fight ==
The Destroyer is almost exactly the same as the fight with the Eater of Worlds, in that it digs around and launches up at you every chance it gets. Just sidestep the body and keep wailing away at it. Occasionally it will launch a few volleys of Death Lasers at everyone fighting him. These hit for about 15-20's on players with 40-50 defense. The Destroyer also spawns Probes throughout the fight. It spawns them very often at first, and then the spawn rate slows down a good bit as you kill them off. Probes drop a 20HP Heart when killed at a 33% drop rate, so for the most part health isn't too much of an issue with this fight.
The Probes are both a blessing and a curse. A curse as they get in your way and can attack you for decent damage with their lasers (a bit more if you collide with them). They are a blessing in disguise, however, as they can be a source of health by killing them when you have less than full health: They can drop Hearts for later healing. Careful management of Health Potion usage and Heart collecting will keep you nice and stocked on health. Just drop to the ground when it's relatively clear and gather some. The Hunter Potion will let you see The Destroyer in the ground, so you'll know if you have to evade instead or can keep going for the hearts.
If you're fighting on a wide, flat plain, it might pay to occasionally just run across it until The Destroyer appears. Doing so might cause it to spread a large portion of its body along the ground, making it an easy target from above. If you have the horizontal space (and speed), make use of it by flying a decent distance back and forth instead of only staying in a particular (horizontal) area to help spread its body out. The more of the body you can keep exposed (and accessible to attacks), the more opportunities you have to deal damage.
On the other hand, if you want to hit the ground (say, to gather Hearts), you can fly straight up and hover a while until The Destroyer jumps straight up at you. You can then drop to the ground quick to gather what you need/want while the The Destroyer recovers from its attack attempt. It takes a while for it to loop back around from a high jump. Remember, outside of solid blocks/tiles, burrowing enemies have little control of their movement. This gives you the time to take a breather or collect some pick-ups on the ground.
Like most other bosses, if everyone is killed The Destroyer leaves. The Destroyer will also leave if you cannot kill it before sunrise.  After a few minutes of bashing away at its health, the machine will ball. Loot from the Destroyer will be dropped from the segment nearest to a player.
For people new to hardmode, and fighting him for the first time, it is important to realize that the probes spawn as you do damage to the Destroyer. So while it may seem like a good idea to front-load a large amount of damage (a Nimbus Rod over the spot where he first spawns, for example), you will probably find yourself overwhelmed by the sheer amount of probes spawning at once. Find a balance between damaging the boss and dealing with the probes to survive the fight.

title: Legacy:Guide:Crafting 101
content:
Crafting is the act of combining one or more materials into a different item, usually at a specific crafting station. The crafting system is deeply interwoven with game progression, with many "key" materials and crafting stations dropped by various bosses, or otherwise available only after a given boss has been defeated.


== Crafting Basics ==
The crafting aspect is slightly different across different versions of Terraria. To access the crafting menu, press the Inventory key while in-game. This will bring up the heads-up display, showing your inventory, equipment slots, and other options. The crafting menu is located in the bottom left of your screen, as indicated in the image below. On  Old-gen console, press  () /  () /  (). From there, switch tabs to access the crafting interface. On 3DS, tap the inventory icon on the touch screen, or press the ZL Button on a New 3DS. From there, tap the crafting icon, then navigate to the desired page with .

		
		
		


== Crafting Stations ==

Many recipes require that you have a crafting station to craft them. The first crafting station available is the Work Bench, which can be crafted without any crafting station. To use a crafting station, it must be placed in the world, and you must be standing close enough to it (see image). Items you can craft using the station will then be added to the list of items you can currently craft. It is possible to stand near many crafting stations simultaneously to craft items using any of these stations. Additionally, some items, such as the Waterfall Block requires that you stand next to multiple different crafting stations to be able to craft them.


== Multi-Crafting Areas ==

		
		
		


== Notes ==
To make a fully complete crafting area, you would need to include either a Demon or Crimson Altar. Unfortunately, those are immobile! If you don't want to locate your crafting area near an altar, you can instead provide a way to get to an altar quickly -- teleporters are good for this. Don't forget the minor stations such as lava and honey blocks (a sink can substitute for water), and a Campfire (for a Marshmallow on a Stick).
On the Nintendo 3DS version:
The player is required to be on the same level as crafting stations to use them, and cannot craft using items from a chest (they must be in the player's inventory).
One can scroll through all recipes previously discovered, no matter if the materials are available or not. This can help the player, however, they will have to scroll for a while late-game.
When crafting, items cannot receive modifiers. Only by using the Goblin Tinkerer may one receive modifiers on crafted items.
On the  Mobile version before 1.3, the Guide was unhelpful with crafting, and could only give you tips (there was no “crafting” button).

title: Guide:Plantera strategies
content:
Plantera is a boss that can be spawned after defeating all three mechanical bosses.


== Spawn condition ==
Plantera can only be spawned by breaking a Plantera's Bulb, by a pickaxe, drill, or various other means.
She must then be killed within the Underground Jungle, otherwise she will become enraged.


== The fight ==
Plantera will attempt to overlap her main bulb with the player's position, resulting in a linear kiting fight. She moves slowly compared to a player with speed-boosting equipment. In a large enough arena, distance can be maintained by constant movement. If the arena is too large, its center may not register as Underground Jungle. This can be avoided by making the arena long and narrow or by widening a natural jungle cave and allowing jungle grass to regrow. Notched edges increase jungle grass tiles on the perimeter, helping maintain biome recognition.
In her first stage, she spits seeds at the player, together with occasional thorny balls that are affected by gravity and do high damage. In Classic mode, her seeds cannot travel through blocks.
The second stage begins at 50% health. The pink petals fall off, revealing a green maw, and Plantera’s speed and damage increases and she spawns tentacles surrounding her body. In Classic mode, these tentacles do not respawn once killed. She also releases spores that can travel through blocks, but which can be destroyed by a single hit.
Plantera enrages if the player leaves the Underground Jungle, gaining defense, attacking more often, and dealing high contact and ranged damage. Surface arenas are generally ineffective. 


=== Expert Mode/Master Mode ===
In these modes, Plantera's seed attacks can travel through blocks, and her tentacles can regrow. In addition, her hooks spawn their own tentacles. This makes dodging the hooks important, either through removing blocks and walls from the arena or by moving down a long tunnel.


=== Attack types ===


== General strategies ==


=== General tips ===


=== Terrain preparation ===
The actual shape of your arena depends on how you want to fight:

Players can widen natural caves in Underground Jungle with Bombs or Dynamite and place platforms for dodging.
More aggressive players may prefer a compact space near the bulb (mainly for the Face Tanking strat)
Plantera's thorn balls do significant damage and are used frequently during her first phase, however, they can only bounce off solid surfaces. If you do not mind taking the extra time, consider digging a hole at least 2 times deeper than you would use for the fight and stick to the top half of your arena (that is, your actual arena has a large space beneath it for the spike balls to fall into and stay away from you). Filling the bottom with a liquid can further slow the balls. Without the added threat of Plantera's spike balls, she is much easier to defeat. 
Make sure the arena is not too big and empty, as taking out too many Mud blocks might turn the Underground Jungle into just regular caverns, enraging Plantera and making the fight much more difficult. Bring a hammer to remove the jungle walls so that in Plantera's second phase, the hooks can only grapple on to the blocks so she cannot reach you with her hooks, and thus you will not take damage from them.


=== Gearing up ===
It is recommended to increase your maximum life to 500 before trying to tackle Plantera and later challenges after her defeat. Life Fruits are very common if many days have passed after defeating one of the Mechanical bosses.


==== Armor ====
At minimum, players should use the Hallowed armor with the helmet that suits the player's class. It grants the Holy Protection buff, making it a great choice.
Chlorophyte armor is also a great choice for a more offensive build.
Turtle armor is a good choice since it provides the highest raw defense at this point in the game, but you will need to defeat enough Giant Tortoises to get three Turtle Shells.
Spider armor offers slightly higher damage bonuses than the respective Hallowed set for summoners.
Squire armor has the best defensive stats of any armor that boosts summon damage, but boosts sentry slots rather than minion slots, so it requires a somewhat different playstyle.
The best offensive set for melee users consists of the Chlorophyte Mask, Monk's Shirt, and Squire's Greaves.
Hallowed Mask and Turtle Scale Mail or Squire's Plating are more defensive options.
The best offensive set for ranged users consists of the Adamantite Mask, Huntress's Jerkin, and Mythril Greaves. if more defense is desired, Chlorophyte Greaves should be used.
The best offensive set for magic users consists of the Hallowed Headgear, Chlorophyte Plate Mail, and Apprentice's Trousers.
Squire's Great Helm and/or Spider Greaves can be substituted into any of the above hybrid sets for additional regeneration or minion-based offense, respectively.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users

The True Excalibur has a very large range and can handle all phases of the fight fairly well due to its piercing. The Chlorophyte Claymore is similar, with slightly less range but high DPS.
The Death Sickle is decent, being able to tear through Plantera and her tentacles.
The True Night's Edge has better potential DPS, but is inconsistent during Plantera's second phase due to its low piercing.
The Mushroom Spear is easy to obtain and deals high damage, but is somewhat risky to use. The Chlorophyte Partisan is a weaker alternative.
The Chlorophyte Saber has a rapid-damage attack with a hitbox that extends with melee speed bonuses, and it inflicts a heavy debuff, becoming incredibly powerful with the Catalyst Band.
With enough damage Modifiers, the Fetid Baghnakhs or the Drippler Crippler (with spamming the attack up) can defeat Plantera in less than half a minute if the player doesn't move. Using a Cross Necklace and enough health regeneration and defense, the player is capable of enduring Plantera's damage for the short duration of the fight. You can use a Flask of Ichor to decrease the boss' defense and a Charm of Myths and Restoration Potions for maximum healing. A Star Veil is also preferable to increase the player's damage output.
For Ranged users

The Chlorophyte Shotbow with Holy Arrows can be used to great effect.
The Megashark with Crystal Bullets is the best gun at this stage. It is even better if equipping a Chaos Cylinder to inflict Ichor debuff via Ichor Bullets.
The Flamethrower deals excellent damage and easily pierces Plantera's Tentacles in her second phase.
You can excavate a tall arena and use a Daedalus Stormbow paired with Chlorophyte Arrows.
The Super Star Shooter is a great weapon to use in her second phase, as the stars can pierce multiple targets.
The Pulse Bow, while rare, can be strong against Plantera, especially in an enclosed arena. It is best used with Ichor or Cursed Arrows.
For Magic users

The Venom Staff shoots multiple projectiles with piercing and Acid Venom. Can be really useful in the second phase to get rid of the tentacles.
The Orange Zapinator deals good damage to Plantera and can deal massive damage in a short time depending on the player's luck.
The Rainbow Rod is both homing and piercing and deals a good amount of damage.
The Cursed Flames deals great damage in the second phase if slowly descending in a vertical tunnel, as each fireball usually hits Plantera twice.
The Tome of Infinite Wisdom, Crystal Serpent and Sky Fracture are solid weapons against Plantera.
The Shadowflame Hex Doll and Magical Harp are very effective for the second phase, as they deal with the Tentacles while also damaging Plantera. The Magic Dagger can also be effective.
Support Weapons would be quite helpful against Plantera namely;
The Golden Shower every so often can prove to be very helpful as it inflicts the Ichor debuff, increasing your damage output even more.
And the Nimbus Rod is always useful (even for non-magic users). It can deal continuous damage which can greatly help the fight, especially in vertical arenas.
For Summoners

The Optic Staff and Blade Staff are the best options to summoners. The latter requires the use of whips for optimal damage.
The Optic Staff mixed in with 3 Spiders deals massive damage, especially in the first phase of the fight.
A Trusty Foxparks can be a great use of a single minion slot.
The Ruinous Staff works well with the Firecracker.
The Queen Spider Staff or Ballista Cane can prove to be incredibly powerful when used with a Tavernkeep's armor set.
The Durendal is typically the best whip at this stage, while Firecracker deals higher damage when paired with Spider Staff in the first phase.


==== Potions ====
Ironskin, Endurance, Regeneration, and Lifeforce Potions will help you survive much longer.
Anything that gives the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied, or Exquisitely Stuffed buff is welcomed help.
Wrath and Rage Potions give very welcomed damage upgrades.
Inferno Potions may be helpful for preventing spores from reaching you.
Ales and a Flask of Ichor are very effective for Melee users.
Likewise with Archery Potions, for Rangers who choose to use arrows.
Mana Regeneration Potion and Magic Power Potion are a must have for Magic users.
Summoning Potions are very useful for summoners, while a Flask of Ichor will help with whips too.


==== Accessories ====
Wings will allow you to dodge Plantera's attacks more effectively.
Alternatively, a mount can be used. A Chillet provides a dash with invincibility frames and boosts damage. The Gelatinous Pillion or The Black Spot can be used as a substitute.
Damage can be greatly boosted through combat accessories such as any Emblem or the Moon Stone.
The Fire Gauntlet should be used for melee to greatly increase damage and attack speed of swords.
This can be stacked with its predecessor, the Mechanical Glove for a further increase in place of an Avenger Emblem
The Magic Yoyo Bag will significantly increase a Yoyo's range and moderately increase its damage.
The Celestial Emblem is the best offensive accessory for mages, and should be used on every magic build.
The Pygmy Necklace is a great choice for summoners/hybrid, as it grants an additional minion slot.
The Old One's Army accessories are amazing for summoners, giving a solid damage boost and an additional sentry slot.
The Heavy Sling or its upgrades can be used to ensure a sentry remains within firing range.
Whipstacking users will want to use the Twilight Grasp and the Snake Band or its upgrades.
The Charm of Myths should be used for its reduction of the Potion Sickness debuff time from 60 to 45 seconds, and additional life regeneration.
Rangers may instead want to use the Catalyst Band to boost damaging debuffs.
The Frozen Turtle Shell reduces damage taken when losing too much health.
The Ankh Shield is very useful for preventing knockback in the second phase.
The Restoration Shield is a decent alternative, but lacks immunity to the Poisoned debuff.
The Cross Necklace or its upgrades can be used to extend the invulnerability period after being attacked. This can prove to be useful during the second phase due to the large amount of Biters.
In Expert Mode:
The utility of the Shield of Cthulhu's dash remains useful, however wings alone may be sufficent for Plantera.
The Worm Scarf will reduce the amount of damage taken. Although it becomes largely innefective in Master Mode due to plantera's high damage.
The Brain of Confusion can prevent the player from taking damage and increase their DPS for 4 seconds, making it an excellent accessory all around.


== Specific strategies ==


=== Teleportation trick ===
Make a long hallway, and place a Teleporter with a pressure plate on each end.
When she is climbing down toward you on one side, jump on the pressure plate used to activate the Teleporter. You will teleport to the other side, and Plantera will need to climb back at you.
Boomerang-type weapons can fly indefinitely when using a teleportation trick, though there are not many hardmode-effective boomerangs available.  Before the boomerang returns, the player can teleport to the other end of the hall, and the boomerang will change directions and pierce enemies along the way.
Note that if the hallway is too long, Plantera will despawn. This was observed in a hallway as small as 200 tiles. If you use the mobile version, you should make the hallway around 125-150 tiles long, as Plantera will despawn within a shorter range of the player.
This method is more difficult in Expert Mode, as her seeds can pass through blocks, all of her projectiles are now homing, and her 'mouths' spawn on her legs, closer to the player.


=== Face Tanking ===
Plantera can be trivially beaten with the Fetid Baghnakhs and the Star Veil/Cross Necklace (even with the melee speed nerf).  
For armor you will want either very high defense or use the Hallowed armor set bonus. For accessories you want to load up on melee speed (such as the Mechanical Glove) and damage reduction (Worm Scarf, Brain of Confusion) and put Warding reforges on all of the accessories. Don't forget to use potions listed above and the "arena" buffs.
The fight: use your hook to attach to a wall near the bulb. This prevents knockback and locks you in place. Break the bulb. Plantera will come right to you and sit on top of you. Hold down the attack key until she dies. That is it. This works even on Master mode.
A similar strat is to use the exact same set up with the Drippler Crippler and spamming the attack up.


=== Minecart tracks ===
Naturally-generated minecart tracks can be used against Plantera, as the varying height makes it easier to dodge the seeds in the first phase and the narrow hallways slows down Plantera in the second phase.
Plantera can then be dodged at the end of the rail by using a bumper and ramming through her, suffering minimal loss on health.
The pros being minimal terrain preparation, cons being depends on chance and rails may lead out of the jungle, resulting in an enraged Plantera.


=== Minecart loop ===
Plantera's method of movement can be exploited, by excavating a massive area of walls and blocks and constructing a minecart diamond loop with blocks in the center for Plantera to hook onto. Optionally, the blocks can include one-way hoiks to allow projectiles to pass through. Due to Plantera not having any other block to latch onto, it will get stuck in the center, while the minecart does all the movement to dodge most of the attacks.
The main con of this arena is how sensitive the spacing is: if a block is too close to the loop then Plantera can hook onto it and potentially move onto the track's path, and if there are not enough Jungle tiles nearby then the loop may no longer be inside a Jungle biome and Plantera will subsequently enrage.


=== Circle and run ===
Make an arena in the Underground Jungle about 2 screens wide and high with platforms, making sure to have the bottom row be platforms, letting the spiky balls she fires fall to the ground harmlessly. Nearby, place a Bed at one end of a long tunnel.
In Phase 1 of the fight, circle around Plantera using wings, firing at her with projectiles.
When Phase 2 begins, use a Magic Mirror to teleport to your spawn point (making sure you do not go so far away as to make Plantera despawn) and progress down the tunnel, firing behind you as you go. Alternatively, you can time your attacks so that Plantera is not blocking the entrance to your tunnel when she enters Phase 2, which eliminates the need for a Bed and Magic Mirror.
Another variant of this technique involves a vertical escape tunnel instead of a horizontal one, which has the advantage of being simpler to excavate with Dynamite.


=== Sentry Spam ===
As a slow-moving boss, Plantera is very susceptible to Sentry attacks. Using the Tier 2 Old One's Army armor sold by the Tavernkeep, a War Table and an accessory such as the Apprentice's Scarf, the player can spawn five buffed sentries. In the first phase, it's best to use these on platforms in a large arena and circle around Plantera, dodging the seeds and keeping Plantera near the sentries. 
In the second phase, use a long horizontal tunnel to escape. If using the Ballista Cane, use the right-click to target the ballistas directly to Plantera and avoid using whips (allowing the piercing projectile to hit Plantera directly). Traps made by the Explosive Trap Cane do not need to be targeted. The other two tavernkeep summons may not have enough power or pierce to damage Plantera sufficiently quickly. 
If using whips, Firecracker pairs very well with both Ballistas and Explosive Traps. If not, use a sidearm that matches the armor (such as the Death Sickle for Squire armor or the Phantom Phoenix for Huntress armor).


== References ==

title: Guide:Skyblock
content:
Skyblock heavily changes game progression and forces the player to create their own artificial biomes to progress. This guide will contain spoilers.


== Recommended settings ==
The player should consider creating a small world for easier access to the Shimmer Island. The Shimmer is extremely useful in Skyblock, so it has an entire section dedicated to its uses here. World size has no other effect.
However, in a larger world, more Hardmode ore pockets generate per altar smashed.
If comfortable with the difficulty, the player should consider setting the world to Expert Mode or higher to obtain exclusive items such as Royal Gel or Shield of Cthulhu.


== Surface ==
Farm slimes for all your resources. They will drop Acorns to get wood, Gel for weapons, and ore. Slimes on Skyblock worlds are more likely to carry an item and additional items are added to their bonus drop pool.
Your starting weapon is essentially useless; get a Slime Spear or Slime Whip as soon as possible, as both only require 50 Gel and your starting Solidifier. Farming for a Zombie Arm or a Slime Staff is very slow, making the previous weapons the best option for a weapon at this point in the game. Consider pairing the whip with Abigail's Flower: plant your grass seeds and put tombstones onto the grass blocks, whether from your own deaths on a non-Hardcore character or from NPC deaths on Hardcore.
Zombies drop Sickles in this seed, which can be used to farm large amounts of Hay for building.
NPCs sell many useful items, so build houses for them immediately. Additionally, Gel can be crafted into Slime Blocks which can be further crafted into furniture for this purpose.
Dirt Blocks can be farmed by using Dirt Bombs in an open area and repeatedly crafting them. The player can also go to the Underground using Ropes and farm Dirt Slimes that spawn in the area. In addition you are able to use Poo on an Extractinator for dirt blocks. Because Wood can be shimmered into Dirt, a tree farm also functions as a Dirt farm.
In the early stage, ropes can be placed horizontally instead of Minecart Tracks to prevent monsters from spawning as there will be no solid tiles.
Building out to the outer 1/6 of the world allows both Goblin Scouts and Foxparks. The scouts drop Tattered Cloth which can be used to summon the Goblin Army.


== Underground ==
The quickest way to get a Furnace is to descend into the underground layer using Rope and/or platforms. There, Slimes will drop Stone, Wood, and Dirt, as well as ores. It is recommended to use Cloud Blocks (or Cloud Platforms) to build a bridge as they are renewable from cloud slimes and negate fall damage.
For an Anvil, you should purchase it from the Merchant to save on Iron Ore. Iron is valuable to create Empty Buckets, which when thrown on the ground as an item, will fill up with water once it rains. An entire stack of buckets can convert to water at once. You can get lava from Lava Slimes that spawn in The Underworld (this seed causes them to always drop lava, even in Classic difficulty), and they drop much more lava than usual. You can get honey by obtaining the Honey Blocks for which the Honey Slimes can be defeated. Liquid duplication can be used to get an infinite supply of any liquid. Additionally, Water, Lava, and Honey Buckets can be converted into one another using the shimmer.
If you are standing near water, you can craft Dirt Blocks into Mud Blocks. Slimes have a chance to drop Jungle Grass Seeds, allowing you to create a Jungle.
The Skeleton Merchant sells Roller Skates, allowing you to create bridges with ease.


== Cavern ==
In the Cavern layer, Slimes can spawn that drop Life Crystals, Cobwebs, and Conveyor Belts. Mimics will drop Gold Chest loot.
Slimes will also spawn containing Granite and Marble blocks, allowing for the creation of an artificial Granite Cave biome. This allows the player access to Granite enemies that drop Geodes, allowing the player access to gems. Marble allows Hoplites to spawn, who drop the high-defense Gladiator armor and the Stress Ball, which is useful for AFK farms.
Alternatively, if the player creates an NPC town in the cavern layer, gem critters will spawn quite frequently nearby, especially in the rain. Catching these with a bug Net and then shimmering them gives their respective gem. Additionally, once the player has access to the gem and acorns, gemcorns can be used to also farm even more gems. Gem critters can also be caught to sell for 15 Silver per, which helps to start collecting money for later in the run.


== Farming Mobs ==
Once you obtain lava, you can start farming mobs in the Surface, Underground and Cavern layer for their loot. 
Original design by Khaios on youtube.


== Evil biome ==
After the Eye of Cthulhu is defeated, the player will get access to their chosen evil biome. Creating a fishing pool in the evil biome will make the player able to obtain Corrupt Crates and Crimson Crates, which can contain loot dropped by destroying a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart, respectively. Additionally, creating an artificial evil biome is required to fight the respective evil boss.


== Jungle and Glowing Mushroom ==
In order to build the biomes, the player has to turn Dirt into the Mud by standing in the water or near any of the Sinks; both the Jungle Grass Seeds and the Mushroom Grass Seeds are rarely dropped from the Slimes on the surface and can be transformed into each other via Shimmer.
The Glowing Mushroom biome can also spawn in the world as an additional island if the world is created with the secret seed toadstool
Turning your starting island into a glowing mushroom biome might come in handy, as it counts as a pylon link biome, which can be used for easy access to the shimmer island, and for the Truffle to move in while in hardmode.


=== Jungle biome specifics ===
There are slimes unique to this area, notably the Bee slimes that shoot bees when damaged/touched by the player and drop the hive block, or the herb slimes that drop the Moonglow plant.
There are alternative ways to build the Jungle Biome:

The player can build the Glowing Mushroom Biome and create a house for Dryad, who sells the Mushroom Grass Seeds that can be crafted into the Jungle Grass Seeds by shimmering them.
Note that Jungle Spores cannot grow if other jungle plants are in the way, so a farm for spores should regularly be cleaned out to make room for Spores to farm.


== Snow biome ==
During night after the player has defeated King Slime, or the Eye of Cthulhu, the Demolitionist will sell Freeze Bombs that turns water into ice. 
Placing ice blocks allows Ice Slime and Spiked Ice Slimes to spawn; in particular, they require either a Snow Biome or ice tiles to spawn on. When Underground, they have a chance to drop Snow and Slush respectively.
Alternatively, using the secret seed winter is coming will generate snow and ice islands.
Unlike regular worlds, only 300 blocks are needed to make Snow biome.
Defeating Deerclops to obtain the Pew-matic Horn is the most reliable way of getting a gun for the Arms Dealer to move in. The other option is to purchase the Revolver or to fish for crates in the evil biome. During Christmas, the Red Ryder can be obtained from presents instead.


== Desert biome, Sand and Glass ==

Sand can be obtained by using Obsidian or Shell Piles on the Extractinator. Unlike the usual 1500 blocks required in other world seeds, only 300 blocks are needed to make the Desert biome in the Skyblock seed. The Extractinator can be obtained via Mimics or Wooden Crate, and the Shimmer Island uses Obsidian to contain the Shimmer. Alternatively, potions can be thrown into Shimmer to obtain Bottled Water, which is further reduced to Glass, then Sand. Afterwards, such a setup can be used to spawn an Antlion to infinitely obtain Sand Blocks.
Alternatively, you can fish in the ocean biome to obtain shell piles to extractinate from Biome Crates. The next thing you should do is lay down a long line of sand in the Ocean biome, which will cause shells to spawn continuously on top of it, which can be turned into more sand. Once you have enough sand, you can make an artificial Underground Desert biome, allowing you to farm Antlion Mandible (which can alternatively be obtained from shimmering mining potions), which allows you to craft the Sandgun. With the sandgun and some ammo reservation, you could easily and efficiently AFK farm infinite sand using a torch setup.
Sand Slimes have a chance to spawn once either a Desert biome is established or sand tiles are present for them to spawn on. When underground, they have a chance to drop Fossils. Note that the Underground Desert biome requires both that the player be in front of unsafe desert walls and that enemies spawn in front of unsafe desert walls. This includes placing the walls behind the sand itself and not just above it.
Additionally, using the secret seed sandy britches will generate desert islands.


== Ocean biome ==
At the edges of the world, the ocean biome will still generate as usual, despite not having any blocks for obvious reasons. From the ocean biome, you are able to get the Angler, and farm infinite sand by exploiting the shell-spawning mechanic unique to the ocean biome. Place sand in a line, and Shell and Starfish will slowly generate, which can be broken down to Shell Pile, and use it at an extractinator for more sand. Additionally, creating an artificial water pool at the ocean is required to fight Duke Fishron.


== Early bosses ==
The King Slime is highly rewarding in Expert Mode, dropping the Royal Gel accessory that makes almost all slimes no longer try to attack you (Projectiles such as a Spiked Jungle Slime's spikes will still deal damage if the slime is attacking another player who does not have the Royal Gel). Wait for a Slime Rain.
The Eye of Cthulhu can randomly spawn at night once the player has 200 HP, 10 defense, and 4 NPCs. Among the items, the boss drops Crimson Seeds or Corrupt Seeds which allow the player to create The Corruption/The Crimson biome. It also drops either of the Altars, which are functional and allow to craft the summoning items to fight the bosses repeatedly as well as to craft the Night's Edge.
Defeating the Brain of Cthulhu or Eater of Worlds will cause a Meteorite shower at night, which is equivalent to a crash event. Small Meteorites will fall from the sky, crashing into the world's topmost solid blocks and becoming Meteorite ore which can then be picked up. They will not crash into platforms. The player can be hurt by the falling Meteorites if they are hit by them.


== The Dungeon ==
Both the Brain of Cthulhu or Eater of Worlds drop Dungeon blocks and all three unsafe wall variants which allows the creation of an artificial Dungeon. Placing the blocks allows the Old Man to spawn and for Skeletron to be fought. However, the Dungeon Guardian still can spawn if the player is below the surface and had not defeated Skeletron yet.
Once Skeletron is defeated and the walls are placed, water can be used to fish up Dungeon Crates. Additionally, Skeletron drops the Hellforge, which can be crafted into the Hardmode Forge in Hardmode and allow the player to create more powerful gear. Additionally, killing Skeletron causes Hell Slimes to begin spawning in The Underworld which drop Hellstone.


== Fishing ==
Fishing can be important in this secret seed because it allows the player to obtain the items that they would normally get from chests in their respective environment (i.e. the player can obtain Boomstick by fishing in the Jungle and catching the Jungle Crate) or to obtain unique items such as Frog Leg. In addition, the player may accumulate a lot of fish that can be sold, cooked into food or be used to brew potions.
By placing the sand blocks in the Ocean, the player can spawn the Angler NPC that will reward the player with both the vanity items or novelty furniture and the functional items in exchange for completing his quests that involve bringing unique quest fish from various biomes and/or environments. The most important items are the Golden Fishing Rod (the most powerful fishing rod), potions for fishing, bait,the ingredients for the Angler Tackle Bag, and the Golden Bug Net.
The Bottomless Water Bucket is guaranteed on the 25th quest, and can be very useful for easily creating fishing pools in each biome.
With the Golden Bug Net, Underworld critters can be caught and used to fish for Obsidian Crates, which can contain the Lavaproof Fishing Hook for the Lavaproof Tackle Bag, Hellforges, and can give Hellstone Bars before Skeletron has been defeated.
Generally, it is very helpful to do Angler quests each day you can. The rewards scale the more quests you do and it gives you access to better fishing gear allowing you easier access to biome specific drops through crates or regular fishing.


== Late Pre-Hardmode ==
At this point, you should make an arena for the Wall of Flesh, preferably out of Planter Boxes for being cheap to buy in bulk, act essentially the same as platforms, and let Lava pass through unlike platforms which get destroyed, which is very useful, since in the skyblock seed, Lava Slimes and Hell Slimes will always spawn lava when defeated. Alternatively, you may want to use full blocks for a bridge, as falling through them can be instantly fatal regardless of how prepared you are. You should also have a Pylon network set up for quick travel between islands or underground farms you may have set up.
Minecart Tracks can also be used, as they can be ridden, or walked on using Roller Skates. Like planter boxes, they are easily able to be obtained in bulk, and lava is able to pass through them, but they also prevent enemy spawns as they are not a solid block. This is especially useful in For the Worthy and Get fixed boi seeds where the Wall of Flesh will spawn buffed Fire Imps during the fight.


== Hardmode ==


=== Early Hardmode ===
Once the Wall of Flesh is defeated, the player is able to create the Hallow biome by planting Hallowed Seeds on dirt. The Hallow can spread quickly to Sand, creating Pearlsand which can be multiplied by using the Sand gun with any form of ammo conservation. Additionally, the player can craft Holy Water to speed up the spread of the Hallow. Another change is that the player can obtain the Hardmode ores by defeating the new slimes; at this point, the progression is very straightforward.
Although Biome Chests are obtainable by Shimmering their respective Biome Keys, only naturally generated Biome Chests contain items, meaning their exclusive items are unobtainable in Skyblock.


=== Jungle Temple ===
On this seed, Plantera drops Lihzahrd Bricks, unsafe Lihzard walls, and the Lihzahrd Altar, allowing Golem to be summoned. In addition to this, the Picksaw is dropped, allowing the player to fix their artificial Jungle Temple if mistakes were made.


=== Lunar Events ===
Upon defeating Golem, the Cultists will spawn in the artificial Dungeon you created previously, allowing for the Lunar Events and Moon Lord to be fought.


== Shimmer Island ==
There is only one other island besides the main one you spawn on, which is the Shimmer Island. There are many uses for the Shimmer, but the ones most useful to this seed are as follows:

Throwing a Slime Crown into it spawns a Slime Rain which is useful for farming more slimes for their drops.
Obtaining more basic blocks, such as stone, clay, and dirt, by shimmering extra ore and bars from fishing, wood from farming trees, or Dynasty Wood purchased from the Traveling Merchant. Additionally, furnaces and anvils purchased from the Merchant can be decrafted into wood, stone, and Iron Bars.
Crafting Unsafe walls to use for spawn purposes. This includes the following uses:
Overgrown Living Wood Walls for critter and gnome farming, in which the latter spawns most frequently behind Living Wood Walls and provides a luck buff once turned into a Garden Gnome.
Cursed Dungeon Walls for dungeon creation/expansion or restoration in case the player broke them.
Infested Spider Walls for farming Cobwebs and allowing access to the Stylist and Spider Fangs.
Treacherous Sandstone Walls and Treacherous Hardened Sand Walls, allowing access to Underground Desert enemies and drops, such as the Desert Spirit Lamp or Ancient Horn.


== With For the Worthy ==
In the For the Worthy special world seed, it removes the Solidifier and the Shimmer Island along with all of its other effects, unless Celebration Mk 10 seed is also enabled.


== With Zenith ==
The Zenith (seed) special world seed starts on an ash island in The Underworld, along with all the other changes caused by the Remix seed. Initially, it is recommended to farm the Lava Slimes that will spawn, as their drops have been switched to that of a normal Slime (additionally containing no lava drops), and gather enough blocks or ropes to get to the cavern layer.
From this point, you can continue the run as in a normal Skyblock world, but there are some important changes that may affect your playthrough:

Trees grow on the surface, but the time it takes for a tree to grow is extended by at least 100 times
Hellbats spawn when approximately 800 blocks away from the center of the world and are an easy source of early lava
The starter island is corrupted, therefore no NPC shops near it will sell pylons
However, pylons still work on the island; they just need to be bought elsewhere

title: Potent Acid
content:
Potent Acid is a Hardmode debuff that causes afflicted enemies and NPCs to lose 90 health per second (60 damage displayed every 0.67 seconds).
Its damage can be increased by Accelerated Afflictions.
Potent Acid is only inflicted alongside Acid Venom, never on its own, resulting in enemies losing 120 health per second (60 damage displayed every 0.5 seconds) when combined. The combination of the two debuffs is referred to as Potent Venom in item tooltips.


== Causes ==


=== From player ===


== Immune NPCs ==


== Trivia ==
When applied by the Flask of Venom, Potent Acid has the shortest duration a player can inflict a debuff to another target in the game.

title: Legacy:Guide:Frost Moon strategies
content:
Only differences from the current guide are listed.
While the Pumpkin Moon consists of 15 waves, the Frost Moon consists of 20. 
The Mechanical Glove is preferred over the Fire Gauntlet, as the On Fire! debuff does not make up for the lost DPS from the lower damage.
For magic users, the Bat Scepter, Heat Ray and Spectre Staff all help against enemies with higher health. The Razorpine and Blizzard Staff are by far the best options once they are obtained, as both possess high single-target damage.

title: Guide:Golem strategies
content:
Golem is a Hardmode boss, found at the end of the Lihzahrd Temple. It has high HP, high defense, and multiple limbs and phases. This boss is not very mobile and its attacks are fairly easy to dodge, but the arena fought in after world generation can affect its difficulty. In multiplayer however, his difficulty greatly increases and becomes extremely challenging due to the faster fist attacks.


== Spawn Condition ==
Golem can be summoned by using the Lihzahrd Power Cell at the Lihzahrd Altar.


== The Fight ==
Golem has a total of four attackable targets, but only two are necessary to defeat:

Golem Head - This is the main target during the first form. It will frequently spew two fireballs that bounce. At half health, it will begin to fire lasers that increase in frequency when its HP lowers.
Golem Body - This is the main target during the second form. Its main attack is a jump attack.
Right Arm - This is an optional target. It uses a punch attack with a reach that can extend across the arena. It is recommended that you take these out first because they will become brutal if you leave them on for the third and fourth phases.
Left Arm - This is an optional target with the same move-set as the Right Arm. It uses a punch attack with a reach that can extend across the arena.


=== First Form ===
Once summoned, Golem will move around while slowly attacking with its fists. The head will continuously spit two fireballs that will bounce around the arena. Dodging the fireballs is your priority, as they will inflict On Fire! and prevent health regeneration. The head (25000/37500/47812 HP) and arms are the targets during this phase, with the head being the main target. Destroying the arms is not strictly necessary, but recommended to make the next phase much easier. Note that Lihzahrd enemies can still spawn in the arena.
When Golem's head HP reaches 50% (12500 / 18750 HP), it will begin using Eye lasers. They start at an average interval, but as the head's HP is reduced, the frequency of the lasers will increase. When the head's hit points reach zero the second form begins. The lasers signal a DPS race and all focus should be concentrated on getting through each laser phase. These eye lasers can pass through blocks.


=== Second Form ===
Destroying the head stops the laser assault and reveals Golem's true form. The body (15000/22500/28687 HP) is the main target and destroying it will end the fight. The body will jump around and if the arms still exist, they will punch devastatingly faster compared to phase one. The head will be attacking while flying around. Note that the Head can pass through blocks.
The head will continue firing lasers at a reset frequency, which, similar in the first form, will increase as the body's hit points decrease.


=== Expert mode/Master mode ===
The only difference in these modes are increased damage and increased health.


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===
If this is your first encounter with Golem, then you will not possess the Picksaw capable of shaping the Lihzahrd Temple's blocks, so your customization is limited.

Golem can pass through walls. The best way to avoid contact with the body is to place a row of platforms about 25-30 blocks from the ground, as Golem is unable to jump that high.
If you decided to fight Golem in the temple, then Lihzahrd and Flying Snake Banners would be useful because they will still keep spawning during the fight. It'll be much easier to get rid of them.


=== Gearing up ===


==== Armor ====
The best set for a melee user consists of a Chlorophyte Mask, Monk's Shirt, and Squire's Greaves, which together provide the best offensive bonuses available, and also provide higher defense than Chlorophyte armor.
Hallowed Mask and Turtle Scale Mail or Squire's Plating (if using minions) are defensive substitutes.
The Turtle armor is the best set available if the player does not want to fight the Old One's Army
For ranged characters the best offensive set consists of Adamantite Mask, Shroomite Breastplate and Mythril Greaves.
Shroomite armor isn't recommended since there is no way to safely activate stealth during a boss fight in singleplayer, unless using the Piranha Gun or playing in a multiplayer server and there's a player aggroing the boss which then becomes the strongest armor available.
A magic user should use Spectre armor and keep the Spectre hood in the social slot and quickly change to it when getting close to dying.
For summoners the Tiki armor is a great choice.
Spooky armor is the best choice available for summoners if the Pumpkin Moon has been completed.


==== Weapons ====
All classes can fare well against Golem.

Weapons from Duke Fishron and Empress of Light are all very strong against Golem, as long as they have been obtained at this stage. These will be omitted in the following content.
For Melee users:

Terra Blade is usually the best weapon for Golem, especially when using the blade itself to damage the fists. The Horseman's Blade and Psycho Knife can kill Golem slightly faster, but do not have the option of fighting at a distance like the Terra Blade.
Scourge of the Corruptor is also extremely useful as it does good damage, splits into three and is homing.
The Eye of Cthulhu with the Magic Yoyo Bag balances high DPS and safe distance.
The Paladin's Hammer is an excellent sidearm for increasing the armor penetration of your other weapons.
The Keybrand can be used as a sidearm by throwing it underneath Golem, doing passive damage, and has respectable damage when thrown from a distance.
Vampire Knives is a great support weapon, as its lifesteal can quickly heal the player when they're low on HP.
For Ranged users:

Piranha Gun can utilize Shroomite's armor stealth while moving, easily shredding the boss.
Nail Gun is expensive to use, but more powerful than most other weapons unlocked at this stage. The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher has cheaper ammunition and somewhat higher damage, but is harder to obtain.
The Stake Launcher and Candy Corn Rifle excel in this fight. The rifle in particular works well in smaller arenas, as each bouncing bullet can hit Golem repeatedly.
Venus Magnum coupled with Crystal Bullets is also a great weapon.
Sniper Rifle is a fairly consistent and good damaging weapon with Chlorophyte Bullets, or Crystal Bullets/Nano Bullets if you are willing to aim.
For Magic users:

The Spectre Staff, Leaf Blower and Inferno Fork are the usually the best magic weapons for Golem. The Bat Scepter has similar damage, but can be difficult to obtain.
Magnet Sphere and Rainbow Gun will allow for great sustained healing when using the Spectre Hood and are also great support Weapons overall.
Golden Shower is the best support magic weapon as it gives +15 armor penetration.
Toxic Flask is a good alternative for the beginning of the fight, as it does a good amount of splash damage. Be mindful of its high mana cost.
For Summoners:

The Desert Tiger Staff does excellent damage against Golem when combined with the Vulgar Display of Flower whip.
The Raven Staff is amazing for this fight, as the ravens can easily stay on top of Golem thanks to its slow movement.
The Deadly Sphere Staff is slightly weaker but easier to obtain.
The Morning Star is incredible for the second phase of this fight.
The Dark Harvest is great for the first phase of the fight.
The Staff of the Frost Hydra is a great sentry for this fight. The Queen Spider Staff and Barnacle Staff are alternatives.


==== Accessories ====
Wings are especially useful for this fight due to the large number of projectiles. The Hoverboard is a strong choice for its horizontal speed.
Hermes Boots and upgrades are less important and can be dropped if alternative speed boosts like Swiftness Potion or Slice of Cake are used.
Master Ninja Gear is helpful for dashing out of danger and dodging attacks.
The Mystic Arts Sash's dodge can stack with the Master Ninja Gear.
The Charm of Myths is useful for potion cooldown reduction and regeneration.
Emblems and Moon Stone enhance damage and suit offensive builds.
The Fire Gauntlet is ideal for melee builds, especially when stacked with the Mechanical Glove.
The Magic Yoyo Bag is highly effective for yoyo builds.
The Putrid Scent offers decent damage and crit boosts. In Crimson worlds, it can be obtained by shimmering Flesh Knuckles.
The Celestial Emblem is the best magic-damage accessory.
The Mana Cloak is helpful for managing mana with high-cost weapons.
The Pygmy Necklace and Hercules Beetle are very useful for summoners.
The Papyrus Scarab and Necromantic Scroll are incredible for summoners.
Squire's Shield and Apprentice's Scarf provide summoner bonuses but they do not stack.
Whipstackers will want to use the Twilight Grasp and Snake Band.
The Frozen Shield provides crucial knockback immunity that will allow you to avoid being thrown around by enemy attacks. It also provides a nice 25% damage reduction when below half health as well as 6 defense.
The Cross Necklace and its upgrades can be used to extend the invulnerability period after being attacked. This can prove to be useful during the second phase due to the large amount of projectiles.
In Expert Mode:
The Worm Scarf will reduce the amount of damage taken.
The Brain of Confusion can prevent the player from taking damage and increase their DPS for 4 seconds, making it an excellent accessory all around.


==== Potions ====
Jungle Juice is the best healing potion available. Greater Healing Potion is a weaker alternative if you don't want to farm Life Fruits.
Ironskin, Endurance, Regeneration, and Lifeforce Potions will help you survive much longer.
Anything that gives the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied, or Exquisitely Stuffed buff is welcomed help.
Wrath and Rage Potions give very welcomed damage upgrades.
Ales and a Flask of Ichor are very effective for Melee users and summoner's whips.
Likewise with Archery Potions, for Rangers who choose to use arrows.
Mana Regeneration Potion and Magic Power Potion are a must have for Magic users.
Summoning Potions are very useful for summoners.
Obsidian Skin Potion will prevent Golem’s fireballs from setting you on fire.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Bunny Cannon ===
The Bunny Cannon works well against Golem: set it up in an area Golem cannot reach (if the blocks are set just right, Golem will not be able to chase you), and fire away. Calculate Golem's health and divide it by the bunny cannon’s damage (350), and that should give an approximate number of explosive bunnies to use.


=== Teleporter Method (Post-Golem) ===
For this method, place 2 Teleporters on opposite ends of Golem's chamber and wire them together. Make sure to have some sort of device such as levers or Pressure Plates to activate them. Summon Golem and teleport rapidly, Golem will have trouble hitting you if you teleport fast enough. This is an effective manner of beating Golem quickly as it nullifies the damage that he can deal, however this method becomes less effective as Golem takes more damage since he fires his lasers more frequently.


=== Hoverboard ===
The hoverboard is especially useful in this fight, as its fast horizontal movement allows for easier dodging. Unlike platforms, it's easy to adapt the height of the hoverboard as needed, and the player can safely attack from higher up in the arena. This is most useful in the first phase, as in the second phase, the head can do contact damage.


=== Honey Flooding ===
Golem's movement is slowed down drastically when submerged in honey. Flood more than half of the room with honey using Honey Bombs or Honey Rockets. This is particularly helpful in For the Worthy special seed, where Golem's mobility gets significantly buffed.
