title: Guide:Eater of Worlds strategies
content:
The Eater of Worlds (or EoW) is one of the bosses in Terraria. It is found in The Corruption. Preparation for this boss is both extremely helpful in the fight, and is relatively simple to complete. The following are some hints, tips, and strategies to help you defeat it when first encountered.


== Spawn Conditions ==
The Eater of Worlds is spawned by fulfilling one of these conditions:

Breaking three Shadow Orbs;
Using Worm Food.
You must then defeat the Eater of Worlds within The Corruption: getting out of The Corruption will make it retreat and despawn.


== The Fight ==
The Eater of Worlds is a huge multi-segmented worm, and thus, its parts tend to linger for a while. You can damage those parts with penetrating weapons and ammo to deal a lot of damage. It is also very mobile if you decide to fight in the Corruption Chasm. Thus, it's important to reach the surface (and its arena if you made it, check below for more info).
Beware that, when a segment dies, the segments in front and behind will detach and separately attack the player.


=== Managing the Worms ===
These two worms form a new head and tail, and they will make the fight more difficult. To prevent that, you can try to prioritize the Head segment, which has the lowest defense of the segments, but it is also the most damaging one. Alternatively, you can prioritize the Tail segment, which however is the opposite (more defense, less damaging).
Careful management of segments can reduce the number of smaller, harder to hit worms. In this case, prioritize the use of non-penetrating weapons, and hit its head and tail. If you destroy a middle segment, concentrate on the smaller worm, since the larger one can be easy to predict and dodge.


=== Expert Mode ===
In Expert Mode, the Eater of Worlds gains a variety of upgrades:

The ability to shoot Vile Spit, a projectile that deals very high damage.
Increased defense against explosives, making them considerably less viable in the fight.
When above the surface, has increased movement speed and fire rate for Vile Spit.
Vile Spit is the Eater of Worlds' most dangerous attack, so it is important to bring sufficient mobility accessories and make an arena that enables you to dodge. 


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain preparation ===

The player must be in The Corruption to summon the Eater of Worlds; moving too far away from the biome during the battle will cause it to flee.
The Eater of Worlds is a very large worm enemy, so dodging it may prove to be difficult. You may want to try fighting it on the surface instead of underground. If summoning this boss via breaking Shadow Orbs, be sure to provide yourself a quick and safe escape back to the surface where your arena will be. A room with a Bed next to your arena can let you teleport there easily, but be careful that the path from the Orb to arena does not go through any non-Corrupted areas (lest the boss despawn). When making your arena on the surface, you have some options:

In Classic Mode, make it fairly tall, thin, and easily climbable with many platforms. That way, not only you can see it coming, but this will force it to climb in a relatively straight line, leaving large portions of its body exposed, and vulnerable to piercing attacks.
In Expert Mode, due to the frequency of the Vile Spit attack, the Eater of Worlds will become much harder to dodge. Arenas built on the surface make dodging the attacks easier, but they come at the cost of increased movement and attack speed from the boss. Multiple wide platforms are normally sufficient for the fight, but you can enhance the arena by adding walls to prevent normal enemies from spawning.
Note that in Expert Mode, the Vile Spits cannot be destroyed on the surface and the player must dodge it, while the spit projectiles can be destroyed by the player when any weapons contact with them (e.g. the vile spit can be destroyed and completely negated by swinging a sword), this is a massive advantage of fighting the boss underground.
Whichever option you choose, make sure the arena doesn't go too high. If it goes too high and the Corruption background disappears, the Eater of Worlds will start despawning. Make sure your arena is low enough by seeing if your jump height (including accessories) is enough to leave the Corruption and have the background return to normal. If that happens, lower your top platform.
It's also not recommended to build your surface arena inside a valley. While it's still above the ground, the hills on either side will provide higher ground for the Eater of Worlds to get to you and make your arena less effective.
To not get interrupted by the Eaters of Souls, it's recommended to place an Eater of Souls Banner to minimize their damage. You can obtain one by killing 50 Eaters of Souls.
If you don't want to fight it on the surface, it's alright to fight it underground instead. Explosives can be used to make an underground arena. If you are breaking Shadow Orbs, hollowing out an entire arena every third Orb or escaping to a surface arena may not be practical; you should modify the terrain around you to have a quick path of escape to a space with good horizontal clearance and any hazardous terrain smoothed out or boarded over. Consider placing platforms periodically to provide extra maneuverability, and use Sticky Bombs or Sticky Dynamite to give you a few seconds of extra time to get to the arena.


=== Gearing up ===


==== Armor ====
It is recommended to have at least 200 health on Classic Mode or 300+ on Expert Mode or above; as the boss can deal high damage from both the sheer amount of segments/projectiles potentially hitting you often, and high per-hit damage from the head's strikes.

Platinum armor is the best available ore armor. If your world doesn't have readily available Platinum Ore, Gold or Tungsten armor are usable too.
Pumpkin armor is a viable option for all classes, having slightly less defense than Iron, but increasing your damage output, which can ensure the fight is completed quickly.
You can get Shadow armor by killing enough segments of the boss without necessarily defeating it, or Ancient Shadow armor by farming the Eaters of Souls.
Fossil armor is a great choice for rangers, especially ones prioritizing damage over pure survivability. Its set bonus isn't that valuable so using a Gi in the torso slot can considerably improve your damage output and speed
The Jungle armor is the best magic armor available. The Wizard set is a good alternative, trading defense for damage.
Jungle armor is also effective on any class due to its high defense.
Mages using Gem staves may want to wear a Gem robe for its unique combination effects. The explosion ability of the Topaz Robe is especially helpful in this fight.
The Flinx Fur Coat is an easily-available armor piece for summoners. Pair it with any high defense head and leg armor pieces, such as those from the Jungle armor set.
Gladiator armor is helpful for melee fighters due to the set bonus nullifying any knockback, allowing you to whale on the boss at an optimal distance for melee weapons.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users
Broadswords do very well against this boss. The strongest ones available include the Blade of Grass and Light's Bane. Very fast swords like the Exotic Scimitar, Katana, or Mandible Blade are also excellent weapons, especially when paired with the Shark Tooth Necklace.
Thrown flails such as the Ball O' Hurt or Flaming Mace can block almost all Vile Spit when spun around, which can effectively make the fight trivial in most cases, yet highly drawn-out. In addition, they can be swung into the Eater of Worlds and inflict massive damage to many of its segments.
Spears such as the Swordfish can damage multiple segments at once, and are most effective if you try to line them up with the boss's length.
For Ranged users
Spiky Balls are especially useful, as they can be thrown down where the Eater of Worlds is likely to surface and damage multiple segments as it passes through.
Bows are very effective here. The Demon Bow is easily available and powerful. If you can't gather enough Demonite, the Gold or Platinum Bowss are usable fallback options.
Jester's Arrows can pierce through infinitely many segments, although the damage drops each segment. They do best when the boss is lined up straight.
Unholy Arrows, which drop from the Eye of Cthulhu and can be crafted, do more damage and have a similar, piercing effect, though it goes through less segments at once.
Bone Throwing Knives can pierce quite a bit, are autofire, and do excellent damage in this fight. They are heavily affected by gravity, so do best when thrown straight down or at an arc.
The Flare Gun is an effective support weapon, as it pierces infinitely and inflicts the On Fire! debuff for 5 seconds. The debuff damage doesn't stack, so switch to another weapon after use until the debuffs start expiring.
The Sandgun is incredibly effective when used with Ebonsand Blocks, sporting high stats and infinite piercing. Cover your arena's platforms with torches or Minecart Tracks to avoid making a mess.
Molotov Cocktails are effective against the Eater of Worlds, leaving behind multiple flames on the ground that do ~40 damage each and hit every segment that moves through them.
On Classic Mode only, Grenades, Sticky Grenades, or Bouncy Grenades can provide cheap, easy to use area of effect damage as long as you can keep a safe distance of 5 tiles. On Expert Mode and higher, they will become near useless due to the boss's 80% damage resistance to thrown explosives, and larger segments resulting in less parts of the boss being caught per blast.
For Magic users
The Vilethorn is good for spreading damage across the boss's entire body. Furthermore, this is a relatively safe weapon to use as it can be deployed in the worms path and will remain for a short time doing damage while giving you time to dodge. It is heavily affected by defense, so it benefits from the Shark Tooth Necklace more than most weapons. It is enough to facetank the boss if having high defense and life regeneration.
Gem staves are powerful options for this fight, especially with the different combinations of staff and robe.
Topaz's small explosion is very helpful in this fight, shredding through segments of the boss.
The Diamond Staff with Topaz Robe is a very effective combination, since it gains the explosion from topaz and the high base damage from diamond. When these two gems' functions are used together, the explosion size is increased.
The Amber Staff with Topaz Robe is also great. The amber ability allows the projectiles to bounce off blocks, and pierce once.
The Emerald Staff projectiles travel quickly, and can stay on blocks. This is valuable as players can lay down "land mines" and let the Eater travel through them, dealing high damage.
Other gem staves are all viable.
The Wand of Sparking and Wand of Frosting have good stats, very low mana cost, and apply the On Fire!/Frostburn debuffs to multiple segments at once, making it fairly effective. If playing in multiplayer, use whichever one inflicts a debuff not inflicted by a teammate's weapon, as debuffs don't stack on the same target.
In Remix worlds, the Magic Dagger will take its place instead, trading mana efficiency for extra piercing.
If the player has obtained it, the Gray Zapinator is ideal due to its piercing capabilities and potential for high burst damage.
If the Crimson is available, such as in a Drunk world, the Crimson Rod is your best support weapon, increasing damage output massively.
For Summoners
The Vampire Frog is one of the strongest summons available.
The Flinx Staff is consistently available and can damage a lot of segments at once if spread out.
Pairing 1 Vampire Frog and 2 Flinx will grant the most DPS available for summoners.
The Abigail's Flower is stronger for single minion type setups and when the boss is coiled up due to its AoE damage.
Using Foxparks in flamethrower mode can pierce several segments at once, dealing high damage, but its use may conflict with damage or bonuses from whips.
The Snapthorn will destroy the Eater of Worlds quickly. The Soulscourge is a weaker alternative.


==== Accessories ====
Accessories that improve mobility such as Rocket Boots (or upgrades), the Blizzard or Sandstorm in a Bottle, or the Magiluminescence are recommended as they can help with dodging.
For Melee or Ranged users, the Pyroclastic Stone can significantly boost damage with its multi-target effect. The Snapping Stone by itself can still significantly increase damage.
For rangers, the Poison Barb can be useful when combined with Jester's Arrows, allowing the player to poison many segments at once.
Accessories with Warding will be most efficient here, but are not required.
The Feral Claws grant autoswing and significantly increase the damage of broadswords and whips, which are already some of the best weapons for this fight.
The Shark Tooth Necklace is useful in Expert or Master Mode due to the boss's higher defense. It pairs especially well with weapons that hit many times per second
The Slimy Saddle mount bounces when hit by the Eater of Worlds and does damage. When used in the open, it can protect you from being trapped. When used against a ceiling, the mount bounces rapidly, dealing large amounts of damage even in higher difficulty modes.


==== Potions ====
Ironskin and Regeneration Potions can really help mitigate any hits you take.
Hunter Potions can be very useful in spotting the Eater of Worlds as it burrows, making it easier to fight even without a raised platform.
A Cooked Fish or other food items will also give you a small buff to all stats.
The Thorns Potion will damage the Eater of Worlds every time it hurts you and is easy to craft.
An easy way to get out of the Chasm if you wish to fight on the surface is to use a Gravitation Potion and a Lucky Horseshoe. Be careful not to ascend too far above the surface or the boss will despawn.
A Burger is a uncommon drop from the Eaters of Souls that provides the Exquisitely Stuffed buff which is very useful during the fight.
A Summoning Potion is highly recommended for anyone using minions due to the extra minion slot it provides.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Slime Mount ===
The Slimy Saddle can be used to deal a high amount of damage in this fight. If trapped between the Eater of Worlds and the top of a cavern, the mount can bounce very rapidly, killing segments quickly. Alternatively, it can be used in a vertical arena to keep the player bouncing upwards and away from the boss, while firing a weapon downward.


=== Minecart ===
One simple way to beat this boss is to set up a very short segment of Minecart Tracks, hammering the ends into bumpers. By riding a Minecart back and forth quickly, the player can do rapid, high piercing damage.
In Expert or Master Mode, drinking an Ironskin Potion and Endurance Potion helps reduce the damage taken by the head segments.


=== Tanking ===
Most of the segments of the Eater of Worlds have low damage, besides the head. With enough defense, the player can simply ignore most of the damage by standing inside the boss and letting invincibility frames do the heavy lifting, although this is riskier in Master Mode. You can use a Grappling Hook and hook it to the ground to be able to remain stationary, or use Gladiator armor to become immune to knockback. Once the Eater of Worlds has been summoned, begin swinging. As the Eater of Worlds tries to inflict damage by passing through you, your weapons will tear it apart, and the fight will be over fairly quickly. This can also be used as an effective farming technique. A Thorns Potion is recommended to increase damage dealt by this method.


=== Farming ===
The EoW can be a good source of money if you sell the Demonite Ore and Shadow Scales that it drops. With even late pre-Hardmode armor and weapons you can quickly defeat this easy-to-summon boss. Once you have recruited the Tavernkeep, his Lightning Aura sentries are deadly against the EoW, because once the head has passed a given point, all the body segments must follow. Even the Rod can kill the boss "cleanly" (from the head back) in a few passes, while the player simply evades the worm and renews or moves the sentry as needed.

title: Stoned
content:
Stoned is a Hardmode debuff that inflicts 20 / 40 / 60 damage to the player  and causes them to turn into stone, rendering them immobile and unable to use items. Additionally, fall damage is greatly increased and the distance required before fall damage can occur is reduced (see fall damage for details). If the player is in reversed gravity, the gravity direction will return to normal. It also disables mounts, hooks, and ignores the effects any accessories that grant immunity to fall damage, including the Lucky Horseshoe and all types of wings. The fall damage immunity granted by Featherfall Potion and Djinn's Curse will still take effect, however.
The debuff can be inflicted by Medusa when the player is in her line of sight and looking at her during her attack state. The debuff lasts 1–4 seconds, depending on how long Medusa has been in the attack state before the player faces her. Medusa cannot petrify any player not facing her direction or otherwise not being within line of sight. Additionally, the Stone Slime also inflicts this debuff on attack.
The debuff can be negated by equipping the Pocket Mirror or its derivatives.


== Causes ==


=== From enemy ===


== Notes ==
Quick Heal works under the debuff.
The debuffs Stoned, Frozen, and Webbed all disable the player's inputs. When more than one of them is active at a time, the priority for the effects is as follows: Stoned → Frozen → Webbed.
Note that if the Webbed effect coexists with any of the other effects, the player will not experience the effects of gravity.
Dying from the Stoned debuff will display one of the following unique death messages:
“<Player name> shattered into pieces.”
“<Player name> can't be put back together again.”
“<Player name> needs to be swept up.”
“<Player name> just became another dirt pile.”

Taking damage while Stoned will play the sound that most blocks and walls make when struck, rather than the player's regular hurt sound.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Can now be inflicted by a slime variant carrying Stone Blocks.
Desktop 1.3.5: Fixed death message always being “<Player name> was slain...”
Desktop 1.3.3: Can now be prevented by the Pocket Mirror accessory.
Desktop 1.3.1: Medusa can no longer petrify players directly above her.
Desktop 1.3.0.4: Medusa now needs a straight line of sight to trigger the debuff while attacking.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Introduced.

title: Artisan Loaf
content:
The Artisan Loaf is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the range that the player can access crafting stations by 4 tiles in all directions. The Artisan Loaf can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 10 Gold during a Waning Crescent, New Moon, or Waxing Crescent. It can also only be used once per player, and the Skeleton Merchant will cease to sell it once the player has consumed an Artisan Loaf.


== Trivia ==
The tooltip quote is a reference to a plot point from the 1990 platform game ActRaiser, where a loaf of bread is used to convince a child named Teddy to go back home.


== History ==

title: Skeletron Prime
content:
Skeletron Prime is a Hardmode mechanical boss which is essentially a more difficult version of Skeletron. It consists of a head and four limbs, but, similarly to Skeletron, only the head needs to be defeated to defeat the boss.
While Skeletron Prime is alive, its exclusive music Skeletron Prime will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning and spawning ==


=== Manual ===
Skeletron Prime can be summoned manually using a Mechanical Skull at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).


=== Random ===
Skeletron Prime can also spawn naturally at the start of the night, as long as it has not yet been defeated at least once in the current world. Its arrival when spawning naturally is announced by the status message "The air is getting colder around you...".
In order for the boss to spawn naturally, the following conditions must be fulfilled at dusk (7:30 PM):

The world is in Hardmode and at least one Demon or Crimson Altar has been destroyed.
In worlds where the Skyblock special world seed is active and the tile threshold is not exceeded, Skeletron Prime can spawn even if no altars have been destroyed.
No boss is already alive, and the Eye of Cthulhu is not already spawning naturally.
None of the following events are active: Lantern Night, Old One's Army, Pumpkin Moon, or Frost Moon.
Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
If the conditions are met, there is a 1/10 (10%) chance for a random mechanical boss to spawn that has not yet been defeated in the world. This gives Skeletron Prime initially a spawn chance of 1/30 (3.33%) per night. If another mechanical boss is defeated first, the chance for Skeletron Prime to spawn increases to 1/20 (5%), and should both of the other mechanical bosses be defeated first, then Skeletron Prime has the full remaining 1/10 (10%) spawn chance per night.
Once Skeletron Prime has been selected to spawn, the status message appears and a hidden countdown of 1 minute 21 seconds begins. Skeletron Prime spawns at the end of the countdown, at 8:51 PM. Another check is performed at that time, with all of the following conditions needing to be fulfilled in order for the boss to spawn:

At least one player is in the surface or Space layer.
Consequently, the natural spawning of Skeletron Prime can easily be prevented by being in a layer lower than the surface at 8:51 PM. Returning to the surface afterward will not cause Skeletron Prime to spawn either (unlike with the Eye of Cthulhu).
This restriction is lifted in worlds where the world spawn point is below the surface, such as worlds with the special world seed Remix active or the secret world seed Mole people. Skeletron Prime can spawn naturally in those worlds regardless of the player's position, whether they are above or below the surface.
No boss is already alive.
The Lunar Events are not active and the countdown for the spawning of the Moon Lord has not begun, either due to manual summoning or defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar.
Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
In singleplayer, exiting the world during the countdown also prevents Skeletron Prime from spawning naturally.
In worlds where the special seeds For the Worthy and The Constant are present but Celebration Mk 10 is not, Skeletron Prime will still be able to randomly spawn, even if it has been defeated before.


=== For the Worthy and Remix ===
Skeletron Prime cannot be summoned in worlds where both the For the Worthy and Remix special world seeds are active, since the boss is part of Mechdusa instead.


== Arms ==


== Behavior ==
Skeletron Prime's head constantly endeavors to remain between 31.5 and 12.5 tiles above the player and within 6.25 tiles of either side of the player. It can accelerate infinitely in order to move back into this area. The head does not actively attempt to make contact with the player.
Skeletron Prime's four limbs all have unique attacks:

Prime Cannon fires bombs every 2.33 seconds that do not destroy tiles, usually up into the air rather than directly at the player. It usually stays above the player.
Prime Saw usually remains under the player, moving up and down.
Prime Vice will swipe around wildly, making occasional lunges at the player. It usually remains diagonal to the player.
Prime Laser shoots red Death Lasers every 3.33 seconds, similar to those of Retinazer and The Destroyer, and is always pointed at a player. It usually stays horizontal to the player.

Every 10 seconds, Skeletron Prime will enter a spinning phase for 6.67 seconds, in which its attacks become more aggressive:

Skeletron Prime's head will grow spikes and start spinning towards the player at 10 mph, exactly like how its pre-Hardmode counterpart Skeletron does. Damage and defense are doubled to 94 / 160 / 240 damage and 48 defense. In Expert Mode, the base spinning speed is 31 mph and is increased the further the player is away, up to a maximum of 76 mph at a distance of 37.5 tiles.
Prime Cannon will aim at the player directly and decrease its cooldown between firing to 0.67 seconds.
Prime Saw will begin homing directly towards the player's location.
Prime Vice becomes more aggressive and frequently lunges towards the player.
Prime Laser will fire lasers every 1.33 seconds.
Skeletron Prime lets out a roar every time it enters the spinning phase.
If Skeletron Prime is not killed before dawn (4:30 AM), it will enrage and permanently behave like a faster Dungeon Guardian, increasing its velocity and usually killing the player instantly upon contact: its damage and defense is increased to 9,999. It will remain in this state until defeated, even if it becomes night again. Killing Skeletron Prime in this form still counts as defeating it and it will drop its items normally.
If the player is more than 375 tiles away, Skeletron Prime will start moving downwards and will quickly despawn.


== Notes ==
The Bombs fired by the Prime Cannon explode upon contact with platforms as well as Planter Boxes.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Unhindered movement is crucial when Skeletron Prime's head starts spinning, as it deals double the regular damage. Wings greatly aid in moving vertically, and flattened terrain or a sky bridge are convenient for horizontal movement.
Although it is a little more time-consuming, focusing on the arms first is very rewarding. Once Skeletron Prime's head is no longer shielded by anything, the fight becomes a lot easier. Prioritize damage on the arm which is causing the most damage or disruption, so it can be destroyed and removed from the fight as quick as possible.
A good idea is to focus on the Prime Laser first, as it is harder to dodge than the other limbs.
Due to Skeletron Prime's overall high defense, inflicting it with Ichor is effective, as it is not immune to it. Note that most Ichor weapons lack in damage compared to other weapons, so they should only be used periodically for inflicting the debuff.


== Trivia ==

Skeletron Prime will open and shut its mouth for the entire duration of the battle, except for when its head is spinning. This is a purely cosmetic effect.
Skeletron Prime's joints that connect its arms and head continuously emit fire and smoke particles in a similar manner to that of Skeletron's joints.
It is the only mechanical boss whose name contains the pre-Hardmode boss's name. Furthermore, it used to be the only mechanical boss that shared boss music with its pre-Hardmode variant. Additionally, its name does not begin with the word The, unlike the other two mechanical bosses.
Unlike Skeletron, Skeletron Prime's defense doubles when its head is spinning.
Although Skeletron Prime's head is immune to Penetrated, its limbs are not.
Normally, Skeletron Prime's head has 2000 less health than Plantera, but in Expert Mode and Master Mode, they both have the same amount.
When Skeletron Prime's head is spinning, the map icon will spin too.
Skeletron Prime is the only boss with more than two arms.
The sprite file for Skeletron Prime's arms is named Arm_Bone_2.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, Skeletron Prime was one of the three mechanical recreations of Cthulhu's missing organs. It is a recreation of part of Cthulhu's skeleton.
 The Bestiary entry for  Skeletron Prime: "Mechanically reconstructed for reviving Cthulhu, this Skeletron has more arms than ever before, and a variety of fierce weapons."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Daytime damage increased from 1000 to 9999.
Can no longer be dodged via accessories when enraged during daytime.
The Paladin's Shield can no longer deflect any instant-kill damage from Skeletron Prime.
Fixed Prime Laser not firing properly.
Fixed Prime Cannon's bombs appearing in the wrong position after exploding in multiplayer.
Changed music track from Boss 1 to a new track exclusive to the boss fight, Skeletron Prime.
Desktop 1.4.1.2: Prime Cannon's Bombs will now explode on contact with Planter Boxes.
Desktop 1.4.1: Skeletron Prime is now vulnerable to Cursed Inferno.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Skeletron Prime AI overhaul: will now act similar to Skeletron and spin faster in Expert Mode.
Prime Cannon's Bombs now explode on platforms rather than going through them.
Added two Master Mode drops, Robotic Skull and Skeletron Prime Relic.
Desktop 1.3.5: Sprite updated. Old sprite was .
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Added an Expert Mode drop, Mechanical Battery Piece.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Increased health, damage and defense of most parts.
Now drops Skeletron Prime Mask.
Fixed bug where the player could defeat Skeletron Prime by destroying the Prime Cannon hand and not Skeletron Prime itself.
Desktop 1.2: 
Now has a chance to spawn naturally at dusk with the message: "The air is getting colder around you...".
Will now drop 20–40 Souls of Fright, instead of 20–30.
Now drops Hallowed Bars and Skeletron Prime Trophy.
Reduced health, damage and defense of all parts and head.
Desktop 1.1: Introduced.

Console 1.0.933.1: Added Expert mode drop, Mechanical Battery Piece. ()
Console 1.0.750.0: Added Expert mode drop, Mechanical Battery Piece. ()
Console-Release: Introduced.

Mobile 1.1.5536: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Guide:Crafting an Ankh Shield
content:
The Ankh Shield is a Hardmode accessory which grants immunity to knockback and all of the following debuffs:

It is crafted at a Tinkerer's Workshop by combining the Obsidian Shield and the Ankh Charm.
Although it is not necessary for game progression, it can be very useful for a variety of reasons. This guide will serve as a tutorial for gathering all the individual items used to craft the accessory.


== Crafting tree ==
In the table below, the top rows contain items you are likely to acquire first, and items below them are the result of crafting them. An item with no other item directly above it is acquired from the environment or from an enemy drop.


== General Tips ==

Due to the amount of farming required to obtain the Ankh Charm, it's recommended to use Water Candles and Battle Potions to increase enemy spawn rates. For surface enemies that drop immunity accessories, it's also good to farm them during Blood Moons, since their spawn rates will increase significantly as well. Note that this spawn rate increase only applies to the Surface layer.
It's also a good idea to find and build a good farming spot. For Underground enemies, a wide and open section of a cave can be used. It can also be good to build a 168×94 rectangle in order to concentrate all spawns in one area.

With the use of lava, traps, and minions and/or sentries it can be very simple to make an AFK farm for items. While AFK farms are by no means required, they can cut down time. If building AFK farms, it is also generally helpful to construct them in places that have enemies which drop items the player lacking in other departments; i.e, a dungeon AFK farm to obtain both a Nazar and Sniper Scope.
Enemy droprates can be improved by improving luck, which is a hidden player stat. See Luck § Influences for ways to improve luck.
Shimmer makes crafting the Ankh Charm considerably easier. Every base immunity accessory can be shimmered to get the other accessory it pairs with. Frequently, it may be a good idea to focus on obtaining a second copy of a common accessory rather than its paired accessory, due to tougher or rarer enemies/environments, or low drop chances. For example, enemies that drop Nazars are much rarer than Pixies, which drop Megaphones, so it is a lot more viable to obtain two Megaphones than it is to obtain two Nazars.
The Obsidian Shield, Bezoar and Nazar can be obtained before entering Hardmode. With the help of Shimmer, one can also obtain an Adhesive Bandage and Megaphone by shimmering a second Bezoar and Nazar, respectively. As a result, the Adhesive Bandage and Countercurse Mantra also become available before Hardmode.


== Ankh Shield ==


=== Ankh Charm ===
In order to craft the Ankh Shield the player needs an Ankh Charm and an Obsidian Shield. This section goes over the necessary Ankh Charm Ingredients.


== Armor Bracing ==


=== Armor Polish ===
The Armor Polish prevents the Broken Armor debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Armored Skeletons and Blue Armored Bones.
If farming for Armored Skeletons in a Cavern, then the Trifold Map may also be obtained from Giant Bats. While Blue Armored Bones spawn more commonly, they require the player to be in the Dungeon and for Plantera to be defeated.


=== Vitamins ===
The Vitamins prevent the Weak debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Corruptors and Floaty Grosses.
Farming in a Corruption biome is recommended, since the Corrupt Slimes and, if in a Desert, Dark Mummies will also drop the Blindfold and Megaphone. Furthermore, Corruptors spawn more frequently than Floaty Grosses, which lead to more efficiency.


== Medicated Bandage ==


=== Bezoar ===

The Bezoar prevents the Poisoned debuff. is a 1% / 2% drop from Toxic Sludge, Hornets and Moss Hornets.
It's better to farm for it in pre-Hardmode, due to the high spawn rate of Hornets and the lack of the stronger enemies found in Hardmode. Obtaining two allows the player to shimmer one of them into the Adhesive Bandage (See below).


=== Adhesive Bandage ===
The Adhesive Bandage prevents the Bleeding debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Werewolves, Angler Fish and, once Plantera has been defeated, Rusty Armored Bones.
During a Full Moon, a significant amount of Werewolves spawn, making it easier to obtain the item.
Farming for a Bezoar in pre-hardmode is really easy, as the enemies deal much less damage and Hornets spawn more frequently. The player can then throw it into the shimmer to create a Medicated Bandage.


== The Plan ==


=== Fast Clock ===
The Fast Clock prevents the Slow debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from regular Mummies, Wraiths and Pixies.
Pixies appear in a Hallow biome, Wraiths can be found at night or after smashing an Altar, whilst Mummies appear in a normal Hardmode Desert.
The fast clock is relatively easy to obtain, due to all its sources being rather common enemies. Pixies spawn in large amounts in the Hallow, Wraiths are common at night and more so during a Blood Moon, and Mummies being easy to find in a Desert biome. Obtaining two allows the player to shimmer one into a Trifold Map.


=== Trifold Map ===
The Trifold Map prevents the Confused. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Clowns, Light Mummies and Giant Bats. Trying to look for Clowns is not recommended, as they are rare enemies that only spawn during a Hardmode Blood Moon. Light Mummies are found in a Hallowed Desert, while Giant Bats appear in the Cavern layer during Hardmode.
Obtaining a Trifold Map is a little harder than shimmering a Fast Clock, only because the enemies that drop it are harder to quickly find. Light Mummies can only spawn on Pearlsand, which may be harder to find than regular Sand. Clowns are a rare and dangerous spawn in Blood Moons. Giant Bats are common in the Caverns, but there are more dangers threats other than the Giant Bats, such as Skeleton Archers.


== Countercurse Mantra ==


=== Nazar ===
The Nazar prevents the Cursed debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Cursed Skulls, Cursed Hammers, Crimson Axes, Enchanted Swords, and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Giant Cursed Skulls.
Due to Cursed Hammers, Crimson Axes, and Enchanted Swords being rare, it's much easier to obtain the item from Cursed Skulls or Giant Cursed Skulls in the Dungeon. Due to the increased variety and difficulty enemies in the hardmode Dungeon, it is faster to farm for it before defeating Plantera.
It may be easier to farm for a Megaphone to shimmer into a Nazar, due to the more common spawns of those enemies.


=== Megaphone ===
The Megaphone prevents the Silenced debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Pixies, Green Jellyfish, Dark Mummies and Blood Mummies.
Infecting a Desert with the Corruption or Crimson will make obtaining the Megaphone, Vitamins and the Blindfold easier. If one doesn't want to infect their Desert, they can farm for Pixies in the Surface Hallow.


== Blindfold(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) / Reflective Shades(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) ==


=== Blindfold ===
The Blindfold prevents the Darkness debuff. It is a 1% / 2% drop from Corrupt Slimes, Slimelings, Crimslimes, Dark Mummies, and Blood Mummies. Dark Mummies can be found in Corrupt Deserts and Blood Mummies can be found in Crimson Deserts.
For efficient Blindfold Farming, corrupting a Surface Desert will spawn both enemies: Corrupt Slimes and Dark Mummies. Corrupt Slimes split into 3 Slimelings when killed, and all yield a 1% / 2% chance of dropping a Blindfold, effectively increasing efficiency by 4-fold.
A similar strategy can be used in a Crimson world due to the presence of Crimslimes and Blood Mummies, however Crimslimes will not split resulting in a lower chance of obtaining a Blindfold, and Blood Mummies only exist on  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version.
If one is in a Crimson world and are farming the Mummies for the Blindfold, it is not recommended to farm during a Sandstorm as this will severely decrease the chance of getting Dark/Blood Mummies to spawn.


=== Pocket Mirror(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) ===
The Pocket Mirror prevents the Stoned(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) debuff. It is a 2.5% / 5% drop from Medusa. Medusa is found in the Marble Caves once Hardmode is activated.
It is worth mentioning that only one Medusa can be active at a time, so AFK farms will be less efficient.
It may be smart to obtain two Blindfolds and toss one in Shimmer, as those tend to be easier to obtain.


== Obsidian Shield ==
The Obsidian Shield is the other ingredient for the Ankh Shield, this section will go over the Obsidian Shield ingredients.


=== Cobalt Shield ===
The Cobalt Shield prevents Knockback. It is found in the locked chests in the Dungeon. By the time the player gets the Nazar they should already have the Cobalt Shield.


=== Obsidian Skull ===
The Obsidian Skull prevents the Burning debuff. It is crafted using 20 obsidian at a Furnace.

title: Midas
content:
Midas is a Hardmode debuff that causes affected enemies to drop 30-50% more coins than usual on death. Entities affected by Midas debuff will also glow golden.


== Causes ==


=== From player ===


== Notes ==
Midas only increases the direct coin drops from enemies, and does not affect the coins dropped from grab bag items such as Treasure Bags.
This means it will not have any actual effect on most bosses that drop a Treasure Bag in Expert Mode, due to all of their coin drops being moved to the Treasure Bag. The exception to this is the Eater of Worlds, as its indivdiual segments still drop coins upon death, in addition to the coin drops from its Treasure Bag.
For enemies that picked up coins in Expert Mode, Midas will only increase the enemy's own coin drops and not the coins that it had picked up.
Midas has no effect on coin drops from the unique effects of Lucky Coin and Classy Cane.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Trivia ==
Midas is the name of a king in Greek mythology who was rewarded by Dionysus with the ability to turn anything that he touched into gold.
The debuff icon displays an item that looks similar to the Lucky Coin, which functions in a similar manner to the debuff when equipped. The main difference is that the Lucky Coin gives a chance for enemies to drop extra coins when damaged, not when slain.

Desktop 1.2: Introduced.

title: Spelunker Potion
content:
The Spelunker Potion is a buff potion which grants the Spelunker buff when consumed. The buff illuminates valuable objects on the screen and highlights them with a yellow tint. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Spelunker Potions can also be found in Pots, Chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
The Spelunker buff highlights the following tiles:


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Highlight colors ==
Ore and other treasures are displayed with a yellow tint, which somewhat alters the color of the highlighted treasure. For instance, Cobalt is displayed turquoise and Orichalcum red.

		
		
		
		
		
		
		


== Notes ==
The sparkling effect appears to be greatest with the "Retro" lighting mode.


== Tips ==
The Metal Detector informs the player of the most valuable treasure if there is any nearby, which can help determine whether it is worth finding and spending a Spelunker Potion.
The effect of the Spelunker Glowstick is similar to that of a Spelunker Potion, but the potion has the advantage of pinpointing the exact location of treasures within the player's screen, unlike the Spelunker Glowstick, which places sparkles over a treasure's general location and requires that it be held or thrown for the effect to activate.


== History ==

Now highlights statues and paintings.

title: Betsy's Wrath
content:
Betsy's Wrath is a Hardmode, post-Golem wand that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When used, it fires three fireballs that travel in arcs. The fireballs explode upon impact with an enemy or a block and inflict the Betsy's Curse debuff, which adds 40 armor penetration against affected entities for 10 seconds.
Its best modifier is Mythical.


== Notes ==
Internally, Betsy's Wrath has a reuseDelay of 10, adding a cooldown of 10 ticks (0.17 seconds) after each use.
The Betsy's Wrath's actual total use time is reduced by 2 ticks, because it has the autouse attribute and its reuseDelay is not 0. The final calculation does not add 1 tick to negate the animation skip feature that applies to useAnimation or reuseDelay.
The explosion covers an 8.75×8.75-tile square area centered on the Betsy's Wrath projectile.
The Betsy's Curse debuff cannot be inflicted against other players in PvP.
Betsy's Wrath can be considered an upgrade to the Golden Shower. Ichor also stacks with Betsy's Curse, for a total of 55 armor penetration.
Betsy herself is not immune to the debuff.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Trivia ==
Like the other Old One's Army weapons, Betsy's Wrath is a direct reference to the weapon of the same name in Dungeon Defenders 2, due to its implementation as part of a crossover event.


== See also ==
Betsy's Wrath at the Dungeon Defenders 2 Wiki


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.1.2: Damage reduced from 110 to 100.
Desktop 1.4.1: Damage increased from 65 to 110.
Desktop 1.3.4: Introduced.

title: Guide:The Torch God strategies
content:
The Torch God is an event that begins once at least 101 Torches of any type are placed in close proximity below the Surface layer in any biome.
It is unique in that instead of having one huge boss or several special enemies to kill like other events, it is more of a mobility and/or endurance test in comparison. The only enemies you need to worry about are unrelated Underground and Cavern layer enemies spawning in the middle of the event area.


== Preparation ==


=== Terrain preparation ===
Find a decently large space underground in order to save time, then carefully use Bombs or Dynamite to create the general shape of your arena. Any holes made by the explosives can be covered up later, and any small bumps can be mined using your pickaxe. Having an open space to move around is useful for this event.
Once you're done carving out the arena, you can start placing Rope and/or Platforms so you can circle around the flames more easily. Keep in mind that your character briefly loses vertical momentum as they descend on multiple platforms, so less can be more.
Finally, place your Torches around the outside of your arena. You can also place down a few tiny rows of random blocks for them near the arena, as if you wish to remove them later, having the Torches more spread out can make it take a bit of extra time. The event will start shortly after you have at least 101 of them nearby, so get ready to run towards the arena to avoid taking any unnecessary damage. A grappling hook can also be used here.
Different Torches have different flame colors. While the flames of Crimson Torches are almost impossible to see, Ultrabright Torches and White Torches will give you an easier time spotting them as they have very bright flames.


=== Gearing up ===


==== Armor ====
It is recommended to have around 200 health at the very least.

An Ultrabright Helmet can be used for greatly increased vision. It is worth noting that it only provides 4 defense, however.
Gold armor/Platinum armor are good options for the amount of defense they give (up to 16 and 20 respectively).
Shadow armor provides up to 19 defense and its set bonus will grant increased movement speed and acceleration. Crimson armor gives the same amount of defense and is also a good choice.
Gladiator armor grants the same amount of defense as Gold armor and its set bonus prevents knockback.


==== Accessories ====
The Frog Leg not only increases jump speed, but also grants auto-jump, letting you hold ↷ Jump to jump repeatedly. If you have a tall enough arena that you start taking fall damage, the Frog Leg will also slightly increase your maximum safe falling distance.
If your world is in Expert Mode or higher, items like the Shield of Cthulhu and Brain of Confusion can stop damage altogether with immunity frames and dodges respectively.
The Royal Gel allows you to ignore random Slime spawns, and the Worm Scarf reduces any damage taken.
Running boots, like the Hermes Boots or Flurry Boots, are a huge help when it comes to mobility. This also applies to their upgrades.
Extra jump accessories such as the Cloud in a Bottle or Sandstorm in a Bottle are helpful for dodging.
The Shiny Red Balloon increases jump height and jump speed. It can be combined with most of the extra jump accessories (except for the Tsunami in a Bottle) mentioned above to free up an accessory slot.
The Lucky Horseshoe will prevent fall damage if you have a tall arena. Additionally, if you have already combined an extra jump bottle with a Shiny Red Balloon, the result can be further combined with the Lucky Horseshoe to create the respective Horseshoe balloon.
The Magiluminescence increases movement speed and acceleration. It also provides some light.
The Panic Necklace briefly increases your movement speed if you take damage, which can come in handy if you're in a pinch.
If you have the Goblin Tinkerer, accessories can be reforged to have defense-increasing modifiers, but this is not necessary.


==== Mounts ====
The Chillet(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can dash through the flames. This is particularly convenient if a platform is built far above or below the torches, allowing for horizontal dodging.
The Slime Mount is also useful for dodging the flames.


==== Hooks ====
Any grappling hook will help with dodging the flames, but the Ivy Whip, Fish Hook and Slime Hook are particularly great options.
Most of the Gem Hooks (from "worst" to best: Amethyst, Topaz, Sapphire, Emerald, Ruby, Amber and Diamond) are also good options if you are lucky and find enough of the respective gem (or farm for them using the respective Gemcorn) to make them.
The Amethyst Hook is acceptable, but has the same reach as the default Grappling Hook.


==== Potions ====
Using Calming Potions will stop extra enemies from spawning, allowing you to focus more on dodging.
Vision-increasing potions like the Night Owl Potion make the projectiles easier to spot.
The Ironskin Potion will reduce the damage taken from getting hit by a flame.
Food buffs (Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied and Exquisitely Stuffed) grant you defense and movement speed bonuses. They also allow life regeneration to be fully effective in Expert Mode and higher difficulties.
Swiftness Potions increase mobility and facilitate easier dodging.


== Tips ==
Since Campfires do not count as Torches for the event, they can be placed around the arena to provide light and increase life regeneration. The Torch rule also applies to Glowsticks and furniture such as lanterns and chandeliers.
Enabling Autopause will be helpful to dodge the fireballs easily by planning your next move every time you open your inventory.
Once the Dryad has moved in, you can buy Grass Seeds and Sunflowers from her to plant the latter underground, which will decrease enemy spawn rates and give you a slight movement speed boost.
The Torch God will not harm town NPCs, so placing the Nurse in a house near the event area negates the need to dodge the projectiles at all, so long as you have the money along with any grappling hook in order to prevent knockback.
Peace Candles also do not count as Torches and lower enemy spawn rates.
Regardless of your preferred class, minions (like the Finch, Flinx and Vampire Frog) can deal with random enemy spawns without your input.


== Alternative strategies ==


=== Minecart Track strategy ===
Another effective way to dodge the fireballs is to create a loop of Minecart Tracks around a wall of Torches in the middle.
The general shape of the loop is up to you, as it can be a diamond, a hexagon or almost whichever shape you like. The final tiles on both sides of the loop can also be hammered to have bumpers on them, which will make your minecart reverse its direction. You can make the shape bigger or taller to be on the safer side.
Test out the track to see if there are any errors with the design before starting the event.


=== Going in a single direction ===
Similar to the Minecart Track strategy, the flame projectiles can be easily avoided by placing all the Torches in the center of a large, open arena.
Prepare the desired space underground, then start moving in one direction (near the edges) during the event. Taking some measures to lower enemy spawn rates and make them easier to deal with may be needed here.

title: Pylons
content:
Pylons are placeable furniture items that appear as a large crystal hovering and rotating above a biome-themed stand. With two or more pylons placed in the world, the player can teleport from one pylon to another one. The system they form is referred to as the Pylon Network.
When the player is near a pylon, they can teleport to another pylon by doing any of the following:

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the pylon, which opens the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.
Pressing Toggle Full Map to open the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.
 Selecting another pylon on the overlay-mode or portrait-mode minimap.
The following conditions must be met by both the pylon near the player and the target pylon (with the exception of the Universal Pylon):

There must be two or more housed NPCs (including the Old Man and town pets) within a rectangular area of 169×124 tiles centered on each of the two pylons.
More precisely, the home tile of the NPC (Dungeon point in the case of the Old Man) must be within this rectangle, and the NPC must be less than 100 tiles away from their home tile.
The pylons must be placed in their respective biome.
Moreover, the following restrictions apply to all pylons (including the Universal Pylon):

Only one of each type of pylon may be placed in a world.
Pylons can only function when the minimap is enabled in the settings.
The player must be within a rectangular area of 61×62 tiles centered on the pylon.


== Types ==


== Crafting ==


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Status messages ==
The following status messages are displayed when pylons are not properly used:

No special status message will be displayed if the player attempts to place a second pylon of the same type in a world. Instead, the pylon will simply not be able to be placed, and its Placement Preview will be fully red.


== Notes ==
 
Most Pylons emit faint light of their respective color when placed. Universal, Aether, and Underworld Pylons only have a fully bright crystal when placed.
When purchasing most pylons (except the Universal Pylon) from an NPC, the following restrictions apply:
The NPC must be a "vendor" that normally sells items, other than the Tavernkeep, the Traveling Merchant, and the Skeleton Merchant:
There must be another NPC near the vendor NPC.
The player must not be in an evil biome (Corruption or Crimson).
As with all biome-specific vendor items, NPCs sell pylons based on the biome the player is in, not the biome the NPC is in.
Similarly, pylons function based on the biome the pylon is in, not the biome the NPCs allowing it to function are in.
A hybrid biome can result in multiple pylons appearing in an NPC's inventory, except the Forest and Cavern Pylons, which are mutually exclusive and only available when the player is not in a Snow, Desert, Ocean, Jungle, Hallow, or Glowing Mushroom biome.
It is not strictly necessary to select a different pylon for teleportation. The player can select the same pylon that is already in their vicinity in order to teleport to that pylon, allowing small jumps from anywhere within a pylon's 60-tile radius.
It is possible to purchase a pylon without placing it down. Therefore, it can be worthwhile to move an NPC into a location long enough to buy the pylon, then move them out to a preferred location.
The Universal Pylon is a post-Moon Lord item, since obtaining it requires a full Bestiary, which includes having to defeat the Moon Lord.
The hovering crystals cannot be painted, since they are not part of the actual tile internally, but rather merely graphics placed on top of it. The actual tile of a pylon only consists of its stand, which can be painted.


== Tips ==
Pylons can be used during the Lunar Events to traverse the world to combat the various pillars, allowing the player to choose the order they want to fight each pillar more easily.
The Pylon Network can also be supplemented by several other forms of teleportation or transportation:
Each player can use a Recall Potion or Magic Mirror or its upgrades to teleport to their own spawn point.
The Shellphone and Magic Conch give access to both Oceans.
The Shellphone and Demon Conch give access to the center of the Underworld (it may be necessary to build a platform there, especially in drunk worlds).
Each pylon plus the three Shellphone landing points can be used as the hub of local rail networks. Once the Mechanic is rescued, they can also be used as Teleporter hubs.
Since the area that the Cavern Pylon can be used in is very large, there are several possible use cases for it:
Creating a Cavern Pylon town immediately outside the Dungeon has many benefits, the most obvious being near-instant access to a deeper part of the Dungeon once Skeletron is defeated.
It is still possible to build a town prior to defeating Skeletron, as the Dungeon Guardian will not spawn unless a player is actually inside the Dungeon (more specifically, when the player is in front of unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls).
Since the Dungeon is right next to the Ocean, this means both Oceans can be conveniently accessed, so long as the Ocean Pylon is at the opposite Ocean from the Dungeon.
If there are at least three NPCs, part of the Dungeon may be considered part of the town instead. While it is not likely to be a large part, it can provide a relatively safe place to deal with enemies without more immediately spawning. (Note that this effect is provided by the town, which does not require a pylon.)
Later in the game, the player will not have to worry about accidentally triggering a battle with the Lunatic Cultist, as it is more likely they enter the Dungeon via their own entrance than the naturally-spawned one.
Aside from the practical benefits, it also provides unique scenery for both the town and the Dungeon.
This setup is not recommended in multiplayer games, where a player in the Dungeon can potentially cause Dungeon enemies to spawn within range to teleport to or attack players in the town.
Alternately, building the Cavern Pylon at the top of the Underground layer near the player's main base may be convenient, especially in multiplayer or when all players have some form of Magic Mirror. This allows the player to convert their base area to The Hallow without reshuffling pylons, if desired. A Dungeon town can then use the pylon of whatever surface biome it is located in, often Forest, allowing quicker access to the Ocean but still quick access to the Dungeon.
Another use for the Cavern Pylon is to put it in or near the Underworld, providing a viable alternative to a conventional Hellevator in the earlier stages of the game. Once players can comfortably defend themselves, creating a town inside the Underworld allows purchasing of an Underworld Pylon, freeing the Cavern Pylon for other uses.
 When the overlay-mode minimap is opened, the player can place down wires by holding the Grand Design and clicking a pylon icon on the map when near another pylon. This will immediately place down a line of wire from the tile overlapping with the map icon to the tile at the same location on screen at the destination pylon.
The Universal Pylon uniquely works anywhere, and perhaps more usefully, does not require NPCs nearby. It can effectively be a free infinite-use Potion of Return for a player carrying it.
A third-party world-editing program can be used to circumvent the one-of-each-pylon rule. Additional pylons will function normally, as long as enough NPCs are present.


== Trivia ==
While pylons will still hover and rotate when the game is paused, they will only hover when the game is "tabbed out".
Pylons resemble the building of the same name constructed by the alien race protoss in the 1998 military science fiction real-time strategy game StarCraft.
This is also referenced in the Universal Pylon's tooltip.
Pylons can be used when the game is paused if accessed through the minimap.
The crystal of the Forest Pylon appears in the 2016 simulation role-playing video game Stardew Valley as the Far Away Stone, as part of a crossover.
Prior to 1.4.5.0, pylons cannot be used when any boss or hostile event is present. The status message "Defeat the current threat before you can use the pylon network!" is shown when attempting to use pylons in this condition.
Additionally, the Cavern Pylon could be used in both the Aether and the Underworld, but only one could be used at a time due to the biome sharing the Cavern classification.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.4: The Tavernkeep no longer sells pylons at all in order to accommodate his fully-stocked shop.
Desktop 1.4.5.3: Pylons no longer attract lightning.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Added Underworld and Aether Pylons.
The minimum required happiness for NPCs to sell pylons has been removed entirely.
Removed the restriction of pylons being unusable when any non-event boss or Martian Probe exists in the world, or during the following events: Frost Moon, Pumpkin Moon, Old One's Army, and any invasion. They can now be used under these circumstances.
Added a network visual effect that connects all pylons on the map when interacting with a pylon to open the fullscreen map.
Pylons now take priority over Wormhole Potions when clicking on either to teleport on the map.
The status messages about nearby NPCs now clarify that NPCs need to live near the pylons, not just be located near them:
"There are not enough villagers near that pylon to access it" changed to "There are not enough villagers living near that pylon to access it";
"There are not enough villagers near the current pylon" changed to "There are not enough villagers living near the current pylon".
Changed status message about pylon being in front of unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Walls from "Ancient forces prevent you from accessing this location . . ." to "Ancient forces prevent you from accessing this location..." (changed to use a proper ellipsis).
Fixed a multiplayer crash related with pylons.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Increased the maximum range where pylons are usable from (it should be impossible to be in range of opening a pylon and not be able to teleport with it).
Can be used during Moon Lord's summoning sequence.
Desktop 1.4.3.3: 
Pylons now require a minimum of two NPCs under all conditions to be sold.
The minimum required happiness for NPCs to sell pylons has been decreased from 0.85 to 0.9 (i.e. the required price modifier changed from 85% to 90%). This means that it is now easier to make NPCs happy enough to sell a pylon.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Fixed an issue where pylon NPC detection only checked for the housing flag, and not the actual NPCs being present near their home.
Now works during the Lunar Events.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: 
Fixed a bug where the Ocean Pylon could be sold underground despite it not working there.
The Tavernkeep no longer sells pylons when his shop inventory is full, i.e. after Golem has been defeated.
The Forest Pylon can now be used in the sky as well.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced with changes up to Desktop 1.4.0.5.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced with changes up to Desktop 1.4.0.5.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced with changes up to Desktop 1.4.0.5.

title: Lava
content:
Lava is a glowing red-orange liquid found deep in the Cavern layer and throughout The Underworld, appearing instead of water at depths below approximately 950 feet (475 tiles) in a small world, 1,450 feet (725 tiles) in a medium world, or 1,950 feet (975 tiles) in a large world (on average). Tiny pools can frequently be found on the outskirts of the Underground Desert(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as well, even as high as 200 feet below the surface.
Contact with lava deals damage (which is not affected by damage variance) and inflicts the On Fire! debuff. Players take 80 damage and the debuff lasts for 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds, whereas enemies, NPCs, and critters take 50 damage and the debuff lasts for 7 seconds. Various items make the player immune to this damage, such as the Lava Charm and its derivatives. Lava also slows movement of entities submerged in it, similarly to water.
Lava flows downwards and horizontally, settling and taking the shape of any block formations below and beside it, the way water does. Lava flows slower than water. After flowing 50 tiles in a direction, lava will begin to evaporate, causing the source to be lost. Unlike water, the color of lava does not depend on the biome the player is in. It also emits a medium amount of flickering light. Lava is opaque, hiding objects, drops, enemies, and players.
Most dropped items of  rarity (which includes all coins) and all of  rarity will be destroyed when submerged in lava past their vertical midpoint. Furthermore, most trees and most types of placed furniture and platforms are destroyed upon contact with lava (with exceptions). Blocks cannot be placed directly within lava, but falling blocks like silt and sand can fall into it, resulting in placement at its bottom. Lava can be moved by the player via a bucket or pump.
In addition to naturally generated lava, it may be produced in a few other ways. Hellstone produces half a block's volume of lava when mined in the Underworld (a full block's volume in Expert Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)). Lava Slimes create a small amount of lava when slain in Expert Mode (except in worlds with the Remix(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) special world seed active). In worlds that combine the Remix and For the Worthy/Skyblock seeds, Hellbats and Lava Bats create a small amount of lava when slain.


== Crafting ==

Like water and honey, lava can be used as a minor crafting station. It works just like those two; in order to use it the player only has to stand nearby. Creation of items from a body of lava does not lower the lava level at all.


=== Used to craft ===

Lava can also be used to make the following items, though not as a crafting station:


== Fishing ==

Fishing in lava requires the use of the Hotline Fishing Hook, Lavaproof Fishing Hook(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrade, or (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) bait found in the Underworld. It is not possible to get other catches normally obtained in water.


== Notes ==

Contact with lava dislodges many placed furniture items and most kinds of platforms. Many placed items are not dislodged by lava, including but not limited to:
Gem Trees, Vanity Trees
Obsidian Platform, Stone Platform, Ash Wood Platform, Planter Boxes
Most Obsidian furniture, Ash Wood furniture
Excluding Lanterns
Web Rope, Silk Rope, Streamers, Chain
Metal bars, Coins
Pressure Plates, Timers, Lever, Switch, Detonator
Pumps, Explosives, Geyser
Most Statues, Vases
Excluding Boulder Statue, Bast Statue
Gems
Underworld Pots
Altars/Replica Altars, Lihzahrd Altar
Potted Lava Plants, Seaweed Planter
Some Crafting stations:
Tinkerer's Workshop
Hellforge, Adamantite Forge/Titanium Forge
Mythril Anvil/Orichalcum Anvil
Water fountains
Demon Altar/Crimson Altar
Christmas lights
Void Vault, Chests, Barrel, Trash Can, Dressers
Hat Rack, Target Dummy, Mannequin/Womannequin
Clay Pot
Critters
Trap Door (closed), Tall Gate (closed)
Monoliths
Relics
Pylons
Some Boulders
Kites
Shadow Orb/Crimson Heart
Replica Shadow Orb/Replica Crimson Heart are dislodged by lava
Tombstones
The following  rarity items are not destroyed by lava.

The exact depth at which lava will begin replacing all water in a world is different for every world and can vary by up to several hundred feet/tiles between worlds; the approximate depths given above are only averages.
The damage from lava can be reduced by defense and damage reduction. Apart from that, the following items allow for reducing or eliminating lava damage:
Obsidian Skin Potion: Grants a buff when consumed which provides lava immunity for its entire duration.
Superheated Blood(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions): Summons a Lava Shark Mount, which provides unlimited lava immunity, as well as fast movement in liquids.
Obsidian Roseand its upgrades: Reduces the base damage taken from lava from 80 to (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 35 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 50 and halves the duration of the inflicted On Fire! debuff from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds.
Ash Wood armor(set bonus)(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions): Halves the base damage taken from lava from 80 to 40 and halves the duration of the inflicted On Fire! debuff from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds.
Equipping both Ash Wood armor and the Obsidian Rose (or its upgrades) provides unlimited lava immunity.
In this case, lava immunity time from the following items will still be consumed.
Various accessories and one type of minecart allow the player to be submerged in lava for some time without taking damage. This immunity is similar to the breath meter while underwater, but it has its own separate bar, is immediately activated upon touching lava, and takes much longer to refill than the breath meter after exiting lava. Each of these items grants 7 seconds of immunity. If multiple of these items are equipped/used simultaneously, the duration of immunity will be stacked, up to a maximum of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 49 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 14 seconds if all of them are used.

The Flipper (and its upgrades), Flipper Potion, and Water Walking Potion have effect on all liquids, including lava.
Players cannot drown in lava, unlike water and honey.
Flying enemies rarely enter lava, but walking enemies will walk into it.
Rain does not turn lava into Obsidian.
The presence of lava prevents grass from spreading to dirt within an approximate two-tile radius.
Occasional lava "drips" from the ceiling are a special effect, which cause no damage. The player can create them with a Magic Lava Dropper(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Lava flowing from a lavafall (flowing over a half-block like a waterfall) is also harmless.
Some entities will not take any damage from contact with lava, including:
Enemies and critters native to The Underworld.
Bosses (except King Slime and Golem).
Entities that can pass through solid blocks (e.g., worms, Snatchers, Biome Mimics during their "pound" attack, etc.).
Tax Collector(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Invincible entities (e.g., True Eye of Cthulhu, Granite Golem during its shield state).
The Beach Ball bounces off of lava.


== Tips ==
Bottomless Lava Bucket, Lava Bombs, and Lava Rockets create lava.
Lava Absorbant Sponge, Ultra Absorbant Sponge, Dry Bombs, and Dry Rockets remove lava.
Silt and Sand Blocks can be stacked until reaching the lava's surface to form a safe bridge over it. They will revert back to lava if mined away, unless exiting the world and re-entering it.
A shallow lava pit underneath a structure will damage all walking enemies as they attempt to jump towards the player in the structure, and, if shallow enough, will gather their drops in one location for easy collection later. One can also use this technique to upgrade regular pits. Standing underneath the pit will lure most enemies toward the player, with even some flying enemies diving into the lava.


=== Lava depth ===
Lava will destroy any item of  and  rarity (other than the aforementioned exceptions) including coins, if it is deep enough for the item to sink past its midpoint. As a result, items with larger sprites can survive deeper lava. This allows making pits with lava just deep enough to burn Copper Coins, but (almost) nothing else. To check if a lava moat has the exact depth required, a player can throw in a Copper Coin and a Silver Coin. The Copper Coin should burn, but the slightly taller Silver Coin should not.
In practice, this lava depth can be achieved with 1 Bucket of lava for each 6 to 8 tiles of pit length.

Thus a moat that is 6–8 tiles wide should have one bucket thrown in, while a moat of 12–16 should have 2.
This implies avoiding lengths where this range cannot be achieved: 1–5, 9–11, 17. A moat 18 or more tiles long can always be filled to proper depth.
When filling a very large moat, it is best to drop individual lava buckets over the width of the moat, and not throw it on the same spot, due to unreliable liquid physics.
If too many items (over 400) accumulate in the world, the oldest ones will despawn. Copper Coins are among the least valuable objects in the game, but each stack of them still counts as an item. An event or enemy farm can produce huge numbers of Copper Coins, so it is worth discarding them, against the risk of despawning more valuable items. Fortunately they are also among the smallest items in the game (with their sprite being 10 pixels high).

A notable exception: The far more valuable Lihzahrd Power Cell also has a height of 10 pixels, and will be destroyed with the Copper Coins.
Other notable heights: Silver Coins and Gel share a 12-pixel height, while block items are 12 pixels tall.


== Trivia ==
In the real world, lava is molten rock, but the term is usually applied only when it is expelled above ground as the result of a volcanic eruption. Lava, as found underground in Terraria, would typically be termed as magma instead.
Dying from lava will display one of the following unique death messages:
“<Player name> got melted.”
“<Player name> was incinerated.”
“<Player name> tried to swim in lava.”
“<Player name> likes to play in magma.”
“<Player name> is bad at the Floor Is Lava.”


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Items with a rarity of  are now destroyed when dropped in lava.
Desktop 1.3.4: Lava is dynamic and has a setting to be more or less dynamic.
Desktop 1.2.4: Now used to make Lavafall Block instead of Lavafall Wall.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Lava makes a bubbling noise when nearby.
Now functions as a crafting station.
Touching lava while in water will now properly put the On Fire! debuff out when leaving lava.
Desktop 1.2: 
When lava touches a half block, it will now create a lavafall.
Lava no longer activates the breath meter.
Desktop 1.1: Now exists as a secondary "layer" behind the placed blocks. Therefore can no longer be removed by dropping sand-like block in it. "Blocked" liquids now disappear only after restart of world.
Desktop 1.0.6: 
The lava's emitted light was reduced.
Now spawned when mining Hellstone.
Shallow lava can again hurt players and enemies.
Blocks can no longer be placed in lava.
Now causes the On Fire! debuff.
Desktop 1.0.5: 
Lava will remove grass (including Jungle grass, Mushroom grass, and Corruption) from Dirt and Mud blocks.
No longer destroys items with a blue rarity or higher.
Very shallow lava will not hurt players or enemies anymore.
Desktop-Release: Introduced.

Console-Release: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile-Release: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Guardian Golem
content:
The Guardian Golem is a Hardmode, post-Golem light pet-summoning item that spawns a Toy Golem light pet upon being used or equipped. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Toy Golem emits a rocket exhaust to catch up to them. The Guardian Golem has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Golem in Master Mode.


== Notes ==
The Glow Mask ID for the pet is 277.


== Trivia ==
The phrase in the Guardian Golem's tooltip,"'Power cells not included.'", is a nod to how most battery-powered toys in commercials and advertisements state a similar warning for "batteries not included", and alludes to how Golem is summoned with Lihzahrd Power Cells.
The buff's tooltip is a reference to the song "Living Doll" written by Lionel Bart for Cliff Richard and The Shadows (then still known as "the Drifters") in 1959. The original lyrics were: "Got myself a cryin', talkin', sleepin', walkin', livin' doll". The tooltip simply replaces "doll" with "idol", as Golem is the Lihzahrdian Idol.
When summoned, the Toy Golem will always attempt to position itself in front of the player. This is likely because it is meant to act as a guardian, hence the name of the item.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.
