title: Guide:The Constant
content:
The Constant is a secret world seed introduced in the 1.4.3 update. It borrows features from Don't Starve Together, including alternate shading, hunger and darkness mechanics, and slightly different world creation and drops.
Survival is difficult in the Constant, but this guide will help.


== Tips ==
By using explosives, the player can harvest Cacti without taking damage.
Spider Nests spawn on the surface in the Constant. Due to the high strength of the spiders, blocking them up is advised. They prove to be a strength in early Hardmode, as they make it easy to farm for spider-related summoning gear like the Spider Staff.
Many special drops are more common in this seed. Farming enemies in the Crimson or the Corruption can get you a Tentacle Spike, a great early melee weapon that does lingering damage to enemies. Similarly, the Bat Bat drops more often from bats.
In Hardmode, you can fight Pigrons to get the Ham Bat with a very high drop chance. This is an excellent weapon for exploration (not so much for bosses).
Many statues will spawn on the surface in this seed, which is useful for those looking for item farms or specialized statues.


== Hunger ==
This is the most challenging feature in this seed. Hunger begins as soon as you spawn, with the Peckish status lasting for five minutes while you search for food, followed by Hungry for another five minutes (which decreases defense, damage and melee speed), followed by Starving, which will kill you in less than a minute.
That means that you have about 11 minutes to find food after you spawn, or you will die.


=== Pre-Merchant ===
Your immediate needs may be satisfied by shaking trees (done by hitting them once with an axe). This will uncommonly drop a fruit item which will satisfy your hunger for 5 minutes. Any two fruit items can be combined with a Bottle at a Cooking Pot to produce Fruit Juice, which will last longer.
Another alternative, especially in easier worlds, is to kill several Eater of Souls or Crimson monsters, all of which drop Vertebra which can be crafted into Monster Lasagna at a cooking pot.
Unfortunately, you may die before reaching the point that you can craft a cooking pot. That's why finding the Merchant is essential.


=== The Merchant ===
The Merchant is the key to most food options. He arrives when you have at least 50 Silver in your possession (which can be obtained through killing slimes or breaking pots in surface caves). He significantly expands your food capabilities in three ways:

First, you can place him in the snow biome to sell Marshmallows for 1 Silver each, which can be cooked to form Cooked Marshmallows fairly cheaply.
Second, in any biome, you can purchase the Bug Net, which allows you to catch and cook critters at a cooking pot.
Third, the Bug Net allows you to catch bait for fishing.


=== Tea ===
After Skeletron is defeated, the Teapot can be crafted for essentially unlimited Teacups, requiring only sand to make bottles.


=== Fishing ===
This is perhaps the simplest way to assuage your hunger, especially since most players will be fishing anyway for the Angler quests.
Most of the common fish you catch (especially Bass) can be crafted into Cooked Fish at a Cooking Pot. Higher-quality fish like Flounder can be crafted at a workbench into Sashimi, while potion-quality fish like Specular Fish can be crafted into Seafood Dinner, a long-lasting food.
Bait can be easily found in the Jungle or by breaking rocks on the surface, releasing worms. Even before you find the Merchant, you can often find a Can Of Worms in a Living Tree.


=== Travelling Merchant ===
The Traveling Merchant often sells high-quality food items, making it worth visiting him when he pops into town.


=== Halloween and Christmas ===
During Halloween, Pumpkins grow all over the ground, which can be crafted using just a Furnace to make Pumpkin Pie. This makes Halloween an excellent time to play the Constant seed. 
Similarly, in Christmas enemies drop Presents which can contain a variety of food-based options. 


== Darkness ==
When in complete darkness, the player will be attacked for 50 damage at a time, resulting in a swift death. This can be alleviated on holding a torch as you walk or by placing numerous light-giving items. However, there are multiple problems with this, such as letting go to fight enemies. Darkness at night is much worse in this seed, too. There are a variety of options to deal with this.


=== Placed Torches ===
This will be your easiest option in the early game. However, Rain will put out Torches, Campfires and Tiki Torches eventually on the surface, which means you'll need to re-place them frequently. Crafted items made from rarer materials (like Lamps) will not be put out.


=== Shine Potions ===
Shine Potions are frequently found in surface chests, and are a great option for early cave exploration. They can be crafted by placing a Bottle on a Table and using the commonly-available Daybloom and Glowing Mushroom ingredients.


=== Armor and accessories ===
Several armor pieces and accessories will remove your need for light entirely:

The Mining Helmet can be purchased from the Merchant for 4 Gold or dropped from Undead Miners with a 1/20 (5%) chance.
The Jellyfish Necklace and its tinkers can provide light when in water, and drops from Jellyfish with a 1/100 (1%) chance.
The Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart can provide dim light. However, they can occasionally fall behind, making them a risky choice.
Magiluminescence, crafted from 12 Demonite Bars or Crimtane Bars and 4 Topaz, is an excllent, permanent light source that is easily available after defeating the Eye of Cthulhu (and sometimes before). It also increases your movement speed and is one of the few accessories to stack with the Hermes Boots, making this a great accessory for exploration and boss fights.
The Creeper Egg or Fairy Bell, both available after defeating one of the Mechanical bosses (specifically The Twins for the Fairy Bell), are permanent, bright Light Pets that will solve your light problems for the rest of the game. Further light pets are available later on.

title: King Slime
content:
King Slime is a pre-Hardmode boss. Fighting King Slime is not required for game progression, but his defeat may reward the player with useful items. Defeating him for the first time also causes the Nerdy Slime town pet to spawn from the boss.
While King Slime is alive, his exclusive music King Slime will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning and spawning ==


=== Manual ===
King Slime can be summoned by using the Slime Crown, in any biome at any time.


=== Random ===
King Slime has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of naturally spawning while the following conditions are met:

The potential spawn point is located in one of the outer lateral sixths of the map (the far left or far right).
The depth at its potential spawn point is above zero.
It is daytime.
King Slime is not currently alive in the world.
The player is not in a Graveyard biome.
There is no water or less than 1 tile of water above its potential spawn point.
There must be standard, green grass at its potential spawn point (off-screen; see NPC spawning)
If the spawn succeeds, King Slime will spawn in a random place around the player and not necessarily on this grass block.


=== Slime Rain ===

If 150 slimes are killed by players, NPCs, traps, lava, and/or summoned minions during the Slime Rain event, King Slime spawns. The following slimes will count toward this total as long as they are killed during the event: Baby Slime, Black Slime, Blue Slime, Green Slime, Jungle Slime, Pinky, Purple Slime, Red Slime, and Yellow Slime. Statue-spawned slimes are eligible as well. Defeating King Slime ends the event shortly after. If all players die, King Slime despawns, and the event continues for some time before ending on its own (between 9 and 15 in-game hours). If King Slime has already been defeated in a world, it only takes 75 slime kills to spawn him. If King Slime is summoned manually with the Slime Crown and then subsequently killed, while the Slime Rain is active, the event ends in the same way as if the player killed the King Slime that naturally spawns at the end of the event. This can be quite helpful for players in later stages of the game who want to get the Slime Rain event over with as quickly as possible.


=== Remix ===

In Remix worlds, killing a slime has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of spawning King Slime, provided the boss has not yet been defeated, is not already alive, and at least one player has more than 140 maximum health and more than 8 defense. Only the death of certain types of slime can trigger this: Baby Slime, Black Slime, Blue Slime, Green Slime, Jungle Slime, Pinky, Purple Slime, Red Slime, and Yellow Slime. Statue-spawned slimes are eligible as well. Slimes killed without the player dealing damage to them will not spawn King Slime.


== Behavior ==
King Slime attempts to deal contact damage to the player by hopping towards them, and additionally summons slimes to aid him in the fight. When unable to reach the player, he may teleport to their location.
As King Slime loses health, he will gradually shrink in size. King Slime starts with 125% size at 100% health remaining, and his size linearly decreases based on his health percentage, down to 75% at 0% health remaining.
If the player dies or gets more than 187.5 tiles away from King Slime, he will teleport to the bottom-right corner of the world and despawn in 0.17 seconds.


=== Jumping ===
King Slime continually jumps towards the player, cycling through a series of four jumps with varying heights:

Performs a normal jump, reaching a maximum height of 6.42 tiles. Once he lands, there is a cooldown of 1 second before his next jump.
Performs another normal jump with another cooldown of 1 second.
Performs a low jump, reaching a maximum height of 3.56 tiles. Once he lands, there is a cooldown of 1 second before his next jump.
Performs a high jump, reaching a maximum height of 17.2 tiles. Once he lands, there is a cooldown of 1.67 seconds before his next jump.
As King Slime loses health, the cooldown after his jumps decreases, allowing him to jump more frequently. Reaching certain health thresholds decreases the cooldown, as shown in the table below.


=== Teleporting ===
King Slime can teleport to the player under the following two circumstances:

The line of sight between King Slime and the player is obstructed by solid blocks.
The player's feet are more than 10 tiles below or above the top of King Slime's hitbox.
As soon as either of these conditions is met, a timer of 5 seconds starts ticking down. When it reaches 0, King Slime teleports to the player's location. If it reaches 0 while King Slime is jumping, the teleportation is delayed until he lands on the ground. Afterwards, the timer resets back to 5 seconds. The timer pauses when neither of the two conditions is met, but it is not reset, meaning it continues where it left off once either condition is met again.
In order to teleport to the player, King Slime tries to find a suitable target location with the following steps:

If the total distance between King Slime and the player is greater than 125 tiles, he will teleport directly on top of the player, even if they are midair.
Otherwise, he tries to find a valid block to teleport on that is 7–10 tiles (Chebyshev distance) away from the player's center.
A block is considered valid for teleporting if it is an unactuated solid block (including platforms, but not planter boxes), does not contain lava, and if the tile above it is not occupied by any unactuated, unsloped solid blocks (including platforms and planter boxes). Additionally, King Slime is required to have an unobstructed line of sight to the player after teleporting there.
If the previous step fails, then he tries to find a valid block to teleport on that is 2–6 tiles (Chebyshev distance) away from the player's center.
If all of the previous steps fail, then he will teleport directly on top of the player, even if they are midair.
Once the target location is chosen, King Slime stays still, disappears over the course of 1 second, and then reappears at the target location over the course of 0.5 seconds. His jump attack cycle is reset from the beginning after teleporting.


=== Spawning slimes ===
King Slime can spawn 1–3 Blue Slimes from his body upon taking damage, with each of these Blue Slimes having a 1/4 (25%) chance to be replaced by a Spiked Slime in Expert Mode. At the beginning of the fight, King Slime can spawn slimes upon taking any hit that brings him below 95% health. Afterwards, he needs to lose at least 5% of his maximum health (100 / 140 / 178 health) compared to his health at the last time he spawned slimes before he can spawn them again, with this process repeating until he dies. For example, bringing him to exactly 1,899 / 2,659 / 3,390 (95%) health causes him to spawn slimes for the first time, after which he will not spawn new slimes until brought to below 1,799 / 2,519 / 3,212 (90%) health.
As a result, King Slime has a maximum of 19 opportunities to spawn slimes, meaning 19–57 slimes in total, or 38 slimes on average. This number will be lower if any of King Slime's slime-spawning opportunities is skipped by reducing his health by more than 5% of his maximum health in a single hit.
Finally, King Slime additionally always spawns 4–7 Blue Slimes upon his defeat. These slimes will never be replaced by Spiked Slimes in Expert Mode.


== Aftermath ==
Defeating King Slime for the first time spawns Nerdy Slime.
The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
If Queen Slime has already been defeated, the Princess will begin selling Royal Romance.
The Demolitionist will begin to sell Freeze Bombs during Night if he was not already.
The Traveling Merchant will be able to sell the Gray Zapinator if he could not already.
The King Slime emote  is unlocked.


== Notes ==
Although being a large and resilient enemy, in addition to boss music playing during the fight, a map icon, and a boss health bar appearing, King Slime is often regarded as a "side-boss" or "mini-boss" (though there is no official word on this from the developers). He differs from other bosses in the following ways:
King Slime can be encountered regardless of the current level of game advancement.
He is the only boss alongside Golem that takes damage from lava.
He can spawn at random in a certain area of the world, which is similar to the spawning of regular enemies, rather than bosses.
The Blue Slimes spawned by King Slime cannot contain bonus drops, unlike the naturally spawned Blue Slimes.
King Slime can spawn partially inside of blocks due to his large size, making him unable to move unless through teleporting.
For King Slime's random spawning, the game internally checks if horizontal distance of King Slime's spawning location from the world spawn is greater than 1/3rd of the world width (1400 / 2133 / 2800 tiles in small / medium / large worlds, respectively). In normal world this only allows him to spawn in outer lateral sixths of world, but the spawning area can be different in special or secret world seeds that change the world spawn point, such as Celebration Mk 10 and How did I get here.
In worlds with the For the Worthy seed active, King Slime starts as twice as large (250% size) at 100% health. His horizontal speed during jumps is also increased in this seed, allowing him to cover more distance with jumps (low jumps: 23 mph → 31 mph, normal jumps: 20 mph → 32 mph, high jumps: 18 mph → 31 mph).


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Piercing weapons can not only damage King Slime, but also kill the additional slimes he spawns.
When King Slime is about to teleport, he shrinks, and his map icon will get closer to the ground. The latter can be used to know when he is about to return if he goes off-screen.
The Blue Slimes that are spawned during the fight can drop Hearts and Stars, which respectively restore 20 health and 100 mana.
Due to the high number of Blue Slimes spawned during the fight, summoning King Slime while in specific areas can be a quick, easy way to farm for specific drops. Examples include Biome Keys, Pirate Maps, Halloween and Christmas drops, or the Cascade, Hel-Fire, Amarok, and Yelets yoyos.
While Blue Slimes cannot drop Souls of Light or Souls of Night, they can be converted to Shimmer Slimes which can.
King Slime himself does not drop any Gel, but the Blue Slimes he spawns do. This makes fighting him a good way to farm Gel, e.g., for Flamethrower ammo or Asphalt Blocks.
Killing King Slime on Expert Mode and selling all drops gives 10 Gold on average.
When King Slime teleports, he can become stuck inside the blocks around him, preventing his movement for a while.


== Trivia ==
Because the Compass and Depth Meter reveal each tile to be 2 feet in length, King Slime would be about 14′ 4½″  (5.24 m) tall and 15′ 3″ (5.56 m) wide.
The source of the Ninja armor appears to be from the ninja inside King Slime.
According to Redigit, the trapped ninja is the Guide's brother, and he was consumed by King Slime as a result of losing the fight against the boss. This statement was most likely a joke and is not considered official lore.
The trophy dropped by King Slime seems to be a Ninjatō covered in slime, a common weapon that ninjas are usually shown to carry. This may be because King Slime drops the Ninja armor.
The images for the ninja inside King Slime and the crown are stored in separate image files. King Slime's sprite without them looks similar to a massive Blue Slime.
The sprite from 1.1 did not have the crown or the ninja.
Both sprites can be found as Ninja and Extra_39 internally.
Despite sometimes being considered the easiest boss in the game, he does the second highest damage of any pre-Hardmode boss, only beaten by the Wall of Flesh in Classic Mode or Skeletron in Expert Mode.
King Slime is one of the only bosses capable of spawning randomly even after he has already been defeated in the world, the other being Deerclops.
King Slime appears in the video game Core Keeper as part of a crossover.
When teleporting, King Slime drops his current crown and seemingly generates a new one upon completing the teleport.
The Spiked Slime, Pirate's Curse, Jungle Mimic, and Golden Slime are the only non-invincible enemies in the game without a Bestiary entry, and King Slime is the only boss whose summoned enemies do not have one.
 The Bestiary entry for  King Slime: "Slimes normally aren't intelligent, but occasionally they merge together to become a powerful force to swallow all things."


== Gallery ==

== History ==

Fixed King Slime potentially spawning item slime variants instead of normal Blue Slimes.
Fixed King Slime desyncing falling through platforms when hitting him in multiplayer.

Changed music track from Boss 1 to a new track exclusive to the boss fight, King Slime.

Now takes up more enemy slots, reducing or outright eliminating additional enemy spawns during his fight (not including Blue Slime minions). This does not impact Slime Rain spawns.
Defeating King Slime for the first time will now spawn the Nerdy Slime.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: Fixed an NPC smoothing issue.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Added the King Slime Relic, a trophy-like Master Mode-only drop.
Added the Royal Delight, a pet-summoning Master Mode-only drop.
Fixed an exploit where King Slime's minions would drop Soul of Light or Soul of Night when underground.
King Slime is now somewhat harder to abuse with Ropes.

title: Guide:Quickly acquiring town NPCs
content:
This guide explains ways to get NPCs the quickest. See NPCs for a more detailed description of each NPC. All NPCs require an available vacant house to move in.


== Pre-Hardmode ==
The NPCs you can get in Pre-Hardmode are:

Guide, who is the starting NPC
Merchant, who requires the players in the world to collectively have 50
Nurse, who requires The Merchant and a player to have greater than 100 health
Demolitionist, who requires The Merchant and a player to have an explosive in their inventory
Dye Trader(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), who requires at least 4 other town NPCs in the world and a player to any dye-related item in their inventory
Angler, who you rescue as the Sleeping Angler in the Ocean biome
Zoologist(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), who requires at least 10% completion of the Bestiary
Dryad, who requires The Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu, or Skeletron to have been defeated
Painter, who requires at least 8 other town NPCs in the world
Golfer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), who you rescue as the Golfer Rescue(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in the Underground Desert biome
The Arms Dealer, who requires a player to have bullets or a bullet-shooting gun in their inventory
Tavernkeep(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), who you rescue as the Unconscious Man(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) after the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu has been defeated
Stylist(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), who you rescue as the Webbed Stylist(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) in a Spider Nest
Goblin Tinkerer, who you rescue as the Bound Goblin in the Cavern layer after a Goblin Army has been defeated
Witch Doctor, who requires Queen Bee to have been defeated
Clothier, who requires Skeletron to have been defeated
Mechanic, who you rescue as the Bound Mechanic in the Dungeon
Party Girl, who has a 1/40 chance to spawn every 2 minutes after 20 other town NPCs are in the world
Make 18 houses.
Start mining ore Underground and in the Caverns. While doing so, mine around Spider Nests to check for the Stylist, look for dye plants, and kill enemies to earn money. Also check for Life Crystals, and loot chests for explosives, bullets, and bullet-shooting guns. NPCs acquired - Merchant, Nurse, Demolitionist, Dye Trader, Arms Dealer, and Stylist.
Once you are ready, fight the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu, Queen Bee, and Skeletron. NPCs acquired - Dryad, Witch Doctor, and Clothier.
Start exploring the Surface to find new enemies for the Bestiary, and when you arrive at the Ocean, look for the Sleeping Angler. Look out for Goblin Scouts. NPCs acquired - Angler, Zoologist, and Tavernkeep.
Craft the Goblin Battle Standard and defeat a Goblin Army.
Return to the Dungeon to find the Mechanic and Goblin Tinkerer.  NPCs acquired - Goblin Tinkerer and Mechanic.
Party Girl will eventually spawn.


== Hardmode ==
Wizard, who you rescue as the Bound Wizard in the Cavern layer
Tax Collector(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), who you transform as a Tortured Soul(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) with Purification Powder in the Underworld
Truffle, who's house must be in a Surface Glowing Mushroom biome
Pirate, who spawns after a Pirate Invasion has been defeated
Steampunker, Who requires a mechanical boss to be defeated
Cyborg, who requires Plantera to be defeated
Santa Claus, who spawns after The Frost Legion has been defeated and the Christmas season is active.
Princess(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), who requires all other NPCs
Make 7 more houses.
Head to the Underworld and bring Purification Powder. On the way, look for the Bound Wizard. NPCs acquired - Wizard and Tax Collector.
Farm enemies in the surface Ocean biome to get a Pirate Map. Use it and defeat a Pirate Invasion. NPCs acquired - Pirate
Defeat all mechanical bosses, then Plantera. While in the Jungle, plant Mushroom Grass Seeds, wait for them to spread, and build a house. NPCs acquired - Truffle, Steampunker and Cyborg.
If you haven't found him already, find the Golfer in the Underground Desert. NPC acquired - Golfer
The Princess can now spawn, being the last NPC.


== Notes ==
In special world seeds, the starting NPC(s) change to:
The Merchant in Not the Bees
Andrew the Guide, Whitney the Steampunker, Yorai the Princess, Amanda the Party Girl, and an Angora Town Bunny in Celebration Mk 10
The Demolitionist in For the Worthy
The Tax Collector in Remix
Whitney the Steampunker, Yorai the Princess, and Andrew the Tax Collector in Zenith
Since Santa Claus is not required for the Princess or achievement, he can be found on your own schedule.
Go to the Dungeon to gather Ectoplasm.
If the Christmas season is inactive, craft a Naughty Present to spawn and defeat the Frost Moon to activate it.
During Christmas, gather presents to get a Snow Globe to spawn and defeat the Frost Legion.
In the Christmas season, Santa Claus will spawn. NPC acquired - Santa Claus

title: Steampunker
content:
The Steampunker is a Hardmode NPC vendor who sells the Clentaminator, various furniture crafting stations, and other steampunk-themed items. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
One of the mechanical bosses (The Twins, The Destroyer, or Skeletron Prime) have been defeated.
The Steampunker will attack nearby enemies using a Clockwork Assault Rifle and High Velocity Bullets for defense.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Steampunker will transform into her Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. She can be returned to her classic look by submerging her in Shimmer again or spraying her with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
(Desktop version) When checking condition for name-based NPC drops, the game specifically requires the NPC's name to be using the corresponding localization string. The game's translation and Resource Packs will not affect name-based item drops: the Steampunker can only drop Ivy if she is originally named Whitney. Using a Resource Pack that changes this name does not prevent it from dropping, and changing any other names of the Steampunker to Whitney does not qualify for item drop.
The Steampunker's move-in requirements do not expressly require a world to be in Hardmode. Summoning and defeating a mechanical boss in a pre-Hardmode world will allow the Steampunker to move in, though this can only be legitimately achieved by carrying over resources from an existing Hardmode world.
If summoned into a pre-Hardmode world this way, the Steampunker will not sell Cogs, the Steampunk Minecart, or the Static Hook until the given world enters Hardmode.
The Steampunker is one of the starting NPC in Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds. This means that it is possible to get most of her items legitimately in a pre-Hardmode world without transferring them from a Hardmode world (e.g. Asphalt Blocks for arenas).
Re-defeating the Eye of Cthulhu and Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu may be necessary to buy the Steampunk Boiler after the Steampunker arrives.
The Steampunker does not sell Dark Blue Solution if moved to the Glowing Mushroom biome. It is sold by the Truffle instead.


== Names ==
The Steampunker may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
Steampunk is a sci-fi/fantasy term used to describe a subculture that incorporates technology and aesthetic designs inspired by 19th-century industrial steam-powered machinery.
The Steampunker occasionally talks about becoming an air pirate. Air pirates are a staple of the steampunk genre.

The Steampunk Wings and Clentaminator sold by the Steampunker are the third and fourth most expensive items to be sold by NPCs, respectively. The only items that are more expensive are the Parrot Cracker (3 Platinum 75 Gold) and the Companion Cube (5 Platinum)
The Steampunker can be seen working on the Cyborg in the credits.
The Steampunker was sprited by former artist Sarah "Waffles" Data.
One of the Steampunker's possible names, Whitney, is also the name of Cenx, who was one of the lead developers of Terraria and Redigit's wife.
If the Steampunker is killed, she will drop the Ivy if her name was Whitney.
The Steampunker’s Shimmered form has green hair, another nod to Cenx.
The name Minerva is a reference to the Roman goddess of handicrafts and wisdom.
The name Zelda may be a reference to the Nintendo game series The Legend of Zelda.
The name Ada is a reference to the 19th-century English mathematician and writer Ada Lovelace, who pioneered work on Charles Babbage's "computer."
One of the Steampunker's quotes regarding the Pirate comments states that he seems to be "pretty well over the bay," which is a 19th-century Celtic phrase meaning drunk.
The Steampunker is the only Hardmode NPC that can also be obtained in a regular pre-Hardmode world that is not a secret world seed.
The quote “I prefer the wide open spaces here in the Desert, great for jetpack joyrides!” is a reference to the mobile game Jetpack Joyride.
She most likely has a Cockney accent, judging by the way she speaks. The accent is typically associated with steampunk themes.
However, when talking about NPCs she dislikes, she uses the word dinnae, which is a Scottish word meaning did not or do not.
Her quote, “I'm mighty curious about that <name of Cyborg> fellow. By what manner of consumption does he maintain such locomotion?” implies that she does not know the Cyborg very well, despite the Bestiary entry for the Cyborg stating that he was built with the combined efforts of the Mechanic and the Steampunker.
 The Bestiary entry for the Steampunker: "The Steampunker has a particular taste for steam-fueled machinery and gadgets. She sells her gizmos with an endearing accent."

title: Pumpkin Moon
content:
The Pumpkin Moon is a Hardmode, post-Plantera, Halloween-themed event summoned with the Pumpkin Moon Medallion any time at night, ending at dawn (4:30 AM). It can be summoned any time of year and does not require the actual Halloween season. During the event, unique and highly difficult enemies spawn at high rates and attack the player. It is similar to the Frost Moon event, but is slightly less difficult. Visually, the moon turns into a jack-o-lantern, though remaining in its current phase.
The entire event consists of 20 waves. Waves progress as the player reaches certain kill scores. After a wave's required score is met, the next wave begins, and the kill score is reset to 0. Status messages will indicate when the wave has advanced, and which wave has been achieved. See the table below for the points awarded for each enemy and the score required for each wave. Expert Mode worlds will gain a 2× point multiplier and Master Mode worlds will gain a 2.5× multiplier. When the event is over, the total score will be displayed by a status message: "The Pumpkin Moon has passed! (Score: <total score>)"
The Pumpkin Moon event always ends at 4:30 AM. The goal of the event is to progress through all 20 waves before the event ends, although the achievement for the event is awarded at wave 15.
The Pumpkin Moon Medallion, which summons the Pumpkin Moon, requires materials only available in Hardmode worlds where the player has already defeated Plantera (although it can still be summoned in pre-Hardmode worlds). As such, it is intended to present a challenge even to players with mid-to-late Hardmode equipment. In the final waves, multiple boss-level enemies are fought at once.
Pumpkin Moon enemies drop powerful weapons and accessories, as well as pet and vanity items. Most drop with extreme rarity, and even players who manage to complete the event will find they need to do so several times before obtaining them. Drop chances for items dropped by bosses increase as waves are completed. In the final wave, the Mourning Wood and Pumpking are both guaranteed to drop their respective trophies.
Reaching the 15th wave before 4:30 AM will display the status message "The spirit of Halloween penetrates the air..." at dawn (4:30 AM). For the entire day and night, all special effects of the Halloween season will occur. At 4:30 AM of the next day, the status message "The spirit of Halloween rests..." will appear and all Halloween effects will no longer occur until the Halloween season begins again or the player reaches the 15th wave of the Pumpkin Moon again.


== Contents ==


== Waves ==

Total points required to reach wave 15: 3410, wave 20: 10160.
The maximum number of bosses/enemies at once depends on the wave. While this number is reached, no more of this type of boss/enemy will spawn.


=== Loot ===
All of the boss-type enemies (Mourning Wood and Pumpking), as well as the Headless Horseman and Scarecrow, have increased chances to drop loot in later waves. This chance starts at 11.11% (16.67%) in wave 1 and grows at a nonlinear rate up to 100% by wave 20 (by wave 12). The formula is as follows (with [math]\displaystyle{ w }[/math] being the wave number in question):

This chance is affected by the luck of the player closest to the enemy upon its death.

Trophies have their own, separate chance to drop (which also applies alongside the general drop chance explained above). Starting at wave 15, there is a chance each Mourning Wood and Pumpking killed will drop its respective trophy. This chance increases at wave 17 and again at wave 19, as shown below. Luck does not affect this chance.

The table below displays the drop rates of all items affected by the loot drop factor explained above.


== Notes ==

Water Candles, Peace Candles, Battle Potions, and Calming Potions have no effect during the event, as the same with some other events.
If the player is killed during the event, the event is not canceled. The player will keep re-spawning and can continue fighting its enemies as the event continues until dawn. In single player games, exiting the world and reentering it will cancel the event.
The Pumpkin Moon does not stack with the Blood Moon. Summoning the Pumpkin Moon while a Blood Moon is active will result in a regular Pumpkin Moon.
Summoning a Pirate Invasion during a Pumpkin Moon will cancel it.
Lingering enemies beaten after the event is over will never drop any rare items.
In Expert Mode, the drop rates are calculated as if they were five waves higher, meaning trophies and guaranteed rare drops will start from wave 10 onwards.
Most enemies have a chance to drop hearts regardless of whether the player is below maximum health.
Any boss enemies that are still on a player's screen by the time dawn breaks will begin to move rapidly in a single direction, rushing off-screen to despawn. It is still possible to pursue or even kill some bosses while this is occurring.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Because spawn rates for areas where Pumpkin Moon enemies cannot spawn are also increased, a Pumpkin Moon can be used to farm for other items, e.g., Pirate Maps at the Ocean, while completely avoiding the Pumpkin Moon enemies.
The early-wave Pumpkin Moon enemies are susceptible to the Ichor debuff, which makes a Flask of Ichor, Ichor Arrows or Bullets, or the Golden Shower very effective.
Players should kill the enemies as soon as they spawn to ensure that more enemies can spawn continuously in order to increase the chances of reaching later waves.
The Pumpkin Moon can be a great way to obtain a large amount of coins quickly.
An area filled with traps could be useful to deal with the regular enemies while the player fights against the mini-bosses.


== Trivia ==
Pumpking is the only boss in the event that flies consistently through blocks and cannot be confined. It behaves similarly to Skeletron, and has a similar size.
Mourning Wood can phase through blocks and (if needed), will go up through blocks and find the player.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: 
Pumpkin Moon can now go up to Wave 20. Wave point requirements for Waves 15–20 match Frost Moon.
Pumpkin Moon's wave composition has been completely rearranged to account for this:
Pumpkin Moon bosses are now capped in number, more closely resembling the behavior of Frost Moon bosses.
Increased the number of enemy slots taken up by Mourning Wood and Pumpking, to be more in line with Frost Moon bosses, dramatically reducing how many can spawn at a time.
All regular enemies in Pumpkin Moon now have low per-player Health scaling in Expert/Master multiplayer (the boss units already had scaling).
Pumpkin Moon trophies now drop using Frost Moon drop rates, instead of dropping from 100% of Wave 15 kills.
Pumpkin Moon boss drop-rate-by-wave multiplier has been reduced, though drops are still more common than Frost Moon levels (this is partly to account for having a higher wave cap, though drops are still slightly less common than before).
Pumpkin Moon's "expert drop bonus" modifier has been reduced slightly, with the base drop rates being increased by the same amount, and the end result being that Classic Mode drops are slightly more generous, while Expert drop rates stay the same.
Pumpkin Moon now receives a 2.5× point multiplier when playing in Master mode. Previously, it received a 2× multiplier in Expert, but no additional gain in Master.
Pumpkin Moon will now display the total score when the event is over.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Reaching the end of the Pumpkin Moon unlocks one in-game day of the Halloween event.
Added alternative music track, Invasion (Otherworldly).
Desktop 1.3.0.4: Fixed invasion progress wrapping around to -32768 when exceeding 32767 points in multiplayer.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Added Headless Horseman Banner, Hellhound Banner, Poltergeist Banner, Scarecrow Banner, and Splinterling Banner.
Trophies can start rarely dropping by Wave 10 in Expert Mode.
Desktop 1.2.2: Music from this event can now be recorded on a Music Box; they will no longer turn into Ankh Charms.

title: Mighty Wind
content:
Mighty Wind is a debuff inflicted on players during a Sandstorm. It slowly pushes affected players in the direction of the wind, hindering (or increasing) their movement. The effect can be suppressed with a hook, by equipping Roller Skates, or by moving at fast speeds with other mounts. Standing in front of background walls at least at waist height also prevents being pushed by Mighty Wind.
Enemies in a Sandstorm are pushed in the same way as players, although they are internally not inflicted with the debuff.


== Causes ==


=== From environment ===


== Notes ==
The player is pushed more if they jump, but less if they are moving themselves left or right.
Knockback-negating accessories, such as the Cobalt Shield, do not protect against Mighty Wind.
The player will be pushed west when the Weather Radio indicates that the wind speed is at zero and is under this debuff.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: Reduced push intensity.
Desktop 1.3.3: Introduced.

Console 1.17: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.4.0.1.

title: Granite Cave
content:
The Granite Cave is a mini-biome found in the Underground and Cavern layers. Granite Caves are generally wide-open caverns dotted with occasional ledges, though their shape may vary due to the presence of overlapping cave systems. They are made entirely out of Granite Blocks and Granite Walls and contain several Pots. Underground Cabins spawned in a Granite Cave will be made out of Granite-themed blocks and furniture.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
Since it is only a mini-biome, the usual NPC spawning rules do not apply to the Granite Cave. Instead, Granite Elementals and Granite Golems require one Granite Block on which they can spawn, inside the player's spawn range; or any Granite Block between 30 and 60 tiles away from the player. A single Granite Block is sufficient (although the chance increases with the number of Granite Blocks) and Granite Walls do not have any impact. However, if the player is standing on a Granite Block, the chance for Granite Elementals and Granite Golems to spawn gets a significant boost. In that case, no further Granite Blocks in the vicinity are required.
In drunk worlds, the generation structure of Granite Caves is swapped with Marble Caves.


== Tips ==
Granite biomes usually have at least a standalone chest in them, so once a player is powerful enough to repel Granite Elementals, they should explore the biome.


== See also ==
Marble Cave
Underground


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Added new Granite rubble piles.
Added two new drops from Granite Cave enemies:
Both the Granite Elemental and Granite Golem have a 5% chance of dropping the Geode, a consumable which will drop two types of Gems upon being thrown, and a 2% chance of dropping the new Spaghetti food item.
Fixed a world generation issue where Granite and Marble biomes that had generated under the Dungeon would still leave some of the Dungeon Bricks hammered in the same shape they were when before the Dungeon generated.

title: The Underworld
content:
The Underworld (also known as Hell) is the deepest layer of the world. It is a large, open cavern that stretches across the bottom of the world, with a ceiling of Ash Blocks and a lower terrain of large lava pools, Ash Blocks, and Hellstone. It also contains numerous Ruined Houses, which are natural structures containing unique furniture and loot. The Wall of Flesh boss can be summoned in the Underworld; defeating it will cause the world to convert to Hardmode.
The Underworld contains many hazards, such as large pools of lava and various difficult enemies. Hellstone, a valuable crafting material only obtainable in the Underworld, inflicts the Burning debuff when touched and releases half a tile of lava when mined. Further, because the Wall of Flesh is summoned by dropping a Guide Voodoo Doll into lava, killing a Voodoo Demon positioned over lava can inadvertently summon it.
The middle two-quarters of the Underworld contains several Ruined Houses, which are towers made from Obsidian Bricks and, less commonly, Hellstone Bricks that contain Shadow Chests, Hellforges, Pots, Obsidian furniture, and other lootable items. Shadow Chests require the Shadow Key to open (acquired in the Dungeon's Locked Gold Chests or Golden Lock Boxes) and contain unique Underworld-only loot. The outer sixths of the underworld are occupied by ash forests, which are barren, fiery-looking forests that feature Ash trees growing on Ash grass.


== Contents ==


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
The Underworld starts at about 1500 tiles (3000 feet) underground in a large world, at about 1000 tiles (2000 feet) underground in a medium world, and at about 650 tiles (1300 feet) underground in a small world.
If any water enters the Underworld, it will quickly evaporate. Therefore, attempting to generate Obsidian here is usually not very effective, due to most of the water evaporating before touching any lava. However, a Water Bucket can still be used to quench somewhat smaller amounts of lava.
No background or foreground shaders can be applied by anything in the Underworld aside from normal light sources. This is apparent when fighting the Moon Lord here, as blocks are not darkened, and the background is still visible, unlike in the rest of the world.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

It is highly recommended to equip protective accessories when visiting the Underworld.
An Obsidian Skull or any of its upgrades will allow walking on Hellstone and Hellstone Bricks.
An Obsidian Rose can also reduce the damage from lava.
A Lava Charm or any of its upgrades will protect from brief contact with lava, and can also be combined with other accessories, culminating in the Terraspark Boots. Note that these charms have become much rarer, appearing solely in 2.5% of lower-Cavern Gold Chests, and 2.5% of Obsidian and Hellstone Crates.
The Terraspark Boots represent a nearly sovereign remedy for the hazards of lava. While they do not provide complete protection against swimming in lava, they allow walking on its surface without harm, and they do offer 7 seconds of protection (extendable by other accessories) for a player who is accidentally dunked.  They also protect the player from taking damage when walking on Hellstone or Hellstone Bricks.   (Or Meteorite, but that's rare in the Underworld.)  Combining all this with their speed and limited flight, they allow moving around the Underworld with fair impunity.
A very common method to quickly travel to the Underworld is to dig a hellevator, a vertical shaft from the surface to the Underworld.
Minions such as the Imp Staff are an effective way to counter Fire Imps, as the player can summon a minion on a fire imp that is otherwise inaccessible. The minion can then stall the imp by locking on and continuously attacking it.
Since the Underworld spans the entire length of the world, it is easy to locate the Underground Jungle, Corruption/Crimson, and Hallow biomes. The bottoms of these biomes are often seen at the roof of the Underworld.
Despite the sequential boss difficulty, it is much easier to survive in the Underworld than in the Dungeon or Underground Jungle due to the much slower spawn rate. In contrast to those biomes, the Underworld can be explored fairly safely. When starting Hardmode, the Underworld is one of the safest areas of the world because there are no new or more difficult enemies spawning there until defeating a mechanical boss causes Lava Bats and Red Devils to spawn.
One way to avoid most of the Underworld spawns (except Fire Imps and Bone Serpents) is to stay in confined quarters while mining Hellstone. Ruined Houses are usually a safe base to tunnel to Hellstone veins from. With care, a player can tunnel directly from shelter through the ash, leaving spaces for lava to drain away from the player as they mine. Obsidian Platforms and Water Buckets will be helpful for this method.
The Ruined Houses are large enough to allow some enemies to spawn inside, but replacing their background walls will prevent that. Tunnels and bunkers will also help.
It is beneficial to seal all lava pools, because that prevents both inadvertent Wall of Flesh summonings and accidentally falling into a pool. Furthermore, it serves as terrain preparation for the Wall of Flesh fight.
The native Underworld spawns can be overridden by placing at least 75 blocks of Meteorite, effectively creating an artificial Meteorite biome.
It is possible to flood parts of the Underworld by digging channels to dump an ocean over the lava. The water will eventually evaporate, but not before it converts the lava surface to Obsidian, sealing off many lava pools.
Luck can be increased in the Underworld by using Bone Torches.
In Expert Mode, killed Lava Slimes will cause lava to pour out from where they die, so it is recommended to have the Royal Gel accessory equipped as it will make Lava Slimes friendly.


== Trivia ==
When the player gets close to the Underworld, the screen will start to waver slightly, like the Shimmering caused by heat.
Just above the Underworld (if backgrounds are switched on), there will be the old background that the Underworld used to have.
There was originally going to be a "Hell alternative" that would have had the color schemes from hell in Disney's Hercules. However, the idea was scrapped.


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===
Unlike the underground backgrounds, these have multiple layers like surface backgrounds do.

		
		
		

		
		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Fixed stars being visible in the Underworld when backgrounds are disabled and there is no light nearby.
Desktop 1.4.4: Added ash forests that spawn on the outer edges of the Underworld.
Desktop 1.4.0.1:

Added two new backgrounds as well as the one introduced in 1.3.0.1 being now animated.
Added Hell Butterfly, Lavafly and Magma Snail critters.
Added two ambient entities in the background: flocks of Hellbats and a Bone Serpent leaping in lava.
Bone Serpents now drop Bone Serpent Kite during Windy Days.
Desktop 1.3.3: Added heat distortion effect.

Added a new background.
Changed music from Eerie to a new track exclusive to the biome, Hell.
Desktop 1.2.4: The Underworld (as well as the Dungeon) has more new furniture generated at world creation.

title: Oiled
content:
Oiled is a Hardmode debuff that can be inflicted by Explosive Trap sentries when the player is wearing a full set of Huntress armor or Red Riding armor. It causes the afflicted enemy to lose 25 health per second (10 damage displayed every 0.4 seconds) if it is also afflicted with any of the following flame debuffs:

This effect does not stack if the enemy is afflicted with multiple of these debuffs at the same time.
Visually, Oiled also causes afflicted enemies to turn gray and drip oil particles.

title: Titan Potion
content:
The  Titan Potion is a buff potion which grants the Titan buff when consumed. The buff increases the amount of knockback the player inflicts on enemies by 50%. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Titan Potions can be found in Pots in the Underworld, as well as in Chests.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Tips ==
The Titan Potion can help deal with large crowds of enemies, pushing them away for a while.
The added knockback is helpful against the Wall of Flesh as it makes it easier to keep the high-damage The Hungry at bay.


== Trivia ==
The Titan Potion's buff icon could be a reference to the Titans of Greek mythology, and how they possessed great power.
Due to having Bones in its recipe, the Titan Potion cannot be transmuted in Shimmer before defeating Skeletron.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Stack limit increased from 30 to 9999.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Buff duration increased from 4 to 8 minutes.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Sprite updated.
Desktop 1.2.4: Introduced.

title: Guide:Surviving in the Jungle
content:
The Jungle is one of the hardest areas to survive in Terraria, as it has some of the toughest enemies in the game along with increased spawn rates. The majority of the Jungle spans Underground, which is where the most of its treasures and hazards are located.
If you're new to Terraria, then you will find exploring the Jungle very hard: Man Eaters will reach out to you through walls and the Hornets can shoot their stingers at you which may inflict the Poisoned debuff. Even the Jungle Slime packs a lot more life than most slimes. Therefore, navigating the Jungle safely usually entails taking it slow and not trying to run past enemies, and tunneling around dangerous areas to reach the treasures.
In pre-Hardmode, the Jungle is usually tackled after dealing with Corruption or Crimson, and can be done before or after visiting the Dungeon, but it's usually avoided before going into the Underworld.
In Hardmode, the Jungle can be explored at any time, but it's usually done after defeating the Mechanical bosses, as it's mandatory to defeat Plantera and Golem and to obtain Chlorophyte, and since there's little significant new loot to obtain in there until then.


== Pre-Hardmode ==


=== Recommended Gear and Items ===
The Flaming Mace (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Starfury, Enchanted Sword, Gold/Platinum Bow, Musket/The Undertaker, Flinx Staff (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Thunder Zapper (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Gem staves are all good options.
Fossil armor (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is the best option for rangers, but it requires braving the equally dangerous Underground Desert biome.
Mages should use the Wizard set to improve their magic weapons' damage and efficiency.
Summoners should use the Flinx Fur Coat (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the best available head/leg armor.
Silver or better armor is recommended for all classes if you don't already have specialized armor, due to its high defense.
An Extra jump and Hook will be useful for navigating the open caverns of the Underground Jungle.
Royal Gel is useful for its ability to pacify otherwise dangerous Spiked Jungle Slimes.
Items to bring

Some Lesser Healing Potions. If you can craft Healing Potions, bring those instead.
Some Torches
Piggy Bank or Safe to store extra loot.
Platforms are useful for traversal.
Optionally, Rope Coils or Glowsticks for larger caverns; a Bug Net, for catching bait; and a bed/wood to set up a forward base closer to the biome.


=== The First visit ===
The Jungle is located on either the left or right side of the world, opposite to the Snow biome and Dungeon. If you find the Snow biome, go to the other side to find the Underground Desert and go past it to enter the Jungle. (Note that underground deserts aren't guaranteed to have visible entrances, so it is better to look for the Snow biome and then go the other way if you find it.)
The Underground Jungle is located directly below the surface, and there are usually cave entrances to it.  On  Old-gen console and 3DS versions, the threat of Dragon Snatchers make the Surface Jungle a lot more dangerous, so the player should quickly go underground.
The enemies found in the Underground Jungle are harder to deal than in any other biome, especially since most of them will poison the player. Additionally more enemies will spawn compared to the regular Cavern, but less than the Dungeon. It is easy to die in this environment, so caution and knowledge of how to deal with the enemies is advised. The most dangerous enemies are:

Hornets will fire stingers that can be hard to see due to them being small and blending in with the background. This attack inflicts the Poisoned debuff, which will slowly kill a player as well as stopping their natural regeneration. They will rarely drop the Bezoar, which provides immunity to the poison.
On  Old-gen console and 3DS versions, a variant called Dragon Hornet will appear. This new enemy has the same behavior but with higher stats, making it more dangerous.
Man Eaters have a lot of health and damage and they are immune to knockback. They don't move a lot, but it is easy to get caught off guard by them due to their ability to go through blocks. They can easily be dealt with by latching and staying above them with a hook or rope. They have a small chance to drop Vines when killed.
Spiked Jungle Slimes are more dangerous than any other slime, due to their ability to shoot poisonous spikes. They should be killed with a long-range weapon while standing far away, as they can easily do a lot of damage up close.
The player will also find Bee Hives in the jungle, which will spawn Bees when destroyed. Despite their very low health, these enemies should not be underestimated, as they hit harder than what it may look, they can poison the player and can be hard to hit without a Melee weapon.
Remember to bring bottles because if you find honey you can get a good supply of Bottled Honey, which is easier than farming glowing mushrooms.

In the Pre-Hardmode Jungle, there are three things to do: Get Jungle Spores, find Ivy Chests and a Larva, used to summon The Queen Bee.
Jungle Spores can be found anywhere underground, and their position is easily given away by its glow. With these, the player can make strong weapons such as the Blade of Grass and Thorn Chakram, the Ivy Whip, and for mage users, the Jungle armor.
Ivy chests appear in Jungle Shrines or Living Mahogany Trees, the former of which can be seen with the glow of the Green Torch placed in them. They contain many useful items that can't be found anywhere else, such as the Boomstick or the Staff of Regrowth.

Larvas are found in bee hives underground. Bee hives should be accessed with caution and good gear, as it is very easy to accidentally summon the boss with an attack. If the player finds Honey and Honey blocks around the Jungle, it means a bee hive is close.

Melee players may also want to find a Sharpening Station in the Underground Cabins, as it provides a free buff which will slightly increase the damage of Melee weapons.


=== Alternative Strategies ===


==== The Slow Method ====
Simply explore the Jungle by digging through the mud, or placing blocks to keep yourself "sealed" inside a protective layer of dirt. Hornets cannot fly or fire through blocks. Man Eaters can pass through blocks, but they are rooted to one position, and are predictable. Simply keep extending your tunnel until you get to the position where your sword can just barely reach the Man Eater when it bobs outwards, and hit it when it comes within range. A good weapon for this method is the Vilethorn, since it can fire through the walls. Then, when ready, break down your bunker, and go fighting again. Rinse and repeat as you advance.
As you go, place torches everywhere - this gives you the chance to actually run and fight later without worrying so much about the darkness.


==== Reworking the Terrain ====
Similarly to the previous, just work upon trying to cut away any major obstacles to your movement, and light up the place as well as possible. Place blocks and doors in positions that tactically block off the enemy or give yourself breathing room; flatten terrain, drain water, add Torches, and otherwise make a better fighting platform to explore.
It is ideal to make the roof fully obstructed with stone slabs or platforms to prevent the nuisance of vines and Bee Hives from spawning as obstructions. A good multi-grapple hook is very helpful for reaching the ceiling. Alternatively, double click with a hammer to slope the grass block and prevent them from attaching. Finally if neither of these are possible, at least block off any 2×2 placement spots for the Bee Hives by making the ceiling as uneven as possible, by placing mud blocks every other tile (B-B-B). This also applies when digging sideways tunnels, which should have a double height 5/6 tile ceiling to allow jumping to avoid monsters or thorns, again fully lined with stone slabs to prevent vines blocking vision.
Apart from thorns, which have much lower damage than the monsters, the floor does not present much danger. In fact where possible it is best to flatten it, this makes it easier to spawn bushes for bait. This does have the useful side effect of possibly making it easier to see thorns (although it may also be necessary to place lighting and a wall for contrast).


== Hardmode ==
The Underground Jungle in Hardmode is one of the most dangerous biomes of the game. Below you'll find all the hint and tips needed to progress through it, until you get to defeat Plantera and get access to the Jungle Temple.


=== Recommended Gear ===
The Underground Jungle can be explored at any time, but there's no real reason to do so until the Mechanical bosses are Defeated, since nothing very special can be obtained without Chlorophyte, which requires the Pickaxe Axe.

The best armor set for all four classes is Hallowed armor.
For a Melee character, the best weapons are the Code 2, The Shadowflame Knife, True Night's Edge or True Excalibur, Light Discs, Death or Ice Sickle, and Gungnir or Mushroom Spear.
The best choices for a Ranged user are the Megashark, the Hallowed Repeater and the Dart Rifle, with Crystal Bullets, Holy/Ichor Arrows, and Ichor Darts.
Mages can use the Rainbow Rod, Crystal Serpent, Nimbus Rod and the Unholy Trident. It is also useful to carry a Golden Shower to increase the damage of the main weapons.
Mobility accessories like Wings, the Amphibian Boots or the Shield of Cthulhu should be brought to avoid the enemies, as well as damage boosting ones such as the Emblems to kill them faster.
Defensive accessories like the Brain of Confusion, Charm of Myths or Star Veil are useful as well.


=== Exploring ===
It is very hard to survive in the new Jungle due to the extremely strong enemies that can now be found, mainly the Derplings and Giant Tortoises. There isn't much to do in the surface, so it's recommended to quickly go underground as the Derplings will stop spawning.
Once underground, the main thing to do is to mine Chlorophyte with the Pickaxe Axe or Drax. With Mining and Spelunker Potions it is easily acquired. The player will need a lot of it, since it's required for Chlorophyte armor and some of the strongest weapons available, as well as being used for Post Plantera equipment.

While mining, the player may find Plantera's Bulb, which can be easily seen since it glows in the dark. The bulb should not be touched until the player feels ready to fight Plantera, as breaking it will summon the boss.

Life Fruits may also be found, and they should be collected since the extra health is extremely useful for bosses.


==== Enemies ====
Just like every other biome in Hardmode, the player will find many new enemies, the most dangerous being:

As mentioned above, the Derplings due to their high damage, health, and knockback resistance, as well as being very mobile. However they are much taller than the average enemy, so they can't go through player tall spaces. They do not spawn Underground.
Giant Tortoises are slow, and their attack is predictable. However, they do massive damage and can easily catch a player off-guard if they attack offscreen. They are also very hard to kill due to them also having high health and knockback resistance. When killed, they have a chance to drop Turtle Shells, which are required for Turtle armor. Even though the set is overall less useful than Chlorophyte armor, melee players should still look for it as it is required for Beetle armor.
Angry Trappers are the Hardmode version of Man Eaters. They are more aggressive and have higher stats, but unlike their counterparts they are vulnerable to knockback, making them rather easy to deal with.
Moss Hornets are the Hardmode version of regular Hornets, having higher stats but the same behavior. They are still dangerous but can be killed like their Pre-Hardmode variant
Arapaimas will only spawn in water, and will do so more frequently than other enemies. Like the Piranhas, when the player submerges, they will engage, and their high stats and numbers will easily overwhelm a player. Water should be avoided because of them.

title: Legacy:Guide:Class setups
content:
Terraria has no formal player class or leveling system. However, weapons can be grouped into four distinct categories based on their damage type – melee, ranged, magic, and summoner. Each class has its strengths and weaknesses and has a wide variety of weapons to choose from.

Melee
The melee class sports high defense and decent crowd control, but many melee weapons have a short attack range, and those that are viable at a distance tend to do lower damage than their close-range counterparts. This encourages melee users to use their defense to tank hits while attacking with their stronger close-ranged weapons. Melee weapons include swords, spears, and yoyos, and boomerangs.

Ranged
Rangers are able to attack from a distance, doing high single-target, piercing, or splash damage. They utilize weapons like bows and guns, as well as thrown objects. Ranged users must constantly acquire ammunition, unless using a ranged weapon that doesn't require ammunition such as the Piranha Gun.

Magic
Mages are fragile but highly varied in attack style, often utilizing special mechanics such as homing, lifesteal, and area-of-effect damage. They are held back by reliance on mana, which regenerates very slowly unless the Mana Regeneration buff is in effect. Magic users can often sustain their mana using Mana Stars when fighting many enemies at once, but must craft or purchase mana potions if they wish to recover mana instantly during boss fights. Most pre-Plantera magic weapons are specialized for crowd control, with weaker single-target damage than other classes.

Summoner
Summoners deal most of their damage using autonomous minions and/or sentries, and their attacks usually have excellent accuracy. However, most summoning armor sets have low defense in exchange for their high damage potential. The summoning class was balanced around the idea of the player also using the strongest normal weapon available to them in addition to minions and sentries.  
Each class gains more complex abilities as the game progresses, enabling more strategic variety in combat. It is advised for players to try out every weapon they find to help determine what works best for them. It is also recommended to use buff potions and healing potions to increase efficiency and survivability in combat (especially during events and boss fights).
In general, it is recommended to focus on gear that benefits one class. Equipment slots are limited, and many armors and accessories only benefit a specific class, especially later into the game. Summoners are an exception to this rule, since summons can deal damage alongside melee/ranged/magic weapons, so summoning gear will always provide a benefit as long as summons are being used. All classes can use at least two minions at all times even without using summoning gear (by using a Bewitching Table), so it's recommended to always utilize these free slots regardless of primary class.
Note that while it's beneficial to only focus on one class between melee/ranged/magic at a time, there is little benefit to specializing in one class over the course of an entire playthrough, and one should strongly consider switching classes if they happen to obtain a powerful weapon from a different class.
Even when not specifically using a hybrid set, backup weapons from another class can be helpful should the situation require a different weapon. For example, Vampire Knives can be used even when the player is not playing melee to rapidly heal health and apply Ichor.


== Pre-bosses ==
Prior to encountering a boss, set bonuses from wooden and ore armor will almost exclusively provide additional defense, and accessories will not discriminate by weapon type when giving bonuses. When combined with the general scarcity of weapons and the need to survive, there is little point to sticking to a "class" this early on. For these reasons, players are recommended to make use of whatever they can get their hands on.  Players can acquire a gun or magic weapon early on by smashing one of the Corruption Orbs (in Corruption worlds) or the Crimson Hearts (in Crimson worlds). Hellstone is obtainable pre-boss by fishing up a Reaver Shark.


== Pre-Skeletron ==


== Pre-Wall of Flesh ==
Defeating Skeletron provides access to the Dungeon, giving access to Necro armor and new weapons from Dungeon and Shadow Chests. By this time you should generally have 200 base mana, plenty for using magic weapons.


== Pre-mechanical bosses ==
At this point in the game, damage bonuses from armor and accessories become more significant, so it is recommended to choose a class to specialize in. Ranger is generally agreed to have the best weapons at this stage. However, melee also improves significantly due to melee armors having significantly higher defense than any other class. Magic is still heavily focused on crowd control, making it an effective class for those who want to take out The Destroyer first. Summoners receive Hardmode upgrades earlier than the other classes because Spider equipment can be crafted at an Iron or Lead Anvil. The Sharanga is powerful enough to be useful in Hardmode.
This is also the point where a fully-defensive build begins to diverge from damage builds thanks to the availability of the Star Veil, coupled with greater access to damage accessories, so it is a good time to decide whether you want to run a primarily offensive or defensive loadout and reforge your accessories accordingly.


== Pre-Plantera ==
At this point, players are expected to have chosen between melee, ranged, magic, or a hybrid of summoning and another class.
As was the case in previous stages, ranged provides the highest long-distance DPS, melee provides the best tanking ability, magic provides the most unique weapon effects.


== Pre-Golem ==
With the Hardmode Dungeon and Temple Keys now available, players have access to a variety of new equipment. Furthermore, any Biome Keys you have obtained are now usable. You could attempt to extend the duration of this stage by killing Duke Fishron or summoning the Frost Moon or Pumpkin Moon, but most players will find it easier and more logical to kill Golem first.
The transition from pre-Plantera to post-Plantera comes with a significant improvement to the equipment available, with the most prominent new items being melee weapons (Vampire Knives) and magic armor (Spectre armor). The classes are very balanced at this stage.


== Endgame ==
Once Golem, Duke Fishron, and Ocram have all been defeated, the player is considered to be in the endgame.


== Other ==

Some equipment sets are not meant for fighting, but for other activities, such as fishing, building and exploring. All equipment is optional and makes it easier to perform the task, but otherwise simply use what is at hand.


== Footnotes ==

title: Gravity
content:
Gravity applies a constant downwards acceleration to the player, affecting vertical speed and how quickly the maximum falling speed is reached. The default gravitational acceleration is 123 mph per second, with falling speed capping at 51 mph. Certain sources may add modifiers to both gravity and the maximum falling speed to increase or decrease their effects.


== Modifiers ==


=== Space ===
Here is the formula to calculate gravity modifier: modifier = (x - offset - 60) * factor1/factor2. Thereafter, the final result will be limited between 0.25 and 1 (0.1 to 1 in Remix and Zenith worlds). Meanings of the parameters are listed below:

x equals to the player's distance to the top border of the world (measured by tiles).
offset is determined by the world size, where a large world is 20, a medium world is 15 approximately, and a small world is 10.
factor1 means whether the world uses the world gen of Remix or Zenith. A normal world is 6, while the former both are 1.
factor2 equals to the distance of the world's Surface (0 feet) to the world's top border.


== Reversing gravity ==

The player can gain the ability to reverse their gravity by consuming a Gravitation Potion or equipping a Gravity Globe(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Pressing the ▲ Up key flips the player's gravity so that they fall up instead of down. In multiplayer, this only affects the player with the item used. Gravity can be changed back to normal afterward with the same key, and can be toggled freely at any time (provided the Gravitation Potion's buff is active or the Gravity Globe is equipped) at no cost and with no cooldown.
Notable aspects of reversed gravity include the following:

Flipping gravity resets the player's fall distance. They can flip gravity rapidly before landing to avoid taking fall damage from a long fall.
Hitting the upper limit of the map while gravity is reversed will not damage the player, but will instead cause gravity to revert to normal. This will not reset the flight timer of wings and Rocket Boots.
The Wisp in a Bottle, as well as its controls, remain upside down in reversed gravity.
Fishing is possible in reverse gravity; the fishing bobber will fall "upward" into the water.
Being in reversed gravity also applies certain restrictions:

Mounts cannot be summoned.
Platforms will not stop players falling upwards, and they will instead fall through them.
Wings cannot be used to glide.
Golf(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) cannot be played; the player will not even be able to swing the club.
Kites(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used but will retain their normal orientation.
With the Flower Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) equipped, flowers will grow on the grass block that the player's head touches. The block which the player is actually standing on will not sprout upside-down flowers, nor will it sprout vines.
Gravity is furthermore reverted to normal when the player becomes inflicted with the Frozen, Webbed, Stoned(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), or Shimmering(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) debuffs, or when they press the “Pet” button in the dialogue window of a town pet.


== Notes ==
Most blocks are not affected by gravity, with the exceptions being Sand Blocks (and its variants), Silt Blocks, Slush Blocks, Coin Piles, and Shell Piles.
These blocks become projectiles when falling, and turn back into block form upon landing on a solid block, including platforms and Planter Boxes.
If the landing location is occupied by any foreground objects (such as Torches, Minecart Tracks, and Campfires), they will instantly break into item form.
Out of these, only Sand, Silt, and Slush will cause the Suffocation debuff if the player's head is trapped underneath them.
If the player does not have a tool with at least 110% pickaxe power in their inventory (i.e., no Cobalt Pickaxe or better), then these gravity-affected blocks can only be swapped out from the top-most block and downwards. With a tool that has at least 110% pickaxe power, gravity-affected blocks can be swapped freely.
Gravity-affected blocks can always be swapped freely with each other, regardless of pickaxe power.
The majority of items are subject to gravity when in dropped form, with exceptions.


== Trivia ==
In reversed gravity, the text during the credits appears upside down as well.


== See also ==
Fall damage


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Overhead chat and multiplayer nameplates now also appear above the player in reverse gravity.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Fixed (again) an issue where Celestial Pillar shields would fly into the sky when reversing gravity.
Fixed an issue where pressing UP to flip Gravity would dismount the player from flying mounts. Now, it simply does not flip Gravity when in mounts.
Fixed a reverse gravity issue where the Floating Piggy Bank's mouseover detection would be in the wrong direction.
Fixed a reverse gravity issue where Blizzard Staff-style weapons would converge in the opposite direction of where the player aimed.
Fixed a reverse gravity issue where the player would get stuck on hammered platforms.
Fixed an issue where Forbidden Set's ring did not flip properly in reverse gravity.
Fixed a reverse gravity issue where some weapons wouldn't flip with the player.
Fixed a reverse gravity issue where cobwebs did not correctly slow inverted players.

title: Stinky
content:
Stinky is a debuff that decreases the luck of afflicted players by 0.25 and causes NPCs to flee from them. Entities inflicted with Stinky turn green and emit green fume particles.
The debuff can be negated by submerging in any liquid except lava. The Wet debuff also makes enemies and NPCs immune to Stinky, but not players.


== Causes ==


=== From player ===


=== From enemy ===


=== Other ===


== Immune NPCs ==


== Tips ==
While having negative luck is generally undesirable, there are some exceptions:

The spawn chance of several Graveyard enemies is boosted by negative luck:
Moss Zombies, which require negative luck to spawn at all, and are necessary to complete the Bestiary.
Hostile Statues, which are rare to encounter with positive luck.
The Groom and The Bride, which are the only sources of Bloody Tears outside of a Blood Moon.
The drop rate of Bloody Tear from The Groom and The Bride is also boosted by negative luck.
Negative luck increases the chance to spawn a distressed Cattiva instead of Foxparks.
Negative luck grants a chance to produce extra Poo, which players may want to farm for Fertilizer.
Negative luck has a chance to boost all entity spawn rates when not near town NPCs.
This can prove useful when farming a large amount of guaranteed drops from a common enemy, such as Pixie Dust from Pixies.


== History ==

Now decreases the player's luck by 0.25.
Can now be inflicted by Poo Boulders, as well as a slime variant carrying Poo.
Can now be removed by water.
Can now be removed from enemies and NPCs via the Wet debuff.
Now causes NPCs to flee.
