title: Not the Bees
content:
Not the Bees is a special world seed. It generates a world dominated by bee-themed biomes and bee-related items and structures.


== While generating ==
All generation descriptions say “Generating bees”.
The time required to generate this seed is also extraordinarily long, possibly due to the fact that the world is generated first (as normal) and then converted to the seed's terrain thereafter.


== Spawn ==
The Merchant replaces the Guide as the starting NPC. As both he and the player spawn in the Jungle, he will also sell the Furnace and Jungle Torches.


== World generation ==
Most of the world is replaced with the Jungle biome, with Bee Hives and Honey Blocks found in abundance. See below for a full list of replaced tiles.
Larvae will often generate outside of Bee Hives.
The Dungeon is painted orange and the Jungle Temple is painted green. Mud Blocks with Jungle grass can spawn inside, as can Mahogany trees. In the Dungeon entrance variant containing Stained Glass windows, the windows are now formed of Hive Walls.
Poo Boulders may be generated.
Water Chests and trees can generate in honey, and Fallen Logs can generate on any surface tile.
The Ice biome will spawn under both Oceans. Water will generate as usual in these biomes. The Aether will be found surrounded by Snow Blocks rather than Stone Blocks.
When entering Hardmode, the two diagonal stripes of the new biomes generated will replace all Hive blocks to the respective Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone Block and all Crispy Honey Blocks will be replaced by Hardened Ebonsand, Hardened Crimsand, or Hardened Pearlsand Blocks, respectively. Note this only affects the initial replacement and none of the biomes will spread to Hive or Crispy Honey Blocks.


=== Replaced tiles ===
All water outside of the center 1/6 of the world is replaced by honey, except for the Snow biomes beneath Oceans and the entire Ocean on the side of the Dungeon.
All Forest trees, Living Wood, Leaf Blocks, and vines are converted into their respective Jungle variants, unless on Floating Islands.
Rarely, parts of the world that spawn above the minimum level needed for Floating Islands will also not be converted, leaving hilltops of dirt above a line.
All Slush blocks are replaced with Honey Blocks.
All Dirt Blocks are initially replaced with Mud Blocks, unless part of Floating Islands or near the Ocean on the side of the Dungeon.
Grass types are replaced with Jungle grass above the lava layer of the Caverns and with Mushroom grass below the lava layer. Corresponding grass is grown on all exposed Mud Blocks.
Because of this, an enormous Glowing Mushroom biome will appear in the lava layer where the original Jungle was.
Stone is replaced with Hive blocks above the lava layer and with Crispy Honey Blocks below the lava layer. This replacement does not occur in the area directly surrounding the Ocean on the Dungeon side.
Likewise with Ebonsand, Ebonsandstone, Hardened Ebonsand, Purple Ice, Crimsand, Crimsandstone, Hardened Crimsand, and Red Ice blocks.
Only Sand Blocks within the Ocean biome opposite of the Dungeon are replaced with Honey Blocks.
Likewise, only Hardened Sand and Sandstone Blocks within the Ocean biomes are replaced with Hive blocks.
Jungle grass that would be within 20 tiles of Ebonstone or Crimstone blocks is converted into Corrupt Jungle grass or Crimson Jungle grass.
Hive and Mud Blocks underneath the Oceans, in the Cavern layer, and above the lava layer, are replaced with Snow and Ice Blocks. In the upper half, Hive Blocks become Snow Blocks and Mud Blocks become Ice Blocks, and vice versa for the bottom half.
Copper Ore, Tin Ore, Iron Ore, and Lead Ore in the approximate lower half of the world are replaced with Dirt Blocks.
Silt and Clay Blocks in the approximate lower half of the world are replaced with Stone Blocks.


=== Removals ===
The Oasis and glowing moss biomes will not generate.
Campsites, gemstone caves, moss chambers, and Thin Ice patches will not generate.
Lava traps and Geysers will not generate.
Boulder traps that use Active Stone Blocks will not generate, but Boulder traps that use Actuators will still generate.
Shell Piles and Moss will not generate.


== Mechanics ==


=== Changes ===
Only half of fishing attempts in Jungle Biome are considered as Jungle fishing attempts.
Only half of fishing attempts in honey are considered as honey fishing attempts.


== Enemies ==


=== Spawning ===
Hornets can spawn above the surface layer.
Poo Slimes may spawn.


== Tips ==

There are few Stone Blocks available early on, so purchasing Wooden Arrows and a Furnace from the Merchant is advised.
Snow Flinx can still be found deep below the outer edges of the world where Snow and Ice Blocks generate (since the number of Snow-related tiles there is sufficient to form an Ice biome). Deerclops can also be summoned in this area.


== Trivia ==
The phrase not the bees references the "NOT THE BEES!" meme which originated from the 2006 horror film The Wicker Man, which also inspired an eponymous achievement.


== Gallery ==

		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.8: Fixed paint not applying to the Dungeon in certain Not the Bees seed worlds.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Reduced the amount of Larvae placed during world generation.
Gem blocks are no longer replaced with Crispy Honey Blocks during world generation.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Added notthebees as an alias for this seed.
Spider Nests now generate in this seed.
All fish should be catchable now.
It should now be possible to 100% complete the Bestiary.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.


== References ==

title: For the Worthy
content:
For the Worthy is a special world seed with features that aim to increase the game's difficulty drastically.


== While generating ==

All generation descriptions and tips are spelled backwards.


== Changes ==


=== Difficulty ===

The world difficulty is increased by one stage, and therefore enemy damage, health, knockback resistance, and drops are increased accordingly.
For example, after selecting “Classic” option in the world creation menu, the actual difficulty will be Expert, and the difficulty displayed in the world selection menu will be “Expert”. This is not reflected in the world creation menu.
A For the Worthy world in Master Mode is displayed as having “Legendary” difficulty (with the color  #32CD32), which does not have any exclusive content despite the name. In Legendary Mode, enemies generally have 4× as much health, drop 3.5× as much money, and deal 5.33× as much contact damage as in Classic Mode (33% more health, 40% more money, and 78% more contact damage than in Master Mode). All other stats, including projectile damage are the same as Master Mode.
This can be unintuitive due to some NPCs appearing to function as projectiles. For instance, Burning Spheres may seem like projectiles, but they are handled as NPCs so that they can be destroyed, meaning they have increased contact damage. On the other hand, the Eye of Cthulhu in its second form and Eater of Worlds' Vile Spit do not have their contact damage increased due to the particular method the game uses in their AI to set their damage stats. The Servants of Cthulhu and Eater of Worlds' segments will still have increased contact damage, however.
Difficulty wise, a Classic Mode For the Worthy world behaves exactly the same as a typical Expert Mode world, and an Expert Mode For the Worthy world behaves exactly the same as a typical Master Mode world, including allowing for Expert and Master Mode-exclusive items to be obtained.
A Journey Mode For the Worthy world will have its difficulty setting increased by 1×. The default difficulty setting in Journey Mode is 0.5×, which will be increased to 1.5× in a For the Worthy world; this results in enemies having 50% more health and dealing 50% more damage than in Classic Mode.
For example, in standard worlds, Eye of Cthulhu in its first form deals 7 / 15 / 30 / 45 contact damage in Journey, Classic, Expert, and Master Mode respectively. After applying the difficulty increase in For the Worthy worlds, this is increased to 22 / 30 / 45 / 80 damage, respectively.


=== World generation ===
Some water pools throughout the world are replaced with lava.
Demonite or Crimtane and Gold or Platinum Ore generate more commonly as well as having larger vein sizes.
Spider Nests, Granite Caves, Marble Caves, and Glowing Mushroom biomes are much more common.
Glowing Mushroom biomes are furthermore much larger.
Floating Islands are always infected with the world's evil biome, with matching water fountains.
Skyware Chests are replaced with locked Gold Chests but still have their respective loot. However, it is still possible to get Skyware Chest loot before Skeletron by opening Sky Crates.
The Dungeon is painted with seemingly random Deep Paint and filled with many more Spike traps. Additionally, the surface building of the Dungeon is inverted (the opening faces towards the nearest Ocean).
The Jungle Temple is painted with Deep Green Paint and is about three times as large as normal.
All Chests, except Chests in the Dungeon, have a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to contain an Angel Statue instead of the first, usually most valuable item in the Chest.
Glowing moss biomes are 50% larger.
It is possible for some random amount of Forest to be replaced with the Jungle, still with all of the same structures that a Forest biome would have, like similar surface caves and a less open Underground than a typical Jungle would have. It is even possible that the Jungle will replace the spawn area and can take up nearly half of the world, from spawn point to one of the Oceans.
It is also possible for the world to generate with no surface Jungle at all.


==== Underworld ====
The Ash Block ground of the Underworld is speckled with 1-block-sized pockets of lava.
Digging up Ash Blocks will sometimes trigger other nearby Ash Blocks to fall (be affected by gravity), similar to Silt. This behavior is closely related to that of Cracked Dungeon Bricks.
All Ruined Houses are made of Hellstone Bricks.


=== Spawn rates ===
The spawn rate is multiplied by 0.8× (resulting in 1.25× faster spawns) and max spawns are multiplied by 1.2×.
These multipliers are applied after the spawn rate and max spawns are capped at 1/60 and 15, respectively, meaning they can increase the spawn rate to 1/48 and max spawns to 18.


=== NPCs, critters, and enemies ===
The Demolitionist replaces the Guide as the starting NPC.
Bunnies (even when they are placed or spawned from Statues) and Demons have a 2/3 (66.67%) chance of being replaced by Explosive Bunnies and Voodoo Demons, respectively.
Hornets and Moss Hornets shoot stingers roughly twice as fast and shoot stingers in random directions upon death.
Web Spit projectiles from the Black Recluse and Jungle Creeper randomly place Cobwebs within a 13×13 rectangular area when the projectile disappears.
Rock Golems release one Boulder projectile upon death.
Vile Spits travel faster. They cannot be destroyed when they are above surface.
Slimes carrying Torches can inflict the On Fire! debuff.
Man Eaters have 40% more range (15.6 → 21.9 tile reach when not extended, 20.3 → 28.4 tile reach when extended) and 17% higher top speed (15.3 → 17.9 mph).
Fighter AI enemies that could only open doors during a Blood Moon are no longer able to do so. However, they may still rarely open doors while the player is in a Graveyard.
Bone Serpents gain 100 extra base health, and +2 defense, +4 base damage, 110% size for all segments.
Before Skeletron is defeated, the following enemies do not drop any loot. Killing them also does not increase their kill count.


=== Gameplay ===
Pots may drop lit bombs that shortly explode, instead of collectible Bomb items.
Trees often drop lit bombs when shaken, instead of their usual items.
Blocks take only half as many hits with a pickaxe or drill to break, rounded up.
Trees and cacti generally require fewer hits to destroy (see Axe power for details).
Red Potions can be found in Chests. When consumed, these apply three random buffs (instead of applying many debuffs like in other world seeds) for 30 minutes.
Tombstones that drop from players deal damage.
After breaking, Boulders split into 2–4 smaller Mini Boulders in random directions, which deal 75% of the Boulder's damage.
Crispy Honey Blocks inflict Burning when touched, have a 1/2 (50%) chance to release lava when mined, and are highlighted by Dangersense Potions.
Spikes and Wooden Spikes cannot be destroyed by explosives.
The Star Cannon and Super Star Shooter only deal 90% damage and their use time is increased by 10%.
The player's light vision is reduced by 12% in the Jungle Temple and by 6% in the Dungeon.
Gills Potion will also cause the player to become unable to breathe outside of water or honey.


=== Bosses ===
Bosses receive numerous changes to their stats and AIs in For the Worthy worlds.


==== Size ====
Many bosses and/or their minions are either larger or smaller than normal. Size scales are displayed in the following tables, with 100% being the original size.


==== Damage ====
As a general rule, bosses and their minions are affected by the same contact damage buffs reported above for regular enemies, while damage from other attacks is not affected. However, there are some exceptions. For instance:

The Eye of Cthulhu's contact damage in its second form is unchanged.
Some other unintuitive changes:
The Lunatic Cultist's damage from Ancient Light and Prophecy's End is increased, because they are NPCs that deal contact damage.
Duke Fishron's damage from Detonating Bubbles and Sharkrons is increased, because they are NPCs that deal contact damage.
The Eater of Worlds' damage from Vile Spit is not increased, despite it being an NPC.


==== Projectile reflection ====

Some bosses or boss parts (Eye of Cthulhu, Skeletron, Plantera's Tentacle) will be able to reflect projectiles in certain states. See the AI section below for details.
Additionally, many bosses and their minions/parts/segments will reflect the projectiles from the Star Cannon and Super Star Shooter, this includes: Eye of Cthulhu and its Servant of Cthulhu, all Eater of Worlds' segments, Brain of Cthulhu and its Creepers, Skeletron (head and both hands), Wall of Flesh and its Hungries and Leeches, Retinazer, Spazmatism, all The Destroyer's segments and its Probes, Skeletron Prime (head and all four hands), Plantera, Plantera's Hook and Plantera's Tentacle, all parts of the Golem, and all parts of the Moon Lord.


==== AI ====
All bosses (with the exception of Duke Fishron, and Deerclops) receive certain changes to their AI:

King Slime
Top horizontal speed during jumps is increased, allowing King Slime to cover more distance with jumps (low jumps: 23 mph → 31 mph, normal jumps: 20 mph → 32 mph, high jumps: 18 mph → 31 mph).
Eye of Cthulhu
First form:
Spawns one more Servant of Cthulhu per each cycle (4 → 5).
When spawning Servants of Cthulhu, its maximum speed is faster (Expert: 36 mph → 41 mph, Classic: 26 mph → 31 mph); acceleration is also increased.
Then it will slowly charge to the player three times; the initial speed is increased (Expert: 36 mph → 41 mph, Classic: 31 mph → 36 mph).
The deceleration between two charges is enhanced and the period of deceleration is shortened (Expert: 1.67s → 1.42s, Classic: 2.5s → 2.25s)
Spawns Servants of Cthulhu and reflects projectiles when transforming from first form to second form.
Second form:
When heading to the player while above 50% health, the initial speed is increased by 20%.
When hanging in the air above the player, its maximum moving speed (which depends on the distance to the player) is increased by 10 mph; acceleration is also increased.
Will spin in place, spawn new Servants of Cthulhu and reflect projectiles after chain dashes, similar to the transformation between first and second form.
Eater of Worlds
All segments have +2 defense.
Maximum speed is increased by 20 mph (Expert: 61 mph → 82 mph, Classic: 51 mph → 72 mph); acceleration is also increased.
Body segments shoot Vile Spit twice as often, and can shoot while below the surface in Expert Mode. Body segments still cannot shoot Vile Spit if in front of background walls.
Killing head segments releases Big Eaters of Souls that can shoot Vile Spit at the player.
When Eater of Worlds is alive, all Eaters of Souls will gain +2 defense and have 1.5× health.
This stat change affects all Eaters of Souls that spawn during the fight and overrides Hardmode stat changes.
Brain of Cthulhu
Brain of Cthulhu has an additional 1.2× damage multiplier, for a total of 65 / 97 / 173 damage.
Brain of Cthulhu has a 1.5× defense multiplier, for a total of 21 defense.
Spawns with 40 Creepers, twice as many as normal.
When Creepers are charging at the player, their acceleration is about 8/3 times compared to Expert Mode. Creeper charging frequency is √(8/3)~1.6 times compared to Expert Mode.
The Brain of Cthulhu itself moves 3 times as fast in its first phase.
The Brain of Cthulhu has fully opaque shadows for the entirety of its second phase after taking its first hit, regardless of difficulty.
Gravity is reversed during its second phase, and cannot be reversed by gravity-reversing items (e.g. Gravitation Potions and the Gravity Globe).
During this phase, the player can leave the top world border. Doing so will kill the player and display one of the following unique death messages:
“<Player name> became an astronaut.”
“<Player name> is now space debris.”
“<Player name> left orbit.”
“<Player name> has ascended.”
“<Player name> departed <world name>.”
Queen Bee
Adds 0.5 enrage coefficient constantly wherever the player fights the Queen Bee. The following discussion shows how the enraged Queen Bee behaves differently.
Phase 0 (Dashing at the player)
Dashing is not strictly horizontal. With more enrage coefficient, the dashing can be more tilted.
Dashing speed increased (FTW contribution is 18 mph).
After dashing at the player, the Queen Bee needs to adjust her position. The enraged Queen Bee can adjust faster.
Braking capability after dashing is also enhanced.
Dashing distance is shortened (FTW contribution is 3.125 tiles in width).
Phase 1 (Spawning Bees)
Spawns Bees more frequently.
Phase 3 (Shooting stingers)
Shoots stingers more frequently (FTW contribution is that the interval of two stingers is 2 ticks shorter).
Stinger speed is increased (FTW contribution is 18 mph).
Precision of stingers targeting the player is increased (FTW contribution is 24%).
In one phase cycle, the Queen Bee will shoot less stingers (FTW contribution is 3).
If the Queen Bee cannot shoot stingers at the player due to its position, its acceleration to adjust itself is increased dramatically.
No changes applied to the second phase (approaching the player to prepare shooting bees) and fourth phase (charging at the player if they are too far away).
Skeletron
When Skeletron is not spinning, its acceleration is increased. Compared to Expert Mode, vertical acceleration is increased by 33%, horizontal acceleration is increased by 71%.
When Skeletron is shooting homing skulls at the player, frequency is increased by 25% (one hand down or life below 75%: 10 → 13 per cycle, two hands down: 20 → 25 per cycle).
When spinning at the player, its velocity is increased by 30%..
This velocity increase is overridden by Red Hat variant's 40% speed increase.
If any Skeletron Hand is alive, Skeletron will reflect projectiles when spinning.
Summons Dark Casters throughout the fight.
When Skeletron is alive, all Dark Casters will gain +6 defense and have 1.5× health; all Water Spheres cannot be destroyed, and their speed is increased by 66.7% (if the Dark Mage is a Red Hat variant, Water Spheres' speed is increased by 33.3% instead).
This stat change affects all Dark Casters that spawn during the fight and overrides Hardmode stat changes.
Skeletron also allows all Dungeon casters, including those that spawn post-Plantera, to teleport to locations without Dungeon walls. They lose this ability again after Skeletron is defeated or despawns.
3 Dark Casters will be spawned when a Skeletron Hand is killed. When both hands are killed, they will continuously spawn, and up to 6 can exist at the same time.
As mentioned above, before defeating Skeletron, the summoned Dark Casters will not drop any loot, nor does killing them increases their kill count.
Wall of Flesh

Has an additional 1.5× health multiplier, for a total of 16,800 / 21,420 / 28,560 health.
The Wall of Flesh's mouth and eyes have +3 defense.
Increased speed, see tables to the right.
Leeches' body segment gains +10 base damage and +14 defense.
Summons Fire Imps throughout the fight.
While the Wall of Flesh is alive, all Fire Imps will gain +10 defense, have 1.5× health, teleport and shoot Burning Spheres faster; all Burning Spheres travel at 72 mph and cannot be destroyed.
Up to 4 Fire Imps can exist at the same time.

Queen Slime
Horizontal speed during low and normal jumps in first phase is increased, allowing her to cover more distance with jumps (low jumps: 23 mph → 37 mph, normal jumps: 20 mph → 37 mph).
Fires 15 Regal Gel projectiles in her second phase instead of 10. Additionally, the spacing between projectiles in both phases is reduced from 36° to 24°.
No longer pauses for a short time before slamming down during her Queenly Smash attack.
When slamming down during her Queenly Smash attack, her acceleration is increased by 100% and her top falling speed is increased by 14.2%.
The Twins
Retinazer
When shooting lasers in its first form, its maximum velocity and acceleration are increased by 15% (Expert: 42 mph → 48 mph, Classic: 36 mph → 41 mph).
Can shoot 5 more lasers during its first form in one cycle (Expert: 9~21 → 14~26 per cycle depending on health, Classic: 9 → 14 per cycle, one cycle lasts 600 ticks)).
Initial velocity of dashing at the player in its first form increased by 10 mph, thus dashing distance increased (Expert: 13%, Classic: 17%).
Maximum velocity and acceleration in the whole second form are increased by 15% (Expert: 49 mph → 56 mph, Classic: 41 mph → 47 mph).
Spazmatism
When shooting cursed flames in both forms, its maximum velocity and acceleration are increased by 15% (first form: 61 mph → 71 mph, second form Expert: 37 mph → 43 mph, second form Classic: 20 mph → 24 mph).
Can shoot 4 more Cursed Flames in its first form in one cycle (Expert: 9~15 → 13~19 per cycle depending on health, Classic: 9 → 13 per cycle, one cycle lasts 600 ticks).
Initial velocity dashing to the player in its first form is increased by 20%, thus the dashing distance is also increased by 20%. The second form is not affected.
Skeletron Prime
Bombs shot by the Prime Cannon can destroy blocks.
This effect is disabled if the Celebration Mk 10 seed is active.
The Destroyer
Has an increased number of segments (80 → 100, not including the head and tail).
Acceleration increased.
Plantera
Maximum speed and acceleration increased by 15% (Expert: 20/34/45 mph → 23/39/52 mph, Classic: 13/26/36 mph → 15/29/41 mph at 100%/50%/25% health).
Projectile cooldown decreased.

Changes to Plantera's Tentacles:
More Plantera's Tentacles are spawned in Plantera's second form (around Plantera: +6, around Plantera's Hook: +3).
Plantera's Tentacles have a 1/10 (10%) chance to reflect projectiles.
Plantera's Tentacle's acceleration dramatically increased.
This acceleration increase makes the Tentacles stay within a small radius around Plantera or her Hook depending on remaining health instead of swinging around, which actually makes the battle more complicated.
Plantera's Hooks will spawn pink thorny bushes around it each time it grabs on a tile. These do 100 base damage.
Golem
Attacks significantly faster, in addition to being able to phase through blocks much faster. In the second stage, the body jumps much higher and the head fires lasers faster.
While Golem is alive, nearby players (125 tiles or less away from the Golem) will have their light vision further reduced by 40%. The resulting effect of this is similar to the effect of the Darkness and Blackout debuffs.
Destroys any torches that come into contact with the body or Golem Fists.
Visual effects of debuffs inflicted to any part of Golem are hidden. (e.g. fire particles of Cursed Inferno; yellow tint of Ichor).
Empress of Light
Cycles faster between attacks (0.75s/0.33s → 0.38s/0.17s for normal/enraged stage).
Lunatic Cultist
Cycles faster between attacks.
Moon Lord
Will erupt 30 Moon Boulders from its head eye after each Phantasmal Deathray attack. These boulders share similar behaviors to Bouncy Boulders, which ricochet on solid blocks, and can exist for a relatively long time. However, they are much faster than Bouncy Boulders.


== Tips ==
Due to the essentially doubled amount of drops, farming the Brain of Cthulhu, and more significantly, its Creepers can be a reliable way to make absurd amounts of money.
Explosive Bunnies can be collected and used as weapons early on, due to their high damage and abundance. However, caution is advised, as they can easily take out the player as well.
Lowered visibility in Dungeons and Jungle Temples can be circumvented by changing the lighting mode to either "Trippy", or "Retro". The former tends to provide the highest increase to visibility.


== Trivia ==
For the Worthy directly references the tooltip of the Red Potion, 'Only for those who are worthy'.
In For the Worthy, several mechanics reference very early versions of Terraria where they were standard behavior: This includes the Locked Gold Chests generating on Floating Islands, all Ruined Houses being made out of Hellstone Bricks, Ash Blocks collapsing at random, and Chests containing an Angel Statue instead of a valuable item.
A For the Worthy world is referred to in the source code as getGoodWorld.
The frame of Demonite Bricks/Crimtane Bricks created by the defeat of the Wall of Flesh in For the Worthy worlds will be slightly smaller, going from 9×9 blocks to 7×7 blocks, likely to stay consistent with the Wall of Flesh's decreased size.

title: Windy Day
content:
A Windy Day is an event that occurs between 7:30 AM and 4:30 PM when the wind speed is greater than or equal to 20 mph. This event only occurs when at least one Life Crystal has been used.The event will stop when the wind speed decreases past 16 mph. The wind can either come from the east or the west, making background objects like trees, vines, plants, banners, and lanterns sway in the same direction.
During the event, unique enemies such as slimes attached to Windy Balloons and Angry Dandelions will spawn, and exclusive items can be obtained.
If Rain occurs at the same time as a Windy Day, it will result in a Thunderstorm.


== Content ==


=== NPC quotes ===
Most NPCs display unique quotes during a Windy Day when spoken to:


== Notes ==
Oftentimes, other enemy kites will frequently drop during the event, along with Ladybug spawns also being frequent. This is because both the other enemy kites and Ladybugs appear when the wind speed is greater than or equal to 20 mph, which is the same wind speed needed to start the event.
However, the event being active does not inherently mean that these things will happen, since the event can still be active even if the wind speeds drop under 20 mph after it has already started.
The Windy Day music only plays in the Forest and Hallow biomes and will override the Town Day theme if near a town.
A side effect of this is if the player is in a town in a surface biome outside of the two above (such as the Jungle) the respective biome's music will play rather than the Town Day or the Windy Day track. This does not apply underground.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==

Windy Balloons and lost kites can occasionally appear as ambient entities, flying around in the background during the event.

title: Celestial Sigil
content:
The Celestial Sigil is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist boss-summoning item that summons the Moon Lord when used. It can be used in any biome, at any time. Rather than summoning the Moon Lord instantly, it triggers a 12-second countdown before he spawns.
The Celestial Sigil can only be used under the following circumstances:

The world is in Hardmode.
Golem has been defeated.
There is no invasion event active, including the Lunar Events.
There is no boss alive.
The Moon Lord is not already being summoned.
The Mysterious Tablet is not visible to any player.
Upon successful use of the Celestial Sigil, the Cultists at the Dungeon will despawn.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
The Celestial Sigil resembles the Mysterious Tablet, the strange idol at the Dungeon's entrance, which spawns along with the Cultists and is destroyed when the Lunatic Cultist is summoned.
The four colors on the rim of the sigil represent the colors of the four Celestial Pillars and the center depicts the Moon Lord's face.
The item was implemented to reduce the amount of time required to farm the Moon Lord. Before 1.3.0.5, simply reaching the Moon Lord could take upwards of 10 to 15 minutes.
It is one of the two boss-summoning items that do not immediately summon the corresponding boss, the other being the Prismatic Lacewing.

title: Tipsy
content:
Tipsy is a debuff that provides the following effects to players:

-4 defense
+10% melee damage
+2% melee critical strike chance
+10% melee speed
+5 Fishing Power
Reduces the average time to produce Poo by 66.67%
While the effects are mostly beneficial, it is still a debuff and therefore cannot be removed manually like buffs. Instead, it can be removed by healing at the Nurse.
Tipsy can also be applied to NPCs (by using the Ale Tosser). This makes NPCs produce Ale particle effect, and grants affected NPCs:

1.1× defense
1.1× damage
0.9× attack interval (about +11% attack speed)
These increases is calculated multiplicatively after all other NPC stat boosts have been calculated.

title: Celestial Wand
content:
The Celestial Wand is a pet-summoning item that spawns Estee to follow the player. When the player is far enough away, Estee will emit a bright yellow beam trail while flying at high speed in order to catch up to them, which resembles that of a Fallen Star. The Celestial Wand can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum, and is always sold alongside the Star Princess set.


== Trivia ==
The Celestial Wand and its companion vanity set, the Star Princess set, are a reference to Rosalina from the 2007 platform action-adventure video game Super Mario Galaxy.
The Estee pet bears a great resemblance to the Power Stars from the 1996 3D-platforming game Super Mario 64, as well as Lumas from Super Mario Galaxy.
Equipping Reflective Obsidian Dye in the pet dye slot causes Estee to resemble Power Stars from Super Mario 64 that have already been collected.
Despite being a star, Estee does not provide any light.

title: Rage Potion
content:
The Rage Potion is a buff potion which grants the Rage buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's critical strike chance by 10%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Summon weapons do not benefit from this potion as they are unaffected by the player's critical strike chance.
It can be considered the Crimson equivalent to the Wrath Potion, although they are not actually mutually exclusive and players can benefit from both effects.
It is possible to naturally acquire a Rage Potion in a Corruption world by purchasing Crimson Seeds from the Dryad in a Hardmode Graveyard biome, and using the Crimson Seeds to make an artificial Crimson biome to fish in.

title: Calming Potion
content:
The Calming Potion is a buff potion which grants the Calm buff when consumed. The buff reduces the enemy spawn rate by 39%, and the maximum number of enemies on-screen is reduced by 40%. This lasts for 12 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Calming Potions can be found in Pots and Crates.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The buff does not reduce enemy spawn rates during the Pumpkin Moon, Frost Moon, or Frost Legion events.
The Calm buff will stack with the buff provided by Peace Candles and the Happy! buff from Sunflowers, further reducing enemy spawn rates.
The Battle Potion has the opposite effect.
The Calm buff also reduces the spawn rate of critters, as do all other artificial reductions to enemy spawn rates, besides the presence of Town NPCs.


== Tips ==
If the player wants to loot the Chests in the Dungeon and already has a sufficient number of Golden Keys, using this potion before entering may be a good idea.
While not directly helpful against bosses themselves, it can be useful to use against some like the Queen Bee or the Wall of Flesh whose biomes typically have numerous enemy spawns which could make the fight harder, or when mining Meteorite to curb Meteor Head spawns.

title: Poisoned
content:
Poisoned is a debuff that prevents health regeneration and causes the afflicted entity to take damage every second for the duration of the debuff. Players lose 2 health per second (1 damage displayed every 0.5 seconds), whereas enemies lose 6 health per second (1 damage displayed every 0.17 seconds).
Its damage can be increased by Accelerated Afflictions.
Visually, the debuff causes afflicted entities to gain a green tint, and the player's eyes will squint while they are afflicted.
The debuff can be negated by equipping the Bezoar or its derivatives.

title: Monster Meat
content:
The Monster Meat is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pig Man that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pig Man flies while carrying an Umbrella from Don't Starve in order to catch up. The Monster Meat can be dropped from most Corruption or Crimson enemies with a 1/1500 (0.07%) chance. On The Constant seed, the drop rate is increased to a 1/500 (0.2%) chance.


== Trivia ==
The tooltip of the item is a reference to Willow's examination quote for the Monster Meat in Don't Starve.
The tooltip of the buff is a reference to Woodie's examination quote for the Pig in Don't Starve.
The Umbrella that the Pig Man carries while flying is ironically made of Pig Skin.
The Eye of Terror in Don't Starve will drop Monster Meat, but the Eye of Cthulhu in Terraria will not.
An Eater of Souls spawned by a Corrupt Statue has a 1/30000 (0.0033%) chance of dropping the Monster Meat, the lowest drop rate of any item from any enemy assuming neutral luck.

title: Durendal
content:
The Durendal is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss whip. It has a 20% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

9 tag damage
Marks enemies with enchanted energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Durendal, the hit deals 30 extra damage and a visual bright flash appears. The mark expires after its effect is triggered once, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the tag damage will still last for its usual duration.
Grants the Durendal's Blessing buff, increasing whip speed by 25% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits.
Its best modifier is Legendary.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The 30 flat damage granted by enchanted energy is applied after other damage bonuses, but before damage of the hit is reduced by enemy's defense.


== Tips ==
The Durendal is a good choice to use with the Blade Staff due to its high summon tag damage and flat damage bonus from the enchanted energy.


== Trivia ==
This item's name is in reference to a historical sword of the same name, wielded by the paladin Roland of Charlemagne's court.
The Durendal's inventory sprite is unique among whips in that it resembles a sword.
The Durendal is internally referred to as SwordWhip.
The design of the Durendal being a sword with a long, segmented, and flexible whip-like blade could be a reference to the urumi, a similar weapon originating from the Indian subcontinent.

title: Slimy Saddle
content:
The Slimy Saddle is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Slime Mount. The Slime Mount offers increased jump height (21 tiles) and movement speed (20 mph), increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles, reduces fall damage by 50%, and enables floating on surfaces of all liquids and continuous auto-jump by holding the ↷ Jump key. Landing on an enemy while riding this mount will deal 40 summon damage and a knockback of 5 (Average), and causes the player to bounce off them. The Slime Mount is affected by summon damage bonuses.
The Slimy Saddle has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by King Slime and a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in King Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.


== Notes ==
Players move at double the normal vertical speed while riding the Slime Mount.
Items that allow double jumps and items that prevent fall damage work as normal while riding the Slime Mount.
The Slime Mount's damage is not variable (i.e., unaffected by the usual ±15% randomization), rendering it very useful for enemy defense tests in-game.
The Slime Mount applies 10 ticks of global invincibility frames upon hit.
Damaging an enemy with the Slime Mount grants the player 0.1 seconds (6 ticks) of invincibility frames, meaning that they cannot take damage immediately after jumping on an enemy.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Since the Slime Mount bounces off of Target Dummies, it is possible to create an elevator with them and the mount.
A player can easily move from the bottom of a large body of water, honey, or lava to the surface by mounting the Slimy Saddle, as the Slime Mount will float to the top.
The doubled vertical speed can be extremely useful, e.g. for traveling down hellevators with great speed, or by using it to dodge attacks.
By grappling to a wall and activating the mount mid-way, the bright particle effects will go about 16 blocks through, thus revealing caverns and valuables. Combined with the zoomed-in overlay map, this is a good way to explore the underground early on. Note that to activate the mount while grappling, there needs to be enough space at the point of activation for the mount to appear. This same practice can be applied in a vertical manner, allowing the player to reveal an Enchanted Sword Shrine from the surface.

Using the Slime Mount just before the flight time of the Rocket Boots ends will propel the player upwards a few extra blocks.
Using the Slime Mount immediately after the start of any jump allows the player to go slightly higher than if they started that jump riding it.
This means if the player dismounts, jumps, immediately re-mounts, then at the top of the jump repeats, they will get significantly more height. For example, with a Sandstorm in a Balloon, this method gives a jump height of up to 96 tiles, compared to 67 tiles staying mounted the whole time; a 43% increase in height.
If the Slime Mount jumps while floating atop a body of water, it may jump again in midair, resulting in a double jump. Note that this is slightly inconsistent.
The Slime Mount can be used as a viable source of damage against enemies and bosses.
It is useful against early-game bosses like the Eye of Cthulhu because it drastically reduces the chance of receiving contact damage from them. However, bouncing on them repeatedly may lead to a rapid ascension which poses the threat of dying to fall damage. Additionally, because of the Slime Mount's high vertical movement speed, the boss might despawn due to the large distance.
Worm-like enemies, particularly the Eater of Worlds, can be fought very effectively in spaces with a low ceiling.
Players can fish while floating on the surface of water using the Slimy Saddle.


== Trivia ==
The Slimy Saddle is among the few pre-Hardmode items with a rarity of , along with most other pre-Hardmode mounts.

title: Music
content:
Terraria has over one hundred music tracks. Each one will play and loop endlessly while the player is in a specific biome or while certain events are taking place. Music is individual to each player, and as such its volume can be lowered or disabled entirely within the settings menu.
The Music Box accessory allows recording the in-game music to play it back at any time.
On the  Desktop version, each music track can be replaced with a custom file through the use of Resource Packs.
The majority of music in Terraria was composed by Scott Lloyd Shelly of Resonance Array. Deerclops' track was composed by Klei Entertainment, the Torch God's track was composed by Prosthetic Orchestra, and the Day Remix track was composed by Xenon and DSniper.


== Otherworldly tracks ==
The 27 tracks of the soundtrack originally written for the canceled game Terraria: Otherworld were added to Terraria with the Journey's End update. When Drunk seed is active while Remix and Zenith seeds are inactive, Otherworld soundtracks will replace the regular soundtrack. Additionally, entering a Drunk world for the first time permanently unlocks a “Music” option in the Party Girl's dialogue window, allowing the player to toggle the soundtrack replacement. Once unlocked, the option to toggle the music will be permanently available across all characters and worlds.

In a multiplayer world, players only hear the altered soundtrack if they have used the “Music” option themselves, which is only present if they have unlocked it before by visiting a Drunk world. However, all players can listen to Otherworldly Music Boxes in multiplayer worlds, regardless of whether they have toggled or unlocked the option before.
Upon leaving the world, the soundtrack replacement resets, reverting the music to the world's default setting.
Every track in Terraria's soundtrack is replaced, but there are fewer tracks in total. Tracks that do not have a Terraria: Otherworld equivalent will use the most relevant track; for example, the Underground Jungle will simply use Terraria: Otherworld's Jungle theme, rather than Terraria's Underground Jungle theme.
Tracks follow the same naming convention as Terraria's, resulting in some duplicated names. Music Boxes for these tracks disambiguate by being called Otherworldly Music Box instead of just Music Box.


== List ==
The following table lists all music tracks as they are ordered internally. The track titles are based on the names of the respective Music Boxes.


== Trivia ==
The track The Towers was released on the soundtrack album Terraria Soundtrack Volume 2 two years before its introduction to the game in 1.3.0.1. It was originally intended for the final boss, but plans had changed in the meantime.
The Martian Madness track was originally released as a 1.3 spoiler.
Volume 5 of the Soundtrack albums features an alternate track for Skeletron, which is a dramatic dubstep track. However, no Music Box of it can be obtained in-game, nor is it in the game files, unlike the alternate track for Queen Bee.

title: Arms Dealer
content:
The Arms Dealer is an NPC vendor who mainly sells ammunition items as well as guns. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
The player has at least one bullet or bullet-firing gun in their inventory (guns and bullets stored in storage items like chests, or portable storage items like the Piggy Bank do not count towards this requirement).
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Arms Dealer is killed, he will automatically respawn after some time.
The Arms Dealer will defend himself against nearby enemies with a Flintlock Pistol, before upgrading to a Minishark during Hardmode. He deals 24 / 36 / 42 damage in pre-Hardmode, which decreases to 15 / 22 / 26 damage in Hardmode to balance the Minishark's fire rate, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.


== Spawning criteria ==
Below is a list of qualifying guns and bullets. At least one of these must be in the player's inventory for the Arms Dealer to spawn.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Arms Dealer will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Tips ==
The easiest way to acquire a qualifying gun is to smash either a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart in The Corruption or The Crimson. They will always drop a Musket or an Undertaker, respectively, on the first break.
The Musket and Undertaker can also be found in Corrupt Crates and Crimson Crates, respectively.
Other qualifying early guns include the Boomstick (from Ivy Chests and Jungle Crates) and the Red Ryder (from Presents).
The Flare Gun and its Flares do not qualify.
Bullets can also be obtained from the Party Girl. When there is a Party thrown, buy the Pigronata, which can drop Party Bullets.


== Names ==
The Arms Dealer may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
The name Brimst may be a reference to brimstone (sulfur), one of the ingredients of gunpowder.
He seems to be attracted to both the Nurse and the Dryad. This is seen in his quote about a date with the Nurse, and the Dryad's quote about him flirting with her. He also flirts with the Mechanic, according to her quote about the pressure plate, but he seemingly has more of an interest in the Nurse.
His interest in the Nurse is further backed by selling her clothes on Halloween instead of his own (though on a technical level, the Nurse does not have a shop interface to sell any items with).

The Arms Dealer and the Demolitionist have a rivalry between them, which is referenced by some of their quotes.
They can also be seen arguing over guns and explosives during the credits.
The Arms Dealer and the Guide appear to not get along. This is evidenced by them frequently arguing through emotes, along with the Arms Dealer's quote “I heard there is a doll that looks very similar to <name of Guide> somewhere in the underworld.  I'd like to put a few rounds in it.”. Despite this, they do not have any effect on eachother's happiness.
The Mechanic and the Goblin Tinkerer will similarly flirt through emotes. These are the only four NPCs to have unique interactions when talking to a specific NPC.
His quote “Hey, this ain't a movie, pal. Ammo is extra.” is a reference to the fact that in most movies, the protagonists or other characters seemingly never run out of ammo.
 The Bestiary entry for the Arms Dealer: "The Arms Dealer has everything anyone could need to shoot things dead, from little round bullets to guns made from sharks."

title: Mana Booster
content:
The Mana Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Mana Nebula buff which immediately increases the player's mana regeneration rate by 10 mana per second for 8 seconds. When a Mana Booster is picked up while the Mana Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Mana Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Mana Booster expires, and the Mana Nebula buff decreases by one level.
Mana Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.


== Tiers ==


== Notes ==
Unlike other sources of mana regeneration, the regeneration provided by the Mana Booster is independent of current mana supply or consumption, and will work even while continuously using a magic weapon.
In multiplayer, any player can pick up Mana Boosters and benefit from the Mana Nebula buff, even if they are not wearing Nebula armor. Additionally, picking up a Mana Booster will grant all nearby players (within a 43.75-tile radius) one instance of Mana Nebula. If the player acquiring the Mana Booster is on a team, only nearby players within that team will obtain the buff.


== See also ==
Damage Booster
Life Booster

title: Parrot Cracker
content:
The Parrot Cracker is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Parrot that follows the player. If the player stays still for long enough, it will perch on a nearby solid block, staying still until the player moves away from it. The Parrot Cracker can be purchased from the Pirate for 3 Platinum 75 Gold if he is spoken to in an Ocean biome.


== Trivia ==
The Parrot Cracker is the second most expensive item to buy, more expensive than the Steampunk Wings (3 Platinum) and Clentaminator (2 Platinum), but is surpassed by the Companion Cube (5 Platinum).
The Parrot Cracker when sold by a Pirate who is homeless or far from home will cost 5 Platinum 62 Gold 50 Silver. This would make it the most expensive item in the game to purchase.
The pet Parrot is similar to the Parrot enemy, which can potentially cause confusion among idle parrots during a Pirate Invasion.
The pet's buff tooltip, "Polly wants the cracker", is a reference to the phrase "Polly want a cracker", which is said to have originated in the 1883 adventure novel Treasure Island by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson, or the popular slogan for the original saltine cracker by the American cookie and snack manufacturer Nabisco in 1876. However, the phrase can be verified to have been in use even before those dates.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) "Wants" contains an errant apostrophe.

title: Bone Key
content:
The Bone Key is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Skeletron Head that follows the player. The Baby Skeletron Head floats around the player and sometimes spins its head, similarly to Skeletron's spinning head attack or the Dungeon Guardians in general. This action may also occur if the player is a bit further away from the Skeletron Head. The Bone Key is always dropped by Dungeon Guardians. Because Dungeon Guardians have extremely high stats intended to instantly kill all players, this can be a difficult item to acquire.


== Notes ==
This item cannot be obtained in a world where Skeletron has already been defeated, as Dungeon Guardians will no longer spawn.
Similar to the Zephyr Fish, the head that follows the player will not teleport to them when they end up a long distance away from it but instead keep moving towards the player. One can instantly teleport it back to themselves by toggling the visibility of it off, then back on again in their pet slot.
Alternatively, if being used as a summon from the player's inventory, they can simply re-summon it.


== Tips ==


== Trivia ==
The Bone Key is most likely designed and named after a 19th century bit key, known erroneously and commonly as a skeleton key.
Despite being extremely difficult to acquire, it only sells for 5 Gold.


== See also ==
Possessed Skull(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a similar pet dropped from Skeletron in Master Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

title: Flipper Potion
content:
The Flipper Potion is a buff potion which grants the Flipper buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to move horizontally and vertically through water, lava, and honey without slowing down, and also allows the player to swim without equipping any swimming accessories, such as the Flipper. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Flipper Potions can be found in Pots and crates.

title: Ice Queen
content:
The Ice Queen is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Frost Moon event. She is the event's final enemy and can move freely through blocks. She is the equivalent to the Pumpking from the Pumpkin Moon, being the Frost Moon's most powerful enemy, coming in at the last waves of the event, and being the event's only flying boss.
Defeating the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event will add 150 / 300 / 375 points to the final score, giving the most number of points for any enemy in the event.


== Behavior ==
The Ice Queen's behavior is characterized by astonishingly fast movement and evasive maneuvers while constantly firing off ranged attacks aimed toward the player. She will hover and attempt to position herself above the player while randomly cycling through the following attacks:

The Ice Queen flies across the screen from left to right while shooting Frost Waves at the player.
The Ice Queen hovers above the player while raining Frost Shards from below her. The Frost Shards from this attack deal slightly more damage (74 / 148 / 222).
The Ice Queen remains stationary before spinning in the air and shooting Frost Shards in randomized directions. The Frost Shards from this attack fly in long horizontal arcs before being affected by gravity and deal slightly less damage (70 / 140 / 210).
As the Ice Queen's health is depleted, her acceleration and maximum horizontal speed increase. Additionally, the firing rates of her attacks increase, as detailed in the following table. Note that these changes happen as the Ice Queen's health passes the listed thresholds, and are not continuous; thus, for example, her frost wave firing rate will be 2.07 waves/second at 100% health and also at 75% health, but as soon as her health drops below 75%, the rate of fire will increase to 2.22/sec.


== Notes ==
The Ice Queen begins spawning during the Frost Moon event at wave 11.
During the final waves of the Frost Moon there may be several Ice Queens on the screen at once.
The Ice Queen has a higher chance of dropping loot in later waves. See Frost Moon § Loot for more details.
The Ice Queen's projectiles inflict the following debuffs:


== Tips ==

Both of the Ice Queen's attacks will inflict the Chilled debuff, which slows the player's movement speed, and Frost Waves will sometimes inflict the Frozen debuff which completely immobilizes the player. Equipping a Hand Warmer or Ankh Shield will negate these effects and potentially make the fight much less frustrating.
Drinking a Warmth Potion is recommended as it will significantly lower the damage the Ice Queen can inflict on the player, and it will last for the entire duration of the event.
The Frozen debuff causes players to exit their mounts. This may kill a player without immunity to fall damage if inflicted at a high enough point in the sky.
The Ice Queen is most vulnerable while executing her twirl attack, when she spins in place rapidly and shoots Frost Shards in all directions. This is the only time she stays in one spot.
The distribution of the Ice Queen's Frost Shards during her twirl attack is weighted such that the projectiles have a significantly higher chance of shooting near-diagonally than near-vertically or near-horizontally. Thus, players standing roughly along one cardinal direction from the Ice Queen (up, down, left, or right from her) have a lesser chance of being hit than players standing diagonally from her.
To mitigate her damage, using wings and possibly movement-enhancing accessories for chasing and dodging, in addition to equipping a Cross Necklace/Star Veil combined with lifesteal (Spectre armor or Vampire Knives), proves very effective.
When attacking with frost waves, she will not fire any towards the player if they are above her. This can be easily be achieved with mounts that have infinite flight time such as the Witch's Broom, and wings using the Soaring Insignia.


== Trivia ==
 The Bestiary entry for the Ice Queen: "If this icy towering monstrosity wishes for someone's soul, they'll surely let it go... right from their cold, dead hands."
This entry may be a reference to Elsa from the Disney media franchise Frozen, since Elsa's most famous song is "Let It Go" and the Bestiary entry for the Ice Queen references the title of that song. Furthermore, Elsa is loosely based on the titular character from "The Snow Queen", an 1844 Danish fairy tale by Hans Christian Andersen.
The comment about stealing souls is almost certainly derived from Andersen's fairy tale.

title: Guide:Eye of Cthulhu strategies
content:
The Eye of Cthulhu is one of the first bosses a player will encounter.


== Spawn Conditions ==
=== Manual ===
The Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned manually using a Suspicious Looking Eye at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM). Only one Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned manually at a time.


=== Random ===
The Eye of Cthulhu can also spawn naturally at the start of the night. Its arrival when spawning naturally is announced by the status message “You feel an evil presence watching you...”.
In order for the boss to spawn naturally, the following conditions must be fulfilled at dusk (7:30 PM):

The Eye of Cthulhu has not yet been defeated in the current world or no placed Demon/Crimson Altars exist in the current world.
At least one player in the world has at least 200 maximum health and at least 11 defense.
At least four town NPCs are present in the world. While the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
No boss is already alive.
None of the following events are active: Lantern Night, Old One's Army, Pumpkin Moon, or Frost Moon.
Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
If the conditions are met, there is a 1/3 (33.33%) chance for the Eye of Cthulhu to spawn. Provided the roll succeeds, the status message appears and a hidden countdown of 1 minute 21 seconds begins. The Eye of Cthulhu spawns at the end of the countdown, at 8:51 PM. Another check is performed at that time, with all of the following conditions needing to be fulfilled in order for the boss to spawn:

At least one player is in the surface or Space layer.
Consequently, the natural spawning of the Eye of Cthulhu can easily be prevented by remaining in a layer lower than the surface for the night. Returning to the surface before dawn will cause it to spawn as normal.
This restriction is lifted in worlds where the world spawn point is below the surface, such as worlds with the special world seed Remix active or the secret world seed Mole people. The Eye of Cthulhu can spawn naturally in those worlds regardless of the player's position, whether they are above or below the surface.
No boss is already alive.
The Lunar Events are not active and the countdown for the spawning of the Moon Lord has not begun, either due to manual summoning or defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar.
Time is not being accelerated by the Enchanted Sundial or Enchanted Moondial.
In singleplayer, exiting the world during the countdown also prevents the Eye of Cthulhu from spawning naturally.
In worlds where the special seeds For the Worthy and The Constant are present but Celebration Mk 10 is not, The Eye of Cthulhu will still be able to randomly spawn, even if it has been defeated before.


== The Fight ==


=== First Phase ===
During this phase the Eye will spend most of its time floating above you. It will summon Servants of Cthulhu which fly towards you to attack, much like Demon Eyes, but can also fly through walls and the ground.
After spawning 3 or 4 Servants, the Eye will charge at you, attempting to ram you 3 times before hovering once more, so be prepared to evade. It turns rather slowly as it charges, giving you time to prepare your next dodge. It can be helpful to begin to evade after the 3rd servant is spawned, as this will often allow you to dodge its first charge.
The Eye has 12 defense during this form, which negates 6 damage from every attack. This means that faster-firing weapons, such as the Minishark, will have their damage affected more than slower firing but higher damage weapons such as the Musket. A Sharktooth Necklace reduces the effect of enemy defense.
The Servants are weak and can be killed for Hearts, or, if there is enough room, the player can simply keep moving in one direction to avoid them. If the player gets swarmed by Servants, temporarily switching to a fast swinging weapon such as a sword or flail will help get rid of them quickly. The Eye does contact damage, so be careful to watch it while you kill the Servants.
Another strategy in this phase is to aim weapons at the pupil of the Eye, since that is where it spawns the Servants. That way, you can kill the servants and damage the Eye. Some piercing weapons can damage the Eye multiple times, such as when firing straight into the air or when using a spear at close range.
If not fighting on platforms, the Eye can go underground momentarily after a charge. Weapons like Whips and spears can hit it through the ground; alternatively, debuffs such as On Fire! from Flaming Arrows apply damage even when the boss is out of reach. Keep in mind that bosses have minimap icons to increase their visibility.
The second phase is triggered when the Eye reaches half health.


=== Second Phase ===
For the last half of the fight, the boss sheds its iris to reveal a fanged mouth. It moves slightly faster and deals more damage when it hits you, but it also has no defense. It no longer summons servants in this phase. Instead, it charges 3 times, and then pauses for a few seconds during which you can attack freely.
Make sure to take advantage of its transformation sequence as much as possible, since it just spins in place for a few moments and you can still damage it.
Dodging is important during this phase, and should be given priority over doing damage. Hermes Boots or a variant of them are extremely useful. With a wide enough arena, running in a straight line while the Eye of Cthulhu does his quick charge is fast enough to avoid any damage, and allows the player to attack continuously.


=== Expert and Master Mode ===
In the first phase of the fight it spawns more servants and enters the second phase at 65% health instead of 50%, spawning 4–5 more Servants in that process. A piercing weapon is recommended for eliminating the Servants.
In this part of the fight, after the 3 normal lunges it will perform a brief series of extremely quick dashes at a steeper angle. As its health goes down, the Eye will use this ability more frequently, until its only action is to dart haphazardly back and forth, making it rather hard to hit. To avoid the lunges, Hermes Boots are practically required.


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain preparation ===

An arena for the Eye of Cthulhu should be large enough to dodge and maneuver around in. The recommended size is just about the size of the screen, as the boss does not require a lot of mobility.
The simplest arena design consists of multiple rows of wooden platforms to have more room to jump and dodge. As the fight will be at night, add Torches to improve visibility. Remember to adjust the distance between platforms depending on your jump height (this is 6 tiles at minimum, depending on which accessories you have, but it can be considerably further if you have a hook), and consider placing some ladders (with platforms or Ropes) to aid your vertical movement.
Another design is a long, relatively flat surface. This allows you to dodge the Eye by running to the left or the right with Swiftness Potions or Hermes Boots.


=== Gearing up ===


==== Armor ====
Ninja armor provides critical hit and speed boosts which benefit all classes. While it has less defense than metal armor, it will help end the fight faster and make dodging easier. It requires defeating King Slime, who can be farmed relatively easily by crafting Slime Crowns.
Fossil armor's is the strongest set available for ranged weapons, but requires entering the dangerous Underground Desert.
Gladiator armor has high defense and provides knockback immunity. It can be farmed from Hoplites in Marble Caves.
The Wizard set provides big buffs to magic weapon's stats. The Jungle armor provides damage and mana bonuses, but requires entering the dangerous Underground Jungle.
The Gem Robes empower Gem staves with different abilities. For this fight, the Amethyst Robe is easy to obtain and has great properties. There are more specifics in the Magic Weapons section below.
The Flinx Fur Coat is the only armor for summoners at this point.
Out of armors made of ore, Gold or Platinum armor have the best defense, although they can be difficult to obtain this early.
A full set of Silver or Tungsten armor is easier to get at this point, and both are good choices for this fight.


==== Weapons ====
In general, long-range piercing weapons are recommended, as they are able to take out Servants and hit the boss.

For Melee Users
Long-range projectile swords can safely attack at a distance. These include the Enchanted Sword found rarely throughout the world, in Enchanted Sword Shrines, or in Golden Crates, the Ice Blade found in Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, the Starfury found on Floating Islands, and the Blade of Grass.
The Mandible Blade can attack rapidly from a distance by being thrown. While it doesn't pierce, it does high damage.
Boomerangs can be of great use due to their long range, but missing with a boomerang can leave the player open to attack while it returns. A Thorn Chakram or Trimarang would be preferred.
Yoyos have good range and allow for fine control. The strongest available is the Amazon, although it requires venturing into the Underground Jungle early on. If a large amount of Demonite or Crimtane Ore has been obtained, a Malaise or Artery can be crafted. A Rally is readily available, but requires some luck and is weaker.
A flail such as the Flaming Mace or Ball O' Hurt can be useful due to their high speed and the ability to use the throw attack to deal high damage.
If Demonite or Crimtane Ore has been found, the Light's Bane or Blood Butcherer are riskier but powerful options, and both have special abilities that aid in the fight (the Light's Bane spawning additional slashes and the Blood Butcherer adding a Bleeding debuff). Other non-projectile swords tend to do poorly against this boss besides clearing out the Servants.
Spears can pierce through the Servants and do high damage to this boss, but can be risky due to short range. The safest spears include the Storm Spear, found in the dangerous Underground Desert, and the The Rotted Fork, a powerful spear found in Crimson Hearts that emits a short shockwave. Other acceptable, but weaker, spears include the Trident found in Water Chests and the Swordfish, found by fishing in the Ocean.
For Ranged users
Guns such as the Minishark and Boomstick are very effective against this boss, but the first is expensive and requires the Arms Dealer to have arrived and the second is only found in the dangerous Underground Jungle. The Musket or The Undertaker are easier to find at this stage of the game, by breaking Shadow Orbs or Crimson Hearts. All guns besides the Musket benefit significantly from the Shark Tooth Necklace and/or Silver/Tungsten Bullets during the first portion of the fight, when the boss's defense is higher.
Bows are easy to craft and do good damage. Among craftable bows, the Gold or Platinum Bow are the best bows available, unless the player happened to find a large quantity of Demonite or Crimtane Ore, in which case they can craft a Demon or Tendon Bow. The Blood Rain Bow is great in this fight, but can only be fished up during a Blood Moon and requires defeating a difficult mini-boss.
Frostburn Arrows deal the most damage to the boss itself and inflict Frostburn, but Jester's Arrows can kill the Servants and hurt the Eye in the same shot. Flaming Arrows are a good fallback option, in case your primary arrow choice runs out.
Bone Javelins are cheap and powerful against the Eye of Cthulhu. They do heavy damage on-hit and add a damaging debuff that stacks. The Bone Throwing Knives is slightly weaker against the boss itself but pierces through the Servants.
The Snowball Cannon is another fast firing weapon to use, doing decently against both phases.
The Snowball Launcher, an immobile turret that shoots snowballs without consuming ammo, can do heavy damage, but requires the Eye to be in front of it. It is best used in spurts after luring the Eye to the target area.
The Paintball Gun, with its fast fire rate and high critical strike chance works well if you can manage to kill the Painter enough times.
Grenades cause high damage and do damage in an area, but can damage the player. Since the Eye will be spawning Servants or charging at the player most of the time, it's difficult to keep a safe distance from the explosion. They can be purchased from the Demolitionist. A good strategy is to throw Grenades behind you as you run away.
Molotov Cocktails avoid the danger of self-injury and work very well, especially in the second stage when Eye of Cthulhu will charge at you through the flaming puddles the Molotov Cocktails leave behind.
Spiky Balls can provide passive damage when scattered about the arena.
Shurikens are an effective consumable ranged weapon which can be bought from the Merchant. Throwing Knives and Poisoned Knives are similar to Shurikens but do more damage.
For Magic users
The Thunder Zapper does great damage, but doesn't pierce and requires exploring the dangerous Underground Desert. Similarly, the Mystic Bloom is a powerful weapon only obtainable by exploring the Underground Jungle.
Gem Staves simple to craft, and their long ranged piercing shots are a perfect fit for the boss battle. The strongest staves in terms of damage and abilities are the Diamond, Ruby, and Amber Staves.
The Amethyst Robe pairs well with those staves by giving them homing properties. The Sapphire Robe pairs well with the Ruby Staff as this combo combines the increased number of projectiles but does not combine the decreases in damage.
The Emerald Staff can do very well when combined with the Amethyst Robe.
The weakest staves (Amethyst, Topaz, and Sapphire Staves) are not recommended as they do not pierce and have low damage.
The Wand of Frosting is relatively easy to obtain and inflicts the strong Frostburn debuff. The Glacier Fang is similar in power but has more variety in usage.
The Daybloom Staff is very weak in the first phase, as the Eye's defense heavily reduces its damage. In the second phase, its lingering projectiles do far more damage and can be left behind for the eye to run into during its dashes.
The Crimson Rod is an excellent side-weapon, as its clouds can be set up to clear out the servants while also dealing steady damage to the boss. Its Corruption counterpart, the Vilethorn, is not as helpful; it lacks some range, and does low damage. However, the lingering thorn can hit the boss and Servants many times, and can even pass through walls to hit it. Both require exploring dangerous biomes and smashing either Crimson Hearts or Shadow Orbs.
In worlds with Remix seed, the Magic Dagger is a viable piercing magic weapon that can be found in chests, trading mana efficiency for power.
For Summoners
The Flinx Staff will likely be the best summon weapon available at this point in the game. Alternatives include the Finch Staff and Abigail's Flower. The Vampire Frog Staff is even stronger, though it may be difficult to obtain at this point as it requires defeating strong Blood Moon enemies.
The Cobwhip is the easiest whip to obtain at this point in the game, although it is weaker than other options.
While rare, Foxparks is a strong option, especially for killing Servants of Cthulhu with the flamethrower attack.
Two somewhat stronger options are Leather Whip, which can be bought from the Zoologist NPC, and the Slime Whip, which can be crafted at a Solidifier.
The Snapthorn is the strongest whip available, but requires exploring the dangerous Underground Jungle.


==== Accessories ====
A Cloud in a Bottle or equivalents can aid in avoiding the rams, although this is less necessary with a good arena.
The Fledgling Wings can be used to give the player short flight time and immunity to fall damage. However, they are very rare.
A Grappling Hook is also very useful if you can grapple onto platforms above you quickly.
Hermes Boots or equivalents help by making it easier to dodge the second phase's rams. In Expert Mode, these are almost required, as the Eye of Cthulhu will perform rapid dashing attacks.
Most movement modifiers do not increase the Boots' maximum speed. However, Magiluminescence has a +20% that stacks with the Boots, making it much easier to outrun the dashes.
The Shark Tooth Necklace will give a significant damage boost to most weapons available at the moment.
For rangers, a Snapping Stone can provide an area of effect attack and boost damage. Similarly, Poison Barb will add damage through the Poisoned debuff. The Harpy Charm can increase critical strike chance and redirect some missed arrows.
A Band of Regeneration can help speed up life regeneration, making lasting a longer fight easier.
Any accessory with the Warding modifier will be useful if you come across one, and the extra four defense can be used to make up for lower-tier armor, like Iron armor or Lead armor.
A White String is a cheap item that players can craft over and over until it gets Warding or Menacing.


==== Potions ====
The most helpful and easily obtainable potions are the Regeneration Potion, the Ironskin Potion, and the Swiftness Potion.
Any food item that gives the Well Fed buff is welcomed, especially so for Expert Mode and Master Mode.
Archery Potion significantly increases the damage output of bows.
Magic Power Potion and Mana Regeneration Potion are good for magic users.


=== Other Tips ===

The Eye of Cthulhu drops either Demonite or Crimtane Ore. While the corresponding set of armor and a number of tools additionally require Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples respectively—which the Eye does not drop—the sword, bow, axe, yoyo, whip, and fishing pole can be crafted with only the bars.
Due to the ease of crafting its summoning item and relatively low difficulty, farming the Eye of Cthulhu is one of the more effective ways of making money prior to Hardmode. It drops 3 Gold / 7 Gold 50 Silver up front, plus ores which can be sold as bars for twice (Demonite) or triple (Crimtane) that amount.
The Eye of Cthulhu will only spawn randomly if a player has more than 10 defense. Taking defense-boosting equipment off before dusk can prevent it from spawning randomly.
The boss looks at the player it will follow, which can be helpful information in multiplayer.
It is most vulnerable during its transformation, because it neither moves nor attacks. However, there is only a brief window of opportunity for this.
Because there are no location-based requirements for summoning, defeating multiple Eyes of Cthulhu in an area can be an effective setup for harder boss fights as the dropped Hearts can be picked up mid-fight as needed, though killing an Eye of Cthulhu for that purpose must be balanced with the time it takes away from killing a night-only boss.
Since Crimtane Ore and Bars sell for a 30% higher price than their Demonite counterparts, farming the Eye of Cthulhu in a Crimson world is more profitable.
In singleplayer, the player can repeatedly pause the game using Autopause in order to properly aim at the Eye of Cthulhu during its dash attacks.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Slimy Saddle Strategy ===
An excellent strategy to beat the Eye in Classic Mode is to use the Slimy Saddle and bounce on the Eye while at the same time attacking it with a ranged weapon. The Eye will move toward you and you will bounce on top of it continuously dealing damage. If you want to try this strategy, make sure you have some forms of preventing fall damage (i.e., the Lucky Horseshoe, Grappling Hook, an Umbrella, or Cloud in a Bottle or Fledgling Wings).


=== Magic Mirror Strategy ===
During the Second Phase, if you have your spawn point nearby, you can run one way and attack, and just when you think that the Eye is going to charge, use a Magic Mirror, Ice Mirror, or Recall Potion to teleport to spawn, now running the other way, evading the attack and being left to open fire.


=== Railway Strategies ===
Another great strategy is to build a long railway at least 400 blocks long, with each end hammered into a bumper. When the Eye spawns, start moving and continue to move whilst shooting at it. It may take longer than other methods, but it requires little mobility and you take minimal damage. Also, this strategy works better if in single player or all players in a multiplayer world are together in the same area.
Alternatively, instead of hammering the ends, the railway can be built into a rhombus with around 200 rails. This keeps the player out of range of the boss for most of the fight, which makes getting hit less likely but also makes it difficult to attack the boss. A fast firing weapon with easily obtainable ammo (like Snowball Cannon or Minishark) will do best with this strategy.


=== Pathway strategy ===
This strategy requires some form of fast running (e.g. Hermes Boots) or a mount such as the Roller Skates or Chillet, together with an arena with 2 long pathways made out of platforms. Make sure that the platforms are parallel to each other and at least 4 blocks apart. Make sure the length of the 2 platforms are around 200 to 500 blocks. 
When the fight begins, run along the 2 platforms attacking the Eye. Switch between the platforms to dodge attacks and avoid the Servants of Cthulhu. If you reach the end of a platform jump or fall to the other platform and switch directions. It is recommended that you use projectile-firing weapons such as bows, gem staves, or projectile melee weapons.


=== Facetank strategy ===
This strategy is very powerful and needs minimal skill to pull off, but requires a considerable amount of preparation. Acquire a full set of Platinum armor, an Ironskin Potion, a Bast Statue, food buffs, and a full set of accessories reforged to Warding. This amount of defense will reduce all of the boss's attacks to one damage, even in Master Mode, making it nearly impossible to die. You can then attack the boss with any weapon of your choice while ignoring its attacks.


=== Lightning strategy ===
This strategy only works during a storm; fight the boss in an arena full of trees, and whenever sparks appear at the top of a tree that signals lightning, try to manipulate the boss's position towards the spark. This is easiest during the phase where Servants are being spawned as the Eye will be positioned above the player at around tree height. If successful, a significant chunk of the boss's health, between 800 and 1200, will be chopped via the lightning strike. Just be careful not to get struck yourself.
