title: Traveling Merchant
content:
The Traveling Merchant is a unique NPC vendor who randomly visits the player's town for one in-game day. His inventory is randomized and different every visit, selling approximately 4–10 different items listed below.
In order for the Traveling Merchant to spawn, at least 2 other NPCs must already be present. The Guide counts as one of these, but the Old Man and Skeleton Merchant do not. He will not spawn during Solar Eclipses, the Goblin Army, Frost Legion, Pirate Invasion, or Martian Madness. He does not require his own house in order to spawn, and will instead spawn next to NPCs, including town pets, spending the day walking around them.
Once the criteria are met, the Traveling Merchant has a random chance of appearing between 4:30 AM and 12:00 PM. He leaves the same day at 6:00 PM, but can only do so once he is off-screen. He despawns if the world is exited.
If threatened by enemies, the Traveling Merchant will defend himself with a Revolver. Once Hardmode begins, he upgrades to a Pulse Bow.


== Items sold ==
Due to elaborate randomizer functions and dependencies upon several variables, it is nearly impossible to state an exact chance of an item being sold by the Traveling Merchant. However, it is possible to group them in six rarity "slots", ranging from "Common" to "Extraordinarily Rare". Note that these slots do not correspond to the Traveling Merchant's shop inventory slots – all sold items might be from only one slot. They are only meant to provide a rough, comparative estimate of an item's rarity. Each shop slot will roll a 1/n chance for every possible item where n is 100 × the rarity slot. This chance is affected by luck, more specifically the luckiest player currently in the world. When multiple items pass this chance, of the item that was tested, the latest will be the selected.
Within the slots, items higher in the list below have a marginally higher chance of being sold, e.g., the Companion Cube is sold slightly more often than the Water Gun (on average), because it is higher in the list.
The Traveling Merchant always sells exactly one painting, which is always in his last inventory slot. In Hardmode, at least one of the sold items is guaranteed to be from the rarity slot 2 ("Uncommon") or rarer.


=== Number of sold items ===
The number of items available for sale in the Traveling Merchant's inventory randomly varies between visits. The average number of sold items is 5.47 / 6.37. The concrete chances for each number are shown in the table below.
As some items are always sold together, the number of sold items can only include the "base" items. This means that Dynasty Shingles and Team Platforms are not counted in this number, since they are always sold together with their "base" items Dynasty Wood or Team Block, respectively. All two/three pieces of the Pretty Pink set, Raynbro's set, Star Princess set, Master Gamer's set, Chef set, and Lilac Dusk set are similarly counted as one item.
Moreover, paintings are also excluded from this number, as the Traveling Merchant always sells exactly one painting in addition to his non-painting wares.

The number of sold "base" items is affected by the player's luck. Higher luck shifts the chances towards the Traveling Merchant selling more than 6 "base" items, while lower luck increases the chances of him only selling 4 to 6 "base" items. Luck merely shifts the chances within the existing bounds, however, so the Traveling Merchant will always sell at least 4 and at most 10 / 11 "base" items (or more under the conditions described below), even with particularly low or high luck. In multiplayer, only the luck of the player with the highest luck currently in the world is considered for this.
Under certain circumstances, the number of sold "base" items is increased:

If the current world is in Hardmode, the number is increased by 1.
If a Peddler's Satchel has been used in the current world, the number is increased by 1.
If the Celebration Mk 10 special world seed is active, the number is always increased by 2.
In worlds that combine the Celebration Mk 10 and For the Worthy seeds, the number is instead always increased by 1.


=== Additional items ===
These items are separate from the randomization of the Traveling Merchant's shop inventory. They are always available, provided the respective conditions are met.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Traveling Merchant will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
The actual "roll" to spawn the Traveling Merchant is not performed once-per-day like a Goblin Army or how most other events are determined. Instead, the roll is performed every tick.
For each tick of the first half of each day (4:30 AM – 12:00 PM = 7.5 hours = 27,000 ticks), there is a 1/108,000 chance to spawn the Traveling Merchant. Thus, the chance of the Traveling Merchant arriving on a given day is: 1-(107999/108000)^27000 = 0.2212001339 ≈ 22.12%.
This means that if a specific item from the Traveling Merchant is desired, but he arrived without that particular item, and it is before 12:00 PM in-game, he can be killed for a chance of another Traveling Merchant spawning.
The chance of him spawning per real-life second is increased if the player is sleeping, although he will never spawn while the Enchanted Sundial or Moondial is active.
In Journey Mode, the Traveling Merchant can spawn even if enemy spawn rates are set to zero.
The inventory of the Traveling Merchant is determined the moment he spawns and remains unchanged until he leaves. Changing the player's luck, switching to Expert Mode using the Enemy Difficulty Slider, or even defeating the Wall of Flesh to enter Hardmode has no effect on the Traveling Merchant's wares when he is already present.
Notably, if he arrived with a Gray Zapinator in pre-Hardmode, it will not automatically be replaced with an Orange Zapinator if the world turns to Hardmode during his visit. This makes the Gray Zapinator available in Hardmode for a short period.
The only exception to this are the items listed under Additional items, as they are separate from the randomization of the Traveling Merchant's inventory.
The Traveling Merchant does not leave during events.
The Traveling Merchant can throw a Party.


== Tips ==
The Traveling Merchant departs by simply disappearing while off-screen. If the player keeps him on-screen when he would normally depart, he will remain until he is off-screen again. If he is kept on-screen until dawn, he will not depart until he is off-screen after 6:00 PM the following evening. This does not, however, change his inventory.


== Names ==
The Traveling Merchant may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


== Trivia ==
Many of the things the Traveling Merchant sells are of Asian origin, often from the Qing dynasty.
Many of his wares may be a reference to the East India Company, and to the goods that were brought to Europe during the age of discovery in general.
He wears an Asian-inspired outfit in his Shimmered form.
A peddler, as referenced by the Peddler's Hat and Peddler's Satchel, is a name for a traveling merchant or salesperson.
The Traveling Merchant is depicted in the painting Visiting the Pyramids.
The name Willy is most likely a reference to the 1949 play Death of a Salesman written by American playwright Arthur Miller, where the main character, Willy Loman, is a traveling salesman.
His quote “Come and have a look! One pound fish! Very, very good! One pound fish!” is a reference to the Pakistani trader and recording artist Muhammad Shahid Nazir, also known as the One Pound Fish Man, who found fame as an internet sensation for his viral novelty song “One Pound Fish”.
The quote “Combination hookah and coffee maker! Also makes julienne fries!” is a reference to the 1992 American animated musical fantasy film Aladdin.
His quote “Hmm, you look like you could use an Angel Statue! They slice, and dice, and make everything nice!” is a reference to the ongoing joke of how Angel Statues are one of the most useless statues in the game; this is also referenced by quotes from the Merchant, Dryad, and Wizard.
Along with the Cyborg, the Zoologist, and the Princess, the Traveling Merchant is one of the only NPCs to sell a new item post-Moon Lord, which is Not a Kid, nor a Squid and Moonman & Company.
 The Bestiary entry for the Traveling Merchant: "The flamboyantly-dressed Traveling Merchant travels far and wide to bring unique, cultural wares from time to time."

Now also has an extra guaranteed item slot in his inventory at all times, which always contains a painting. Paintings have been removed from all of his other inventory slots, which will slightly increase the odds of obtaining the rest of his wares.

title: Demon Heart
content:
The Demon Heart is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently grants the player an extra accessory slot, for use only within Expert and Master Mode worlds. This effect does not stack and may only be used once per player. The Demon Heart is always dropped from the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. If a player opens the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag after they have already consumed a Demon Heart, another one will not be obtained.
When a player who consumed a Demon Heart is in a Classic Mode world (a non-Expert or Master world), the extra accessory slot is disabled, removing all functional or display effects from any items equipped in the slot, and darkening the slot itself. Players in Classic worlds are also prevented from equipping items in the sixth or seventh slot, though an equipped item in the slot may still be taken out, and placed back into the inventory.


== Notes ==
If a player equips wings in the extra slot(s) while in Expert/Master Mode, and then goes back to a Classic world, the immunity to fall damage is still applied.


== Trivia ==
The Demon Heart is one of the few Expert Mode items that cannot be equipped in any accessory or equipment slots, the others being the three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit (and the Minecart Upgrade Kit itself).


== History ==

title: Water
content:
Water is an abundant liquid found in nearly all biomes, forming pools of various sizes as well as the large Oceans on either side of a world. It is less common in Deserts and only naturally occurs above a certain depth, beneath which lava pools tend to appear instead. It is absent in The Underworld, where it evaporates if made to flow there. Each biome has its own unique water color, which can be changed using water fountains. Several aquatic and amphibious critters and enemies exclusively spawn in or near water. Water can be fished in and it flows more freely than lava and honey.
By default, players cannot swim in water and will sink to the bottom. If the player's feet are in at least one tile of water, movement is hindered noticeably, and once they are fully submerged in water, the breath meter will appear, indicating their remaining breathing time before drowning damage will be incurred. Certain accessories, potions, and mounts can boost movement through water, enable swimming, allow walking along its surface, or even grant stat bonuses while submerged (see below). Entering water removes and provides immunity to the On Fire!, Hellfire, and Stinky debuffs. In Expert Mode, entering water in a Snow biome inflicts the Chilled debuff.
Bodies of water break the player's fall upon impact and negate any fall damage. This applies even when landing on the water's surface due to the Water Walking buff or similar effects.
Projectiles move slower through water than air. Candles, most Torches, and fire projectiles of all kinds (such as Flaming Arrows) do not emit light underwater, but Glowsticks and some other light sources do. Most Torches and Campfires are knocked free when water touches them, with the exception of Cursed, Ichor, and Coral variants.


== Crafting ==

Like lava and honey, water can be used as a minor crafting station. It works just like those two; in order to use it the player only has to stand nearby. Creation of items from a body of water does not lower the water level at all. A sink or water fountain may be used in place of a water fluid tile, and similarly offers unlimited water to recipes.


=== Used to craft ===

Water can also be used to make the following items, though not as a crafting station:


== Water colors ==
Water changes color depending on the player's environment. The color can also be changed with water fountains.


== Items interacting with water ==
The Flipper allows the player to swim upward by jumping repeatedly from any point within the water.
The Gills Potion allows the player to breathe underwater.
The Breathing Reed allows the player to breathe while in shallow water and also increases the breath meter.
The Diving Helmet increases the breath meter.
The Diving Gear allows swimming and increases the breath meter.
Neptune's Shell allows swimming and allows the player to breathe underwater.
The Water Walking Potion, Lava Waders, Obsidian Water Walking Boots, Water Walking Boots, and Terraspark Boots allow the player to walk on the surface of water.
The Trident, Flipper Potion, Fishron Wings, Hardy Saddle, Superheated Blood, and Shrimpy Truffle allow the player to move at normal or boosted speed in water.
The Jellyfish Necklace, Jellyfish Diving Gear, and Arctic Diving Gear cause the player to emit light when in water.
Fishing poles allow the player to fish in water.
Pumps and buckets can move water.
Bottomless Water Bucket, Wet Bomb, and Wet Rocket create water.
Super Absorbant Sponge, Ultra Absorbant Sponge, Dry Bombs, and Dry Rockets remove water.
The Freeze Bomb turns water into Ice Blocks.


== Notes ==

Underground pools of water may sometimes be spotted via the glowing Jellyfish that spawn there.
The game occasionally has difficulty leveling out large volumes of liquid that flowed into a new space. Exiting and reloading the world, or relocating the liquid elsewhere, can sometimes remedy the problem.
If the player already has the Chilled debuff and enters water, it will stay on the player until they leave, where the countdown will start again.
Water cannot directly spread the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow, as the tints it receives from the player being in such biomes are purely visual.
When For the Worthy and The Constant special world seeds are active, and Remix is inactive, rain will create new water tiles above surface under certain conditions (see Rain § Notes for details).
If natural water is unavailable, water may still be obtainable:
Wet Bombs create water and can be found in crates obtained through lava fishing or crafted from Dry Bombs at sinks/water fountains.
Wet Rockets can be crafted from Dry Rockets at sinks/water fountains.
Water Buckets can be obtained by decrafting craftable sinks via Shimmer, or by transmuting Lava Buckets.
When an Empty Bucket is dropped as an item into the world with the Throw button while it is raining, and there are no background walls behind the dropped item, it will turn into a Water Bucket after some time has passed.
While Freeze Bombs convert water to Ice Blocks, there is no way to melt Ice or Snow back to water.


== Trivia ==
Water is a liquid substance that covers roughly 71% of the earth's surface. Taking this into consideration, it is unlikely that Terraria takes place on earth, as water covers little of most worlds, if a Terraria world represents the whole world. On the other hand, it is possible that a world in Terraria is only an island that comprises a smaller portion of the entire actual world, considering that even a large world's landmass is considerably small, that massive amounts of land and water can be seen in the world's backgrounds, and that each Terraria world is surrounded at the edges by two bodies of water of unknown real volume in the Ocean biomes.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: All water recipes can now also be crafted at water fountains.
Desktop 1.3.4: Water is now dynamic and has a setting to be more or less dynamic.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: In Expert Mode, water in a Snow biome gives the player Chilled debuff.
Desktop 1.2.4: Actuated tiles no longer remove the water over them on world load.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Sped up the water moving code by 5–10%.
Fixed a bug where moving very large quantities of water could leave some water floating.
Fixed an issue where the player could not jump while in reversed gravity in water.
Running underwater no longer causes flashes of the Suffocation debuff.
Desktop 1.2: 
When water touches a half block, it will now create a waterfall.
Water can now change colors depending what biome it is in, or if it is a Blood Moon.
Desktop 1.1: Water is now in a secondary "layer" behind the placed blocks, and can therefore no longer be removed by placing blocks on it. "Blocked" liquids disappear only after restarting the world.
Desktop 1.0.5: 
Candles, Torches, and Flaming Arrows do not emit light in water (except placed Candles).
Bats and flying enemies can no longer enter water and slimes float on its surface. All of them do not make a splash sound when hitting water.
Water evaporates when reaching the Underworld.

Console-Release: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile-Release: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Beguiling Lyre
content:
The Beguiling Lyre is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Faun that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Faun will fly in order to catch up to them. The Beguiling Lyre has a 6/125 (4.8%) of being dropped from Iron and Mythril Crates.


== Trivia ==
Prior to 1.4.5.0, the item was called Tartar Sauce and summoned the Mini Minotaur pet. It was a reference to YouTuber Toby Turner, better known by his stage name Tobuscus. It was likely changed due to Tobuscus later becoming a controversial figure, thus Re-Logic no longer wanting to be affiliated with him.
The Beguiling Lyre is still internally referred to as TartarSauce.
The name of the item and its corresponding pet were a reference to his Mini Minotaur song. In the song, it is said that mini minotaurs hate tartar sauce and are allergic to it. Its buff tooltip, "How do you defeat a mini Minotaur?", was also a direct quote from the song.
The Mini Minotaur's appearance, the red loincloth, and the hammer were probably a reference to the Maulotaur from the 1994 dark fantasy first-person shooter game Heretic, where it is a powerful enemy, and its 1995 sequel Hexen, where the player can summon the Maulotaur to aid them in combat.
In Greek mythology, the Minotaur is a mythical creature with the head and tail of a bull and the body of a man. He dwelt at the center of the Labyrinth, and was eventually killed by the Athenian hero Theseus.
Also in Greek mythology, Tartarus was a deep abyss used as a dungeon for administering divine punishment to the wicked and as a place from where souls were forever judged. While the tartar in both names may have been a coincidence, it could have been a reference.
In Roman mythology, the faun is a half-human and half-goat mythological creature, and sometimes linked with the satyr in Greek mythology.

title: Brain in a Jar
content:
The Brain in a Jar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Spider Brain, a miniature version of the Brain of Cthulhu, that follows the player. The Brain in a Jar has a 1/4 (25%) of being dropped by the Brain of Cthulhu in Master Mode.


== Trivia ==
The Spider Brain bears a resemblance to Mother Brain, a prominent antagonist from the action-adventure game series Metroid, with both having one eye and being contained inside a glass container.
The item references brain in a vat, a scenario used in a variety of thought experiments which involves removing a person's brain from its host body, suspending it in a vat of life-sustaining liquid, and connecting its neurons by wires to a supercomputer that provides it with electrical impulses identical to those a brain normally receives, so that the brain would continue to have perfectly normal conscious experiences.

title: Daybroken
content:
Daybroken is a debuff that is applied by the Daybreak and the Solar Eruption for 5 seconds. It causes the afflicted enemy to take 100 damage per second (25 damage displayed every 0.25 seconds), and the Daybreak is able to stack this debuff up to 8 times, octupling the damage in the process for a total of 800 damage per second (200 damage displayed every 0.25 seconds). Enemies that die while afflicted with the debuff inflict it for 5 seconds onto nearby enemies within 6.25 tiles.

title: Advanced Combat Techniques
content:
Advanced Combat Techniques is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the defense of Town NPCs by 8, their attack damage by 25%, their attack speed by 20%, and their health by 250. Advanced Combat Techniques can only be obtained by fishing during a Blood Moon. It can only be used once per world, and others cannot be fished up once one has already been used. However, multiple copies can be obtained until the first is used. The chance of fishing it up when conditions are met is 1/360 (0.28%) with 50 Fishing Power and 1/180 (0.56%) with 100 Fishing Power (assuming neither Crate Potion nor Chum Caster is used and that the body of water is not too small).
When used, the status message “The book's knowledge empowers your villagers!” is displayed.


== Notes ==
This item has a catch quality of Extremely Rare (See Fishing § Catch quality).
Different from quest fish, the player can obtain another Advanced Combat Techniques as long as one has not been used, regardless of whether there is already an Advanced Combat Techniques in their inventory.
Using a Sonar Potion will allow the player to better see when Advanced Combat Techniques has been hooked.
The effects on NPC damage and defense stack with Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two. The two items can be consumed in any order.
NPCs also gain stat boosts when certain bosses are defeated in the current world.


== Achievements ==

Drop chance from fishing increased by ~33%.

title: Skeleton Merchant
content:
The Skeleton Merchant is a unique NPC vendor who randomly appears in the Cavern layer. He is not a town NPC and will despawn when off-screen, although enemies will not spawn near him.
The Skeleton Merchant's stock changes at dawn (4:30 AM) daily, and he does not need to respawn for it to do so. The majority of the items in his inventory will vary, depending on the current moon phase.
The Skeleton Merchant will defend himself against nearby non-skeletal enemies by throwing Bones, while ignoring most other skeletons.
Unlike other NPCs, the Skeleton Merchant does not have a map icon.
He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. His current name will be displayed (e.g. Rattles Magoo) rather than it displaying as Skeleton Merchant.


== Items sold ==


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Skeleton Merchant will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
He cannot be teleported by the Portal Gun or King Statue.
The Skeleton Merchant does not attack other skeletons listed below, nor will they harm him via contact damage. The Skeleton Merchant can still inadvertently damage other skeletons if they are hit by the bones from the Skeleton Merchant, and he can still be harmed by certain non-contact attacks or projectiles like the Skeleton Archer's arrows.

The Skeleton Merchant cannot spawn if the player has a Shadow Candle placed nearby or is holding a shadow candle.
If he has already spawned, placing a Shadow Candle will not negate his spawn rate reduction effect. This is because despite similar mechanics, the Skeleton Merchant is not considered a town NPC in regards to reducing enemy spawns. He does, however, count as seven NPCs for the sake of enemy spawn limits when spawning NPCs, mechanically similar to bosses. In most cases this effectively blocks virtually anything from spawning, including critters. This creates a problem when the player is preparing to farm enemies in the Underground or Cavern layers. It is necessary to have the Flymeal or a strong external damage source (lava, Boulders, Jungle Temple traps) to kill him to continue farming, or just go far enough for him to despawn.
The Skeleton Merchant also does not increase the chance for critters to spawn, unlike actual town NPCs.
The Skeleton Merchant does not spawn on Jungle grass or evil biome blocks, or inside water. He also cannot spawn on blocks that have natural Underground Desert or Spider Nest background walls behind them.
Despite being a skeleton, the Skeleton Merchant is not immune to the Poisoned debuff.
In worlds with Remix enabled, the Skeleton Merchant may spawn in the Underground layer, as it is considered Cavern when spawning enemies.


== Tips ==
Using the Hunter Potion and Lifeform Analyzer helps with finding the Skeleton Merchant.
Selling items to the Skeleton Merchant can help a player clear out their inventory in the middle of a long caving session.
If a player notices a suspiciously low number of enemies on their Radar, it could be a sign that the Skeleton Merchant has spawned.
If the Skeleton Merchant spawns in front of a Detonator explosive trap, interacting with him may unwillingly hit the plunger on the detonator trap, killing both him and the player.


== Names ==
The Skeleton Merchant may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


== Trivia ==
Several of the possible names for the Skeleton Merchant are references to popular culture:
"Jack Sellington" and "Skellington" are references to Jack Skellington from the 1993 American animated fantasy film The Nightmare Before Christmas.
"Bones McGee" is a reference to Leonard H. "Bones" McCoy, a character in the American science fiction franchise Star Trek.
"No-Eyed Wiley" is a reference to One-Eyed Willy from the 1985 American adventure comedy film The Goonies.
"Mandible Calavera" is a reference to Manuel "Manny" Calavera from the 1998 adventure game Grim Fandango.
"Billy Marrows" and "Gloomy Mays" are a reference to the late American television salesperson Billy Mays.
"Tom" may be a reference to Tom "Bones" Malone, member of the American blues and soul revivalist band The Blues Brothers.
"Tom" may also be a reference to Tim, a skeleton enemy.

He can be seen retrieving a Slap Hand from a pile of bones in the credits.
The quote about Slime Oil is a reference to the “miracle medicine” peddlers of the 1800s, who were commonly called "snake oil salesmen."
The quote “The only things constant in this world are death and taxes, I've got both!” is a reference to Benjamin Franklin's famous quote, "In this world, nothing can be said to be certain, except death and taxes."
The quote “You would not believe some of the things people throw at me... Wanna buy some of it?” is a reference to a young scavenger named "Squirt the Peddler" in the 2012 action role-playing game Diablo III. Squirt periodically asks the player a near-exact variation of this question, but refers to "things people throw away" instead of "things people throw at me".
The quote “Chicken Bones? Why are you asking, do you need any?” is a reference to the Re-Logic developer, Chicken Bones.
The quote “Stay away from the spiders. They'll suck out your insides and leave you a hollow shell of a man. Trust me on this one.” suggests that he came to be after being killed by a spider, likely a Wall Creeper or Black Recluse from a Spider Nest.
Even though he is not a town NPC, he will throw confetti during a Party.
He is one of two NPCs that does not have a map icon, the other being the Old Man.
Despite the fact one of his quotes makes a joke on the idea, the Skeleton Merchant does not sell Maggots.
If the Skeleton Merchant is slain, no message pops up to announce his death, unlike most NPCs.
The counterweights he sells resemble dice used in the tabletop role-playing game Dungeons and Dragons. This is a possible reference to weighted dies used for cheating, which may be provided by a disreputable merchant such as the Skeleton Merchant.
He is the only NPC that always despawns once off-screen. The Traveling Merchant also despawns when off-screen, but only after 6:00 PM.
Unlike the Traveling Merchant, he does not seem to interact with other nearby NPCs.Verify
The Skeleton Merchant's Shimmered form transforms him into a Zombie. This is most likely a reference to the fact that Zombies turn into Skeletons when submerged in Shimmer.
 The Bestiary entry for the Skeleton Merchant: "Most skeletons are out for blood, but not the Skeleton Merchant. He just wants to sell supplies, such as rare torches and yo-yo gear."

title: Starfall
content:
A Starfall is an event that has a 1/10 (10%) chance to occur every night. During the event, Fallen Star rates are increased by 200–400% and falling stars appear in the background. If there are few clouds in the sky (such as during a Lantern Night), Enchanted Nightcrawlers can spawn on the surface during a Starfall.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
The chance for a Starfall to occur each night is increased to 1/5 (20%) in a Celebration Mk 10 world.
Starfalls are not the only cause that increases the rate at which Fallen Stars spawn; Fallen Star rates also have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance (1/2 (50%) in a Celebrationmk10 world) to be increased every night between 0% and 50%. However, this slightly increased Fallen Star rate does not fulfill the requirements for spawning Enchanted Nightcrawlers.


== Tips ==
The frequency of Enchanted Nightcrawlers spawning on the surface makes this event useful for obtaining bait for fishing.

title: Guide:Completing the Bestiary
content:
This guide describes how to complete 100% of the Bestiary in one world without bringing anything from another world. It assumes you have gone through a classic walkthrough, that you are in a world created in 1.4 without special seeds.


== Early Game ==
At the early game, you should not need to worry about completing the Bestiary. You will likely have completed multiple entries already, mostly Town NPCs, critters, and common enemies such as Slimes and Zombies. Your lack of power or wiring equipment, however, make it more difficult to farm at this stage, so do not stress about filling in the Bestiary in early pre-Hardmode.


== Checking for Rare Creatures ==
Some creatures become significantly rarer in Hardmode, so you should beat them during pre-Hardmode. You can increase your chances of seeing them by using a Water Candle / Battle Potion / increasing the spawnrate in Journey Mode:

Giant Worm (186) in Underground layer
Tim (204) in Cavern layer
Ice Bat (231) in Ice biome
Doctor Bones (264) in Jungle at night
Devourer (335) in Corruption


== Getting the Other Evil ==
Now that you are ready, you can beat the Wall of Flesh and go in Hardmode. To complete the bestiary, you will need to get some Crimson in your world if you are in a Corrupt World or some Corruption if you are in a Crimson World, but it is only doable once you are in Hardmode.


=== The Graveyard ===
To complete the Bestiary, you will need the other evil in your world. To do that, you need to gather at least 7 Tombstones created after your deaths (or after your NPCs' deaths if you are in Hardcore). Place the tombstones around the Dryad to buy some Corrupt Seeds/Crimson Seeds from her (you must be in Hardmode). If you did not beat them already, be sure to kill some Ghosts, Maggot Zombies, Ravens and Hoppin' Jack, which spawn in Graveyard biomes. You will also see some Rats while in the Graveyard biome, and Maggots will spawn after killing Maggot Zombies; simply walk near them to complete the Graveyard part of the Bestiary.


=== Other Evil Surface ===
Now that you have some evil seeds, plant them in a place where there is a lot of pure grass. After some time, Vile Mushroom/Vicious Mushroom will spawn, which you will want to gather. You can then transform them into Thrown Powder to spread the evil even more. If you prefer Thrown Water, convert some sand with the powder so you will be able to make some. Before leaving the biome for now, summon then kill the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu.


== Early Hardmode ==
Now you should focus on your progression on early Hardmode, beat the Goblin Army and Pirate Invasion, Queen Slime and at least one of the Mechanical bosses.


== Completing the Biomes ==
Now you should have enough supplies and should be able to complete the different biomes. Be sure to get a Clentaminator, some Green, Blue and Purple/Red Solution and some powder/water of the other evil.


=== The Tundra ===
While you are on the surface, capture two Penguins, and kill monsters at night and while it is raining until you have seen the 7 critters and monsters (numbers 92+).
Once you unlocked the entry for all of them, go underground. Use your Clentaminator with green solution if the Ice biome is not pure, then start throwing your powder or water around to corrupt the biome with the other evil. Wait around until you beat Pigron (purple if it is Corruption, red if it is Crimson). You can then use the other solutions to transform the biome again and kill the other two Pigrons. If your underground snow bestiary is not complete, spend some time there with a water candle and battle potion to beat them. An additional (and maybe easier) way to defeat the pigrons which does not require making your underground snow biome corrupt, crimson and hallow is finding a pigron statue. Pigron statues will spawn purple pigrons, red pigrons and pink pigrons.


=== The Desert ===
This part should take some time as you will need to convert a desert into 4 parts: one Hallow, one Corrupt, one Crimson and one pure, then wait for a Sandstorm. There are four kinds of Sand Sharks, one for each type of desert during a Sandstorm. You will have to beat each in order to complete the Sandstorm event in the Bestiary. You should also beat each type of Mummy this way. Now the Desert, Sandstorm, Corrupt Desert, Crismon Desert and Hallowed Desert should be complete. If not, you should wait longer in this area or put some water in it if number 96 or 97 are missing (these are oasis critters).
Once you are done, go underground and free the Golfer if you have not already. Then do the same as was done for the Underground Snow biomes by creating corrupt, crimson and hallowed areas. There is a ghoul for each to beat, and you will have to beat a Lamia in Corruption/Crimson and one in Purity/Hallow. After that, you should have completed the 4 Underground Desert bestiary sections.


=== The Rest ===
The rest should not be hard and by now you should have completed most of the Bestiary:

Party
Windy Day
Rain (if 356 (Rainbow Slime) is not unlocked, go to the Hallow and wait while it is raining)
Graveyard
Underground
Granite
Marble
Underground Mushroom (except 108 (Truffle Worm))
Spider Nest
Snow (except 23 (Cyborg) and 26 (Santa Claus). Make sure you have unlocked 22 (Tax Collector) by purifying the Tortured Soul!)
Underground Snow
Desert
Underground Desert
Sandstorm
Jungle
Meteor
The Underworld
The Corruption
Underground Corruption
Corrupt Ice
Corrupt Desert
Corrupt Cave Desert
The Crimson
Underground Crimson
Crimson Ice
Crimson Desert
Crimson Cave Desert
The Hallow (except 126 (Prismatic Lacewing) and 527 (Empress of Light))
Underground Hallow
Hallow Ice
Hallow Desert
Hallow Cave Desert
Surface Mushroom (except 21 (Truffle))
Goblin Invasion
Pirate Invasion
If a creature is not unlocked yet, go to the biome (or create it) and spend some time in it.


== Blood Moon ==
Now that you have completed the different biomes, you can continue your progression and beat the other mechanical bosses if they are not already dead.
Capture two Bunnies and two Goldfish, take three evil powder of each kind then convert one Bunny, one Goldfish and one Penguin to each evil by throwing one powder at them, then kill them.
It is then time to fish. Summon a Blood Moon with Bloody Tear or wait for one to happen and begin fishing. You will have to kill at least one Wandering Eye Fish, one Zombie Merman, one Hemogoblin Shark, one Blood Eel, one Dreadnautilus, and one Blood Squid from Dreadnautilus to complete the Blood Moon part. Use the Chum Caster as soon as possible to fish them up more easily. A Sonar Potion will allow you to see if you are going to pull up one of these enemies.


== The Endgame ==
Now you can continue your progression by killing Plantera, Empress of Light, Golem and Duke Fishron. Complete the Dungeon, the Temple, Underground Jungle, the Solar Eclipse (during it, let at least one mothron egg hatch to kill a Baby Mothron), Ocean and defeat the Old One's Army. You must also fill out the Martian Madness by finishing one event and killing one Martian Probe. Note that the Martian Probe spawn chances are highly increased when you are near a Water Candle.


== Halloween ==
With your new gear, you should be able to beat the 15th wave of the Pumpkin Moon. Once it is done, you will have one day of Halloween. Alternatively, set your device's date to October. There are 11 creatures to unlock: go directly to the Caverns, increase the spawnrate because you will have to kill three different skeleton in costume, which are quite rare. Once they are beaten, go in the surface again and place a cemetery if it is  day. You will have to beat one special type of Bunny, one of Slime, two types of Demon Eye, three types of Zombie, and Hoppin' Jack which spawns at night (though it can also be found in a Graveyard).


== Christmas ==
This one will be tougher. You have to beat the 15th wave of the Frost Moon, which will unlock one day of Christmas (or set your device's date to December). Once the Christmas seasonal event is active, beat as many monsters as possible. There is one type of Bunny, 4 types of Slime, and 2 types of Zombie. Open as many Presents as possible, as you will have to quickly start and beat the Frost Legion. If it is still day, Santa Claus may spawn. Otherwise, you will have to beat the Frost Moon again to make him spawn.


== The End ==
The only monsters remaining are linked to the Lunar Events. Kill them all, then the four pillars and finally the Moon Lord and the Bestiary will be 100% complete. You can now buy the Universal Pylon from the Zoologist.

title: Palladium armor
content:
Palladium armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palladium Breastplate and Palladium Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Palladium Mask, Palladium Helmet, and Palladium Headgear, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Palladium Bars (162 Palladium Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Palladium Bars (234 Palladium Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is  Cobalt armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:

Hitting an enemy grants the Rapid Healing buff for 5 seconds, providing a flat health regeneration of 2 HP per second.
Further hits will refresh the duration. The buff is not canceled when the armor is removed.
Being flat health regeneration, it applies separately from the normal type. This also causes this regeneration to bypass the Bleeding debuff.
While this buff is applied, the player emits visual orange heart particles.


== Set ==


=== Helmet variants ===


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The set bonus buff can be triggered with the player's minion attacks, and can be triggered when attacking critters or Target Dummies.


== Tips ==
Compared to the melee version of Adamantite armor, the melee Palladium armor is still valuable. It grants 18 less defense than the Adamantite armor, so the player will take 9 / 14 / 18 more damage. This means that if they get hit less often than every 4.5 / 7 / 9 seconds (the time needed to heal the damage the Adamantite armor would have prevented), the player's survivability is greater with Palladium armor.
The Rapid Healing buff stacks additively with the Life Drain's buff.
Using minion weapons that can rapidly attack any enemy such as the Blade Staff is a good strategy when using Palladium armor, as it can effectively keep the Rapid Healing buff always enabled whenever the player is engaged in battle.

title: Crystal Ball
content:
The Crystal Ball is a Hardmode furniture item which functions as a crafting station. It is purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Crystal Ball grants the Clairvoyance buff and opens its crafting menu.
The Clairvoyance buff boosts the following magic-related stats:

+20 maximum mana
+5% magic damage
+2% magic critical strike chance
−2% mana cost
The Clairvoyance buff lasts until the player dies or leaves the world. The buff can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
Unlike equipment buff items, the Crystal Ball must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.


== Crafting ==


=== Used to craft ===


== Notes ==
The Crystal Ball can be activated limitlessly with no cooldown period. It is never consumed, and all players may use it to give themselves the buff.


== Trivia ==
The Crystal Ball emits a small amount of blue light when placed. It periodically sparkles, increasing its glow for a short time.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: 
Stack limit increased from 999 to 9999.
Buff duration of 10 minutes removed. The buff now lasts until the player dies or leaves the world.
Now used to make the Blizzard in a Bottle and the Sandstorm in a Bottle.

Now used to make Endless Quiver, Endless Musket Pouch, Magic Water, Lava and Honey Droppers, Living Cursed, Ichor, Demon, Frost, Ultrabright Fire Blocks, and Water Candle.

title: Lantern Night
content:
The Lantern Night is a peaceful event that generally occurs the night after a boss or invasion has been defeated for the first time. During the event, many lanterns can be seen floating up into the sky in the background. The player will have a flat +0.3 increase to their luck stat and the Party Girl will sell the Release Lantern.
If a boss is summoned or another event (Blood Moon, Frost Moon, Pumpkin Moon, etc.) is activated during the event, it will stop, and will not continue even after the boss despawns or the event ends. However, if a Lantern Night is set to start but a boss or event is active when night begins, the Lantern Night may be pushed back instead; see the Notes section below for details.
In addition, a Lantern Night fulfills the requirements for Enchanted Nightcrawlers to spawn naturally only if a Starfall is also ongoing.


== Contents ==


=== NPC quotes ===


== Notes ==

A Lantern Night is initiated in the following ways:
Defeating any boss for the first time, with the exceptions of the Mourning Wood, Santa-NK1, and Everscream.
The Eater of Worlds and the Brain of Cthulhu are counted as the same boss for this purpose, meaning that defeating one of them will only start a Lantern Night if neither of the two was killed before.
Defeating any invasion for the first time, with the exceptions of the Frost Moon and Pumpkin Moon.
Defeating the Pumpking or the Ice Queen for the first time will start a Lantern Night, however.
After defeating the Moon Lord, Lantern Nights may happen randomly, with a 1/14 (7.14%) chance of happening per night. After a random Lantern Night occurs, the next random Lantern Night can occur no sooner than 5-10 nights later.
Only one non-random Lantern Night can be scheduled at once. Thus, if two Lantern Nights are triggered in the same 24-hour period (from one nightfall to the next), only one Lantern Night will actually be scheduled.
Lantern Nights can be pre-empted by certain events. If a boss, invasion, Pumpkin Moon, Frost Moon, Blood Moon, or impending doom is active when night falls, and the night was supposed to be a Lantern Night, then the Lantern Night will not activate.
When this occurs, the next night will be eligible for a Lantern Night. Thus, when a Lantern Night is pre-empted, it gets delayed, not canceled.
Similarly, the post-Moon Lord random Lantern Nights can pre-empt non-random Lantern Nights: If a given night is eligible for a random Lantern Night and has a non-random Lantern Night scheduled, then if the 1-in-14 random chance succeeds, a Lantern Night will occur randomly, but the non-random Lantern Night will remain scheduled, thereby happening the following night.
Active Lantern Nights prevent Eye of Cthulhu or any mechanical boss from naturally spawning, and a Lantern Night that lasts until dawn prevents a Goblin Army, Pirate Invasion, or Solar Eclipse from starting immediately afterwards.


== Tips ==
Because of a significant luck increase, this event is best spent hunting for rare drops.
The Enchanted Nightcrawlers can be caught for easy bait.


== Trivia ==
This event was teased during the development of 1.4.0.1 as "something straight out of Tangled", a 2010 Disney film where lanterns are released into the sky to honor the birthday of the character Rapunzel.
The scene in question is itself inspired by the real-life Chinese traditional Lantern Festival that marks the final day of the traditional Chinese New Year celebrations.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

title: Guide:Crafting a Shellphone
content:
The Shellphone, like other notable compound items (such as the Ankh Shield and Terra Blade), is an extremely powerful and helpful item to have on hand, which combines the function of Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. Like a real-life cell phone, it can tell you the weather, the time, and where you are, among other things. What's more, it can teleport you to four different locations, including the world's spawn point, either Ocean (whichever is farther), the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via Bed. Its usefulness however comes with a cost: its construction is highly time-consuming and some components are extremely difficult to find. This page will guide you on how to craft this item.


== Basic diagram ==


== Items needed ==


=== Magic Mirror or Ice Mirror ===
Magic Mirror: An extremely easy item to obtain, as it simply requires finding an Underground Cabin with a chest, and it can be crafted as well. You must acquire 32 of either Gold Ore or Platinum Ore (only one type, as they cannot be mixed), 20 Sand, and 3 Diamonds. Melt the ores into bars and the sand into Glass, and then assemble a Magic Mirror.
Ice Mirror: Found under mainly the same conditions, except as secondary loot in Ice Chests.


=== GPS components ===

Gold or Platinum Watch: Six varieties of watches can be crafted with any of the early pre-biome ores. To craft the GPS, you will need to obtain one of the highest-quality watches, which display the time to the nearest real-life second or in-game minute, as opposed to every minute or half minute. In order to craft the required watch, you must acquire 40 of either Gold Ore or Platinum Ore (only one type, as they cannot be mixed), and 3 of either Iron Ore or Lead Ore. Melt all of these into bars. Use the iron or lead to create a chain, and then go to a work bench and assemble a Gold Watch or Platinum Watch.
Depth Meter: This is dropped by several types of bats (Cave Bat, Ice Bat, Spore Bat, Jungle Bat and Giant Bat), as well as the trio of Salamander, Giant Shelly, and Crawdad. A Bat Statue can be used to easily obtain one.
Compass: The compass can be obtained upon the death of certain monsters (Mother Slime, Piranha, Snow Flinx, Undead Viking, and Armored Viking), including the trio of Salamander, Giant Shelly, and Crawdad. A Piranha Statue can be used to easily obtain one.


=== Fish Finder components ===

All ingredients are obtained from the Angler. You will initially have a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of obtaining each of these items upon completing one of the Angler's quests, although the chance will go up as you complete more quests. An Enchanted Sundial, Bed, or Journey Mode (if applicable) will prove useful, allowing you to fast-forward time to the next day once you have completed the current day's quest.
Completing a quest with any component in your inventory will guarantee not getting a duplicate of that component (unless you possess them all). However, if you leave a component in a chest and get a duplicate, it should not be discarded, as in the Aether biome, duplicates can be Shimmered to get the other accessories.


=== R.E.K. 3000 components ===

Radar: This can be found in Wooden chests, making it easy to find early on. It can also be obtained from Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates (although this may take more time), and is sold by the Skeleton Merchant (only during a Waxing Gibbous).
Lifeform Analyzer: Sometimes sold by Traveling Merchant.
Tally Counter: Dropped by pre-hardmode Dungeon enemies (excluding Dungeon Slimes and trap-like enemies).


=== Goblin Tech components ===

DPS Meter: Sometimes sold by the Traveling Merchant
Stopwatch: Sometimes sold by the Traveling Merchant (he may sell both at once)
Metal Detector: Dropped by the rare Nymph. A Lifeform Analyzer and Hunter Potions can be used to track down one. It will only have a 50% chance of dropping (100% in Expert mode).


=== Craft the PDA ===

Note that the PDA can be used separately from the Magic/Ice Mirror. This can be useful because the PDA is the last item in this crafting tree that can be equipped or receive modifiers. However, crafting the Cell Phone will help you in many cases.


=== Craft the Cell Phone ===

Note that this is no longer an accessory and as such cannot be equipped nor receive modifiers.


=== Craft the Shellphone ===

Magic Conch: This can be found in Sandstone Chests, Oasis Crates, and Mirage Crates.
Demon Conch: This can be acquired by fishing in lava.


== Farming and Tips on getting the Shellphone ==
To obtain these items, it may help to farm them. Make sure you have spare money to buy items from the Traveling Merchant.


=== All Items ===
The Enchanted Sundial can be used to skip a day, allowing you to reset the Angler's quest and make the Travelling Merchant to spawn more often. You can also sleep in a Bed to make the time pass faster.
In Journey Mode, the time can be sped up or even skipped as well.
Place Water Candles and use a Battle Potion to increase the spawn rate of required enemies.
Place the right Torches and a Gnome to increase Luck so to increase the drop chance. You may also use a Ladybug and a Luck Potion.
Do loads of fishing. Fishing will give you fish to craft potions that can help you.
Defeat Skeletron in order to access the Dungeon enemies and drop the Tally Counter.
Exploring caves a lot helps get many of the items needed, as many of the items are obtained from underground enemies.


=== GPS ===
Watch: The Watch does not need farming, as it is craftable. You could use Spelunker Potions to help find the needed ore, or get the metal bars from fished Crates. The Extractinator might also be useful in getting the needed ores/bars.
Compass: You may use Piranha Statues to farm Piranhas, as they have a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of dropping a Compass. Note that statue-spawned Piranhas have a 1/375 (0.27%) chance instead.
Depth Meter: Bat Statues are useful for farming Bats. Bats have a 1/100 (1%) chance of dropping a Depth Meter. Note that statue-spawned Bats have a 1/500 (0.2%) chance instead.


=== Fish Finder ===
Do fish quests for the Angler every day, as the Fish Finder can be acquired randomly by completing quests for the Angler. The quests from the Angler reset at 4:30 AM.
After finding an ingredient, keep it in your inventory or portable storage to avoid obtaining a duplicate of said ingredient.
If you forget to do so, you may still throw duplicates into shimmer to turn them into one of the other ingredients.
Consider getting multiple copies of a quest fish in order to almost instantaneously complete a quest if that quest fish is asked for again.
There is no realistic way to farm the Fish Finder aside from getting loads of quest fish and offering them to the Angler when he asks for one.
Journey Mode makes this trivial since you can research quest fish and speed up/skip time.


=== R.E.K 3000 ===
Tally Counter: Enter a pre-Hardmode Dungeon with decent weapons, and start hunting.
Radar: If no surface chests are found with it, or your world was generated before 1.3, you can find it in Wooden Crates. Use Fishing Potions, Crate Potions, and Sonar Potions to increase your chances. You can also create new worlds and use them to packmule items including the Radar.
Lifeform Analyzer: Buy from Traveling Merchant (see above for tips).


=== Goblin Tech ===
Stopwatch: Buy from Traveling Merchant (see above for tips).
DPS Meter: Buy from Traveling Merchant (see above for tips).
Metal Detector: Create a long tunnel in an Ice biome. Run from end to end of the tunnel until a Lost Girl/Nymph spawns. A Lifeform Analyzer can also be used to find them more easily.

title: Potion Sickness
content:
Potion Sickness is a debuff inflicted on the player upon using a healing item. While inflicted, it prevents the consumption of healing items. Its duration can be reduced by 25% by equipping the Philosopher's Stone, Charm of Myths, or Catalyst Band. Equipping multiple of these accessories will not cause the effect to stack.

title: Wet
content:
Wet is a debuff that can be inflicted on enemies, NPCs, and players. While active, the afflicted entity becomes immune to the On Fire!, Hellfire, and Burning debuffs. Wet also renders enemies and NPCs immune to the Stinky debuff, but not players. Players in the Bat mount form are pulled out of it when Wet, and players riding the Cute Fishron mount gain its "liquid boost" effects. Being submerged in lava immediately cancels the Wet debuff.
Visually, Wet causes water to drip down the character model.

The debuff is effective for locating worms while they are traveling through blocks. It can also be used to locate invisible players that are using Invisibility Potions or Shroomite armor.

title: Forest
content:
The Forest is a pure biome that comprises the majority of the surface world and is typically where the player initially spawns. The global landscape of a Forest includes lots of grass, plenty of trees, lakes and ponds of water that come in various sizes, and occasional hills that can reveal cave entrances. Forests often contain one or more Living Trees that sometimes have an underground treasure room.
The Forest changes noticeably in the outer sixths of the world. Goblin Scouts, which are fairly uncommon and drop Tattered Cloth, begin to spawn. The King Slime also has a very low chance to spawn and can easily surprise and overwhelm an unsuspecting player. Enchanted Sword Shrines are only found in the outer thirds of the world in the Forest as well.


== Contents ==


== Mountain Cave ==

The Mountain Cave is a structure typically found in the Forest biome. It consists of a high Dirt mountain and a zigzag cave leading to underground within it, serving as an option for early-game players to go underground easily. Pots and Wooden Chests can often be found in the cave.


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
Generally, the Forest is the simplest biome in the game as the enemies encountered here are easily defeated once some basic gear has been acquired. The player's first base is often built here, as building materials such as Clay, Stone, and Wood are found quickly, the spawn rates are generally low, and the initial spawn is usually within the Forest.
There is a small chance for low tier ores to spawn on the surface in a forest. The various types of ores that can be found consist of Copper or Tin, Lead or Iron, and sometimes Silver or Tungsten. Pockets of Clay and Stone can also be found on the surface.
Surface Chests can be found scattered all over the Forest and include many exceptional starter items.
In Hardmode, the biome receives a slight buff, with new enemies spawning at night.
Sakura and Yellow Willow trees have a 1/20 (5%) chance of replacing a regular Forest tree on world generation.
Fallen Logs can be found in the Forest, where Fairies spawn at night. When broken by an axe they will drop some Wood, and breaking all of them will permanently stop surface Fairies from spawning (although they can still be spawned by shaking trees).


== Tips ==
Regular Forests can be erased by the spread of Corruption, Crimson, and The Hallow. Converted Forests can be restored to their pure form by using Purification Powder purchased from the Dryad or its stronger Hardmode equivalent, the Clentaminator, with Green Solution purchased from the Steampunker.


== Trivia ==

The Forest has the most of music tracks, having five including those from Terraria: Otherworld.
According to NPC happiness, the Forest is the most popular biome: only two NPCs dislike it and four NPCs like it. In pure numbers this is better than every other biome. The Hallow is the only biome that comes close to this number.


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===

		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Added Stinkbugs, which spawn in the Forest.
Desktop 1.4.1: Shaking trees in the forest now has a chance to drop a Living Wood Wand or a Leaf Wand.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Added new backgrounds.
Some pre-existing backgrounds are updated and others now animated.
Added new background scenery, including a blimp, flock of birds, hot air balloon, Wyvern, and the Eye of Cthulhu.
Added new music, including the Storm and Windy Day music, which play during those respective events in the Forest. Also added Otherworldly Overworld Day and Night Tracks, originally from Terraria: Otherworld, which plays once the player has entered the Drunk special world seed and pressed the "Music" option in the Party Girl's menu.
Added Torch Zombies, which spawn in the Forest at night and drop Torches.
Angry Dandelions now spawn in the Forest during the Windy Day event.
Enchanted Sword Shrines, which usually spawn in the Forest, no longer spawn in every world. However, when they do, they have a 100% chance of having a real sword. Breaking the real sword now has a 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping the Terragrim instead of the Arkhalis.
Added Fallen Logs.
Forest Pylons will now be sold by any happy NPC in the Forest biome for 7 Gold 50 Silver to 8 Gold 50 Silver. While any number of pylons can be placed in a Forest biome, only one Forest Pylon can be functionally used per world.
Ladybugs now spawn during the day if the wind speed is greater than or equal to 20 mph, which increase the player's luck when nearby. Its gold counterpart, the Gold Ladybug, also has a very rare chance to spawn.
Living Trees now spawn in clusters, are connected underground, always have an underground room, with rounder and larger tops.
Living Wood Chests, which typically spawn in Living Trees on the Forest Surface, now have a chance of including the Finch Staff, Ladybug Minecart, and the Sunflower Minecart.
Shaking trees in the forest has a chance to drop either Acorns, an Apple, an Apricot, Coins, Eucalyptus Sap, a Grapefruit, a Lemon, a Peach, or Wood. Birds or Squirrels, or sometimes their gold counterparts, may also fall or fly out of the tree.
Slimes spawning in the Forest during a Windy Day now have a chance to be attached to a Windy Balloon and have the chance to drop a variety of Kites.
Surface chests now include Can Of Worms, Step Stool, Sunflower Minecart, and Wood.
Sakura and Yellow Willow trees now have a 1/20 (5%) chance of replacing normal Forest trees during world generation.
The Golfer, Guide, Merchant, and Zoologist NPCs now like living in the Forest, while the Dye Trader and Painter dislike it.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Added Armed Zombies which are more powerful and spawn in the Forest at night in Expert Mode.
Enchanted Sword Shrines have a chance to spawn in the outer thirds of the world with a 1-block wide shaft going up to the Surface, revealing the Enchanted Sword Shrine underground that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of having a real sword, and breaking the real sword has a 9/10 (90%) chance of dropping an Enchanted Sword and 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping an Arkhalis.
Gold Critters now have a very rare chance to spawn in the Forest.
Pinky now drops Pink Gel.
Red Squirrels now spawn regularly alongside normal Squirrels.
Surface chests now include Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage, Herb Bags, Radar, and Wand of Sparking.
Desktop 1.2.4: 
Grasshoppers now spawn in the Forest when destroying grass.
Multiple Angler quest fish can now be caught in the Forest (only when the Angler asks for them), including Bunnyfish, Cap'n Tunabeard, Dirtfish, Dynamite Fish, Fallen Starfish, the Fish of Cthulhu, Harpyfish,  Slimefish, Wyverntail, and Zombie Fish.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Butterflies, Ducks, and Mallard Ducks now spawn in the Forest, along with Fireflies which only spawn at night and Worms which only spawn when it's Raining.
Desktop 1.2.2: 
Christmas Zombies, including Santa and Sweater Zombies, now spawn in the Forest at night during Christmas.
Desktop 1.2.1: 
Costumed Demon Eyes and Zombies, including Nurse, Pixie, and Superhero Zombies and Owl and Spaceship Demon Eyes, now spawn in the Forest at night during Halloween.
Hay now drops when cutting grass with a Sickle.
Hoppin' Jack and Ravens now spawn in the Forest at night during Halloween.
Pumpkins now grow naturally in the Forest during Halloween.
Desktop 1.2.0.3: 
Blue Jays, Cardinals, and Squirrels now spawn regularly in the Forest.
Desktop 1.2: 
Blue Berries and Yellow Marigolds can now grow in the Forest.
Living Trees now spawn occasionally on the Forest surface and have a chance of having an Underground room with a chest including a Leaf Wand, Living Wood Wand, and/or a Living Loom.
Multiple new Demon Eye and Zombie variants can now spawn in the Forest at night.
Multiple variations now exist. Trees and background can vary from instance to instance, even in the same world.
Surface chests now include Climbing Claws, Rope, and the Umbrella. They also now include Tin Bars and Lead Bars as opposed to Copper Bars and Iron Bars respectively in worlds which have those ores.
The new Painter NPC now sells the Through the Window painting when in the Forest.
Wraiths now have a 1/100 (1%) chance of dropping the Fast Clock.
Zombies now have a 1/250 (0.4%) chance of dropping the Zombie Arm.
Desktop 1.1: 
4 new Hardmode enemies now spawn in the Forest at Night: Possessed Armors, Wandering Eyes, Wraiths, and Werewolves, the latter of which only spawns during Full Moons and have a 1/60 (1.67%) chance of dropping the Moon Charm.
Bald Zombies now spawn at night alongside normal Zombies.

Daybloom now grows on the Forest surface.

title: Cosmic Skateboard
content:
The Cosmic Skateboard is a Hardmode, post-Golem pet-summoning item that spawns an Alien Skater that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Alien Skater turns its skateboard into a rocket-powered hoverboard to catch up to them. The Cosmic Skateboard has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer in Master Mode.


== Trivia ==
The Alien Skater's buff tooltip, "How do you do, fellow humans?", is a reference to a cutaway gag in the American television sitcom 30 Rock, in which Lenny Wosniak walks up to a group of high-school students and asks "How do you do, fellow kids?" while holding two skateboards.

title: Ogre
content:
The Ogre is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss mini-boss that spawns in the Old One's Army event during wave 7 in Tier 2, and waves 5 and 6 in Tier 3.


== Behavior ==
The Ogre moves slowly towards the Eternia Crystal and attacks it and the player in the following ways:

The Ogre will hurl out a ball of Ogre Spit into his hand before tossing it at the player. This attack is used when the Ogre is farther away from the player, and, while it only damages targets struck by the ball itself, it inflicts the Oozed debuff onto any nearby player for 15 seconds upon contact with tiles, slowing them down significantly.
When a target is within close enough proximity to the Ogre, he will occasionally jump into the air and land with a shockwave, inflicting damage in an area of about ten blocks in both directions on the ground, dealing large amounts of damage and knockback.
The Ogre's last attack is a simple swing of the club, which he only does if a target is directly in front of him. This attack deals very high damage (122 / 245 / 367 in Tier 2 or 157 / 315 / 472 in Tier 3) and extreme knockback, encouraging players to keep their distance.


== Variants ==


== Notes ==
The club swing attack of the Ogre can deal minor knockback to players equipped with shields.


== Tips ==
Although the Ogre has a powerful close-ranged club swing attack, he can be easily maneuvered around due to his generally slow speed, making it easy for the player to keep their distance and dodge his snot ball and melee attacks.
Using yoyos with the Yoyo Bag equipped can be an extremely effective method of killing the Ogre.
In Tier 3, the club swing attack deals 472 damage in Master Mode, which can kill players in one hit. This is easily the most damage that can be dealt by a single attack from any of the enemies in the Old One's Army event, even surpassing all of Betsy's attacks.
An easy method to dodge the Ogre's stomp is to either jump before he lands or to constantly stay in the air by using wings, accessories that provide extra jumps, or by using flying mounts, such as those from The Black Spot, Witch's Broom, Shrimpy Truffle, or Cosmic Car Key.
Another easy way to dodge his jump attack is to fight the Old One's Army in space, where the very low gravity prolongs his jump to extreme lengths. This makes it easy to walk away before he lands.
It is not very wise to use a platform above the ground when fighting the Ogre for he may leap onto said platform when performing his leap. Despite the particles of the slam coming from the ground, the Ogre's slam hitbox is still carried with him to greater heights.
The Oozed debuff does not affect the speed of flying mounts that are not in contact with the ground, making them quite useful while fighting Ogres.
It is recommended to kill the Ogre before he is halfway between the Mysterious Portal and the Eternia Crystal because he will then begin to target the Crystal. His snot balls can also hit the player at this stage.


== Trivia ==
The Ogre has an Expert Mode-exclusive Treasure Bag in the game's files, but it is unobtainable, as he never actually drops it.
The Ogre only drops the Master Mode-exclusive Ogre's Club item in Tier 3 – never in Tier 2. This is in contrast to the Dark Mage, who can drop the Master Mode-exclusive Dark Mage's Tome in Tier 1 and in Tier 3.
Other than the Master Mode-exclusive drops, the Ogre Trophy, and the Creeper Egg, all of the Ogre's loot drops are not affected by luck, unlike most uncommon loot drops. Thus, they will always drop at their listed drop rates.
The Master Mode-exclusive drops (the Ogre's Club and the Ogre Relic) as well as the Ogre Trophy are affected by luck, just the same as other items of their kind are. However, the Creeper Egg is affected by luck only in Tier 3, but not in Tier 2.
An ogre is a legendary monster usually depicted as a large, hideous, man-like creature that eats ordinary human beings, especially infants and children. In mythology, ogres are often depicted as unnaturally large and tall, along with having disproportionately large heads, immense weight, abundant hair, unusually colored skin, a voracious appetite, and a strong body.
 The Bestiary entry for the Ogre: "A tall, hulking demi-human from the Old One's Army with unfathomable strength and vitality. He carries a big stick."


== Gallery ==

		
		
		
		


== See also ==
Ogres at the Dungeon Defenders 2 Wiki


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Now drops War Table and War Table Banner.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
No longer drops Squire's Shield and Apprentice's Scarf.
Increased the odds that the Tier 2 Ogre will drop a weapon from 33% to 50%. In Expert/Master mode, this has been increased from 50% to 100%.
Tier 3 Ogres also have a higher chance of dropping a weapon, up from 1/6 to 1/4 chance.
Desktop 1.4.1: Now correctly fills out its Bestiary entry completely upon its first defeat, like other main bosses.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Added Relic drop and special pet.
Desktop 1.3.4: Introduced.

Console 1.17: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.

title: Spider Nest
content:
Spider Nests, also known as Spider Caves or Spider Caverns, are mini-biomes located in the Cavern layer. They feature distinct almost pitch-black Spider Walls and there are numerous Cobwebs filling the area. The Spider Walls make Cobwebs rapidly grow back, which is a unique feature of the biome. Spider Nests can rarely contain Web Covered Chests. The Webbed Stylist NPC can also spawn here.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
The spider- and Cobweb-spawning properties of the biome are a result of the special wall tile present. Removing all the wall tiles with a hammer will effectively remove the biome.
Another unique property of the background wall type is the reduced chance of dropping Cobwebs. Instead of every Cobweb destroyed dropping one Cobweb item, only 1/4 (25%) of Cobwebs in front of this background wall will drop a Cobweb item.
The size of a Spider Nest is always between 500 tiles and 3499 tiles, inclusive. Most of the time they are in the Cavern layer and not in a Glowing Mushroom biome, but there are rare exceptions.
In worlds with The Constant enabled, Spider Nests or small patches of Spider Walls often generate at or near the surface.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Mining out all tiles near the Spider Nest, aside from the walls, may allow for a money farm to be made.
The Dangersense Potion can be useful in locating Spider Nests due to its ability to detect Cobwebs.
Creating three-block-high diagonal tunnels into a Spider Nest using a hammer to slope the floor and ceiling will prohibit spiders from exiting (or entering, if they spawn outside), but not the player. This can be a good tactic to trap and easily kill spiders. Similarly, spiders cannot fit into two-block-wide vertical tunnels and can be used the same way.
If one finds themselves crossing through a Spider Nest while creating a hellevator, in order to prevent Cobwebs from generating and slowing the player down during freefall, it can be advised to place ropes or torches on the background walls, thus occupying the space where Cobwebs are unable to grow. Alternatively, one may also use a hammer to remove the walls.


== Trivia ==
The biome features unique background objects, such as a human corpse covered in webs.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Can now generate within the Not the Bees seed.
Desktop 1.2.3: The Stylist NPC can now be found within Spider Nests.
Desktop 1.2: Introduced.

Console 1.02: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile 1.2.6508: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.
