title: Boss health bar
content:
When a player is within the range of a boss or mini-boss, a red health bar will appear on their screen that represents the boss' total remaining health. On the  Desktop version and  Console version, the bar is displayed at the bottom of the player's screen, while on the  Mobile version, it is displayed below the minimap. When there are multiple bosses in the player's range, only the most recent boss that had been damaged or the closest one in proximity to the player will be shown.
The boss health bar also has a togglable option that enables a numeric display for boss health called "Boss Health Bar Numbers" in the settings. The maximum and remaining health of the boss will be shown on the bar when the option is on.


== Notes ==
The icon on the left of the boss health bar is the map icon for that boss.
Some bosses' health bars have special displays:
The Eater of Worlds' health bar counts the total health of all segments.
The Brain of Cthulhu's health bar counts the total health of both the Creepers and the Brain itself.
Skeletron and Skeletron Prime's health bars only show the remaining health of the head.
Retinazer and Spazmatism have individual health bars.
Golem's health bar shows the total health of the head and the body, but not the fists.
The Martian Saucer's health bar shows the total health of its four weapon parts and the core.
All four Celestial Pillars have two bars, a blue-colored one for their shield and one for their actual health. The shield bar will overlay the health bar and shows the remaining enemy kills needed to destroy the shield on the bar if the numeric display is on.
The Moon Lord's health bar shows the total health of all of his damageable parts, including all three eyes and his core.
 The boss health bar will display on the bottom of the screen if the player is using a controller or keyboard and mouse.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Added an option that displays the health of the boss in the middle of the bar.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced.

title: Frostbite
content:
Frostbite is a Hardmode debuff that is a stronger version of Frostburn, preventing health regeneration and causing afflicted entities to lose health over time. Afflicted enemies lose 25 health per second (10 damage displayed every 0.4 seconds), while afflicted players lose 8 health per second (1 damage displayed every 0.13 seconds).
Its damage can be increased by Slime and Accelerated Afflictions. It can also trigger the extra damage over time from Oiled.
Visually, the debuff causes afflicted entities to emit blue fire particles and a small amount of light.

=== From player ===

title: Graveyard
content:
The Graveyard is a mini-biome that starts to appear when at least five Tombstones are near the player and completes when at least seven Tombstones are near the player. Some special visual effects can be seen in the Graveyard, and these effects grow stronger as more Tombstones are added, capped at nine Tombstones: colors desaturate, lightning randomly strikes in the background, and Ecto Mist accumulates on the ground.
When at least seven Tombstones are nearby, the Graveyard biome will gain additional functional effects: unique Graveyard enemies spawn here day and night, as well as the usual creatures originally spawning at night. The spawn rate is not increased, but the enemy spawn reduction of towns is weakened. NPC vendors have unique trades here, and the Ecto Mist on the ground enables unique crafting recipes for the player.
Sunflowers can prevent the forming of Graveyards: each Sunflower nearby negates the presence of one Tombstone.


== Contents ==


=== NPC quotes ===
Most NPCs display unique quotes when spoken to in a Graveyard:


== Notes ==
All Tombstones within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the player are considered when determining whether the area is a Graveyard biome.
Each Sunflower within the same area makes the Graveyard biome require one additional Tombstone to form (e.g. six Tombstones are required to form the biome if one Sunflower is nearby); additionally, Sunflowers will not grant the Happy! buff if there are at least five Tombstones within this area.
While night-only enemies can spawn at daytime through the graveyard, nocturnal bosses still cannot be spawned during the day.
NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed, making it possible to build a Graveyard without sacrificing a character.
Although most NPCs will complain when in a Graveyard, it does not actually affect their happiness at all. As a Graveyard is always in combination with a different biome, their happiness value will be based on the other present biome.
However, the Painter will not sell the paintings Daylight, First Encounter, Good Morning, Underground Reward, Through the Window, Place Above the Clouds, and Sky Guardian if he is spoken to in a Graveyard.
Normally, certain enemies with the Fighter AI cannot open doors and Tall Gates unless during a Blood Moon. In a Graveyard, these enemies have a 1/60 (1.67%) chance to open a door or Tall Gate even outside of a Blood Moon.
An underground Graveyard will generate Ecto Mist, but not spawn its enemies.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
A large amount of Ecto Mist coats surfaces in Graveyard biomes, which can obscure items like Pressure Plates.
The large number of enemies spawns, including the particularly powerful Ghosts, can make the Graveyard fairly dangerous during the early game. Players may wish to avoid letting Tombstones accumulate around their base and spawn point.
This is especially true for Mediumcore players, as generating Tombstones over and over at the same spawn point can lead to a softlock situation, where it becomes almost impossible to retrieve items without being attacked.
Tombstones require two adjacent tiles of free space in order to be placed. Their placement can be prevented altogether by rendering at least every other block of a surface invalid, which includes placing platforms, Torches, furniture, or saplings, sloping the blocks with a hammer, deactivating them with Actuators, or simply digging them out.
Placing Sunflowers around common death spots such as arenas can help to prevent a Graveyard from being created without the need to constantly mine Tombstones.
Strategically placed Sunflowers with an overlapping radius can also create a pocket of non-Graveyard within the biome. This can be especially useful in worlds where the secret world seed What a horrible night to have a curse is enabled, allowing the player to go just outside a structure during the day without spawning Graveyard enemies while inside.
Collecting Tombstones in the early game and creating a Graveyard can be a way to easily obtain Abigail's Flower and farm Maggots as bait from Maggot Zombies.
The Dryad sells Crimson Seeds in a Corrupt world and Corrupt Seeds in a Crimson world during Hardmode when housed in a Graveyard biome, facilitating the presence of both evil biomes in one world without bringing items from other worlds.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
The Peace Candle now reduces the boosted spawn rates of Graveyard biomes by 33%.
Statue enemies and Moss Zombies now spawn in Graveyard biomes.
Spectre Goggles are now also sold by the Mechanic in Graveyards.
Echo Coating is now already sold prior to defeating Plantera, provided the Mechanic is present in the world.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Hoppin' Jacks can now spawn in the Hardmode Graveyard at any time of the year.
Increased Graveyard threshold of Tombstones by 1.
Added an achievement.
Desktop 1.4.0.3: Ecto Mist clouds can no longer be removed by disabling Blood and Gore.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.4.0.3.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.4.0.3.

title: Deerclops
content:
Deerclops is a pre-Hardmode boss encountered in the Snow biome. Fighting Deerclops is not required for game progression, but defeating it rewards the player with coins and other useful items.
While Deerclops is alive, its exclusive music Deerclops will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning and spawning ==
Deerclops can be summoned manually by using a Deer Thing in the Snow or Ice biome, at any time.
Deerclops can also spawn naturally at midnight (12:00 AM) in the surface Snow biome during a Blizzard when the following conditions are fulfilled:

At least one player in the world is in the surface Snow biome.
This player has at least 200 maximum health or at least 9 defense.
There are no town NPCs within a 240×135-tile rectangle centered on this player.
There are no other bosses already alive.
None of the following events are active: Old One's Army, Pumpkin Moon, Frost Moon, or any invasion.
Note that this excludes certain events, such as the Blood Moon. They do not prevent Deerclops from spawning.
No Martian Probe is alive.
The countdown for the spawning of the Moon Lord has not begun, either due to manual summoning or defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar.
In Remix and Zenith worlds, Deerclops will only naturally spawn in Snow biomes on the Surface layer, where the Blizzard visual effect is not displayed.
Deerclops will not spawn in the Cavern layer where the Blizzard effect is displayed.
If Deerclops has previously been defeated in the world, there is only a 1/4 (25%) chance for it to spawn naturally at midnight.


== Behavior ==

Deerclops has four / five attacks:
If it is close enough to the player, Deerclops will raise its arms and smash the ground after a brief delay, summoning an escalating wave of Ice Spikes that quickly travels toward the player. Every third consecutive wave does not travel as far as the standard version, has a slightly longer delay before triggering, and spreads outwards from both directions. Ice Spikes freeze the player for 0.33 / 0.67 / 0.83 seconds.
If it is not close enough to its target to use the Ice Spikes attack, Deerclops will "scoop" and then throw numerous chunks of Debris into the air, which travel in large, vertical arcs before falling back down. The chunks of Debris can pass through blocks. The visual appearance of the Debris changes depending on the blocks Deerclops is standing on while performing the attack. However, this does not affect the amount of damage the Debris chunks deal to the player.
Deerclops will occasionally stand in place and roar, inflicting the Slow debuff on all players within 50 tiles for 12 / 24 / 30 seconds, unless they are already affected by the debuff.
If the player is above Deerclops for enough time, it momentarily remains still before roaring and summoning five Shadow Hands around the player.
In Expert Mode, Shadow Hands will be periodically summoned that either move toward the player slowly, move towards the player quickly and curve, or spin in place. Shadow Hands predict the player's movements and are summoned more frequently as Deerclops's health is lowered.
If the player is more than 30 tiles away from Deerclops, it becomes cloaked in a shadowy aura, emits black smoke particles, turns a dark shade of purple while its eye turns magenta in coloration, and two reddish, semi-transparent afterimages begin closely orbiting around it. Deerclops is completely immune to damage while in this state until the player is again within 30 tiles of its current location, causing it to revert back to its regular appearance and behavior.


== Notes ==
When Deerclops is alive, the opacity of the Blizzard visual effect will be reduced.
If all players are dead or there are none nearby, Deerclops will go to the Snow biome it spawned in (if possible) and wander around there instead of immediately despawning. This will happen until a player gets close to the boss, at which point the fight will resume as normal. Once one in-game day (24 real-world minutes) has passed since Deerclops's spawn, it will despawn as soon as no players are near. Leaving and re-entering the world will also cause it to despawn.
While Deerclops is alive, time cannot be accelerated by sleeping in a bed.
Deerclops cannot pass through solid blocks, but if the player is above it, far enough away, and Deerclops cannot reach them, it will quickly rise through the blocks in order to reach the player.
Defeating Deerclops is not required for the Slayer of Worlds achievement.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

There are no prerequisite bosses that are required to be defeated in order to summon this boss. However, Deerclops' strength may warrant waiting until the player has defeated the Eater of Worlds or the Brain of Cthulhu to fight it.
With sufficient skill, the Deerclops can be defeated earlier in game progression, which can be helpful to the player during pre-Hardmode.
A Warmth Potion is useful when fighting Deerclops, as the boss is affected by its buff. In addition, one may find it useful to bring a Hand Warmer to the battle, since the Frozen debuff can easily cause the player to die quickly if inflicted.
Building a platform of non-solid blocks about 6 tiles (twice the height of the player) up in the air, along with staircases made of solid blocks on either side to allow Deerclops to get on, can elevate it high enough above the ground to prevent the boss from using its debris attack entirely, making the fight much easier.Verify
Due to being able to inflict Slow from a large range, accessories like the Anklet of the Wind or Magiluminescence alongside Swiftness Potions can help make the fight much more manageable.
Avoid lingering directly above Deerclops, as the Shadow Hands it summons in this situation are very dangerous.
The player can run between Deerclops's legs without taking damage. This is useful for avoiding the first two Ice Spike attacks, but the player should not stick around for the third.
Players should place their spawn point away from where Deerclops can wander, as it can stay around the spawn area.
This is especially recommended for Mediumcore players, as they can be left defenseless near Deerclops if they die in the middle of the fight.
Conversely, moving the player spawn to where the Deerclops was summoned can allow players to eventually kill it even on higher difficulty and with early game equipment. The Deerclops will remain until the player respawns, never recovers health, and only despawns after a full day has passed. Hammering the surfaces or placing furniture can prevent the area from becoming a Graveyard.
The Frozen debuff from the Ice Spike attack is capable of interrupting a player's extending grappling hook, causing them to drop to the ground. Avoid moving over large gaps to prevent unnecessary damage.
Combining the Frog Leg and the Tsunami in a Bottle and taking the Deerclops to flat terrain with no floating platforms is an effective strategy. Being on the ground next to the Deerclops momentarily prompts the Ice Spike attack, even during the automatically jump from the Frog Leg. With the Tsunami in a Bottle the player is able to jump high enough to dodge the attack consistently, while attacking with a weapon that has good range. This can avoid its other attacks altogether as it always uses Ice Spike if the player is on the same horizontal plane as the Deerclops.
Jumping at about a 30° angle away from a point about five blocks below the Deerclops puts the player in an area safe from both variations of Ice Spike.
Due to its tall hitbox, a player with high defense and healing can remain stationary and deal a large amount of damage with the Snowball Launcher without being significantly impacted by the Slow debuff.


== Trivia ==

Deerclops is part of the Don't Starve Together crossover. Many of the items of this crossover are dropped by Deerclops.
Deerclops's purple invulnerable form in Terraria resembles its Winter's Feast form in Don't Starve Together.
Deerclops is a portmanteau of deer and cyclops.
Clop is also a cross-linguistic onomatopoeic term for the sound of a horse's hooves, and may be used for other animals' hooves in some places.
It is the only non-event boss in Terraria to not despawn immediately after killing the player.
Deerclops is one of the two bosses that consists of a single destructible entity, the other being the Empress of Light.
All other boss fights are composed of either multiple bosses, multiple segments, or summoned minions that play a part in their battles.
 Between the versions 1.4.3 and 1.4.3.6, there was an NPC named DeerclopsLeg in the files which did not appear during the fight. It was invincible and had its own AI. It was removed in the 1.4.4 update, with its NPC ID replaced with that of the Stinkbug.
Deerclops is the first non-event crossover boss, as well as the first pre-Hardmode crossover boss.
 The Bestiary entry for  Deerclops: "Hailing from a distant land, this cyclopic monstrosity lurks in cold places, wreaking havoc on those who disturb it."


== Gallery ==

		
		
		


== See also ==
Deerclops at the Don't Starve Wiki


== History ==

Shadow Hands damage detection moved to match its hands better.
Fixed cases of Shadow Hands hurting players despite extremely low, unfair visibility.
Fixed Deerclops' Ice Spike animation and roars desyncing in multiplayer.
Fixed Deerclops' screen shakes not working in multiplayer.

The player can now dash through Deerclops' legs using a Shield of Cthulhu or Solar armor (previously they would collide with it).
Fixed Shadow Hands appearing on top of non-targeted players in multiplayer.
No longer spawns when the Journey Mode's spawn rate slider is set to 0×.

Now grants an achievement upon defeat.
Now has a chance to drop Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester.
Now takes up more enemy slots, reducing or outright eliminating enemy spawns during its fight.
Removed the unused Deerclops Leg NPC.

Deerclops's health now scales at a modified rate in Expert and Master, like other bosses.
This reduces its health from 7000 / 14000 / 21000 to 7000 / 11900 / 15172.
Fixed an issue where Deerclops's health did not scale up with increased player count in Expert/Master multiplayer games.
Now only remains present in the Snow biome for 1 day when no players are present, instead of 3 days.
Deerclops's boss health bar will disappear from the screen when suitably far enough away from it that the boss fight is not active.
Defense increased from 0 to 10.
After defeating Deerclops, it now only has a 25% chance to spawn again naturally under proper conditions. This was previously a 100% chance.
Now drops Healing Potions.

Added immunity to Confused.
Damage is now affected by Warmth Potions.
Now correctly drops coins.

title: Magical Pumpkin Seed
content:
The Magical Pumpkin Seed is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Squashling that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Squashling will twirl and fly after the player to catch up to them. The Magical Pumpkin Seed has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being obtained from harvesting fully-grown Pumpkins during the Halloween seasonal event.


== Tips ==
During the Halloween event, Pumpkins will randomly grow on grass tiles. Pumpkin Seeds can also be purchased from the Dryad and planted by the player.
Pumpkins can be harvested by any means (such as actuators) in order to obtain the Magical Pumpkin Seed. This will make an effective farming system when combined with Conveyor Belts leading to the player's house or another collection point.
Destroying them can also be done manually with weapons or ammo.


== Trivia ==
The Squashling may be a reference to the Squashlings from the 2004 massively multiplayer online role-playing game World of Warcraft and the 2014 digital card game Hearthstone, which appear during a similarly Halloween-themed seasonal event called Hallow's End.


== History ==

Desktop 1.2.1: Introduced.

title: Guide
content:
The Guide is usually the first NPC a player encounters. He spawns near the player when the world is created. He provides tips mainly aimed at new players via the “Help” option and displays crafting recipes (including the crafting station required) of items shown to him via the “Crafting” option.
Unlike most other NPCs, the Guide spawns upon world creation, before a house is available. He will, however, move into the first house built. If he is killed, a proper house will need to be built before he can respawn, but he has no additional requirements.
The Guide will defend himself against nearby enemies using a Wooden Bow, firing Wooden Arrows initially and then upgrading to Flaming Arrows during Hardmode. He deals 8 / 12 / 14 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Guide will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
(Desktop version) When checking condition for name-based NPC drops, the game specifically requires the NPC's name to be using the corresponding localization string. The game's translation and Resource Packs will not affect name-based item drops: the Guide can only drop the Green Cap if he is originally named Andrew. Using a Resource Pack that changes this name does not prevent it from dropping, and changing any other names of the Guide to Andrew does not qualify for item drop.
While NPCs cannot usually be attacked directly by players, the Guide Voodoo Doll will allow players to attack the Guide.
This trait is shared with the Clothier, his respective item being the Clothier Voodoo Doll.
Killing the Guide in The Underworld via the use of a Guide Voodoo Doll, or allowing the Guide to die in the Underworld while he is in contact with lava, will summon the Wall of Flesh.
The Guide, like any other friendly NPC, will not respawn unless it is daytime.
The stats of weapons shown in the Guide's crafting recipe list use adjusted damage and critical strike chance based on any bonuses the player currently has equipped, such as the Molten armor's set bonus. Un-equipping items that adjust damage and critical strike chance while speaking to the Guide allows seeing the base values.
Killing the Guide grants the player a minor, temporary luck boost (see Luck § Ladybug luck for details).
The Guide does not provide information about Shimmer transmutations of items.
The Guide provides hints on how to summon every boss, with the exception of Queen Slime and the Empress of Light.
The Guide is replaced as the starting NPC by various other NPCs in special world seeds and secret world seeds:
The Demolitionist is the starting NPC in For the Worthy worlds.
The Party Girl is the starting NPC in Drunk worlds.
The Merchant is the starting NPC in Not the Bees worlds.
The Tax Collector is the starting NPC in Remix worlds.
The Zoologist is the starting NPC in Vampirism worlds.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Considering there are no downsides to having the Guide unhappy, the player could simply put the Guide anywhere in the world without any consequences. The best place for the Guide is the Glowing Mushroom biome with the Truffle, who loves the Guide.


== Names ==
The Guide may have any of the following names:


== Advice ==
The Guide displays one of the lines listed below when his “Help” option is selected. He cycles through the lines when the option is selected repeatedly. Much of his advice text depends on the player's current game progression.
Some lines may vary depending on what game platform Terraria is played on.

In the Tutorial(Console and Mobile versions), the Guide has some additional dialogue to teach the player how to progress.


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
One of the Guide's names is Andrew, named after Andrew Spinks (aka Redigit), the lead developer of Terraria.
The Green Cap is dropped if a Guide with that name is killed.
The Guide's Shimmered form is a reference to Redigit's avatar.
For players who use help from other sources rather than the Guide, his role is usually minimal. Otherwise, he lives up to his name, as a primary source of in-game hints and information.

Redigit said during an AMA on Reddit that he created the Guide Voodoo Doll so players could get revenge on him for always opening the door.
The Guide opening doors for enemies at night is a recurring joke among the fanbase, which is also referenced during the credits.
The Guide is depicted in two paintings, Guide Picasso and The Creation of the Guide.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, there is an organization called "Order of the Guide", whose purpose is to preserve old legends and knowledge. The Guide is most likely a member of this order.
This is referenced in-game after beating the Wall of Flesh, with any new Guides that spawn in afterward referencing their predecessor suddenly bursting into flames.
The Guide and the Arms Dealer appear to not get along. This is evidenced by them frequently arguing through emotes, along with the Arms Dealer's quote “I heard there is a doll that looks very similar to <name of Guide> somewhere in the underworld.  I'd like to put a few rounds in it.”. Despite this, they do not have any effect on each other's happiness.
The Goblin Tinkerer and the Mechanic will similarly flirt through emotes. These are the only four NPCs to have unique interactions when talking to a specific NPC.
In the past, Redigit has said the Guide is the Wall of Flesh, the brother of the ninja seen inside King Slime, the great-grandson of the Nymph, and the son of the Moon Lord. These statements were most likely jokes and are not considered official lore.
The Guide says that he has much in common with the Zoologist and the Clothier. This may be referring to the fact that they are all cursed with some sort of transformation that is out of their control (if the Guide is indeed the Wall of Flesh).
According to the Voodoo Demon's Bestiary entry, the Guide is said to be the "chosen one whose soul is linked with the world's guardian himself", most likely referring to the Wall of Flesh.
The Guide has the first Bestiary entry.
 The Bestiary entry for the Guide: "The Guide always offers useful advice and crafting recipes. His origins and unusual connections to this world remain a mystery."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Increased defense from 15 to 30.
Increased health regeneration by 500%.
Increased arrow damage from 8 to 12.
Fixed the Green Cap's drop condition affected by game translation and Resource Packs.
Desktop 1.4.4.8: Added the following advice: "You can even remove people from their home from the housing interface! ⚷ Open / Activate the banner hanging in their house. You can also ⚒ Use / Attack to assign them to a new home."
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Changed two advice texts:
"Smashing a shadow orb will sometimes cause a meteor to fall out of the sky. Shadow orbs can usually be found in the chasms around corrupt areas." to "Shadow orbs can usually be found in the chasms around corrupt areas. Smashing too many will unleash the Eater of Worlds. Defeating this foe may cause meteors to fall out of the sky!"
"Smashing a crimson heart will sometimes cause a meteor to fall out of the sky. Crimson hearts can usually be found in the chasms around crimtane areas." to "Crimson hearts can usually be found in the chasms around crimson areas. Smashing too many will unleash the Brain of Cthulhu. Defeating this foe may cause meteors to fall out of the sky!"
Added "Jan" as a possible name.
Desktop 1.4.3.3: The Guide now has a hint about how to find Deerclops if the player has not yet defeated it.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Massively overhauled the Guide's help dialogue, adding hints and tips for content all the way up to the Lunar Events, addressing all new NPCs since 1.1, replacing outdated information, and bringing some previously bugged lines back into circulation.

title: Guide:Queen Slime strategies
content:
Queen Slime is an optional early Hardmode boss fought in The Hallow. She is the Hardmode counterpart of King Slime.


== Spawn Conditions ==
Queen Slime can be summoned by using a Gelatin Crystal in The Hallow, which is found in the Underground Hallow in the same places as Crystal Shards.


== The Fight ==
In her first phase, Queen Slime jumps around in a similar fashion to King Slime, though much faster. Upon being damaged, she summons Crystal Slimes, Heavenly Slimes, or Bouncy Slimes. Crystal Slimes will fire several crystal spikes upward, Heavenly Slimes will fly towards the player, and Bouncy Slimes will fire bouncing shots towards the player. After a few jumps, she does one of two things, chosen at random:

Will stay in one place for a few seconds, before jumping very quickly towards the player and attempt to stomp them, dealing high damage.
Will stay in one place for a few seconds, before firing 6 Regal Gel that bounce twice before breaking. Sometimes, she will perform this attack multiple times in a row.
Killing the smaller slimes should be a priority during this phase, as they can quickly overwhelm the player.
When at 50% health, Queen Slime will grow wings and begin to fly like a Slimer. Her AI also changes:

She will occasionally shoot Regal Gel in 10 directions.
She will occasionally attempt to fly above and drop down onto the player.


=== Expert/Master Mode ===
Queen Slime receives few changes in higher difficulties, beyond her minions having a faster attack rate and/or more projectiles. Continually moving or using crowd control weapons can reduce or eliminate these minions completely, making the fight fairly straightforward.


== General Strategies ==


=== Terrain Preparation ===
Queen Slime shoots out bouncing projectiles that can be a challenge to dodge, especially in the second stage. Fighting in an off-ground arena with platforms on the bottom will allow the projectiles to fall out safely. For example, a Sky Bridge consisted of platforms is extremely recommended. If Lava Waders or its upgrades are available, it may be a good idea to use Bubbles and lava instead of platforms, as the neither the Queen Slime in the first phase nor the slimes she summons can stand on them. This will come at the cost of slowing down each time the player moves through the lava. Alternatively, setting up a basic arena, and using the gravity strategy (see Specific Strategies below) is perfectly suitable. Using the Trusty Chillet mount to dash through the minions that Queen Slime summons while dealing damage is also a viable technique, due to their long immunity frames provided. 


=== Gearing Up ===


==== Armor ====
Titanium armor provides solid stat bonuses and the powerful Titanium Barrier.
Adamantite armor forgoes the special set bonus for higher stats. Melee and ranged users can swap to Frost Breastplate and Mythril Greaves/Spider Greaves for even higher stats.
Frost armor provides roughly the same melee/ranged bonuses as Adamantite or Titanium, and inflicts a useful Frostbite debuff that is often strong enough to kill spawned slimes with only a single scratch.
Orichalcum armor provides acceptable stats with a set bonus that helps killing the spawned slimes.
Palladium armor provides lower stat bonuses, but the Rapid Healing greatly increases natural regeneration.
Hallowed armor becomes a great choice if you have already defeated a mechanical boss, since the Holy Protection buff does wonders for survivability.
Spider armor is a good choice for summoners due to the increased minion slots.
Obsidian armor is a useful alternative for whip users due to its increases to whip speed and range.
Forbidden armor is a viable armor set for both summoners and mages due to the efficiency of its set bonus.


==== Weapons ====
It is important to have weapons that can deal with the crowd of slimes that she summons, as well as weapons that can reach her in her winged form.

For Melee users
The Shadowflame Knife is good because of its accuracy and bouncing projectiles, as well as the ability to inflict Shadowflame on multiple minions.
The Bananarang has a higher damage output than the Shadowflame Knife, but is less consistent due to the lack of bouncing projectiles
The Sergeant United Shield is extremely effective at taking out the Queen's minions during her first phase, however it has trouble keeping up in the second phase.
Yoyos are excellent in this fight due to their range and being easy to aim. Good choices include Amarok or Hel-Fire (or Yelets if you already defeated a mechanical boss).
The Obsidian Swordfish has high damage and pierce with its flames, and is especially useful for the first phase.
Flails such as the Drippler Crippler, Chain Guillotines, or Dao of Pow are useful in this fight for their high amount of damage and reach.
The Ice Sickle is weaker than most of the above options, but is relatively safe and easy to obtain.
For Ranged users
The Dart Pistol or Dart Rifle with Crystal Darts is useful due to its high damage output and its semi-homing ricochet ability, which can kill all of the nearby slimes that are summoned. The other dart types can also be effective for their debuffs.
The Daedalus Stormbow, while also being useful for killing the smaller slimes, can still do a hefty amount of damage to Queen Slime when paired with Holy, Ichor or Cursed Arrows and a Magic Quiver.
The Ore Repeaters are weaker but still strong alternatives.
The Shadowflame Bow, Marrow, and Ice Bow have better stats but lack arrow variance.
The Onyx Blaster is extremely powerful against Queen Slime when used with Crystal Bullets and supported with Ichor; however it has issues against the slimes. The Megashark is a stronger alternative but requires the defeat of The Destroyer.
The Barrel Launcher does weak damage against Queen Slime herself, but can easily handle the minions she produces and requires no ammo. It is best used during the first stage.
For Magic users
The Meteor Staff is a high damage weapon that can be used for most bosses at this point in the game, but it uses a lot of mana very quickly, so a lot of mana potions will be required.
The Lightning Strike is a similar weapon to the Meteor Staff, although being slower but less mana-hungry. It can also electrify water which is very helpful if fighting the boss underwater.
The Crystal Storm also deals respectable DPS, especially if using the Blessed Apple mount in the second phase, as Queen Slime will ram into all of the projectiles.
The Flower of Frost and Cursed Flames tomes have great crowd control due to their debuffs. The Frost Staff is a weaker alternative.
The Life Drain is extremely useful for killing large groups of slimes with little aiming required. It also provides a noticeable increase to regeneration, but it should be used primarily for healing due to its lackluster performance against single targets and high mana drain.
The Nimbus Rod can provide some additional DPS against all targets. Casting it immediately before starting the fight is a decent option, as it does not constantly drain mana and its clouds linger for a significant duration.
The Killing Deck has good crowd control and is easy to aim in both phases, although optimal damage requires either staying close or timing attacks carefully.
The Sky Fracture is a decent choice all around, being able to hit Queen Slime herself easily as well as effectively deal with her slime minions, although it is a bit harder to aim properly in the second phase.
The Spirit Flame deals very high damage, but is only really useful in the second phase: During phase one, it is too hard to control which enemy it targets, often hitting a slime minion instead of Queen Slime herself (or vice-versa). In phase two, it becomes useful against Queen Slime if you can follow her closely, as the minion slimes are far less likely to be right next to her when she is flying.
The Crystal Serpent can deal high damage to Queen Slime because of her large size, but it will not deal with the smaller slimes well.
The Golden Shower is useful in this fight, as with most Hardmode boss fights, for its defense-lowering ability, although as a penetrating weapon, it is also reasonably useful on its own for clearing out the slime minions.
If The Twins were fought beforehand, the Rainbow Rod crafted from the souls is one of the best options for fighting Queen Slime, due to the area of effect damage and piercing in addition to it having homing capabilities, letting the player kill all the minions quickly while constantly dealing damage to Queen Slime.
For Summoners
Abigail's Flower, despite being a pre-Hardmode summon weapon, receives a massive buff in Hardmode that makes it one of the best summon weapon for Queen Slime, but only when paired with the Firecracker. This is because the Firecracker explosions combined with Abigail's own area damage kill most of the minions as soon as they spawn, making it much easier to avoid damage.
The Sanguine Staff is the best staff for this fight that doesn't require a whip, due to its high drop rate, damage, and aerial tracking, which allows it to consistently hit Queen Slime through out the second phase. Keep in mind that the Dreadnautilus is a rare and formidable enemy in its own right.
The Ruinous Staff is a reliable, slow-firing minion that deals fantastic damage to the boss especially when paired with the Firecracker, although crafting it requires Forbidden Fragments, making it somewhat hard to obtain.
Whips, while not very reliable as primary weapons, greatly increase minions' damage with their damage tags. Their effectiveness increases with the use of Flasks, especially Ichor Flasks.
The Firecracker has very high DPS when used as a main weapon if both the player and their minions are attacking the same target due to its ability of creating explosion on tagged enemies after minions hit them. However its short range makes it a somewhat risky choice unless using Obsidian armor.
The Cool Whip's snowflake effect and long range can be useful for clearing out minions in Phase 1. In Phase 2, if minions such as the Spider Staff cannot hit Queen Slime, then whips may be your only damage source; in this situation, Cool Whip does the most damage.
Using the Firecracker for the first phase and the Cool Whip for the second phase, with Obsidian armor, is better than using either one alone when using weaker minions such as the Spider Staff and Imp Staff.
The Pirate Staff and Spider Staff provide high damage during the first part of the fight, but struggle to catch up to Queen Slime during her second phase.
The Queen Spider Staff can help quite a lot with dealing with the many minion slimes, depending on where you place its sentries. In the second phase, the Barnacle Staff can be placed mid-air and has high accuracy.


==== Accessories ====
There are many great accessories available at this point.

Frozen Wings, Fairy Wings, Harpy Wings, or Fin Wings are the best wings available at this stage. Lightning Boots or better will provide better ground movement. Amphibian Boots can also be used because they increase the ascent speed of wings. Those two accessories will allow you to move almost freely through the air and on the ground.
The Cobalt Shield or its upgrades prevents knockback, which can be useful in the second phase as projectiles can cover the screen.
The Frozen Turtle Shell is a defensive accessory that reduces damage if your health starts getting low. The Expert Mode-exclusive Worm Scarf is also effective.
The Expert Mode-exclusive Brain of Confusion is an accessory that grants you a chance completely dodging an attack, making it very handy for this fight. However, the boss herself and the minions she summons are all immune to the Confused debuff, making it less effective.
The Cross Necklace (or Star Veil) will make rapid hits more survivable.
The Charm of Myths enhances survivability by providing regeneration and reducing the duration of Potion Sickness.
It must remain equipped to keep the cooldown reduction.
An Emblem provides additional damage for your primary damage type;
Yoyo fighters should use the Yoyo Bag or Magic Yoyo Bag to make targeting easier.
The Harpy Charm can be used to redirect missed arrow shots.
The Magic Quiver is recommended for bow users, especially if using the Jester or Unholy Arrows.
The Phoenix Quiver is an upgrade to both the Harpy Charm and Magic Quiver and is very powerful, redirecting some missed arrows and adding a damage over time effect.
Magic users who wish to rely less on Mana Potions can equip a pair of Magic Cuffs/Celestial Cuffs. Slimes drop mana stars frequently.
The Putrid Scent provides a generic increase to DPS and is a decent filler accessory.
Summoners should be wearing the Pygmy Necklace for the extra minion slot and damage.
The Squire's Shield/Apprentice's Scarf are great choices for summoners, although they don't stack.
The Berserker's Glove is an excellent accessory for summoners, due to its defense increase, bonuses to whip speed and size, as well as enabling whip autoswing. Its recommended to reforge this to Warding rather than Menacing due to the massive defensive boost it provides (+12 defense on Warding), which helps patch up summoner armors generally low defense.
Whipstacking summoners can benefit from the Snake Band, Silver Bracer and Wicked Armlet, or their upgrades.
One such upgrade, the Armlet Of Ruin, adds an area of effect ability every six seconds, even without whipstacking.
As with most situations in general, it is best to reforge your accessories with damage, critical strike chance or defense increasing modifiers.


==== Potions ====
Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, Lifeforce Potion, and Ironskin Potion will greatly increase survivability.
Gravitation Potions are very useful for dodging during her second phase, especially when paired with the Shield of Cthulhu.
Any food item that provides the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied, or Exquisitely Stuffed buff is helpful.
Mana Regeneration Potion is a must for mages.
Swiftness Potion will increase mobility.
Rage Potion and Wrath Potion will improve DPS.
Magic Power Potion, Archery Potion, Ale or Sake, and Summoning Potion will further improve it for mages, rangers, melee, and summoner users respectively.


== Specific & Most Effective Strategies ==


=== Gravitation Potions ===
Due to her flight allowing her to keep up with you but out of range of her attacks, which are affected by gravity, makes maneuvering with the Gravitation Potion an extremely effective strategy in the 2nd phase. Use a strong weapon with range, or flying summons such as the Imp or Sanguine Staves, and you should fairly easily dodge all her attacks while flipping gravity and falling while hitting her in return. The Slime Mount is recommended for this in order to boost your falling speed in space and quick fall out of range of her if she approaches too closely. This, paired with the Shield of Cthulhu can make her second phase a breeze.


=== Skybridge ===
Fighting on a long skybridge can make avoiding the spawned slimes much easier. Queen Slime is fairly slow in her first stage, but her winged form can keep up with the mounts summoned by the Goat Skull and Blessed Apple. Be careful if you reverse directions as all previously summoned slimes will still be alive.
Alternatively, during the second stage, Queen Slime follows a fairly predictable pattern. The player can run back and forth on the skybridge, jumping over projectiles, and Queen Slime will remain at roughly the same height the entire time, making targeting easier.


=== Minecart Track ===
A long Minecart track makes this boss very easy to defeat, as it can keep up with her fastest speed and outpaces most of the minions. It is similar to using a mount on a skybridge.


=== Water Walking on the Ocean ===
Using Water Walking Boots or its tinkers or Water Walking Potion, Queen Slime can be fought over the Ocean. Her projectiles will sink into the ocean, and 2/3 of the slimes she summon cannot shoot while they are floating.
Make sure to keep moving with this strategy as Queen Slime will repeatedly sink into the Ocean and then teleport to your position in the first phase.


=== Swimming in the Ocean with Mounts ===
Using the Lava Shark mount, Queen Slime can be fought inside the Ocean. This strategy works the same way as the Water Walking strategy. However, it provides better mobility and it's safer, as it's very unlikely that Queen Slime will be able to deal contact damage to you, and considering almost no minion slimes can reach you while you are underwater. 
The Lava Shark mount can be hard to obtain, through opening Obsidian Crates from fishing in lava.


=== Lava Layer ===
Like nearly all bosses, Queen Slime is immune to lava, but her minions are not. A thin layer of lava can be used to take out most of her minions. Combined with Lava Waders, Terraspark Boots, Water Walking Potions, or Obsidian Skin Potions, you can easily decimate her.

title: Sanguine Staff
content:
The Sanguine Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Sanguine Bat minion. It flies in an elliptical loop between the player and the target enemy. Sanguine Bats arrange themselves along a semicircle around the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Sanguine Staff has a 1/2 (50%) / guaranteed chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Notes ==
The Sanguine Bat pierces infinitely on the way to its target and then on the way back to the player.
The Sanguine Bat applies -1 tick of local immunity frames upon hitting an enemy and only resets its local immunity frames at beginning of every attack cycle, which means that the bat cannot hit the same target more than once per attack cycle.
Each attack cycle of Sanguine Bats (from leaving the player's side to coming back) lasts 1.1 seconds, regardless of how far away the target is.
The Sanguine bats can target enemies up to 62.5 blocks away.
The Sanguine Bats emit a red afterimage while moving.
If dyed with Critter Shampoo, basic, bright, black compound, and gradient dyes will have little effect on the bat's colors. Silver compound dyes and some dyes obtained from Strange Plants will be discolored due to the bat's glow (such as Reflective Gold Dye coloring the bats a fiery orange, and Negative Dye making them completely black). More intense strange dyes will work properly as they override the bat's color completely.
Sanguine Bats emit a faint red light.


== Tips ==
As Dreadnautilus is not considered by the game to be a boss nor a powerful enemy, the player is able to set their spawn point by where they were fighting Dreadnautilus if they happen to die, with the ability to skip the respawn timer thus making the Sanguine Staff considerably easier to obtain.
Like the Blade Staff and Terraprisma, the Sanguine Staff's precise movement, tracking, and fixed idle position make it an ideal choice against fast bosses and crowd control.
The Sanguine Staff's high base damage and moderate attack speed pair well with the Firecracker's damage multiplier.


== Trivia ==
Sanguine is an adjective meaning blood red. It is derived from the Latin term sanguis, which means blood.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Removed mana cost (cost 10 mana previously).
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Knockback reduced from 8 to 3.
Fixed a bug where Sanguine Bats could hit a single target more than one time if the player was very close to the target.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Drop chance increased from 1/5 (20%) to 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%).
Attack duration increased from 60 to 66.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.

title: Burning
content:
Burning is a debuff inflicted when the player comes in contact with Hellstone, Hellstone Bricks, Ancient Hellstone Bricks, or Meteorite. The player loses 30 health per second (5 damage displayed every 0.17 seconds) and has their movement speed reduced until they are no longer in contact with the block.
Its damage can be increased by Slime.
Visually, the debuff causes afflicted entities to emit fire particles and a small amount of light.
The debuff can be negated by equipping the Obsidian Skull or its derivatives, by drinking an Obsidian Skin Potion, or by equipping a full set of Molten armor.


== Causes ==


=== From environment ===


=== From enemy ===


== Notes ==
If the player is going at full speed while inflicted by this debuff, they will emit sounds and visual effects as if they are sprinting using Hermes Boots even if the player is not wearing them.


== Trivia ==
The debuff was created for the sole purpose of preventing Hellstone/Meteorite abuse. Before 1.2, these blocks used to directly damage the player when touched and used to grant invincibility frames. Players could voluntarily take direct damage from one of those blocks and use the immunity to avoid higher damage, such as lava or a Hardmode boss.
Prior to 1.3.0.1, all biomes that contained blocks that inflict this debuff had the same music as a Blood Moon.


== History ==

Molten armor set bonus and Superheated Blood (Lava Shark) now grant immunity to burning blocks.
Can now be inflicted by a slime variant carrying Hellstone.
Desktop 1.3.0.2: No longer caused by developer items in Classic Mode.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
No longer caused by developer items when worn in Expert Mode.
Sloping Meteorite, Hellstone, and Hellstone Brick no longer prevents this debuff.

title: Shadow Candle
content:
The Shadow Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light, and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants Shadow Candle debuff to the player.
The Shadow Candle debuff nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns. The debuff is applied to any players holding or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Shadow Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice.
Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Shadow Candle will turn it off. Shadow Candles that are turned off will not activate the Shadow Candle debuff.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
Shadow Candles will also stop the Town Day/Town Night music tracks from playing in their vicinity.
While having the Shadow Candle debuff, standing still and not using items, being near town NPCs, or being in front of safe background walls will not prevent Chaos Elementals and other enemies with such particular conditions from spawning.
Having the Shadow Candle debuff will completely prevent the Skeleton Merchant from spawning.
The evil bars dropped from decrafting the Shadow Candle into Shimmer is dependent on the world evil; it will drop Demonite Bars in Corruption worlds and Crimtane Bars in Crimson worlds.
In Drunk worlds, the two world evils switch every in-game day, meaning the Shadow Candle will alternate between both bars each day.


== Tips ==
At least 4 placed Shadow Candles are needed to completely cover a town.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Now used to craft The Beheaded's Head.
Holding the Shadow Candle will now also remove the requirements to not stand in front of safe background walls and to have moved or used an item in the last 5 seconds when it comes to spawning of enemies with special requirements such as Chaos Elemental, making held and placed Shadow Candles fully functionally identical. Previously held Shadow Candles only removed the requirement for not being near friendly town NPCs.
The debuff icon is now also displayed while holding the Shadow Candle.

title: Day and night cycle
content:
The day and night cycle of the Terraria world refers to the rising and setting of the sun and moon, and the ways this can affect the world.

Day begins at 4:30 AM, while night begins at 7:30 PM.
Day and night each have their respective theme music in some surface biomes.
For the "Morning Rain" track, morning lasts from 4:30 AM to 7:30 AM.
Some surface enemies only spawn at night (see Enemies below).
Some NPCs sell unique items at night, like the Arms Dealer, who sells Illegal Gun Parts at night.
Note that the sun in Terraria rises at the left of the map, even though the left is referred to in-game as "West" (the same for right/East), e.g. when a Goblin Army, Frost Legion, or Pirate Invasion begins approaching.


== Time ==

All newly-created worlds begin at 8:15 AM.
One minute of in-game time lasts one second of real-world time, meaning one hour in-game lasts one minute real-world. Therefore, one full Terraria day lasts 24 real-world minutes (15 during the day, 9 during the night).
In-game time can be displayed with the following:
Any placed Grandfather Clock will display the current hour for all players within about 80 tiles horizontal and about 50 tiles vertical of the clock. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on it displays the exact time in a status message.
On  Desktop,  Console,  Old-gen console, and  Mobile, having a Gold/Platinum Watch, GPS, PDA(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), or Cell Phone(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in the player's inventory displays the exact time (the Tungsten/Silver Watch and Tin/Copper Watch will display time to the nearest in-game half-hour and hour respectively).
Time Hair Dye(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) colors the character's hair dependent on the time, providing a rough estimate.
Using the Enchanted Sundial(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Enchanted Moondial(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), time can be sped up to the next dawn or dusk respectively (i.e. to 4:30 AM or 7:30 PM) once every seven days.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Sleeping in Beds makes time pass at five times the normal rate: 1 in-game hour takes 12 real-world seconds instead of 1 real-world minute. A full day and night takes 288 real-world seconds (4 minutes 48 seconds).
This also works in multiplayer worlds, but requires all players to be in bed.
Sleeping is not possible during events or when bosses are alive.
Time can also be sped up  and frozen  using the power menu in Journey Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Time rate can be altered from 1× to 24× its normal rate (using 24×, an in-game day will last 1 real-world minute).
This effect will stack with a Bed. With just the Bed and Journey Mode, an in-game day can be passed in 12 real-world seconds. The Enchanted Sundial or Moondial negates the Bed and Journey Mode, and works on its own.
Furthermore, it is possible to set time to one of four presets: .


== Enemies ==
At the surface layer, unique enemies spawn at night. Nocturnal enemies will run or fly away when day starts.
Additionally, the Eye of Cthulhu, Skeletron, The Twins, The Destroyer, Skeletron Prime, and Ocram(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) can only be summoned at night, and will flee or become nigh-unkillable at dawn. In contrast, King Slime can only spawn randomly during the day, though it can be summoned with the Slime Crown at any time.
The following enemies only spawn during the night:

Naturally, all enemies exclusive to the Blood Moon also only spawn at night, and all enemies exclusive to the Solar Eclipse only spawn during the day.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
   On the title screen, the sun or moon can be dragged around.
Before formal server software was released for Terraria, and while it was necessary to open a second window of the game to host a server, dragging the sun or moon around would directly change the time of day within the server.
When the sun or moon is in the improper place after being dragged, when the world loads the sun will slowly move towards the proper place instead of instantly snapping there. However, if the moon is present on the title screen instead of the sun or vice versa, the sun/moon will instantly snap to its normal location.
Doing this in the  Desktop version,  Mobile version, and  Nintendo Switch version will cause the title screen music to change from "Journey's End" to the old Title Screen music and changes the Terraria logo to the old logo.
While wearing Sunglasses, the sun appears to be wearing them as well. The sun will also have the old sun texture from before 1.2. Un-equipping the Sunglasses will cause it to revert. This has no functional effect.
Internally, the time counter is increased by 1 each tick, and is reset to zero at both dawn and dusk. During the daytime, the counter is allowed to go up to 54000, and during nighttime, it is only allowed to go up to 32400.
Despite the sun and moon both always having the same relative position to each other, there are still moon phases (there can be a new moon even though the moon is not visible).

title: Solar Flare armor
content:
Solar Flare armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord melee armor set consisting of the Solar Flare Helmet, Solar Flare Breastplate, and Solar Flare Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Solar Fragments.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

+78 defense
+12% damage reduction
+29% melee damage
+26% melee critical strike chance
+15% melee speed
+900 aggro
+15% movement speed
+3 HP/second health regeneration
Grants the Solar Blaze buff, which builds the longer the player avoids taking damage, gaining up to a maximum of three charges. Each charge takes 3 seconds to build. The number of charges built is indicated by a shield that appears in front of the player, with two and three spikes appearing on the shield, corresponding with the charge count.
Taking damage depletes one charge and creates an explosion called Solar Radiance around the player.
While there is at least one charge built, the player can activate a special dash attack by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key. Striking an enemy with the dash damages it and causes a damaging Solar Radiance explosion, so enemies always take damage twice. A Solar Blaze charge is consumed if at least one enemy was hit. The dash has a 1-second cooldown.
Furthermore, the Solar Blaze buff provides +20% damage reduction, regardless of the number of charges. Combined with the base damage reduction from the armor's set bonus, it grants a total of 29.6% damage reduction.
Each piece equipped (even if hidden by vanity items) causes the player to emit light, with a higher light level for each additional piece equipped. Additionally, equipping the full set causes the player to emit pulses and afterimages while moving.


== Set ==


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Solar Radiance explosion deals 150 base melee damage and inflicts a knockback of 15 (Insane). It is affected by melee damage bonuses, including the damage bonus from the Psycho Knife when in stealth. It is not affected by knockback bonuses, cannot critically strike, and does not gain the ability to inflict debuffs granted from flasks, the Magma Stone, and Frost armor.
The Solar Flare armor's dash also deals 150 base melee damage and inflicts a base knockback of 9 (Very strong). It is affected by most melee bonuses.
It can receive the following bonuses:
Melee damage and melee critical strike chance bonuses, including those from the Psycho Knife when in stealth.
Knockback bonuses from the Titan Glove or its upgrades and Titan Potion.
It cannot receive the following bonuses:
The ability to inflict debuffs granted from flasks, the Magma Stone, and Frost armor.
The knockback bonus from the Psycho Knife when in stealth.
The damage dealt by the dash is not subject to the usual ±15% randomization. It will always do the same amount of damage to enemies with the same defense, apart from critical hits.
Taking fall damage also triggers the Solar Radiance explosion discharge and consumes one charge.
The dash causes the player to move at 52 mph.
This dash will cause the player to move 11 mph faster than the Dungeon Guardian and 1 mph faster than the dash of Biome Mimics when the player is too far away.
The dash effect of the armor overrides the dash effect of the Tabi, Master Ninja Gear, and Shield of Cthulhu accessories.
The damage reduction can be combined with similar effects from other items, such as the Endurance Potion. See Damage reduction for details.
The Solar Blaze buff tooltip still displays "Damage taken reduced by 30%", even though the damage reduction effect was changed in 1.4.0.1 to 20%. However, combined with the damage reduction of 12% that was added to the armor's set bonus, the buff does reduce damage by 29.6%.
The shield can also be dyed using the chest dye slot.


== Tips ==
In comparison to Beetle armor, Solar Flare armor provides slightly more defense than Beetle armor with the Beetle Shell. While the damage reduction of Beetle armor is higher, the 12% damage reduction from Solar Flare armor's set bonus stacks with some other buffs. It can almost reach the damage reduction levels of Beetle armor this way: With Endurance, Ice Barrier, and the Worm Scarf, Beetle armor offers at most 73.6% damage reduction, while Solar Flare armor offers 71.2%, which is only 2.4 percentage points less.


== Trivia ==
Solar Flare armor essentially combines the effects of Turtle armor (damage reflection), Beetle armor (damage reduction), and the Shield of Cthulhu (dash).
A solar flare is a sudden increase of brightness on the Sun. More powerful flares are then followed by a coronal mass ejection, which is a significant release of plasma from the Sun's surface.


== See also ==
Vortex armor
Nebula armor
Stardust armor


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Solar Radiance no longer triggers when taking damage from non-enemy hazards.
Clarified the Solar Flare armor tooltip (functionality unchanged).
Desktop 1.4.4: The damage of Solar Radiance explosions is now affected by melee damage bonuses.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Each armor piece now provides 1 HP/s of health regeneration.
Increased the melee critical strike chance bonus of the Solar Flare Helmet from +17% to +26%.
Increased the melee damage bonus of the Solar Flare Breastplate from +22% to +29%.
Instead of 30% damage reduction when charges are active, the armor now has 12% damage reduction at all times, and 20% additional damage reduction while charges are active.
Reduced the recharge time of shield charges from 4 seconds to 3 seconds.
Changed tooltip of the set bonus from "Solar shields generate over time protecting you, \ consume the shield power to dash, damaging enemies" to "Solar shields charge over time to protect you & let you dash \ A charge is used to damage enemies you touch \ Consumed charges explode & damage enemies".
Increased sell value from no value to 31 Gold 50 Silver per set.
Desktop 1.3.0.6: The dash ability now only consumes charges when it hits an enemy, and hit enemies will now additionally produce a Solar Radiance explosion.
Desktop 1.3.0.4: Fixed solar shields being visible even when the player is dead.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Introduced.

title: Guide:Weapon playthroughs
content:
This guide provides weapon recommendations for players limiting themselves to certain weapon types. Aside from the main damage types (melee, ranged, magic, and summon), most weapons can be grouped in subtypes.


== Notes ==
For all intents and purposes, armor and accessory choices are left to the player's discretion. However, each weapon listed here was tested while paired with the gear recommendations from Guide:Class setups. All weapon recommendations can be obtained in their proper stage of progression, which is also established by said guide.
Weapons marked with + are sidearms that supply helpful debuffs or secondary DPS.
Weapons marked in bold are dropped from a boss within its progression tier.
Weapons marked with C are for crowd-control.
Weapons marked with * are miscellaneous weapons that are sometimes regarded by the community as belonging to a category, for instance, the Daybreak being a spear.
Each weapon is ranked by effectiveness; weapons with a slash separating them are counterparts.
For weapons with an "n/a" for Endgame, it simply means there are no options post-Lunatic Cultist.
Certain weapon categories are omitted due to lack of meaningful progression.

title: Guide:Surviving in the Hallow
content:
The Hallow is the thematic opposite to the evil biomes. Despite its whimsical appearance, it is still a dangerous biome to be in, especially in early Hardmode. It can spread just like the evil biomes, and in comparison to them, most Hallow enemies are fast and deal high contact damage.
Traversing the Hallow may be important, as after defeating the Wall of Flesh, two diagonal strips in a "V" formation will infect the world, one Hallow and the other Corruption/Crimson. Gelatin Crystals can be found underground and used to summon Queen Slime, who can be killed to get valuable loot in early Hardmode, such as Crystal Assassin armor and the Gelatinous Pillion. The Underground Hallow can also provide Souls of Light and Crystal Shards.


== Terrain ==
The terrain consists of whatever biome the Hallow is generated over, converted into Hallowed blocks. This makes the difficulty of traversing the Hallow dependent on the natural terrain it generated over.
Hallowed grass is similar to regular grass, in that it will still grow Mushrooms and Dayblooms. Trees grown on Hallowed grass will provide Pearlwood, which despite providing stronger alternatives to normal wooden equipment, is not of much use even in early Hardmode.
The Pearlstone found in the Hallow, especially underground, requires the same amount of pickaxe power as Ebonstone and Crimstone. It is advisable to have at least a Molten Pickaxe or a Hardmode ore pickaxe to mine through it, since it may take a bit longer to mine compared to regular Stone Blocks. Explosives are also helpful for exploration.
Crystal Shards and Gelatin Crystals will quickly start growing on Pearlstone underground, the latter of which will spawn Queen Slime when used in the Hallow. Unlike the Eater of Worlds and Brain of Cthulhu, she will not despawn if the player exits the Hallow, so she can safely be brought to a more open arena.
If you want to fight Queen Slime, consider checking out Guide:Queen Slime strategies for more information on that fight.


== Recommended gear ==
It is recommended to have at least 400 health, 200 mana and the best gear available in pre-Hardmode.

Melee users should at least have Molten armor.
For rangers, Necro armor gives the biggest ranged damage bonuses.
Mages have a choice between Jungle armor and Meteor armor. If you have a Gray Zapinator, it should preferably be used with the latter.
Summoners can use Bee armor if they want an extra minion slot, or Obsidian armor if they wish to focus on using whips.
Spider armor can quickly be obtained at the beginning of Hardmode.


=== Weapons ===


===== For Melee users =====
The Night's Edge is a strong option for dealing with Hallow enemies.
Alternatively, the Breaker Blade deals more damage and knockback, but has less range.
An Amarok can be easily obtained early on, has good range and inflicts the Frostbite debuff. A Hel-Fire is another, slightly weaker option that is acquired similarly.
The Dark Lance and Sunfury are effective weapons that can handle enemies at close range.


===== For Rangers =====
The Phoenix Blaster or Clockwork Assault Rifle are effective guns that are easy to aim with.
A Shotgun can also be used, but deals less damage at longer distances.
The Molten Fury is a useful bow, and can be replaced with any Hardmode ore repeater later.
The Toxikarp must be fished up in the Corruption, but does not use ammunition, has decent range and inflicts the Poisoned debuff.


===== For Mages =====
For single target damage, the Flamelash or Flower of Fire are great options.
The Laser Rifle or Demon Scythe are useful for crowd control.


===== For Summoners =====
The Spider Staff can quickly be obtained early on, and is the most reliable minion available. They also inflict the Acid Venom debuff.
Alternatively, Abigail's Flower gains a damage buff in Hardmode, but should be used with the Firecracker.
The Spinal Tap and Firecracker are the best whips the player can obtain.
The Queen Spider Staff is the only sentry that becomes available in early Hardmode, and inflicts the Acid Venom debuff.
If you have not obtained it yet, but have defeated the Tier 1 Old One's Army, the Ballista Rod can also be used.


=== Accessories ===
Any Emblem dropped by the Wall of Flesh (Warrior, Ranger, Sorcerer, Summoner) should be used.
Lightning Boots or its upgrades, or Amphibian Boots are very useful for mobility.
Wings are always useful to have in Hardmode. If you do not have any yet, a Horseshoe balloon can be used instead.
If you are playing on Expert Mode or higher difficulties, the Worm Scarf will reduce any damage taken. Alternatively, the Brain of Confusion can prevent damage altogether, but has a cooldown.
Melee users and summoners will benefit from having the Power Glove.
The Magic Quiver is useful for rangers focusing on bows or repeaters, but is a rare drop from Skeleton Archers.
Celestial Cuffs can be used by mages to quickly recover mana. Alternatively, if you do not mind the Mana Sickness debuff, the Mana Flower can be used.
Summoners should use the Pygmy Necklace for an extra minion slot.


== Other tips ==
Unlike the Corruption or Crimson, town NPCs can live in the Hallow without leaving. In fact, it is a good idea to have your base Hallowed, as this will stop the evil biomes from spreading towards it.
NPCs that are happy enough will also sell Hallow Pylons, which are useful for fast travel.
The Hallow cannot spread through Mud Blocks, and as such there is no Hallowed Jungle grass, possibly making it more difficult to farm surface Hallow enemies. If the Hallow strip of the Hardmode "V" formation happens to hit the Jungle, it may be necessary to buy Hallowed Seeds from the Dryad in order to spread the Hallow somewhere else.
The Crystal Serpent is a great weapon that can easily be obtained at the beginning of Hardmode. It can very rarely be fished up in the Hallow in any layer.


== Surface Hallow ==
None of the surface Hallow enemies can fly, so a good strategy for dealing with them is to attack them from a distance, using Rope and Platforms to locate to a spot that they cannot reach. Some additional measures, such as boxing yourself in, may need to be taken at night due to Gastropods, however.

Pixies can occasionally inflict the Silenced and Slow debuffs upon contact. Despite appearing to fly, they actually only hover through terrain. While they aren't too big of a threat on their own, multiple of them can end up overwhelming the player, especially at night.
Unicorns are very fast, along with having high health and knockback resistance. They can easily catch an unprepared player off guard, but can only jump up to a height of 7 blocks. A long-range weapon like a gun or yoyo can be used to easily kill them.
Gastropods spawn during the night. They are slow, but common with high health and defense, and can also shoot high-velocity lasers to hit you from afar. While they are the most threatening of the surface Hallow enemies, their laser attack gets canceled out when hit, meaning a fast weapon that attacks continuously can be used to immobilize them.
Alternatively, Gastropods are considered slimes, so the Expert Mode-exclusive Royal Gel will make them completely harmless.
All three surface Hallow enemies have one guaranteed drop along with a few rare drops. Pixies drop Pixie Dust, and rarely drop the Fast Clock and Megaphone. Unicorns drop Unicorn Horns and rarely the valuable Blessed Apple, while Gastropods drop Gel and rarely Chocolate Chip Cookies.
Consider using bombs to collect large amounts of Pearlstone. Pearlstone can be used to make an artificial Hallow biome or farm Hallow enemies later on.
Once Plantera has been defeated, Prismatic Lacewings start appearing at night, and disappear during the day. These are harmless critters, but players should be careful when approaching them, as killing a Lacewing will summon the Empress of Light. She is a difficult boss that will likely require post-Golem gear, but will drop valuable loot when killed, such as powerful weapons and Empress Wings. She can be seen as a timed boss fight, however, as she will enrage during the day, causing her attacks to instantly kill you.
Just like most other critters, the Prismatic Lacewing can be caught with a Bug Net for future use. Players can also keep a Guide to Critter Companionship in their inventory for an easier time catching Lacewings, or if you simply do not want to fight the Empress of Light yet.
For a specific guide on the Empress of Light herself, consider checking out Guide:Empress of Light strategies for more information on that fight.


== Underground Hallow ==
Most of the value in the Hallow lies in the cavern layer, within the Hallowed portion of the Hardmode V spread. Each enemy here has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping a Soul of Light, a valuable crafting material.
If the player is willing to take a bit more time, an enemy farm will provide a safe and efficient way of getting the valuable enemy drops from the Underground Hallow.
There are many new enemies for you to deal with: The Illuminant Bat, Chaos Elemental, Illuminant Slime, Enchanted Sword and very rarely the Hallowed Mimic.

Illuminant Bats are comparable to Giant Bats: They have higher stats, but in return do not inflict the Confused debuff (or Feral Bite in Expert Mode). Similarly, any long-ranged weapon will work on the Illuminant Bat, such as boomerangs or bows.
Chaos Elementals are fast and unpredictable, occasionally teleporting if they can't reach the player. It is recommended to carve a more open area to make them easier to deal with. They are notable as they very rarely drop the Rod of Discord, a powerful tool.
Illuminant Slimes act just like a regular slime. Due to the limited mobility of slimes, they are generally less dangerous than other enemies.
Enchanted Swords are an uncommon enemy that can move through blocks and can inflict Cursed on hit. This makes them potentially the most dangerous enemy to be hit by, but due to low knockback resistance and tendency to stop moving when hit, you can knock them away with any weapon that can attack through blocks, such as whips or the Night's Edge. They are very easy to spot.
Hallowed Mimics are the Biome Mimic of the Hallow. They are passive until damaged by the player, but have immense health, damage, and the ability to move through blocks. Their loot is very valuable, and there are a number of ways to defeat them, such as with decent open space, but depending on the situation you likely want to leave them alone. You can craft Keys of Light later to summon them manually in a more open area.
Alongside these enemies, pink Pigrons start spawning in hallowed Ice biomes, while four new enemies can appear in a hallowed Desert: Light Mummies on the surface, along with Light Lamias and Dreamer Ghouls underground. Crystal Threshers can appear on the surface during a Sandstorm.

Pigrons can become nearly invisible and appear when they are about to attack you, but make audible growls as they approach. Any weapon that can attack through blocks can be used to kill them. Pigrons may drop valuable Bacon.
Light Mummies will start running faster once reduced to 50% health or lower, but otherwise behave similarly to Zombies. They can drop Light Shards, which can be used to craft the Dao of Pow or the Sky Fracture.
Light Lamias aggressively chase you, attempting to deal contact damage. It is best to carve out a larger area in the Underground Desert, preferably in pre-Hardmode, so that they are less likely to reach you.
Dreamer Ghouls will inflict the Confused debuff upon contact, making them a bit more threatening in close quarters. Any long-range weapon can be used to kill them. They may drop Light Shards.
Crystal Threshers "swim" inside sand blocks and jump out to deal contact damage, although they cannot swim through any other blocks. You can take advantage of this by baiting them into jumping out of the sand and into non-sand blocks where they become more vulnerable to attack. The best way to deal with them, however, is to place platforms above a height that they cannot reach, and attack from above with any weapon that shoots projectiles. They can only jump up to a height of 16 blocks for reference. Crystal Threshers can drop Light Shards and Shark Fins.
