title: Guide:Vanity
content:
While Terraria has a variety of good-looking armor sets, as with many other sandbox games, there are many players who may wish to customize their appearance with their own personal flair. As vanity is inherently a means of creative expression, this guide will not serve as a compilation of completed outfits. Rather, it will guide you through how dyes and social slots work, and equip you with the knowledge you need to create your own unique look.


== Practical use ==

For those unconcerned with their character's appearance, social slots represent an additional form of storage space for armor and accessories. Extra accessories that you don't wish to equip can be moved into social accessory slots, to be removed later when managing inventory back at your base. 
Informational accessories, such as the Metal Detector, will still work when equipped to a social slot; however, their modifiers wont take effect.
On the  Desktop version, right-clicking a piece of equipment in the inventory (or Piggy Bank) will automatically equip it to an applicable slot. This is a handy way to carry and switch between multiple armor sets, but it is not nearly as convenient for accessories. This is because accessories are equipped in descending order from top to bottom, and this order is not reset upon closing the inventory. Instead, if there are two accessories that you often swap with each other, it is recommended to pair them to an accessory slot and its corresponding social slot for quick swapping, by right-clicking the social slot. Double-tapping substitutes for right-clicking on the  Mobile version.
To the right is an example accessory loadout that utilizes social slot swapping. The top three accessory slots can be swapped to trade damage (Avenger Emblem/Celestial Stone/Destroyer Emblem) for survivability (Worm Scarf/Frozen Turtle Shell/Cross Necklace), and the bottom slot allows a quick switch between class-specific accessories. The two empty social accessory slots can be saved for vanity or for accessory storage.
On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, the effect of a Philosopher's Stone is only applied the instant a Healing Potion is drunk; this means that it can be kept in a social slot until healing is needed.  If upgraded to a Charm of Myths, the regeneration will only be available when it is equipped.


== Character ==
On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, the player's character style can be changed using a Dresser. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, the player's eye and skin color can also be changed.


=== Hairstyles ===
Aside from the hairstyles that can be chosen during character creation, there are a number of unique hairstyles that can only be obtained from the Stylist. Most of the more elegant female hairstyles are purchased from the Stylist, and she also offers a variety of wacky hairstyles for male characters.
The Stylist can also change the player's hair color for an additional fee.


== Dyes ==
Dyes are applied to all patches of color on the affected equipment, which may cause undesired effects on certain pieces like Nurse Pants (on which the skin will be dyed as well). As a rule of thumb, the deeper the colors on a piece of visible equipment, the more strongly it will be affected by dyes. Unsaturated colors like black and silver are often unaffected by basic dyes, and require Bright Dye to undergo a color change.
Compound Dyes can also be used for a color combination containing either black or silver, but their effects on any particular equipment piece can only be determined through trial and error.


=== Obtaining dyes ===
Dye materials can usually be obtained from naturally-occurring plants or from specific enemies. Dyes are crafted from materials at a Dye Vat, or received directly from the Dye Trader upon trading in a Strange Plant. See Dyes.


== Vanity accessories ==
Aside from accessories that exist purely for vanity, many functional accessories can also be used to modify a character's appearance. Only one accessory from each of the below categories can be visible at a time.
If multiple accessories from one of these categories are equipped, only the accessory from the lowest slot will be shown.

The Master Ninja Gear is visible as a combination of the Black Belt, Tabi, Shoe Spikes, and Climbing Claws. To completely hide the Master Ninja Gear in a social slot, the feet, waist, and arms must be separately overridden by other accessories.
Leinfors' Luxury Shampoo(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Yoraiz0r's Scowl(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) do not interfere with other visible accessories.


== Specific tips ==
If using the Neptune's Shell or Moon Charm as vanity accessories, it is essentially required to use the same dye for all of your armor slots, as the head, torso, and legs of the werewolf/merfolk are separately affected by dyes.
While the Obsidian Rose and Nature's Gift can be used as hairpins, the Jungle Rose(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) and Seashell Hairpin are head slot items that can be used to similar effect.
Ice Skates make for an excellent pair of boots, and can be dyed a combination of black/silver and a different color. The Tabi also works as a pure black pair of boots.
On female characters, any leg-modifying accessory can help offset the female sprite's narrow legs.
Santa Pants can be used as a pair of boots without requiring an accessory slot, but the boots will be white unless using a compound dye with silver (which colors the upper leg gray).
The Hand Warmer can be used as a pair of elbow-length gloves that aren't as bulky as the Titan Glove and variants, or dyed Bright Orange to approximate the color of pale skin, leaving a white-colored sleeve. The Yoyo Glove can be worn as a pair of black gloves that simply cover the hand.
Unlike the Nurse Pants, Mrs. Claus Heels will not display dyes on the leg region. To dye the skirt on Mrs. Claus Heels a different color, combine the desired color with silver to create a compound dye.
The Djinn's Curse, Mermaid Tail, Lamia Tail, Silly Sunflower Bottoms, and Moon Lord Legs(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) significantly modify the wearer's leg shape.

title: Giant Glowing Mushroom
content:
Giant Glowing Mushrooms are similar to trees, but grow randomly in Glowing Mushroom biomes when enough space exists. They can be chopped down with an axe, which yields Glowing Mushrooms and, less often, Mushroom Grass Seeds. Giant Glowing Mushrooms also give off light, similar to Mushroom grass and Glowing Mushrooms.
Giant Glowing Mushrooms grown in surface and underground biomes each have distinct graphics: Underground versions grow with plain, straight stalks, while Surface versions can display more complex branch formations.
They have similar requirements as trees:

If there is a ceiling, it must be at least 16 tiles above the floor.
There must be no wall right on top of the floor for them to spawn, but there can be wall behind the floor and from 1 tile above it.
They will grow only when there is a flat patch of 5 blocks.
They will grow at least 2 tiles from each other.


== Notes ==
When using a Clentaminator to spread the Jungle, the Giant Glowing Mushrooms will be converted into Mahogany trees, while spreading the Glowing Mushroom biome will break the Jungle trees.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Painting Giant Glowing Mushrooms, Glowing Mushroom plants (including Mushroom vine and cattail), and Mushroom grass will change the color of the light emitted from them.


== Trivia ==
Although in changelogs these have been referred to as Giant glowing mushrooms, or simply Giant mushrooms, in the source code they are referred to as Mushroom Trees.
On the in-game minimap, they are simply labeled as trees.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Can now glow different colors when painted.
Desktop 1.2: No longer need to be grown underground; the surface variant can now grow on the Surface level.
Desktop 1.0.5: Giant Glowing Mushrooms will now grow back over time. They now grow dynamically on Mushroom Grass, instead of only spawning during world generation.
Desktop-Release: Introduced.

Console 1.4.4: Can now glow different colors when painted.
Console 1.02: No longer need to be grown underground; the surface variant can now grow on the Surface level.
Console-Release: Introduced with generation mechanics from Desktop 1.0.5.

Switch 1.4.4: Can now glow different colors when painted.
Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced with generation mechanics from Desktop 1.2.

Mobile 1.4.4: Can now glow different colors when painted.
Mobile 1.2.6508: No longer need to be grown underground; the surface variant can now grow on the Surface level.
Mobile-Release: Introduced with generation mechanics from Desktop 1.0.5.

3DS-Release: Introduced with generation mechanics from Desktop 1.2.

title: Chasms
content:
Chasms are deep tunnels found in The Corruption or The Crimson. They generally begin at surface openings, and are lined with a thick layer of Ebonstone/Crimstone, respectively. They tend to reach depths around where the Cavern layers begin. Large clusters of Corruption/Crimson enemies tend to spawn and collect in these cavities.


== Corruption Chasm ==

A Chasm in the Corruption is a long vertical pit beginning at the surface, dropping straight down into a dark abyss. The walls are made of Ebonstone, with Ebonstone Wall backgrounds. An intersecting horizontal tunnel generally connects Chasms near their bottoms, and contains several Demon Altars. Shadow Orbs tend to appear below Chasm floors, buried some distance beneath. They are usually enclosed in Ebonstone, rendering them inaccessible without mid-tier tools or explosives, such as dynamite or bombs.


== Crimson Chasm ==

A Crimson Chasm is lined with Crimstone, and begins at a more slanted entrance, rather than a vertical pit. Crimson chasms are less linear, and can branch or zigzag. They tend to lead to large chambers that appear to have the shape of hands, and branch out into veins, each of which lead to Crimson Hearts; These are usually enclosed in Crimstone, rendering them inaccessible without mid-tier tools or some form of Explosives capable of destroying tiles. Crimson Altars can be found concentrated at a single layer on the descent into the chasm.


== Tips ==


=== Corruption ===
Players without the ability to mine Ebonstone and who have not yet obtained a climbing aid like Grappling Hooks will want to avoid falling into chasms. Some chasms can be very difficult or impossible to climb out of by merely jumping between ledges.
Beginning players may want to cover corruption chasm entrances with Blocks or Platforms to avoid inadvertently falling in when traversing the surface.
Running Platforms across the shaft at intervals can help, as can running Ropes down the length of the shaft.
Using Purification Powder on the Ebonstone will turn it into Stone, which can be mined with any Pickaxe. This is useful for getting to the Shadow Orbs without access to explosives.


=== Crimson ===
As Crimson chasms tend to be slanted rather than vertical, they are usually easier than Corruption chasms for beginning players to navigate without climbing aids. It is still possible, though less likely, to suffer fatal fall damage or become trapped in Crimson chasms until they die or save and exit the world if no such tools, such as ropes or platforms, are available.
Chambers containing Crimson Hearts are frequently flooded with water. In such cases the player may need a water-breathing item, such as Gills Potion and/or Flipper Potion, to reach them safely.
Similar to the corruption counterpart, Crimstone can be returned to the purified state with Purification Powder, allowing access to the Crimson Hearts.

title: The Black Spot
content:
The Black Spot is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that spawns a rideable Pirate Ship Mount which can fly infinitely and can charge through and damage enemies. The Black Spot has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Flying Dutchman in Master Mode.
The Pirate Ship Mount has a maximum horizontal flight speed of 36 mph, a diagonal speed of 54 mph, and a vertical speed of 41 mph. It moves slightly slower (30 mph) while in water. Upon achieving a horizontal speed of 27 mph, a ring of gold particles appears around the player and trails behind the mount, indicating that the Pirate Ship Mount begins dealing 100 base summon damage and a knockback of 12 (Insane) upon ramming enemies, which also grants the player 0.1 seconds worth of invincibility frames.


== Notes ==
The Pirate Ship Mount increases the player's height to 4.125 tiles.
The Pirate Ship Mount applies 30 ticks of global invincibility frames upon hitting enemies.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Obtaining The Black Spot prior to defeating a mechanical boss is a challenging (given the difficulty of the Master Mode, early-Hardmode Pirate Invasion) but rewarding task. See Pirate Invasion § Tips and Guide:Pirate Invasion strategies for tips.
It is advisable to remove mobility accessories when using the mount, as they will not boost its movement.
Although the Pirate Ship Mount has decent speed, its acceleration, turning, and stopping rates are relatively slow, making it less agile than other flying mounts. The acceleration also makes its ramming capabilities difficult to use. Other mounts, such as the Witch's Broom or UFO Mount (both have an acceleration of 49 mph/second, compared to the Pirate Ship Mount's 37 mph/second), may be more suited e.g. for dodging incoming attacks.


== Trivia ==
The item is a reference to the 1883 adventure novel Treasure Island by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson, where pieces of paper marked with a black spot signify that the person receiving it will be deposed of leadership or executed.
The buff tooltip may be a nod to the 2013 American biographical action-thriller film  Captain Phillips, where the pirate Abduwali Muse says "Look at me. I'm the captain now." after taking the crew hostage. The phrase is now commonly used as an internet meme.
Prior to the 1.4.1 update, the Pirate Ship Mount had an extraordinary speed of 81 mph (91 mph diagonally, and no decrease in water). Therefore, it was often considered to be among the best mounts in the game, despite being obtainable before any of the mechanical bosses had been defeated.

title: Sunflower
content:
The Sunflower is a plant-like furniture item which inhibits biome spread and graveyards, and which grants the Happy! buff to players in their vicinity, increasing their movement speed and reducing enemy spawns.
Sunflowers are placed on normal grass during world generation. They do not have growth stages like most plants, nor do they grow naturally or from seeds. They can be mined with a pickaxe or drill, and they can be purchased from the Dryad for 50 Silver each, unless a Blood Moon is occurring.
Sunflowers can only be placed on regular, Hallowed, Jungle, or Ash grass, at any height. They cannot be placed on bare Dirt Blocks; nor Corrupt, Crimson, or Mushroom grass; nor in Clay Pots or Planter Boxes; nor in liquids.


== Effects ==
A placed Sunflower has the following effects:

The two tiles directly underneath a Sunflower cannot become Corrupted, Crimsoned, or Hallowed, even in Hardmode. In some cases, this can prevent Corrupted and Crimson grass from spreading sideways. It also blocks other conversions in a small area around it—see Biome spread § Sunflowers for details.
Each Sunflower decreases an area's evil biome tile count by 80 tiles. Furthermore, when determining whether NPCs will reject a house, each Sunflower in the area decreases the evil score by 40 points. For the exact size of each area, see Biomes § Biome existence requirements and House respectively.
Each Sunflower decreases Tombstone count by 1, helping prevent the formation of a Graveyard biome.
It provides the Happy! buff to players within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Sunflower, which grants:
+10% movement speed
×1.1 movement speed multiplier to itself and all movement speed buffs to the left of it in the buff list (effectively making the buff grant +21% movement speed)
17% reduced spawn rates
20% reduced spawn limit


== Notes ==
It does not provide the Happy! buff if there are 5 or more Tombstones in the same area.
The Happy! and Peace Candle buff's spawn reduction effects stack with each other.
The Happy! buff stacks with Asphalt Block's movement speed multiplier.
The Sunflower emits faint light but does not count as a valid light source for housing. The petals of the Sunflower are fully bright in the dark.
On  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, liquids break Sunflowers.


== Tips ==
If placed in large quantities, Sunflowers can allow NPCs to live near evil biomes.
When a new evil biome is generated at the start of Hardmode, it may spawn over existing NPC houses and/or Pylons, making the housing invalid. Placing enough sunflowers will remedy this issue until the player is able to obtain a Clentaminator.
The Happy! buff reduces all spawns, including critters, which may be undesirable when farming critters and bait.


== Trivia ==

In the release trailer for 1.3, a variant of sunflower was shown with a golden interior as opposed to the regular sunflower (some are seen in the beginning of the trailer). It never ended up in the final update and its effects are unknown.
Sunflowers' ability to resist Corruption and Crimson may be a reference to their real-world reputation for cleaning up nuclear radiation.
A sunflower is used as the loading icon on the  Desktop,  Console,  Mobile, and  Switch versions.

title: Flask of Gold
content:
The Flask of Gold is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips to inflict the Midas debuff for 2 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Gold cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Weapons and projectiles affected by the flask will emit glowing golden sparks.


== Tips ==
The Flask of Gold also makes pickaxes and melee weapons provide light, making it a sidegrade to the Shine Potion, since it also improves money drops but requires constant use of weapons or tools.
The Lucky Coin and its upgrades operate independently, and can make hunting and events even more profitable.
The total cost of buying the Gold Dust is 85 Silver. So, even with the Midas debuff's lowest benefit possible (10%), the player will get a return on investment after earning just 8 Gold 50 Silver. Killing a Mimic, the Queen Bee, or any Hardmode boss will do, but mass-killing pre-Hardmode bosses may be very profitable, and the Solar Eclipse or Slime Rain are ideal.
Note that in Expert Mode and above bosses drop their money inside Treasure Bags, which are not affected by Midas.

Golden Bullet

title: Saddles
content:
The Dusty Rawhide Saddle, Royal Gilded Saddle, and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount, Majestic Horse Mount, and Dark Horse Mount respectively, which can charge through and damage enemies.
All three horse mounts are functionally identical and are sold by the Zoologist for 25 Gold each after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary.


== Types ==


== Notes ==
The horses' top running speed is 46 mph, reachable in 3.2 seconds.
When surpassing 38 mph, they will start dealing damage to enemies and critters they run into, similarly to the Unicorn and Goat Mounts. They will deal 30 base summon damage and inflict a knockback of 7 (Strong).
When using a saddle, the respective horse mount will appear in a puff of gray smoke.
They reduce fall damage by half.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
A horse mount is best used on a large platform without obstacles, extending across the map. This facilitates maintaining maximum speed without having to worry about slowing down.

title: Torch God's Favor
content:
Torch God's Favor is a permanent booster item that permanently grants the player the ability to automatically convert regular Torches and Campfires in the player's hand to the current biome's torch or campfire variant, which increases the player's torch luck in most areas. The Torch God's Favor can only be obtained by surviving The Torch God event if at least 95 Torches were fired during the event.
Torch God's Favor is a one-time consumable whose effect cannot stack (similar to the Advanced Combat Techniques or the Demon Heart). When first used, the ability is switched on by default and can then be toggled off and on via a toggle appearing  to the left of the inventory /  in the tools menu below the inventory.
Torches and campfires placed with the ability toggled on will permanently remain converted to the biome variant they were placed as, even if freed and picked up.


== Biome Torches and Campfires ==
Below is a list of biome Torches and their respective biomes in order of priority, where items appearing earlier in the list take precedence over items appearing later in the list.

Below is a list of biome Campfires and their respective biomes in order of priority. Note how they differ in order to their biome Torches.


== Notes ==
Bone Torches, Demon Torches and Aether Torches will be swapped in when Torches are placed in the Dungeon, The Underworld and The Aether respectively, despite not affecting Torch Luck in those areas.
Ice Torches take precedence over Jungle Torches and Mushroom Torches even though the Jungle and Glowing Mushroom biomes both take precedence over the Snow biome for most other purposes like fishing and enemy spawning.
Coral Torches will not be swapped in while in the Ocean, despite being a biome-specific Torch.
Players who have already used a Torch God's Favor, or have one in their inventory, will not be able to initiate The Torch God event.
The inventory's trash slot is not considered part of the inventory for The Torch God event, so having a Torch God's Favor there will not prevent the event from initiating.
Consuming the Torch God's Favor unlocks the Bestiary entry of the Torch God. It also makes the crafting recipes for the Torch God's Flavor and Music Box (Torch God) available.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Converting torches while in the Dungeon is an easy way to obtain Bone Torches, which, while cosmetic in the Dungeon itself, are the only means of boosting torch luck in the pure biomes and the Underworld.
A profit of 10 Copper per Torch bought from the Merchant (at base happiness) can be made by converting regular Torches to Demon Torches in the Underworld, then picking up and selling them. However, a player who has progressed to the point that they are comfortable enough in the Underworld to spend time on this has much more profitable options; see Guide:Making money.
Any Wood and regular Torches can be converted to Glowing Mushrooms and Mushroom Torches by converting Campfires to Glowing Mushroom Campfires and decrafting the latter with Shimmer. However, this requires a Glowing Mushroom biome, where Glowing Mushrooms grow in abundance and can be harvested directly.


== Trivia ==
The Torch God's Favor emits a small amount of light when dropped. It is also fully bright in the dark when dropped or placed inside an Item Frame or an Item Flask.

title: Suffocation
content:
Suffocation is a debuff that is inflicted as long as the player's hitbox intersects with any Sand Blocks, Silt Blocks, and Slush Blocks. It causes the player to lose 20 health per second (5 damage displayed every 0.25 seconds).


== Causes ==


=== From environment ===
These inflict Suffocation for as long as they intersect with the player.


=== Self-induced ===


== Notes ==
Suffocation will be caused only be the blocks listed above, and not by any other blocks the player may get clipped inside of. For example, Obsidian forming over the player or being hoiked into other blocks will not cause Suffocation damage.
Additionally, other things that "suffocate" the player (e.g. drowning) also do not inflict this debuff.


== Trivia ==
The Suffocation debuff icon features a blue face, which is a common symptom of asphyxiation.
It also shows two open palms crossed over the throat, which is the universal sign of choking.
Dying from suffocation will display one of the following unique death messages:
“<Player name> couldn't breathe.”
“<Player name> was buried alive.”

title: Bone Javelin
content:
The Bone Javelin is a consumable ranged weapon crafted from Sturdy Fossils. Upon hitting an enemy, it will stick to the enemy and inflict the Penetrated debuff for 15 seconds, dealing 3 damage per second (3 damage displayed every 1 second). Up to six Bone Javelins can be stuck onto an enemy, dealing a total of 18 damage per second (18 damage displayed every 1 second).


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Even though the base damage can be amplified with armor, accessories, and buffs, the continuous damage of one Bone Javelin will still be 3 damage per second.
Bone Javelins appear to have a strange effect on Granite Golems. When the Granite Golem turns invincible by crossing its arms, all Bone Javelins will immediately disappear, but 1 damage will be dealt multiple times to the Granite Golem when the invincibility wears off. This is probably due to the damage over time being inflicted by having negative health regeneration, while the Granite Golem does not reset its regeneration stat immediately when turning invincible.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Tips ==
The Bone Javelin is a great supporting weapon in pre-Hardmode boss fights, even after obtaining better weapons. Since 6 stacks are the maximum for the Penetrated debuff, landing 6 shots and changing to the main weapon with higher DPS will maximize the damage output.


== Trivia ==
The Penetrated debuff can never be applied to players, so it lacks a unique debuff icon. It uses the Distorted debuff's icon as placeholder.
Bone Javelins act similar to a Daybreak which both stick to an enemy and inflict a stacking damage debuff.

title: Snow biome
content:
The Snow biome, also known as the Tundra, is a Surface biome that takes on an arctic appearance with its constant snowfall, its ground made of Snow and Ice Blocks, and its Boreal trees. It can be of moderate difficulty in the early game, becoming relatively easy with some basic equipment. The biome is always found in the direction of the Dungeon, opposite the Underground Desert and Jungle. It extends Underground and transitions to the Ice biome in the Cavern layer.
Specific features of the Snow biome include a different water color and a snowscape background. Boreal Trees and Shiverthorn frequently grow in the snow. Penguins wander the surface, and typical enemies include Ice Slimes, Frozen Zombies, and Demon Eyes. When the player touches water or Shimmer in the Snow biome in Expert or Master Mode, it inflicts the player with the Chilled debuff until 5 seconds after they leave the liquid. During rain, the biome undergoes a Blizzard, decreasing visibility.
The trees in the biome can appear to be pines, snowy evergreens, or leafless trees, but they always yield Boreal Wood when cut down. Acorns placed on Snow Blocks always grow into Boreal Trees.
A Snow biome is made of at least 1500 Snow or Ice Blocks nearby, causing the water color and the background to change, but Snow plants and enemies can spawn on even a single block of Snow or Ice.
The Corruption, Crimson, and Hallow can spread to this biome through its Ice Blocks, either upon world generation or via improved biome spread in Hardmode.
During a Blood Moon, Penguins become Corrupt or Vicious.
In Hardmode, the Snow biome gets a bit of a boost. Ice Elementals and Wolves begin to spawn at night, and Blizzards can spawn the rare Ice Golem, a recurring lumbering giant with a frost beam attack that chills and even freezes players. Also, any enemy killed in the Snow biome in Hardmode has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of dropping the Amarok, a powerful yoyo that inflicts the Frostbite debuff on enemies.
The Dungeon holds a single Ice Chest, which is unlocked with a Frozen Key, obtainable from the Snow biome during Hardmode, but is only usable after Plantera is defeated. Enemies killed in the Snow biome have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping the Frozen Key. The Ice Chest holds the Staff of the Frost Hydra, a sentry summon weapon.
Fishing in the Snow biome has a chance of yielding Atlantic Cod, Frost Daggerfish, and Frost Minnow. Atlantic Cod is used to craft Cooked Fish and Frost Minnow is used to craft Warmth Potions. Frost Daggerfish are consumable ranged weapons and can be useful at the beginning of the game. Frozen Crates and Boreal Crates can also be caught in the Snow biome in pre-Hardmode and Hardmode, respectively, and always include one unique item from Frozen Chests (alongside other loot).


== Contents ==


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
If the player has consumed the Torch God's Favor, they can toggle Biome torch swap to place Ice Torches instead of regular Torches if they try to place regular Torches when in the Snow biome.
Player-created Snow biomes are possible by placing more than 1500 Snow Blocks and/or Ice Blocks in an area.
Water does not turn into Ice Blocks in a Snow biome. Ice Blocks are generated only on world creation.
Snow biomes are somewhat resistant to surface Hallow and Corruption/Crimson spread, since Snow Blocks cannot be transformed. However, Ice Blocks are affected and will be transformed into Pink Ice Blocks (Hallow), Purple Ice Blocks (Corruption) and Red Ice Blocks (Crimson), which mostly affects the Ice biome.
Grass will not grow on Dirt Blocks in a Snow biome.
From surface to underground, the Snow biome initially generates in a trapezoidal shape, before it is overridden by other possible features, like deserts.
The Snow biome will always be located on the opposite side of the world as the Underground Desert and the Jungle. Both the Snow biome and Jungle can generate near or at spawn.


== Trivia ==

The Angler calls the Snow biome Tundra.
This may just be an example of the Angler's usual childish tendencies.
It is only partly accurate to classify the Snow biome as a tundra in the physical-geographical sense. Arctic tundra is typically characterized by a very cold climate and permanently frozen soil, supporting only certain kinds of low-growing vegetation. Scattered trees grow in some tundra regions, but due to the frigid temperatures and permafrost they are not as plentiful as in Terraria's Snow biome. Nonetheless, the Snow biome presents a harsh, cold environment that could be likened to a tundra.
The name Boreal Wood implies it originates in the north, meaning the aurora which can be seen in the background at night is likely the aurora borealis. On Earth, the aurora is visible between 60° and 75° North in latitude.

=== Backgrounds ===

		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		


== History ==

Added new backgrounds and updated the graphics of some pre-existing ones.
Added alternative music track, Snow (Otherworldly).
Biome now requires 1500 blocks, increased from 300.

Now generates farther away from Spawn.
Shaking Boreal trees in the Snow biome has a chance to drop either Acorns, Boreal Wood, a Cherry, some coins, or a Plum.
Snow Pylons will now be sold by any happy NPC in the Snow biome for 7 Gold 50 Silver to 8 Gold 50 Silver. While any number of pylons can be placed in a Snow biome, only one Snow Pylon can be functionally used per world.
The Cyborg, Mechanic, Santa Claus, and Tax Collector NPCs now like living in the Snow biome, while the Arms Dealer, Nurse, Stylist, and Tavernkeep dislike it.

Any enemy killed in the Snow biome in Hardmode now has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of dropping the Amarok yoyo.
Enemies now, once again, drop Frozen Keys instead of Frozen Key Molds. However, the Frozen Chest in the Dungeon cannot be unlocked until Plantera is defeated.
If the player falls into water in the Snow biome in Expert Mode, they are affected with the Chilled debuff when in the water and for five seconds after getting out.

Two Angler quest fish can now be caught in the Snow biome (only when the Angler asks for them), including the Pengfish and Tundra Trout.

Desktop 1.2.1: Enemies within the Snow biome no longer drop Frozen Keys. Instead, they now drop Frozen Key Molds which can be crafted into Frozen Keys.
Desktop 1.2.0.3.1: Fixed random crashing when in a snow biome in multiplayer.

Now generates in all worlds (instead of 1/3 of worlds not generated during the Christmas season, and all worlds generated during the Christmas season).

Can now be infected by the Corruption/Crimson and Hallow (creating Purple, Red, and Pink Ice Blocks).

Unique enemies added, including the Corrupt Penguin, Ice Elemental, Ice Golem, Ice Slime, Wolf, and Zombie Eskimo, along with the new Penguin critter.

title: Friendly Boulder
content:
The Friendly Boulder is a pet-summoning item that spawns a harmless Friendly Boulder that rolls around to follow the player. When the player is flying or far enough away, the Friendly Boulder will roll through the air toward the player. The Friendly Boulder can be obtained as a rare drop from naturally generated Boulders.


== Crafting ==


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Notes ==
During world generation, a small number of regular Boulders will be replaced with special Boulders that drop the Friendly Boulder item when they break. Depending on world size, 2 (small worlds), 4 (medium worlds), or 6 (large worlds) special Boulders can be generated. This number is doubled when No Traps seed is active.


== Trivia ==
Both the Friendly Boulder item and pet are identical in appearance to a placed Boulder.

title: Chillet
content:
Chillet and Chillet Ignis are pre-Hardmode mount-summoning items. When used, they summon the Chillet or Chillet Ignis mount, respectively, which increases damage dealt by 10% while mounted and is capable of performing "Rocket Slam", a dash. Dashing into an enemy deals 32 base summon damage, inflicts a knockback of 6 (Average), and grants the player 0.17 seconds of invincibility frames. Chillet and Chillet Ignis are functionally identical, and either variant can be obtained from the Huge Dragon Egg at a 1/2 (50%) chance.
 Trusty Chillet and Trusty Chillet Ignis are upgraded, Hardmode-exclusive versions of Chillet and Chillet Ignis obtained via crafting. They have increased maximum speed, jump reach, dash speed, and dash damage (150 base summon damage), but are otherwise identical to their pre-Hardmode counterparts.
Like other Pals, Chillet and its variants can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate.


== Types ==


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Riding Chillet increases the player's hitbox height by 0.25 tiles, for a total of height of 2.875 tiles.
Chillet reduces fall damage by 50%.
Chillet's dash performs a tiny hop when activated.
Chillet's dash inflicts 20 ticks of global invincibility frames upon hitting enemies.
The knockback of Chillet's dash can be increased by the Titan Glove (or its upgrades) and Titan Potion.
Chillet's dash will end immediately when facing away from the direction of the dash.
After Chillet's dash ends, there is a cooldown of 0.5 seconds before another dash can be performed.
The Traveling Merchant sells the Pal Metal set if the player has Chillet, Chillet Ignis, Cattiva, Foxparks, Digtoise, or their "Trusty" variants in the inventory or in any portable storage item when speaking to him.


== Tips ==
The large amount of invincibility frames Chillet's dash grants on hit consistently protects the player from contact damage, making it an incredibly powerful tool against bosses like the Eye of Cthulhu, Queen Bee, and Skeletron. With Featherfall Potions and extra jumps, this can even be great into Hardmode bosses such as Duke Fishron and Plantera.
Chillet's dash having a uniquely vertical angle compared to other dashes can be utilized in conjunction with extra jumps to activate them immediately after performing a dash from the ground.
Having to face the same way to keep dashing is unique to Chillet's dash and has both drawbacks and advantages:
It limits the effectiveness of the dash as a means of attacking while retreating, as this would force the player to face the opposite direction of the dash. Dashes performed in this way have a very short window in which they are able to hit enemies and do not move nearly as fast, though they are still able to redirect Chillet's momentum.
It can be utilized to intentionally cut dashes short if they would overshoot their target area, or if they were unintentional in the first place.
Due to how the cooldown period before Chillet is able to dash again begins once Chillet exits the dashing state, ending dashes almost immediately after starting them can allow Chillet to dash again faster than any other dash in the game would allow, while still being able to redirect its momentum with each "microdash".


== Trivia ==
Chillet and Chillet Ignis are part of the crossover with Palworld. Their signature move in Palworld, "Rocket Slam", is referenced in Terraria by the dash attack. Moreover, the damage increase while mounted is a reference to Chillet's partner skill in Palworld, which increases the player's attack stat and changes the element of their weapons to dragon-type.
While the Huge Dragon Egg is worth 1 Gold, the hatched Chillet and Chillet Ignis only sell for a hundredth of this value. The trusty upgrades have the same sell value as well.
Chillet and Chillet Ignis have different rarity levels despite being functionally identical and obtainable from the same source.
Similarly to all other Pals, this is likely intended to make the colors of their rarities match their respective color schemes, instead of following the standard rarity system.
Tooltip lines that objectively describe an item's function (as opposed to lines serving as flavor text) very rarely end with a period. Chillet's and its variants' tooltips are some of the only such instances, along with the tooltips of the Barrel Launcher, Catalyst Band, Guide to Old World Parkour, and Portal Gun.

title: Workshop Hub
content:
The Workshop Hub is a menu option in Terraria which allows players to toggle/import worlds or Resource Packs installed from the Steam Workshop or from a local file. It also allows players to publish worlds or Resource Packs to Steam Workshop, or publish an update for their worlds and Resource Packs.
The Workshop Hub can be accessed via the main menu by pressing the “Workshop” button, but only while playing on a Steam copy of the game. While playing on a GOG.com copy of the game, the button will be replaced with “Resource Packs”, which opens the “Use Resource Packs” menu directly.


== Menu options ==


=== Import Worlds ===
The Import Worlds screen shows a list of the players currently subscribed Steam Workshop worlds. Each item in the list shows data like the worlds name, creation date, difficulty, and size. Unlike the Select World menu, only one button exists to "Import" the selected world, making a unique copy of it with a set name.


=== Use Resource Packs ===
The Use Resource Packs screen shows a list of available Resource Packs the player has installed, either via their ResourcePacks folder or from the Steam Workshop. Packs subscribed through Steam Workshop will have the  Steam icon on the upper-right corner of the item. The player can view the description of each pack or enable them, ordered from most to least significance. Packs on the top of the Enabled Packs list will overwrite the packs below them and all enabled packs can be reordered with the arrow buttons.


=== Publish Worlds &  Publish Resource Packs ===
The Publish Worlds and Publish Resource Packs screens show a list of the player's current worlds or loaded resource packs, allowing them to publish to the Steam Workshop. Once clicking “Publish” on a given item, players are able to give the item a custom icon, set the visibility of the content to others, and give their world or resource pack relevant tags to help others find it on the Steam Workshop.
To update an existing published Workshop item, simply publish the same world or resource pack again in this menu.


== Notes ==
Note that for Terraria, subscribed Steam Workshop items will be automatically downloaded and made available regardless of the current Steam account. As a result, if multiple Steam accounts have logged in on the same device, one may find other accounts' subscribed Workshop items showing up in the game.


== Gallery ==

		
		
		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: 
Fixed several issues that could cause updating a Steam Workshop item to publish it as a new entry.
Fixed the Publish Workshop Item menu not having its header text centered.
Desktop 1.4.2: Introduced.

title: Guide:Duke Fishron strategies
content:
Duke Fishron is an optional Hardmode boss. The fight has small room for error, which makes him one of the hardest bosses in the game, especially if he is fought before the Mechanical bosses and Plantera.


== Spawn Condition ==
Duke Fishron can be spawned by using a fishing pole with a Truffle Worm as Bait in the Ocean. Truffle Worms can be found underground in the Glowing Mushroom biome during Hardmode. Although the boss is intended to be fought post-Golem, he can be fought as early as right after the Wall of Flesh has been defeated, giving the player powerful tools throughout Hardmode.


== The Fight ==
Duke Fishron has two phases in Classic mode.


=== First Phase ===
Duke Fishron will attack in three different ways during the first phase. The first thing Fishron will do is begin his charging flurry. He will charge towards the player exactly five times, with a short pause between each charge.
After each charge, he will execute one of the two Projectile attacks:

The first attack fires around 20 Detonating Bubbles;
The second attack will create two small Bubbles on either side of where he is located that will each generate a Sharknado. The Sharknados are not only tall and do damage, but they also fire Sharkrons towards the player.


=== Second Phase ===
When Duke Fishron falls below 50% health, he will stay stationary for a second, then his eyes will glow as he enters his second stage. His damage and speed increase significantly. However, his defense drops to 40.
His charge flurry only has 3 charges, but they are a bit faster than before. He still has two kinds of projectile attacks, but their patterns change:

The Detonating Bubble attack now causes him to move around in a circle, dropping the bubbles in a circle around his original location. This spreads out the bubbles, making it more difficult to pop them all. It also makes it difficult to hit Duke Fishron consistently, so this can be a good time to refill your mana with a Mana Regeneration Potion or re-apply Ichor.
His Sharknado attack upgrades to summon a Cthulhunado. He will fire a special bubble that homes in towards the nearest player. The bubble deals no damage on contact, but it will spawn a Cthulhunado, an upgraded version of the Sharknado that is much taller, deals more damage, fires more Sharkrons, and lasts much longer.
Duke Fishron's charging attack is his primary attack and can be difficult to dodge when without proper mobility accessories.
The key to dodging it is to try to move perpendicularly to where he is aimed, right before he makes his charge. For example, if you are horizontal with him when he is about to charge, you need to quickly move up or down. (The fastest way to drop down is to briefly mount a Slimy Saddle or Gelatinous Pillion). If he is right above or below you, then you need to quickly move left or right. Do not fly all the way into the space layer, or the reduced gravity will render you helpless. If using a flying mount to dodge, diagonal movement is much faster than horizontal movement.
As long as the player keeps in mind what attack Duke Fishron will do next, the player can put him in a position that makes it hard for the player to hit the Cthulhunado themselves. For example, during the charging flurry before the Cthulhunado attack, the player can move towards the edge of the screen, horizontally. That way, the player can run the other way knowing that they will not encounter Sharkrons from that direction. This also means that attacks towards Duke Fishron will also be towards the direction of incoming Sharkrons.
Also, note that Duke Fishron's first attack will always be bubbles.
Cthulhunado are quite tall; getting over them will require fast Wings or an infinite flight mount like the Cosmic Car Key.
The Cthulhunado attack is a bit more difficult to deal with. It is taller, and does more damage than the original, plus it fires more Sharkrons. 
However, there is one thing that makes it a bit easier to deal with: the Cthulhunado will spawn in the location where you were when the bubble hit the player. This gives the player more control over where the Cthulhunado spawns, so the player has more of a chance (if they have the proper mobility) to make sure it does not spawn in an inconvenient place. Therefore, the best way to avoid being damage by the Cthulhunado is to precisely control its position, preferably in corners of the arena, by intentionally hitting the homing bubble. The player likely does not have the speed to outrun the attack, but the Cthulhunado can be spawned in a more convenient location. 
Once the bubble strikes the player, they should do all they can to quickly move, to prevent the Cthulhunado from spawning on top of them. Contact with a Cthulhunado, either immediately after its spawning or later, should be avoided by all possible means, as they deal 100 contact damage. The player should use mobility items such as the Rod of Discord, Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi, or any Grappling Hook to dodge them.


=== Expert Mode ===
Duke Fishron’s Phase 2 lunges are delayed by a second, requiring that you time your dodges a bit later than usual to avoid them.
When Duke Fishron drops below 15% health, he will transform again and the background will notably darken, while making himself invisible except for his glowing eyes.
He will only be able to use his charge attacks in this stage, but he will gain the ability to teleport behind the player before attacking. The charges will come in a set pattern: After teleporting, he will successively charge once, then twice, and finally three times before the pattern resets. Note that the first charge attack he does right after transforming to Phase 3 is done without teleporting, so if the player moved away from the boss when Phase 3 starts, the first dash they will encounter is a 2-dash. 
While his contact damage is reduced, the high speed of his charges can cause you to get hit many times in a quick succession. Pay attention to his attack pattern, and make sure to not stand still during the fight. Dashing around can help avoid attacks more easily; be sure to move perpendicular to the direction that Duke Fishron will dash in. You should also try to get away from any Cthulhunados left from the second stage.

Because Duke Fishron is untargetable while teleporting, minions and many slower homing weapons will almost stop working entirely. As there won't be many opportunities to deal damage, you should try to deal as much burst damage as possible during his charges. Slow, highly-damaging weapons like the Sniper Rifle and Tactical Shotgun work well during this phase.
Note that, after the battle is over, care should still be taken. If he has launched a Cthulhunado, it may still fire Sharkrons. He may also have died in the Cthulhunado, so do not charge into it to collect his drops until it dissipates.


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===
The arena must be located in the Ocean, unless you are very confident that you can beat an enraged Fishron, which is usually not recommended.

Make an arena with 3 - 5 rows of Platforms, each about 50 tiles apart due to the height of the Cthulhunados. The arena should span at least the width of the Ocean.
The arena must be very tall: the tornadoes are very tall, require a significant amount of flight time to fly over.
Asphalt blocks can be used on the bottom layer of the arena, boosting your speed to over 70mph.


=== Gearing up ===
It is highly recommended to defeat Golem first, as these tips will mostly take that into account. For more information about this boss, check its own strategy guide.
Duke Fishron's damage is very high compared to the other bosses, especially on his second and third phases, so attempting to obtain high defense may prove ineffective as they may only turn two-hit attacks into three-hit attacks while still dealing around 130+ damage in his first phase (assuming the player has around 75 defense) and 200+ damage if Duke Fishron's health is below 50%.
While the Truffle Worms can spawn at any point in Hardmode, Duke Fishron may be challenging to inexperienced players and the battle can last longer due to high health of the boss, his high speed and comparatively low damage of the weapons at this stage of the game. However, if the player defeats Duke Fishron before any of the mechanical bosses or even before Plantera, they will be rewarded with powerful equipment that continues to be relevant even after defeating Golem.


==== Armor ====
For melee users, the best offensive set consists of the Chlorophyte Mask, Monk's Shirt or Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso, and Valhalla Knight's Greaves. Alternatively, Spooky Breastplate can be worn if you prefer a hybrid set. Additionally, a mix of the Hallowed Mask, Valhalla Knight's Breastplate, and Valhalla Knight's Greaves provides high offensive stats and optimized survivability.
For ranged users, the best offensive set consists of any Shroomite headpiece, Shroomite Breastplate, and Red Riding Leggings. The Hallowed Helmet and the Adamantite Mask are viable, more accessible alternatives that boost all weapon types and increase critical strike chance.
The Red Riding Dress has slightly worse ranged bonuses, but it makes up for it with its large boost to summon damage.
The full Shroomite set has better damage output when stealthed, but maintaining stealth is not feasible in singleplayer mode.
For magic users, the best offensive set consists of either Spectre armor or a hybrid set consisting of Hallowed Headgear, Spectre Robe, and Dark Artist's Leggings.
Using the Dark Artist's Robes instead of the Spectre Robe will grant higher defense in exchange for some offensive stats.
Spectre Hood can be used to heal when your health is running low.
For summoners, the best set consists of Spooky armor. Tiki armor is also viable if player uses the Firecracker whip. For more survivability, Valhalla Knight armor can be used.
If defense is preferred, Beetle armor can be used with the Beetle Shell, regardless of class.
In high difficulties like Legendary Mode and Master Mode, the Hallowed armor's Holy Protection set bonus provides outstanding survivability, allowing you to dodge a high-damage attack every 30 seconds. It is available after one mechanical boss has been defeated.


===== Pre-mechanical bosses =====
For melee users, the best set consists of the Adamantite Helmet, Frost Breastplate, and Mythril Greaves, offering as much offensive power as possible without compromising defense.
For ranged users, the best offensive set consists of the Adamantite Mask, Frost Breastplate, and Mythril Greaves. If you prefer a hybrid set, Spider Greaves can be used.
For magic users, the best offensive set consists of the Adamantite Headgear, Mystic Robe, and Forbidden Treads. The Forbidden Robes can be used for an extra minion and better defense.
For summoners, the best offensive armor set is Spider Armor.
The Crystal Assassin armor provides a better dash than the Shield of Cthulhu at the cost of below average damage and defense.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users:

The Terra Blade scales with melee speed as well as damage and critical chance, and its large projectile makes hitting Duke Fishron and the Detonating Bubbles easy.
The Influx Waver is a very powerful choice if you have defeated Martian Madness already.
The Christmas Tree Sword works very well against Duke Fishron, as the boss chases the player, flying directly into the trail of ornaments.
The Seedler is an excellent option due to its auto-targeting nature.
Both of Betsy's melee drops (Sky Dragon's Fury, using right-click, and Flying Dragon) are among the highest-DPS options available.
The Possessed Hatchet has lacking DPS, but a very reliable homing projectile and inflicts the powerful Hemorrhage debuff.
The Eye of Cthulhu is the best Yo-yo that can be used at this point.
The Paladin's Hammer has relatively low damage, but can be used as a support weapon as it applies the Broken Armor debuff, cutting Fishron's defense down even further.
The Vampire Knives is very useful for stealing life. With enough defensive builds, it is capable of face-tanking the boss in Master Mode.
The Scourge of the Corruptor is somewhat low in damage, but it makes up for this by homing in on Fishron during the fight.
The Sergeant United Shield or Brand of the Inferno are useful during the third phase of the fight, for those who are bold enough to try parrying the Duke's attacks.
The Mushroom Spear and the True Night's Edge are the best pre-Plantera melee weapons against this boss.
The Bananarang and Chain Guillotines are the best options against this boss before any mechanical bosses with the former being better in the second phase and the latter being better at fighting him at a close range.
The Shadowflame Knife may deal less damage but is still effective against the boss and the easiest of the three to use due to its better range.
For Ranged users:

The Xenopopper is the best gun for the fight when used with Nano Bullets or Crystal Bullets, but will often be unable to target Duke Fishron when he is offscreen.
The Chain Gun, Tactical Shotgun, and Sniper Rifle are also highly effective. Chlorophyte Bullets are more accurate but have lower damage output.
The Piranha Gun is good for Duke Fishron's third phase as it can latch on to teleporting enemies.
The Aerial Bane is the best bow with its extremely high DPS and splitting arrows, dealing damage to the Sharknados as well. It should be used with Venom Arrows. The Eventide has slightly less damage but is less affected by gravity. The Stake Launcher is weaker than both, but still strong and is easier to obtain.
Ichor Arrows, Bullets, or Darts will reduce his defense significantly, since he is vulnerable to Ichor.
The Snowman Cannon is powerful against him, if you have defeated the Frost Moon.
The Elf Melter has consistent, high damage and a wide hitbox, popping the Detonating Bubbles at ease. Also, the boss tends to stay within its range as it chases you.
The Flamethrower is a weaker alternative. It is also available earlier, in the pre-Plantera phase of progression.
The Megashark and Onyx Blaster are weaker, but they are available much earlier in progression.
The Daedalus Stormbow with Ichor Arrows is the best ranged option for dispatching Duke before defeating any other Hardmode boss. Similarly, if the player has defeated all mech bosses, Chlorophyte Shotbow is a stronger alternative, which has slightly lower damage upper limit but is significantly easier to aim.
The Marrow, Ice Bow, and Shadowflame Bow are three very similar bows available at the start of Hardmode that, when combined with the Golden Shower, are viable to use when fighting Duke Fishron pre-mechanical bosses. The Titanium Repeater and Adamantite Repeater, if fighting the boss pre-mech, are also viable options.
The Uzi combined with the Chaos Cylinder is a very powerful and viable combination when using Ichor Bullets and Crystal Bullets, and may be more desirable than using a bow as, although being more difficult items to obtain, outperforms the bows in DPS.
For Magic users:

The Razorpine is very strong due to its excellent DPS, although it requires you to get closer than with other weapons.
The Nightglow is also very strong because of its homing ability and high DPS.
The Golden Shower spellbook is helpful as it reduces his defense and easily pops all the Detonating Bubbles. It should be used as a supportive weapon due to low damage output.
Betsy's Wrath is a much stronger alternative to the Golden Shower that also lowers his defense more, at the cost of having to get a bit closer.
The Bat Scepter is effective due to its homing nature allowing one to focus on dodging, especially during the third and final phase in Expert/Master Mode. The Spectre Staff is a weaker alternative that is easier to obtain.
The Blizzard Staff is very good for attacking while he is stationary.
The Arc Surge, Laser Machinegun or Charged Blaster Cannon can be used if the player has already defeated Martian Madness.
The Magnet Sphere can deal a lot of damage and only needs to be cast once in a while.
The Heat Ray is also a viable option with decent single-target damage.
The Spirit Flame, Crystal Serpent, Orange Zapinator, Lightning Strike, Rainbow Rod, and Unholy Trident are the best pre-Plantera magic weapons against this boss, with the former four being available at the start of Hardmode. Assuming the player wants to fight the boss during early Hardmode in Expert or Master mode, the Cursed Flames are very effective against its third phase.
For Summoners:

Should the daytime Empress of Light be defeated beforehand, the Terraprisma is definitely the best minion available.
The Xeno Staff is a consistent and powerful minion. It should be used either with the Dark Harvest or Kaleidoscope for maximum damage.
The Desert Tiger Staff is a powerful alternative. It should be used with Vulgar Display of Flower.
The Deadly Sphere Staff is a decent option with lower obtaining difficulty.
While most sentries are unable to hit this boss effectively, the Barnacle Staff can float in the air over the ocean.
If you are fighting the boss at an early stage, the Sanguine Staff paired with Firecracker and Snapthorn (or Durendal if you have defeated at least one mechanical boss) is the best weapon pre-Plantera. The Cool Whip can also be brought to deal slightly more damage via the Frostbite and A Nice Whip buffs.


==== Accessories ====
Quick aerial movement is a must-have for the fight. The most natural option is to use Wings, though without boosts, most wings do not have enough vertical speed to consistently dodge the Duke. Frog Leg can make them significantly faster, making it easier to get over the Cthulhunados and dodging his attacks while flying.
Alternatively, one can obtain the Jetpack. The high vertical speed makes it an ideal choice for dodging Duke Fishron without the need of the Frog Leg, though having the Frog Leg can make it even more effective at dodging Cthulhunados. The Empress Wings also have impressive vertical scaling.
The Amphibian Boots allow for increased ascent speed with wings and fast running, even on normal tiles.
The Master Ninja Gear and Shield of Cthulhu provide a dash, which is invaluable for mobility. The latter can also be used in the third phase to dash into the boss and avoid hits via immunity frames.
The Mystic Arts Sash has a dodge chance that stacks with Master Ninja Gear.
Cross Necklace or its upgrades can prevent heavy damage from getting trapped inside a Sharknado or a big group of homing bubbles.
Charm of Myths will both allow for increased regen and reduced time for the Potion Sickness debuff. The Philosopher's Stone effect can be used without the need of investing an accessory slot by keeping it on a vanity slot until needing to heal.
An Ankh Shield will protect from the Bleeding debuff and those caused by Feral Bite, and will also provide knockback resistance.
Accessories that increase damage are a must have for ending the battle sooner:
The best universal offensive accessories include Putrid Scent, Shark Tooth Necklaces, Emblems, Avenger Emblem, Celestial Stone, and the Destroyer Emblem.
Melee users have access to the Fire Gauntlet and Mechanical Glove for weapons that benefit from melee speed (such as Terra Blade or Influx Waver).
Ranged users can eqiup the Sniper Scope and Recon Scope and/or any Quivers if the bows are the main weapons.
The Mana Flower upgrades and the Celestial Emblem are effective for Magic users.
Summoners can use the Pygmy Necklace, Papyrus Scarab, Necromantic Scroll,  Hercules Beetle, Twilight Grasp,  and Ouroboros Ring with the former three increasing the amount of minion slots,  the next two increasing summon damage, and the latter two buffing whips. Note that the Lucky accessories will not be useful for the minions as they cannot deal critical hits on their own. The Templar's Sling can be used to bring sentries closer to Duke Fishron.
In general, it is preferably to reforge accessories to Menacing/Lucky as opposed to Warding. However, Warding can sometimes be perferable if fighting Duke Fishron pre-mech in Legendary Mode. High defense along with the Worm Scarf, Endurance Potion and Lifeforce Potion allows the player to take one hit from the Duke rather than be killed instantly.
If you are using The Eye of Cthulhu or another yoyo, use a Magic Yoyo Bag.


==== Potions and Buffs ====
Inferno Potion is highly recommended as it will destroy the Detonating Bubbles that Duke Fishron spawns before they reach the player.
If you are facing him at night, a Shine Potion, Night Owl Potion, and Hunter Potion will improve visibility.
Regeneration Potion and Ironskin Potion, Endurance and Lifeforce will improve survivability.
Any food item that can provide the Well Fed buff or better is very welcome.
Mana Regeneration can be very useful for mages.
Wrath Potion and/or Rage Potions for a boost in damage output.
Tipsy debuff, which is obtained by drinking Ale or Sake and the Flask of Ichor are very beneficial for Melee users. These effects also affect whips.
Likewise, the Archery, Magic Power and Summoning potion buffs provide damage increase for Ranged, Magic and Summon players.
Water Walking Potions can be used as a substitute for a platform in the Ocean.
Swiftness Potion can help you evade Duke Fishron's attacks.
Gravitation Potions can free up an accessory slot. It is recommended to use Featherfall Potions with them.


==== Mounts ====
The Cosmic Car Key mount is a good replacement for Wings. While its movement is generally slower and less versatile due to being unaffected by other mobility accessories, it can save accessory slots for other defense or damage improvements.
The Expert Mode-exclusive Witch's Broom is better, as it is faster and is able to travel in water. However, it requires the player to have done the Pumpkin Moon.
The Superheated Blood mount can be used in this fight due to its high mobility through water without having to use asphalt blocks.
Gelatinous Pillion can help you to move fast vertically, which is very useful during the 3rd phase. In addition to this, it has relatively high speed on land and provides flying time comparable to pre-Plantera, which is effective for players who have not defeated a mechanical boss yet.
Trusty Chillet has the best dash and good horizontal mobility, making it able to synergize with extra jump accessories. Additionally, it allows to directly dash into the boss while keeping momentum and not losing health, which is very important during his third phase.
The Roller Skates are a very useful mount to use in the first and second phases when fighting the boss pre-mechanical boss, due to them allowing you to preserve momentum and move faster.


== More In-Depth Strategies ==


=== Minecart Strategy ===
This strategy differs from others in that it does not use a skybridge, replacing it with looped minecart track above the ocean, so the player won't have to deal with his enraged behavior. It does, however, need some more work than other ones, especially when building the arena. 


==== Materials ====
600-1200 normal minecart tracks for building loop + 2 booster tracks
Any kind of hammer


==== Arena Preparation ====
The essence is to make looped minecart track approx. 60 tiles above Ocean itself. It should consist of at least 600 tiles; while shape is pretty loose, it should have at least two places in which player drastically changes altitude, as well as at least 100 tiles long flats.
One should also make a "Starter" - a short molo with boosters, from which player will summon Duke Fishron and quickly escape to the loop.
It should be noted also that arena shouldn't exceed Ocean biome.


==== Execution ====
When everything is done, player should sit in a minecart on "Starter" and summon the Fishron. As soon as it is done, one should quickly go to loop (boosters will help). At this point, everything that remains is to shoot Fishron while maintaining speed on track, healing a/o replenishing mana when needed.
Some tips:

Use a homing weapon, especially if your arena is pretty large. Fishron will spend most time off-screen, and high speed will often change directions you are facing.
Though stock minecart should not be used, Mechanical Cart is not a good choice. Even though with it provides defense bonus, as well as speed to avoid Fishron's charges, it can easily outrun him causing Fishron to despawn, which is possible on larger arenas. Higher speed means also that you will more often run into Sharknados.
Try to make arena consisting of approximately 800 tiles, but do not make it horizontally-long. If you do so, Fishron will frequently run into you, and Cthulunados in his second stage will quickly kill you as there is no way to dodge them.


=== Teleporter strategy ===
For the third phase, a possible strategy is placing a teleporter with a pressure plate on top at surface level, and an actuated teleporter on a platform 200 blocks above, which you can use to fall endlessly, and giving Fishron a hard time hitting you.


=== Chillet strategy ===
Chillet grants the player a dash that avoids damage. This means that the player can dash through Duke Fishron's charges in Phase 3 if timed correctly, as well as many attacks in the earlier phases. Since Chillet cannot fly, an tall arena with multiple layers of platforms is preferred. The Bundle of Balloons can give Chillet extreme mobility. As of 1.4.5.7, for good mobility, the Chillet mount should be buffed using the Little Kinship Peach to the Trusty Chillet.


=== Single Layer Arena strategy ===
A very compact but effective arena design is to use a single layer of flat arena on the ground without any platforms on top of it. This requires asphalt blocks, (or sand blocks with Dunerider Boots if fighting the boss pre-mech) so you get a very high horizontal movement speed, but needs great execution of controlling where Sharknados and Cthulhunados are. A good way of fighting the boss this way is to fish him up at one end of the arena, run to the other side while he dashes 5 times. After he does the Bubble attack, circle around him, drop down, and run straight back to the other side. This way, you outrun the tornados immediately after they are placed. This also works for Phase 2, but needs more caution as the Cthulhunado spawns where the homing bubble hits you. In Phase 3, the Gelatinous Pillion mount is recommended. 


=== Slime Mount strategy ===
The Gelatinous Pillion has extraordinary vertical acceleration, making it one of the best ways to dodge Phase 3 attacks. By timing the jumps correctly according to the boss's dashes, you can easily completely avoid being hit. Note that when the boss enters Phase 3, you should quickly get away from any Cthulhunado that is present in your arena, then activate the mount. If you have not defeated Queen Slime yet, the Slimy Saddle paired with any Extra jump accessory can also be useful and is even safer to use.

title: Titanium armor
content:
Titanium armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Titanium Breastplate and Titanium Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Titanium Mask, Titanium Helmet, and Titanium Headgear, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 59 Titanium Bars (236 Titanium Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 85 Titanium Bars (340 Titanium Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is  Adamantite armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:

Attacking grants the player the Titanium Barrier buff, which spawns Titanium Shards that spin around the player. The shards spin faster the more there are, and up to 7 shards can exist at once. Each Titanium Shard deals 50 damage with a knockback value of 15 (Insane), and cannot deal critical hits. Each shard dissipates on enemy hits or after 10 seconds has passed.


== Set ==


=== Helmet variants ===


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==

Most dyes do not affect the color of this armor much, with a few exceptions like Intense Rainbow Dye.
If the player teleports while the Titanium Barrier buff is active, the shards will quickly move to the player's position instead of teleporting.
A Lightning Aura sentry can be used to continuously refresh the Titanium Barrier set bonus, though Target Dummies and statue-spawned enemies cannot be exploited for this purpose. Traps will not trigger the set bonus at all.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: 
Shards can now only generate once every 10 ticks (1/6th of a second), for a maximum of 6 shards a second.
Titanium armor no longer spawns shards from statue spawned enemies.
Desktop 1.4.1: Titanium Mask bonus increased from 8% to 9%.
Desktop 1.4.0.3: Titanium armor's set bonus is no longer trigged by Target Dummies.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Sprites updated.
The full set bonus has been changed to providing a barrier of Titanium Shards instead of Shadow Dodge. The Shadow Dodge set bonus is now the Holy Protection set bonus from the Hallowed armor.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Internal cooldown of Shadow Dodge passed from 20 to 30 seconds.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Required bars increased from 12 to 13 for each of the headpieces.
Required bars increased from 24 to 26 for the Titanium Breastplate.
Required bars increased from 18 to 20 for the Titanium Leggings.
Fixed exploit where the Shadow Dodge buff would not be removed if it was the last buff in a full buff list.
Desktop 1.2.2: Fixed a bug involving having a large number of buffs causing the player to become invincible (buff slots were increased to fix this bug).
Desktop 1.2.1: Updated female sprite.
Desktop 1.2: Introduced.

Console 1.0.933.1: No longer used to craft Dragon armor, Spectral armor, and Titan armor.  ()
Console 1.0.750.0: No longer used to craft Dragon armor, Spectral armor, and Titan armor. ()
Console 1.09: Dragon armor, Spectral armor, and Titan armor can now be crafted with Titanium armor pieces.
Console 1.02: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile 1.3.0.7: No longer used to craft Dragon armor, Spectral armor, and Titan armor.
Mobile 1.2.11964: Dragon armor, Spectral armor, and Titan armor can now be crafted with Orichalcum, Palladium, or Titanium armor pieces.
Mobile 1.2.6508: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Brain of Confusion
content:
The Brain of Confusion is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Brain of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. It grants the following effects while equipped:

Upon taking damage, the player has a 1/6 (16.67%) of dodging an attack, negating damage from that attack. Upon dodging, the player also receives the Cerebral Mindtrick debuff for four seconds. Despite being a debuff, it increases critical strike chance and summon damage by 10%. While the debuff is active, the player cannot dodge another attack.
Upon taking damage, nearby enemies have a 3/5 (60%) chance of receiving the Confused debuff. The chance, duration, and area of effect of the debuff are based on the amount of damage taken.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Worm Scarf.


== Inflicting Confused on enemies ==


=== Chance ===
The base chance to inflict the Confused debuff is 3/5 (60%). It is increased by 1/250 (0.4%) per point of damage taken, hence with 100 or more damage taken, the debuff is guaranteed to be inflicted.


=== Duration ===
The debuff duration is determined randomly, and the bounds depend on the amount of damage ([math]\displaystyle{ \text{dmg} }[/math]) taken:

The values are in seconds.


=== Range ===
The range within which enemies are affected is determined randomly as well. There are certain damage ([math]\displaystyle{ \text{dmg} }[/math]) thresholds that affect which equation to use:
[math]\displaystyle{ \text{range}_{\text{min}} = \begin{cases}
\left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{dmg}}{2} \right\rfloor + 200 & \text{if} \  \text{dmg} \leq 600 \\
& \\
\dfrac{3}{4}  \times \left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{dmg}}{2} \right\rfloor + 275 & \text{if} \  600 \lt  \text{dmg} \leq 1333 \\
& \\
\dfrac{3}{8}  \times \left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{dmg}}{2} \right\rfloor + 487.5 & \text{if} \  1333 \lt  \text{dmg} \leq 2200 \\
& \\
\dfrac{3}{32} \times \left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{dmg}}{2} \right\rfloor + 796.875 & \text{if} \  2200 \lt  \text{dmg} \\
\end{cases} }[/math]

[math]\displaystyle{ \text{range}_{\text{max}} = \begin{cases}
2\times \text{dmg}+300 & \text{if} \  \text{dmg}\leq 100 \\
& \\
\dfrac{3}{2} \times \text{dmg}+350 & \text{if} \  100\lt  \text{dmg}\leq 233 \\
& \\
\dfrac{3}{4} \times \text{dmg}+525 & \text{if} \  233\lt  \text{dmg}\leq 500 \\
& \\
\dfrac{3}{16} \times \text{dmg}+806.25 & \text{if} \  500\lt  \text{dmg} \\
\end{cases} }[/math]
The values are in pixels; divide by 16 to obtain tiles.


=== Examples ===


== Notes ==
The effect of inflicting Confused debuff to nearby enemies cannot be triggered if the player is damaged from non-enemy sources (such as Thorny Bushes, lava and Spikes), but the dodge effect can trigger regardless.
Despite being a debuff, Cerebral Mindtrick cannot be removed by the Nurse.
Upon attempting to inflict the Confused debuff to nearby enemies, a brain visual will fly upwards from the player.
Upon dodging an attack, a circle of brain visuals expands outwards from the player.
The brain visuals created by the Brain of Confusion are not affected by dyes.
The chance that the Confused debuff is inflicted, as well as its duration, is calculated for each enemy within range individually.
The dodge chance of the Brain of Confusion stacks with other dodge items (Black Belt and Mystic Arts Sash). Dodging chances are treated as independent events, instead of stacking additively:


== Tips ==
The added chance to dodge nearly matches the percentage of damage prevented by the Worm Scarf (16.67% for the Brain of Confusion vs 17% for the Worm Scarf). This means that both accessories will, on average, prevent the same amount of damage but in a different way, although depending on the scenario one of them may provide more value:
The Brain of Confusion can be superior in the following ways:
Especially in higher difficulties where taking damage in the first place can be extremely dangerous, a chance to dodge can prove to be more useful in tight situations (as taking 17% reduced damage from the Worm Scarf may still be too much). The same can be said vice versa, as the chance to dodge may never activate at all.
The Brain of Confusion provides a short-term DPS increase from the 10% critical strike chance and summon damage increase after a successful dodge.
Successfully dodging an attack does not reset the player's regeneration timer, nor does it require waiting for health regeneration to restart. Compared to taking damage, avoiding hits allows the player to recover more health in the same amount of time — this is especially noticeable when the player has high health regeneration or a high regeneration timer.
Succeessfully dodging an attack will negate the debuffs and knockback from the attack, and provides a longer duration of invincibility frames than actually getting hit by the attack.
The Worm Scarf can be superior in the following ways:
The 17% damage reduction does not have a cooldown and can be triggered when getting hit in rapid succession (such as when face-tanking), while the Brain of Confusion's dodge effect has a 4-second cooldown in form of the Cerebral Mindtrick debuff.
The 17% damage reduction is consistent and does not rely on chance.
If the player has any other sources of additive-stacking damage reduction (Endurance Potion, Frozen Turtle Shell when at 50% or less health, melee Chlorophyte armor set bonus, Turtle armor set bonus, Solar Flare armor set bonus), equipping the Worm Scarf will reduce a larger effective percentage of damage than the Brain of Confusion.
For example, a 100-damage attack will deal 90 damage after using an Endurance Potion. Equipping the Worm Scarf will further reduce the damage from 90 to 73, meaning the Worm Scarf provides an effective 18.89% damage reduction in practice, as opposed to the usual 17%. In comparison, Equipping the Brain of Confusion will still only reduce the damage taken by 16.67% on average.
The best of both worlds would be to use both accessories together, through buying evil counterpart seeds from the Dryad in a Hardmode Graveyard biome and building an artificial Crimson or Corruption biome.


== Trivia ==
Prior to the addition of Cerebral Mindtrick in 1.4.0.1, the Brain of Confusion was sometimes considered to be a disappointment compared to the Worm Scarf, as its sole function was to occasionally confuse enemies.
Unlike the Worm Scarf, having six or more Brains of Confusion equipped (e.g. via inventory editors) at the same time does not grant a 100% chance to dodge attacks.
Brain of Confusion appears as a crossover Chaos VI shard in Dungeon Defenders 2.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
The effect of inflicting Confused debuff to nearby enemies no longer triggers when taking damage from non-enemy hazards.
Clarified Brain of Confusion tooltip.
Can no longer be removed by the Nurse.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Halved the critical chance and summon damage bonus of Cerebral Mindtrick from 20% to 10%.
Reduced the duration of Cerebral Mindtrick from 5 to 4 seconds.
Fixed an issue where dodged attacks could still result in debuffs on the player.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Now grants a chance to dodge an attack. A successful dodge inflicts the player with Cerebral Mindtrick, which provides a 20% bonus to critical strike chance and summon damage for 5 seconds.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.0.933.1: Introduced. ()
Console 1.0.750.0: Introduced. ()

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile 1.3.0.7: Introduced.
