title: Guide:Mechdusa strategies
content:
Mechdusa is an early Hardmode boss exclusive to worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix seeds. Composed of all three mechanical bosses, it is essentially a forced triple boss fight. Its resulting massive size, wide variety of strong attacks, and high culmulative health come together to create an extremely long and difficult battle.


== Spawn Conditions ==
Mechdusa can only be spawned in a world with both the For the Worthy and Remix (Don't Dig Up) seeds active, through one of two methods:

If at least 1 Demon/Crimson Altar has been smashed, and any mechanical boss has not been defeated yet, it has a 1/20 chance of spawning each night
Using an Ocram's Razor


== The Fight ==
The Mechdusa is three separate bosses merged into one, all of which must be defeated. They have a combined health of 256,800 / 327,420 / 436,560, shared between them. Those bosses are Skeletron Prime, The Destroyer, and The Twins.
When the Mechdusa spawns, the bosses are all connected together. Skeletron Prime is at the center, restricting the movement of the others from their normal behavior for as long as it is alive.
While the Twins are attached to Skeletron Prime, Retinazer will generally stay to the left while Spazmatism will generally stay to the right. This can be useful when trying to avoid their attacks; for instance, phase two Spazmatism is less likely to hit players who stay on the left.
Skeletron Prime will try to position itself 28.125 blocks to the side of and between 17.75 and 21.875 blocks above the player when not "spinning". Its spin attack no longer actually spins, but Prime's head will still move towards the player at 0.6x the normal speed, or 0.75x after the Destroyer's death. Skeletron Prime's arms are unaffected by being a part of Mechdusa, other than them hovering near the head which is in a different spot than normal.
The Destroyer's head will follow Skeletron Prime's position, while its body will follow each previous segment as normal. While Skeletron Prime is alive, Probes will fire lasers every 6 seconds, as opposed to the normal 2, and are completely unable to directly ram the player, instantly adjusting their position to avoid contact.
When not dashing, the Twins move to be 11.71875 blocks above and 7.03125 blocks to the side of Skeletron Prime's head, as opposed to positions relative to the player. They will wait twice as long between dashes in phase 1 and four times as long during phase 2, as well as twice the time gap between shooting projectiles (1.5x as long after the Destroyer dies).
The ideal sequence of killing is: The Destroyer - Retinazer - Skeletron Prime - Spazmatism. As Skeletron Prime restricts the movement of the other two bosses heavily, killing it at first will result in an extremely difficult battle. Letting Spazmatism enter second phase before killing Skeletron Prime also makes the fight much harder to handle, as Skeletron Prime can drag the flamethrowing Spazmatism to a very high speed. If you are struggling with Prime Vice and Prime Saw, they can also be chosen as your first targets.


== General Strategies ==


=== Terrain Preparation ===
Due to Mechdusa's large size and the ease of running away from it, a large arena makes the fight much easier. A surface arena provides the most space, but requires using lava to block enemy spawns and has low gravity. The spawning island also makes a good arena with very little threat from enemy spawns, but can be lacking in vertical leeway if you do not clear out space using Dynamite or a Gravedigger's Shovel.
A surface arena is faster to make, while an underworld arena is easier to build and use for the fight.
One option for staying away from Mechdusa is to outrun her using Dunerider Boots. Hardened Sand Blocks can be crafted at a Solidifier, and particularly on the surface, a Gravitation Potion can allow the player to run at high speeds on both the ground and the ceiling to pass behind Mechdusa.
Note that if the Celebration Mk 10 seed is not active in the world, Skeletron Prime's bombs will destroy blocks. Because of this, using explosion-proof blocks for an arena (such as Dungeon Bricks, Titanstone Blocks, or other Hardmode Ore bricks) is highly recommended.
Another option is to use a Featherfall Potion to dodge attacks by jumping. In this case, you can include a layer of platforms as well; if Mechdusa spawns on a platform, the Destroyer component will be exposed for huge amounts of damage upon spawning, letting you easily kill it before it can threaten you.
Teleporters are another option for passing by Mechdusa. Teleporting up or down at the edges of a runway can automate the process of going over or under Mechdusa to continue running the other way.


=== Gearing Up ===


==== Mounts ====
Early Hardmode has many strong mounts that can greatly help in this fight, either as an aid to mobility or to replace it entirely.

Golf Cart Keys has solid all-around stats and good acceleration coupled with the ability to ram enemies horizontally for iframes.
Lilith's Necklace is the easiest to obtain of these mounts due to the permanent surface nighttime, and has better speed and jumps than the golf cart, in return for the inability to ram enemies. It also has the smallest hitbox, making it easier to dodge lasers.
Gelatinous Pillion has the fastest vertical mobility and can help avoid damage when above Mechdusa, but is noticeably slower horizontally.
Blessed Apple has the highest run speed of any mount at this point, which can enable quick getaways with the Shield of Cthulhu.


==== Armor ====
Adamantite armor is best for melee and mage players and good for ranger due to high stats.
Frost Breastplate and Frost Leggings provide higher defense, which should be used for melee weapons like the Drippler Crippler that do not benefit much from melee speed. Mythril Greaves/Forbidden Treads are also options for all three classes in case the player wants to create an offensive build, with the former armor piece being best for the melee and ranger classes and the latter for mage players.
Frost armor is the best option for ranger, with much better defense than Adamantite Mask in return for slightly less damage.
Spider armor is the best choice for summoners, with some value for Obsidian armor if whip range is the main issue.
Melee Adamantite armor is a viable choice for summoners if high defense is preferable. It also provides an attack speed bonus, pairing well with the Firecracker.
Titanium armor could deal more damage than its competitors by making use of the Titanium Barrier buff, but Mechdusa will rarely be close enough to make good use of it.
Orichalcum armor and Forbidden armor can deal high damage to the Destroyer, but have worse stats otherwise.
Crystal Assassin armor can be useful as a replacement for a Shield of Cthulhu, but is otherwise worse than other options.
If one part of Mechdusa has already been defeated, the best defensive set consists of Hallowed Mask, Squire's Plating and Squire's Greaves, which provides 69 defense and allows you to ignore most projectiles.
Full set of Squire armor can also be used if more life regeneration is wanted.


==== Weapons ====
Mechdusa is very large and has many different components that can be damaged, so weapons with an area or piercing effect have a strong advantage at the beginning. Due to the different nature of the bosses that make it up, you may want to switch out weapons as the fight progresses, such as switching to single-target damage once the Destroyer portion dies. These recommendations focus on specifically the best weapons for each class; there are cases of weaker, easier-to-obtain weapons that may be more desirable, such as Dao of Pow compared to Drippler Crippler.

Melee Weapons

The Flint is the overall best melee weapon against Mechdusa if running away from it. When charged, it is extremely effective against The Destroyer, kills Prime Vice and Prime Saw quickly, and deals high damage to Skeletron Prime and The Twins as well.
The Drippler Crippler has great range and extreme damage particularly against The Destroyer, capable of killing it in a few seconds if the tail coil is exposed.
The Shadowflame Knife is good for the Twins and Skeletron Prime, and decent against The Destroyer.
The Bananarang has good single target damage and long range, but is weak against The Destroyer.
Ranged Weapons

The Daedalus Stormbow is great against the Twins and Skeletron Prime with Ichor Arrows and against the Destroyer with Unholy Arrows. However, it requires some open space above the player for it to be fully effective, which can limit its effectiveness if you are consistently jumping into a ceiling, and it struggles to hit the Destroyer if you never leave a solid floor. It also has the risk of letting Spazmatism enter second phase before killing Skeletron Prime, which makes the fight much more difficult.
The Uzi and Onyx Blaster are good options with Crystal Bullets against The Twins and Skeletron Prime, or with Explosive Bullets against The Destroyer. Compared to Daedalus Stormbow, they have lower damage, but can control which boss to damage more easily.
The Dart Rifle or Dart Pistol with Crystal Darts are great for sniping the Destroyer and deal lots of damage to the Twins and Skeletron Prime, with Ichor Darts being more effective at cleanup once only 3 enemies remain.
Cursed Darts can do more damage to the Destroyer, but only if the body is exposed above solid blocks, requiring specific aim. They do not perform as well as Crystal Darts when shot directly up.
Do not use the Star Cannon. It may seem appealing for killing the Destroyer, but Mechdusa reflects all Star Cannon projectiles due to For the Worthy's effects.
Magic Weapons

The Life Drain is highly effective against the Destroyer segment of the fight when it is coiled up, allowing the player to almost instantaneously get rid of a third of the trouble that comes along with this boss.
Similarly, the Clinger Staff is one of the best weapons against the Destroyer, being able to consistently kill it in around 10 seconds with no further input from the player if the coil is exposed. It can also get decent damage against the other bosses, but the fight is too focused on running away for it to see much use there.
The Nimbus Rod has similar use in the middle of the fight for doing some damage as a support weapon as Mechdusa passes through it, but cannot deal much damage to the coil.
The Cursed Flames, Crystal Storm, Crystal Serpent and Sky Fracture are good weapons against Skeletron Prime and The Twins.
The Golden Shower pierces multiple times, dealing high damage if hitting multiple parts at once. It can also serve as a second weapon to inflict Ichor debuff.
The Orange Zapinator has the best overall damage among mage weapons, particularly if it gets a lucky damage multiplier. However, while highly unlikely, the erratic nature of the projectile can potentially result in it killing Skeletron Prime first, making the fight much more difficult.
The Shadowflame Hex Doll needs to be close to the boss to deal good damage, but is a very high damage option if you can stay close. Make sure to have another weapon available if using this option, for Spazmatism's second phase.
Summon Weapons

The Sanguine Staff is hard to get, but the best summon for damage both for summoners and non-summoners. Use it with Firecracker.
The Blade Staff is easier to get and works well against the Destroyer coil. Use it with Cool Whip.
The Queen Spider Staff is the best sentry available at this point, most useful if you can keep the Twins and Skeletron Prime centered near your sentries.
The Barnacle Staff is useful as it is able to deal damage to airborne enemies, which Mechdusa will always be.
The Firecracker is the best option for high-damage slow minions like the Sanguine Staff.
The Cool Whip is the best option for low-damage fast minions like the Blade Staff.
Overall, the Drippler Crippler, Flint, and Clinger Staff are the best options against the Destroyer, and the Daedalus Stormbow and Dart Rifle/Dart Pistol are the best options against the Twins and Skeletron Prime. Having a way to inflict Ichor is also very useful for better damage; Flasks of Ichor and ichor ammo are options, but if inflicting ichor through a secondary weapon, Golden Shower has the best range and pierce, although it should be noted that its effectiveness will be reduced if playing on this seed, as unless playing on Journey Mode the minimum difficulty will be Expert, where The Destroyer has damage reduction against this weapon.


==== Accessories ====
Defensively, the Cobalt Shield or its upgrades provide knockback immunity. With good defense, Mechdusa will do very little damage with its projectiles, making knockback the only thing that can threaten the player. For mobility, Dunerider Boots are the main advantage for not using a mount due to their immense speed boost on a sand bridge. Wings can also work for dodging vertically, but tend to be harder to use while the Destroyer is alive. Using a mount for the fight alongside Featherfall Potions is generally the easiest way to approach the fight. These are the most important accessories to consider for the fight.

Other mobility accessories

A Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons or Green Horseshoe Balloon is the only kind of mobility accessory mounts can use, and also give a huge vertical mobility boost to wings.
Harpy, Frozen, Fairy, or Fin Wings are the best options for wings at this point, though this requires either killing Wyverns or doing fishing quests.
Frog Leg and its upgrades boost jump and flight speed to help dodge attacks.
Shield of Cthulhu provides a dash, which can let you instantly reach max speed with the Blessed Apple.
Other defensive accessories

As the fight is very long, Charm of Myths will provide a lot of extra HP.
Flesh Knuckles and their upgrades are very effective against Mechdusa's lasers, which are the hard attacks to dodge.
Worm Scarf and Brain of Confusion are less effective against lasers with good defense, but are more effective against the Prime Vice and reduces some damage from passing through the Destroyer's body. You should not be taking melee hits from Mechdusa for the most part.
Cross Necklace or its upgrade can give much more time for attacking the Destroyer's coil at the start of the fight, but is less useful after unless you are struggling with the Prime Vice.
Damage accessories

Your class Emblem is the highest damage-boosting accessory available at this point.
Magic Quiver can be useful with Unholy Arrows for boosting their velocity, but has a weak damage bonus.
Berserker's Glove can provide extra attack speed on top of defensive benefits, most useful for whips. The best melee weapons for this fight do not benefit much from melee speed.
The Squire's Shield or Apprentice's Scarf can be helpful if you can use sentries effectively. They also provided general buffs to overall summon damage, boosting the amount of damage minions provide.


==== Potions ====
Due to the high HP and low damage of Mechdusa, defensive potions are disproportionately strong. A food buff should also be used for its various benefits; the Traveling Merchant's food items, or fishing in an oasis can be a good source of Plenty Satisfied, meanwhile Exquisitely Stuffed is much harder to come by, but can be farmed by killing Eater of Souls or Crimeras for Burgers, or opening Presents during Christmas for Sugar Cookies, Christmas Pudding, and Gingerbread Cookies.

Mobility

Featherfall Potions provide a high degree of control over vertical mobility. Extremely strong with mounts, very strong otherwise. Holding up allows you to stay in the air for a long time, avoiding lasers or jumping over Mechdusa entirely. Harder to use if also using Gravitation Potion.
Gravitation Potions allow you to fall above Mechdusa onto a ceiling and run along that for better value from Dunerider Boots.
Swiftness Potions give better air speed and acceleration when not using a mount.
Survivability

Ironskin Potions and Regeneration Potions are easy to craft and extremely strong for this fight. Over a 3 minute fight, a Regeneration Potion is as impactful as a Worm Scarf, while an Ironskin Potion is effectively an extra Flesh Knuckles.
Greater Healing Potions are available now and very helpful for burst healing.
An Endurance Potion and Lifeforce Potion can be nice small bonuses for extra survivability, but can be annoying to craft.
A Heartreach Potion can help with grabbing hearts dropped by Probes.
Damage

Where appropriate for the weapon type, Ale, Archery Potions, and Magic Power Potions should always be used. Summoning Potions are also useful, but are harder to obtain.
Greater Mana Potions are available for mages now and are the best way of restoring mana.
Rage Potions and Wrath Potions are hard to farm, but are nice damage bonuses as well.


== Specific Strategies ==
The simplest approach to Mechdusa is to run away. Skeletron Prime will speed up until it catches up with its intended idle position, but while it tries to catch up, all of its limbs, the Twins, and the Destroyer will be further away from you, and projectiles will take longer to reach you due to your higher speed, giving you plenty of time to decide whether to jump or not.
The faster you move, the more difficult it is for the Prime Vice to catch up and hit you, and the slower projectiles towards you will be. However, this also makes it more likely to despawn parts of Mechdusa, preventing you from actually winning the fight. Running away also makes it disproportionately hard for melee and summon weapons to deal damage.
If using Wings, fly up and down as you run away, always sticking to the air. This will make the Destroyer more threatening, due to it being above the ground, but will make dodging the Prime Vice easy. Focus on killing the Destroyer first, and once Spazmatism reaches phase 2, use jumping to push Spazmatism higher into the air so it can't spray cursed inferno on you on the ground.
Alternatively, you can circle around Mechdusa. This keeps Skeletron Prime relatively still and makes many projectiles miss due to you moving perpendicularly to them. However, this is much harder while the Destroyer is still alive, due to its large body cutting off your path below Prime's head and the swarm of death lasers that the Destroyer can send due to you going high enough for it to rise above the floor. The Golf Cart mount can circle anyways, due to gaining iframes when dashing into the Destroyer's body, though you still need to worry about lasers.
Skeletron Prime is much slower than normal, and due to For the Worthy's effects, the Destroyer also has more segments. This means you have a long time to attack most of the Destroyer's segments at once before it uncoils from its spawn. For this, check where Mechdusa spawns on the map, and run there. The coil starts at the ground level the boss started at, but will go down if Skeletron Prime goes up, and up if Skeletron Prime goes down. This lets you attack the coil by either making it spawn on a platform, so you can drop down and attack the exposed coil below, or by lowering yourself down below where it spawned. Depending on your arena, this may require digging below a solid floor, necessitating good mining speed buffs. Skeletron Prime will start "spinning" 10 seconds after spawning, and this serves as a soft time limit, as with its extreme contact damage it will force you away from the coil at that point.
The best ways of attacking the coil are with a Drippler Crippler or Clinger Staff. The prior does much more damage, while with the latter you can place the pillar then focus on your own positioning. Drippler Crippler can kill the Destroyer in around 4 seconds on Legendary difficulty, while the Clinger Staff needs around 10. Summoners can quickly kill the coil with Sanguine Staff and Firecracker, while Rangers can kill the coil with Explosive Bullets, Sandgun, or Hellwing Bow. Killing the Destroyer early in the fight allows you to circle around the rest of Mechdusa freely, and the large amount of probes released is an easy source of hearts to heal back damage taken.


=== Despawning ===
If Skeletron Prime is more than 375 blocks distance away, it will despawn and take the other two parts with it. However, if you stay within that range, but with the Twins and Prime offscreen for 12.5 seconds, the Twins and Prime will despawn, with the Twins generally despawning first due to their limited speed. This allows you to kill only the Destroyer for post-mech gear such as Hallowed Armor or Old One's Army gear. This can sometimes happen in normal clear attempts as well if the player is moving at high speeds away for a long time, such as with Dunerider Boots or a minecart track.

title: Jungle Shrine
content:
Jungle Shrines are structures generated at world creation in random areas of the Underground Jungle. A shrine contains a single Ivy Chest, which contains a single rare Underground Jungle item, as well as a variety of other usual Underground and Cavern items. All Jungle Shrines in a world are composed entirely of either Iridescent Bricks, Mudstone Bricks, Rich Mahogany, Tin Bricks, or Gold Bricks, and contain a single placed Green Torch.
The material of the shrine can be used to determine the location of the Floating Island that contains a Shiny Red Balloon, Iridescent Bricks meaning it's probably on the far left side of the world, and Gold Bricks meaning it's likely on the far right side of the world. The random value of the material can also be used to determine other things about the world, like the depth of the Shimmer and Dungeon.
Some of the Jungle Shrine's rare items can be acquired from Jungle and Bramble Crates, which can be fished in the Jungle Biome.


== Loot ==
Each Ivy Chest will always contain one primary item, and can potentially contain multiple secondary items, or none at all. Besides one of the items listed here, they will also contain common items depending on the height they were found: Underground or Caverns.


== Notes ==
Ivy Chests can also be found at the base of Living Mahogany Trees.


== Trivia ==
Shrines may be used for housing if they are big enough and supplied with missing furniture requirements. This does not require the player to destroy existing walls or the Jungle Torch and then re-place them. Alternatively it is entirely possible to destroy the entire Shrine and then use the materials to build a house elsewhere.
Jungle Shrines can sometimes generate in a Bee Hive; sometimes even in the Jungle Temple, which might allow easy access to the Temple before obtaining a Temple Key.
Prior to  Mobile version 1.3.0.7, a larger exclusive version of the Jungle Shrine, called the Jungle Sanctum, could generate, but it has since been removed.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: The Ivy Chest now has a chance to contain a Bee Minecart.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: The Ivy Chest now has a chance to contain Flower Boots.
Desktop 1.2.4: The Ivy Chest now has a chance to contain a Fiberglass Fishing Pole.
Desktop 1.2.3: The Ivy Chest now has a chance to contain a Honey Dispenser.
Desktop 1.2: 
The Gold Bricks now have a chance to be replaced with Iridescent Bricks.
Shrines now have a chance to have the Iridescent Brick Wall background.
Gold Chests now are replaced by Ivy Chests.
Now spawns with a Green Torch.
Desktop 1.1: 
Shrines now have the Gold Brick Wall background.
Desktop 1.0.6: 
Nature's Gift no longer appears in jungle shrine chests.
Shrines now have the Mud Wall background.
Desktop 1.0.5: Normal Chests are now replaced with Gold Chests.

title: Sonar Potion
content:
The Sonar Potion is a buff potion which grants the Sonar buff when consumed. The buff displays the name of a fishing catch above a fishing pole's bobber when it receives a bite while fishing, along with a sound effect. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
The Sonar Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
In addition to displaying the regular item name text (with rarity color), the buff adds a semi-transparent color mask onto the text shown:

The Sonar Potion does not display any text when Duke Fishron is caught.
If Pickup Text is disabled in the game settings, the Sonar Potion will not display any text, but will still play the sound effect.


== Tips ==
The Sonar Potion is especially useful, allowing the player to choose what to reel in, and not waste bait on unnecessary fish as the cast can be left in the water until another fish bites at the line. This can be useful for Angler quests as well as when fishing crates. It's also handy with the Chum Bucket, as the chum goes away after 10 reel-ins, regardless of what was caught.
If the player has an ample amount of bait or/and high Fishing Power, using Sonar Potion may lead to a substantial time loss. Despite this, the potion still may prove useful if the player chooses to catch the enemies that appear during the Blood Moon.


== Trivia ==
The Sonar Potion has the same crafting recipe as the Gills Potion.
The fish detected by the Sonar Potion can be seen biting the bobber.


== History ==

Now plays a sound upon the player hooking a fish.
When a fish is detected by the Sonar Potion, it can now be seen biting the bobber.
Desktop 1.4.4: Stack limit increased from 30 to 9999.
Desktop 1.4.0.3: Fixed a bug where having pickup text on and fishing with the Sonar Potion would delete the item caught.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Sprite updated.

title: Gelatin Crystal
content:
The Gelatin Crystal is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Queen Slime when used. It can only be used in The Hallow or Underground Hallow, at any time.
Crystal Shards have a 1/50 (2%) chance to be replaced by a Gelatin Crystal upon generation. A Shard will drop a Crystal when broken.


== Notes ==
Gelatin Crystals can be detected by the Metal Detector.
The Gelatin Crystal will cycle between pink and blue, unlike Crystal Shards.
Gelatin Crystals will generate in worlds created before 1.4.0.1 and after, so it is unnecessary to create a new world to obtain them.
Unlike Plantera's Bulbs, there is no minimum distance restriction between two Gelatin Crystals. The distance is only restricted by the generation of Crystal Shards.
The Gelatin Crystal will still be identified as a Crystal Shard on the minimap.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Similar to Crystal Shards, Gelatin Crystals can be farmed quickly by placing rows of Pearlstone Blocks or Pink Ice Blocks in straight lines in the Underground Hallow.


== Trivia ==
The Gelatin Crystal periodically emtis faint light and is fully bright in the dark in its placed form. It is also fully bright in the dark when dropped or placed inside an Item Frame or an Item Flask.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Now glows in the dark in item form.
Desktop 1.4.4.8: Now grants the “Like a Boss” achievement.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Stack limit increased from 20 to 9999.
Can now be detected by the Metal Detector and its upgrades.
Can now naturally grow on Pearlsand, Hardened Pearlsand, and Pearlsandstone Blocks.

title: Mechdusa
content:
Mechdusa is a Hardmode boss exclusive to worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix seeds. Technically, it is not considered a separate boss, but is merely a combination of all three mechanical bosses. It resembles a large serpentine-like creature composed of the three bosses: The Destroyer's head is attached to Skeletron Prime's head, and The Twins are individually connected via tendrils to Skeletron Prime's eye sockets instead of to each other. There are also two extra Probes attached to The Destroyer's head.
Mechdusa can be summoned manually with Ocram's Razor anywhere at any time. In addition, if any of its constituent bosses have not yet been defeated and a Demon or Crimson Altar has been destroyed, Mechdusa has a 1/20 (5%) chance to spawn naturally at dusk (7:30 PM). If spawning this way, its arrival is announced by the status message “What a horrible night to have a curse.”
While Mechdusa is alive, its exclusive music Boss 5 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Behavior ==
Mechdusa functions as a fusion of the three mechanical bosses, inheriting all of their abilities: Skeletron Prime attacks using its arms, The Twins attack with their respective patterns, and The Destroyer and the Probes shoot lasers. Each mechanical boss has its own health bar.
Skeletron Prime acts as the "main" part of the boss, restricting the movement of the other parts. It can still charge at the player every 10 seconds, but its spiked head will not spin during this attack. Defeating Skeletron Prime separates other parts and allows them to move around freely as normal: The Twins follow the player, The Destroyer starts burrowing, and the extra two Probes start flying like normal Probes.
The Twins are initially attached to Skeletron Prime's head. When attached, they can still move freely during their charge attacks and Retinazer's laser barrage attack, but after these attacks, they will attempt to stay above Skeletron Prime again.
The Destroyer's head segment is also attached to the Skeletron Prime's head initially. The Destroyer cannot move on its own when attached, and its segments are pulled along Skeletron Prime's head instead. When attached, The Destroyer can still occasionally shoot laser barrages, and release Probes when damaged.
The two extra Probes are initially invulnerable. They will be freed and vulnerable when The Destroyer or Skeletron Prime is defeated.


== Notes ==
Mechdusa cannot trigger the Mecha Mayhem achievement.
In Zenith worlds, The Twins, all parts of Skeletron Prime, and Probes have their maximum health reduced by 20% compared to regular For the Worthy worlds.
When attached, the Destroyer's head has the same sprite as its tail segment.
Mechdusa occupies 111 NPC slots in total.
The spawning sequence of the components of Mechdusa is: Skeletron Prime's head, Retinazer, Spazmatism, The Destroyer's head segment, the two Probes (first the right one, then the left), Prime Cannon, Prime Saw, Prime Vice, Prime Laser, The Destroyer's body segments, and finally The Destroyer's tail segment.
Since Mechdusa spawns in seeds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix seeds, the bosses' pattern changes should be accounted for (scaled damage/health, size changes, etc).
In Zenith worlds, the Prime Cannon's bombs will not destroy tiles since the Celebration Mk 10 seed is active.
Defeating Mechdusa will drop all of the mechanical bosses' Treasure Bags.
The Treasure Bags and healing potions themselves drop after their respective boss is defeated. If only a single bag is needed, then it is not necessary to defeat the other bosses.
Because For the Worthy internally advances the world's difficulty by one stage, defeating Mechdusa in Classic Mode will still drop Treasure Bags.
When spawning naturally, Mechdusa spawns exactly 81 seconds after the status message has appeared. Unlike the normal mechanical bosses, being in a layer lower than the surface at that moment will not prevent the boss from spawning naturally. In singleplayer, exiting the world during the 81 seconds will still prevent it from spawning.
If The Constant special seed is also active in the world and Celebration Mk 10 is not, Mechdusa will be able to spawn naturally even after defeating one of its component bosses.
Waffle's Iron is dropped alongside the Treasure Bag of whichever component boss is defeated last.
It does not matter whether a component boss despawns; Waffle's Iron will still be dropped as long as the last remaining boss is defeated.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Make sure to be well prepared, as this boss can be quite difficult due to the limited area size in many regions.
It is advised to destroy Skeletron Prime last, as this will keep the other bosses stuck together without them flying around separately.
Since the Twins will attempt to stay above Skeletron Prime when not charging, this makes evading Spazmatism's flamethrower attack in its second phase easier.
Just like against The Destroyer, it is advised to use piercing weapons to hit all three bosses simultaneously.


== Trivia ==
Mechdusa's name is a portmanteau of mech, short for mechanical (alluding to the three bosses it is comprised of), and Medusa, a creature from Greek mythology who can petrify anything looking her in the eye.
There does not seem to be any connection between the boss and the Medusa enemy found in the Marble Cave biome.
The nature of the boss as a combination of three others is actually closer to another creature from Greek mythology, the Chimera. The Chimera is usually depicted as a lion with an extra goat's head and a snake for a tail. In general, chimera can describe anything that is made of very different parts.
Mechdusa and the Moon Lord are the only two bosses in Terraria whose summoning item's tooltips do not state the boss's name. The Celestial Sigil, the Moon Lord's summoning item, reads "Summons the Impending Doom".
Mechdusa's music is Boss 5, referencing how the namesake of its summon item, Ocram, originally used that theme.
The status message “What a horrible night to have a curse.” is a direct reference to the 1987 action role-playing game Castlevania II: Simon's Quest, where the message is displayed whenever it becomes night.
Furthermore, the status message is shared with the tooltip of the Bloody Tear.
The quote is also referenced by the painting A Horrible Night for Alchemy.
Using the status message as a world seed enables the vampirism secret seed.
Mechdusa is internally referred to as mechQueen in the game's source code.
As Mechdusa is not considered a separate boss, it does not have a separate NPC ID.
This makes Mechdusa unable to be spawned in outside of seeds combining For the Worthy and Remix.
The concept of the boss started in Re-Logic's work chat, when Redigit created a collage of the three mechanical bosses as a joke.


== History ==

Changed music track (when Otherworldly music is disabled) from Boss 1 (Otherworldly) to Boss 5. Boss 1 (Otherworldly) is now only played when Otherworldly music is enabled.
Now replaces the mechanical bosses on any seed combination containing For the Worthy and Remix, not just Zenith.

title: Flying Dutchman
content:
The Flying Dutchman is a Hardmode mini-boss that spawns during the Pirate Invasion event. The Flying Dutchman emits golden particles while hovering approximately 26 tiles above the player, and is armed with four cannons that fire explosive cannonballs toward the nearest player while occasionally spawning standard Pirate Invasion enemies that fall from the deck and onto solid ground. The boss will be defeated and drop loot upon depleting the health of all four cannons.
The Flying Dutchman does not disappear after the Pirate Invasion is over (though it will explode if it has not been engaged before the invasion ends), and defeating the Flying Dutchman will not end the invasion. Several Flying Dutchmen can appear during a single Pirate Invasion, or none at all. They only appear when the event progress has passed 50%, and where there is at least 40×30 tiles space.


== Parts ==


== Notes ==
The Flying Dutchman cannot move down through platforms.
If the player moves too far from the Flying Dutchman, it will despawn.
When spawning enemies, the Flying Dutchman cannot spawn Parrots or Pirate Captains.
Killing a Flying Dutchman adds 5.55% percent completion to the event in single player.
While the Flying Dutchman does not despawn once the invasion is over, it will continue to spawn pirates that immediately flee.


== Tips ==
Any weapons that can hit multiple targets at once are good for taking out the cannons.
Due to the way it moves and the way the cannonballs fire, it is very easy to find positions where it cannot hit the player, yet they can hit it.
Weapons that can be used in these situations include any kind of summoning weapon, the Daedalus Stormbow, the Meteor Staff, the Nimbus Rod, and the Flying Knife.
Due to the fact that they stop upon hitting a wall, and continuously spawn pirates, the Flying Dutchmen can be stopped above a half-block deep pit of lava (or other trap) and used to farm the various items pertaining to the Pirate Invasion.
Farming for the Lucky Coin, Discount Card, or Gold Ring is most efficient from killing the Flying Dutchman, rather than from common pirates. After getting event progress to 50%, one can ensure 10 Flying Dutchmen per event by getting high enough above the ground (using a small platform or flying mount), but not too high, so that spawned enemies will be in the "Active Rectangle" and will despawn after 12.5 seconds, and then spawn again. Using this method, only Flying Dutchmen and Parrots can reach the player. Parrots can be killed safely as they do not count towards event progress.
A Minecart with a sufficiently long track is useful for dodging the Flying Dutchman's attacks, and can then be attacked with ranged or magic weapons from the Minecart.


== Trivia ==
The sail gore that the Flying Dutchman is torn into upon death behaves differently from normal gore; they appear to drift gently in the wind instead of falling directly to the ground.
The real-life Flying Dutchman is a legendary ghost ship that can never make port and is doomed to sail the oceans forever, a myth that is likely to have originated in the 17th century. In ocean lore, the sight of this phantom ship is a portent of doom.
 The Bestiary entry for the Flying Dutchman: "When the pirates face strong opposition in their pillaging raids, they bring their majestic floating galleon as backup. Cannons away!"


== History ==

Now drops the Barrel Launcher with a 1/10 (10%) chance.
Health scaling in Expert Mode and higher reduced from 100% of base health to 85%.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Now has substantially increased drop rates, with a 1/15 chance to drop any of them except Coin Gun (which has a 1/50 chance).
Now guaranteed to drop 1 piece of Golden Furniture.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: Now unlocks its full Bestiary entry in one kill.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Can now drop The Dutchman.
Added two Master Mode drops, The Black Spot and Flying Dutchman Relic.

title: Mechanical Eye
content:
The Mechanical Eye is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons The Twins when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.
If the Twins have not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Eye.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
In worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix special world seeds, the Mechanical Eye is not consumable and is instead a crafting material for the Ocram's Razor, an item used to summon Mechdusa. Its tooltip also displays 'Part of a set'.
Like other mechanical boss summoning items, the Mechanical Eye can be brought to pre-Hardmode worlds and can be used to summon The Twins there.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
The Mechanical Eye is the only mechanical boss-summoning item with no visible winder.
The crafting recipe of the respective summoning items for the mechanical bosses reference themes of Darkness, Light, and Balance. The Mechanical Eye specifically references Light in that it requires only Souls of Light.
Darkness, Light, and Balance are also referenced in the crafting recipes of the Onyx Blaster, Dao of Pow, and Sky Fracture respectively.


== See also ==
Mechanical Skull and Mechanical Worm, the other mechanical boss-summoning items.

Stack limit increased from 20 to 9999.
Now used to craft Ocram's Razor.
Desktop 1.3.1: Sprite updated. Old sprite was .
Desktop 1.2.1: Drop chance reduced from 1/1000 (0.1%) to 1/2500 (0.04%).
Desktop 1.2: Now a Hardmode drop from enemies. Recipe changed.

title: Old Man
content:
The Old Man is an NPC whose primary function is to summon Skeletron, and can be found at the Dungeon's entrance. When spoken to at night, the Old Man will give the player the option to “Curse”, which summons Skeletron. When spoken to during the day, the Old Man will tell the player to return at night. He will also judge players with 300 maximum health (15 hearts) or less, or 10 defense or less as unworthy, but still allows them to summon Skeletron.
The Dungeon can be entered without defeating Skeletron, but traveling deeper than ground level within it (below zero depth) will spawn Dungeon Guardians that will most likely kill the player on contact (see Guide:Dungeon Guardian strategies).
When Skeletron is defeated, the Old Man is freed from his curse and will arrive as the Clothier (as long as a vacant house is available), in addition to allowing access to the Dungeon.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Old Man will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
The Old Man can be hurt with lava, Dart Traps, which cause normal damage and debuff effects, and explosives. He will also take damage from a rolling Boulder and Suffocation like all other NPCs. However, enemies cannot hurt him, and he does not defend himself against them (unlike other NPCs), although he will still run away from them.
If the Old Man dies or the player fails to defeat Skeletron, the Old Man will respawn at the Dungeon entrance the following day (at 6:30 AM).
When respawning in this way, the Old Man can spawn on-screen.


== Quotes ==


== Trivia ==
Other NPCs will "interact" and emote with the Old Man and engage in conversations.
He is the only NPC that will not defend himself and is not damaged by enemies. He also cannot be drowned.
He is one of only two friendly NPCs that does not have a map icon, the other being the Skeleton Merchant.
The Old Man is depicted in the painting The Cursed Man.
Upon summoning Skeletron, the Old Man dies, which makes it seem as if he turns into Skeletron, further supported by his Bestiary entry.
He can, however, respawn the following day while Skeletron is still alive but dies if Skeletron is beaten.
The Old Man's Shimmered form is reminiscent of the Shimmered form of the Clothier.
 The Bestiary entry for the Old Man: "This hapless Old Man carries the burden of a heavy curse. It's said at night he transforms into a horrific demon which guards the Dungeon."


== History ==

Desktop 1.3.0.1: Sprite updated.

title: Block Swap
content:
Block Swap is a building mechanic that allows the player to replace placed blocks, background walls, and certain types of furniture items in a single step, rather than having to remove existing tiles manually first. Block Swap can be activated or deactivated via a toggle located  to the left of the main inventory /  in the tools menu below the inventory.
When Block Swap is enabled, the player can place tiles over existing placed tiles, "swapping" the two. The previously placed tiles are freed and dropped for collection, as if they were mined normally.
Swapping blocks and furniture items still requires that the player possess a tool with sufficient pickaxe power to free the target tile, as the game performs a check for a tool of sufficient power before allowing Block Swap to occur. Additionally, certain tiles can only be swapped under certain conditions, while some can never be swapped via Block Swap at all (see Exceptions below).
Swapping background walls does not require the player to possess any hammer, and it is not affected in any way by hammers in the player's inventory.


== Exceptions ==
Some tiles can only be swapped under certain conditions, and some cannot be swapped at all.

The following types of furniture items can be swapped with an item of the same type:
Torches. They will keep their on/off state when swapped. Liquid-resistant Torches (Coral, Cursed, Ichor) that are placed inside liquids can be only swapped with other liquid-resistant Torches.
Campfires. They will keep their on/off state when swapped. Liquid-resistant Campfires (Coral, Cursed, Ichor) that are placed inside liquids can be only swapped with other liquid-resistant Campfires.
Unlocked Chests. They will keep their contents when swapped. The Dead Man's Chest will send out a wire signal when swapped.
Dressers. They will keep their contents when swapped.
All other furniture items cannot be swapped.
Ropes, Chains, and streamers cannot be swapped, except under the following conditions:
They can be swapped with platforms, as long as there is any platform directly to the left or right of them.
They can be swapped with Planter Boxes, as long as there is any Planter Box directly to the left or right of them.
They can be swapped with any tracks (Minecart Track, Booster Track, Pressure Plate Track), as long as there is any track directly to the left or right of them.
When placing tracks in this way, the resulting track will always be a regular Minecart Track.
If the player does not have a tool with at least 110% pickaxe power in their inventory (i.e., no Cobalt Pickaxe or better), then gravity-affected blocks can only be swapped out from the top-most block and downwards. With a tool that has at least 110% pickaxe power, gravity-affected blocks can be swapped freely.
Gravity-affected blocks can always be swapped freely with each other, regardless of pickaxe power.
Hive blocks can be swapped in by using a Hive Wand, but cannot be swapped out for other blocks.
Inactive Stone Blocks cannot be swapped out. Actuated Stone Blocks can be still swapped out, however, like other actuated blocks.
Platforms and Planter Boxes that intersect the player's hitbox can only be swapped with other platforms or Planter Boxes, not for any other block.
Trees, cacti, Fallen Logs, and the blocks supporting them cannot be swapped.
Any type of grass on Dirt (including Corruption, Crimson, Hallowed, and mowed variants) cannot be swapped with Dirt Blocks or a different type of grass.
Likewise, any type of grass on Mud (such as Mushroom grass, Jungle grass, and infected variants) cannot be swapped with Mud Blocks or a different type of grass.
Any type of moss on Stone Blocks cannot be swapped with Stone Blocks or a different type of moss.
Likewise, any type of moss on Gray Bricks cannot be swapped with Gray Bricks or a different type of moss.
Ash grass cannot be swapped with Ash Blocks.
Bubbles, Hellstone, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, Smoke Blocks, Living Fire Blocks, Logic Sensors, and temporary Ice Blocks placed by the Ice Rod cannot be swapped out.
Grates with any liquids inside them cannot be swapped.
Blocks in front of Unbreakable Walls cannot be swapped.
If the For the Worthy seed is enabled, Crispy Honey Blocks cannot be swapped out.


=== Background walls ===
Some background walls cannot be swapped.

Single floating walls, i.e., walls that are not connected to other walls or blocks, cannot be swapped.
Similar to when breaking them normally, unsafe walls cannot be swapped out if they are not directly connected to empty air or to any safe walls.
Unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls cannot be swapped out before defeating Skeletron.
Unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Walls cannot be swapped out before defeating Golem.
Unbreakable Walls cannot be swapped out.


== Cooldown ==
When swapping blocks (and furniture items), the "best" pickaxe or drill in the player's inventory is used, i.e., the one with the highest pickaxe power. If multiple items in the player's inventory have equal pickaxe power, the topmost item is prioritized, and then the leftmost item. After attempting to swap a block, there is a cooldown before the player can attempt again, depending on whether enough damage has been dealt to the block to break it or not (see Pickaxe power for more details):

If not enough damage is dealt to the block to break it, the cooldown is equal to the best pickaxe's/drill's mining speed after speed modifiers and mining speed bonuses are applied (see Tool speed for more details).
If enough damage is dealt to the block to break and replace it, the cooldown is equal to the best pickaxe's/drill's mining speed after speed modifiers and mining speed bonuses are applied, plus the use time of player's selected block after block placement speed bonuses are applied (see Placement speed for more details). Note that the base use time of blocks is 10 (Very fast), and the use time stat displayed for blocks on the wiki actually represents a different stat called use animation.
This means drills can benefit from mining speed bonuses when used for Block Swap, despite not benefiting from them otherwise.
If the For the Worthy seed is enabled, the damage dealt to the blocks is doubled.
When swapping walls, the wall is simply broken and replaced in a single hit, with the cooldown afterwards being equal to the use time of the player's selected wall after wall placement speed bonuses are applied. Note that the base use time of walls is 7 (Insanely fast), and the use time stat displayed for walls on the wiki actually represents a different stat called use animation.


== Notes ==
Paint and coating on the existing tiles will be removed upon swapping.
Swapping an inactive actuated block will cause the newly placed block to remain inactive.
Swapping a sloped tile will cause the newly placed tile to keep the slope.


== Tips ==
Block Swap can be used to extract ore veins that are hanging over a cliff and would cause the player to fall when broken.
This does not grant the Ooo! Shiny! achievement.
Chlorophyte Ore can be swapped with Mud Blocks to collect the Chlorophyte while allowing it to grow back.
This does not grant the Photosynthesis achievement.
Blocks beneath a Demon Altar or Crimson Altar can be swapped without destroying the altar.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Fixed being able to Block Swap tiles with Unbreakable Wall behind it.
Desktop 1.4.5.1: Swapping a sloped block with a platform will now keep the slope again.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Placement speed bonuses now apply when using Block Swap.
The cooldown after fully swapping a block is now based on both the best pickaxe's/drill's tool speed and the selected block's use time, instead of just the block's use time.
Players can now swap blocks that are touching lava.
Swapping a sloped block with a platform will now clear the slope.
Grates with liquid in them can no longer be swapped.
Players can now swap Ropes with Planter Boxes if there is already a Planter Box to the side of the Rope.
The passive mining boost in the For the Worthy seed now also applies when using Block Swap.
Campfires and Torches are now properly limited to their water-resistant variants when swapping them underwater.
Fixed being able to swap platforms with solid blocks that players are standing in.
Fixed certain hanging objects like Boulder Statues not breaking when swapping their anchor blocks with platforms.
Fixed Christmas Trees not properly breaking objects when placed by Block Swap.
Fixed auto-paint and auto-actuation failing when using Block Swap to swap similar items, such as one Chest with another.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Torches and Campfires can now be swapped.
Ropes can now be swapped with platforms or Minecart Tracks if there is already a platform/Minecart Track to the side of the Rope.
Desktop 1.4.1: Gravity-affected blocks can now be swapped out from the topmost tile downwards. With a high enough pickaxe power, they can be swapped anywhere like other blocks.
Desktop 1.4.0.4: Fixed a bug where swapped blocks maintained their cracked texture.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced with changes from Desktop 1.4.0.4.

title: Flask of Ichor
content:
The Flask of Ichor is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips to inflict the Ichor debuff for 10–19 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Ichor cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Tips ==
The Flask of Ichor will make melee weapons and whips glow when they are used. In combination with yoyos or whips, it can be a good lighting source in dark areas.
The light being emitted from the weapon provides the same amount of light as the Ultrabright Torch.
The Flask of Ichor offers the greatest DPS increase of any flask as long as the player deals damage at least 4 times per second.

title: Piece of Moon Squid
content:
The Piece of Moon Squid is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pet-summoning item that spawns a Moonling, which resembles the Moon Lord's head, that follows the player. The Piece of Moon Squid has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord in Master Mode.


== Trivia ==
The Piece of Moon Squid's tooltip, "'The forbidden calamari.'", is likely a reference to a common internet meme, where some form of an object similar to food, which in reality is not edible, is nicknamed "Forbidden <food>", for example, sea glass being referred to as "forbidden fruit snacks". Calamari is fried squid, referring to the Moon Lord's cephalopodic appearance.
The Moonling itself marginally resembles the Ancient Vision, an enemy summoned by the Lunatic Cultist if the player attacks a duplicate of the Lunatic Cultist while the Phantasm Dragon is still alive.
The buff tooltip, "A friend from beyond", is a reference to the 1920 short story "From Beyond" by American writer H.P. Lovecraft, which is the story of a man who witnesses alien creatures in an alternate dimension. The Moon Lord, which the Piece of Moon Squid drops from, also happens to be a reference to H.P. Lovecraft – this time, the cosmic entity Cthulhu, a fictional character Lovecraft created.

title: The Constant
content:
The Constant is a special world seed. It is a crossover with Klei Entertainment's Don't Starve Together.


== World generation changes ==


=== Surface ===
Marble patches occasionally spawn throughout the world on the surface with a few white-painted statues.
Spider Nests or small patches of Spider Walls often generate at or near the surface.


=== Underground ===
The world generates with "wavy caves", which travel up and down in sharp zig-zag patterns, or travel diagonally downwards.
Lead Ore and Platinum Ore will never generate (i.e. only Iron and Gold Ore will appear in Constant worlds).


== Player ==
The player has a hunger system, which goes down over time and can be increased by consuming food items. When the player's current hunger level decreases, they will emote.
The player's initial hunger starts at Peckish, which lasts 5 minutes. After that, the player becomes Hungry, which lasts 5 minutes and lowers the player's stats to be similar to Weak.
Finally, the player starts Starving, which further lowers the player's stats and makes the player lose health equal to 2% of their max health per second indefinitely.
Consuming any food immediately replaces the hunger debuffs with the respective Well Fed buff. After the buff ends, the player gets the Peckish debuff, and the cycle continues.
The player gains a custom hurt sound based on Don't Starve-related characters.
Male characters' hurt sound is the same as Wilson's:   
Female characters' hurt sound is the same as Willow's:   


== Other changes ==

The world has a constant sepia screen shader which significantly darkens the world. This effect can also be seen when generating the world.
The shader will be disabled if the player equips the Radio Thing.
The shader will also not work under the Retro or Trippy lighting modes.
It will be pitch dark on the surface during normal nights. When a New Moon, a Full Moon, or a Blood Moon occurs, the player will be able to see things normally on the surface.
When the player enters completely dark areas, the status message “It is very dark...you feel in danger...” will be displayed after 1 second, and after another 2 seconds, (3 seconds in total after entering the dark area), the player will take 250 damage. Afterwards, the player will continue to take 250 damage per each additional second spent in the darkness. This continuous damage will last until the player is illuminated by any type of light or dies. When the player gets illuminated, they will stop receiving damage from darkness, the 3-second damage timer will be reset, and the status message “The danger of the dark has passed.” will be displayed. Dying from darkness will display the following unique death message: “<Player name> was killed by something in the dark!”
The 250 damage is unaffected by random damage variance, but can be still reduced by the player's defense and damage reduction normally. It can be also avoided through dodges, invincibility frames, or the Shimmering debuff.
Additionally, the player becomes immune to darkness damage when the game is unfocused, or when the camera is being moved through Golf, FPV Goggles, Binoculars, Sniper Rifle, or Rifle Scope (or upgrades).
If For the Worthy seed is enabled, the respective status messages for darkness damage will not be displayed.
Cacti will hurt the player when touched or chopped, with a base damage of 6.
Torches, Campfires, Tiki Torches, and Lamps exposed to the sky will be "extinguished" when it rains.
Torch and Campfire variants which can be placed in water (i.e., the Coral, Cursed Flame, and Ichor varieties) will never be extinguished.
Other pieces of furniture that produce light and/or seem to be fire-based, like Candles, Candelabras, Furnaces, Fireplaces, Lamp Posts, etc., will also remain lit.
Don't Starve items will have their drop rate increased, these being the Ham Bat, the Bat Bat, Monster Meat, the Tentacle Spike, and the Glommer's Flower. Abigail's Flower has a higher spawn chance as well.
The paintings related to Don't Starve that are sold by the Traveling Merchant will be more common.
In Expert worlds, Wall Creepers and Black Recluses saved on the minimap can always respawn.
Rare clouds in the background are more common.
Of these rare clouds, Don't Starve-related clouds are more common.


== Tips ==

Early options for food include regular Mushrooms, shaking trees, converting Vertebrae or Rotten Chunks into Monster Lasagna, and getting the Merchant to move in to buy a Bug Net (or to buy Marshmallows if he is in a Snow biome).
The Mining Helmet, Jellyfish Necklace and Magiluminescence can help keep the darkness away before light pets are found.
By using explosives, the player can harvest Cacti without taking damage.
To avoid damage from cacti while retaining Desert enemy spawns, place platforms 2 tiles above the Sand. This will prevent cacti from growing, but still allow enemies to spawn.


== Trivia ==
"The Constant" directly references the world with the same name in Don't Starve.
Several world generation changes in the Constant seed recreate specific Set Pieces or items in Don't Starve:
The Marble patches recreate the Marble Sculptures set piece.
The Spider Caves on the surface recreate Spider Dens.
Several game mechanics in The Constant seed are based on mechanics in Don't Starve, these include:
The shader is based on the shader effect in Don't Starve.
A world can only have Iron and Gold Ores due to the fact that only Iron Ore and Gold Nuggets exist in Don't Starve.
The hunger mechanic is directly based on Don't Starve's Hunger mechanic.
In Don't Starve, the player is also able to see things normally during Full Moon nights.
However, the player cannot see things during New Moons in Don't Starve, which is not the case in Terraria.
The mechanic of players getting damaged in completely dark areas is based on a similar mechanic of survivors being attacked by Charlie in complete darkness.
The player getting damaged by Cacti is based on Don't Starve's Cactus, which damages the player by 6 health when harvesting it.
Exposed Torches and Campfires extinguish when Rain starts, as in Don't Starve, Rain will make Torches and Campfires burn out faster.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.4: The Constant's filter is now correctly hidden when combined with Skyblock.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
The Constant's filter is now hidden when mixed with other world seeds.
Added a sound effect for when the player is starving on The Constant worlds.
Desktop 1.4.4.6: Cacti are now highlighted by Dangersense Potions on Constant Seeds.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Darkness damage increased from 50 to 250, and the time before being hurt decreased from 8 to 4 seconds.
Eating regular Mushrooms will reset hunger back to full duration Peckish if the player is Peckish, Hungry, or Starving.
Desktop 1.4.3: Introduced.

title: Title messages
content:
A title message is a mock slogan displayed as Terraria's window title at the top of the game window. These messages often reference popular culture or other video games. A title message is chosen at random from the list below each time the game is started, and remains unchanged until either the game is exited completely and restarted, or a language button in the language selection menu is clicked, at which point a new message is randomly chosen.
A title message can only be displayed if Terraria's current settings allow a title bar to be present on Terraria's game window. When the game is set to full-screen, or "Borderless Window" mode is enabled (Settings → Video → Resolution), no title will be displayed normally. The title message will always be visible as part of the process collection in the Windows "Task Switcher" Alt+↹ Tab.
The current title message appears in the top-left corner of the game window on Windows 7, Windows 10, and Windows 11. It appears in the top-middle of the game window on Windows 8 and 8.1, macOS, and Ubuntu.
There are 68 different title messages.


== Messages ==


== Notes ==
If the game is in full-screen mode, the title message can generally still be seen by switching to another window to display the task bar, then hovering over Terraria's task bar icon to display a window preview.
In 1.4.0.1, the message "Also try Edge of Space!" was replaced with "Also try Breath of the Wild!". This may have been because in the years since 1.3.0.1's release in 2015, Edge of Space was perceived by many players to have been abandoned/unfinished by its developers, leading to it attaining a "Mostly Negative" rating on Steam.

title: Lunar Events
content:
The Lunar Events are a series of four late-Hardmode events initiated by defeating the Lunatic Cultist boss. Once the boss is defeated, four different sections of the world each show a large moon in their backgrounds and spawn several unique enemies at high spawn rates, with one corresponding Celestial Pillar in each. These areas can be found on the minimap via icons that represent each of their Celestial Pillars.
Defeating a Celestial Pillar reverts an area back to normal. In order to damage a pillar, one must first kill 100 enemies from within its section, which removes the shield that protects the pillar and makes it vulnerable to attacks.
Defeating all four Celestial Pillars triggers the status message "Impending doom approaches...", signifying that the Moon Lord, Terraria's final boss, is about to spawn. It spawns one minute after the message appears.
After defeating the Moon Lord for the first time, only 50 enemies will need to be defeated to remove the shields protecting the pillars.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
The defeat of a pillar is announced in a status message:
"Your mind goes numb..." – first pillar defeated
"You are overwhelmed with pain..." – second pillar defeated
"Otherworldly voices linger around you..." – third pillar defeated
"Impending doom approaches..." – fourth pillar defeated
Celestial creatures do not drop coins, even with the Lucky Coin (or its derivatives) equipped. They also do not drop Presents during Christmas, Goodie Bags during Halloween, or Biome Keys.
In a singleplayer world, the Celestial Pillars will not disappear when the player dies or exits Terraria completely. The pillars must be destroyed in the world, otherwise they will stay in the world indefinitely.
The Moon Lord may not be summoned via the Celestial Sigil while the pillars are still active.
Exiting the world after the "Impending doom approaches..." status message has appeared will cancel the event and prevent the Moon Lord from spawning.
Most other in-game events cannot naturally occur while the Lunar Events are active. This includes the Blood Moon, Goblin Army, Pirate Invasion, and Solar Eclipse. However, Slime Rain can still occur, and the Traveling Merchant and other NPCs can spawn as usual.
Like with all other events, sleeping is disabled while the Lunar Events are active.


== Tips ==

It is a good idea to defeat the pillar of the player's preferred class first, as that pillar will provide the most effective weaponry for the rest.
It can be helpful to launch the Lunar Events even if the player does not have the means to survive them fully yet as gradually defeating pillars grants access to stronger equipment. Even if the fight against the Moon Lord is lost, the player will be much better prepared than before.
Because neither sentries nor the pillars despawn or leave when the player dies or leaves, as enemies do, sentries can continue attacking a pillar with no players nearby, as long as the shield is already gone.
Flying in and out of the celestial area, letting only a limited number of enemies spawn at a time, can prevent getting overwhelmed. The shield will still be shattered eventually. Once it is broken, the pillar can be attacked from safe distance, e.g., from above (with any suitable ranged weapon or melee projectile) or from the side (with a long-lasting, gravity-unaffected projectile such as the Influx Waver's Influx Waver projectile). Flying mounts or the Static Hook can be useful for hovering mid-air.
Setting up Teleporters, Pylons, or acquiring the Magic Conch before starting can immensely speed up the fight. Though it is very difficult to determine exactly where the pillars will spawn, the two closest ones will be around one-fifth of the map away from the center, and the furthest about three-fifths. On subsequent fights, the pillars will spawn in approximately the same locations as before, though which pillar is where may be randomized.


== Trivia ==
The music played during the Lunar Events was made available as part of the second Terraria Soundtrack volume under the title "Lunar Boss" despite not being implemented in the game.
This is one of the only two events in the game whose enemies do not drop coins, along with the Old One's Army.
The Lunar Events are one of two combat-focused events that cannot be summoned via an item, the other being the Martian Madness.
The Lunar Events are also known as Lunar Apocalypse and Lunar Invasion.

title: Underground Corruption
content:
The Underground Corruption is a biome. It is the underground version of the surface-level Corruption, appearing at and below the cavern layer. Just like the surface Corruption, it is mainly composed of Ebonstone which spreads to nearby tiles. Although it is available in pre-Hardmode, most of its exclusive contents will only appear during Hardmode. After the Wall of Flesh is defeated for the first time, a diagonal stripe of Corruption is generated, creating additional Underground Corruption biome. 
The Underground Corruption does not suppress the spawn of other underground and cavern enemies. During Hardmode, all enemies killed in the Underground Corruption have a 1/5 (20%) / 9/25 (36%) chance to drop a Soul of Night.
Note: Most characteristics of the surface Corruption also apply to the Underground Corruption. See The Corruption for more extensive information.

== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Added Otherworldly Underground Corruption track from the canceled Terraria: Otherworld.
Reduced the drop rate of Souls of Night in Expert Mode from 9/25 (36%) to 1/5 (20%), the same as in Classic Mode. Internally, the elevated drop rate used to be implemented via an extra, independent 1/5 (20%) drop chance exclusive to Expert Mode, which was now removed.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Corruption chasms that extend into the underground layer are now classified as the Underground Corruption, complete with music. Unique enemies will not spawn pre-hardmode.
