title: Guide:Practical tips
content:
There are many things in Terraria that are not evident from the get-go, and many other things that a player would do differently on their future playthroughs. It is true that much of the joy lies in exploring, but some helpful advice is in order.


== Settings and controls ==
The settings and game controls contain several features that improve the player's quality of life. Some notable ones are:

(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Right-clicking any enemy with a summon weapon will cause your minions to target it.
 Take advantage of your mouse's middle and side buttons by rebinding your game controls.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Autofire can be enabled for all weapons in the settings.
The cursor modes, Auto Select and Smart Cursor, are incredibly helpful to make using tools and placing blocks more convenient (e.g. automatically switching to an axe when hovering a tree, or switching to a torch when pointing at an empty space).
, each hotbar slot has a key binding, and it can be worth changing these in settings to keys that are easier to reach in a pinch.
In the settings, there is an option called "Autopause". This causes the game to pause while the player is interacting with any inventory.


== Exploration and travel ==
It can be more time-efficient to explore the surface for Mountain Caves rather than digging a hellevator immediately. Mountain Caves contain large quantities of pots and chests, and will generally lead to the Underground and Cavern layers. Life Crystals are also more common in these large caves.
Mountain Caves that generate in the evil biomes often have Shadow Orbs or Crimson Hearts exposed, saving the player from having to use Bombs.
On flat open areas, hooks can be used to pull a player across the ground, by shooting it at the ground ahead and then releasing it while being pulled in. This allows the various Boots to get to full speed without having to build up beforehand.
It can be easier to craft a gem hook than the Grappling Hook.
There are various items and accessories that can affect movement speed:
Boots boost run speed, and various upgrades provide a double-jump among environmental immunities like water walking or lava immunity.
Amphibian Boots are best suited for combat as they reduce fall damage and boost wing speeds, while Terraspark Boots and its components are suitable for exploration due to their environment immunities.
Swiftness Potions are easy to obtain and sharply increase movement speed for a limited time.
The Magiluminescence boosts movement speed and acceleration while also providing a moderate amount light around the player to help when in caves.
Sunflowers increase movement speed whilst in their vicinity, and the Slice of Cake increases movement speed for two minutes when used.
Asphalt Blocks become available in Hardmode, dramatically increasing the player's speed when running across them.
Gravitation Potions allow you to easily explore Floating Islands. With practice, they can eliminate the need for an arena.
A Featherfall Potion or an Umbrella effectively extends flight time by causing players to fall slower. This will also eliminate all fall damage risk from using a Gravitation Potion.
The Cloud in a Bottle and its variants provide a double-jump. See this page for a comparison.
The ascent speed of wings can be greatly increased by equipping a Frog Leg. Balloon accessories provide a similar, though less dramatic bonus.
The Magic Conch teleports you to either Ocean, and the Demon Conch to The Underworld.
Minecarts can also be used to travel faster, although they are restricted to Minecart Tracks. See below for more information.
When flying with wings, the Ice Rod can create blocks mid-air which can then be used to reset your flight duration.


=== Skybridge ===
A skybridge or sky bridge is a long structure built high in the sky, usually with only with a single layer of blocks or platforms. They often span most of the world and are often built just below the space layer to prevent Harpies and Wyverns from spawning. Skybridges can be used for travel, as a boss arena, and to intercept Fallen Stars and coins (during coin rain) for easy collection. Additionally, artifical biomes and even towns can be created in the sky as an isolated place to farm enemies and events.
Various blocks are suitable for building a skybridge:

Dirt Blocks are abundant and allow herbs and Strange Plants to grow on the skybridge.
Platforms are useful for fighting bosses, maximizing mobility in all directions and leaving a clear line of fire to the boss.
Planter Boxes function similar to platforms and can be used to grow herbs.
Asphalt Blocks in Hardmode provide a large boost to movement speed.
Ice Blocks and Sand Blocks are a pre-Hardmode substitute if the player equips Ice Skates or Dunerider Boots respectively.
Minecart Tracks provide very high movement speed and maintain the player's momentum. They do not obstruct Fallen Stars or other items, but platforms or blocks can be placed below or above the minecart track to collect items.
Frozen Slime Blocks maintain the player's momentum, similar to a minecart track.
However, Roller Skates provide the same functionality on any block type (including minecart tracks!) and have an additional speed boost.
Conveyor Belts and chests connected with timers can be used to automatically farm Fallen Stars. Due to their slow speed, not all Fallen Stars will reach the end of the belt in time to be collected (especially on larger worlds). A conveyor belt spanning an entire large world and ending at the world center should collect about 60% of Fallen Stars that fall on a given night.
Aetherium Platforms can be placed above Conveyor Belts to provide a static walking surface while still allowing items to pass through to the belt. Another option is Minecart Tracks.


=== Subway ===
A subway is a long horizontal shaft dug underground. Like skybridges, it can be floored with Asphalt or Minecart Tracks. The Digging Molecart is perfect for digging subways as it automatically mines blocks and places tracks.
They can double as a barrier to prevent the spread of Evil or Hallowed biomes: in order to work as one, it must be at least 7 blocks tall, and must not contain any Corruptible soil.


=== Hellbridge ===
A hellbridge is a long row of blocks, platforms, or minecart tracks built in The Underworld, much like a skybridge. It can be used to avoid lava, farm enemies, and fight the Wall of Flesh, and it can help to catch Voodoo Dolls before they drop in lava.
Much like a skybridge, various blocks are suitable for building a skybridge. In particular:

Ash Blocks are abundant and allow Fireblossoms and Strange Plants to grow on the skybridge.
Obsidian, Stone, and Ash Wood Platforms can touch lava without being destroyed. This is especially noteworthy in Expert Mode, where Lava Slimes spawn a tile of lava on death.
Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone can create artificial evil or Hallow biomes to farm Souls of Night, Souls of Light, and biome-specific Mimics in Hardmode.


=== Lava ocean ===
An alternative to a hellbridge is flattening and filling the Underworld with lava (eg: with Sticky Bombs and Lava Bombs), then using Lava Waders or a Lava Shark Mount to travel, farm enemies, and fight the Wall of Flesh. But care must be taken to collect drops, especially Voodoo Dolls, before they fall in lava.


=== Hellevator ===
A hellevator is a vertical shaft of mined blocks that generally extends all the way from the surface to The Underworld. Besides easy access to The Underworld, it can serve as a good place to look for Hardmode ores when they spawn. The following are tips when creating and using a hellevator:

Explosives and Mining Potions speed up the process greatly. Scarab Bombs are especially useful when thrown directly below the player.
Gills Potions will help when digging through water, while Obsidian Skin Potions do the same for lava.
Avoid building the hellevator near the Jungle; you may reach the Jungle Temple, which is made of blocks that cannot be mined until much later.
Riding the Slime Mount greatly increases falling speed, which reduces travel time.
If the player has been to the Underground Desert, Digtoise can be used to mine the hellavator while the player does something else.
Fall damage can be negated in the following ways:
A small pool of water just above the Underworld, where it will not evaporate. Alternatively, honey, Pink Slime Blocks or Clouds can also be used, and do not evaporate.
A line of Rope to catch onto.
The Lucky Horseshoe and wings completely negate fall damage.
The Cloud in a Bottle, Flying Carpet, Rocket Boots, or any hook can be engaged just before landing.
The Featherfall Potion. Holding ▼ Down while falling will accelerate the fall to the normal speed. The Umbrella can be used to the same effect.
Using Shoe Spikes and/or Climbing Claws will allow you to slide down walls.
The Ram Rune ground pound can be used to accelerate downward quickly and prevents fall damage.
The Cobalt Shield will prevent knockback by any enemies who find their way into the shaft through side entrances.
Similar to the subway, the hellevator can also be incorporated as part of your defense against the spread of the Evil or Hallow biomes. In this case, the hellevator must be at least 3 blocks wide to prevent the biomes from spreading through it.


=== Teleporters ===

Teleporters are among the fastest forms of travel, but also the one of the most expensive and time-consuming, as they require a large amount of Wire for greater distances.
To use, you must wire two Teleporters together and then trigger them with a signal, such as that from a Pressure Plate or Switch. With one wire color, each end of a Teleporter pad can be wired to one destination each, making two possible destinations (each must have its own triggering mechanism). Using all four wire colors, each end of the Teleporter can be wired to four destinations each, for a total of eight possible destinations (two red, two blue, two green, and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) two yellow).
The Grand Design(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is incredibly helpful when wiring Teleporters at long distances, as it can instantly place Wire over the world.


=== Spawn ===
The player's spawn point can also facilitate travel. There are numerous methods to quickly teleport to your current spawn (Recall Potions, Magic Mirror and its upgrades, or even just exiting the world), and Potion of Return(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) even allows two-way travel. Therefore, it is advantageous to place your spawn point near the places you visit most often, and any transportation network you build should be connected to it as well.
Furthermore, it is possible to arrange two-way teleportation between a custom-made spawn point (a clicked-on bed in a valid house) and the world spawn. To do so, install a Weighted Pressure Plate in the house so that stepping on it will actuate part of the wall, making the house (and the spawn point) invalid. (An example.) Then, using a Magic Mirror or a similar item while standing on the pressure plate will teleport you to the world spawn, while using it anywhere else will teleport you to the bed.  If your main base is at the world spawn, this allows easily teleporting between it and the currently explored area.


=== Minecarts ===


==== Basics ====
There are 3 track components:

Minecart Track, made with Iron Bars and Wood at an Anvil.
Booster Track, purchased from the Mechanic for 50 Silver each. Direction of boost can be switched using Mechanisms or a Hammer. Mainly used to instantly accelerate or decelerate a Minecart.
Pressure Plate Track, made out of a regular Track segment, and a Pressure Plate. They can only be placed horizontally.
Tracks can be laid in the air without support. You can grapple to them, but you will pass through them when walking or flying normally.


==== Behavior ====
Hammering the rails at the end of a track changes its behavior:

Closed: The default option, stops the Minecart in place.
Bumper: It reverses the travel direction.
Open: It's an unprotected track, causing the Minecart to fall.
When two tracks intersect it is possible to switch branch by using a Hammer or a wire signal. Hammering or signaling an intersection repeatedly will cycle through the possible branches of the intersection. Using a Hammer eventually disconnects the intersection, although this will not happen with a wire signal.
Holding down ▲ Up or ▼ Down button will force the Minecart to take the upper or lower path of a switch track regardless of the current state. This allows a branching rail network to be easily navigated.


==== Advanced Rail systems ====
Pressure Plate Tracks only work on horizontal tracks, and will cause a cart to derail if they are laid on a diagonal section. If you need to place a Pressure Plate on a diagonal track, place a Platform in the air next to the track on the side you will pass by, and put a regular Pressure Plate on top of it.
You can make a safe track section that leaves a house by putting it in its own room with a door made with Actuated blocks triggered by Pressure Plate Tracks. However, the space left by the Minecart Track will make the house unsuitable for NPCs.
On a Track intersection, you can use a Switch or Lever to cycle through the different branches. Additionally, Colored Torches can be used to indicate the branch that is currently active.
To make a single Bumper end Track that can send you both up and down without manual input, you will need to build two rows of 3 Rail tracks on top of each other, and then hammer each one a certain amount of times (see picture)
Open ended tracks can be hammered upwards to make jumps. With trial and error, many different jumps can be chained together for much faster travel. You can also hold an Umbrella to greatly extend the distance gained from jumps.

		
		
		


=== Pylons ===
Pylons are purchased from NPCs for 10 Gold each. They provide a point-to-point network across every major biome. Pylons have many advantages as well as disadvantages:
Advantages:

They do not require any wiring
They can be obtained prior to defeating any boss
They allow instant travel
Disadvantages:

They require at least 2 NPCs nearby to be functional
There can only be one of each type per world.


=== Hoiks ===
Hoiks are exploits in which sloped blocks are used for fast travel. This occurs when a character sprite shares space with a sloped block: The character is immediately displaced a couple of tiles in a predictable direction.
By chaining Hoiks together with a line of strategically placed shaped blocks, entities can be moved rapidly in any direction. Hoiks have a horizontal travel speed of 60 to 120 tiles per second, while vertical travel speed is 180 tiles per second.


== Building ==

Building barebones, speedrun-style houses can save time at the start, but this may become a problem quickly. Using platforms to meet the enclosed room requirement will leave your NPCs vulnerable to enemies that fly and/or have ranged attacks, and will likely result in time wasted waiting for them to respawn. Additionally, towns with more than three NPCs living in them will lower their happiness, causing everything to become more expensive. Instead, spread your NPCs out, preferably putting them near their preferred NPCs and biomes.
Doors can be very unsafe due to NPCs opening them freely, and certain enemies can open doors during a Blood Moon. Stacking furniture against the doors will keep them from opening inwards.
Forgoing doors entirely in favor of a roof platform entrance, paired with hoiks that serve as a one-way exit that also allows you to shoot projectiles through.
It is a good idea to raise your entrance off the ground, accessible by Rope. This can be paired with a trench beneath the base to catch enemies, which can also be filled with lava.
Evil biomes should be contained to prevent damage to the world and NPC housing. Sunflowers are an easy way to seal off evil biomes on the surface, but will not be effective in Hardmode. See Guide:Maintaining world purity for more tips.
The Clentaminator can be used to easily purify blocks. Additionally, Dynamite can be used to create a wide gap preventing evil spread.


== Survival ==
If you have a weak weapon, taking your time to kill enemies is more dangerous than ignoring them and moving on. More enemies will spawn while you finish one off, and you may become overwhelmed.
Although using five Life Crystals will allow the Eye of Cthulhu and Goblin Army to start spawning, the benefit of the extra health far outweighs the consequences. The Eye of Cthulhu can be avoided by simply exiting and rejoining the world, and the Goblin Army can be avoided by not breaking any Shadow Orb/Crimson Hearts. The player can also dig trenches to collect the Goblins and kill them faster. Furthermore, having the Goblin Tinkerer is much better than delaying it.
Exiting and rejoining the world will put you at spawn and remove all enemies and bosses, but will also remove any dropped items.
Keep Recall Potions in your hotbar. Although Magic Mirrors are non-consumable, they are noticeably slower.
In Hardcore, Recall Potions become essentially necessary.
Blocks should be used to trap enemies, box yourself in, and seal off tunnels and your hellevator.
Yoyos and wall-piercing weapons can attack through blocks.
Towns, Peace Candles, and background walls are common ways to reduce enemy spawns.
Keep the Nurse handy for healing.
Drinking a Dangersense Potion or holding a trap item will highlight traps.
Fishing is a low-risk activity that grants a multitude of useful items throughout game progression, namely crates.
Fishing for crates, albeit time-consuming, is also much safer than breaking altars, which risk Pirate Invasions and random mechanical boss spawns.
Be mindful of the height at which Wyverns start spawning when building an arena for the mechanical bosses.
In the later game, weak bosses like Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned and killed for an easy supply of hearts before fighting another boss.
The Queen Bee can be used for this purpose while fighting Plantera.
You can cover lava to prevent Voodoo Demons accidentally spawning the Wall of Flesh.


== Items ==
Platforms can be placed on trees, allowing a quick way to escape enemies.
Trees can be punched (with an axe) to drop food, among other items. This is a good side task while exploring in the early game.
After the player uses the maximum number of Life Crystals, the remainder can be used to craft Heart Lanterns.
Additionally, collecting Life Crystals wherever found allows for the Metal Detector to detect other, potentially more useful, items.
White String is very cheap to craft (at only 30 Cobwebs) and can potentially grant various stat boosts via modifiers.
Possibly the most potent of these is Warding, which grants 4 defense outright, which is more than what many early-game armor pieces offer.
The cheapest way of obtaining food is through fishing, as Bass can be cooked into Blackened Fish or Cooked Fish, both of which offer the minor food buff.
Many of the catches from fishing can also be prepared to give the second-best food buff. If trying to fish solely for this reason, the Desert is usually the best biome to do this in.
Alternately, food can be grown and crafted into Pumpkin Pies, which are easy to obtain and grants the minor food buff. Pumpkin Seeds can be purchased from the Dryad.
Once twenty Life Fruits and an Aegis Fruit have been consumed, additional Life Fruits can be used to craft Jungle Juice, which is the best healing potion available pre-Cultist.
Shimmer is a powerful resource that can be found in the Aether. It can be used to de-craft items and endlessly reroll Reforges without any cost for crafted equipments, tools, or weapons. Shimmer can also be used to create permanent booster items.
Farming Chlorophyte Ore is generally slower than mining for it, but it remains helpful if you require large amounts of it in the long term, such as creating ammunition or for building.
The Shellphone and Ankh Shield seem like powerful items, but in reality they save only a few slots: most of the Shellphone's information is useless for normal gameplay, and the Ankh Shield's debuff immunities are only helpful in select scenarios.
The Rod of Discord similarly has not enough benefit for its investment; one is practically required to create a farm for it, and the player can become overreliant on it (although using it is ultimately up to one's choice).
When farming Souls of Night or Souls of Light, the player should go to the bottom of the Underground Corruption/Crimson/Hallow, down where The Underworld is. This will still count as the respective biome and any mob that spawns there will drop the soul when killed. Due to the open space, mobs are less likely to be trapped within blocks, and the player will gain souls faster.


== Inventory and storage ==

First off, notable controls: Throw can be rebound to another button you are less likely to press accidentally. Quick Stack transfers all of the same item from the player's inventory to nearby storage items, but does not transfer items in the hotbar or favorited items. Stacks of items can be picked up, crafted, and bought quickly by holding the ⚷ Open / Activate button. More controls can be seen in the Inventory page.
The following is a series of questions to help you decide whether a given item is worth keeping:

Can I put it in another slot?
Armor, vanity items, accessories, dyes, and other equipment items have their own slots, and the first 3 can be placed in separate Loadout slots for extra storage.
Bait, Wire, Actuator, Solutions, Gel, and Fallen Stars can be put in ammo slots.
If you have a Piggy Bank, Safe, or Defender's Forge, you can use those to store extra items (with 40 slots each) and retrieve them at any other Piggy Bank/Safe/Defender's Forge, regardless of world. The Money Trough allows you to summon a floating Piggy Bank anywhere, without needing to place one down. Similarly, the Eye Bone summons a pet which follows you and functions exactly like a Piggy Bank.
Is it useful?
Most Furniture and vanity items, among other things, have no functional use beyond building, collecting, or cosmetics.
Gems are very valuable early on for gem hooks. However, once you collect 15 of a given gem or get another hook, gems become much less valuable.
Herbs are very useful due to their use in making buff potions.
Is it easy to obtain?
Statues and Pets, regardless of their value, are very rare in the world. If you trash one, you may not see another of the same type for hours of gameplay.
Basic ammunition like Wooden Arrows and Musket Balls can be easily bought from the Merchant/Arms Dealer respectively.
Is it the best item I can get?
Copper and Tin Ore are outclassed quickly by better ores and generally not worth keeping because of this.
If you already have one block type for bridging and exploring, other placeable blocks are much less valuable.
Can I use it now?
Potions can be used instead of trashed.
Statues and chests can be placed for later collection, provided you do not forget where you placed them.
Torches can be placed down to light up areas. Gel and wood can be crafted into torches to condense the two into a useful item.
Certain blocks and items can be turned into platforms at a workbench.


=== Hotbar ===
Your hotbar holds up to 10 items that you can use without opening your full inventory. These slots are for items you use regularly and/or need to be able to use at a moment's notice. On  Desktop, each hotbar slot has a key binding, and it can be worth changing these in settings to keys that are easier to reach in a pinch. This section will focus on items you generally should consider for your hotbar.
The most common choices for hotbar slots are weapons, a pickaxe, blocks, platforms, light sources, Recall Potions or a Magic Mirror, explosives, and items that can help with movement, like Ropes or Minecart Tracks. Other tools like a Staff of Regrowth or a hammer are also good choices, depending on how often you use them.


==== Weapons ====
You should have at least one weapon in your hotbar, possibly more for different situations. Pairing a broadsword or whip with a bow helps cover the bow's weakness with small, fast-moving targets like Cave Bats, for instance. Another common use for extra weapons is to inflict debuffs, such as using the Golden Shower to inflict Ichor.
You can buffer/scrollwheel switch to other hotbar slots while still using your current weapon. If your weapon has autoswing, it will continue swinging until you release the ⚒ Use / Attack button during the end of its animation, and then it will switch to the new slot. If it does not have autoswing, you will switch to the new hotbar slot after that weapon completes its current animation. These behaviors will still happen with the autofire setting set to on, in which case switching off of a weapon without autoswing with the ⚒ Use / Attack key held will cause you to switch your weapon and start using the new weapon. Switching between weapons with autoswing is more difficult, requiring you to stop attacking, switch, then start attacking again.


==== Pickaxes ====
What pickaxe you use depends on pickaxe power and mining speed, but just prioritizing pickaxe power is generally the safer option.


==== Blocks and platforms ====
You can jump and place platforms under your feet to quickly scale a wall or stop a fall, or use them with Smart Cursor to move diagonally along stairs. You can use blocks to control enemy movement, keep yourself safe, cover dangerous lava or Spike pits, and so much more. Dirt and other soft blocks are generally best due to being easy to mine, while platforms are mostly interchangeable outside the underworld, where Stone or Obsidian Platforms are useful due to not burning in lava.


==== Light sources ====
Torches are your permanent light source but with short range, while Glowsticks and especially a Flare Gun can light up distant spaces and even work underwater, but are temporary. Auto Select can allow you to use all of these quickly without using a hotbar slot for them by hovering the cursor over empty space, but this has some limits due to only autoselecting over certain ranges.
Some weapons, such as bows with Flaming Arrows or a Starfury, can also light up an area, with the Starfury in particular being able to light up anywhere on screen.


==== Recall Items ====
Recall Potions, a Magic Mirror, and Potions of Return allow you to teleport back to spawn, or to a bed. Recall Potions can be better than the Magic Mirror due to a faster use time, but are consumable.


==== Explosives ====
Dynamite and Bombs can be bought from the Demolitionist, and let you destroy huge numbers of blocks at once, much faster than pickaxes in most cases. They allow for fast tunneling, quickly collecting ore veins, and breaking through blocks you would not otherwise be able to mine through, such as Ebonstone or Crimstone. Having them in your hotbar can make it easier to consistently use them.


==== Movement Aids ====
Rope and Minecart Tracks are useful items for movement, letting you move up or to the side quickly and without placing physical blocks or platforms. They are very easy to obtain and quick to place over a long range, letting them break pots from a distance or stop the Sandgun from placing sand, for instance. Rope eventually becomes less useful as the player gets better mobility and especially if they are using Featherfall Potions that can lead them to grabbing onto rope by accident, but Minecart Tracks remain an extremely fast mobility option for the whole game.
An Umbrella or Trident can also affect your movement in some situations, which can be useful for avoiding fall damage or quickly moving through water.


=== Tips ===
When you leave base, any items you bring with you should serve some purpose for what you plan to do. Buff potions, informational accessories, and recovery potions are valuable additions while exploring, for instance, while Iron Bars are only valuable while crafting. Other tips are as follows:

Herbs should not be trashed, a common mistake in the early game. They are very useful when crafted into potions that can help with virtually any activity.
The trash slot can be used as a temporary extra slot. Note that exiting the world, dying, or placing another item there before taking the current one will delete the item.
Your character can equip 5/5›6/6›7 accessories directly, and that same amount in your Social slots. This gives you at least 10 more inventory slots, and you can further use loadouts to triple your available accessory slots and carry up to 3 copies of a given accessory without using any inventory space. This works for saving any accessories during exploration that you want to use or sell later.
You can also stack armor with armor slots, to store up to 6 of each armor slot.
By chance, if you encounter an NPC, it is better to sell off your junk than throwing it away.
The Encumbering Stone saves a lot of hassle as it simply restricts items from being picked up.
Many common items are also used as ammo, and can be stored in your Ammo slots. These include Gel, Fallen Stars, Sand, and in  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile, Bones, Wire and Bait.


=== Storage items ===
Each type of storage item has unique use cases. All portable storage items retain their items when broken. The player can put them into their inventory and place them at any time for access. Regularly stashing coins in a personal storage item is helpful to prevent having to retrieve it when one dies; this stash is also automatically withdrawn to pay for NPC purchases. The inventory of a portable storage item is unique for each player.


== Mining ==
Spelunker Potions are extremely useful and valuable. They highlight any valuable treasure and ores that are on your screen.
As of 1.4.5.0, drills are no longer bugged to be slower than intended.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Left Ctrl button toggles your mining style to Smart Cursor, which is extremely useful for strip mining or digging straight down.
A hellevator is a must-have once you have equipped yourself with decent mining equipment or plenty of explosives.
It is also a good place to start looking for Hardmode ores near the beginning of Hardmode.
Traps can be found randomly while exploring, by using a Dangersense Potion, or by holding any wire-related item (for example, a Pressure Plate) or equipping a Mechanical Lens and looking for horizontal Wire lines. If the lines are short and not straight, it may be some Explosives, Statues or Geysers(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Geysers can only be found in the lava layer.
These methods can also be used to find any Dead Man's Chests(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), as the chest is connected with wires around the traps.
Modifiers that affect speed will affect the mining speed of tools; The Light modifier provides the greatest increase.
Mining speed can be boosted using the Mining Potion, Ancient Chisel, Slice of Cake, and Mining armor; they all stack.
Additionally, the Mining armor's helmet can be upgraded into the Ultrabright Helmet, providing enhanced vision.
    When the minimap is expanded, hovering over an ore pocket will display its name next to the cursor.
Items that emit light through walls such as the Starfury or Firecracker can reveal the minimap.
Hardmode ores are restricted to certain layers:
Cobalt and Palladium Ore can be found in all Underground layers;
Mythril and Orichalcum Ore can be found in Cavern layers;
Adamantite and Titanium Ore can only be found in the lower Cavern layer (which is where Lava replaces Water).
Pickaxe progression is practically linear, but there are notable bumps:
Although the Molten Pickaxe can destroy most blocks it can mine in one hit, its slow mining speed means that lower tiered pickaxes can mine the weakest block types faster (namely the Bone Pickaxe). However, it remains the fastest pre-Hardmode pickaxe for mining Stone Blocks and above.
It is preferable to save Adamantite and Titanium Ore for armor and weapons, as the respective pickaxes do not allow mining any new blocks that the Mythril and Orichalcum Pickaxes would not.
Compared to the Pickaxe Axe and Drax, the Chlorophyte Pickaxe and Chlorophyte Drill has more range, identical mining speed, and cannot be used as an axe. As Chlorophyte is very valuable, the Chlorophyte tools are hardly worth crafting.
The Picksaw has a slower mining speed than the Shroomite Digging Claw, but the Picksaw is able to mine Lihzahrd Bricks and has a +1 range bonus.
The post-Moon Lord Drill Containment Unit(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a flying mount that can rapidly mine any block around the player, and is the fastest form of controlled mining in the game, surpassing the Luminite Pickaxes.


=== Mining through water ===
Use Gills Potions or a Diving Helmet.
Horizontally dig a tunnel of at least three tiles into the walls and mining the two tiles above the tunnel to create an air pocket.
As torches do not work underwater, consider bringing Glowsticks, a Flare Gun, or Cursed/Ichor Torches.
When you come across water while digging downward, place blocks in the water where you want the walls of your tunnel. Sand and Silt can be useful here.
Once your tunnel is completely sealed off from the rest of the body of water, you'll need to drain the water inside of its walls. If there is a cave nearby, you can dig an outlet to let the water drain into that. Otherwise, dig a cavity off to the side starting from the bottom of your tunnel. If you are digging sideways, you need to place blocks behind you before digging through the water to prevent flooding your tunnels.
If you have access to pumps, you can use them to move water from it to any nearby cave or reservoir. Simply place an Inlet Pump at the lowest point of your tunnel and wire it to an Outlet Pump where you want it to end up. Finally, place a trigger such as a Lever, connect it to the circuit, and use it to start draining the water.


=== Mining through lava ===
Use Obsidian Skin Potions.
You cannot place blocks directly on lava like with water, but you can drop Sand or Silt onto it to cover it up.
Bombs can explode through lava and can easily be used for small to medium sized lava pits.
You can also alternatively flood your tunnels with water. Make sure to bring a pickaxe capable of mining Obsidian.
If you are doing this in the Underworld, water rapidly evaporates in it, so it must be replaced with honey.


=== Mining Hellstone ===
Superheated Blood can make mining Hellstone extremely easy because it makes you completely immune to lava damage.
Obsidian Skin Potions are a must. You can use a Magic Mirror to quickly escape before the buff ends.
Alternatively, you can completely surround the Hellstone veins with a layer of blocks. That way, when the Hellstone is mined, the lava it leaves will be safely contained.
If the player places 50 pieces of Meteorite ore or more on the screen where they are mining, they can create an artificial Meteorite biome. In this biome, all monster spawns are replaced by Meteor Heads, which are more predictable, and tend to do less damage than the naturally spawning creatures of The Underworld. If the player can withstand the Meteor Head attacks, they can mine Hellstone in relative peace.
There are often Hellstone ore veins next to the Ruined Houses, and with the thin wall of Obsidian Brick between the Hellstone, in which makes a great natural barrier. The player can mine most Hellstone ore veins, and if some of it is out of reach, mine a single block to drain the lake, as the house can function as reservoir.


== Combat ==
For nocturnal bosses, starting the battle just after the sun sets (7:30 PM) will provide the maximum amount of time to defeat the boss. In Hardmode, the Moon Charm and/or Moon Stone and their upgrades are also useful at night.
Boss battles can be won or lost before the battle ever starts.  Choose your equipment and have it ready; find and/or make potions and placed buffs; use the highest-tier food you have available; set up an arena appropriate to the boss; learn the strategies for the boss you're facing.
Prepare your Boss-fighting arena with adequate lighting, Campfires and Heart Lanterns for health regeneration, and Stars in Bottles for mana regeneration if you use magic. Bast Statues(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) will provide a significant defensive boost. Garden Gnomes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (if underground) proper torch placement will reduce damage taken and increase damage dealt due to the luck. The Torch God's Favor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) helps with this. Honey pools can also be used for extra health regeneration.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Sunflowers provide the Happy!(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) buff to nearby players, which grants a +10% movement speed bonus and 17% reduction in enemy spawn rate.
Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.  Depending on the game stage, this can include items such as Lesser Healing Potions or Honeyfins. On the  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile versions, Restoration Potions and Eggnogs(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) are healing potions with a shorter cooldown and the same net healing per second considering Potion Sickness.
Due to the shorter cooldown, they can be used earlier than Honeyfins without overhealing, which can lead to a higher amount of healing over the course of the whole fight.
Likewise, carry mana potions if you use Magic weapons.
The Strange Brew(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is also an option, which yields very similar healing abilities to Healing Potion with added chances to trigger periods of invulnerability upon consumption.
On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, Restoration Potions can save a slot, but will likewise trigger both cooldowns.
It is suggested to build houses for the Dryad and the Nurse NPCs in your arena. The former casts the Dryad's Blessing(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) buff, which increases your defense and provides you with a thorns-like effect, while the latter can heal and remove debuffs instantly, at the cost of some coins.
Bosses are displayed on the Minimap: Follow the boss's icon to track it when you're struggling to find it. You can identify the boss icons by checking their respective wiki pages.
Once you have freed the Mechanic in the Dungeon, you can use Wire to enhance your arena with Traps and helpful Heart and Star Statues. The former helps to damage the enemies, though be careful to set them up correctly in order not to hurt yourself during the battle. The latter will spawn heart and star pickups, respectively. Connect these devices to timers to activate them infinitely.
Remember to use the Sharpening Station(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Ammo Box(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), Crystal Ball, Bewitching Table(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), War Table(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Alchemy Flask(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Slice of Cake(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) before you go to explore or battle bosses/invasions. These will give boosts that are useful to have, with the first five being class-specific.  They give Sharpened(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Ammo Box(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), Clairvoyance, Bewitched(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Strategist(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Alchemic Enhancement(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Sugar Rush(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), respectively.
Don't avoid using summon weapons or sentry-summoning weapons on non-summoner builds since those are always a damage increase, especially with the aforementioned buffs.
It may be useful to summon and kill the Eye of Cthulhu or King Slime before summoning any harder boss in order to spawn an extra one-use pool of Hearts. Note that this will take up a big chunk of the spawnable healing Hearts, which will cause Heart Statues to not spawn as many/any Hearts.


== Buffs ==
Although alleviated in modern versions, each player is limited to 44(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) / 22(Old-gen console version) / 10(3DS version) active buffs and debuffs at a time, and exceeding that will cancel buffs (but not debuffs), starting with the leftmost one. Because of this, some buffs are worth dismissing if you're close to the buff limit:

Pets and light pets do not grant any combat benefits.
Each minion type takes up a buff slot. Aside from some prehardmode minions which tend to have finicky invincibility frame mechanics that add diminishing returns to each minion of a specific type summoned which necessitates mixed minions for optimal DPS, it's best to stick to 1-2 minion types.
The Ammo Box, Sharpening Station, and Crystal Ball are all class-specific and can be dismissed if you don't use those classes' weapons. The Bewitching Table and War Table can be useful for all classes as minions and sentries don't need to be actively used, but can still be dismissed if you don't have or want to use them. The Slice of Cake only affects mining speed (useless in combat) and non-sprinting movement speed, and is both weaker and significantly shorter in duration than a Swiftness Potion as a speed buff.
Objects that grant buffs to nearby players such as Campfires, Sunflowers, Heart Lanterns, Star in a Bottles, Bast Statues, Peace Candles (and/or Water Candles), banners (any number of them count for one slot), Honey (from taking a dip or certain accessories), and being near a Dryad using Dryad's Blessing will all count towards the buff limit.
Various accessories and mid- to late-game armor or weapons (especially whips) can trigger buffs.
The Tipsy debuff is only beneficial for melee users, and Flasks don't do anything if you don't have a melee weapon or whip.
Plenty of debuffs can be blocked with various immunity accessories.
When using Quick Buff, be careful what potions are in your main inventory. Those not related to combat, or potions you don't want to accidentally use outside of combat, can be stashed in a portable storage item. Using a recovery potion will also trigger a cooldown debuff, as will the Rod of Discord.


== Skipping ahead ==
Skipping ahead, or sequence breaking, is the process of skipping major parts of game progression. This section lists notable progression skips:


=== Pre-Hardmode ===
The Fossil Pickaxe allows speed runners to skip early game progression. Entering the Underground Desert before crafting anything besides a bed and setting an Underground Cabin as their spawn, crafting the Fossil Pickaxe, mining the Crimtane or Demonite also in the area, and then crafting Light's Bane or Blood Butcherer can bypass a significant amount of early game. The player can then enter the Evil biomes and obtain Tissue Samples or Shadow Scales and also craft the next pickaxe, since the player does not actually need to survive the fight and likely will not with starting health and no equipment. That allows the player to mine Hellstone and craft Molten armor which is the highest tier of armor in pre-hardmode without ever exploring most of the map, using any Life Crystals or defeating any bosses. The player can then craft the Molten Pickaxe and then strip mine the Underground for Life Crystals and chests.
It is possible to obtain Hellstone before fighting any bosses:
On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, fishing up a Reaver Shark from the Ocean, while potentially taking some time, allows the player to skip all the mandatory pre-Hardmode pickaxes – it has the same pickaxe power as the Molten Pickaxe and is faster. Therefore, it can be used to mine Hellstone.
On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, the player can complete fishing quests from the Angler and obtain the Golden Bug Net. This can be used to catch critters in the Underworld that can be used as bait for lava fishing. From this, it is possible to obtain Obsidian Crates which have a chance to contain Hellstone. The process is very tedious however so it may not be worth the time commitment for most players. Once enough Hellstone has been obtained, a Molten Pickaxe can be crafted and used to mine naturally generated ore.
The Dungeon has a limit of 15 spawned enemies at once. This means that if there are 15 enemies following the player, Dungeon Guardians will not be able to spawn, allowing the player to loot the Dungeon before defeating Skeletron. Servants of Cthulhu and Bees are good choices for filling this enemy cap.
Pots below the Surface layer have a chance to drop Golden Keys when in front of unsafe dungeon walls. This can be used as an additional source of keys, if there are not enough in the Dungeon itself. Dungeon Bricks at the Surface layer can be used for crafting unsafe walls, since they can be mined with any pickaxe.
As the Old Man prevents the Cultists from spawning, Skeletron is required to be killed in order to spawn the Lunatic Cultist. However, Skeletron can be skipped and fought later.
It is also highly recommended to do so the player can go to the Dungeon and obtain Bones that are required to craft the Mechanical Skull.
The only pre-Hardmode boss defeat required to progress into Hardmode is the Wall of Flesh itself. It is possible to kill this boss with only Dynamite.
The player can also blow up the Hellstone in Hardmode, which can allow the player to create a Molten Pickaxe.


=== Hardmode ===


==== Hardmode ores ====
The player needs only two tiers of Hardmode ores in order to progress:
The first, which is either Cobalt or Palladium Ore is used to create the respective pickaxes or drills.
The second, which is either Mythril or Orichalcum Ore can only be destroyed via the afforementioned tool. The second tier Hardmode bars are used to create the Hardmode Anvil, which in turn is used to create the summoning items for all three mechanical bosses, skipping Adamantite or Titanium Ores entirely.
With Power Bombs, the player can obtain the third tier of Hardmode ore (either Adamantite or Titanium) while only needing a Molten Pickaxe; the player will still need to mine enough Cobalt or Palladium to craft the Power Bombs, and bomb enough Mythril or Orichalcum to craft a Hardmode Anvil.
It is entirely possible to obtain Hardmode ores without destroying any altars at all (thus preventing the mechanical bosses and Pirate Invasion from spawning naturally) by fishing up Hardmode crates; a powerful fishing setup can be obtained in pre-Hardmode to aid in acquiring the Hardmode crates as soon as Hardmode is activated.


==== Duke Fishron ====
Truffle Worms can be obtained at the beginning of Hardmode, used to spawn Duke Fishron, which then can be used as a great source of weapons and equipment such as the Tsunami or Fishron Wings.


==== Jungle Temple ====
Other than glitched world generation, the Jungle Temple can be entered early through the following ways:

Multiple hoik variations can be used to enter the Temple:
Place three platforms, stacked, in front of either sides of the door and hammering each of them once will allow you to walk through the door if the ▼ Down key is held.
Place 4 Minecart Tracks on both sides of the door and ride a Minecart into the door.
(Old-gen console version) Teleporting into the Temple is possible using a Rod of Discord or Teleporters. However, the target location needs to be free of Lihzahrd Brick Walls, which can be achieved by using any Hardmode hammer or hamaxe.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Entering the Temple from the top is possible via Shimmering. The Shimmer can be transported from The Aether to the Temple with a pump.

		
		
		


== Higher difficulties ==

Because almost every tip on lower difficulties can be used on higher ones, that leaves very few tips exclusive to higher difficulties to warrant their own page (except "Be more careful!"). That said, although this entire guide is helpful, the Survival section does include a few advanced game techniques you can take advantage of.
For Expert Mode, since most of the changes are enemy AI, the player should read each boss' strategy article they are struggling on. It is redundant to state all boss changes and strategy elsewhere. A quick way to find the articles is via the navigational template at the bottom of this very page. Master Mode is no different except for stat increases. Bosses aside, some important facts deserve mention:

Enemies have 10% (20% in Master Mode) extra knockback resistance, making it more difficult to use short-range weapons like the Copper Shortsword. A Wooden Bow, Spear, or other high-reach weapon is recommended as a replacement weapon as soon as possible.
Zombies may now spawn wielding a Zombie Arm, which has much higher damage and reach than a normal Zombie's attack. These enemies should never be attacked at close range; players without jump boosts may need to use a platform or rope pillar to jump over them without getting hit.
Powerful Expert Mode Accessories are dropped from bosses you may otherwise skip, such as the Shield of Cthulhu, Worm Scarf, Brain of Confusion, and Soaring Insignia.
Contrary to popular belief, defense is still very effective on higher difficulties. Having a defense build (see Guide:Class setups) and all accessories reforged to the Warding modifier boost survivability and can be the difference between life and death.
In the same vein, ignoring defense and relying on dodging is often not feasible for anyone but the most skilled players. Think of your health as a resource: the more hits you can take, the longer you can survive; the longer you can survive, the more damage you can deal.

title: Guide:Game progression graph
content:
Terraria is a huge world which reveals its content to the players in discrete chunks. Unlocking additional parts of the game is often described as game progression.
This guide is a graph that summarizes the bulk of the game as chunks with dependency lines indicating mandatory steps to unlock them. Depending on the difficulty of the challenge, players may also have an implicit need to finish other (lateral) parts of the game before proceeding.
The boxes below are color-coded depending on whether they contain a biome, (lesser) boss, or other entity, with occasional additional emphasizing of crucial steps in bold.

title: Heart Lantern
content:
The Heart Lantern is a functional lantern that grants the Heart Lamp buff, providing a health regeneration of 1 HP per second to all players within a rectangular area of 170×125 (  ) / 100×84 ( ) tiles.
Like other lanterns, the Heart Lantern is a mechanism that can be toggled on or off if wired, though this does not affect the buff.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
In Celebration Mk 10(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Zenith(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) worlds, the Heart Lantern can be purchased from the Princess for 7 Gold 50 Silver.


== Tips ==
As with the Campfire, it may be useful to keep a Heart Lantern in the hotbar in dangerous areas, so that it can be placed easily for quicker regeneration.
It is also useful to have one placed permanently in the player's base, along with a Campfire and a honey bath.
The combined and continuous health regeneration from Heart Lanterns, Campfires, and honey can make many boss fights less difficult. Including one or more of these in any arena is usually a good idea.

title: Honeyed Goggles
content:
The Honeyed Goggles is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bee Mount which grants limited flight. The Honeyed Goggles have a 1/20 (5%) / 11/100 (11%) chance of being dropped from the Queen Bee.
While the Bee Mount is slow on the ground, it is capable of flying and will greatly increase in speed while doing so. While flying, the player's vertical speed is kept constant. The Bee Mount can fly in the air for 10.66 seconds before it enters a "tired" state, during which it slows and glides down. The glide can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Afterwards, it requires a 3-second rest period on the ground in order to begin flying at full speed again. If the player takes off again immediately after landing an exhausted bee, it will fly, but much slower than usual. Its rest period is indicated by a "heavy breathing" animation that stops when the Bee Mount has fully recovered.


== Notes ==
The bee's flight time is divided into two different halves. During the first half, it can hover in place, and during the second half, it gradually becomes "fatigued" and drifts downwards at an accelerating rate.
Landing with the Bee Mount recovers the first half of its flight time instantly, but the fatigue is recovered over the course of a few seconds. If the player takes off again before the bee's fatigue is fully recovered, it will drift downwards even during the first half of its flight.
Unlike most other limited-flight mounts, the Bee Mount only loses half of its flight time when summoned in mid-air.
The bee's flight time can be greatly extended by gravity-decreasing effects such as a Featherfall Potion or the low gravity of Space, up to nearly 27 seconds.
Like the UFO Mount summoned by the Cosmic Car Key(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the bee will disappear if submerged in liquid, and cannot be re-summoned until the liquid is exited.
The bee's flight time is increased by boosts to the players' remaining flight/jump time. This includes additional jumps such as those added by the Bundle of Balloons.
The bee's flying speed reaches 31 mph when flying forward, 41 mph flying upwards and 51 mph flying diagonally, according to the Stopwatch. Its walking speed is only 10 mph.
This mount can be equipped and unequipped for longer flight time.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
If combined with several accessories that increase flight time (like Cloud in a Balloon), it is capable of reaching Floating Islands, even on large worlds.
The Honeyed Goggles is an incredibly useful mount to acquire early in the game as the flight can help traverse the terrain and help in avoiding damage from bosses and other enemies.
Paired with a Featherfall Potion, the Honeyed Goggles can be an equivalent to pre-Hardmode wings for traversing, especially useful for boss fights.
Long flight time paired with hovering ability makes Honeyed Goggles a very useful mount for building. Additionally its walking speed matches block placement speed with the Brick Layer or its upgrades.
Unlike most means of transportation the Bee mount is not affected by reduced gravity and retains full flight speed and control. This makes this mount extra useful when navigating Floating Islands or the "true" surface in Remix and Such great heights worlds.


== Trivia ==
The Bee Mount's flight goggles appear raised on its forehead while the bee is grounded, and lower over its eyes when taking off.
The Shrimpy Truffle could be considered an indirect upgrade to the Honeyed Goggles.
The Honeyed Goggles, along with most (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) / all  other pre-Hardmode mounts, is one of the few pre-Hardmode items with a rarity of .

title: Resource Pack
content:
Resource Packs are add-on files which allow players to customize the game's sprites, musics, sound effects and translations.


== Installing a Resource Pack ==

Resource Packs can be installed by being placed in the ResourcePacks folder. It can be accessed by clicking the "Open Folder" option in the Resource Packs menu in-game. This folder is generated when the game is launched. The file directories of the folder are:

On Windows Vista and later, %USERPROFILE%\Documents\My Games\Terraria\ResourcePacks
On Windows XP, %USERPROFILE%\My Documents\My Games\Terraria\ResourcePacks
On Mac, open Finder and press "Go" on the top. Then press "Go to folder...". Type in ~/Library/Application Support/Terraria/ResourcePacks
On Linux, $XDG_DATA_HOME/Terraria/ResourcePacks
This is typically ~/.local/share/Terraria
If the game is purchased on  Steam, Resource Packs can also be downloaded from the Steam Workshop, where they will be installed and updated automatically. Resource Packs downloaded from the Steam Workshop are not stored in the ResourcePacks folder, instead they are stored in folders named with the pack's Workshop ID in Steam's library folder. Default file directories are:

 Windows: C:\Program files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\105600\<Workshop ID>
 Linux: ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/workshop/content/105600/<Workshop ID>
Installed Resource Packs can be enabled from the Workshop Hub or by selecting the "Resource Packs" option in the main menu, where they can be moved between "Available Packs" and "Enabled Packs".
Resource Packs installed via the Steam Workshop can also be directly used in tModLoader.


=== Notes ===
Note that for Terraria, subscribed Steam Workshop items will be automatically downloaded and made available regardless of the current Steam account. As a result, if multiple Steam accounts have logged in on the same device, one may find other accounts' subscribed Workshop items showing up in the game.


== Creating a Resource Pack ==


=== Contents ===
Resource Packs require a pack.json file; otherwise, it will not be recognized by the game. It may optionally include an icon.png file for display in the Resource Packs menu. A valid pack.json file will look like the following:


==== Example folder structure ====
Pack Name
icon.png (optional)
pack.json
Content
Images
Acc_Back_1.png
Localization
en-US_Content.json
Music
Music_77.ogg
Sounds
Player_Killed.xnb


==== Images ====
Images are placed inside the Content/Images folder of the Resource Pack. They must share the same file name (albeit with a png extension) and canvas dimensions as the default images. The default Terraria images can be located here:

On Windows Steam version, C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Terraria\Content\Images.
On Linux Steam Version, ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/Terraria/Content/Images
On macOS Steam version, Library/'Application Support'/Steam/steamapps/common/Terraria/Terraria.app/Contents/MacOS/Content/Images.
On GOG version, C:\GOG Games\Terraria\Content\Images.
Tip for Mac users: To open and view the contents of Terraria.app, right click and select "Show Package Contents"
These default images are stored with the xnb file extension.


==== Music ====
Music files are placed inside the Content/Music folder of the Resource Pack. They can be in either wav, mp3 or ogg format.


==== Sounds ====
Sound files are placed inside the Content/Sounds folder of the Resource Pack. They should be in xnb format.


==== Localization ====
Localization files are placed inside the Content/Localization folder of the Resource Pack. They can be in either a csv or json format.
The name of the localization file must start with one of the following language code for the game to properly detect and apply the changes:

A valid example of json formatted localization file, for example: en-US.json file will look like the following:


=== Notes ===

If there is no icon.png included in a Resource Pack, it will use a default placeholder icon instead.


== See also ==
The Ultimate Guide To Content Creation And Use For The Terraria Workshop (March 29, 2021), an in-depth guide on creating Resource Packs by Leinfors.


== External links ==
TConvert, a tool for extracting xnb files for viewing, editing, and saving.
See Modding:Audio on Stardew Valley wiki about tools for extracting xwb files (in-game music).

title: Ecto Mist
content:
Ecto Mist is a visual effect produced by any Graveyard mini-biome consisting of seven or more Tombstones. It is translucent and floats along the ground, and appears on top of solid blocks. Occasional wisps appear in the air while Ecto Mist is visible. With each additional Tombstone placed (up to a maximum of nine), the mist gets thicker and the background gets darker.
Ecto Mist can, in conjunction with a crafting station, be utilized to craft certain unique items, most notably blocks and walls that are generated naturally and do not drop as items when destroyed. The player does not need to be in direct contact with the mist for that; being in a Graveyard is sufficient. Crafting an item this way also does not "consume" Ecto Mist nor cause it to disappear, similar to liquids.
Ecto Mist cannot be used to craft the following naturally-generated objects:

Any ambient objects
Pots
Gem Stashes
Coin Stashes
Enchanted Sword rocks, fake or real
Larva
Plant blocks (mainly grass, flowers and vines, but also including Plantera's Bulb and thorny bushes) - these can instead regenerate given enough time
Walls that are crafted via Ecto Mist are different from their natural counterparts in ID: for example, the Spider Wall will not spawn Cobwebs nor allow for the creation of artificial Spider Nests, and it is not possible to create an artificial Underground Desert biome using crafted sandstone walls, as these also have a separate ID. The natural counterparts must be obtained by throwing the crafted version to Shimmer.


== Crafting ==


=== Used to craft ===


== Trivia ==
Ecto-mist is the name given to light, swirling gray mist that marks the presence of paranormal activity. This is a visual effect often used in horror movies to give the atmosphere a more ominous feel.

title: Clumsy Balloon Slime
content:
The Clumsy Balloon Slime is a rare entity that can be found in the Space layer, in any weather. In pre-Hardmode, it cannot spawn in the central vertical section of the map, which is around one-tenth the width of the entire map. This restriction is removed in Hardmode.
The player can break its balloon as if it were an enemy, and then it will transform into the Clumsy Slime. Afterwards, the Clumsy Balloon Slime will no longer spawn.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.


== Notes ==
The Clumsy Balloon Slime does not damage the player, nor can the slime itself take any damage.
Only one Clumsy Balloon Slime can exist at a time.
If the Clumsy Slime Town Slime is killed, it will respawn naturally without the need to break another Clumsy Balloon Slime's balloon.

title: Cursed Sapling
content:
The Cursed Sapling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Cursed Sapling that follows the player. It appears as a small, dark blue tree stump with a jagged head, a jack-o-lantern face, and roots on which it walks. The Cursed Sapling is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.


== Notes ==
If the Cursed Sapling gains too much distance from the player, it will propel itself toward the player while emitting a trail of flames, ignoring blocks and giving off a decent amount of light. If it cannot reach a stable spot to stand on, the Cursed Sapling will start flying around the player in circles.
This is a useful feature as a pet, as the light it provides when flying helps find nearby caves. It can, however, make fishing more difficult as the sound the sapling makes when hitting water is identical to that of a bobbing line, forcing the player to rely on sight (or the use of Sonar Potions) to determine whether anything has been hooked.


== Trivia ==
Unlike most pets, the Cursed Sapling item has the same name as the pet it summons.

title: The Dirtiest Block
content:
The Dirtiest Block is a pet-summoning item that spawns The Dirtiest Block that follows the player. It can be found extremely rarely as a block that looks identical to Dirt Blocks. Upon world generation and depending on world size, up to 3 (in small worlds), 6 (medium), or 9 (large) random Dirt Blocks will be replaced with The Dirtiest Blocks.


== Notes ==
Grass cannot grow on The Dirtiest Blocks.
In a Celebration Mk 10 world, the maximum amount of The Dirtiest Blocks that can generate is multiplied by 5 (up to 15, 30, or 45 depending on world size).
In a Not the Bees world, The Dirtiest Block can also replace Mud Blocks.
The Dirtiest Block will only generate 50 tiles from the left and right true world edges, 50 tiles from the top, and 200 tiles from the bottom.
World generation tests blocks at random positions until a valid block to replace with The Dirtiest Block is found. Regardless of world size, this process is capped to a maximum of 2999 replacement attempts, making it possible to have fewer than the maximum number of The Dirtiest Blocks in a world.
In a Skyblock world, the generation of The Dirtiest Block is unchanged, making the chance for it to appear much higher.


== Tips ==
Using dyes on the pet can make it look like other blocks.
The Dirtiest Block can be found more easily by spraying areas of Dirt Blocks with White or Yellow Solutions, as they can convert normal Dirt Blocks but not The Dirtiest Blocks.

title: Spider Staff
content:
The Spider Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Spider minion. It runs towards enemies and latches onto them, repeatedly dealing damage while latched and inflicting the Acid Venom debuff for 2–4 seconds. It can climb background walls and jump high.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Spider Staff cycles through three visually distinct types of Spider minions. The first minion is a Venom Spider, the second a Jumper Spider, the third a Dangerous Spider, the fourth a Venom Spider again, and so on. All three types are functionally identical.
Each spider minion has an internal hit cooldown of 0.35 seconds, meaning it can hit an enemy up to 3 times per second.
Each spider minion applies 15 static invincibility frames for its type, meaning multiple spiders of the same type will be capped to 4 hits per second.
Therefore the 4th, 5th, and 6th spiders attacking an enemy will not be able to hit at the same rate as the first 3, with each one only adding an extra hit per second. As a result the maximum number of hits for spiders is capped at 12 times per second with 6 spider minions.
For example, 3 spiders will attack an enemy 9 times per second, but 6 spiders will only attack 12 times per second; 11 spiders will also only attack an enemy 12 times per second.
With only 3 spider minions, the invincibility frames do not actually come into play, since their internal hit cooldown lasts longer than duration of the invincibility frames.
The spider minions can target enemies within a Manhattan distance of 50-tile, and will automatically return to the player's side if their distance from the player is greater than the radius of 87.5 tiles.
The spider can target enemies within a Manhattan distance of 43.75-tile centered on the player while returning to the player.
When not attached to background walls, the spider minion has a maximum horizontal movement speed of 31 mph, which increases as the player's speed increases.
When attached to background walls,the spider minion is unaffected by gravity and has a maximum movement speed of 46 mph.
When latched onto an enemy, the spider minion follows the target closely at a maximum speed of 72 mph.
Additionally, if the spider is attached to background walls, this maximum speed is slightly reduced.
The spider minion jumps toward its target when the following conditions are met:
It is on the ground.
It is below the target, with a vertical distance to the target greater than 6.25 tiles and less than 23.75 tiles.
Its horizontal distance to the target is less than 3.125 tiles.
The spider minion begin latching onto the target when the horizontal or vertical distance between their hitbox and the target's hitbox is less than 0.625 tiles.
This means that if a grounded spider is within 6.25 tiles below the target's center but outside 0.625 tiles from the target's bottom, or is more than 23.75 tiles below the target's center, it will neither attack nor jump, and will instead continuously follow the target.


== Tips ==
The Spider Staff is easily acquired when first entering Hardmode, as most players will have already found a Spider Nest before it begins. Simply return there to kill the Black Recluses that begin spawning in Hardmode.
If several spiders latch onto a single target that can receive knockback, the target will often be carried away from the player, but in some cases can carry the enemy towards the player instead.


== Trivia ==
The second type of spider, the Jumper Spider, resembles a Mexican redknee tarantula. The third type of spider, the Dangerous Spider, resembles a black widow.
The staff appears to be a four-legged spider.
The Spider Staff and the Queen Spider Staff are the only items available prior to defeating any mechanical boss that can inflict the Acid Venom debuff.
Contrary to the real world where spiders do not have wings, the spider minions will use wings to follow an airborne player when there are no background walls.

title: Guide:Crafting Terraspark Boots
content:
Terraspark Boots are a highly useful movement accessory which can be crafted before Hardmode and can easily last you into the endgame. While the crafting tree is complex, most of the materials required are easy to come across.


== Basic diagram ==


== Ingredients ==


=== Step 1: Spectre Boots ===
There are four types of base level running boots that exist which increase the player's movement speed by a very high margin, allowing them to sprint. Most of these boots have no additional effects (except for Dunerider Boots) and can be used interchangeably in crafting.
The Dunerider Boots grant even more speed on sand, but this effect will not be transferred to its upgrades.


===== Hermes Boots =====
The Hermes Boots are likely the first variety of sprinting boots that the player will encounter, and are very easy to discover early on. They can be found in Gold Chests in Underground Cabins which generate in most biomes in the Underground and Cavern layers.


===== Flurry Boots =====
Flurry Boots are also very easy to encounter in the early game generating within Frozen Chests, acting as an Ice biome counterpart to Hermes Boots.
Since the Ice biome sometimes spreads near the spawn point even if the player does not spawn directly within the Snow biome, Flurry Boots may be encountered if the player tunnels down deep enough near spawn. This is most likely to happen with small worlds.
They can also be fished up in Frozen Crates, and Boreal Crates in Hardmode.


===== Sailfish Boots =====
The Sailfish Boots are obtained from opening Wooden Crates and Iron Crates found via fishing, and are semi-common rewards from opening them, with a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being received from the former and a 133/3125 (4.26%) chance of being received from the latter. The Wooden Crate is the most common Crate found via fishing, with the Iron Crate being second-most common.


===== Dunerider Boots =====
Dunerider Boots can be found in the Underground Desert, specifically in Chests located in Underground Desert Cabins. This biome is extremely dangerous to new players, so you'll probably be best off avoiding this one. You can also fish them up in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates.


==== Rocket Boots ====
After defeating a Goblin Army and rescuing the Goblin Tinkerer, the Rocket Boots can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for a base price of 5 Gold.


==== Crafting the Spectre Boots ====
The Rocket Boots can be combined with one of any of the base level running boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop to yield the Spectre Boots, combining the effects of its two components.


=== Step 2: Lightning Boots ===


===== Aglet =====
Aglets are quite common accessories that are frequently found in Surface wooden Chests. They can also be found by opening Wooden Crates, which are obtained from fishing, with a 1/100 (1%) chance. Another way to obtain them is from the Skeleton Merchant during a New Moon for 2 Gold 50 Silver.


===== Anklet of the Wind =====
The Anklet of the Wind can be found in Ivy Chests, which generate within Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle. They can also be found by opening Jungle Crates, with a 19/100 (19%) chance.


==== Crafting the Lightning Boots ====
These two accessories can be combined with the Spectre Boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop, yielding the Lightning Boots.


=== Step 3: Frostspark Boots ===


===== Ice Skates =====
Ice Skates, just like the Flurry Boots, can be found in Frozen Chests. If one cannot find a pair in their world, they can also fish in the Snow biome and try to obtain these from Frozen Crates or Boreal Crates with a 1/6 (16.67%) chance.


==== Crafting the Frostspark Boots ====
Combine Ice Skates with the Lightning Boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop to craft the Frostspark Boots.


=== Step 4: Obsidian Water Walking Boots ===


===== Water Walking Boots =====
The Water Walking Boots have a 1/10 (10%) chance be found in Water Chests, which can be found submerged in the Ocean and in other biomes' water pools. The player also can obtain them from Ocean Crates and Seaside Crates. While they can be found underground, the easiest way to search for them is in the Ocean.


===== Obsidian Skull =====
The Obsidian Skull can be crafted from 20 Obsidian at a Furnace. Obsidian may be obtained by mixing lava with water.


==== Crafting the Obsidian Water Walking Boots ====
Combine Water Walking Boots with the Obsidian Skull at a Tinkerer’s Workshop to craft the Obsidian Water Walking Boots.


=== Step 5: Lava Waders ===


===== Lava Charm =====
The Lava Charm can be found in Chests in the Lava layer with a 1/20 (5%) chance. However, since they aren't guaranteed to appear in a world, fishing in lava for Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates can yield the Lava Charm with a 1/20 (5%) chance, although this may take a while. Alternatively, it can also be obtained by throwing a Magma Stone into Shimmer.


===== Obsidian Rose =====
The Obsidian Rose is also required to craft Lava Waders and can be obtained from Fire Imps in the Underworld with a 1/20 (5%) drop rate chance. 


==== Crafting the Lava Waders ====
Combine Obsidian Water Walking Boots with the Lava Charm and Obsidian Rose at a Tinkerer's Workshop to craft the Lava Waders.


=== Step 6: Terraspark Boots ===


==== Finalizing the Terraspark Boots ====
Combine Frostspark Boots with the Lava Waders at a Tinkerer's Workshop to craft the Terraspark Boots.
