title: Guide:The Twins strategies
content:
The Twins are the Hardmode version of the Eye of Cthulhu. They are part of the trio of the mechanical bosses, alongside The Destroyer and Skeletron Prime.


== Spawn Condition ==
The Twins can be spawned by fulfilling any of these conditions:

Smash a Demon / Crimson Altar. Then every night there is a 10% chance of one of the mechanical bosses spawning, with the specific boss that spawns being chosen randomly out of those that have not been defeated.
Use the Mechanical Eye at night.
They must then be defeated before the night ends.


== The Fight ==
The Twins, as the name suggests, are two separate monsters, both of which must be defeated. They have a combined health of 43,000 / 64,500 / 82,238, shared between them. Retinazer is distinguished by its red iris and that it fires lasers. Spazmatism is distinguished by its green iris and that it fires cursed flames.
When reduced to 40% health, they will transform, gaining a slight boost in offense and defense. Each Eye transforms independently once reduced to 8,000 / 12,000 / 15,300 HP (Retinazer) / 9,200 / 13,800 / 17,595.2 HP (Spazmatism); the other eye remains in its original form until it is reduced to the appropriate amount. When one is destroyed, the other will continue attacking in the same pattern.
It is a good idea to focus on one Eye, since the fight becomes easier if a single Eye has been defeated. Also, the fight becomes considerably harder if both Eyes are on their second form.


=== Retinazer ===
In its first form, Retinazer will fire lasers at the player at a steady but somewhat slow rate. This is occasionally interrupted by charging attacks, which mirror that of its partner. Retinazer does slightly less damage than Spazmatism, but this is offset by its higher accuracy thanks to the speed of the lasers. When not charging, Retinazer will always be aligned diagonally with the player, positioned above them.
When it changes into its second form, it will no longer engage in charge attacks. Instead, its lasers will progressively fire at a faster rate as it loses health. This is occasionally supplemented by a weaker but much more rapid laser attack that tracks extremely well. To avoid this, try to fall as fast as you can, and you can be left unscathed. With wings it is possible to "zig-zag" up and down to dodge the lasers. This is made trickier as the fight goes on, with Retinazer using more rapid and fast lasers that are much harder to dodge.


=== Spazmatism ===
Spazmatism varies between firing Cursed Flames from a distance and engaging in charging attacks. The flames do more damage than the lasers from Retinazer, but are not as fast and thus easier to dodge. However, the Cursed Inferno debuff can be very dangerous for its high damage over time and its ability to stop health regeneration. Its charge attacks are faster and more aggressive than Retinazer.
Spazmatism's second form changes his attack pattern dramatically compared to Retinazer. Its Cursed Flame attack becomes a constant stream of flame, which will last for several seconds (and deal large amounts of damage). However, it does not chase the player quite as quickly as it does in its first form, making avoiding the attack somewhat easier. Once it stops spewing flame, it will charge with greatly increased speed, which also does a lot more damage. Dodging these charges is quite difficult. Much like Retinazer, falling as fast as possible while he is charging can help. Misdirecting Spazmatism's charges is easier than it sounds; by jumping as he slows down, he will charge over the player. This causes Spazmatism to charge from either above or below, making him easier to dodge by running.


=== Expert/Master Mode ===
In Expert Mode, both Twins fire faster projectiles and have shorter cooldowns between attacks. 


== General Strategies ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain preparation ===
The Sky above the surface is highly recommended for The Twins arena, as vertical movement is required to dodge most of the attacks.

A very long Sky Bridge (if possible made out of Asphalt or Frozen Slime Blocks) is optimal. Continuously running with Spectre Boots or their upgrades causes both to miss you with their projectiles very often, and keeps each Twin at a stationary horizontal position most of the time, allowing you to fire continuously at it without switching your aim. Wings will help dodge each of The Twins' second phases. Using Asphalt can negate the need for Boots, while using them can allow you to avoid taking damage completely. However, try not to run too fast if you use Boots and Asphalt, as Retinazer may fall behind and despawn. Spazmatism, however, is fast enough to keep up. Regular Stone Blocks can be used too if the player has obtained the Blessed Apple or the Goat Skull.
The Asphalt variation of this strategy is only possible if another mechanical boss has been defeated, as Asphalt Blocks can only be crafted with the Blend-O-Matic sold by the Steampunker.
The standard boss arena of several layers of platforms with furniture buffs makes maneuvering around easier.
Also, a wall on both sides of a small area can block Spazmatism's Cursed Flame, but be careful not to run out of time from covering behind the wall. It is helpful to have a one block hole one block up to shoot through. This is more useful if you want to try tanking the boss with the above tip of heart statues. If you can tank the hits with the help of heart statues, you can gun down Retinazer while Spazmatism is only able to charge at you.
The player can use a Minecart Track when building a sky arena to avoid The Twins' attacks whilst using a ranged weapon.


=== Gearing up ===
If a mechanical boss has been defeated, Life Fruits will begin to grow in the Underground Jungle, increasing health by 5 per Life Fruit until the player reaches 500 health. It is recommended to get as much Life Fruits as possible.

Adamantite armor provides the greatest overall increase to all stats. Melee and ranged users should substitute in a Frost Breastplate to increase damage output and defense without sacrificing anything important. If more offense is desired, Mythril Greaves or Spider Greaves should be substituted into the leg slot.
Titanium armor is a defensive alternative for Adamantite armor, the Titanium Barrier buff increases survivability.
Crystal Assassin armor has respectable defense and stat boosts, which makes this set a viable alternative to Hardmode ore sets. It provides a dash as part of its set bonus, allowing players to replace Shield of Cthulhu with another accessory.
Orichalcum armor provides very high critical strike chance and its set bonus can hit both Eyes.
Palladium armor provides lower stat bonuses, but the Rapid Healing buff greatly increases natural regeneration.
Hallowed armor becomes a great choice if a mechanical boss has been defeated. The Holy Protection buff allows the player to dodge an attack.
Spider armor is the best choice for summoners who do not use whips frequently.
Obsidian armor provides strong bonuses and high minion damage to summoners. The increased whip range and speed can potentially outperform Spider armor, especially if using minions that have difficulty reaching The Twins.
The armor sets available from the Tavernkeep combine summon damage increases with stat increases to one of the other classes. Note that they're only available if you've defeated another mechanical boss, however.
These armor sets also increase the players' sentry slots. If the player stays in roughly the same spot and uses the Barnacle Staff, it can provide helpful DPS against the Twins.
Forbidden armor provides less powerful stat bonuses than other armor sets at this tier, but encourages the player to use magic weapons for active damage, supplemented by minions and sentries.
The Frost armor provides excellent stat increases as a set bonus, making it a strong alternative to Adamantite or Titanium armors and also useful for hybrid melee and ranged damage users.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users

The Shadowflame Knife is one of the few long-range melee weapons at this stage. As its projectiles ricochet, it can sometimes hit both eyes at the same time if aimed right. The Bananarang and Chain Guillotines are similar alternatives.
The Light Disc can also be used if you have already defeated The Destroyer.
Yoyos with the Yoyo Bag can be useful.
If a mechanical boss has been defeated, using the Yelets with the Magic Yoyo Bag is very powerful.
While most flails are risky to use, the Drippler Crippler's projectiles are very strong here.
The Ice Sickle could also be used, as Spazmatism will spend most of the time behind the player, so shooting constantly backwards with the piercing projectile will hit him multiple times and deal quite reasonable damage.
For Ranged users

The Daedalus Stormbow is a great bow, especially if combined with Ichor Arrows or Cursed Arrows, even better with a Magic Quiver and its upgrades, as they greatly increase arrow velocity, making it much easier to hit your shots.
The Adamantite and Titanium Repeater with Holy Arrows or Ichor Arrows are easy to use and have decent damage.
The Hallowed Repeater is an upgrade if another mechanical boss has already been defeated.
Guns such as the Megashark, Uzi, Onyx Blaster, Gatligator, and Clockwork Assault Rifle can be quite effective when paired with Ichor, Crystal, or Cursed Bullets.
Keeping an Endless Musket Pouch and Endless Quiver allows the user to have backup ammo in case the player runs out of special bullets or arrows.
The Dart Rifle / Dart Pistol with Crystal Darts or Ichor Darts is an effective weapon, especially the former, which can hit both Twins at the same time.
For Magic users

The Crystal Serpent is one of the strongest weapons mages can use in early Hardmode.
The Crystal Storm and the Sky Fracture are also very powerful choices.
The Cursed Flames deals very high damage if each fireball hits twice, but is somewhat difficult to use.
The Killing Deck can do high damage when close. When further away, it needs manual firing instead of autoswing to reach an effective range.
If one other mechanical boss has been defeated, the left-click attack of the Tome of Infinite Wisdom deals high damage.
The Spirit Flame's homing abilities and high damage allows the user to deal consistent damage.
The Shadowflame Hex Doll can also be very strong, despite its short range.
The Golden Shower inflicts the Ichor debuff, decreasing the defense of The Twins.
It can be used as a substitute for Ichor Bullets, Ichor Arrows, and Flask of Ichor for other classes, allowing other classes to use more potent ammo or flasks. However, this requires the player to constantly reapply the debuff.
The Nimbus Rod's rainclouds last for 1 minute, which can add DPS to all classes.
If a mechanical boss has already been defeated, the Unholy Trident is a powerful choice if aimed correctly.
The Lightning Strike can be used to damage Spazmatizm while avoiding Retinazer, and deals high damage.
For Summoners

The Sanguine Staff has perfect tracking and high base damage, which make it a decent choice.
The Ruinous Staff requires grinding, but is a solid and reliable weapon.
The Blade Staff is strong with whips that have particularly high summon tag damage.
The Spider Staff is a poor choice for this fight if not using an arena, as it can be difficult for the spiders to reach The Twins or stay attached. However, if one creates an arena full of walls, the spiders will latch on while they change forms, dealing hundreds of damage.
Although being a pre-boss weapon, the Abigail's Flower can do well with its buffs gained after entering Hardmode. It is generally best to go all-in with this weapon, as Abigail will get better the more minion slots you use on her.
The Firecracker increases damage output for minions, which is particular potent with ones that have high base damage, such as the Sanguine Staff or Abigail's Flower (if used all-in).
In contrast, the Cool Whip works better for fast-moving minions like the Blade Staff due to its high tag damage.
The Durendal is a powerful choice if a mechanical boss has already been defeated.
The Barnacle Staff sentry has good accuracy and can float in the air. The Queen Spider Staff has more damage but requires The Twins to fly low to the ground or on platforms.
If a mechanical boss has already been defeated, the Ballista Cane is a powerful choice when facing The Twins.


==== Accessories ====
Accessories that improve mobility are a must, since The Twins use quick attacks.

The Amphibian Boots, Frostspark Boots, or Terraspark Boots and Wings are a must, especially for the Sky Bridge method. They allow the player to dodge, and also allow the player to retreat temporarily if health is running low.
The Gelatinous Pillion can replace both the boots and the wings, as its quick vertical movement makes it excellent for dodging the flames from Spazmatism in the first stage and flying out of range in the second stage.
The increased movement speed and acceleration granted by the Roller Skates can aid in dodging, and can be used in conjunction with the player's wings and hook, despite being a mount.
Even though it doesn't prevent Cursed Inferno, the Ankh Shield can still be used to prevent knockback and for some useful extra defense.
The same is true for the Obsidian Shield and the Cobalt Shield.
An Emblem of the player's respective class greatly increases damage output.
Shield of Cthulhu's dash is essential throughout the fight.
Worm Scarf greatly decreases damage, but is exclusive to Corruption worlds.
The Brain of Confusion is very useful for players as it provides a chance to dodge an attack, but is exclusive to Crimson worlds. It doesn't prevent getting inflicted with the Cursed Inferno debuff, however.
The Charm of Myths reduces the cooldown of Potion Sickness as well as increasing passive health regeneration.
It can be quickswapped in the accessory slot if using it on a vanity slot, taking advantage of its reduced Potion Sickness cooldown.
The Cross Necklace or its upgrades increases invulnerability frames for a brief period upon taking damage, which can greatly mitigate damage, especially from Spazmatism's charges.
The Putrid Scent provides decent offensive bonuses.
The Moon Charm gives an increase to various stats, increasing survivability and damage.
The Magic Cuffs (or Celestial Cuffs) are helpful if using magic weapons, but requires the user to take damage.
The Magnet Flower, Arcane Flower, Mana Cloak, or Mana Flower allows the user to automatically consume mana potions.
The Magic Quiver and its upgrades greatly increases arrow damage.
The Pygmy Necklace adds an extra minion slot.
The Squire's Shield/Apprentice's Scarf are great choices for summoners, although they don't stack.
Whipstacking users will want to equip the Snake Band, Silver Bracer, Wicked Armlet and/or their upgrades for enhanced damage.
The Heavy Sling and its upgrades can be useful to bring a sentry closer to the boss.
Feral Claws enable autoswing for melee weapons and whips and its upgrades increase melee knockback and size, making them useful for both melee and summoners.
The Berserker's Glove, an upgrade to the Power Glove, also increases defense, but melee users might prefer to use the Power Glove instead so it can later be crafted into the Mechanical Glove.
If possible, reforge all accessories to Warding. This will decrease most of the damage to an acceptable value, allowing you to focus on dodging the high-damage attacks, such as Spazmatism's cursed fireballs and dashes(the fireball itself doesn't hurt that much, but the Cursed Inferno debuff it inflicts does cause rapid HP loss).


==== Potions ====
Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, and Ironskin Potion will help prevent fatal damage. Two of each will likely cover the entire night.
Lifeforce Potion is harder to craft, requiring Prismite, but it can boost maximum health to 480 (600 if on 500 HP using Life Fruit).
Any food item providing the Well Fed buff is very useful.
Gravitation Potion can be especially useful, as it eliminates the need for any arena and may free up an accessory slot.
Swiftness Potion greatly increases mobility.
If you have access to a world with Corruption, a Wrath Potion is a good bonus to all classes, but is not necessary.
Similarly, Crimson worlds have access to Rage Potion which also provides a good bonus.
For magic users, the Magic Power Potion and Mana Regeneration Potion is a must.
The Archery Potion will greatly boost the damage and speed of arrows.
Melee users greatly benefit from the effects of Ale or Sake.
The Summoning Potion adds an extra minion slot to the fight, which all classes can benefit from.


=== Miscellaneous ===
Because The Twins are vulnerable to many debuffs, melee and summoners can use flasks. The Flask of Ichor for Crimson worlds greatly increases the damage output of all weapons, and the Flask of Cursed Flames for Corruption worlds can give a very slight increase to DPS. But it's not reccomended to use the Flask of Poison since The Twins are immune to Poisoned, they won't take any additional damage. Also keep in mind that flasks don't stack with eachother, so you should choose your flasks wisely.
Crystal Bullets and Ichor Bullets are a must have if using guns, and Holy Arrows and Ichor Arrows for bows.
The Ice Rod is useful against Retinazer because the spawned Ice Blocks can block his lasers.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Retinazer Cheese ===
This strategy requires you take out Spazmatism first. Once you defeat Spazmatism you need to get Retinazer into its second form. Then go inside a small box of solid blocks and use summons (preferably with summon armor), the Meteor Staff or the Daedalus Stormbow (preferrably with Holy Arrows and the Magic Quiver/its upgrades) to take down Retinazer. Because Retinazer does not charge in its second form and its lasers do not pierce blocks, you will be completely safe.


=== Running Skybridge Strategy ===
A helpful strategy is a Skybridge with any fast running accessory or potions. Simply run either left or right, focus on Spazmatism, and occationally dodge his Cursed Flame balls in his first phase by flying up until he finished his attack (if your wings go fast and high enough, the Flame balls will simply pass under your feet as they are not fast and do not home). The second phase of Spazmatism is harder, requiring more dodging. Simply run out of the way if you can go fast enough or fly in a tall arch over him while he uses his Cursed Flame breath. His dashed should be easy to dodge as well with the minimap, timing, or simply speed and flight. This works with a Minecart, just watch out for the Flame balls or dismount and fly when he does the attack. 


=== Close-ranged Unicorn Strategy ===
Another helpful strategy that also utilizes a Skybridge is using a Blessed Apple and any kind of yoyo (the Yoyo Bag is recommended) or a long range weapon. Running with the Unicorn and shooting the yoyo behind you will deal a lot of damage, and you won't get hit very much as the Unicorn is slightly faster. Warning: Using this strategy may lead to The Twins despawning if you go too fast.


=== Minecart Strategy ===
A strategy that is helpful for all classes is to use a Minecart Track extending as far as possible. For shorter Minecart Tracks, both ends can be hammered to allow the Minecart to go in both directions without losing speed. As the Minecart can go faster than The Twins, the player can use a long range weapon, such as a repeater or a yoyo (with the Yoyo Bag) to deal damage from a relatively safe distance. Warning: Using this strategy may cause The Twins to despawn if the player travels too fast.


=== Sentry Farming ===
After gaining access to the Tier 2 equipment sold by the Tavernkeep, The Twins become much easier to defeat. Wearing the Squire armor and using the Ballista Cane will give the best results because of the high defense and health regeneration provided by the armor, as well as the Ballista Panic! buff doubling the firing rate. Acquiring one of the accessories dropped by the Ogre is recommended for this method. When building your arena, be sure to use platforms whenever possible to maximize the opportunities your Ballistas have to fire. Make sure that you have Heart Lanterns and Campfires set up to give yourself the most health regeneration. Having a good pair of wings, the Cobalt Shield or its upgrades, and the Lightning Boots, Frostspark Boots, or Terraspark Boots are recommended for maximum mobility. The Summoner Emblem will make the fight go much faster, rounding out your accessories. A few Greater Healing Potion are all the healing you'll need in case you get backed into a tight spot. Once The Twins have been summoned in, simply kite them around your Ballistas, taking damage periodically, preferably from Retinazer's laser for minimal damage. With the best modifiers on your gear and all the relevant buffs, The Twins will go down in two to three minutes. If you find yourself taking too much damage and needing to heal more, consider swapping out the Summoner Emblem with a Charm of Myths so you can heal more often.


=== The Black Spot ===
It is very easy to defeat The Twins with The Black Spot. The only thing you need is high, consistent damage until dawn. Keep in mind that circling around in the skies may summon a Wyvern, so it's nice to have a weapon against segmented enemies (such as the Medusa Head).
Note: The Black Spot was nerfed to be slightly slower in 1.4.1, which may result in taking more damage than intended.


=== Bouncing Strategy ===
It is very effective if you are able to keep The Twins low to the ground to bounce on them repeatedly using a Slimy Saddle. It works especially well to pair this with the Meteor Staff, raining meteors down on whichever Eye you happen to be bouncing on.

title: Lunatic Cultist
content:
The Lunatic Cultist is a Hardmode, post-Golem boss. Defeating it initiates the Lunar Events, and also causes the Clothier to begin selling the Solar and Lunar Cultist sets depending on the time of day.
Unlike most bosses, the Lunatic Cultist does not drop any weapons, accessories, or materials. However, it does drop the Ancient Manipulator, a placeable crafting station used to craft many endgame items.
While the Lunatic Cultist is alive, its exclusive music Lunatic Cultist will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning ==
The Lunatic Cultist is summoned after killing the Cultists that spawn at the Dungeon's entrance after Skeletron and Golem have been defeated.


== Behavior ==
The Lunatic Cultist makes its first brief appearance at the Mysterious Tablet after all four Cultists are killed. The Lunatic Cultist is immune to damage during its summoning animation, in which it begins to draw energy from the Mysterious Tablet as glowing particles start flowing from the tablet towards it. After this, the Mysterious Tablet breaks into pieces while the Lunatic Cultist rises into the air while its mask tilts up and shakes, appearing to laugh at the player. The Lunatic Cultist then warps to a position above where the player was after it was summoned and begins using its attacks in a set pattern. Between each attack, the Lunatic Cultist teleports to a position above the player's current location.
The Lunatic Cultist has the following attacks:

Fires a burst of three / four homing, high-velocity Fireballs that explode upon contact with the player or solid blocks, inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 0.5–2.5 / 1–5 / 1.25–6.25 seconds.
Fires an Ice Mist at the player, which passes through blocks while spinning forward and firing six ice shards in a hexagonal formation over four half-second intervals before dissipating.
The angle at which the ice shards are fired will be fixed upon their first launch, and is unaffected by the spinning animation of the Ice Mist.
Summons a Lightning Orb above itself. The Lightning Orb then fires a lightning bolt at the player's current location once per 0.5 seconds, for a total of 5 lightning bolts.
Lightning bolts will only be fired when the Lightning Orb has a clear sight to the player.
In multiplayer, the Lightning Orb will fire lightning bolts at all players that are less than 125 tiles from it.
Performs a ritual to summon extra enemies. At the start of ritual, the Lunatic Cultist disappears before spawning two semi-transparent / almost opaque decoys of itself, called Ancient Cultists, while surrounding a large, glowing circular rune called the Lightning Ritual. The positions of the Lunatic Cultist and its decoys randomize each time the ritual is performed, and hitting a decoy will immediately kill it. If a decoy is killed, or the Lunatic Cultist and its decoys are unharmed for a total of 5 seconds, the ritual is considered as complete, the Lunatic Cultist and the decoys will laugh at the player, and a Phantasm Dragon will be summoned at the center of the rune. If a Phantasm Dragon is already present, an Ancient Vision is summoned instead. Decoys that were not killed during the ritual become invincible and fly in formation alongside the Lunatic Cultist and cast one homing Shadow Fireball each while it performs its usual attack patterns. These decoys will also appear during subsequent rituals. Up to a maximum of six decoys can be summoned by the Lunatic Cultist at one time, and hitting the real Lunatic Cultist during the ritual causes all / three of its summoned decoys to immediately disappear.
During this ritual, the health bar below the Lunatic Cultist will be temporarily hidden, and homing projectiles and minions are rendered incapable of targeting the Lunatic Cultist.
If the ritual is completed by leaving the Lunatic Cultist unharmed, hitting the real Lunatic Cultist before it teleports to perform subsequent attacks will still cause decoys to disappear; the Phantasm Dragon or Ancient Vision will still be summoned in this case, however.
The exact attack pattern of the Lunatic Cultist:

Fireball
Ice Mist
Lightning Orb
Fireball
Ice Mist
Ritual
When the Lunatic Cultist is below 50% of its maximum health (16,000 / 24,000 / 30,600), its defense drops to 27, and it changes its attack pattern, adding a new attack:

Fires two volleys of five destructible Ancient Lights that travel through blocks. Ancient Lights are spawned with 400 / 800 / 1,200 health and linger in midair before exploding upon contact with the player or after an extended period of time, making them susceptible to being targeted by homing projectiles and minions.
The decoys will not cast Shadow Fireballs during this attack.Verify
The exact attack pattern of the Lunatic Cultist when below 50% maximum health:

Fireball
Ancient Light
Lightning Orb
Ancient Light
Ice Mist
Lightning Orb
Ritual
In Expert Mode, when the Lunatic Cultist is below 50% of its maximum health, its Fireball, Ancient Light, and Lightning Orb attacks during its attack pattern has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to be replaced by the Ancient Doom attack:

Summons destructible Ancient Dooms in open spaces around the player. If not destroyed by the player, the Ancient Doom will disperse into four purple Prophecy's End projectiles in the cardinal directions after 7 seconds, dealing massive amounts of damage (especially in Master Mode).
A base amount of 3 Ancient Dooms will be summoned during the attack, plus 3 extra Ancient Dooms for each existing decoy, capped at 9 Ancient Dooms summoned per attack.
Ancient Dooms will be summoned in a 41×41-tile square area centered on the player, and they cannot be summoned in solid blocks.
The chance for this attack to replace basic attacks increases to 1/4 (25%) when the Lunatic Cultist reaches 33% maximum health (16,000 / 20,400), and further increases to 1/3 (33.33%) after reaching 25% maximum health (12,000 / 15,300).
This attack will not be performed if there are at least 10 Ancient Dooms existing in the world, or the targeted player is more than 125 tiles away from the Lunatic Cultist.
The Lunatic Cultist visibly laughs at the player while executing the attack.


== Homing projectile resistance ==
The Lunatic Cultist will only take 75% of the damage from homing projectiles, with this damage reduction being applied before defense. The following is a list of homing projectiles that deal reduced damage to the Lunatic Cultist:


== Aftermath ==
Once the Lunatic Cultist is killed, the Lunar Events will be initiated with the message “Celestial creatures are invading!”
Additionally:

The Clothier will begin selling the Solar Cultist Clothes during the day and the Lunar Cultist Clothes at night.
The Lunatic Cultist emote  is unlocked.


=== Lunar Events ===

Every time the Lunatic Cultist is defeated, the Lunar Events will begin. During this, four celestial pillars will spawn in the world, each themed around a damage class. Defeating all four pillars will summon the final boss.


== Notes ==
Defeating the Lunatic Cultist will also fully unlock the Bestiary entries for the Phantasm Dragon and Ancient Vision, even if they were not encountered during the fight.
The Lunatic Cultist targets every player, so if one is too far away from it (e.g. by using a Magic Mirror or Recall Potion), it will despawn.
If a player teleports away before the Lunatic Cultist's spawning animation finishes, the tablet will finish its animation while the Lunatic Cultist despawns.
If the player loses against the Lunatic Cultist or it despawns, it cannot be fought again immediately. Instead, the player has to wait for the Lunatic Devotees and Cultist Archers to respawn at the Dungeon, which takes 12 minutes (12 in-game hours) from the destruction of the Mysterious Tablet.
The Cultists will never spawn if Skeletron has not yet been defeated in the current world, since the Old Man takes spawning priority over the Cultists.
Most homing projectiles and minions will not target the real Lunatic Cultist during its ritual, although minions that deal contact damage may accidentally damage it. Some exceptions include projectiles produced via on-hit effects such as the Flaming Jack projectiles from The Horseman's Blade and the Spectre Mask's damaging orbs, which will still target the real Lunatic Cultist.
The Lunatic Cultist will always spawn at the Dungeon entrance's original location, regardless of modifications (similar to the four Cultists), meaning that if the four Cultists are teleported or otherwise moved away, and then killed there, the Lunatic Cultist will still spawn, and instantly despawn if the player is far enough away from the Dungeon entrance.
Removing the floor at the entrance to the Dungeon (where the Old Man spawns) will prevent the Cultists from spawning.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

The player should avoid defeating the Lunatic Cultist if they are not yet ready for the Lunar Events. Beating the Lunatic Cultist causes the Lunar Events to begin immediately, and there is no way to de-summon them thereafter (aside from defeating all of the Celestial Pillars).
The real Lunatic Cultist can be distinguished from its decoys in a number of ways:
The real Cultist has pointed, angry eyes, while the decoys' eyes are round and neutral.
The real Cultist has a line on its hood while the decoys do not.
The real Cultist does not emit light, while the decoys do; however, this may only be apparent if fought at night.
When the ritual starts, the real Cultist is the copy that is furthest away from the player.
When hovered over, decoys will always display as having 10000/10000 health, while the real Cultist will display its true health value instead.
Using Autopause grants as much time as needed for identifying the real Cultist.
Attacking a decoy Cultist is not a bad idea if the player uses the Vampire Knives. The resulting Phantasm Dragon is very long and may be easily targeted to restore some life.
Many of the Lunatic Cultist's attacks can be blocked by hiding behind solid blocks, including its lightning bolts and fireballs. A weapon that attacks through blocks or a yoyo can be used to deal damage.
There is little reason to farm the Lunatic Cultist itself, as its only non-vanity drops are Greater Healing Potions and the Ancient Manipulator, the latter only needing to be obtained once. However, defeating it is the only way to access the Lunar Events and Lunar Fragments.
If the lock on mechanic selects the Lunatic Cultist as the target, the target is dispelled every time it teleports.
Depending on the world size and generation, one of the Celestial Pillars will often spawn immediately within the vicinity of the player upon defeating the Lunatic Cultist. If this happens when the player is unprepared, and the background changes to indicate a Celestial Pillar has spawned near the player, it is recommended to immediately pick up the Lunatic Cultist's drops and teleport back to a safe base using a Magic Mirror or Recall Potion to prevent from being unexpectedly ambushed by dangerous enemies spawned from the Lunar Events.


== Trivia ==

The Lunatic Cultist is the smallest boss in the game and the only one without an awakening message.
The Lunatic Cultist's attacks appear to be based on the four Celestial Pillars from the Lunar Events, and/or their class counterparts.
The fireball attack mirrors the Solar Pillar's meteor spray and flaming motif.
The lightning attack references the Vortex Pillar's thundering background and its Vortexians' lightning strikes.
The ice attack, as well as the Ancient Dooms, while not directly visually reminiscent of the Nebula Pillar, parallels the unique projectile mechanics of many magic weapons.
The summoning circle corresponds to the summoner class by creating clones and evoking additional enemies, and the Phantasm Dragon bears resemblance to the Stardust Dragon. The Ancient Lights also share a resemblance to the Stardust Pillar's coloration and motifs.
Crowno's set is visually similar to the appearance of the Lunatic Cultist and was added to the game much earlier, indicating that it possibly served as an inspiration for the Lunatic Cultist. However, the Lunatic Cultist was designed first, according to Crowno.
The Lunatic Cultist's appearance, especially its mask, resembles a plague doctor costume, which was an outfit worn by plague doctors during European epidemics of the bubonic plague in the 16th and 17th centuries that were intended to protect them from airborne diseases.
 The Lunatic Cultist was once named "Insane Cultist" during development, according to an unimplemented achievement.
The Lunatic Cultist has an Expert Mode Treasure Bag in Terraria's game files, but it is unobtainable, as it never actually drops it.
The reason for this may simply stem from the Lunatic Cultist's overall lack of distinct drops aside from the Ancient Manipulator.
The decoys share map icons with the real Lunatic Cultist.
This is the only boss whose music starts before the boss itself spawns, making it easier to obtain the Music Box (Lunatic Cultist).
The term lunatic is nowadays usually used as an informal synonym for insane, mentally ill, etc. The word itself, however, originated from the fact that diseases were historically thought to have been caused by the moon, tying in with the moon-themed events following this boss.
The Lunatic Cultist, Brain of Cthulhu, Moon Lord, King Slime, Queen Slime, Empress of Light, and, in Expert Mode, Duke Fishron are the only bosses that can teleport.
When the Lunatic Cultist is killed, the status message “Celestial creatures are invading!” appears before “Lunatic Cultist has been defeated!”, probably hinting that the summoning ritual might have finished before the Lunatic Cultist died.
When the Lunatic Cultist despawns after a player has teleported away from it, it plays its dying animation.
Wearing the Lunatic Cultist Mask and the Lunar Cultist Robe causes the player to look very similar to the Lunatic Cultist, however, the boss is still taller than the player, and is therefore distinguishable.
The Lunatic Cultist is one of the few bosses in which all of its attacks' damage, other than contact damage, does not increase linearly in Master Mode.
It is the only non-event boss not to have an Expert Mode-exclusive drop.
The Lunatic Cultist has the most types of "servants" out of all the bosses, totaling four.
If the Lunatic Cultist picks up coins in Expert Mode, the real Cultist will shimmer slightly while its decoys will not.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, the Lunatic Cultist and their cult worshipped Cthulhu, and sought to restore/resurrect their master. To this end, they forced the Mechanic to forge the mechanical bosses as new mechanical organs for Cthulhu; however, as the mechanical brain was never completed before the events of the game, this plan never came to fruition.
 The Bestiary entry for the Lunatic Cultist: "A fanatical leader hell-bent on bringing about the apocalypse by reviving the great Cthulhu through behind-the-scenes scheming."

title: Silenced
content:
Silenced is a debuff that prevents the player from using any item which uses mana, stopping them from using magic weapons and summon weapons. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it does not affect summon weapons.
The debuff can be prevented from afflicting the player by equipping the Megaphone or its derivatives.


== Causes ==


=== From enemy ===


=== From debuff ===


=== Other ===


== Notes ==
The Silenced debuff will still prevent the player from using the Space Gun with a full set of Meteor armor, despite it costing no mana.
The Silenced debuff only prevents item usage via ⚒ Use / Attack. Items used via other methods can still be used (e.g. the Forbidden armor's set bonus).
Although inflicted by a small pool of enemies, it is recommended that mages worried about this debuff should bring a Megaphone or make a Ankh Shield as the debuff is extremely deadly when there are many enemies on screen.


== Trivia ==
The effect of Silenced is related to how in popular fiction, casting magic sometimes requires saying certain words out loud. Therefore, being silenced would prevent casting any magic.

title: War Table
content:
The War Table is an animated furniture item which fulfills a house's table requirement that is dropped by the Dark Mage and the Ogre during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/8 (12.5%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 3.
Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the War Table grants the Strategist buff, which increases the player's sentry capacity by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
Unlike equipment buff items, the War Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 5×4 tiles being available.


== Tips ==
The player may wish to complete the Old One's Army event at Tier 1 (prior to defeating any mechanical boss, which upgrades the event to Tier 2) as the War Table becomes significantly more difficult to obtain after.
Obtaining it before Tier 2 also makes completing said tier easier: normal sentries are not affected by the Etherian Mana cap that Old One's Army sentries are subject to in the event.
The War Table can be used outside of the Old One's Army event, and it increases the summoning cap of any sentry.


== Trivia ==
The War Table is an item originally from Dungeon Defenders 2, where it is used to select which map to play next.


== See also ==
War Table at the Dungeon Defenders 2 Wiki
War Table Banner


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Now drop from Ogres.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Stack limit increased from 999 to 9999.
Now grants the Strategist buff when activated, which increases the player's maximum number of sentries.
Desktop 1.3.4: Introduced.

Console 1.17: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.1096.2: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.

title: Santa Claus
content:
Santa Claus is a unique Hardmode NPC vendor who sells various decorative Christmas-themed items. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
The Frost Legion event has been completed at least once.
Santa Claus will only spawn during the Christmas seasonal event (December 15 – December 31, or unlocked for one in-game day outside of those dates by reaching the Frost Moon event's 15th wave), after which he dies.
Santa Claus will defend himself against nearby enemies by throwing baubles.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Santa Claus will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Tips ==

Christmas can be activated at any time by setting the device's date to any date between December 15th and 31st. If a change of the device's time is undesired, third-party software such as RunAsDate allow launching the game with a simulated time and date.
 Change the computer's date in the system settings.
 Disconnect from  Xbox Live /  PSN and change the console time.
 Disconnect from automatic date/time updates and change the time manually. This might not work on all devices.
 Go to "System Settings" and go to "System", click on "Date and Time", turn off "Synchronize Clock via Internet", and set the time there.
Changing the time back to normal will cause him to die at the next sunrise.
If he is spawned in while it is not Christmas via TShock or similar third-party software, he will die instantly.
As long as the Frost Legion is defeated once in a world, he will arrive every time Christmas content is active in that world. They do not need to be defeated each Christmas.


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
If a Snow Globe is obtained and brought into a pre-Hardmode world, Santa Claus can be obtained outside Hardmode by defeating the Frost Legion and having available housing for him.
Santa Claus sells 39 items at any given time, more than any other NPC.
Two other NPCs sell more items only during certain conditions. The Golfer sells 39 items only if the player has a golf score of 2000 or higher. If the Golfer is happy enough, he will additionally sell a pylon, therefore expanding his supplies to 40. Also, the Tavernkeep will have 40 items available once Golem has been defeated.
It is not possible to buy back items sold to this NPC since the last item slot cannot hold any sold items.
In the  Console version, he has a description in the housing section saying "A jolly old fellow".Verify
“Ho ho ho, and a bottle of... Egg Nog!” is a reference to the fictional sea song “Dead Man's Chest”, originally from Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel Treasure Island which was first published in 1883. The song contains the verse "Yo ho ho, and a bottle of rum".
The Pirate also makes this reference, saying, “Yo ho ho and a bottle of....blinkroots!”
He has the least number of possible names out of all NPCs, having only one.
In the housing menu, he is described as "Santa Claus the Santa Claus".
Santa hating the Tax Collector is likely a reference to Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol, where protagonist Ebenezer Scrooge (whom the Tax Collector is based on) despises everything to do with Christmas, hence Santa hating him.
This is the only NPC to love or hate a biome – all other NPCs simply like or dislike certain biomes.
Santa Claus' interaction quote during a Thunderstorm, “Oh ho... whoah! There goes Dasher. There went Donner, too!”, is a reference to the fact that Donner is the German word for thunder, as well as one of Santa's reindeer.
Santa Claus' Shimmered form could be a reference to the Ded Moroz, a legendary figure in Slavic mythology who is similar to Santa Claus.
Besides the Old Man, Santa Claus is the only NPC to not display his name underneath his portrait when speaking to him.
 The Bestiary entry for the Santa Claus: "Only present during a specific time of year, Santa Claus makes a big entrance and an even bigger, rather explosive exit. Ho! Ho! Ho!"


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Fixed Santa Claus' portrait not showing his name.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: Fixed Santa Claus having a Traveling Merchant Party quote rather than his own.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Now attacks enemies in sight by throwing baubles.
Sprite updated.
Desktop 1.2.2: Now sells the Christmas Tree and items to decorate it.
Desktop 1.1.1: Introduced. Sells Santa Hat, Santa Shirt, Santa Pants, Red Light, Green Light, and Blue Light.

Console-Release: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile 1.2.10061: Santa now requires the Frost Legion to be defeated before he can spawn.
Mobile-Release: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Moon Lord
content:
The Moon Lord is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist boss. He is the final boss of the  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile versions of Terraria.
While the Moon Lord is alive, his exclusive music Moon Lord will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Lunar Boss (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning and spawning ==
The Moon Lord will spawn after destroying the four Celestial Pillars or can be summoned manually using a Celestial Sigil in any world where Golem has been defeated. The status message “Impending doom approaches...” indicates the Moon Lord's spawning countdown. During the countdown, the screen will go dim and all objects, tiles, and walls will oscillate back and forth, and then go back to normal, and the sound volume will gradually decrease, eventually becoming completely silent. If the Moon Lord is spawned by destroying the Celestial Pillars, the countdown lasts 60 seconds, and the screen effect will appear 5 times; each time the screen will go darker and all objects and walls will oscillate more violently. If using a Celestial Sigil to summon the Moon Lord, the countdown lasts 12 seconds, and the screen effect will only appear once. After the countdown, the screen flashes for 1 second, then the Moon Lord spawns.


== Behavior ==
A special void shader will be applied while the Moon Lord is on-screen: the sky will turn completely dark and the world will appear hazy and shadowy with blur effects. In multiplayer, this only happens to players who are within 130 tiles of the Moon Lord's location. 
The heart in the Moon Lord's chest is his core, which is the part that must be destroyed in order to defeat him, but it only becomes vulnerable when all of the body's eye targets are destroyed. The three eyes, contained in his forehead and both of his hands, are periodically closed via an eyelid, and may only be damaged when they are open. There is a 20 second loop for this eyelid behavior in the head eye. The eye stays mostly shut for around 14-15 seconds. When it opens, it shoots 2 Phantasmal Bolts in 1 second than a Phantasmal Deathray for around 3 seconds. After that, the head eye closes again in arond a quarter of a second. The hand eyes have a 10 second loop. It is open for most of the time, firing  Phantasmal Bolts and Phantasmal Eyes, then summons 6 Phantasmal Spheres over 3 seconds, snapping shut after. When destroyed, each eye then spawns an invulnerable True Eye of Cthulhu.
The Moon Lord will teleport to the nearest player in a large flash of white light (which lasts 1 second) upon being summoned, if the targeted player moves more than 150 tiles away, or upon the player despawning, if the player he is targeting dies. The Moon Lord will attempt to position himself with the player directly in front of him, just below his head, while positioning his two hands on either side of the player some distance away. This positioning can put the core below an arena surface, possibly blocking damage from weapons that do not pass through blocks.
When the Moon Lord is alive, no enemies or critters will spawn near players that are less than 281.25 tiles from the Moon Lord's Core.


=== Attacks ===

The Moon Lord performs attacks with eyes on its hands and head. Upon defeating each eye, it detaches as a True Eye of Cthulhu to continue attacking, leaving behind a thorny crevice. True Eyes of Cthulhu are invincible and will only despawn if either all players die or the Moon Lord is defeated. Moon Lord's parts and the True Eyes of Cthulhu deal no contact damage.
Different parts of the Moon Lord each have differing attack cycle, and some parts can perform identical or similar attacks. Possible attacks from specific parts are listed below.
This section only describes attacks used by the Moon Lord. See § Attack pattern section for the order of attacks in different phases.


==== Moon Lord's Hand ====
The hand eye spins while spawning 7 Phantasmal Eyes, initially moving in random directions for 2.25 seconds. Afterward, they try to home in on the player for 1.5 seconds, gradually losing their homing ability over this duration, moving at 31 mph to 72 mph in this state. The Phantasmal Eyes explode upon colliding with a solid block, after 10 seconds, or reaching less than 1.875 tiles away from the player, dealing damage in a 1.875×1.875-tile square.
The Phantasmal Eyes can only dive down when homing. This means that they will ignore players above them.
Moves away from the core while its eye spawns 6 Phantasmal Spheres over the course of 3 seconds. The Phantasmal Spheres initially hovers at where they are spawned. After another 1.37 seconds, the hand eye shuts, redirecting the Phantasmal Spheres to charge at 123 mph.
By default, the Phantasmal Spheres will charge in the direction of the player. However, if the player is positioned between 0–21.875 tiles above the hand eye's height when the Phantasmal Spheres are redirected, the Phantasmal Spheres will charge diagonally downwards, disregarding the player's location.
Phantasmal Spheres do not deal damage during the first second after they are spawned. They can pass through blocks, and dissipate between 5.95 seconds to 7.2 seconds after spawning.
Looks at the player before firing 2 Phantasmal Bolts in quick succession. Phantasmal Bolts travel at 164 mph, pass through blocks, and will attempt to aim at where the player would be after 0.33 seconds based on their current speed/direction. The attack lasts 1.5 seconds, with the aiming direction indicated by a line starting from the eye. A sound effect is played at 0.92 seconds, and the aiming direction will be locked at 1.18 seconds. This means the player can dodge these shots by suddenly changing their speed/direction.


==== Moon Lord's Head ====
The head eye shines brightly and charges for 3 seconds before firing a Phantasmal Deathray: a large laser with a maximum length of 150 tiles that sweeps through a 120° sector over the course of 3 seconds. The starting location of the Phantasmal Deathray and its sweep direction depends on the location of the target: if the target is to the left of the Moon Lord, it starts at 60° counter-clockwise from the direction to the player and sweeps clockwise; if the target is to the right of the Moon Lord, it starts at 60° clockwise from the direction to the player and sweeps counter-clockwise.
Phantasmal Deathrays do not deal damage during the first 0.33 seconds after they are spawned.
By default, the Phantasmal Deathray is cut off by solid blocks. However, if the line of sight between the center of Moon Lord's Head and the player is blocked by solid blocks, the length of the Phantasmal Deathray will be set to the distance from Moon Lord's Head to the player plus 9.375 tiles (still capped at 150 tiles), causing it to pass through solid blocks to reach the player.
Existing Phantasmal Deathray immediately disappears if the head eye is killed.
If the For the Worthy special world seed is active, the head eye also erupts 30 Moon Boulders after each Phantasmal Deathray attack. Moon Boulders share similar behaviors to Bouncy Boulders, ricocheting on solid blocks for up to four times, dissipating upon the fifth time. They are much faster than Bouncy Boulders (reaching a top speed of about 230 mph) and ignore the invincibility frames given by the Moon Lord's other attacks. Moon Boulders also dissipate after 1 minute 30 seconds, or if they hit a solid surface when rolling on the ground.
The Moon Lord opens his mouth and attempts to attach Moon Leeches to all players within 187.5 tiles from the mouth. Moon Leech inflicts the Moon Bite debuff to the associated player for 14 seconds / 16 seconds, which prevents any lifesteal effects for its duration.
One Moon Leech Clot is spawned for each player inflicted with the Moon Bite debuff at 2 seconds / 3 seconds / 4 seconds after the Moon Leeches are spawned (i.e. 3 Moon Leech Clots for each player). Moon Leech Clots are enemies that take 1.5 seconds to travel from the player to the Moon Lord's mouth. Any Moon Leech Clot that reaches the mouth without being killed restores a total of 1,000 health to Moon Lord's parts (ones that have not yet been defeated).
The health restoration priority (from high to low) is Moon Lord's Head, Core, the Hand to the left of the player, and the Hand to the right of the player. If a part restores to full health before depleting the 1,000 health heal amount, the remaining health will be restored to parts with lower priority.
If the player is able to outrun the Moon Leech, no debuff will be inflicted, and the Moon Leech will despawn at 5.5 seconds after spawning.
Moon Leech attack no longer appears after the head eye is killed.
The head eye fires 2 Phantasmal Bolts (with the same behavior as the hand's Phantasmal Bolt attack).


==== True Eye of Cthulhu ====
The True Eyes of Cthulhu have attacks similar to the hand and head eyes. When idle, they will try to hover at 12.5 tiles above the nearest player, and stay 6.25 tiles away from each other to prevent stacking together.

Fires 2 Phantasmal Bolts at the player, with the same behavior as the hand's Phantasmal Bolt attack.
The eye spawns 6 Phantasmal Spheres in a hexagonal formation around itself over the course of 1 second. After 0.75 seconds, the eye "throws" Phantasmal Spheres towards the player at 123 mph, accompanied by a sound effect. This attack does not have the height restriction of the hand's Phantasmal Sphere attack: the projectiles will always charge in the direction of the player.
Phantasmal Spheres from the True Eyes of Cthulhu deals no damage during the first 0.5 seconds after they are spawned.
The eye spins while spawning 14 Phantasmal Eyes over the course of 2.33 seconds. Phantasmal Eyes has the same behavior as the hand's Phantasmal Eye attack.
The eye shines brightly and charges for 3 seconds before firing a Phantasmal Deathray, with its maximum length, duration, sweeping speed, and direction identical to the head's Phantasmal Deathray attack. Phantasmal Deathray fired by True Eye of Cthulhu is 60% thinner and cannot pass through blocks.
When a True Eye of Cthulhu is performing the Phantasmal Deathray attack, the void shader visual effect will be centered on it, causing the screen to get darkened when the player moves away from it.
The attacks a True Eye of Cthulhu can perform are unrelated with the part that spawned it. For example, a True Eye of Cthulhu spawned from Moon Lord's Hand can still perform the Phantasmal Deathray attack, while a True Eye of Cthulhu spawned from Moon Lord's Head is able to perform the Phantasmal Eye attack.
When performing most of their attacks, the eyes will not actively pursue the player. The will catch up with the player after an attack ends.


=== Attack pattern ===
The exact attack patterns used by the Moon Lord's parts are listed below.
Initially, when no eyes are defeated, each eye will loop through their attacks based on a set timer. Hand eyes require 600 ticks per loop, while the Head eye requires 1200 ticks per loop.
The eyes are only vulnerable when they are open, and become invulnerable when they are fully closed. The Hand eyes take 21 ticks (0.35 seconds) to fully close, while the Head eye takes 15 ticks (0.25 seconds) to fully close.

The True Eye of Cthulhu also loops through attacks based on a set timer, which requires 1200 ticks per loop. Additionally, when an eye is killed, the spawned True Eye of Cthulhu will align its attack timer based on the Head eye's timer. A newly spawned True Eye of Cthulhu's attack timer will be directly set to a certain value, determined by the following formula:
[math]\displaystyle{ \text{True Eye of Cthulhu timer}=\left(\text{Head eye timer}-400\times\text{Amount of existing True Eyes of Cthulhu}-588\right)\mod1200 }[/math]

[math]\displaystyle{ \text{Head eye timer} }[/math] is the 1200-tick timer of the Head eye. It still counts normally after the Head eye is defeated.
If the value of [math]\displaystyle{ \text{True Eye of Cthulhu timer} }[/math] is lower than 0 after calculation, add 1200 to it.
If the resulting timer falls inside an attack phase, the remaining time of that phase will be treated as hovering time, and the True Eye of Cthulhu will start attacking when the next attack phase arrives. If the resulting timer falls inside a hover phase, the True Eye of Cthulhu will start attacking as soon as the current hovering phase ends.
This ensures each eye's attacks will be offset from each other by 1/3 of a cycle.


== Parts ==


== Aftermath ==
The Moon Lord has a unique death animation that lasts 10 seconds. At the first second of the death animation, all existing Moon Lord's projectiles and Moon Leech Clots will be removed. After defeating the Moon Lord, the credits will appear while the song Journey's End plays. Besides his other loot, the Moon Lord always drops Luminite, allowing the player to craft endgame armor sets, tools, furniture, and accessories.
Additionally:

The Princess will begin selling Music Box (Journey's End).
The Steampunker will begin selling Yellow Solution, White Solution, and Brown Solution used for the Clentaminator.
The Dye Trader will begin rewarding the player with Skiphs' Blood in exchange for Strange Plants.
The Cyborg will sell the Portal Gun Station, so long as the player has the Portal Gun from the Moon Lord in their inventory.
The Traveling Merchant now has the chance to sell the Not a Kid, nor a Squid and Moonman & Company paintings.
The Rod of Harmony, Terraformer, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket become available via Shimmer transmutation.
Hairstyle 134 is unlocked if the Martian Madness has been defeated already.
The world icon gains a special border in the world selection menu.
The Moon Lord emote  is unlocked.


== Notes ==
Invincibility frames inflicted by the Moon Lord's attacks (except Moon Boulders) belong to invincibility group 2. This means that invincibility frames granted by other attacks are bypassed by Moon Lord's attacks.
If the player leaves the world after the message “Impending doom approaches...” is displayed, the Moon Lord will not spawn.
This could be useful for players who are not ready or willing to fight the Moon Lord yet and/or if they do not have enough Lunar Fragments to use.
Since projectiles deal lower damage to NPCs than they do to players, NPCs are unlikely to be killed by the projectile attacks of the Moon Lord.
Moon Lord's shader visual effect can be replicated with the Void Monolith.
In Expert Mode, the Treasure Bag will not drop a Portal Gun if the player opening it already has a Portal Gun in their inventory. However, he will always drop it in Classic Mode.
The Moon Lord appears behind all blocks and walls, similar to a background object. This effect is purely visual.
Consequently, he can be made completely invisible when behind enough opaque blocks or walls.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Keeping a distance while dodging the Moon Lord's attacks is crucial. In particular, his Phantasmal Deathray should be avoided at all costs.
Useful items that increase the player's mobility include Gravitation Potions, fast wings like the Fishron, Betsy's, or Empress Wings, the Rod of Discord, items allowing to dash (e.g. the Tabi or its upgrade, the Master Ninja Gear), the Soaring Insignia, and numerous mount-summoning items like the Gelatinous Pillion, Shrimpy Truffle, Cosmic Car Key, or Witch's Broom. The player might also consider constructing a skybridge made out of Asphalt Blocks or Minecart Tracks (with a minecart boosted by the Minecart Upgrade Kit).
Items that provide high horizontal speed (Minecart Upgrade Kit-boosted minecarts, Soaring Insignia with hoverable wings, Hexxed Branch, etc.) allow the player to outrange the Phantasmal Deathray from the True Eyes of Cthulhu.
Using homing weapons or ammo like Chlorophyte Bullets allow the player to focus on dodging.
It is possible to avoid the deathray by staying close to the Moon Lord's head, and moving up and around the central eye as it fires the ray. The ray does not sweep as quickly when near its origin point, due to the nature of rotational movement, so being as close to its origin as possible makes it easier to maneuver around.
Due to the Phantasmal Deathray only checks the line of sight between the center of the Moon Lord's Head and the player, and its hitbox cannot fit through 2–3 tiles wide openings, it can still be blocked by solid blocks below the head eye with an opening in the center.
Teleporting away from the Moon Lord to get healing from the Nurse might result in her death, due to the Moon Lord immediately teleporting to the player.
In multiplayer, the Moon Lord will attack the nearest player. Players can take turns teleporting home to get healing from the Nurse.
The Moon Lord is vulnerable to almost all debuffs, most notably Ichor and Betsy's Curse, which can dramatically speed up the fight. However, since the Moon Lord's eyes remove all debuffs when they close, the player will have to reapply them accordingly.
It is advisable to kill the eye on the head first. It remains closed for significantly longer than the eyes in the hands, and killing it will prevent the Phantasmal Deathray and Moon Leech attacks from occurring. If the player waits to kill the head last, they may have to deal with two True Eyes of Cthulhu for a longer amount of time.
Moon Bite only disables the lifesteal from Vampire Knives and the Spectre Hood's set bonus. Other sources of health regeneration such as Life Drain and Life Nebula are not affected by the debuff.
Some of the Moon Lord's attacks can be avoided using the 200 NPC spawn limit, and the True Eyes of Cthulhu can be prevented from spawning completely if the limit is reached.
Due to the Moon Lord's attacks bypassing regular attacks' invincibility frames, special setups are required to bypass his attacks.
Moon Leech Clots will always reach the Moon Lord's mouth in the same amount of time. They travel toward it at a variable rate, remaining completely stationary (or at least apparently so) if the Moon Lord is in his default position behind the player. As a result of this, though it may seem counterintuitive, it is actually beneficial to be closer to the mouth to destroy Moon Leech Clots, as they will not move away as quickly.
While the Phantasmal Spheres the Moon Lord shoots can pierce all NPCs, the Phantasmal Bolts get destroyed upon contact with an NPC, potentially being a viable option for players trying to avoid the bolts.
For those farming the Moon Lord for the Meowmere and Star Wrath in order to craft the Zenith: For each kill, there is a 58.33% chance of obtaining neither, a 38.88% chance of obtaining one, and a 2.77% chance of obtaining both.
The loot dropped by the Moon Lord is calculated at the end of its death animation. A player in Journey Mode can defeat the Moon Lord at a lower difficulty, then adjust the slider while its death animation is playing to change the loot pool to Expert or Master.


== Trivia ==
Despite a mid-development comment by Cenx that this would not be the case, the Moon Lord resembles common depictions of Cthulhu, a creature first imagined by H. P. Lovecraft in his 1928 short story The Call of Cthulhu. Fans commonly speculated prior to the release of 1.3 that Cthulhu would be the final Terraria boss (which in turn arose partly due to an early concept design floated by the development team).
Terraria's final boss was originally going to be the Moon itself descending on the world, but Cenx later stated that this idea had been scrapped.
Due to the colors of the boss and the names of a few of his projectiles, this boss may have been inspired by the Vortex Pillar.
Despite being the final boss, the Moon Lord is one of many bosses with the fewest debuff immunities, being immune only to Confused and Shimmering.
NPCs are unable to attack the Moon Lord.
According to Cenx, spriting the Moon Lord took over a month.
The Moon Lord is the only boss with a unique death animation sequence.
The Moon Lord's Core still shows as beating during his death animation.
Redigit once joked that if the community could put together 10,000 signatures and 15 dollars, he would make the lower half of the Moon Lord a boss.
This was not implemented, but in the 1.4.0.1 update, the legs of the Moon Lord have been introduced as the Moon Lord Legs item, obtainable from Chests in drunk worlds.
The Moon Lord seems to share some mechanics with two pre-Hardmode bosses, including Skeletron, having multiple parts that each are destroyable, and the Brain of Cthulhu, requiring the player to defeat separate parts before truly damaging the boss.
The Moon Lord is the only boss who drops three Expert-exclusive items in his Treasure Bag.
The Moon Lord drops the most coins of any boss, and overall any enemy, in the game.
In Expert Mode and Master Mode, his coin drops are higher than the total coin drops of all the Hardmode bosses in the game.
(Desktop version) While fighting the Moon Lord or during the period before it spawns, an eye, presumably the True Eye of Cthulhu in one of the Moon Lord's hands, appears on RGB-enabled keyboards.
In the past Redigit said the Moon Lord is the father of the Guide. This statement was most likely a joke and is not considered official lore.
If a body part of the Moon Lord is spawned in separately, e.g. using mods or hacks, the music track Boss 1 plays instead of the Moon Lord track. Autopause needs to be enabled for this to work.
The Moon Lord appears in the video game Palworld as a part of a crossover.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, though it was initially theorized (and joked by staff) that the Moon Lord was Cthulhu's brother, it appears that he is Cthulhu itself, or at least is what it implies. This entity was detrimental to existence, and was finally banished by the Dryads, an ancient race of whom the Dryad NPC is the only survivor, ripped out his organs and banished it to the moon. It further appears that the Celestial Events and his eventual battle are his final attempt at total conquest, as stated directly.
In the same post where the developers, namely Arkhayla, joked that the Moon Lord was Cthulhu's brother, they also said his name was Steve. However, this has been confirmed to not be true.
The eyes on Moon Lord's body are named True Eye of Cthulhu, overall solidifying his true identity.
 The Bestiary entry for the Moon Lord: "The mastermind behind all terrors which befall the world, freed from his lunar prison. Practically a god, his power knows no limits."
The Moon Lord's Bestiary entry is the last entry listed and is the only entry that does not have biome/event filters or a background, instead having an empty black background.
The Moon Lord's Bestiary entry has cthulhu as one of its search aliases.


== Gallery ==

		
		
		
		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: 
Added warnings to several attacks.
Phantasmal Eye attack now stops homing after 1.5 seconds, and its explosion range reduced from 9×9-tile to 1.875×1.875-tile.
Phantasmal Bolt attacks now lock their direction briefly before shooting.
Phantasmal Spheres' and Phantasmal Deathrays' contact damage is disabled briefly after they spawn.
Phantasmal Deathray locks its target earlier, allowing for better coordination in multiplayer.
Moon Lord's void shader now centers on the True Eye of Cthulhu whenever it fires a deathray.
Moon Lord and True Eye of Cthulhu no longer deal contact damage.
True Eyes of Cthulhu maintain better distance from each other and overlap less.
True Eyes of Cthulhu now synchronize their attack patterns with Moon Lord, preventing some impossible-to-dodge situations.

title: Optic Staff
content:
The Optic Staff is a Hardmode, post-The Twins summon weapon that summons a miniature version of The Twins as minions. The pair of minions, named Spazmamini and Retanimini, fly towards enemies to dash through them and fire lasers at them, respectively. Each pair of Twins counts as a single minion towards the minion slot cap.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
Up to 22 Twins can appear at once with maximum minion capacity, as opposed to the usual 11, due to a pair counting as one minion.
Spazmamini's charge deals the listed damage of the weapon (24 base damage) while Retanimini's laser deals 115% of the listed damage (27 base damage).
Retanimini's lasers are fired at a rate of once every 0.75 seconds on average.
Spazmamini charges at enemies once every 0.67 seconds on average.
Spazmamini applies 12 ticks of static invincibility frames upon hitting an enemy.
The Twins minions can target enemies up to 125 tiles away.
They will, however, attempt to return to the player's side if their distance from the player is more than 75 tiles, which can interrupt their attacks.
Spazmamini will only charge at its target when its distance from the target is less than 31.25 tiles.
Retanimini's lasers move at a speed of 123 mph, emit light, and disappear after 1.67 seconds if they do not hit an enemy or solid block.


== Tips ==
Unlike most flying minions, the Twins cannot pass through blocks unless the player has moved out of range.
The Twins are good against dense enemy crowds such as those in the Solar Eclipse, Pumpkin Moon and Frost Moon.


== Trivia ==
Unlike the actual boss, the minions are not connected by a tendril. Furthermore, Spazmamini does not spew Cursed Flames like Spazmatism does.
It is possible to get non-matching amounts of Retaniminis and Spazmaminis by maxing the projectile cap and lowering it.


== History ==

Base damage increased from 21 to 24 (Spazmamini's damage is 100% of base damage).
Retanimini's damage scaling reduced from 1.25× to 1.15× of base damage (still a slight increase due to the increased base).

Retanimini's lasers no longer pierce. As a result, they are no longer impacted by immune frames.
Retanimini damage increased from 24 to 26.
Spazmamini damage reduced from 30 to 21.
Spazmamini now has more flexible charging range when pursuing targets.
Twin minions now return to the player more quickly.

Enemy immune frames caused by Spazmamini and Retanimini attacks have been reduced from 16 to 12.
Increased Spazmamini's movement speed while pursuing enemies.
Desktop 1.4.1: Now use independent immunity timers.

Added requirement of 10 mana.
Fixed bug where Twin Minion pairs could become uneven or re-summoning would fail.

title: Golem
content:
Golem is a Hardmode, post-Plantera boss fought in the Jungle Temple. It attacks the player by stomping on them, launching its fists, and firing barrages of projectiles. Defeating Golem is a prerequisite for unlocking the Lunar Events, the Martian Madness, and Tier 3 of the Old One's Army.
While Golem is alive, its exclusive music Boss 4 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning ==
Golem is summoned by using a Lihzahrd Power Cell at the Lihzahrd Altar located in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple, at any time, and only if the current world is in Hardmode after Plantera is defeated. Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Lihzahrd Altar, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is summoned directly above the altar.
The Lihzahrd Altar can be relocated after being mined with a Picksaw or better. However, Golem will become enraged while outside of the Underground Jungle.


== Behavior ==
Golem consists of four parts: the body, the head attached to the body, and one fist at the end of both of its arms. The body is invincible initially and the head must be defeated in order to damage the body; defeating the body concludes the boss fight. It is not required to defeat the two fists, similar to Skeletron's hands.


=== First form ===
Golem continually jumps into the air and endeavors to land on top of the player, with a short cooldown after each jump. When the line of sight between the player and Golem's body is blocked by solid blocks, it will leap onto the player, allowing it to pass through all solid blocks (similar to the behavior of a Biome Mimic).
Golem periodically launches its fists that extend from chains at the player. The fists can travel through solid blocks but have a limited range, and glow bright orange shortly before being launched. A fist is launched more frequently as its health is decreased. Defeating a fist causes Golem to jump around more often, which compounds when both fists are destroyed.
Golem's head shoots ricocheting fireballs from its mouth which have a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 5–7 / 10–14 / 15–21 seconds. When the head falls below half health (12,500 / 18,750 / 23,906 HP), its eyes begin to fire yellow lasers called Eye Beams at the player that can travel through blocks. Golem's head faces towards the side that the player is on (for instance, facing left if the player is to the left of the head). Only one of Golem's eyes will fire an Eye Beam if the head is facing left or right, but if the player is horizontally aligned with the head, it will look straight ahead and fire two Eye Beams at once in this case, one from each eye.
When the head is below half health (as indicated by it shooting Eye Beams), the damage of the fireballs is increased from 36 / 72 / 108 to 48 / 96 / 144. Additionally, they are fired more frequently as Golem's head takes more damage:

Unlike the fireballs, the Eye Beams are not fired in regular intervals. Their cooldown is randomized instead, although it always lasts a certain minimum amount of time. This minimum cooldown is 1 second initially and decreases with the remaining health of Golem's head, down to 0.25 seconds at less than 20% HP. Furthermore, the cooldown is approximately halved while the line of sight between the player and the center of Golem's head is obstructed by solid blocks. 
The cooldowns of the fireballs and Eye Beams are even lower in multiplayer, depending on the number of players on the server.


=== Second form ===
Once the health of Golem's stone head is depleted, it detaches from its body, becomes immune to damage, and begins hovering above the player while passing through blocks. Golem's body now becomes the main target. Similar to before, the head continues firing projectiles (though it now always fires two Eye Beams at once), the body continues jumping around (now faster, and speeding up as its health is decreased), and the fists continue attacking the player if they have not been destroyed (now more frequently). The body's health must be completely depleted, at which point the invincible head is also destroyed and the fight ends.
Again, the frequency of fireballs fired from the head increases as Golem's body takes more damage:

Reducing Golem's body's health decreases the cooldown of the Eye Beams as well, and increases their damage and velocity:

A blocked line of sight increases the Eye Beam's damage by 50% and their velocity by 150%.


=== Enraged behavior ===
Golem becomes enraged while outside the Underground Jungle, causing it to jump faster and, if its head is below 50% health, fire its Eye Beams faster. It will return to its normal state upon returning to the Underground Jungle.


== Parts ==


=== First form ===


=== Second form ===


== Aftermath ==
Cultists spawn at the Dungeon's entrance which, when killed, summon the Lunatic Cultist and then the Lunar Events (as long as certain other conditions are also met – see details).
For this to happen, Skeletron must have been defeated at least once, as the Old Man spawning will override the Cultists' spawning.
Martian Probes begin spawning randomly, which can trigger the Martian Madness event.
Summoning the Old One's Army after Golem has been defeated triggers the most difficult "Tier 3" version of the event, enabling the player to fight Betsy.
Lihzahrd furniture can be decrafted via Shimmer.
The Steampunker will begin to sell the Steampunk Wings, as well as the Lihzahrd Furnace (if she's in a Jungle).
The Party Girl will begin to sell the Celebration.
The Golem emote  is unlocked.


== Notes ==
It is the only boss alongside King Slime that takes damage from lava. However, this only occurs to Golem's body when its head is detached.
Golem's map icon maps its head's location.
Despite this, Golem will despawn if the head chases the player too far away, as distance is measured from its body instead.
Golem's fist attack will only fire at the player when they are between the two fists or to the same side as the fist.
Unlike most bosses, Golem is affected by the low gravity in Space.
 Jungle Temple traps can only be dropped in worlds with the special world seed Skyblock enabled and where the tile threshold is not exceeded. This condition is checked upon entering the world, or occasionally during gameplay.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

In some cases, the terrain surrounding the Lihzahrd Altar will cause Golem to get stuck when it spawns. It can attack with its fists and projectiles but will be unable to jump around. Players can also recreate this condition by placing blocks near the altar.
The three Lihzahrd Bricks under the Lihzahrd Altar cannot be actuated, hence it is impossible to relocate the altar prior to defeating Golem for the first time.


== Trivia ==

In Jewish folklore, a golem (/ˈɡoʊləm/, GOH-ləm, Hebrew: ‎גּוֹלֶם) is an animated anthropomorphic being that is created entirely from inanimate matter (usually clay or mud). The word was used to mean an amorphous, unformed material in Psalms and medieval writing.
In Golem's first form, its head appears looser the more its health gets lowered, bouncing on its own whenever Golem jumps.
The gore sprite of the Lihzahrd Brick-themed sun symbol seen on its body has a sad, frowning face.
Because the Compass and Depth Meter reveal each tile to be 2 feet in length, Golem would be about 26′ ½″ (9.49 m) tall. Its head alone would be about 13′ 3″ (4.83 m) tall.
Despite the sprite update in 1.4.0.1, Golem's achievement icon and gore sprites were not updated.
 The Bestiary entry for  Golem: "A remarkable display of ingenuity constructed by the Lihzahrd clan. Powered by solar energy cells, it is ready to guard the Temple."


== History ==
