title: Wall of Flesh
content:
The Wall of Flesh is the final pre-Hardmode boss. Once it is defeated, the world permanently converts to Hardmode, which brings new content and challenges.
To defeat the Wall of Flesh, the player must attack either its eyes or its mouth. They all share the same health counter, so attacking any of the three will deplete the total health of the boss. However, the eyes have less defense (thus take more damage) than the mouth. No other parts of the Wall of Flesh can be damaged.
See below for information on the two exclusive debuffs from the boss, Horrified and The Tongue.
While the Wall of Flesh is alive, its exclusive music Boss 2 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Wall of Flesh (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning ==
The Wall of Flesh can be summoned by dropping a Guide Voodoo Doll into lava in The Underworld while the Guide is alive, which destroys the Guide Voodoo Doll and kills the Guide in the process. Alternatively, the boss can also be summoned by letting the Guide die within lava in The Underworld. He can die by any means (the player, an enemy, or the environment), as long as he is touching lava when he dies.
The Wall of Flesh is summoned just beyond the player's screen on the side where the Guide Voodoo Doll was dropped into lava (or where the Guide was killed by lava), then moves in the direction of the player. As a general rule, it spawns at least 75 tiles away from the player.


=== Technical details ===
When the Guide Voodoo Doll is destroyed or the Guide is killed in lava, the game checks whether all players are horizontally at least 75 tiles away from the location of the doll/Guide. If they are, then the Wall of Flesh is spawned at that horizontal position. Otherwise, the game moves one tile towards the closest lateral world border and checks again, repeating this until it encounters a tile that is horizontally at least 75 tiles away from any player. It stops 20 tiles before the true world border (i.e. 21/22 tiles away from the visible world border), even if a player is still within 75 tiles at that point (e.g. standing directly against the visible world border).
After locating the horizontal spawn position, the game determines a valid vertical position. The spawning tile must not be occupied by a solid block and its liquid level must not exceed 100 (i.e. at most approx. 39% of the tile can contain liquid). Again, the game begins at the vertical position of the doll/Guide and checks if that location is valid. Then it checks one tile above that spot and one tile below it, then two tiles above and two tiles below, and so on, until finding a valid spot. If the game finds no valid spot after 1000 attempts (i.e. 1000 tiles above and below), then it reverts to the initial vertical position. Finally, the vertical limits are enforced: If the vertical position that was encountered is higher than 10 tiles below the Cavern–Underworld border, it is forcibly moved down to that position (even though the tile there was not considered valid before), and if it is lower than 80 tiles below that border (roughly the vertical center of the Underworld), it is forcibly moved up to that position (again, even though the tile at that position was not considered valid before).
The center of the Wall of Flesh's mouth appears at the determined location, and the eyes are spawned relative to it. The boss quickly aligns itself vertically with the player after spawning.


== Behavior ==
The Wall of Flesh is very tall, occupying the entire screen vertically. It slowly sweeps across the Underworld in a single direction, forcing the player to constantly move away for the duration of the fight while also contending with the Underworld's usual hazards.

The Wall of Flesh moves faster as its health depletes; see below for details. It can reach up to 17 mph / 41 mph at very low health levels. Due to the Wall of Flesh's higher movement speed in Expert Mode, the speed at which it draws players via the Tongue debuff in Expert also increases as its health decreases.
Additionally:

 The Wall of Flesh has small mouths called The Hungry, each attached by a long vein, which move towards and damage players. As the Wall of Flesh's main body takes damage, they deal more damage and become more resistant to attacks. When sufficiently damaged, they detach and fly towards players at high speed.
The Hungry will always drop a Heart when killed. In Expert Mode, they only have a 1/5 (20%) chance to do so, and they respawn as long as the Wall of Flesh is alive.
In Expert Mode, the Hungry gain extra knockback resistance with each additional player in multiplayer, and become immune to knockback when there are at least 5 players.
The Wall of Flesh's eyes fire purple Eye Lasers. As its health depletes, the lasers increase in damage, frequency, and velocity.
The Wall of Flesh "burps" Leeches from its mouth that chase players. These will also always / with a 1/5 (20%) chance drop a Heart when killed.
It randomly lets out a roar.


=== Movement speed ===
The movement speed of the Wall of Flesh depends on its health as follows:


== Parts ==


== Aftermath ==
When the Wall of Flesh is killed, it leaves its drops in a midair 9×9-tile frame of Demonite Bricks (in Corruption worlds) or Crimtane Bricks (in Crimson worlds). Any liquid within the frame is removed. It will also always drop the Pwnhammer, which is required to generate Hardmode ores in the world (through breaking Demon or Crimson Altars with a hammer of 80% hammer power or higher, of which the Pwnhammer is the first obtained).

In Expert Mode or higher difficulties, its dropped Treasure Bag includes a Demon Heart, which provides the player an additional (sixth / seventh) accessory slot.
After the player has consumed a Demon Heart, additional ones will neither drop from Treasure Bags nor be consumable.
The Merchant will begin selling the Drum Set and Drumstick if he was not already.
The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he was not already.
The Wall of Flesh emote  is unlocked.


=== Hardmode ===

After defeating the Wall of Flesh for the first time, the status message “The ancient spirits of light and dark have been released.” displays and the world permanently converts to Hardmode. Hardmode brings new biomes, new and tougher enemies, and a vast array of new equipment.
Two diagonal stripes of Hallow and Corruption or Crimson form in a "V" pattern from the top of the world all the way to the bottom of the Underworld. Corruption/Crimson and Hallow will spread at a much faster rate, eventually covering vital areas such as the Jungle and any NPC housing if no action is taken.


== Notes ==
Being able to summon the Wall of Flesh depends on the Guide being alive. He cannot respawn if it is nighttime or there is an event in progress. Due to this, the waiting time between multiple fights is often much greater than with other bosses. Timing the fight to finish just before dawn has a chance to allow two or even more fights, especially if the Guide already has an assigned house.
It is possible for the Guide to respawn while the Wall of Flesh is alive, but only one Wall of Flesh can be alive at a time.
When the Wall of Flesh is alive and all players in the Underworld have been killed, the screen gradually fades to black over the course of 4 seconds, after which the Wall of Flesh will despawn and the screen will return to normal visibility.
The Wall of Flesh's eyes move up and down on its body to avoid any blocks they encounter. Solid blocks and liquids 4–5 tiles above and beneath the eyes will cause them to shift their positions.
The Tongue debuff can still move players that have knockback immunity (e.g. using the Cobalt Shield or its upgrades).
In a world where the special world seed For the Worthy is active, the Wall of Flesh's eyes and mouth are much smaller, while The Hungry are much larger. Fire Imps with higher defense and faster Burning Spheres also constantly spawn throughout the fight.
As a result of the spawning mechanics, the Wall of Flesh can move towards the side of world which is laterally shorter. For example, when a Guide Voodoo Doll is dropped into lava more than 75 tiles away from the player in the right half of the world, and the player is on the right side of the location of said doll, the Wall of Flesh will be summoned on the left side of the player and move rightwards.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

If the Wall of Flesh is accidentally summoned, use of the Magic Mirror, despite killing the player, is usually inconsequential in practice, as the player is taken directly to their Spawn Point, meaning dropped money and, if playing on Mediumcore, dropped items can be recovered easily. Note that this does not work in Hardcore as hardcore characters only have 1 life.
If the Wall of Flesh was recently summoned, make sure the Guide has respawned before attempting to summon the Wall of Flesh again to avoid the unnecessary loss of Voodoo Dolls.
A common "arena" to fight the boss should consist of a long horizontal bridge spanning at least 1000 blocks.
The two main types of Wall of Flesh arenas are solid bridges and platform bridges, each with their own pros and cons.
Solid bridges are made out of solid blocks, blocking lasers from the bottom eye and allowing bouncing projectiles to rebound against it, but come at the cost of blocking most of the player's own projectiles and not allowing dropping down through to evade attacks.
Platform bridges allow projectiles to pass through them, allowing the user to damage all parts of the boss more often and drop down from them if needed to dodge lasers. However, it does not block the bottom eye's lasers, and certain projectiles like Beenades do not work well unless they hit solid blocks. In Expert Mode and higher, it is recommended to build these out of Stone Platforms, Ash Wood Platforms or Obsidian Platforms which will not be destroyed by dying Lava Slimes.
If the player does not want to build a bridge, acquiring the Lava Waders or their upgrades is necessary; they can also use the Water Walking Potion.
Focus on The Hungry first before damaging the wall itself. The Hungry's damage and defense are boosted as the body takes damage, which will make them more difficult to kill if left for later.


== Trivia ==
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, the Wall of Flesh is the world's guardian. Once it is defeated, the world itself will search for a new guardian to take its place, and the Hallow is released as a temporary guardian.
The Wall of Flesh was inspired by the Demon Wall from the Japanese role-playing game series Final Fantasy.
The Hungry are the only Underworld enemy not immune to the On Fire! debuff.
The lead developer of Terraria, Redigit, has said that the Guide is the Wall of Flesh on the official Terraria Discord. This explains the relevancy of his death to the appearance of the boss.
The aforementioned claim is consistent with the fact that the Wall of Flesh is directly referred to as male with the use of "him" in a loading screen tip.
However, the Steam Trading Cards, the "Still Hungry" achievement that is awarded upon its defeat, and even the Guide himself, say that he is instead a sacrifice to the Wall of Flesh. In addition, the Guide respawns after the Wall of Flesh is defeated.
The Wall of Flesh is one of two pre-Hardmode bosses that have at least 10,000 HP in Expert Mode, the other being Deerclops.
Although Skeletron and the Eater of Worlds can have more, they are not single-unit enemies.
The Wall of Flesh is one of the four bosses that do not make the common roar sound when summoned, the others being the Lunatic Cultist, the Queen Bee, and the Empress of Light.
The Wall of Flesh is commonly abbreviated as "WoF".
The loot's frame is always spawned at the wall's mouth, and its size is correlated with the size of the mouth. If the mouth's size changes (e.g. via external mods or the For the Worthy seed), the frame's size changes accordingly.
The Wall of Flesh is the only boss that drops a mount-summoning item in Master Mode. All other Master Mode-exclusive mount-summoning items are dropped by mini-bosses.
The veining at the back of both eye and mouth is identical to the veins trailing the Eye of Cthulhu.
The Wall of Flesh is one of the two bosses that need a town NPC to be alive before being summoned. The other is Skeletron.
In Journey Mode, if Godmode is activated, using a Magic Mirror or similar method to teleport away during the Wall of Flesh fight will not kill the player; instead, they will be dragged all the way back to the Underworld via The Tongue debuff.
The Guide's Steam Trading Card describes the Wall of Flesh as "the god of eternal nightmares".
This is, debatably, one of only two or three entities besides the player that can place blocks in the world, the others being the Antlion and Snow Balla. The Wall of Flesh only leaves behind blocks after its defeat.


=== Bestiary entriesWall of Flesh: "Serving as the world's core and guardian, the towering demon lord exists to keep powerful ancient spirits sealed away."The Hungry: "The Wall of Flesh's many mouths, attached by bloody veins. As a last resort, they can tear away and hungrily chase down threats." ===

title: Mechanical Worm
content:
The Mechanical Worm is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons The Destroyer when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.
If the Destroyer has not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Worm.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
In worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix special world seeds, the Mechanical Worm is not consumable and is instead a crafting material for the Ocram's Razor, an item used to summon Mechdusa. Its tooltip also displays 'Part of a set'.
Like other mechanical boss summoning items, the Mechanical Worm can be brought to pre-Hardmode worlds and be used to summon The Destroyer there.
The evil crafting material dropped from decrafting the Mechanical Worm into Shimmer is dependent on the world evil; it will drop Rotten Chunks in Corruption worlds and Vertebra in Crimson worlds.
In Drunk worlds, the two world evils switch every in-game day, meaning the Mechanical Worm will alternate between both materials each day.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
Like the Mechanical Skull, it looks like a wind-up toy.
The crafting recipe of the respective summoning items for the mechanical bosses reference themes of Darkness, Light, and Balance. The Mechanical Worm specifically references Darkness in that it requires only Souls of Night, due to the fact that the boss it summons is a callback to a boss from a biome where Souls of Night themselves can be found.
Darkness, Light, and Balance are also referenced in the crafting recipes of the Onyx Blaster, Dao of Pow, and Sky Fracture respectively.


== See also ==
Mechanical Skull and Mechanical Eye, the other mechanical boss-summoning items.

title: Confused
content:
Confused is a debuff that causes the player's controls to reverse. When applied to the player, ◀ Left acts as ▲ Up and ▶ Right; ▶ Right acts as ◀ Left; ▲ Up acts as ▼ Down, and ▼ Down has no effect. See Notes for more detailed control behavior. When applied to enemies, a purple question mark appears above them, and causes them to move away from the player rather than towards them. Enemies with ranged attacks will be unable to use those attacks.
Around 60% of enemies (including all bosses) in Terraria are immune to the Confused debuff. Many of the vulnerable enemies include slimes, bats, and most fighters.
The debuff can be negated by equipping the Trifold Map or its derivatives.


== Causes ==


=== From player ===


=== From enemy ===


=== From debuff ===


=== Other ===


== Immune NPCs ==


== Vulnerable NPCs ==


== Notes ==
When the player is inflicted with Confused, the control behaviors are as follows:
↷ Jump controls are unaffected.
When the player is walking, riding a Minecart, or using a ground mount: ◀ Left makes the player go right, and ▶ Right makes the player go left.
▲ Up makes the player jump down surfaces. This includes platforms, Planter Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), furniture, liquid surfaces when Water Walking, etc.
Interacting with Ropes: ▼ Down makes the player grab onto the Rope, but will not make them ascend along the Rope; ▲ Up makes the player descend along the Rope.
Using Featherfall Potion or similar effects: ▲ Up makes the player fall faster.
Using the Inner Tube(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Flamingo Mount(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions): holding ▲ Up makes the player descend in liquids.
Using the Anti-Gravity Hook(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Static Hook(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions): ▲ Up, ◀ Left, and ▶ Right make the player move in the opposite direction, respectively. ▼ Down has no effect.
Using regular wings: the player can fly normally, but with inverted horizontal controls.
Using wings with vertical boost (e.g. Jetpack): the boost can be activated by holding ◀ Left and ↷ Jump at the same time.
Using wings with hover ability (e.g. Hoverboard): the hover can be activated by holding/clicking ▲ Up while flying, depending on the Hover Controls setting.
Using flying mounts (e.g. UFO(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lava Shark(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in liquids): ◀ Left makes the player ascend to upper-right; ▶ Right makes the player go left; ▲ Up makes the player descend; ↷ Jump makes the player ascend; ▼ Down has no effect.
Activating set bonuses: when set to "Down", double tap ▲ Up to activate; when set to "Up", double tap ◀ Left to activate.
On the  Console version, players inflicted with Confused have reversed movement, but not reversed aiming.

title: Raven Staff
content:
The Raven Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Raven minion. It flies and charges through enemies. The Raven Staff is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Notes ==
Once Raven minions make contact with an enemy, they can deal damage to all enemies that are currently colliding with them for duration of a single tick, but become unable to deal any damage for the next 16 ticks (0.27 seconds).
Because of this, it is possible for Raven minions to visually pass through a line of enemies while only dealing damage to one of them.
The Raven minion is unable to turn around towards its target for this 16-tick duration, and will continue moving in its previous path until the duration is over.
The Raven minion applies 10 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hitting an enemy, although in practice this does not come into play due to the internal hit cooldown mentioned above.
Raven minions can target enemies up to 56.25 tiles away, and can continue attacking their current target until their distance from the player is more than 87.5 tiles, in which case they automatically return to the player's side.

title: Special world seeds
content:
Special world seeds (previously named secret world seeds) are world creation modifiers that alter the created world in strange or unique ways.
Unlike regular world seeds, which only affect the usual world structure, special seeds can produce worlds with characteristics that would not be attainable through normal world generation (i.e., they can affect the game's mechanics while playing in that world). For instance, they may change enemy statistics and behavior, item drops, graphics, theme music, and more.
Special world seeds can be activated in the Seed Menu, which is accessible by clicking the  seed icon next to World Seed during world creation. Any number of special seeds can be activated simultaneously, forming a combination special seed. Some of these combinations have additional unique effects. Alternatively, special world seeds can also be activated by inputting their activation seed ("code" in the following infoboxes) into the World Seed, and a  sound effect will be played upon activating a seed. Only one special seed can be activated at a time in this way; entering another special seed will automatically disable previously activated special seeds.
There are 9 different special world seeds.


== Notes ==
The game checks an entered seed for special seeds in two ways:
As text: The game converts the input to all lowercase letters, then removes any characters that are not (lowercase) letters or numbers. For example, Not the Bees! gets converted to notthebees.
As an integer: The game attempts to read the input as an integer.
If this is successful, it takes the absolute value and returns the pure mathematical number. (e.g. 005162020 and -5162020 are both treated as 5162020).
If this fails because the input contains invalid characters or the number is too large, the game instead uses a hashing algorithm (CRC32) to generate a unique number from the input. Note that it is possible for this result to lead to a valid numerical secret seed code. This is why now aunt brush is a valid Drunk seed: the hashing algorithm converts it into 5162020.
It then checks both the integer and the text against a list of valid codes, returning the corresponding special seed if one is found.
Most special seeds only have text codes, except for the Drunk seed (which only uses a numerical code) and Celebration Mk 10 (the only seed to use both numerical and text codes).
The seed being randomized can technically lead the game to create a Drunk world or a Celebration Mk 10 world without specifying the seed, but the chances of it happening are astronomically low (1/2,147,483,648 (0.000000047%) for Drunk seed, 1/1,073,741,824 (0.000000093%) for the Celebration Mk 10 seed).
This is due to the random seed being a random number between 0 and 2147483647; the random seed can match the one needed for one of these special seeds. The chances are doubled for the Celebration Mk 10 seed due to the fact that two seed numbers trigger the special seed.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
The smiley-faced moon seen during the generation of a Drunk world is a reference to an astronomy hoax that was said to happen the same day Journey's End was released on PC.
Unlike the other special seeds, Drunk and Celebration Mk 10 world seeds are interpreted as numbers, so any number of 0s can be added in the front (e.g. 000005162020 for Drunk). In addition, there are numerous unintended strings that generate these two special seeds (due to the use of the CRC-32 algorithm), such as:
Drunk (case-sensitive): 
Celebration Mk 10 (case-sensitive): 
Coincidentally, the third seed references Yoraiz0r, a Terraria programmer.
Combining all secret seeds as well as all special seeds except for Skyblock creates a world colloquially known as "True Zenith", which can be considered the highest world difficulty possible in Terraria.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Renamed secret world seeds as special world seeds.
Added special seed skyblock.
Added special seed combinations.
Inputted seeds are now converted to lowercase and have all non-alphanumeric characters removed, then checked for special seed matches. Previously, special world seeds can only be activated by specific strings.
Added a new seed selection window to the world creation menu, which allows you to easily enable special seeds.
Desktop 1.4.4.6: Master For the Worthy and Zenith Seeds now show their difficulty as "Legendary" in the world selection menu.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Added three secret seeds no traps, don't dig up and get fixed boi.
Added an achievement for entering any secret seed.
Made changes to several secret seeds, including Not the Bees, For the Worthy, Celebration Mk 10, and The Constant.

Added secret seed theconstant.
Worlds using secret seeds now have unique icons in the World Select menu to better tell them apart.

Chest loot is now replaced by Angel Statues instead of Dirt Blocks in "For the Worthy" and the chance for this to occur was lowered from 1/5 (20%) to 1/15 (6.67%).
Glowing moss biomes are now 50% larger than normal in "For the Worthy".

title: Legacy:Guide:Crafting Frostspark Boots
content:
The Frostspark Boots are a highly useful accessory for movement. It allows faster ground speed, flight, and mobility on ice. The Frostspark Boots can be acquired in pre-Hardmode.


== Ingredients ==
To craft the Frostspark Boots, you will need the following materials:

Rocket Boots
Hermes Boots or Flurry Boots
Aglet
Anklet of the Wind
Ice Skates


== Overview ==


=== Step 1: Spectre Boots ===


==== Running boots ====
There are two types of base level running boots that exist which increase the player's movement speed by a very high margin, allowing them to sprint. Both of these boots have the same effect and can be used interchangeably in crafting.


===== Hermes Boots =====
The Hermes Boots are likely the first variety of sprinting boots that the player will encounter, and are very easy to discover early on. They can be found in Gold Chests in underground cabins which generate in most biomes in the Underground and Cavern layers.


===== Flurry Boots =====
Flurry Boots are also very easy to encounter in the early game generating within Ice Chests, acting as an Ice biome counterpart to Hermes Boots. Since the Ice biome often spreads underneath the spawn point even if the player does not spawn directly within the Snow biome, Flurry Boots are highly likely to be encountered if the player tunnels down deep enough near spawn.


==== Rocket Boots ====
After defeating a Goblin Army and rescuing the Goblin Tinkerer, the Rocket Boots can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for a base price of 5 Gold.


==== Crafting the Spectre Boots ====
The Rocket Boots can be combined with any of the two base level running boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop to yield the Spectre Boots, combining the effects of its two components.


=== Step 2: Lightning Boots ===


==== Aglet ====
Aglets are quite common accessories that are frequently found in Surface wooden Chests.


==== Anklet of the Wind ====
The Anklet of the Wind can be found in Ivy Chests which generate within jungle shrines in the Underground Jungle.


==== Crafting the Lightning Boots ====
These two accessories can be combined with the Spectre Boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop, yielding the Lightning Boots.


=== Step 3: Frostspark Boots ===


==== Ice Skates ====
Ice Skates can, just like the Flurry Boots, be found in Ice Chests.


==== Crafting the Frostspark Boots ====
Combine Ice Skates with the Lightning Boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop to craft the Frostspark Boots.

title: Guide:Solar Eclipse strategies
content:
The Solar Eclipse is a post-Mechanical Boss Hardmode event. A Solar Eclipse has a 1/20 (5%) chance of occurring upon any particular dawn, and can be manually summoned using a Solar Tablet.
This is the longest timed event in the game. Once all three Mechanical Bosses are defeated, it gains a new monster (the Reaper). Once Plantera is defeated, the event gains numerous new monsters and a boss, Mothron, with correspondingly powerful rewards. 


== The Event ==


=== Always present ===
Frankenstein, Fritz(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Swamp Thing are simple enemies that behave like Zombies, although they have some variation in speed and power. They can be taken out easily by most weapons.
Creature from the Deep(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and The Possessed(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are also simple enemies with contact damage only. The Creature from the Deep, though, can swim very quickly in water and leap out at the player, and The Possessed can climb on walls, becoming immune to knockback. Fighting in arenas away from water and without background walls renders them mostly harmless.
Vampires are the only flying enemies in this event (before defeating all Mechanical Bosses), and can be difficult to see in the darkness, especially in their bat form. Players should constantly keep an eye out for them when outdoors, and preferably use homing or area attacks that can catch them even when they haven't been seen. They take 10x damage from the Stake Launcher.
Eyezor is a dangerous enemy, able to shoot lasers from a respectable distance. Including some kind of vertical wall or obstacle in your arena to take shelter behind can make their lasers ineffective.


=== After defeating all mechanical bosses ===
Reapers can travel through blocks, making house- or box-based strategies more difficult. They are highly vulnerable to knockback and cannot fly. Sentries or minions near the player can often handle them easily, as can using weapons that surround the player (like Swords).


=== After defeating Plantera: ===
Psycho(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Butcher(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have very high contact damage. Psycho goes semi-invisible and waits for the player to come near, while the Butcher charges faster and faster. Neither can fly or pass through blocks, making them susceptible to the same strategies used against Frankenstein and other weak monsters.
Dr. Man Fly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a slow enemy that throws clouds of poisonous gas. As one of the few ranged enemies, it should be taken out before common foot soldiers.
Deadly Spheres(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are another flying enemy. They can pass through blocks until they get close to the player, which is when they transition to a more aggressive state that cannot pass through blocks.
Nailhead(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a very powerful, very slow-moving enemy that shoots out a rain of nails that can cover a large chunk of the screen. Nails can kill the player in just a few hits. This enemy should be a major priority to be either dodged or killed. Attacks that can travel off-screen such as the Spectre Staff or Yoyos using the Magic String or upgrades can be very effective.
Mothron(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is the strongest enemy of this event, fulfilling a role similar to a boss. It charges horizontally at the player after matching their height, and occassionally pauses to lay eggs which hatch into Baby Mothrons(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Destroying the eggs prevents them from hatching and often locks Mothron into a cycle of laying more eggs. Having plenty of open space and good vertical mobility is key to defeating Mothron.


== Preparation ==


=== General Tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===
Most enemies can be blocked by walls. Staying in a tunnel just under the surface and using weapons that can attack through walls like the Nettle Burst can be effective, especially in earlier tiers. 
After Plantera is defeated, Mothron makes this strategy ineffective. Instead, a large, flat space with several rows of platforms above it can be used. Ideally, some solid blocks should be placed either horizontally or vertically to block attacks from Eyezor or Nailhead. 


=== Gearing up ===
The event can happen naturally at any time after defeating one Mechanical Boss, but the hardest enemies are intended to be defeated post-Plantera. This guide will focus on post-Plantera equipment.


==== Armor ====
For melee, DPS is maximized with the Chlorophyte Mask, Monk's Shirt(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Squire's Greaves(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)/Valhalla Knight's Greaves(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Beetle armor with Scale Mail can also be used, but is ideal only when using the Terra Blade.
Rangers should use Shroomite armor with the headpiece that suits their weapon.
Shroomite armor's set bonus becomes useless in later waves, so the Shroomite Leggings can be replaced with Tiki Pants for an extra minion or Red Riding Leggings(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for a 3% advantage in critical strike chance and 25% summon damage.
Mages should use the Spectre armor with Spectre Mask(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), switching to the Spectre Hood when at low health.
Dark Artist's Leggings(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used along with Hallowed Headgear in place of Spectre Pants, but does not facilitate armor switching.
Summoners should use Tiki armor (if favoring Whips) or Spooky armor. They can also switch to the Squire's Great Helm(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) after summoning, losing two minions to gain constant regeneration greater than that provided by Palladium armor.
While weaker than most of the above armor, the  Tier 2 armors sold by the Tavernkeep allow for the placement of many sentries, which can be of great benefit in this event.


==== Weapons ====
For all classes

Weapons obtained from defeating Duke Fishron or the Empress of Light are very powerful and can easily win this fight. They won't be mentioned individually.
For Melee users

Seedler(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Flower Pow both drop from Plantera and both have homing or self-aiming projectiles, useful against hard-to-see vampires and the very mobile Mothron.
The True Excalibur and the True Night's Edge are very strong swords, with True Excalibur better for keeping enemies away and True Night's Edge better for long-range attacks. Together, they can be upgraded into the Terra Blade in the middle of the event if Mothron drops a Broken Hero Sword.
The Keybrand can be thrown into the ground, doing high damage and knockback to weak enemies dealing heavy damage to Nailhead if it stays in that location.
The Paladin's Hammer is very good for crowds and decent against Mothron, especially for reducing defense.
The Scourge of the Corruptor has wide-spreading, homing projectiles that can excel in this fight.
Vampire Knives can be used to quickly heal in critical situations, but have lower DPS than most other options.
For Ranged users

The Venus Magnum, Tactical Shotgun and Sniper Rifle are the strongest guns if no other events have been fought yet.
Crystal Bullets give the highest single-target damage. For Venus Magnum and the Sniper Rifle, the bullets from the Endless Musket Pouch(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are converted into High Velocity Bullets, good for crowd control.
Nano Bullets can be effective for the Tactical Shotgun, as they can cause the Confused debuff on multiple enemies at once, and the bouncing/homing property ensures bullets aren't lost. While doing only half the bullet damage, Chlorophyte Bullets do not miss and do not lose damage the way Nano Bullets do after a bounce.
The Grenade Launcher and Rocket Launcher can do high damage, but can be risky if enemies get close. They are better used in a high arena, far from grounded enemies, or with Hunter Potion to keep track of enemies.
The Chlorophyte Shotbow and Phantom Phoenix(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can handle large groups of enemies.
Chlorophyte Arrows have high damage and can bounce towards enemies if they miss, useful against grounded enemies.
Holy and Ichor Arrows are other strong options.
The Piranha Gun is very strong against single targets and can chew through weaker enemies fairly quickly as well.
For Magic users

The Spectre Staff and Wasp Gun have homing attacks that can be used safely behind walls or when dodgin Mothron in the air. The Wasp Gun's own damage reduction, increased by the Hive Pack and used in combination with Golden Shower, can negate Mothron's defense completely and most of Nailhead's, giving significantly higher damage.
The Leaf Blower and Inferno Fork have high single-target damage.
The Shadowbeam Staff and The Nettle Burst have high pierce, able to handle to large crowds. Nettle Burst can be used through walls, useful when Mothron is not present.
The Tome of Infinite Wisdom(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can switch between high single-target damage and large crowd-damaging projectiles.
The Magnet Sphere, Rainbow Gun, and Nimbus Rod are all very good secondary weapons. Betsy's Wrath can also work well as a primary weapon with its wide, gravity-affected area of effect and high damage.
For Summoners

The Desert Tiger Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) has high damage, especially when paired with the Firecracker(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). It can get distracted in crowds, though, leaving the player vulnerable.
The Pygmy Staff and Optic Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) can handle the event well, although they can both be replaced by the Deadly Sphere Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as soon as it is obtained.
The Sanguine Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) continues to work well.
The Morning Star(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Vulgar Display of Flower(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are convenient and strong whips.
Sentries are very helpful in this event. The Staff of the Frost Hydra is very strong, and the Tier 2 Tavernkeep sentries like the Ballista Cane(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Flameburst Cane(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be placed near the player to keep flying enemies away, or any of the sentries can be used against clumped grounded enemies.


==== Accessories ====
Wings are useful against Mothron.
The Frog Leg makes all wings ascend significantly faster, making dodging attacks easier.
The Master Ninja Gear greatly helps in dodging the attacks and is recommended for all classes.
Damage increasing accessories such as any Emblem, the Sniper Scope or the Magic Quiver are extremely important for the Moon events.
Accessories should be modified to Lucky or Menacing for the event.


==== Mounts ====
The use of mounts can save accessory slots that would've been used for mobility.

The Chillet(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is very helpful, allowing the player to dodge.
The Roller Skates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) continue to be useful.


==== Potions ====
Due to the length of this event, the buff provided by the Alchemy Flask is useful for stretching out potion duration.

Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, Lifeforce Potion, and Ironskin Potion will greatly increase survivability.
Any food item that provides the Well Fed buff is good.
Mana Regeneration Potion is helpful for mages.
Rage Potion and Wrath Potion will improve DPS.
Magic Power Potion, Archery Potion, Ale or Sake(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) and Summoning Potion will further improve it for Mages, Rangers, Melee, and Summoner users respectively.
Flasks are useful in this fight, as they can affect many enemies at once. The Flask of Nanites can make most enemies harmless, while Flask of Ichor can lower defenses and Flask of Venom can spread out damage over many enemies.


== Specific strategies ==


=== Money farming ===
The Solar Eclipse can make a lot of money. Melee and Summon users can employ the Flask of Gold, while Rangers can use Golden Bullets. 
All classes can use the Lucky Coin, which causes enemies to drop coins on hit. This is especially useful when combined with the Wasp Gun, which uses a large number of rapid weak attacks.
Sentries can kill a lot of weaker armies, making sentry-focused armor a strong choice.

title: Underground Crimson
content:
The Underground Crimson is a biome. It is the underground version of the surface-level Crimson, appearing at and below the Cavern layer. Just like the surface Crimson, it is mainly composed of Crimstone and spreads to nearby tiles. Although it is available in pre-Hardmode, most of its exclusive contents will only appear during Hardmode. After the Wall of Flesh is defeated for the first time, a diagonal stripe of Crimson is generated, creating additional Underground Crimson biome. 
The Underground Crimson does not suppress the spawn of other underground and cavern enemies. During Hardmode, all enemies killed in the Underground Crimson have a 1/5 (20%) chance to drop a Soul of Night.
Note: Most characteristics of the surface Crimson also apply to the Underground Crimson. See The Crimson for more extensive information.

title: Strange Glowing Mushroom
content:
The Strange Glowing Mushroom is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Truffle that follows the player. The Baby Truffle emits a small amount of blue light similar to Glowing Mushrooms. The Strange Glowing Mushroom can be purchased from the Truffle for 45 Gold.


== Notes ==
Unlike other pets, the Baby Truffle will not fly to the player should they go too far away. It simply disappears, reappearing at the player's position (or when the player lands), similar to how the player can go into stealth with the Shroomite armor.
Despite being a normal pet, the Baby Truffle gives off a dim blue light.

title: Nectar
content:
The Nectar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Hornet that follows the player. This pet will not teleport to the player when it is far away. The Nectar has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 1/9 (11.11%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee.


== Notes ==
This pet is not affected by liquids but will play a "splashing" sound when entering any liquid.


== Trivia ==
In real life, only adult hornets feed on nectar, along with plant foods rich in sugar, and only attack and kill other insects to feed to their offspring. Hornet larvae then produce a sweet secretion, containing sugars and other essential nutrients, that is consumed by adult workers and queens.

title: Frostburn
content:
Frostburn is a debuff that prevents health regeneration and causes the afflicted entity to lose 8 health per second (enemies display 2 damage every 0.25 seconds, while players display 1 damage every 0.13 seconds) for the duration of the debuff.
Its damage can be increased by Slime and Accelerated Afflictions. It can also trigger the extra damage over time from Oiled.
Visually, the debuff causes afflicted entities to emit blue fire particles and a small amount of light.

title: Guide:Surviving in the Ocean
content:
The main threat of the Ocean biome is the very water it is composed of, which players can drown in.


== Recommended gear ==
At least 160 maximum health.


=== Weapons ===
Ebonwood Swordin worlds with Corruption
Shadewood Swordin worlds with Crimson
Ebonwood Bowin worlds with Corruption
Shadewood Bowin worlds with Crimson
Rally(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
Spear
Gem staff


=== Armor ===
Cactus armor
Ebonwood armorin worlds with Corruption
Shadewood armorin worlds with Crimson
Iron/Tin armor


=== Miscellaneous ===
Trident greatly enhances underwater movement speed and jump height while held
Flipper allows the player to swim upwards by repeatedly pressing ↷ Jump
Breathing Reed doubles the time the player can spend underwater
Inner Tube(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) allows the player to rapidly float to the surface by equipping it
These items can be found in the Ocean's own Water Chests, as well as in fished Ocean Crates. They will make diving into the Ocean much safer.
Other useful items include the following, which can be found commonly as part of normal Chest loot:

Gills Potion allows the player to breathe underwater for 4 minutes
Shine Potion provides light without the need to hold or throw Glowsticks
Flipper Potion(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) allows the player to swim upwards by repeatedly pressing ↷ Jump
Recall Potion or Magic Mirrors can be used to teleport out instantly if the player gets attacked by a Shark or starts drowning
Spelunker Potion highlights Chests, even in the dark
Hunter Potion highlights enemies, even in the dark


== Exploration and plundering ==

The Ocean contains Water Chests and Corals along the seabed. Some Oceans extend into a cave-like structure which contains additional Water Chests.

Consider building a platform across the surface of the Ocean, which will make it easier to stay at the surface without falling back in. Construct lines of Ropes to quickly return to this platform if none of the items that allow swimming are available.
Diving into the Ocean without any preparation is possible as well, since the player's breath usually lasts long enough to loot at least one or two Water Chests. Autopause helps with this, and Glowsticks improve the visibility of the Chests. Recall with a Recall Potion or Magic/Ice Mirror when breath runs out.
Sharks, Pink Jellyfish, Crabs, and, in Hardmode, Orcas will threaten the player in the Ocean. The Pink Jellyfish can become a problem if they swarm the player, but their glow reveals them from far away, which makes avoiding them easier. They are also easily knocked back by most early-game weapons. Sharks, however, often ambush the player with their high speed and damage, and are not as susceptible to knockback.
Visibility is also a concern down at the Ocean depths. While Pink Jellyfish give off light, Sharks and Crabs do not, and can strike unexpectedly from the darkness at any time. The most readily source of aquatic lighting available are the Glowsticks dropped by Pink Jellyfish, as most Torches do not work underwater. The Mining Helmet or Shine Potion can help provide light, as well as the rarer Jellyfish Necklace dropped by Pink Jellyfish. A Hunter Potion can be used to clearly see the locations of enemies. The Starfury swords works as an alternative way to light up the Ocean.


== Evil biome takeover ==
If the player is not careful, the ocean may be taken over by an evil biome. In this case, the ocean will be treated like an evil biome, meaning enemies like Corruptors or Pixies can spawn, and will make the biome signifigantly harder to traverse. This can be avoided by using Green Solution with a Clentaminator or Terraformer to purify it.

title: Truffle
content:
The Truffle is a Hardmode NPC vendor who sells various mushroom-themed items. He can arrive homelessly as soon as Hardmode starts (with no biome requirement), but he can only move into vacant houses that are located in (or near) a surface Glowing Mushroom biome (i.e. one that is above 0 elevation).

Surface Glowing Mushroom biomes do not generate naturally and therefore must be manually created. 100 tiles of Mushroom grass and Glowing Mushroom plants are required to create a Glowing Mushroom biome.
If the Truffle spawns into a vacant house in a surface Glowing Mushroom biome, he is considered unlocked and can then be reassigned to a house at any elevation, as long as it is in a Glowing Mushroom biome. Moving a homeless Truffle into suitable house is not considered unlocking him; in this case, he can only be reassigned into houses in surface Glowing Mushroom biomes.
After the Truffle dies, if the Truffle is unlocked, he can respawn into vacant houses located in Glowing Mushroom biomes at any height; if he is not unlocked, he can only respawn into vacant houses located in surface Glowing Mushroom biomes. Otherwise, he can only respawn homelessly.
When threatened by enemies, the Truffle will release Mushroom Spores, which hover in midair and explode into spore clouds upon contact with enemies.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Truffle will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
Biome detection range for a house is different from the range for biome existence requirements. See House § Truffle for details.
If other NPCs are waiting to move in, they may move into a Glowing Mushroom biome home before the Truffle can. When attempting to spawn the Truffle, try to make sure enough houses exist for other NPCs that have not yet spawned.
For the Truffle to move in, the house must be in a Glowing Mushroom biome in the Surface or Space layers.
When the Remix seed is active, the Truffle's housing requirements are unchanged; a valid house must be in the true Surface or Space layers, not the false "surface" in the Cavern layer.
When the Mole people seed is active, the height restriction is ignored; the Truffle can move into houses as long as they are in a Glowing Mushroom biome.
To unlock the Truffle if he has already been assigned a house in a surface Glowing Mushroom biome in homeless state, the player has to kill the Truffle currently in the world to let him spawn into said house.
Trying to move the Truffle to an invalid house will result in the status message “This housing does not meet the requirements for a Truffle”.
The Truffle is male and has a chance to be teleported by a King Statue.
Despite his requirement to live in a Glowing Mushroom biome, the Truffle can sell other Pylons due to hybrid biomes. The exception to this are the Forest and Cavern Pylons, which are mutually exclusive and only available when not within one of the other biomes.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The Truffle can spawn even when there is no Glowing Mushroom biome on the surface. As he has no requirement to sell Dark Blue Solutions, one can create an artificial surface Glowing Mushroom biome using the Clentaminator with the solution in the Jungle.


== Names ==
The Truffle may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
Almost all of the Truffle's names are types of mushrooms or toadstools or named after parts of one.
Agaric refers to a type of fruiting body of a mushroom, characterized by a rounded cap, cylindrical stalk, and lamellae (or gills) within the cap's underside.
Amanita and Muscaria refers to the scientific name for the Amanita muscaria, a mushroom species which the Truffle's Shimmered form resembles.
Chanterelle refers to several species of edible, warm-colored mushrooms, known for having a mild, peppery taste.
Cremini is the browned, immature stage of the portobello mushroom widely cultivated in Eurasia and North America.
Enoki is a thin, white mushroom species native to East Asia and commonly used in Japanese and Chinese cuisine.
Maitake is a mushroom species that grows at the base of trees and is native to China, North America, and Europe.
Morels are a genus of edible fungi characterized by cone-shaped caps with a honeycomb-like appearance.
Porcini is an edible mushroom cultivated throughout the Northern Hemisphere known for its versatility in cooking.
Reishi is a fan-shaped reddish fungus native to East Asia that grows at the base of trees.
Shiitake is an edible brownish mushroom native to East Asia but is cultivated and consumed globally.
Shimeji refers to a popular group of edible mushrooms native to East Asia that includes shiitake and enoki mushrooms, among others.
The name Leinspores is a pun on Leinfors, a former QA team member at Re-Logic, and spores, a particle that fungi use for reproduction.
The Truffle's eyes and the top of his head glow in the dark.
The Truffle is often confused as having one eye, despite him having two eyes on the "It Can Talk?!" and "Real Estate Agent" achievement icons, as well as developer confirmation. This confusion stems from the Terraria Jazwares figurine toys.
The Truffle's Shimmered portrait references this by actually having only one eye, although his attacking sprite still has two.
The Guide's help text about the Truffle (“I've heard of glowing mushrooms growing big enough on the surface to gain sentience. Wonder if there's any truth to that...”) and the "It Can Talk?!" achievement implies that the Truffle grows from ordinary Glowing Mushroom plants on surface.
This might be explaining why many NPCs try to eat him or use him in potion, as they still treat the Truffle as an ordinary plant.
The Clothier's quote, “I'll give you a discount on your wears if you can convince <name of Truffle> to come over for a...sizing.” suggests that the Clothier wants to eat him.
Since the Clothier loves the Truffle and NPCs charge lower prices when NPCs they like are nearby, this means the Clothier will keep his promise if the player fulfills request. The Truffle will then mention in multiple quotes that the Clothier is actively trying to eat him.
The Truffle's defensive weapon, the mushroom spores, has the highest DPS of any NPC.
He is the only NPC who sways their arms side to side while walking, rather than keeping them bent the way that the other NPCs do.
He is the only NPC that requires a specific biome to live in.
The quote “You haven't seen any pigs around here have you? My brother lost his leg to one.” is a reference to the historical use of pigs to locate truffles.
The quote “As if living underground wasn't bad enough, jerks like you come in while I'm sleeping and steal my children.” is a reference to players exploring Glowing Mushroom biomes and collecting Glowing Mushrooms.
These quotes and the painting My Son indicates that Truffle is a species rather than an individual.
The quote “I don't know the 'Truffle Shuffle,' so stop asking!” is a reference to the 1985 American adventure comedy movie The Goonies.
The quote “I tried to lick myself the other day to see what the big deal was, everything started glowing blue.” references the use of magic mushrooms as a recreational drug.
The Truffle's Shimmered form makes him look like the Mushrooms found on the surface.
 The Bestiary entry for the Truffle: "Harnessing the hidden power of the glowing mushroom, the Truffle forges weapons and tools exclusively in his mushroom home."


== Gallery ==

		
		
		
		


== History ==

NPCs can now arrive homelessly when there are no available houses.
For Truffle, this means he can arrive when there is no available house in a surface Glowing Mushroom biome.
Moving a homeless Truffle into a suitable house does not count as unlocking him.

Now sells a new painting.

title: Frozen
content:
Frozen is a debuff that causes the player to briefly freeze in place, being completely unable to move or use any weapons or items, rendering the player completely vulnerable to most attacks.
The debuff can be negated by equipping the Hand Warmer or (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) a full set of Snow armor. Additionally, if the player has the Warmth buff, the duration of the debuff will be halved.
All enemies that can inflict Frozen can inflict the Chilled debuff as well (with the exception of Deerclops(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)).


== Causes ==


=== From enemy ===


== Notes ==
If the player is currently attacking with a spear when being inflicted with Frozen, the spear will remain in place, continuing to deal damage.
The debuffs Stoned(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Frozen, and Webbed(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) all disable the player's inputs. When more than one of them is active at a time, the priority for the effects is as follows: Stoned → Frozen → Webbed.
Note that if the Webbed effect coexists with any of the other effects, the player will not experience the effects of gravity.


== See also ==
Cursed

title: Moon Charm
content:
The Moon Charm is a Hardmode accessory that, when equipped during nighttime, transforms the player into a werewolf and applies the Werewolf buff, which provides several stat bonuses. Additionally, the Moon Charm replaces the sound the player makes when damaged with the hurt sound that regular Werewolf enemies also have. The Werewolf buff does not pacify Werewolf enemies or make the player immune to damage from them. Although the regular Werewolf enemy is colored blue, the player Werewolf will be colored brown. The Moon Charm has a 1/60 (1.67%) chance of being dropped by Werewolves. 
The Werewolf buff provides the player with these bonuses:

+2% melee critical strike chance
+5.1% melee damage
+5.1% melee speed
+5% movement speed
+3 defense
Slightly increased jump height and jump speed
+0.5 health regeneration per second (similar to the Band of Regeneration, but with half the speed)


== Crafting ==


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
The Merfolk buff (granted by Neptune's Shell) overrides the Werewolf buff, replacing the graphics and canceling the bonuses granted by the Moon Charm during nighttime.
Armor will be hidden while the Werewolf buff is active, but will still grant its effects. Accessories will remain visible.
Certain parts such as the tail from the Fox set and Space Creature set will remain visible.
Dyes in the respective armor slots will also affect the werewolf's fur color. (For example, if there is red dye affecting the chest piece, the werewolf's chest fur will be dyed red.)
Equipping the Moon Charm in a vanity slot will give the player the appearance and sounds of a werewolf at any time, including during the day, but they will not receive the buff.
Setting the Moon Charm to invisible will prevent the appearance or sounds of a Werewolf for the player, but the stat changes still take effect.
The Moon Charm does not stack with its upgrades.


== Tips ==
The Moon Charm is a reasonably good accessory for melee classes. Non-melee classes may be more interested in upgrades, the Moon Shell and Celestial Shell.
Many boss fights can only take place at night, when the Moon Charm is active.
Moon Charms can be farmed more easily by using a Bloody Tear to summon a Blood Moon during the full moon, greatly boosting enemy spawn rates—including Werewolves.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.1: Effect no longer stacks with Celestial Shell and its derivative accessories.
Desktop 1.3.0.6: Can now hide the Moon Charm's werewolf transformation, or equip the charm to a Vanity slot for purely aesthetic transformations.

Desktop 1.2.3: Fixed issue where Merfolk / Werewolf transformations were visible when the player was invisible.
Desktop 1.2: 
Overall boost to effects, also triggers every night instead of just full moons.
Now used to craft the Moon Shell.

title: Guide:Skeletron Prime strategies
content:
Skeletron Prime is the Hardmode version of Skeletron. It is one of the three Mechanical bosses, alongside The Destroyer and The Twins. It can deal a lot of damage with its four limbs, and its high health and defense allow it to take a lot of punishment. The limbs have the added effect of blocking non-piercing shots aimed at its head.


== Spawning Conditions ==
Skeletron Prime can be spawned by fulfilling any of these conditions:

After smashing a Demon/Crimson Altar, it will have a 10% chance of appearing when night falls, until it is defeated for the first time. This condition is shared with the rest of the trio, so there's a chance that The Destroyer or The Twins will spawn instead.
Use a Mechanical Skull at night.
Either way, it must then be defeated before all involved players die, or before daybreak, whichever comes first.


== The Fight ==
Skeletron Prime is a flying boss that consists of five parts:

Prime Saw, a melee arm, with 9000 / 13500 / 17212 health.
Prime Vice, a melee arm, with 9000 / 13500 / 17212 health.
Prime Laser, a ranged arm that fires lasers, with 6000 / 9000 / 11475 health.
Prime Cannon, a ranged arm that fires grenades, with 7000 / 10500 / 13387 health.
Skeletron Prime, the head, with 28000 / 42000 / 53550 health.
Killing the head will count as a victory, and any remaining limbs will be destroyed.
Each limb has a unique attack pattern, listed below. Although killing the limbs is not necessary, they can block attacks to the head (especially Prime Saw and Prime Vice), and destroying them makes the fight much easier. It is safest to take out the most dangerous limbs at the beginning, as the fight gets significantly easier without their interference.


=== Prime Saw ===
Prime Saw is one of the two melee limbs. It lunges at the player, dealing a lot of damage if its attack connects. However, compared to the other limbs, the Saw is not as aggressive, and has a predictable pattern. Accordingly, it is a lesser threat despite the high damage, and a low priority.


=== Prime Vice ===
Prime Vice is one of the two melee limbs. Compared to the Saw, it does less damage, but it is more aggressive. It lunges at the player, attacking many times before retracting.
Although its pattern can be somewhat predictable, its behavior when Prime is spinning makes it a very dangerous limb, capable of dealing significant damage if the player is not careful.


=== Prime Laser ===
Prime Laser is one of the ranged limbs. It will consistently remain above the player, firing lasers at a moderate rate. Its shots deal significant damage and it is Prime's most threatening limb in Expert mode. The laser starts shooting much faster when Prime enters its spinning state, making it an even bigger problem.
Its damaging, fast, and accurate shots arguably make it Prime's most dangerous limb in Expert/Master Mode. Because of this and its relatively low health, it should ideally be destroyed before the others.


=== Prime Cannon ===
Prime Cannon is the other ranged limb. It shoots bombs that do not deal contact damage. They only deal damage by explosion upon contact with blocks or platforms.
Despite having high damage, the inaccuracy of the bombs makes the Cannon significantly less threatening than any of the other limbs. It can safely be ignored in favor of more dangerous targets.


=== Skeletron Prime ===
Skeletron Prime "proper" is the head, which must be destroyed to win. Skeletron Prime will try to float above the player at all times. It will close in to do its spinning attack, which doubles its attack and defense and empowers its other limbs, making them attack more frequently. Once it finishes spinning, it will retreat again.
Like Skeletron, if the head is not destroyed by morning, it will enter its enraged state, being locked in its spinning attack, gain significant speed increase, and its damage and defense will both increase to 9999. In this state, a single hit will kill the player, while the head will only take one damage per hit and two damage per critical hit.
Killing the head is a lot easier once some of its limbs are down, especially the Vice and the Laser. Focusing only on the head still works should the player wish to end the fight as soon as possible, but usually it is safer to focus on the arms first.
Moving diagonally will make dodging the spinning head easier, as players can move faster in diagonal directions than in others.


=== Expert Mode/Master Mode ===
In this mode, the spinning head is much faster, and increases speed the further away the player is.


=== For the Worthy ===
In this special world seed, the bombs that the Prime Cannon shoots will destroy tiles and potentially ruin an arena. This can be prevented with Dungeon Bricks as they are immune to explosions. Other blocks, along with platforms, can alsoch be made immune to explosions by placing storage items su as Chests or Dressers on them.


== General Strategies ==


=== General tips ===

When using Summon weapons, it is recommended to use the targeting function to focus one arm at a time and reduce the threat Skeletron Prime poses. Simply right-click near one of the weapons to target it and your minions will prioritize that arm. Alternatively, a Whip can be used to focus targeting.
Debuffs can be useful, although the boss is immune to Poisoned. Frostbite, Cursed Inferno, Hellfire, Acid Venom and Shadowflame can add extra DPS and be spread over multiple parts. Ichor is especially useful as it enables the player to cut into the boss's high defense.
If the player gets too far from the head while it is not spinning, it will fly back to the player extremely quickly, which can be difficult to dodge. Keep within a reasonable distance.


=== Terrain preparation ===
As with all bosses, an arena made out of Wood Platforms or Minecart Tracks greatly increases your mobility, and it will also moot the Prime Cannon. You will want several rows of platforms, each around 50 or so blocks long. The platforms should be suspended off the ground. A solid ceiling should be avoided since Skeletron Prime will often retreat a fair distance when not using his spinning attack. It is also best to use Frozen Slime Blocks as they keep the mobility of any speed enhancements.
In For the Worthy worlds where the Celebration Mk 10 special seed isn't present, Skeletron Prime's bombs will destroy susceptible blocks, and thus building an arena with blocks that are immune to explosions is essentially mandatory. Dungeon Bricks can be obtained by fishing in the Dungeon for Stockade Crates; Be aware that fishing in the Dungeon requires some setup to get a usable water pool and a safe area. Alternatively, Cobalt Bricks and Palladium Columns can be crafted from the weakest tier of Hardmode ores. However, this usually necessitates smashing an Altar, which runs the risk of a mechanical boss to naturally spawn. Crates can be fished up to obtain these ores without smashing an altar, but can be tedious due to the low chance of getting Hardmode ores from crates.


=== Gearing up ===


==== Armor ====
Adamantite armor provides the overall greatest increase to all stats.
Titanium armor is a great choice due to its high stats. It also provides the Titanium Barrier.
Frost armor and Forbidden armor provide stat bonuses and allow you to mix different damage types.
Crystal Assassin armor's respectable defense, stat boosts and dash ability can make it a viable alternative to Hardmode ore sets.
Orichalcum armor provides very high critical strike chance and its set bonus can hit multiple parts.
Palladium armor provides lower stat bonuses, but the Rapid Healing greatly increases natural regeneration.
Hallowed armor becomes a great choice if you have already defeated a Mechanical Boss, since it provides the Holy Protection buff.
Spider armor is the most practical choice for Summoners. However, for Blade Staff users, the Obsidian Armor remains extremely viable well into Hardmode due its set bonuses applying to whips.
 The armor sets available from the Tavernkeep combine summoning with one of the other classes. This is only available if you've already defeated one Mechanical Boss.


==== Weapons ====


===== For melee users =====
The Flint deals extreme damage to both the head and the arms during the spinning state, but a different weapon should be used when the Prime is not spinning.
The Bananarang is a very effective weapon due to its long range and decent damage. The Shadowflame Knife and Chain Guillotines are similar alternatives.
Once you have defeated The Destroyer, the Light Disc can be crafted to have similar effect.
The Yelets with the Magic Yoyo Bag is a strong and accurate choice.
If another mechanical boss has been defeated, the Excalibur is a high-risk, high-reward weapon.
The Drippler Crippler does heavy damage to Skeletron Prime or its arms if aimed well. Due to it being a flail, it may be hard to land a hit; being close to Skeletron Prime while using the spinning attack can do high damage at the risk of tasking a lot a damage back from Prime. The Dao of Pow is a weaker alternative.
Using Flasks is also useful. Ichor or Cursed Inferno are the best options for this fight.


===== For ranged users =====
The Daedalus Stormbow is very powerful, especially when combined with Holy Arrows.
The Dart Rifle and Dart Pistol are both very strong. With Cursed Darts and vertical moving, they can kill the Prime very quickly, while Crystal or Ichor Darts are easier to use.
If you have defeated The Destroyer, the Megashark is a very powerful option due to its rapid speed and respectable damage. The Uzi has similar power and can be obtained earlier, but only rarely.
The Onyx Blaster and Clockwork Assault Rifle are very powerful guns made even stronger with Crystal Bullets.
The Adamantite Repeater and Titanium Repeater are easy to obtain and do decent damage, especially when paired with Ichor Arrows' armor penetration and high velocity.
If one mechanical boss has already been defeated, the Hallowed Repeater is an upgrade.
If one mechanical boss has been defeated, then the Phantom Phoenix is another viable choice, but requires clearing the Old One's Army which can be difficult.
The Super Star Shooter is extremely effective, but requires farming Fallen Stars.
It is recommended to use a secondary weapon that inflicts Ichor, such as a Dart Rifle/Dart Pistol with Ichor Darts, as the lowered defense will increase damage.


===== For magic users =====
You can use the Crystal Serpent which functions similarly to Crystal Bullets and deals high damage.
The Sky Fracture is also powerful, and boosts the Nimbus Rod thanks to its high crit rate.
The Meteor Staff is powerful and easy to craft, provided you have some leftover Meteorite Bars from Pre-Hardmode.  In the right arena, it's overhead area attack does a nice job taking out some hands without having to aim.
The Lightning Strike is another strong weapon that attacks from above and does not get blocked by the hands.
The Golden Shower deals below-average damage but inflicts the Ichor debuff, allowing your other weapons to deal even more damage.
The Flower of Frost is a decent weapon that inflicts Frostbite.
The Magic Dagger can be useful at the start of the fight due to its piercing.
The Blood Thorn can offer good coverage due to placing the spikes on platforms immediately which allows to keep up with Skeletron Prime's movement.
If another Mechanical Boss has been defeated, the Unholy Trident and the left-click attack of the Tome of Infinite Wisdom are some of the strongest weapons available.
The Rainbow Rod is available if you have defeated The Twins previously. The projectile is homing and piercing, meaning it is all but guaranteed to hit three sections of the boss with each cast while at the same time allowing you to focus on dodging.
Beating a Hardmode goblin army can provide access to the Shadowflame Hex Doll, dropped by the Goblin Warlock. The scattering attack can hit multiple limbs and the head rapidly, dealing substantial damage in little time.


===== For summoners =====
The Sanguine Staff is an extremely good summon weapon, due to its perfect tracking and high damage.
The Blade Staff is also a viable option due to its fast tracking and attack speed. As Skeletron Prime is vulnerable to Ichor, Ichor Flasks can greatly increase the effectiveness of the Blades, as together they ignore 40 defense (45 on Mobile). Whips can boost its damage further.
If you have already defeated The Twins, you can use the Optic Staff to summon miniature versions of them.
The Spider Staff is very useful for defeating the laser and cannon, as they don't move much and allow the spiders to cling for longer. If planning to use them as a main source of damage against Skeletron Prime, order the spiders to target its head and do not use whips.
The Queen Spider Staff is a great choice if you tend to remain in one area the entire battle. The Barnacle Staff does less damage but is better at hitting flying enemies.
Whips, especially the Cool Whip with its armor-ignoring snowflake projectile, are effective at dealing damage to several body parts at once or empowering your minions.
The Durendal is preferred if at least one mechanical boss has been defeated prior, as it provides high Summon Tag damage.


==== Accessories ====
Accessories that increase your mobility such as the Lightning Boots are extremely useful. In Expert Mode, the head can reach up to 31 mph, so exceeding that speed is important.
There are a multitude of wings available to the player at this point, but some useful wings are:
The Fairy Wings are helpful thanks to their accessibility and solid flight time.
The Frozen Wings or Harpy Wings can be used if the player has the items used to craft them (Do not bother with farming for the materials, only use these wings if you happen to have the Ice Feather or Giant Harpy Feather on hand.).
If one Mechanical boss has been defeated, the Jetpack can be bought from the Steampunker during certain moon phases
If one Mechanical boss has been defeated, the Flame Wings and the Butterfly Wings can offer more flight (Do not bother with farming for the materials, only use these wings if you happen to have the materials need on hand)
As an alternative to wings, a flying mount such as the Gelatinous Pillion or The Black Spot can be used. The Chillet and Roller Skates mounts provide excellent mobility but require platforms (or, for Roller Skates, minecart tracks) as they do not allow flight.
An Emblem for your class can increase your damage output significantly.
The Berserker's Glove increases the speed of melee weapons and whips, it also gives 8 defense.
The Moon Charm grants good general melee boosts.
The Magic Quiver (and its upgrades) offers decent boosts for bows. In particular, the Phoenix Quiver can increase the accuracy of the Daedalus Stormbow.
The Mana Cloak is helpful for mages as it automatically uses mana potions.
The Pygmy Necklace is a good accessory for summoners.
The Squire's Shield/Apprentice's Scarf are great choices for summoners, especially if you have the Tavernkeep's sentries.
The Heavy Sling can be used to keep a sentry near Prime at all times.
The Frog Leg (and its upgrades) makes all wings significantly faster, which helps when dodging its attacks.
The Charm of Myths increases your base health regeneration and reduces the cooldown on potions, making it a good choice if you have trouble dodging its attacks.
The Cobalt Shield or its upgrades make you immune to knockback, preventing Skeletron Prime from knocking you around.
Whipstacking users will want to equip the Snake Band, Silver Bracer, Wicked Armlet and/or their upgrades for enhanced damage.
The Shield of Cthulhu can greatly increase your mobility as well as provide some extra defense.
The Worm Scarf will reduce damage taken, making it a powerful choice.
The Brain of Confusion has a chance to dodge an attack, providing the player with a useful Cerebral Mindtrick buff.


==== Potions ====
Greater Healing Potions are recommended.
For buff potions, the Swiftness Potion, Ironskin Potion, and Regeneration Potion will help out immensely.
The Endurance Potion will complement the defense boost of the Ironskin Potion.
Rangers with Bows should bring along an Archery Potion or two.
Mages greatly benefit from Mana Regeneration Potions and Magic Power Potions.
Damage increasing potions like the Rage Potion and Wrath Potion are good for everyone.
The Lifeforce Potion increases your max health and allows you to take more hits.
A Summoning Potion will help with extra damage, even non-summoners can benefit from having a summon from something like the Optic Staff.


=== Specific Strategies ===


==== Gelatinous Pillion ====
An effective way to avoid his spinning head attack is to use a Gelatinous Pillion and jump on top of his head with the mount. You can even use this to your advantage to get extra hits as it keeps bouncing you up.

title: Suspicious Grinning Eye
content:
The Suspicious Grinning Eye is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Suspicious Eye, a miniature version of the Eye of Cthulhu, that follows the player. It normally shows a blue iris and pupil, but when moving faster than 31 mph the pupil slides up and reveals a mouth, similar to the Eye of Cthulhu's second form. The Suspicious Grinning Eye has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu in Master Mode.


== Trivia ==
The tooltip is a reference to the Suspicious Looking Tentacle item (or Suspicious Looking Eye light pet) and how the name of the pet, Suspicious Eye, is seemingly missing the word looking.
While the Suspicious Grinning Eye is equipped, the Suspicious Eye pet will always be in front of the player if they are standing still. After equipping the Suspicious Looking Tentacle, however, the Suspicious Eye pet will be pushed to the other side of the player and Suspicious Looking Eye light pet will hover in front instead.
Due to the pet's similarity to the Suspicious Looking Eye light pet, dyeing it with Teal Dye will make it look almost identical.
