title: Guide:Zenith
content:
The Zenith seed, also known as the Everything or Get fixed boi seed, is a special world seed that combines most aspects of all other secret world seeds and adds its own challenges. This guide is written with the Legendary Mode difficulty in mind.


== Preparation ==
Many players can become intensely frustrated by this seed if they are not properly prepared, as it combines numerous mechanics from other seeds. One recommendation for those who find the beginning too difficult is to prepare by playing these other seeds, so they can focus on individual changes. These include:

Remix: This seed flips the usual order of progression and has the player start in the Underworld. It makes the Surface a completely corrupted, inhospitable region, and moves weather events, Ocean creatures, and fishing to the lower layers of the world. It also shifts around the tiers of several weapons. It has significant changes up to post-Golem. Play this seed if you can't figure out where everything is in Zenith.
The Constant: This seed adds Hunger and Darkness mechanics, as well as making Cacti deal damage. Its changes are only relevant in world exploration, so it's not necessary to progress past a few bosses to get an idea of this seed. Play this seed if you frequently die to darkness or hunger in Zenith.
No Traps: This seed has far more traps and introduces the Bouncy Boulder and Life Crystal Boulder. Zenith generates 3x as many traps, while No Traps generates 15x as many, but it can help with forcing the player to consider the risk of traps constantly as they move around. Explosives in Underground Cabins and Geysers in Ruined Houses in particular are relevant in both seeds. Most changes stop being relevant after entering Hardmode. This seed can help the player get used to playing around traps, though it should be noted that No Traps has far more traps than Zenith does.
Not the Bees and Celebration Mk 10: These seeds don't strongly benefit the player from playing them. CelebrationMk10 has mostly cosmetic and/or beneficial changes, and primarily the cosmetic changes make it into this seed. Not the bees, on the other hand, completely changes most of the world generation, and little of this is carried over into Zenith other than larger Bee Hives and the presence of many Larvae. There is a strip of bee-related blocks near the top of the world, but this layer is unlikely to be encountered often in this game. There are additional bee-related changes unique to this seed, detailed below. The Blood Moon being more common and the buffed properties of the Wizard Hat, allowing an extra minion, are retained from the Celebration seed.
The Drunk world seed places the Dungeon under a Living Tree, which makes fighting Skeletron and Lunatic Cultist much more difficult, and it also includes both Evil biomes.
For the Worthy: This is the only other seed to allow Legendary difficulty. The bosses in this seed are close or identical in difficulty to Zenith, making it a good space to practice dealing with the sheer enemy difficulty without the wrenching world generation changes.
However, it also includes multiple other changes not included with the other seeds. These include:

Crispy Honey Blocks will generate throughout the Glowing Mushroom biome layer above the Underworld, and have a chance to release lava when mined.
The "True Surface" contains both evil biomes, and the two outer 1/6s of the world are converted to distinct evil biomes.
Living Trees, the Jungle Temple and Pyramids are painted red or purple.
Dungeon enemies do not drop any loot until Skeletron is defeated.
Hellbats will drop lava upon death (instead of Lava Slimes).


== World generation ==
This seed is unique in that there is a mini-game during world-generation. Dragging around the smiley-faced moon allows the player to hit shooting stars. Hitting more stars increases the prevalence of beneficial Pots, Heart Crystals, and Chests outside of Underground Cabins, as well as the prevalence of dangerous traps. The overall effect is generally small and can be ignored, though as Pots are generated before Bee Larva, this can reduce the chances of random Queen Bee spawns killing the player.


== The First Day ==
When play begins, the player finds themselves on a large island in the middle of the Underworld with a large collection of NPCs. This Ash island is surrounded by two lava lakes and the only enemies that spawn are Lava Slimes  - who are weaker and do not drop Lava - and  Mimics - who drop Gold Chest loot.
Beyond the surrounding lakes are Ruined Houses and standard Underworld enemies, including Hellbats, who now drop lava upon death. Depending on world generation, normal Underworld enemies may spawn near the edges of the starting island, forcing the player to use blocks to fend them off. 
The NPCs that spawn will sell helpful materials, but they will all die at the end of the first day, so getting a good amount of gold on the first day is important. If one manages to collect 10 Gold on the first day, the player can buy the Slime Staff from the Princess which is a solid earlygame weapon that can safely dispatch enemies in the mushroom layer.
If you don't get enough money, try breaking pots and with luck you can find a Coin Portal. Pulling a Mimic to the NPCs or into a pit can also be tried.
Talk to the Tax Collector at the end of the day to collect the available money before they die. When the NPCs have finally died, check if they dropped useful loot like the Paintball Gun.
You will also spawn with the Hunger debuff. At this early point in the game, the only source of food will be Pomegranates and Spicy Peppers dropped from Ash trees. Eating any Food item will decrease hunger, preventing you from dying.


== Getting Settled ==
As soon as time allows, you can start building your base. Note that the Wall of Flesh fight will still take place in the underworld, so it's recommended to build you base sidewards or downwards instead of upwards to protect your NPCs.
The first goal is to shake trees to drop bombs and Fruit and break Pots to drop Rope and Fallen Stars. The bombs will destroy trees and give you blocks and wood, the Fallen Stars can be sold or used for mana crystals, and the Fruit can be sold or used to ward off starvation. Note that you can get more Fruit from shaking trees each day. Ash Wood can be used to make weapons and armor, but on Legendary enemies deal so much damage that the extra defense is miniscule; the armor will also reduce lava damage, but not by enough to let an earlygame character survive. Ash Wood Platforms play a much bigger role in letting you avoid enemies and Lava, letting you explore higher layers. Do note that the Ash Trees are the only abundant and easily accessible wood in this seed. So it's recommended to replant them as soon as you fell them. 
As soon as the Cooking Pot becomes available, Rock Candy can be crafted thanks to the abundance of Gem Bunnies and Gem Squirrels. The best medium-term solutions to food are Fishing or cooking Critters, both of which generally require the Bug Net from the Merchant, or Cooked Marshmallows that can be obtained from the Merchant once you find the Snow biome. Long-term solutions include buying large amounts of Pad Thai from the Traveling Merchant, crafting the Teapot and Teacups after defeating Skeletron, or planting Pumpkin Seeds on Grass for Pumpkin Pies. 
If you haven't already also kill a few Lava Slimes for Gel that can be crafted into Torches, as this helps with building Housing and for getting good light in higher layers. Platforms can be used to trap large numbers of Slimes and safely kill them, especially with the Underworld's high spawn rates.
The money you collected previously will also help with spawning the Merchant who sells a plethora of useful items such as the Piggy Bank, the Mining Helmet, the Bug Net and the Iron Anvil. Buying the latter is even recommended since it can take quite a while until you find stone to build a Furnace. This it allows you to directly process ingots you find in chests or Crates. Examples for early uses would also be crafting a Cooking Pots, as to not starve all the time, or a Sawmill which allows you to craft cheap containers with Dressers as well as Beds. The Lesser Healing Potion he sells can also be used as a Bottle (crafting station) which lets you save the sparse bottles you can find for brewing potions.
Don't forget to plan ample space in your base for Herbs in Clay Pots, since plants are going to be in a very limited supply.
The starting island is also big enough, that one half can be used for fighting bosses and events, while the other half can be used to grow Gem trees which give very useful crafting materials. Consider Shimmering a Magic Mirror to get an early supply of Diamonds to grow. Later on, this plantation can also be upgraded to grow your own Chlorophyte.


== Gearing up ==
What items to go for can be quite the daunting prospect. The following chapter should give a good overview of what to strife for.
Whatever you do though, don't use Iron or Lead for armor and weapons. The increased stats are negligible and you will need a large amount of it for Tools, Crafting stations, Buckets, Ironskin Potion and especially Minecart Tracks, so it's best to save it. 


=== Hooks ===
The first and easiest Hook to get will be the Squirrel Hook sold by the Zoologist. This one should be sufficient until your Gem tree farms generate enough gems to craft a Gem hook. The next, and last hook before Hardmode starts, is the Ivy Whip, which can be skipped if deemed unecessary.


=== Tools ===
There are three similiar pre-Hellstone ore pickaxes that can be gained early on and can fastrack the players progress. The Fossil Pickaxe and the Reaver Shark with the first being the easiest to be obtained. Whichever is used is up to personal preference.
The Gravedigger's Shovel becomes an extremely powerful tool until well into Hardmode, due to the constant need to dig upwards as well as the high amount of soft blocks generated from the additional mushroom layers and the false surface.
Both the Digtoise and the Digging Molecart are exceptional tools when it comes to building Hellevators, trenches against corruption, and Arenas. The cart is especially well suited for building arenas, since the Tracks it lays are good for placing walls and since it can also remove the tracks it has layed before. 
The re-seeding ability of the Axe of Regrowth becomes also quite useful since most Herbs and Trees need to be regrown quite often or the player will run out fast. Its ability to place grass is also very helpful with placing Sunflowers around your world.


== Early & General exploration ==
Directly above the Underworld layer is a Glowing Mushroom biome layer that contains Crispy Honey Blocks and basic ores. Zombies and Demon Eyes spawn on this layer. No Heart Crystals can spawn in this layer, though the player can find Chests with surface loot that greatly helps earlygame and can't be trapped. 
Be very careful when mining in the layer above, as this layer contains Crispy Honey Blocks which, in this seed, release lava upon mining. Be aware that if that lava isn't properly contained, it will flow down into your base. Torches provide more light to recognize and avoid Crispy Honey, and these blocks also take one more hit to mine than the Mud around them. Players should mine funnels to safely drain lava.
Consider roping up to check the start of the mushroom layer on both ends of the starting island. If you see mud wall in the mushroom layer, the Jungle is directly above, and that portion of the mushroom layer will have very little Crispy Honey and wide open spaces that make it much easier to traverse. This also tells the player where to find the Snow, Desert, and Dungeon Biomes. The downside is that the Jungle is extremely dangerous to explore early on.

If the player encounters a massive Crispy Honey barrier, it's a Bee Hive. As safely mining through a Bee Hive is slow and dangerous, the player should find a way around it; even returning to the Underworld in search of another path up is faster and safer.
Pots may drop Slimes, which can immediately attack the player for huge damage and potentially kill them. Use Rope or Shuriken to break pots from safety, and make sure to always have space to move away and catch your breath.
If the player finds a Gas Trap in the chest, they can survive by placing a Campfire and using 2 Lesser Health Potions, the first between 40 and 50 HP and the second as soon as possible.
The player should use blocks to avoid having to fight most enemies, as they have too much HP and damage and too little useful loot.
Above this buffer is a false "surface". Here, trees grow and weather occurs. Surface versions of all the regular biomes appear, including the Desert, Snow biome, and Jungle. This is one of the best spots for early players to gather loot, establish bases, and farm creatures. Happiness is not tracked in this seed, making it easier to get pylons.

This is also the layer to find Stone, which does not generate in the Glowing Mushroom layer. If the player spawns directly below the Snow biome or Underground Desert, it will be necessary to travel left or right to get enough stone for a Furnace. If the player enters this layer in the Jungle, they can buy a Furnace directly from the Merchant.
Aside from the very center (i.e. directly above spawn), most of this layer counts as the Ocean biome 50% of the time, allowing the player to fish up Ocean Crates, find the Angler, buy an Ocean Pylon, and potentially find Sharks for Shark Fins.
Players using magic weapons can find Fallen Stars trapped in slimes or from broken Pots, allowing them to increase their mana capacity.
There are numerous threats on this level:
Traps abound in this level. However, Wire is not visible until Skeletron is defeated. This means it may take quite a while to clear out pressure plates and other traps by trial and error, or by paying close attention. Dangersense Potions from Shiverthorn are fantastic for identifying and avoiding Traps, both from pressure plates and from Dead Man's Chests.
Crispy Honey Blocks give players the Burning debuff on contact and may release Lava when mined.
Players will take damage in Darkness. This can be fixed by purchasing the Mining Helmet from the Merchant, using Shine Potions, holding and placing Torches, finding enough Crimtane Ore or Demonite Ore and Topaz to craft the Magiluminescence, or using weapons or other items that produce light.
Very large Bee Hives generate in this layer. The player should avoid entering these due to the risk of summoning Queen Bee, though they can obtain Honey Buckets from them and farm Hornets on top. Hive Walls also skyrocket spawn rates, making them solid options for early enemy farming.
Priority should be placed on getting a minion early on such as Abigail's Flower, Flinx Staff, or Slime Staff, as they can damage enemies through walls. Remember that contact damage is multiplied by a large factor on this seed, often resulting in instant death upon contact, so the player should be careful that the minion does not knock the enemy into them.
Crafting an Obsidian Skull can let the player walk on Crispy Honey Blocks without being damaged. Alternatively, the player can use Pylons or a Bed to avoid moving through the mushroom layer again.
Chests can contain Moon Lord Legs and Red Potion, both of which are excellent for early exploration. Red Potions can give the otherwise-unobtainable Lifeforce buff pre-Skeletron, but these potions are far more valuable when drunk immediately to support exploration with their array of long-lasting and powerful buffs.
Periodically saving your money with a Piggy Bank or similiar while exploring is also a good way to not lose too much money upon death.


== Outposts, Fast Traveling and Fishing ==
Due to the high danger, it's also very useful to set up smallscale houses with a Spawn point. These are veritable timesavers since they allow the player to continue spelunking nearby after death  This tactic becomes especially useful after the Demon Conch has been acquired, which allows you to easily teleport to your hell base, since it frees up the Magic Mirror for traveling back to your outpost.
Since the layers are smaller than in standard seeds, fishing becomes way more important as not all biome specific chests may be able to spawn. This means that items such as the Ice Skates can become very hard to obtain. Due to the higher difficulty, you are also going to craft many fish based potions. So it's urgently recommended to turn some of your secondary bases into an easily accessible fishing base. These can then be further turned into Towns, to reduce spawnrates, and connected via Pylon to your mainbase allowing you to traverse the map quickly and flexibly. 
If you don't have enough NPCs to populate these houses, the Town Slimes as well as the pets sold by the Zoologist can become very useful. Also don't forget to set up spawn reducing items such as the Peace Candle and the Sunflower.
It's recommended to save the Mushroom Pylon for a Space based fishing safe house since Sky Crates are the best source of important Pre-Hardmode Accessories such as the Lucky Horseshoe.


== Early bosses ==
The Underworld you spawn in actually serves as an excellent boss arena, as it is generally very wide, flat, and has few obstacles. A bridge of Platforms (or two) should be enough to fight King Slime or the Eye of Cthulhu.
Note that King Slime has a chance to spawn when killing any slime if he has not yet been defeated, meaning that a Slime Rain is not needed for him to spawn. To avoid potentially inconvenient spawns while exploring, it can help to kill him once with a Slime Crown to prevent his random spawns elsewhere.
The Eye of Cthulhu can spawn at any world height during the regular day/night cycle. However, it will not despawn at day, allowing for longer fights. This boss now gains a spin attack in the second phase, where it temporarily reflects projectiles and releases numerous Servants of Cthulhu. Using area of effect or multiple projectile weapons such as the Boomstick or piercing weapons such as the Diamond Staff can help deal with these extra minions.
Due to changes to boss despawning behavior, if the player doesn't want to fight a random Eye of Cthulhu spawn, they should wait far away from their bed for the spawn, wait for the Eye to become visible on-screen, and only then teleport away to safety. Otherwise, the Eye will follow the player all the way back to spawn without despawning.
Upon defeating the Eye of Cthulhu, it is recommended to craft the Magiluminescence, which removes the darkness problem entirely and provides significant boosts to movement speed, even with boots.


== True surface ==
The top part of the Underground layer is filled with lava pools as the player approaches the surface, requiring more care in digging.
The surface itself, as well as the leftmost and rightmost parts of the map, are entirely infected by the Corruption and the Crimson. The surface is always night time, and enemy spawnrates are much higher. 
The surface is incredibly hostile. Much of it is covered with pools of Lava. The player is constantly under the effects of greatly reduced gravity, and any contact with the top of the world causes an instant death. A grappling hook can be very helpful to players looking for Floating Islands. However, all Skyware Chests are now replaced by Locked Gold Chests. They still retain the typical sky chest loot though.
Building a base on the surface is possible if it is raised high off the ground far enough away from the evil biomes, but Forest pylons do not work there--if desiring to build an artificial surface island for a pylon base, a Mushroom pylon base (particularly one close to the dungeon's entrance) would probably be the best choice. Ocean pylons also work when high enough off the surface. Finding a Magic Conch will aid in quickly reaching the surface.
It also may be useful to create a tunnel that goes from the underworld to the surface, as it allows one to get to the true surface without a need for pylons or the Magic Conch.


== Pre-Skeletron Mechanisms ==
As always, buyable Mechanisms will only be available after Skeletron has been defeated. This doesn't mean that you won't be able to set up your own mechanisms though. With a bit of trial and error, you can simply re-use the existing invisible wires of dismantled traps. 
This can e.g. allow you to place Heart statues in your arena for a quick and easy heal during bossfights even though it shouldn't be available yet.
You can also use this setup to farm items such as Shark Fins, Bezoars, Obsidian Roses and others via Statues quite efficiently. If you use the auto jump of the Frog Legs to jump against a low ceiling, you can even spawn a large amount of enemies in a short time without the use of Timers.


== Deerclops ==
Deerclops is another optional boss, but one which is much easier than the other pre-Hardmode bosses due to its lack of For the worthy AI changes and the fact that it does not despawn on death. Navigating it can be difficult due to not having a wide open area to summon it in. This can be fixed by creating an artificial Snow biome in the Underworld or by excavating a large arena in the Snow biome. Note that the Warmth Potion drastically reduces the damage taken from all of its attacks. With enough defensive gear and potions, it can even be face tanked on legendary difficulty before killing any of the evil bosses. The Houndius Shootius it drops is the best sentry in pre-Hardmode, while the Pew-matic Horn is one of the strongest Guns in pre-Hardmode.


== Queen Bee ==
Queen Bee is faster, can charge diagonally and shoots stingers much faster in this seed. However, Bee Hives are larger, providing more effective arenas (watch out for low-lying hives that have Hive blocks replaced by Crispy Honey Blocks that burn the player).
However, the most effective strategy against the queen is luring her to hell via a teleport and then fighting her on a minecart track. Simply built a minecart track that spans the whole starting island with a Spawn point in the middle. Preferably with a house made from Platforms on top of the tracks since those won't hinder movement or the minecart. Get an accurate gun such as Flintlock Pistol or a The Undertaker and as soon as she gets into the range of the weapon, proceed to shoot her while steadily driving away from her. Note that she doesn't have to be in view to be hit and that the map overlay is your friend. As soon as she comes too near, teleport back to your spawn point and drive in the opposite direction as soon as she comes in range. If the house is built correctly one won't even have to re-mount the minecart at this point. Then repeat until she is dead.


== Evil biome bosses ==
The Eater of Worlds and Brain of Cthulhu are very difficult in this seed for two different reasons. 
First, summoning them is difficult due to the extreme boosted spawn rate and difficulty of evil biome enemies. Preparing an arena is the most difficult part, as all prehardmode evil biome enemies have extremely high stats, speed, and knockback resistance, letting them kill even late prehardmode players in 2~3 hits. For these reasons, it may be better to create an artificial Corrupt or Crimson biome in the underworld. Ebonsand and Crimsand are readily available at the beaches and can be mined with any pickaxe. If you use a delayed charge, such as a Sticky Bomb, to destroy the last Crimson Heart / Shadow Orb you can safely spawn the respective boss in your arena by teleporting back to your Spawn point prepared via Beds beforehand.
Second, these bosses have received AI changes in this seed. The Brain of Cthulhu now has completely opaque mirror images coupled with much higher defense, and it reverses gravity in the second portion of the fight which will nullify platforms and likely kill you if fought on the surface and not under a roofed arena, while the Eater of Worlds releases a buffed Eater of Souls every time one of its segments, excluding its tail, is destroyed, and it shoots unbreakable Vile Spit even when underground.
It is recommended to break a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart well before the fight so the Goblin Army to spawn, allowing access to the Goblin Tinkerer for reforging and combining accessories. Building a base at The Aether to gain Permanent boosters via Shimmer is also recommended.
These two bosses are very difficult even with on-tier equipment, so it may be necessary to chip away at them through multiple attempts to obtain Tissue Samples or Shadow Scales. Gathering 6 of either enables the player to craft a Nightmare/Deathbringer Pickaxe and mine Hellstone. Molotov Cocktails, Boulders, and  are a cheap way to kill Creepers or Eater of Worlds segments. Scattering Spiky Balls before or during the fight can also deal significant damage. 
Regardless of class, it is also a good idea to use Summon weapons and a Summoning Potion for extra damage. With luck a Bewitching Table can also be acquired from the dungeon before killing Skeletron, allowing you to bring three summons without using any Equipment.
The Volcano sword is especially effective against both evil bosses, as its high damage bypasses defense, cleaves through several Creepers/segments at once, and sets the true Brain of Cthulhu on fire, allowing the player to easily spot the real one during the second portion of the fight. It also synergizes well with the Flask of Poison for another damaging debuff.
The Inferno Potion also allows you to passively ignite the bosses just by being nearby, doing considerable damage over time to the many Creepers/segments while automatically destroying Vile Spit projectiles.


== Old One's Army Tier 1 ==
The Old One's Army can be summoned now. It is recommended that the player fights it in the spawning area. This event allows players to gain the War Table and accessories such as the Apprentice's Scarf which combined allow the player to summon three sentries, which makes a big difference against difficult bosses. Flails or Bows with Jester's Arrows are efficient ways to fight the enemies, using sentries placed high on platforms, or flying minions such as the Imp Staff to defeat Etherian Wyverns.
At this point one side of the invasion can be taken care of by the Explosive Trap Rod and a well placed Crimson Rod. The other side as well as the boss can simply be defeated by using the Grey Zapinator and the Meteor armor. 
It's also recommended to farm 60 Defender Medals before the event upgrades its tier to the second level in Hardmode. This allows you to buy a full set of armor as well as the corresponding weapon which can easily deal with the new difficulty.


== Skeletron ==
Skeletron is difficult for several reasons. First, the Dungeon now spawns deep under a Living Tree, leaving the player without a large natural place to fight. Second, the Dungeon is still near the Corruption or Crimson and has boosted enemy spawns. Third, upon losing his hands, Skeletron now spawns many Dark Casters as well as skull shaped projectiles.
Players can make Peace Candles to decrease surrounding spawns while mining out a large arena. It is recommended to teleport to your arena as soon as Skeletron spawns. Be aware that Skeletron despawns if the arena is too far away. 
This arena can also serve for the Lunatic Cultist later in the game. 
Using Queen Bee drops such as the Bee Gun can help significantly in this fight, as the seeking bees can defeat the enemy casters and allow you to soley focus on dodging.
If you get mana problems, consider using a Mana Flower or its upgrades
It is also imperative that you get all the Buffs you can. All the potions, environmental, food, kite and furniture buffs you get.
If you don't need the honey buff and the armor penetration of the Stinger Necklace, you can also use the Magic Cuffs for more mana and less Mana Sickness.
If you use the Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons, multi tapping the Jump key can also give a strong diagonal speed buff to the next platform in your arena where you can repeat the process.
Even though they heal for the same amount of health per second of Potion Sickness, it is also recommended to use Restoration Potions over the Honeyfin since it can be used sooner without overhealing and thus can lead to a higher net healing over the whole fight.


== Dungeon ==
The Dungeon has an increased number of traps. Finding the Mechanic is a priority, as now that Skeletron is defeated, Wire can be seen, resulting in an easier time finding traps. For this reason, players should craft The Grand Design.


== Preparing for Hardmode ==
Due the increased difficulty it can be a good idea to build most of the structures you need in Hardmode right now. Be it boss arenas, chlorophyte farms or Pylon supported fishing bases, the more you finish now, the less you have to contend with the supercharged hardmode enemies. It's, of course, also recommended to protect biomes from the spread of the hardmode biomes. Thanks to the Hallow spawning right next and below the Jungle, that part is relatively safe. So we mostly have to build a hellevator on the Dungeon side of the world and built a trench above the lower mushroom layer as well as below the upper mushroom layer where the infected parts end. The Digging Molecart and Digtoise are highly recommended for this project. On another note, you might also want to stock up on potion ingredients now while you can still fish in relative peace.


== Wall of Flesh ==
The Wall of Flesh is very difficult in this seed, as it has smaller hitboxes, high health and speed, and spawns Fire Imps during the fight, whose projectiles can't be destroyed. 
Fortunately, your starting area provides a Hell Bridge across much of the map, but it will also kill off your NPCs. Make sure to build houses in the Underworld in a way that won't impede your fight.
Alternatively, you can teleport your NPCs via the King Statue/Queen Statue to a safehouse outside the underworld. 
An Imp Statue can be used to farm Fire Imp Banners for the arena, more than halving Fire Imp damage and letting the player even outright ignore them if they have enough defense.
One option is to build a long Minecart track across the Underworld for this fight, as it will be useful for many future fights. It also prevents Fire Imps from spawning in the player's path and helps with dodging the projectiles since they spawn farther away. If using this approach, the Roller Skates combined with the Shield of Cthulhu provides a great amount of maneuverability and additional invulnerability while being able to constantly outspeed the boss.
An alternative is using Gravitation Potion to run on the ceiling, also avoiding imps directly in the player's path. It is impossible to destroy the imps' fireballs while the Wall of Flesh is alive.
Players can also guide the path the Wall of Flesh will take by making the ceiling and floor 3 blocks thick and 21 blocks apart. This squeezes the Wall into a tighter space where weapons like Night's Edge can deal loads of damage to it.
The Golf Cart mount is able to outspeed the Wall all the way until it reaches its lowest HP threshold, while also having great jump height to avoid lasers, Hungry, and Imps.


== Early Hardmode ==
When Hardmode starts, the Mimics that offered basic loot now offer standard loot.
The Hallow no longer spawns in a diagonal stripe. Instead, it replaces large strip of underground evil biome on the same side as the Jungle, occupying roughly 20% of the world.
If you have easy access to a pyramid in an evil biome, it can be easily converted into a chokepoint to farm materials for the powerful Onyx Blaster right at the start of hardmode. With it gaining supportive summoning weapons like the Spider Staff directly afterwards should be unproblematic.
The first Hardmode ore will also have spawned. Note that it can also spawn near your base in the middle of hell allowing you to mine your first nodes in relative safety.
Generating the strongest Ore requires smashing six Demon Altars or Crimson Altars instead of three, as both types of ore generate. Alternatively, hardmode Crates can give you the needed ores. In addition other useful loot like the Barnacle Staff, Scaly Truffle, the Sundial and others can be gained this way. Since one can now also fish for the Prismite, which is used in the powerful Lifeforce Potion, it is even recommended to go fishing. Not smashing the altars also prevents the Pirate Invasion and Mechdusa from spawning letting you gear up in relative peace. 
The amount of hardmode ore needed is actually quite minuscule. You only need enough for an upgraded anvil, an upgraded forge, a t2 hardmode ore pickaxe and a t3 hardmode ore armor. As for the latter Frost armor is recommended since its Frostbite debuff works greatly when fighting Wyverns, Queen Slime, Mechdusa and Plantera if combined with Crystal Darts and a Dart Pistol or Dart Rifle. It's also farmed quite easily since Frost Golems are largely harmless in the underground terrain and one can also use both t3 ores when crafting it.
Similarly, both Crimson and Corruption exist in this world, allowing combos such as Cursed Darts with the Dart Pistol. Which type of Mimic spawns when placing a Key of Night in an empty Chest will alternate every day. 
If the player has built a minecart track as suggested, it can be used to easily fight the very dangerous Biome Mimics.
Wyverns can be dangerous due to the decreased maneuverability in the space layer and the high spawnrate. Due to their limited moveset they can still be easily outmaneuvered though. It's recommended to fight them in your secondary base in the space layer since the NPCs, combined with the Sunflower and Peace Candle, reduce the spawning enemies to a managable level.
Their flight speed is also lower than ones falling speed. So they're basically helpless against ranged attacks when dropping from a high altitude. 
If these don't work, it can also help to fight them as low as possible, or to use minecarts or mounts for fights instead. Mounts can also help with farming Wyverns directly, by simply outspeeding the Wyvern horizontally as the player glides through the world with a Featherfall Potion. 
Venom Dart Traps can now be created for efficient farms against events like the Goblin Army and the Pirate Invasion.


== Queen Slime and Mechdusa ==
As described before, a very long minecart track in the Underworld is an excellent way to fight these bosses. Alternatively, using Gravitation Potion in an above-ground arena can help, especially if a roof is built.
If using the minecart track, Teleporters and Pressure Plate Track, as well as tracks hammered into bumpers, can allow safe turnarounds.

Queen Slime has roughly the same speed as the minecart when flying, so this method allows the player to remain safe throughout the fight, with turning around being the most dangerous part. Lilith's Necklace can also keep up with her flying and dodge her stomps, while also benefiting from jumping freely.
There is no way to fight the mechanical bosses individually in this seed. Instead, the three boss-summoning items must be combined into Ocram's Razor, which summons Mechdusa. This boss can be spawned anytime, not just at night.
Mechdusa is a very difficult boss, but has some features that make it not quite as difficult as it first seems. The main points in the player's favor are:

All parts except the main Destroyer body have their max health reduced by 20%.
There is no time limit.
The Twins and the Destroyer are attached to Skeletron Prime and cannot move freely.
Most strategies revolve around defeating the Destroyer first, as there are many weapons that do intense damage due to piercing (such as the Daedalus Stormbow with Unholy Arrows, the Drippler Crippler, the Dart Rifle, the Nimbus Rod and Clinger Staff, or Whips). This part can often be killed faster than the others, and eliminates the threats of lasers and of Probes. It is useful, if possible, to collect the hearts dropped by Probes. Alternatively, a solid block floor will block almost all of the lasers, and Probes themselves cannot ram the player in this seed.
One interesting feature of this boss is that different parts despawn at different distances, with the Destroyer despawning last. If using the minecart rail in the Underworld, doing fast can cause this, allowing the player to defeat the Destroyer alone. This still unlocks things such as Life Fruit, Hallowed Bars, the Steampunker, and the second tier of Old One's Army.
The minecart can still be used if not trying to despawn, by keeping an eye on how close the boss parts are, especially the Twins. When on the left, Retinazer's lasers can hit hit more easily, but Spazmatism has difficulty attacking the player with cursed flames. The opposite is true on the right side. Killing Skeletron Prime separates the parts, so should be left for last.
The player can achieve enough jump height to simply circle around Mechdusa via Gravitation Potions, Featherfall Potions, and/or a Mount, even in the underworld. Bombing out the ash in the center island can provide large amounts of vertical space for maneuverability. If moving around Destroyer is an issue, Teleporters can quickly let the player change their height.


== Old One's Army Tier 2 ==
The second tier of Old One's Army is now available, and it can reward the player with strong items like the Phantom Phoenix, Ballista Cane, or the Creeper Egg. The latter can replace the Magiluminescence, freeing up an accessory slot. If you plan to defeat Plantera quickly afterwards though, you can skip the pet in favor of the Wisp in a Bottle.
Weapons such as the Dao of Pow, Hallowed Repeater, or Magical Harp can be useful against large groups. Meanwhile, the Barnacle Staff is extremely good against flying enemies. 
If you saved up 60 Defender Medals during the first tier, you can directly buy a full set of armor and the corresponding cane. For instance, the Squire armor combined with the Ballista Cane and the Barnacle Staff can nearly solo the second tier of this event with only the Ogre needing extra damage. 
It is also recommended to do this tier around eight to nine times. The 210 Medals rewarded from it will allow you to directly buy the third tier armor and corresponding weapon as soon as they become available.


== Solar Eclipse ==
Solar Eclipses can also randomly appear as soon as the first mechanical boss has been defeated. Solar Eclipse enemies will only spawn in the cavern layer and underworld; however, the event itself will still boost spawn rates in every layer for farming.
Contrary to most other invasions, this event also unlocks additional enemy types based on the worlds progression. 
It is recommended to farm useful items such as the Moon Stone or Neptune's Shell right now, since the Eclipse becomes exorbitantly more difficult after Plantera has been defeated. 
This is due to stronger enemy types that will spawn including the mini-bosses Nailhead and Mothron.
The Nailhead is a tanky enemy whose projectiles are not only very difficult to see, but can also kill the player in one or two hits, which becomes extremely dangerous with the high amount of enemies on the screen. It's recommended to try to outrange him of it spawns.
Mothron itself is equally dangerous due to its high speed, damage, ability to ignore blocks and possibility to spawn at the same as the Nailhead. It is recommended to wait for it to spawn in a sealed off arena so it can be fought separately to the remaining invasion. It is also very vulnerable when laying eggs and often restarts the process if the egg is destroyed before hatching.


== Plantera ==
Plantera is faster, larger, shoots more rapidly and now releases thorny bushes when her tentacles attach to anything. Having a large arena is essential, and fortunately the large Bee Hives that spawn in this world can be a good start. A long horizontal or vertical tunnel also helps with phase 2 by allowing the player to avoid Plantera's immense lateral acceleration. During this phase she will also spawn not one but nine tentacles that deal damage and soak up the players attacks, so weapons that pierce can and deal damaging conditions can be quite useful. A combination of Frost armor and the homing Crystal Darts can be quite useful here until the tentacles have been defeated.
Note that Plantera only despawns if the player is far enough away for a sufficient amount of time, so the player can use this to lure Plantera to wherever their jungle based arena is.
Be warned that Jungle Mimics spawn in this world which can severly hinder bossfights, so a walled off arena might be a good idea but be wary of Planrtera's thorny bushes. Besides having the same damage and attacks as the Corrupt or Crimson Mimics, they also have a 'stuff cannon' attack that floods the inventory.


== Full House ==
With Plantera defeated, the Cyborg can finally spawn which also allows the last NPC, the Princess, to spawn.
The Cyborg sells, among other things, Nanites which can be crafted into powerful crowd control ammunitions and flasks thanks to the Confusion they apply. Since a high percentage of enemies aren't immune, this can make many invasions, both dungeons, and other encounters by several magnitudes easier. 
The Princess sells all the items needed for the Greedy Ring, which can be harder to come by. 
The Truffle now also sells the Autohammer which is needed for Shroomite Bars.
Meanwhile the Witch Doctor unlocks his last tier of inventory and now offers the Vial of Venom, Leaf Wings and multiple powerful Summoner items.


== Hardmode Dungeon ==
The Hardmode Dungeon is relatively unchanged, except for enemies' greatly increased contact damage. Both evil Biome Chests are available in the Dungeon. The surface with its high amount of enemy spawns is an excellent place to farm Biome Keys, especially since Corrupt/Crimson versions of the Snow biome and Desert exist there.


== The Moon Invasions ==
The Frost Moon and the Pumpkin invasions can also be summoned now. 
Besides the higher attributes and the fact that they can spawn everywhere in the world, they're relatively unchanged though. 
Both have similar enemies that are susceptile to the Flask of Nanites, a seemingly similiar difficulty and similiar but great loot that can set one up to defeat all of the remaining invasions.
With knowledge and preparation, the Frost Moon becomes the easier of the two invasions though and thus is recommended to be done first.
One reason is that the ornament attack of the Everscream can be easily avoided by a sufficiently high plattform making the boss way less dangerous. The other reason is that the events main boss, the Ice Queen, as well as Flockos damage is reduced heavily by the Warmth Potion. Combined with the Endurance Potion and, if needed, other dammage reducing gear, their threat is drastically reduced making the whole invasion easier.


== Old One's Army Tier 3 ==
The third tier of the Old One's Army is also available now and can reward one with powerful items after Betsy has been defeated. 
The boss itself is the problem though, since there is a high chance of her ripping the player or the crystal apart before one can manage to deplete her over 125.000 health points.
Thus, it's recommended to go full summoner here since it benefits the event Sentries as well as all other summons. 
The most efficient way is by getting a T3 Tavernkeep armor as well as weapon, Pumpkin Moon accessories and the Morning Star. 
With Buffs one can easily reach six sentries and six Minions in addition to a very high damage boost. This way the Ballista Staff can easily reach over 450 damage per hit for example.
If this is strategy is followed, Betsy only needs to be tagged with the Morning Star. This forces all 15 event sentries, as well as the other 12 summons, to target her while also allowing the summons to land critical hits which should kill her in short order.
If one should still die, a Teleporter from ones spawn point back to the crystal can also be quite handy.
As for non-event sentries, the Barnacle Staff is still great for dealing with the non-boss flyers. If available, the Staff of the Frost Hydra can also be used. 
The minor bosses can easily be dispatches by using a weapon fitting to the Tavernkeep armor like a Terra Blade with an Flask of Ichor.


== Golem ==
The Jungle Temple itself is often nearer the center of the surface, inhospitable and difficult to reach. It is much larger than usual, has more traps (including TNT Barrels and Gas Traps), and, most importantly, prevents the player from seeing, using, or cutting Wire within it until the Golem is defeated. It is also painted a dark color that is difficult to see in.
Using the Hunter Potion, Dangersense Potion and Spelunker Potion together lets one navigate the dungeon without much trouble though. 
Also use Nanite-based weaponry as well as Summon weapons to keep the enemies away while disabling the traps.
The Rod of Discord will make navigating the temple far easier, including entering the Golem's chamber directly from the outside which removes the need to travel from the entrance to the room. It can also be used to lead Golem from the (possibly small) chamber it spawns in out to a larger, pre-prepared arena. If the rod isn't available, one can also teleport to a Bed directly underneath the temple.
Be warned that Golem will enrage if the outside arena is not considered part of the Underground Jungle. Golem will also despawn if one teleports away too far. 
If one wants to fight Golem inside the temple, consider setting up a safe space near the Golem chamber using Trapdoors. Those can't be opened by enemies and thus allow a fallback point to recuperate when preparing the arena or when making the journey to the chamber itself.
It's also possible to re-purpose the existing traps in the chamber to create Mechanisms even though tool usage is prevented. Simply cover the natural traps with blocks and then set up your Heart statues and Timers nearby.
Golem itself is far harder in this seed. During the fight, the player's vision will go dark, similar to the Blackout debuff, and Golem will destroy any light source it touches. In addition, Golem has much smaller hitboxes and, in its second form, can jump much higher.
Seeing Golem can be made easier by painting the arena with Illuminant Coating, or, in rematches, by fighting in the Underworld where there is more visibility (although this will enrage Golem).


== Duke Fishron ==
Duke Fishron hasn't been changed in this seed. His high damage and speed still make him an formidable foe.
If you're having trouble, build one rectangular box at each end of the ocean and connect them via Teleporters and Pressure Plates. The boxes themselves are ideally connected via a third teleporter to your oceanic fishing spot. 
The blocks of the boxes will negate most of the attacks, such as the Sharkrons, with exception of his charge attack. If he charges, simply take a step back to teleport to the other side and continue attacking him. Note that in phase three, you will probably only stay for a few seconds on each side before teleporting back. 
It's also best to use weapons that ignore blocks like Betsy's Wrath. If these aren't available, then you will need to add arrow slits to your boxes. 
It's recommended to add Heart statues to each side that are activated when the pressure plate on the opposite box is triggered. This, combined with a Heartreach Potion, will allow you to instantly heal in case you're too slow with activating the mechanism.
If you're still having problems, consider using immunity gear such as the Cross Necklace, the Black Belt and the Brain of Confusion.


== Empress of Light ==
The Prismatic Lacewings spawn naturally at all times of day, making them much easier to collect. They also don't despawn even when released outside the Hallow.
The Empress of Light will always be fought in enraged mode if on the true surface, and she will despawn at night. 
However, she can be fought underground in her normal mode (albeit with faster attacks due to AI changes). By far easiest is to just summon and fight her in the Underworld with arenas already made for other bosses. Otherwise, this fight proceeds as normal.
Note that the Terraprisma will only drop when she is defeated while enraged on the true surface.


== Endgame ==


=== The Lunatic Cultist ===
The Lunatic Cultist can be fought in the same arena as Skeletron but the arena can also be farther away since he can teleport to the player.
His attacks are faster, but the biggest danger here are the Prophecy's End and Ancient Vision projectiles, which count as NPCs and have doubled contact damage. These can easily one-shot the unwary player.


=== The Celestial Pillars ===
The Celestial Pillars spawn scattered throughout the Underground, Cavern or rarely on the true surface layers which can make it difficult to reach them without dying.
Thus a well built network of Pylon bases, Hellevators and Minecart Tracks is important. 
The pylon network can also help getting around quickly while still having the players Spawn set to their Moon Lord arena. Simply use a Demon Conch, or one of it's upgrades, to teleport to your hellbase to use the pylon there to get around. Then, when the boss spawns, teleport directly back to the arena.
Fighting the pillars underground is also different. Some pillars, like the Solar Pillar, become easier since the enemies are hindered by the blocks. Most actually become harder though since the enemies can one or two shot the player in addition to the limited space to dodge. Especially the Stardust Pillar, with it's many Milkyway Weavers, can amount to a high death count in the beginning.
The first pillar, that should be fought, is the one whose weapon you need the most, followed by the Stardust Pillar for the Stardust Dragon Staff. The last should be the one with the easiest access since the Moon Lord spawns shortly after killing it and quickly teleporting back and forth before destroying it to heal up, is a viable strategy.


=== The Moon Lord ===
The Moon Lord doesn't get increased contact or ranged damage. His only major change is, that after using the Phantasmal Deathray, he emits a large amount of Moon Boulders from his head, which bounce off of blocks. These can be avoided by luring him above solid blocks, by teleporting away, or by simply flying away quickly. They also stop completely after the main eye has been defeated. So destroying it should be priority number one. If the player starts at the bottom of the arena, they can easily fly upwards to mainly target that eye.
It is not necessary to fight the Moon Lord underground; again, though, remember that the top of the world is an instant-kill zone, and fall speed is dramatically reduced above the surface line. While not nearly as large as the space available in a normal world, the starting island and potentially the mushroom layer above it provide a huge area with no reduced gravity to maneuver around the Moon Lord. He can also be fought in a large enough arena, but be aware that opaque walls can completely cover and thus turn him invisible.
If you make it this far, congratulations on defeating the hardest world difficulty in Terraria!

title: Alchemy Flask
content:
The Alchemy Flask is a post-Skeletron crafting station used to craft potions. It has the same effect as the Alchemy Table when crafting potions: 1/3 (33.33%) chance for each ingredient not to be consumed. It is obtained by throwing an Alchemy Table into Shimmer. It fulfills a house's table requirement.
Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on an Alchemy Flask opens its crafting menu and grants the Alchemic Enhancement buff, which increases the duration of certain buffs by 20% (see Notes for complete list). The duration increase only applies to newly received buffs; existing buffs' duration will not be changed. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().


== Crafting ==


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


=== Used to craft ===

View in a separate page here.


== Notes ==
The Alchemy Flask will only extend the duration of the following buffs:

This includes all buffs from consumable potions, with the only exceptions being food buffs, Torch Blessing, Honey, and flask effects.
All items that can be crafted at an Alchemy Flask, Placed Bottle, or Alchemy Table are decrafted into a random subset of their ingredients when thrown into Shimmer. See Decrafting exceptions for details.
The Alchemy Flask emits some light when placed.


== Trivia ==
This item is part of a crossover with the game Dead Cells, sharing a similar design and recycling the same use sound as health fountains, which are used to restore the player's health and flask charges.
The Alchemy Flask is the largest crafting station in the game, taking up 16 tiles in total.

title: Ice biome
content:
The Ice biome, also known as the Underground Tundra or Underground Snow biome, is a biome that is the underground version of the Snow biome, starting at the Cavern layer and stopping at the lava layer. It is composed mainly of Snow Blocks and Ice Blocks. Thin Ice can be found generated over water and breaks when a character falls over 4 tiles onto it (unless using the Ice Skates or another accessory crafted from them). The Ice biome is the only place where Frozen Chests can be found naturally.
The player is considered to be in an Ice biome if they are below the border of the Underground and Cavern layers, and there are at least 1500 Snow or Ice Blocks nearby (reduced to only 300 Snow or Ice Blocks in Skyblock worlds).
In Hardmode, the Corruption, Crimson, and Hallow can spread through it, generating Purple, Red, and Pink Ice Blocks respectively. They are unable to spread through Snow Blocks. In these infected areas, all of the Ice biome's enemies can spawn, in addition to the enemies from the respective underground evil biome or Hallow. Furthermore, the Pigron spawns exclusively in infected Ice biome areas.


== Contents ==


== Notes ==
Most enemies in the Ice biome as well as in the Snow biome inflict the Chilled debuff, and more rarely the Frozen debuff.
An artificial Ice biome can not be made using Slush Blocks.

title: Vital Crystal
content:
The Vital Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health regeneration. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Life Crystal into Shimmer.

== Notes ==
Unlike many health regeneration items, which directly increase health gained per second, the Vital Crystal speeds up the natural health regeneration ramping by 20%.
For example, when only taking natural life regeneration into account, 5 seconds after taking damage, the player will receive the same amount of health regeneration that would normally take 6 seconds to reach.

title: Vampire Frog Staff
content:
The Vampire Frog Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Vampire Frog minion. It hops towards enemies to deal contact damage. The Vampire Frog Staff has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen.
Its best modifier is Fabled.


== Notes ==
The Vampire Frog minion applies 10 ticks of static immunity frames upon hitting an enemy, meaning it can hit up to six times per second.
The Vampire Frog, as well as the Flinx and the Pirates, are the only minions that are capable of swimming in all liquids whilst pursuing enemies.
The Vampire Frog minions can target enemies up to 50 blocks away from the player.


== Tips ==
This minion can be obtained earlier than the Hornet Staff and is fairly useful for close-range defense and clearing out enemies in open areas. However, Vampire Frogs are prone to getting stuck behind blocks. For more agile minions that can target airborne targets, the Flinx Staff may be preferable.
It can do relatively high damage at this point of the game, especially when paired with the Shark Tooth Necklace.
Because the Vampire Frog inflicts static immunity frames, summoning more than one will reach the maximum of 6 hits per second (summoning two of them can help with tracking fast enemies). Therefore, this minion should be used alongside other minions such as the Flinx Staff or Finch Staff.
This minion is effective against the Wall of Flesh if the upper eye is targeted, as the Vampire Frog will jump and fall constantly, hitting both eyes and the mouth.


== Trivia ==
The Vampire Frog may be a reference to the Vampyrius vampyrus, also known as the vampire tree frog or vampire flying frog, an endangered frog species endemic to Vietnam.
The tadpoles of the species have hook-like fangs adapted for consuming the unfertilized eggs in its clutch, which is its sole source of nutrition in the tadpole stage. The parents return repeatedly to lay more eggs for the tadpoles to eat. The fangs are reabsorbed during metamorphosis and are absent in the adult frogs.


== History ==

Now use independent immunity timers.

title: Webbed
content:
Webbed is a debuff that immobilizes the player completely. It is inflicted by Web Slimes and, in Expert Mode, by Black Recluses and Jungle Creepers, through their web spit attack. Unlike the Frozen or Stoned debuffs, it will instantly stop the player in place, preventing them from falling or sliding across the ground. While affected by the debuff, the player will be unable to use any items except for healing items.


== Causes ==


=== From enemy ===


== Notes ==
Webbed is the only debuff in the game that completely disables most of the player's inputs and cannot be prevented whatsoever. Therefore, it is commonly used in large multiplayer servers to stop a player.
The Stoned, Frozen, and Webbed debuffs all disable the player's inputs. When more than one of them is active, the priority for the effects is as follows: Stoned → Frozen → Webbed.
Note that if the Webbed effect coexists with any of the other effects, the player will not experience the effects of gravity.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.1: Jungle Creepers now spit web in Expert Mode.

title: Bleeding
content:
Bleeding is a debuff. When inflicted to players, it prevents natural health regeneration. Any other form of health regeneration bonuses, such as those granted by the Band of Regeneration or the set bonus of Palladium armor, will not be affected. The player is not prevented from using recovery potions, such as Bottled Water, while afflicted.
When inflicted to enemies, the debuff causes them to lose 12 health per second (4 damage displayed every 0.33 seconds). Its damage can be increased by Accelerated Afflictions.
Visually, the debuff causes affected entities to continuously release small blood droplets. The drops of blood will not appear if Blood and Gore is disabled in the game settings.
The debuff can be negated by equipping the Adhesive Bandage or its derivatives.

All enemies immune to Bleeding are also immune to the stronger version of the debuff, Hemorrhage.

title: The Torch God
content:
The Torch God is an event that is initiated by clustering a large number of Torches underground. It consists of dodging projectiles, and survivors are rewarded with the Torch God's Favor, an item which grants the player the option for their Torches to automatically match the biome they are placed in. Torches placed in their matching type of biome positively influence the player's luck in most areas.
The event can begin in any biome when there are at least 101 Torches of any type are found in a 41×41-tile rectangular area centered on the player's center, while the player is below the surface layer. It is possible for the event to start with less than 101 Torches placed if the player is moving, due to the game's calculation incorrectly counting some Torches more than once. The Torch God event cannot take place for any character who has already consumed the Torch God's Favor or has one in their inventory.
As the Torch God begins, torch flames shoot off at the player as projectiles, one at a time. They are fired in a random order, at a rate of 3 projectiles per second, and deal 40 / 80 / 120 base damage. Projectiles can pass through blocks to reach the player, but they can collide with blocks again after passing the player. Each Torch shoots one projectile and extinguishes itself afterward, as if it was switched off via wire. For the entire duration of the event, the player is inflicted with the Blackout debuff, significantly reducing their field of vision.
The Torch God ends once all nearby Torches have been spent, to a maximum of 200 attacks. If at least 95 Torches were fired, the player is rewarded with the Torch God's Favor item. All Torches re-light when the event ends. If the player dies or leaves underground, the event ends early and nothing is awarded; if the player moves into an area without Torches, the event will also end early, however, the Torch God's Favor will still be awarded if at least 95 Torches were fired.
While The Torch God is alive, the music Torch God will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Wall of Flesh (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Notes ==

This event is unique in that the player only needs to dodge and survive to complete it. There are no enemies or bosses to attack.
The Torch God is tied to one player at a time. In multiplayer, only one player is targeted by the torch fireballs and is affected by the Blackout debuff. Other players who have consumed the Torch God's Favor still hear the change of music for nearby players' events.
Torch fireballs match the color of the Torch they are fired from. This is purely cosmetic; all fireball colors have the same behavior and stats.
If the world is left while the Torch God is still ongoing, spent Torches will not re-light. They will have to be reactivated or replaced.
Passing the event, dying, or leaving the world temporarily invalidates the existing Torches. They can re-initiate the event after a short delay if the area is re-entered.
Any combination of Torch types can be used to summon the Torch God.
Torches placed during the event can fire off at the player too.
Torch fireballs do not harm critters, enemies, or players who have already consumed the Torch God's Favor.
After the Torch God ends, there is a 60-second cooldown before the event can start again for a player.
The Bestiary entry of the Torch God is unlocked once the Torch God's Favor is consumed.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

Starting the event in an open area offers the player more room to dodge.
Only proper Torches become part of the Torch God. Non-Torch light sources like lanterns can provide light to the area without becoming fireballs.
Items that give the player a dodge chance, such as the Brain of Confusion, work against torch fireballs.
Taken as an agility challenge, having mobility items like grappling hooks is preferred to help dodge the torch fireballs.
Taken as an endurance challenge, having armor, buffs, and accessories that offer high defense is preferred to reduce the damage from the torch fireballs.
The player can lessen enemy spawns using a Calming Potion and Peace Candle to reduce dangerous distractions from enemies, allowing the player to focus on dodging the fireballs.
Alternatively, the player can activate the event in a town for a greater spawn reduction. If the player fails, however, that town may become inaccessible until the player either completes the event or removes the Torches.
Some Torches make their associated fireballs harder to see, while other Torches make it easier to see. The best, brightest Torch for dodging purposes is the White Torch, but is made from Diamonds and thus may be resource-intensive. The second best Torch is the Ultrabright Torch, and it is uncommonly sold from the Traveling Merchant. The third best Torch is the Ichor Torch. Depending on the environment, the Ice Torch, Hallowed Torch, and Jungle Torch might be the fourth best.
The Torch God's Favor does not count as being in the inventory if it is in the trash slot, in a storage item like a Chest, or tossed to the ground. A player can use this to repeat the event.


=== Arena ideas ===

These are some brief ideas for creating a favorable environment to take the event in:

Create a large open area and line Torches around one edge to provide maximum dodging time.
Build a small, square arena with the Torches clustered in the center. Lay down Ropes and walkways to be able to circle the Torches.
Make a hellevator with a rope line and a Torch every 10 tiles, then place 101 Torches at the top and head down the rope line. By the time the player reaches the bottom, they should obtain Torch God's Favor.
Lay down a loop of Minecart Tracks around a cluster of 101 Torches. Hammer the rails so that the Minecart rides in circles around the Torches, and make use of bumpers and rail intersections as necessary.


== Trivia ==
The Torch God, as well as its reward, was most likely introduced as a response to the controversial "bad torch luck" feature introduced in 1.4.0.1, which would punish players for using the wrong Torch type in a given biome (e.g. using Ice Torches in the Underground Jungle as opposed to Jungle Torches).
The Torch God was initially discussed on live stream by Terraria streamer Pedguin on May 24th, 2020, as a way for Redigit to punish players for placing the wrong Torch. Redigit commented in the chat that he liked the idea.
The Torch God event is called HappyFunTorchTime in the game's source code.
When shot, each fireball emits the sound used by several casters and magic weapons.
 A Torch God NPC exists in-game, with an NPC ID of 664. It is classified as a boss and seems to be used for displaying the required info of the Torch God's Bestiary entry.
If it is summoned via third-party software or mods and is killed, it would only drop 5–15 Lesser Healing Potions and some Hearts. Doing so would also unlock the Torch God's Bestiary entry.
While the "boss" is alive, the music Boss 1 will play.
The Torch God is one of the few entities in the Bestiary that has a 5-star rarity, making it one of the only 4 bosses with a 5-star rarity.
 The Bestiary entry for the The Torch God: "An unseen deity responsible for a torch's eternal flicker, however easily angered by the unsightly, ungrateful abuse of torch placement."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Torch God's flames no longer hurt players other than the one who is going through its trial.
Desktop 1.4.5.0: Changed music track from Boss 3 to a new track exclusive to the event, Torch God.
Desktop 1.4.4: Now grants an achievement when complete.
Desktop 1.4.3.3: Fixed an issue where Torch God's projectiles from Corrupt Torches generated snow dust.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Added Bestiary entry.
Now properly plays an Otherworldly track when that setting is toggled.
Desktop 1.4.0.5: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.0.5.5: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.0.5.0: Introduced.
