title: Angler
content:
The Angler is a unique NPC concerned exclusively with fishing. He does not sell anything, but rather assigns quests to players. Quest objectives generally involve catching him rare fish from particular biomes or layers, for which he offers various rewards. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
He has been rescued as the Sleeping Angler, who can be encountered randomly in the Ocean biome on Sand Blocks or on the surface of the water. Interacting with him in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will wake him. If the Sleeping Angler is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Angler NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house.
The Angler will defend himself against nearby enemies by throwing Frost Daggerfish. He deals 10 / 15 / 17 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. 
The Sleeping Angler is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.


== Quest walkthrough ==
The day's quest is determined at 4:30 AM each day, regardless of whether or not the Angler has been spoken to.
Players can speak to the Angler and select his “Quest” option to learn which quest fish he wants for the day, and where it can be caught.
The location where this quest fish can be caught is stated directly underneath the Angler's quote.
Note that this step is not strictly required, and the quest fish can be caught without talking to the Angler, but the chance of choosing the right location is low.
The player will need a fishing pole, bait, and a sizeable amount of liquid (see Fishing) to catch the quest fish.
The fish will only be catchable while its quest is in effect (from 4:30 AM of that day until 4:30 AM of the next day, and before the player's daily catch has been turned in).
The quest fish can only be caught if it is not already in the player's inventory. It can be caught multiple times if it is placed in the player's trash slot, in a container, or on the ground.
Speaking to the Angler with the quest fish will remove one instance of it from the player's inventory and reward them with items.
For this, it does not matter whether the quest fish was caught before or after its respective quest was given.


== Quest list ==


== Quest rewards ==
After completing a quest, the Angler will reward the player with four types of rewards at most: main reward, decoration reward, coin reward, and bait reward. Chances for various items in the rewards will be affected by number of quests completed and the Angler's happiness, but not affected by luck.


=== Chance multiplier ===
The chance multiplier affects the chances for main reward, decoration reward, and bait reward, but has no effect on coin reward.
First, the base chance multiplier is calculated as follows:

Then, determine the final chance multiplier by happiness：
[math]\displaystyle{ \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} = \mathit{Base\ chance\ multiplier} \times 0.9 \times \frac{1 + \mathit{Price\ modifier\ (purchasing)}}{2} }[/math]

[math]\displaystyle{ \mathit{Price\ modifier\ (purchasing)} }[/math] is the price modifier when purchasing items, calculated with happiness.


=== Main rewards ===
Main rewards are guaranteed upon completing a quest. Fixed rewards are obtained when completing a certain amount of quests or giving certain type of quest fish; otherwise, a random reward will be obtained.
Rewards will be determined by the order in the following tables, fixed rewards first, then random rewards; the process ends when a reward is obtained. The "base chance" in the table means the base chance for obtaining items in the current row when drops in all previous rows failed; the actual chance for obtaining items in a certain row will be increased by the chance multiplier, increasing from the base chance of [math]\displaystyle{ \frac{1}{p} }[/math] to [math]\displaystyle{ \frac{1}{\lfloor p \times \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} \rfloor} }[/math]. This means the actual chances for random rewards near the bottom of the table will be lower than the chances listed.


==== Accessory rewards ====
When determining accessory drops, the game assumes each accessory has its own virtual base chance (three at 1/40 (2.5%) chance, three at 1/30 (3.33%) chance, and one at 1/25 (4%) chance) and calculates chance of dropping an accessory with the following formula:
[math]\displaystyle{ \mathit{Accessory\ chance} = \left( 1 - \left( 1 - \frac{1}{\lfloor 40 \times \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} \rfloor}\right)^3 \left( 1 - \frac{1}{\lfloor 30 \times \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} \rfloor}\right)^3 \left( 1 - \frac{1}{\lfloor 25 \times \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} \rfloor} \right) \right) \times 0.8 }[/math]
The accessory reward list initially contains all 7 accessories. The game will check the player's inventory, all portable storages, and accessories equipped in all loadouts (including the current loadout and social slots). If the player already own one of the accessories, that accessory will be removed from the list (if owning an upgrade for an accessory, all ingredients of the upgrade will be removed). The rewarded accessory will be a random accessory in the list, with equal chances. If all 7 accessories are removed, then the rewarded accessory will be a random accessory among the 7 accessories, also with equal chances.


=== Decoration rewards ===
Completing a quest has a [math]\displaystyle{ 1 - \frac{100 - \mathit{Quest\ completed}}{100} \times \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} }[/math] chance to obtain decoration reward, so it is guaranteed after completing the 100th quest.
There are a total of 19 decoration rewards, the player will be randomly rewarded one of them.


=== Coin rewards ===
Coin rewards are always granted when completing a quest, unaffected by chance multipliers. Coin rewards will increase with quests completed, ranging from 1 Silver to 10 Gold.
The base amount is calculated with the following formula:
[math]\displaystyle{ \mathit{Coin\ amount} = \Bigg\lfloor\bigg\lfloor\Big\lfloor\frac{\mathit{Quests\ completed}+50}{2}\Big\rfloor\times\mathit{R}\times0.0015\bigg\rfloor\times1.5\Bigg\rfloor }[/math]

[math]\displaystyle{ R }[/math] is a random integer between 50 and 200 (inclusive).
If the world is in Hardmode, coin amount ×2.
If the difficulty is Expert Mode or higher, coin amount also ×2.
Actual coins rewarded are calculated as follows:

If disregarding the rounding, each quest completed increases coin reward by 1 Silver 41 Copper on average. This increment becomes 2 Silver 81 Copper on average when in Hardmode or Expert Mode, or 5 Silver 63 Copper when both are fulfilled.


=== Bait rewards ===
Completing a quest has a  [math]\displaystyle{ \frac{51}{\lfloor 100 \times \mathit{Chance\ multiplier} \rfloor} }[/math] chance to obtain bait rewards. If rewarded, the possible amount of baits is 1–7.

The amount of Quest completed for guaranteeing bait reward depends on Angler's happiness, ranging from 34 quests (maximum happiness) to 58 quests (minimum happiness).
Base chances for Master Bait and Journeyman Bait are increased by the chance multiplier in the same way as random rewards in main rewards. The type of the bait is determined with the following order. This means the actual chance for Journeyman Bait is slightly lower than the listed value.

The base amount for baits is 1, with six independent rolls that each increases the amount of bait by 1 upon succeeding. Let the amount of quest completed be [math]\displaystyle{ q }[/math], the chances for each roll to succeed are:


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Angler will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
The Angler is one of the few town NPCs that can be obtained regardless of the current stage of game progression (the others being the Guide, Stylist, and Golfer).
The Sleeping Angler spawns randomly, like the other bound NPCs. It is not guaranteed that he will initially spawn on either shore. The player may need to wait a while at a shore before he appears.
The Sleeping Angler is able to float on both water and honey.
If a quest is not completed before the next day begins (4:30 AM the following day), a new quest begins, whether or not the Angler is spoken to.
It is possible to catch quest fish before the Angler has spawned in a world. However, most quest fish require fishing in a specific environment, making this an unlikely catch.
The Angler will never assign quests that require the player to catch fish from the Crimson in a Corruption world, or from the Corruption in a Crimson world.
No quest fish will be caught if the day's quest catch already exists in the player's inventory. It is possible to catch more than one quest fish in a day if the player drops previously-caught quest fish on the ground, or stores them in a Chest or other storage item. For this case, a fish in the player's "trash slot" does not count, so putting the first one there allows picking up a second quest fish. Holding the item in the air with a cursor does not count as holding. Quest fish are stackable, meaning if the player keeps adding the newest quest fish caught to a stack in the trash slot, there is no maximum number of quest fish in a player's inventory.
If the Angler is killed after being saved, and there is no suitable house for him to live in, he will settle in as soon as one becomes free, like any other NPC.
The number of completed quests is tied to the character, rather than the world. The minimum number required for a particular reward can be accrued by completing quests in multiple worlds. The number of completed quests for the purposes of achievements is instead a running total for all characters in all worlds, so multiple characters can contribute to earning achievements.
The current fishing quest for a world's in-game day is tied to the name of the characters. It is, for example, impossible to have two characters with the same name claim rewards in the same world.
The Angler provides all three components of the Fish Finder, which is one of the sub-assemblies of the Cell Phone. Three more of his gifts can be combined into the Angler Tackle Bag, which is required to craft the Lavaproof Tackle Bag.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
In multiplayer, advancing the day forward to dawn using console commands does not reset the quest cooldown; the player still needs to wait another 24 minutes (24 in-game hours) for a new quest. However, advancing the day to midnight and waiting 4.5 minutes until dawn does work.
If the game does not save after the player turns in the daily quest, the game can be closed without saving to turn in the quest again with different rewards. This can be done multiple times to attain desired rewards without having to wait 24 minutes for a new quest.
A Love Potion can be used to increase the Angler's happiness, boosting the chance of special rewards.
Building mini-biomes is useful for quick access for fishing biome-specific fish, as some biomes such as the Jungle, Corruption, or Crimson may be more time-consuming and/or dangerous to travel to.
When attempting to get new accessories from fishing (e.g. to gain the ingredients for the Fish Finder), the player should hold accessories they already have gained from quest fishing in their inventory, to avoid receiving duplicates. Alternatively, players can use the Shimmer to cycle between the three accessories. However, if all of them have been obtained already, then only two of them should be held in the inventory in order to minimize the chances of receiving another. Completing quests in pre-Hardmode also increases the chances of getting one of them.
Doing the achievements can be more easily done on Journey Mode by skipping the day cycle using the Time menu and using the Duplication menu for the quest fish.
Catching multiple quest fish of the same type and keeping those in storage saves a lot of time if the same fish is required in future quests. Note that the player has to move the quest fish out of their inventory before being able to catch the same fish again.


== Names ==
The Angler may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
The Angler is a child, similar to the Princess. He has a shorter sprite compared to most other NPCs' sprites.
The Angler is not allowed to try Ale from the Tavernkeep as seen in the quote “How come <name of Tavernkeep> won't sell me any ale? I want to try some! What a grouch!”. This refers to the fact that the Angler is presumably below the legal drinking age.
This is also confirmed by several of his quotes:
“Let a kid give you some advice, never touch your tongue to an ice block! Wait, forget what I said, I totally want to see you do it!”
“What, you think I like parties because I am a kid? Well, you're right, so get to partying!”
“I'm a kid, you need to give me a house! Are you dumb!?”
While most NPCs die via the usual death animation, the Angler simply vanishes in a puff of smoke. He also has a unique death message: Instead of “<Name of Angler> was slain...” the message reads “<Name of Angler> has left!”. This is likely due to rating concerns, as depictions of children being killed tend to result in an "Adults Only" rating from the ESRB, which might have limited the game's distribution.
He seems to be an orphan, judging by his quote “I don't have a mommy or a daddy, but I have a lot of fish! It's close enough!”.
The Angler is allergic to bees, as shown by his dialogue about the Bumblebee Tuna.
The Angler often seems to disregard the player's safety, as shown by his quotes, for instance “Hey! Just the sacrifi- I mean competent fishing master that I've been looking for! ”
Despite his professed love of fishing, he is never himself seen fishing, and the only fish he provides to the player are mounted as trophies.
The Pirate is seen holding one of his quest fish in the credits, but this might have been provided by the player.

The quote “<Name of Angler> wants YOU as the official <name of world> errand monkey!” is a reference to the famous World War I U.S. propaganda poster featuring Uncle Sam with the caption saying "I want you for U.S. Army".

The Angler makes several references in his quotes about certain quest fish:
Batfish: The 1960s American live action television series Batman starring the eponymous fictional superhero. Besides its theme song, the show was known for prefixing all the hero's equipment with the word bat.
Bumblebee Tuna: The real-life brand Bumble Bee Foods, LLC, a company that produces canned tuna, salmon, other seafoods, and chicken under the brand name "Bumble Bee", among others. Bumble Bee Tuna is one of their products.
Clownfish: The 2003 American computer-animated adventure film Finding Nemo.
Pengfish: The fictional superhero Superman.
The Angler always mentions the Demolitionist in the Dynamite Fish quote, even if he has not moved in.
The quests for the Dynamite Fish and the Pengfish are the only two quests whose quote does not end with exclamation marks.
The Angler incorrectly refers to The Hungry as "the Hunger" when talking about the Hungerfish.
Like all other quest fish, the Jewelfish is worth nothing when sold, despite the Angler's quest dialogue claiming that it will make him rich.
It is possible to give the Angler a Bunnyfish and receive a Bunnyfish Trophy as a reward, suggesting he immediately gave it back.
The Angler's quote referencing the act of touching one's tongue to an ice block references the fact that very cold objects, such as ice blocks, cause the saliva in the tongue to freeze inside the pores of the tongue, causing the tongue to become stuck to the ice.
Despite his dislike of the Desert for its apparent lack of fish, several fish can be caught in the Desert, including two quest fish.
The Angler's Shimmered form is a kappa, a turtle-like creature from Japanese folklore. Its Japanese name "河童" translates to river-child which makes sense with the Angler being a child and fisherman.
In response to a question on Discord, Redigit jokingly claimed that the Angler's parents are dead, sparking the theory of The Groom and The Bride being the Angler's parents. Likewise jokingly, Redigit commented, "This is now canon."
 The Bestiary entry for the Angler: "The Angler, a rude fishing genius, sends others to find weird, rare fish. He rewards random items, entertained by any misfortunes."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.6: The chat window now only shows a notification near the quest button when a quest is available.
Desktop 1.4.4.6: 
The Angler's Accessory Drop Duplicate Protection has been adjusted to make it more flexible and player friendly.
Instead of only selectively applying duplicate protection to the 2 triple sets of accessories independently, he now applies the duplicate protection to all 7 accessories, including the Fishing Bobber.
If the player has any of the 7 accessories (either in their individual form or their tinkered forms) in their inventory, the Angler will always give a non-duplicate accessory whenever he rolls to drop an accessory at all. He will only begin dropping duplicates again once the player has all 7 in their inventory.
This will also result in a general increase in the number of accessories he drops.
The Mermaid and Fish Costumes have been moved to be before Accessories in priority order since Accessories will be more common.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Angler Quests now give 2x as much coins in Hardmode.
Angler no longer drops furniture items as part of his regular drop pool. Instead, he now has a chance to give a bonus furniture drop when completing quests. The odds of getting a bonus furniture drop increase as completed Quests count increases.
Bottomless Water Bucket is now guaranteed on the 25th quest completed.
Bottomless Water Bucket can now be obtained in pre-Hardmode.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Removed "Bryce" as a possible name.
Angler's Quest rewards are now more likely to give informational accessories.
Additionally, he will not give the player duplicates of an accessory they have in their inventory, unless they already have them all.
Added 2 new quotes, informing the player of the number of quests they have completed.
Fixed some inconsistent or inaccurate Fishing Quest dialogue text.
Desktop 1.3.4.2: Now correctly shows up on the Lifeform Analyzer.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Sprite updated.
Angler's quests now always give gold coins.
Added Fisherman's Pocket Guide, Weather Radio, Sextant and Golden Bug Net.
Quests now tell where to find the quest fish.
Golden Fishing Rod only requires 30 completed quests now (instead of 50).
Several drop chances changed.
Desktop 1.2.4.1: 
Fixed bug where "Wyverntail" was named "Whyverntail".
Angler's quests now show when using other languages.
Fixed bug where Sleeping Angler would move slowly on tiles if attacked by enemies.
Desktop 1.2.4: Introduced.

Console 1.07: Introduced fishing on Console editions, including the Angler NPC, fishing quests, and their rewards.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile 1.2.11212: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Rod of Discord
content:
The Rod of Discord is a Hardmode tool that has a 1/500 (0.2%) / 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by Chaos Elementals. When used, it instantly teleports the player to the location of the cursor and inflicts the Chaos State debuff on the player for 6 seconds. Using the Rod of Discord while this debuff is active causes the player to lose health equal to 1/7 (14.29%) of their maximum health.
It can be upgraded into the Rod of Harmony by throwing it into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated.


== Crafting ==


=== Shimmer transmutation ===


== Achievements ==


== Notes ==
In worlds with the Celebration Mk 10 seed, the drop rate of the Rod of Discord is increased to 1/100 (1%) regardless of world difficulty.
The Rod of Discord cannot be used to teleport into the Jungle Temple prior to defeating Plantera.
More precisely, the player will not be teleported pre-Plantera to any location that is below the surface and has an unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Wall as background wall. In worlds with the Remix seed enabled, this restriction extends above the surface.
The health loss inflicted by Chaos State cannot be reduced in any way or negated through dodge effects. It also bypasses and does not trigger invincibility frames. It does not bypass invincibility from Godmode, however.
The Rod of Discord's teleport range is limited to 60 tiles horizontally and 37.5 tiles vertically from the player's center.
The target location must be at least 3 tiles high and 2 tiles wide. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button will always place the player's feet at the cursor position. Thus, in order to teleport into a 3-tile-high opening, the player must aim at the floor. Unsuccessful teleports play the same sound, but do not inflict the debuff.
While riding a mount, the target location must usually be higher, depending on the mount's height. For instance, while riding the Unicorn Mount, the location must be 5 tiles high.
Teleporting resets fall damage to begin at the height at which the player teleported to.
Using the Rod of Discord when moving maintains the player's momentum.
Using it does not cancel Shroomite armor's stealth.
If the player only taps the ⚒ Use / Attack button with the Rod of Discord on the  Mobile version, they will be teleported slightly to the right (and above if blocks or furniture are obstructing the path). Using the thumbpad can yield mixed results if the aim mode is set to "Aim & Use" rather than "Aim Only".
The Rod of Discord cannot be used to teleport past Unbreakable Walls (generated naturally in Dual Dungeons worlds).


== Tips ==
The Rod of Discord is arguably the most powerful movement tool in the game; besides being an obvious boon to traversing terrain, it allows the player to dodge high-damage or difficult to avoid attacks, including the Moon Lord's Phantasmal Deathray, contact damage from the Dungeon Guardian, and several of the Empress of Light's attacks. It is also very useful in helping to catch Truffle Worms.
While it is one of the rarest items in the game, it can be obtained immediately after the start of Hardmode.
Since this item is one of the few ways to deal self-damage on command, it can be used with the Shrimpy Truffle or the Panic Necklace to activate the speed boost. Furthermore, it allows easy obtainment of The Frequent Flyer achievement.


== Trivia ==
Dying from teleporting during the Chaos State will display unique death messages:
"<Player name> didn't materialize"
"<Player name>'s legs appeared where their head should be."
In earlier mobile versions, using the Rod of Discord would instantly kill its user, and the death message would read "Structures".
Despite not being a weapon, the Rod of Discord can be placed on a Weapon Rack.
The Rod of Discord emits pink light when dropped. It is also fully bright in the dark when used or placed inside a Weapon Rack, an Item Frame, or an Item Flask.
Successfully using the Rod of Discord leaves behind pink glowing particles at the location of the player, as well as produces those particles at the teleport location. It also coats the player with glowing particles which gradually lose their glow as they disappear.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: 
Sprite updated. Old sprite was 
Now used to craft the Rod of Harmony via Shimmer.
Desktop 1.4.1: Teleport range is now limited to 960 pixels (60 tiles) horizontally and 600 pixels (37.5 tiles) vertically from the player's center.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: 
Now has an increased drop rate of 1/400 (0.25%) in Expert Mode.
Now leaves a trail when teleporting.
Desktop 1.3.0.4: Teleporting now quickly shifts the viewpoint instead of instantly setting it to the destination point.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Chaos State damage reduced from one sixth to one seventh of user's total health, and duration decreased from 8 to 6 seconds.
Desktop 1.2.4.1: Can now be placed in the Weapon Rack.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Chaos State damage reduced from one fifth to one sixth of user's total health, and duration decreased from 10 to 8 seconds.
Now works properly in reverse gravity.
Using a Rod of Discord releases all hooks.
Desktop 1.2.1.2: 
Inflicts Chaos State upon use to deter teleport spamming.
Can no longer be used to enter a Jungle Temple (unless the Lihzahrd Walls at target location are removed).
Using Rod of Discord near the edge of world will no longer cause the game to crash.
Desktop 1.2.0.3: The Rod of Discord now properly drops.
Desktop 1.2: Introduced.

Console 1.02: Introduced.

Switch 1.0.711.6: Introduced.

Mobile 1.2.6508: Introduced.

3DS-Release: Introduced.

title: Golfer
content:
The Golfer is an NPC vendor who sells golfing-related items. More items will be unlocked as the player's golf score increases, including clubs, trophies, and paintings. He will move in once the following criteria are met:

There is an available vacant house.
Rescuing him as the Golfer Rescue, who can be rarely encountered in the Underground Desert. Interacting with him in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free him. If the stationary Golfer is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Golfer NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.
The Golfer will attack nearby enemies with his golf balls to defend himself.
He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.


== Items sold ==


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Golfer will transform into his Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. He can be returned to his classic look by submerging him in Shimmer again or spraying him with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
In multiplayer, the Golfer's shop unlocks are per player, so everyone must golf in order to purchase his full inventory.
Like all Underground Desert entities, the Golfer Rescue only requires any unsafe variant of Sandstone Wall or Hardened Sand Wall to spawn, instead of an actual Underground Desert biome (see Underground Desert § Spawning mechanics for details).


== Tips ==
Finding the Golfer in the Underground Desert can prove somewhat difficult if there is no proper cave system, even with the Lifeform Analyzer. A Hunter Potion can help to locate him.
Due to the much more dangerous enemies spawning in the Underground Desert in Hardmode, it is safer to find the Golfer in pre-Hardmode. This is also one of the few ways to easily get an Ocean Pylon early, as he loves the Angler.
The Golfer can be a lot harder to rescue in Expert and Master Mode, so his position should be reached as fast as possible if the hurt sound is heard or the damage indicator is seen.
It is possible for the Golfer to spawn in a world generated pre-1.3.0.1 by manually creating an Underground Desert. All it needs is to build a few blocks where enemies can spawn, then place 50 tiles high Treacherous Sandstone Walls upwards, starting at behind the spawning blocks.
This can also be achieved with regular Sandstone Walls by converting them into their Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow variants (e.g. use the Clentaminator; converting them back to pure walls is not necessary). This causes the background walls to turn into "naturally generated" walls, which allow biome-specific enemies to spawn, including the Golfer.
A golf score of 2000 can be reached quickly by putting into a hellevator with a Golf Cup at the bottom and Cobweb at the top.


== Names ==
The Golfer may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


=== Golf score quotes ===


== Trivia ==
Several names of the Golfer are references to fictional and real-world professional golfers:
Lion Pines – Tiger Woods
Arnie Palmfrond – Arnold Palmer
Jake Nicklelisp – Jack Nicklaus
Gunner McLovin – Shooter McGavin
Billy Bones – Bobby Jones
The name Harry Madison and Gunner McLovin (Replacement for Shooter McGavin) is a reference to Happy Madison Productions, an American film company which takes its name from the comedy films Happy Gilmore from 1996, and Billy Madison from 1995.
The name Jim Mulligan is a reference to the mulligan, a stroke that is replayed from the spot of the previous stroke without a penalty.
The surname McLovin as a replacement for McGavin may be a reference to the 2007 teen comedy movie Superbad.
The Golfer's quote “Huh? You eat WHAT for breakfast?” is a reference to the 1996 American sports comedy movie Happy Gilmore.
His quote “Don't go chasing water hazards, please stick to the fairways and greens that you're used to.” is a reference to the song “Waterfalls” by TLC.
The quote “I'm not the type to scream and thrash around just because my ball lands in the water. I stay calm, and collected, and focus on the next shot.” could be a reference to the fact that many golfers have suffered a brief bout of anger due to a misplaced shot.
Though the Golfer's quotes suggest that golf balls are influenced by wind speed, this is not the case in Terraria.
The Golfer is loosely inspired by the real-world professional golfer Tiger Woods and was introduced because there was a need for an NPC who sells golf-related items.
The fact that he is found in the Underground Desert is likely a reference to a bunker or "sand trap", a common golf course hazard that also bears resemblance to sand pits made by antlions.
The Golfer was first shown off in the Town Night spoiler video released by Re-Logic on YouTube on October 1, 2018.
Once the player has a golf score of 2000 or higher, he will sell a total of 39 items at a time. If he is happy enough, he will also sell a pylon, rounding up his stock to 40 items. He is tied with the Tavernkeep for the most items sold by any NPC.
However, the NPC with the most items sold at any time, without certain pre-conditions, is Santa Claus at 39 items.
Any items sold to the Golfer cannot be bought back once his shop has 39 items or more.
According to Redigit, the Golfer is the Zoologist's older brother, referenced by some of his quotes.
As stated when he is spoken to in a Graveyard, the Golfer's friends and family (aside from the Zoologist) are deceased.
The Golfer's Shimmered form transforms him into an anthropomorphic dog. This is also a reference to the Zoologist, who is a werefox.
Unlike the Zoologist, the Shimmered Golfer continues to talk normally and is in his dog form regardless of the current time or moon phase. This makes it unclear if the Golfer is a lycanthrope in his Shimmered form.
Even though kinship between him and the Zoologist may be seen as the origin of this phenomenon, it is explained in his sister's Bestiary entry that her condition was caused by a cursed bite. Thus, each of the siblings were cursed separately, that is if the Shimmered Golfer is cursed.
 The Bestiary entry for the Golfer: "The Golfer is a wise, middle-aged man who sells all sorts of golfing equipment. He's got game and knows how to score."

title: Seaweed
content:
Seaweed is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Turtle to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Turtle will fly with a propeller to catch up to the player. Seaweed has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being found in Ivy Chests, located in the Underground Jungle's Jungle Shrines or Living Mahogany Trees. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it also has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from Jungle Crates and Bramble Crates.


== Trivia ==
On the  Mobile version and Nintendo 3DS version, there used to be a coding error where the Seaweed obtained from fishing would have the description of the pet-summoning Seaweed.
The pet turtle is a reference to Tank, a pet tortoise from the animated television series My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic.
The Seaweed junk and the Seaweed pet-summoning item is one of the three pairs of items that share the same name. The other pairs of items are: the Princess Dress from Goodie Bags and the Princess Dress from the Clothier; Corrupt and Crimson Deathweed Planter Boxes.

title: Party Girl
content:
The Party Girl is an NPC vendor who sells festive novelty items and furniture.
Unlike other town NPCs, the Party Girl only has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be eligible for spawning every 2-minute interval, during which she is subject to regular NPC spawn rate, once the criteria below are met. In other words, she will take on average 40 times longer to spawn than regular NPCs. Along with this percentage chance, she will move in once the following criteria are met:

There is an available vacant house.
20 other town NPCs are in the world. Note that while the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
If the Party Girl is killed, she will respawn with normal spawn chances instead of being rarer.
The Party Girl will defend herself against nearby enemies by throwing Happy Grenades. She deals 30 / 45 / 52 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Party Girl also has a 1/4 (25%) chance of dropping 30–60 Happy Grenades upon death.
During a natural Party, she will give a Slice of Cake to the first player that talks to her.


== Items sold ==


== Music toggle ==
Entering a Drunk world for the first time permanently unlocks a “Music” option in the Party Girl's dialogue window, allowing the player to toggle the game's default soundtrack for the Terraria: Otherworld soundtrack. Once unlocked, the option to toggle the music will be permanently available across all players and all worlds.
Every song in Terraria's soundtrack is replaced. Songs that do not have a Terraria: Otherworld equivalent will use the most relevant song; for example, the Underground Jungle will simply use Terraria: Otherworld's Jungle theme, rather than Terraria's Underground Jungle theme.
Every new song has its own unique Music Box, all of which are called "Otherworldly Music Boxes".
In a multiplayer world, players only hear the altered soundtrack if they have used the “Music” option themselves, which is only present if they have unlocked it before by visiting a Drunk world. However, all players can listen to Otherworldly Music Boxes in multiplayer worlds, regardless of whether they have toggled or unlocked the option before.
Upon leaving the world, the soundtrack will revert to the default.


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Party Girl will transform into her Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. She can be returned to her classic look by submerging her in Shimmer again or spraying her with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Notes ==
The Party Girl will replace the Guide as the starting NPC in Drunk worlds. Furthermore, she is one of the starting NPCs in Celebration Mk 10 world and is initially named “Amanda”.


== Tips ==
Though the Party Girl is mostly seen as a source of novelty and decorative items, a few of her items are fairly useful:
The Bubbles that she sells have a variety of practical uses, such as holding honey and water in midair to provide health regeneration and activate the Cute Fishron's speed boost, respectively.
Pigronatas drop Party Bullets, which have better stats than Silver Bullets.
The Slice of Cake she offers to players provides a buff that is useful for building.


== Names ==
The Party Girl may have any of the following names:


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
The Party Girl and the Princess are the only female NPCs who do not appear annoyed or rude during a Blood Moon. The Party Girl is the only female NPC to not make any comment about the Blood Moon at all.
Redigit and Cenx have stated that the Party Girl was inspired by the character Pinkie Pie from the Canadian-American children's animated fantasy television series My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic.
The names Sparkle and Trixy are likely references to the characters Princess Twilight Sparkle and Trixie from the same series.
The Party Girl's Shimmered form resembles Rainbow Dash from the same series.
The Party Girl was sprited by former Terraria spriter Sarah "Waffles" Data.
The name Bambi may be a reference to the 1942 American animated drama film Bambi and its eponymous character.
The Party Girl is depicted in the painting Unicorn Crossing the Hallows.
It is possible for the Party Girl and the Dryad to both be named Isis.
The Party Girl may occasionally throw confetti at the player regardless of whether there is an active Party.
The quote “There was a sudden crash of thunder at the disco, and I panicked!” is a reference to the American pop rock band Panic! at the Disco.
The quote “We have to talk. It's... it's about parties.” is a reference to the Nedroid.com comic "Party Cat" by Anthony Clark.
The quote “Oh, are you all wet? Well, shake it off!” is a reference to the song “Shake It Off” by American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift.
The Party Girl states that she hates the Tax Collector because he apparently shuts down her after-parties. However, it is stated by the Tax Collector that he actually likes the Party Girl.
 The Bestiary entry for the Party Girl: "Positive beyond comprehension, the Party Girl will use any excuse to celebrate. She sells party favors and flashy things."

title: Scaly Truffle
content:
The Scaly Truffle is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a Pigron Mount that allows the player to fly for a limited time and run faster on land. The Scaly Truffle is obtained by fishing in the cavern layer of an Ice biome overlapping a Hallow, Corruption, or Crimson biome in Hardmode.


== Notes ==
The Pigron Mount's maximum flight time is 2.67 seconds, comparable to the Bee/Butterfly/Flame Wings.
The top running speed of a Pigron Mount is 46 mph, reached after approximately 5.8 seconds.
It cancels fall damage.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==

Although the Pigron enemy has multiple variants, the Pigron Mount can only have the appearance of a slightly more red Hallow Pigron.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Pigron Mount can be dyed in the mount equipment slot to fit a player's preference. The biome-specific colors can be recreated with Purple Dye for the Corruption Pigron, and Red Dye for the Crimson Pigron.
The Pigron Mount will yawn after standing still for 15–25 seconds.Verify
Its buff tooltip, "Now you see me..." is referencing how Pigron enemies can turn nearly invisible. It is a slight twist on first half of the phrase "Now you see it... Now you don't!" popularized by stage magicians performing disappearing acts.
Scaly Truffle is likely a reference to truffle hogs (a kind of domesticated pig), which are used to locate truffles. "Scaly" refers to semi-regular protrusions (scales) from the fruiting body of a fungus, like those found on the caps of portobello mushrooms.

title: Neptune's Shell
content:
Neptune's Shell is a Hardmode accessory that aids maneuverability in water, honey, and Shimmer by granting indefinite breathing time while submerged, swimming via the ↷ Jump key, and eliminating the slow movement speed usually caused by submerging underwater. Entering applicable liquids with this accessory equipped transforms the player into a merperson and grants the Merfolk buff. While in this form, the breath meter will refill as if the player is in open air, therefore effectively preventing drowning.
Neptune's Shell has a 1/50 (2%) / 99/2500 (3.96%) chance of being dropped by Creatures from the Deep.
Neptune's Shell can be considered an upgrade from the Diving Gear in most respects, but it lacks the extra mobility on Ice Blocks from the Arctic Diving Gear and the extra lighting underwater of the Jellyfish Necklace.


== Crafting ==


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
Swimming functions similarly to that of a Flipper or Flipper Potion, and its speed nears that of flying through the air with wings.
Swimming in honey activates all the perks of the Merfolk form but does not allow the player to move at full speed.
Landing in and "jumping" from water alone (by swimming up past the surface), without touching land, does not reset flight time for wings or variants of Rocket Boots.
The Merfolk form is affected by dyes, these are applied via the player's armor slots rather than the one attributed to the accessory slot that the shell is equipped in.
The Merfolk effect takes priority over the benefits of the Moon Charm and its upgrades, causing the player to lose the Werewolf's bonuses while in water.
Neptune's Shell can also be equipped as a vanity accessory, which causes the Merfolk form to appear regardless of whether the player is in water. This is merely the appearance of the Merfolk, the buff will not take effect while it is equipped as a vanity (caution should be taken when in water, as the player will need to watch their breath meter).
Wearing a Fish Bowl or having the Gills buff in For the Worthy will activate the Merfolk appearance and infinite breathing time, but not the Merfolk buff.
Neptune's Shell does not stack with its upgrades.


== Tips ==
An easier/faster way to get Neptune's Shell is by placing a Water Candle and/or consuming the Battle Potion because the Solar Eclipse does not have a set spawn rate.


== Trivia ==
The name of the item refers to Neptune, the Roman god of the sea.
The player in Merfolk form resembles the Zombie Merman and Icy Merman enemies.

title: Lighting mode
content:
The lighting mode determines the way light from all sources renders in the world. The lighting mode can be changed from the settings menu. On the  Desktop version, it can also be cycled by pressing ⇧ Shift+F9 while in-game.
The lighting mode also dictates whether the game will use certain performance-intensive visual effects, like the smoothing of liquid flow,  along with the following shader effects:

The reddish lighting and vignette applied during a Blood Moon
The distortion effect around Celestial Towers
The heat distortion effect in the Desert and The Underworld
The amplified background dust effect seen during Sandstorms
The sepia filter applied in a The Constant world or while the Radio Thing is equipped
The effects above will only be applied in the Color or White lighting modes, and are deactivated in the Retro and Trippy modes. On the  Console version and  Mobile version, these effects are controlled by a separate setting and are unaffected by the lighting mode.
The chosen lighting mode will have an effect on the performance of some devices. Refer to the table below for each mode's performance impact.


== Modes ==


== Notes ==
Light-producing animations become more active in the Retro and Trippy modes. Torches and other spark-releasing light sources produce sparks more actively. The same is true for the sparkle effect from Gold Chests and other sparkling items, as well as the bubbles released by Lava. This is most likely due to the difference in load.
Because of the way Retro and Trippy modes spread the light, they technically make light sources more effective. This can be taken advantage of when any vision-reducing debuff is active, or if the player is inside Dungeon or Jungle Temple in For the Worthy or Zenith worlds.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.4: Fixed lighting related crash with non-Color modes.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Fixed an issue where blocks would not be visible at all in extremely dark locations in the Underworld with Trippy/Retro lighting.
Desktop 1.3.5: Improved Retro lighting consistency.
Desktop 1.3.0.5: Fixed a rare lighting crash.
Desktop 1.3.0.2: Fixed an issue with black squares appearing on backgrounds when using Retro lighting.
Desktop 1.2.3: 
Optimized lighting code for better performance.
Lighting no longer loads on servers, saving memory.
Fixed a bug where the Platinum Candle did not emit light in a non-Color lighting mode.
Desktop 1.1.1: 
Lighting update will no longer skip as much on lower quality levels.
Fixed the shadow glitch of trippy lighting.
Lighting will now be set to Retro instead of crashing if Terraria is unable to switch to the new lighting mode.
Desktop 1.1: New lighting engine that allows smooth sub-tile light transitions instead of per-tile, and colored light instead of all-white light. Lighting options added.

title: Goat Skull
content:
The Goat Skull is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Goat Mount that grants mounted players an extra jump and can charge through and damage enemies. The Goat Skull has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh in Master Mode.
Once a high enough speed is reached, the Goat Mount leaves a trail of fire on solid blocks behind itself, similar to Flame Waker Boots, and from that point on, it will be able to damage enemies on contact. The invulnerability is granted for 1/10th of a second when the player and the Goat Mount dash through an enemy, much like the brief invulnerability after taking damage.


== Notes ==
The Goat Mount cannot swim. It does not prevent damage from lava.
If the player has Water Walking Boots, Obsidian Water Walking Boots, or Lava Waders equipped, then the Goat Mount will also walk on water.
The top running speed of the Goat Mount is 61 mph, reachable in 3.56 seconds. At top speed, it is nearly twice as fast as a player wearing Lightning Boots and is equivalent to the Wisp in a Bottle's top speed. However, the Goat Mount can reach up to 80 mph when falling down after having reached max speed.
When surpassing 51 mph, the Goat Mount will start dealing damage to enemies and critters it runs into, similarly to the Unicorn Mount and the horse mounts(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). It will deal 60 base summon damage and inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong).
The Goat Mount does not benefit from the effect of Asphalt Blocks, making players with Lightning Boots travel slightly faster on these blocks (64 mph with boots and 61 mph on a Goat Mount). The Goat Mount also does not benefit from Swiftness Potions.
While riding the Goat Mount, the player will be damaged by one-block-deep lava, but not given benefits or slowed down by one-block-deep honey.
While the player is mounted on the Goat Mount, they will only take 20% fall damage, though they will not take fall damage if they have any accessories that negate fall damage equipped, such as the Lucky Horseshoe or a set of wings, regardless of the height the player fell while on the Goat Mount.
The Goat Mount makes the player five tiles in height, unlike most other mounts, which only raise the height to four tiles.
All items providing an extra jump, like the Cloud in a Bottle, will stack with the mount, allowing a triple jump. If a Bundle of Balloons is equipped, it is possible to jump 5 times before hitting the ground.
Further adding the Fart in a Jar or upgrades and Tsunami in a Bottle or upgrades allows the player to jump 7 times before hitting the ground.
When using the double jump, the player has a green and yellow sparkling effect in the mount's trail. The color of the particles created by double jumping, as well as charging, are affected by dyes.
If the Goat Skull is used during the dash of the Shield of Cthulhu, both the damage from the dash of the Shield and the Goat Mount's charge will be dealt to the enemy.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The Goat, Unicorn, and Basilisk Mounts' charge abilities operate the same way sprinting accessories do in terms of momentum. This means that mounting while sprinting, dashing with the Shield of Cthulhu or Tabi, or moving quickly through the use of a canceled grapple will immediately cause the Goat Mount to begin charging, even if the distance covered would normally not be enough to trigger it.


== Trivia ==
Using any auto-firing weapon such as the Terra Blade, yoyos, or a Minishark, and firing it in the opposite direction the player is walking in will cause the Goat Mount to walk "backwards".
On flat ground, the Goat Mount travels at the same speed as an unmodified Terra Blade beam.
The Goat Mount is functionally identical to the Unicorn Mount, but mounting and dismounting will not provide any light.
This item is a reference to the Icon of Sin, the final boss of the first-person shooter Doom II. The boss takes the form of a large bio-mechanical goat head on a wall, similar to the Wall of Flesh itself.
The buff tooltip "This ride is totally metal!" refers to the soundtrack of the numerous games of the Doom franchise, which are made up of metal music.

title: Guide:Lunatic Cultist strategies
content:
The Lunatic Cultist is a post-Golem boss. Defeating him will summon the Celestial Towers, leading to spawning the final boss, the Moon Lord. While his small health bar means he'll be taken out quite quickly, his attacks can be damaging and hard to dodge.


== Summoning ==
He spawns after the 4 other Cultists are slain. The Lunatic Cultist will be invincible when he first spawns. After he moves away from his spawn point, you can begin to deal damage to him. You can use this lengthy summon animation to get into position in an arena you've built near the Dungeon.


== Attack Pattern ==
After moving away from his spawn point, the Lunatic Cultist will begin to cycle through three attacks:

A rotating ball of ice that fires six shards at equal intervals before disappearing
Three homing fireballs that explode on impact
A stationary orb similar to the Magnet Sphere that summons streaks of lightning in a straight line.
Once the Lunatic Cultist is damaged enough, he adds a fourth attack, which summons in two spreads of five destroyable Ancient Light projectiles.
After performing 4 to 5 of his attacks, the Cultist will spawn in duplicates of himself that remain stationary. If one of these duplicates is damaged (or after a certain amount of time without damaging any one of them), a Phantasm Dragon will spawn, or an Ancient Vision if a Phantasm Dragon is already present. Two duplicates will also start attacking besides him, occasionally shooting a projectile. If the real Lunatic Cultist is damaged, neither of these two powerful minions will spawn in. The amount of duplicates the Lunatic Cultist spawns in increases, the more clones you hit. It is recommended to fight the Cultist at night, as the fake cultists will glow. Also, the fake cultists have completely black eyes while the real one has a white dot in the corner.


=== Expert mode/Master mode ===
In Expert Mode, when the health of the boss is below 50%, the Cultist may also spawn Ancient Dooms that fire purple projectiles in a cross shape. These projectiles are far more damaging than the other attacks and may be difficult to see at night. They become more common the lower the boss's health is.


== General Strategies ==


=== General tips ===


=== Terrain Preparation ===
A basic arena with some rows of platforms will suffice. If the player made an arena for Skeletron, they can reuse it here.


=== Gearing up ===
While the Cultist himself doesn't require as much preparation as Plantera or Duke Fishron, killing him will start the Celestial Event and eventually the Moon Lord, so it is better to fight with the best gear available.


==== Armor ====
For Melee characters, the Beetle armor is the best available. The Beetle Scale Mail is better for offensive bonuses, while the Beetle Shell is better for those that can't avoid taking hits frequently. The best mixed set consists of Hallowed Mask, Valhalla Knight's Breastplate for valuable life regeneration / Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso for a significant melee speed boost / Monk's Shirt for the highest raw damage, and Valhalla Knight's Greaves.
For Ranged characters, the Shroomite armor is the strongest available. Due to shroomite armor's set bonus being hard to utilize in singleplayer, you can use Adamantite Mask or Hallowed Helmet which boost all weapon types and provide the highest damage for rocket type weapons; Red Riding Dress is optimal when using minions; and Red Riding Leggings provide higher stats than shroomite leggings, especially when using minions.
The Spectre armor is the strongest for a Mage. The Spectre Hood should be used only when at low health to maximize damage output. The mixed set consisting of Spectre Mask, Dark Artist's Robes and Dark Artist's Leggings provides higher damage than the full spectre set (especially when using minions), at the cost of not being able to easily switch to the Spectre Hood to quickly heal up.
The Spooky armor provides the highest damage for summoners, Tiki armor provides a bit more defense and a significant whip range bonus, which is especially important when using low range whips like Firecracker. Valhalla Knight armor is a sentry focused set which grants excellent survivability.


==== Weapons ====
For Melee users:

The Flairon is a very strong choice with its homing, high damaging projectiles.
The Terra Blade, Flying Dragon and the Influx Waver are the strongest projectile swords available, with the Influx Waver being particularly powerful against single targets. Note that the large projectiles of Terra Blade may hit the duplicates accidentally, so it should be used with caution during the rituals.
The Starlight is even higher in DPS, and the nature of his attack patterns means that dodging can be easier if you are closer, making this an excellent option for facetanking.
The Kraken is the best yoyo at this stage, which deals high damage and will help with taking out the Lunatic Cultist and the Phantasm Dragon he summons. In addition, it is incredibly useful for hitting only the real cultist during the ritual, since it follows the cursor very accurately. The Eye of Cthulhu is a weaker alternative.
The Vampire Knives should be used due to their healing effect. But due to the low damage output, a different weapon should be used when not at low health.
The Paladin's Hammer has high damage and quick attacks, while the Possessed Hatchet trades some power for a homing effect.
For Ranged users:

The Xenopopper with Nano Bullets is the strongest gun available. The Chain Gun should be used with Chlorophyte Bullets due to its low accuracy and the Cultist's small hitbox, which is weaker but still a good choice. The Sniper Rifle is also a viable choice.
The Snowman Cannon is the best launcher available, which is very useful with its homing high damaging projectiles. It is also very useful for quickly taking out the Phantasm Dragon, as its explosive projectiles hit many segments at once.
The Eventide and Tsunami are the strongest bows available. The Aerial Bane has higher damage output but is heavily affected by gravity. Bows should be used with caution as the falling arrows may hit the duplicates unintentionally.
Using the Piranha Gun will help as it deals continuous damage to the Cultist and prevents him from summoning minions. It synergizes especially well with the Shroomite Armor's set bonus, as the damage of projectiles is determined at the moment they are generated.
The Electrosphere Launcher is very useful as the Cultist's movement pattern has him stay in one place for an amount of time which allows for many hits from this weapon.
For Magic users:

The Arc Surge is the strongest magic weapon against the Cultist, but it is a very rare drop from the Martian Saucer.
The Toxic Flask does insanely well, being able to deal around 4000 dps due to the low movement of the cultist, even without a mage-focused build. It can also defeat the Phantasm Dragon within a couple of seconds.
The Nightglow is a very strong weapon with high damage and requires no aiming. The Razorblade Typhoon is a slightly weaker alternative requiring little aiming, but still strong enough and can kill the Phantasm Dragon more quickly.
Even though the Lunatic Cultist only takes 75% damage from homing weapons, these two still have good damage output and allow you to focus on dodging.
The Razorpine, Blizzard Staff, Betsy's Wrath and Laser Machinegun have stronger single target damage but require aiming.
The Charged Blaster Cannon is a very strong magic weapon, being able to shoot a charged laser for a long time, though it is an extremely rare drop from normal enemies in the Martian Madness event.
Magnet Sphere will do a lot of damage, and can be used in combination with other weapons.
The support weapons Nimbus Rod, and the Rainbow Gun should be used with caution, as their stationary attacks could accidentally damage a duplicate of the Cultist, causing the Phantasm Dragon and/or an Ancient Vision to spawn in.
For Summoners:

The Terraprisma is the strongest minion available, though you will have to face the monumental task of beating Empress of Light during the day. The Tempest Staff and Xeno Staff are great alternatives. The Deadly Sphere Staff and Raven Staff are weaker, but still do well.
The Kaleidoscope and Electric Eel are the strongest whips available, with the former stronger against the Cultist himself and the latter stronger against the Phantasm Dragon he summons. If you don't want to fight the Empress of Light or Duke Fishron, the Dark Harvest and Morning Star are the next best options.
Through utilizing Whip stacking accessories, summoners can effectively stack up 3-4 tag slots at this stage of the game, making it a very powerful strategy to go with. Stacking up the speed buff and high tag damage from Dark Harvest and Kaleidoscope, respectively, is a very effective damage boosting method.
The Ballista Staff is the strongest sentry available. The Staff of the Frost Hydra is a weaker alternative.


=== Accessories ===
Wings are important for every boss fight. The best ones available are the Fishron Wings. Betsy's Wings provide horizontal speed but less vertical power.
Expert mode players who have obtained the Soaring Insignia may opt for the Empress Wings, as it has slightly better vertical mobility, with no loss to maximum height.
The Frog Leg makes all wings significantly faster, making dodging his attacks easier.
The Frozen Shield is a powerful accessory that grants immunity to knockback, and reduces damage taken.
The Expert Mode-exclusive Worm Scarf and Brain of Confusion are still viable till this stage, giving flat damage reduction and a chance to dodge an attack completely, respectively.
The Cosmic Car Key or other infinite-flight Mounts can be useful, freeing accessory slots that would otherwise be used for mobility, but are slower and clumsier than wings.
The Witch's Broom is widely considered as the best mount in the game, although being Expert Mode-exclusive.
The Master Ninja Gear greatly helps in dodging the attacks and is recommended for all classes. It stacks with the Mystic Arts Sash. It also gives the dashing ability which is helpful when using wings. The Expert Mode-exclusive Shield of Cthulhu is a weaker substitute to the Master Ninja Gear's dash.
The Magic Yoyo Bag is very useful for melee characters with Yoyos as it can increase their damage output and range.
The Destroyer Emblem and/or the Celestial Shell are always good to have.
For summoners, whip stacking accessories such as the Silver Bracer, Mobius Strip, and their upgrades (such as Twilight Grasp and Ouroboros Ring), are very helpful.
Other damage increasing accessories include every other Emblem, the Fire Gauntlet and Mechanical Glove for melee builds, the Sniper Scope and Recon Scope for ranger builds, the Celestial Emblem and Sorcerer Emblem for sorcerer builds, and the Papyrus Scarab, Necromantic Scroll, for summoner builds.
The Cross Necklace or its upgrades can help when battling the Phantasm Dragon.
The Charm of Myths reduces the Potion Sickness cooldown as well as providing some extra health regeneration.
To make the most out of all accessory slots, all accessories should be reforged to Lucky, Menacing or Warding.


==== Potions ====
Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, Lifeforce Potion, and Ironskin Potion will greatly increase survivability.
Any food item that provides the Well Fed buff, such as coffee or chicken nuggets are good.
Mana Regeneration Potion is a must for mages.
Swiftness Potion will increase mobility.
Hunter Potion will show the real cultist when cloning itself.
Rage Potion and Wrath Potion will improve DPS.
Magic Power Potion, Archery Potion, Ammo Reservation Potion, Ale or Sake and Summoning Potion will further improve it for Mages, Rangers, Melee, and Summoner users respectively.


== Specific Strategies ==


=== Staying close ===
Almost all of the Lunatic Cultist's attacks are volleys of projectiles that spread out the further they go. By remain very close to the boss and slowly circling him using a flying mount, the attacks are closer together and easier to dodge. This strategy favors the use of short-range melee weapons like Starlight or The Horseman's Blade but can work with any class.

title: Guide:Glossary
content:
This is a glossary of terms used by the Terraria community. Actual in-game terms, such as melee speed, should not be listed here.


== Shorthands ==


== A ==
all-in
To dedicate all or most minion slots to a singular minion. See Guide:Class setups for examples of this term being used. Contrasted with minion mixing.
armor mixing
The process of using armor pieces from different armor sets to optimize for stat boosts rather than Set Bonuses. See Guide:Armor progression for a guide on armor mixing.


== B ==
bossing
Used as a measurement of a particular skill of a weapon in defeating bosses. Contrasted with mobbing.


== C ==
class
An informal term used to refer to any of the four main damage types: melee, ranged, magic, or summon damage.
Less broadly, it is also used in the context of specific accessory and armor combinations that often only buff one of these damage types. To "play a class" would mean intending to specialize into said armors and accessories, and oftentimes avoiding some mixed equipment.
From 1.3.0.1 to 1.4.0.1, certain ranged weapons were classified as dealing "throwing damage".
content mod
A mod that expands gameplay, such as adding new weapons, enemies, or biomes. Contrasted with quality of life mod.
crit, crit chance
Shorthand for critical hit or critical strike chance, respectively.


== F ==
facetank, face-tanking
The act of being able to withstand a boss or enemy's attacks effectively, to the point that dodging attacks becomes less pertinent. See tank. See Guide:Moon Lord strategies § Regenerative Facetank for an example of this term being used.


== G ==
glass cannon
Any entity that can deal large amounts of damage but cannot effectively or sustainably survive large amounts of damage. Contrasted with tank.


== H ==
hellevator
A vertical shaft of mined blocks that generally extends all the way from the surface to The Underworld.
hoik
A sawtooth series of sloped blocks, sometimes referred to as teeth, which can rapidly move entities across distances. It is often used as a method of fast travel or to attack through blocks.


== M ==
mech, mech boss
The mechanical bosses.
minion mixing
Using different kinds of minions at once, usually due to a limitation imposed by the kind of immunity frames inflicted by a weapon. Contrasted with all-in.
minion slot, minion cap
What the game counts towards the maximum amount of minions that can be summoned by the player.
mobbing
Used as a measurement of a particular skill of a weapon in clearing out nearby enemies ("mobs") that have just spawned, often useful if the player is exploring, building, or otherwise preoccupied. Contrasted with bossing.


== P ==
post-
A prefix applied to a boss's name to mean the stage after the boss had been defeated, e.g. post-mechanical bosses.
pre-
A prefix applied to a boss's name to mean the stage before the boss had been defeated, e.g. pre-Plantera. Can also be applied to Hardmode: pre-Hardmode.
progression skip, sequence breaking, skipping ahead, tier skip
The process of skipping the game's "intended" progression, e.g. defeating Duke Fishron before the mechanical bosses. See Guide:Skipping ahead for a list of common progression skips.


== Q ==
quality of life (mod), QoL
Features, especially those from mods, that make the game less tedious or improve the user experience in a non-intrusive way. Contrasted with content mod.


== S ==
sentry slot, sentry cap
What the game counts towards the maximum amount of sentries that can be summoned by the player.
skybridge
A long bridge built high up in the sky, usually only with a single layer of blocks or platforms. Besides the travel and/or arena advantages, it can also let you intercept Fallen Stars and coins for easy collection.
survivability
Things like defense, life regeneration, or the ability to dodge/parry attacks; survivability is reflected as an improvement in the player's capability in surviving as long as possible before/until they die.


== T ==
tank
Any entity that can survive large amounts of damage relatively well. For players wishing to achieve "tank" setups, survivability bonuses can help. Contrasted with glass cannon.
tModLoader, tMod, TML
A free program which allows playing Terraria with mods.
torch luck
By placing or holding Torches in the correct locations, players can increase their luck.
Prior to 1.4.0.3, Torch luck could have a negative value.
true melee

A subclass of melee weapons that are usually defined by the community in the following ways:
Melee weapons that deal damage solely with their sprite (e.g. Copper Broadsword) or with its sole projectile (e.g. Copper Shortsword). This means weapons that create secondary projectiles (e.g. Starfury) are excluded.
Most swords and spears can sensibly fit within this definition. However, flails, boomerangs, and yoyos also fit and are held to debate within the community.
Sometimes in addition to the above, melee weapons that require direct hits to create projectiles (e.g. Horseman's Blade and Bladetongue).


== V ==

V, The V, Hardmode V
The signature generation of the corresponding world evil and The Hallow that appears at the beginning of Hardmode.


== W ==
whip stacking
Whip stacking is the process of using certain accessories to let multiple whips in the hotbar stack their different tag effects.
Initially, whip stacking could be done by default. In 1.4.5.0, the feature was removed completely. It was then reimplemented in 1.4.5.7, where certain accessories were now required to whip stack.


== Footnotes ==

title: Bamboo Leaf
content:
The Bamboo Leaf is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Red Panda to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Red Panda will fly towards them while surfing on a bamboo leaf to catch up to them. The Bamboo Leaf can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 75 Gold.


== Trivia ==
The red panda is a small arboreal mammal native to the Himalayas and China. Despite the similarities in name and diet, it is not closely related to the giant panda.

title: Shimmering
content:
Shimmering is a unique debuff related to Shimmer. It has different effects depending on whether it is inflicted on a player or non-player entity:

Players are inflicted with the debuff when they are submerged in Shimmer or when their fishing pole's bobber touches Shimmer. They become unable to move or use items, be dismounted, become invincible to damage from enemies (except bosses), and start going down through solid blocks until they reach an opening of 2×3 tiles or reach the Underworld layer. There is also an "unstuck" mechanic to prevent the player from being in the Shimmering state for too long.
Enemies, NPCs, and critters are inflicted with the debuff when they are submerged in Shimmer or when they are sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, with the exception of enemies that are immune to the debuff. They start turning transparent and become completely invisible, then become increasingly opaque once they leave the Shimmer. If the afflicted entity has a special transmutation, it will transform into the respective entity/item when it is almost invisible.
Equipping the Chromatic Cloak will grant the player a more controllable Shimmering.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Notes ==
After being inflicted with Shimmering, a non-player entity's opacity will decrease by 1% per tick, resulting in it being completely invisible after 1.67 seconds. Entities with a special transmutation will transform when they have 10% opacity, i.e. after 1.5 seconds. After leaving the Shimmer, the entity's opacity will increase by 0.1% per tick, and it will become fully opaque again after 16.67 seconds. Upon taking damage, the entity's opacity will increase by 10%, i.e. 1.67 seconds will be subtracted from the total gradual change time.
If the player is in the Shimmering state for more than 20 seconds, they can press any of the movement keys (▲ Up, ◀ Left, ▼ Down, ▶ Right) to be teleported to an open space nearby. If no movement key is pressed and the player remains in the Shimmering state for more than 60 seconds in total, they will be forcefully teleported.
The following enemies' attacks can still deal damage to the player during Shimmering state: The Torch God (projectiles), King Slime, Spiked Slime, Eye of Cthulhu, Servant of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds, Vile Spit, Creeper, Dark Mage (projectiles only), Old One's Skeleton, Queen Bee (projectiles only), Bee, Skeletron and its arms, Deerclops (projectiles only), Wall of Flesh, The Hungry, Leech, Queen Slime and all her minions, The Destroyer, Probe, The Twins (projectiles only), Skeletron Prime and its arms, Ogre (projectiles only), Plantera, Plantera's Tentacle, Plantera's Hook, Empress of Light (projectiles only), Golem, Duke Fishron, Sharkron, Betsy (projectiles only), Lunatic Cultist, Phantasm Dragon, Ancient Vision, Moon Lord, True Eye of Cthulhu.
The player cannot enter the Shimmering state in reversed gravity. Gravity will be reset to normal as soon as the player becomes afflicted with the debuff.
The descent speed in the Shimmering state can be sped up by holding the Portal Gun.


== Tips ==
Shimmering can be used to gain early access into the Jungle Temple.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Shimmer invincibility no longer applies to bosses or the Torch God.
Desktop 1.4.4.5: Added a failsafe that will protect players who get stuck in an excessively long Shimmering state.
Desktop 1.4.4.4: Shimmering no longer grants the player invincibility against bosses.
Desktop 1.4.4: Introduced.

Console 1.4.4: Introduced.

Switch 1.4.4: Introduced.

Mobile 1.4.4: Introduced.

title: Sparkle Slime Balloon
content:
The Sparkle Slime Balloon is a Hardmode novelty consumable item. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Sparkle Slime debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles, causing them to become tinted purple and drip with pink and purple slime for 30 seconds. This debuff is only cosmetic and deals no damage.
The Diva Slime spawns and moves in after throwing or discarding a Sparkle Slime Balloon into Shimmer.
Queen Slime always drops 25–75 / 25–74 Sparkle Slime Balloons upon her defeat, and they are also dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds.


== Immune NPCs ==


== Trivia ==
It resembles the Regal Gel projectiles of Queen Slime.
The tooltip is a reference to the "Gamer Girl Bathwater" product sold by Belle Delphine in 2019.
Other adult jokes in this game include Golden Shower, Master Bait, and Mourning Wood.


== See also ==
Slime (debuff), a debuff that similarly causes targets to drip slime

Stack limit increased from 99 to 9999.

title: Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle
content:
The Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Grinch that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, a red balloon will carry the Baby Grinch to catch up with them. The Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle is dropped by the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 1.11%–2.22% (3.33%–6.67%) chance depending on the current wave.


== Trivia ==
This item is a reference to the 1957 children's story, How the Grinch Stole Christmas! by Dr. Seuss, specifically from the 2000 live-action film adaptation. In the film, the first of several flashback scenes depicts the Grinch as a baby when deuteragonist Cindy Lou Who asks several of the local residents of Whoville about the Grinch's past.

title: Mechanical Skull
content:
The Mechanical Skull is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Skeletron Prime when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.
If Skeletron Prime has not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Skull.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


=== Used in ===


== Notes ==
In worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix special world seeds, the Mechanical Skull is not consumable and is instead a crafting material for the Ocram's Razor, an item used to summon Mechdusa. Its tooltip also displays 'Part of a set'.
Like other mechanical boss summoning items, the Mechanical Skull can be brought to pre-Hardmode worlds and can be used to summon Skeletron Prime there.


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==

The Skull Lantern and Mechanical Skull are very similar in appearance to the skull in the original sprite for Skeletons.
Like the Mechanical Worm, it looks like a wind-up toy.
The crafting recipe of the respective summoning items for the mechanical bosses reference themes of Darkness, Light, and Balance. The Mechanical Skull specifically references Balance in that it requires both Souls of Night and Souls of Light.
Darkness, Light, and Balance are also referenced in the crafting recipes of the Onyx Blaster, Dao of Pow, and Sky Fracture respectively.


== See also ==
Mechanical Worm and Mechanical Eye, the other mechanical boss-summoning items.
Suspicious Looking Skull, Ocram's summoning item of similar appearance to the Mechanical Skull.

title: Dark Harvest
content:
The Dark Harvest is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that is dropped by Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

15 tag damage
Marks enemies with dark energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Dark Harvest, it triggers a Reaping effect, causing up to 3 nearby targets to take 15 damage. Reaping is not affected by any damage bonuses and has 50 armor penetration. The dark energy is not consumed upon activating its effect and its duration can be refreshed.
Grants the Harvest Time buff, increasing whip speed by 35% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits.
Its best modifier is Legendary.


== Notes ==
The Reaping effect has a range of 25 tiles, and it "jumps" from one enemy to the next. This means that it can hit an enemy up to 75 tiles away from the first one, if all four enemies are lined up 25 tiles apart.
Internally, the Dark Harvest applies 15 summon tag damage to enemies that are marked with the dark energy, and the Reaping projectiles created when minions or sentries hit a marked enemy will not deal damage to that marked enemy.
The Reaping effect does not inflict any knockback to enemies.
The damage of the Reaping effect is affected by the summon tag damage penalty of Blade Staff minions.


== Tips ==
Due to its special Reaping effect, it significantly outperforms other whips except Constellation and Possession when paired with piercing minions during events such as the Pumpkin Moon. However, it does not have a clear advantage when facing single targets.
The Dark Harvest works very well as a second whip if using whip stacking, providing high tag damage and whip speed bonus.


== Trivia ==
This weapon is similar to a kusarigama, a Japanese weapon consisting of a sickle with a weighted chain attached to it.
The Dark Harvest is internally referred to as ScytheWhip.
Unlike all other whips, which swing in varying arcs, Dark Harvest only swings from top to bottom.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Damage increased from 100 to 110.
Tag effect damage increased from 10 to 15.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Use time reduced from 30 to 27.
Attack speed bonus from Harvest Time reduced from 50% to 35%.
Reaping (Dark Harvest's special tag debuff) will now proc damage on the affected target as well as nearby targets. This acts as an effective 10 tag damage.
Fixed an issue where the whip speed buff would incorrectly apply the buff to melee weapons.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Range increased.
Damage penalty for each additional target hit per swing reduced from 30% to 10%.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Introduced.

Console 1.4.0.5.4.1: Introduced.
