title: Witch's Broom
content:
The Witch's Broom is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Witch's Broom, allowing the player to fly and hover indefinitely in any direction. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event in Expert Mode with a 5–20% chance depending on the current wave.


== Notes ==
The broom mount behaves similarly to the UFO mount from the Cosmic Car Key, with the same vertical speed and faster horizontal speed. Unlike the UFO mount, the player can still ride the broom in liquids.
The broom mount has a top speed of 46 mph when flying horizontally and 41 mph when flying vertically. When flying diagonally, however, it can reach 62 mph at maximum. When in liquids, the speed is reduced to 23 mph when flying horizontally and 21 mph when flying vertically, 26 mph when flying downward diagonally, and 31 mph when flying upward diagonally, respectively. However, when in Merfolk form granted by Neptune's Shell, Moon Shell or Celestial Shell, the broom acts like it is not submerged in liquid.
Because of this, one can fly at the same speed as, if not faster, than the Dungeon Guardian (41 mph consistently).
The broom's hitbox is the same size as the player: 2 by 3 tiles, so unlike the UFO mount, the broom can fit through doorways making the Rod of Discord less essential for traversal.
The broom cannot fly downwards through "bottom" platforms (that is, hammered to the lower half of the block), and will instead bounce off them. Other platforms can be passed downward with only a slight delay.
Falling from maximum speed and mounting the broom allows it to fly at 51 mph.
Similarly, it is possible to fall from a height at max speed and then mount the broom and fly diagonally. This reaches a speed of 66 mph.
The lantern hanging from the front of the broom also provides a small amount of light.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
When using this mount, it may be useful to replace accessories such as any wings or boots.
While they lack infinite flight time (unless the Soaring Insignia is equipped), using wings with hovering abilities in tandem with Lightning, Frostspark, or Terraspark Boots can provide more speed and mobility.
Using wings with a fast ascent speed such as Fishron Wings, it is possible to fly upwards with the wings, deploy the mount and maintain the speed of the wings beyond the duration of the wings.
The mobility of this mount and the ability to use items while riding it makes it a good mount for construction.
This mount is effectively a direct upgrade to the Cosmic Car Key, because it can be obtained earlier, can fly through liquids, and has a smaller hitbox than the Cosmic Car Key (letting the player go through doors while mounted). The only downside is that it cannot be obtained in Classic Mode worlds.


== Trivia ==
It is the only Expert Mode-exclusive item to be dropped by an event boss.
It is also the only dropped Expert Mode-exclusive item to not be obtained in a Treasure Bag (excluding Treasure Bags themselves).

title: Clay Bud Staff
content:
The Clay Bud Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Clay Bud minion. The Clay Bud walks and jumps into enemies, dealing contact damage to them when slamming down with its arms. If the Clay Bud strays too far away from the player, it will propel itself up by using the leaves at top of its head and fly to the player. Much like Pals, the Clay Bud minion can be petted by using ⚷ Open / Activate.
Its best modifier is Fabled.

=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Clay Bud inflicts 30 ticks of local invincibility frames on hit, meaning it can hit for up to 2 times per second.
The Clay Bud can target enemies within a 31.25-tile range.
The Clay Bud always knocks enemies away from the player.
The Clay Bud is always spawned at the player's position, rather than the cursor's position.


== Tips ==
Unlike some other pre-Hardmode minions which use static invincibility frames and can interfere with other minions of the same type, the Clay Bud minion uses local invincibility, meaning that its damage output will linearly scale with how many Clay Buds are summoned.

title: Bast Statue
content:
The Bast Statue is a furniture item that grants The Bast Defense buff to players in its vicinity, increasing their defense by 5. The buff effect can be toggled via wire. The Bast Statue can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. It can also be found as a furniture in Underground Desert Cabins.
The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Bast Statue, similar to Heart Lanterns and Campfires.


== Notes ==
Multiple statues will not stack their effects. Two Bast Statues in a player's vicinity will still only grant +5 defense.


== Trivia ==
Bastet or Bast was the Egyptian goddess of protection against disease and evil spirits, cats, perfume, ointments, fertility, pregnancy, children, music, the arts, and warfare.
The buff name "The Bast Defense" is a pun on the phrase "the best defense is a good offense", a proverb commonly used as the prime strategic principle of war.

title: Clothier Voodoo Doll
content:
The Clothier Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon Skeletron after it has been defeated. It has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance to drop from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon.
When equipped in an accessory slot (but not social slots), the Clothier Voodoo Doll allows the player, Fallen Stars, and other NPCs to harm and kill the Clothier. As long as the Clothier Voodoo Doll is equipped, the Clothier will summon Skeletron upon dying at night (7:30 PM to 4:30 AM). The Clothier can die by any means to summon Skeletron. In worlds with the Remix seed, killing the Clothier with the Voodoo Doll equipped will always summon Skeletron, even between 4:31 AM and 7:29 PM.
Unlike the Guide Voodoo Doll, the Clothier Voodoo Doll is not destroyed upon use, and has no effect when dropped into lava.
The Clothier Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
The reusable nature of this accessory allows the player to easily make a small amount of money, as Clothier drops the Red Hat upon death, worth 2 Silver, and Skeletron drops 5 Gold, barring the value of his other drops.
However, this can only be done once per night as Clothier will not respawn until day.


== Trivia ==
In popular culture, a voodoo doll is a figurine resembling a person, which can be harmed in order to magically inflict harm on the person being mimicked.


== History ==

title: Mourning Wood
content:
The Mourning Wood is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Pumpkin Moon event. It is the Pumpkin Moon equivalent of the Everscream, which behaves in an almost identical way to the Mourning Wood.
Defeating the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event will add 75 / 150 / 187.5 points to the final score.


== Behavior ==
The Mourning Wood alternates between two attacks:

The Mourning Wood fires a volley of Flaming Wood at the player that travels in straight lines and can pass through blocks.
The Mourning Wood fires a jet of Greek Fire projectiles, which are affected by gravity and remain on the ground for a short while, dealing damage to players that touch them.


== Notes ==
The Mourning Wood begins to spawn during the Pumpkin Moon event at wave 6.
The drop chance of the Mourning Wood's dropped items increases linearly with the wave it is in (lowest drop chance in wave 4, highest drop chance in wave 15). In wave 15 it will also drop a trophy and other loot.
The Mourning Wood can initially pass through blocks when it spawns within them, floating towards the player until it reaches an open area. It resembles a Wraith's behavior. Otherwise, it walks on surfaces and cannot jump.
It does not despawn after killing all available players.
The closer to death a Mourning Wood is, the faster it moves, a trait shared with several other enemies.


== Tips ==
Pay attention to when a Mourning Wood stops walking, as it is about to perform one of its two ranged attacks.
It is advisable not to enter a small room while fighting a Mourning Wood because its "Flaming Wood" attack can go through walls.
The Mourning Wood's "Greek Fire" attacks cannot pass through water, therefore submerging the mini-boss at least halfway up is an easier way to defeat it. Note the "Flaming Wood" attacks do pass through water.
The Mourning Wood can be defeated with relative ease by aiming the North Pole above it so it gets hit by several of its snowflake projectiles.


== Trivia ==
Mourning is the grief over someone's death, and fits in well with the Halloween theme of the Pumpkin Moon.
The name is a pun on "morning wood", a slang term referring to nocturnal erections during REM sleep.
Other adult jokes in this game include Golden Shower, Master Bait, and Sparkle Slime Balloon.
Real-life Greek fire was an incendiary weapon used by the Byzantine Empire in naval battles. Some historians believe it could be ignited on contact with water, which contradicts the properties of the projectile in-game.
According to the Splinterling's Bestiary entry, Mourning Woods reproduce by snapping cuttings from their bodies and thrusting them into the soil. The cuttings eventually grow into Splinterlings.
The Mourning Wood is the only event mini-boss to drop an Expert Mode-exclusive item, the Witch's Broom.
Additionally, it is the only enemy that can drop two mount-summoning items at once: the Witch's Broom and the Hexxed Branch.
 The Bestiary entry for the Mourning Wood: "These enormous murder trees nightmarishly stomp about, prepared to shower endless fiery destruction upon all life."


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: 
Health increased from 12000 to 14000.
Defense increased from 28 to 34.
Increased the number of enemy slots taken, to be more in line with Frost Moon bosses, dramatically reducing how many can spawn at a time.

Increased the Pumpkin Moon wave point progression per kill in Master Mode from 150 to 187.5.

Witch's Broom was added to the Expert Mode drop pool.
Now has Master Mode drops: it will always drop the Mourning Wood Relic on death and also has a 25% chance of dropping the Hexxed Branch mount.

title: Ocram's Razor
content:
Ocram's Razor is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Mechdusa when used. It can only be used in worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix seeds. It is crafted with the Mechanical Eye, Mechanical Worm, and Mechanical Skull and can be used in any biome, at any time.
This item has no function when brought to other worlds, and its tooltip will display 'It has no effect in this world' instead.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Achievements ==


== Trivia ==
In order to craft one Ocram's Razor from scratch, the player would need to obtain:
15 Iron / Lead Bars
9 Souls of Light
9 Souls of Night
6 Rotten Chunks / Vertebrae
3 Lenses
30 Bones
This item's name is a reference to Ocram, a boss exclusive to the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version of Terraria, and Occam's razor, a problem-solving principle which can be interpreted as  "The simplest answer to a question is the most likely to be correct."
The chest-like appearance of the Ocram's Razor could also be a reference to Pandora's box, an artifact in ancient Greek mythology that unleashed curses upon the world when its owner, Pandora, opened it out of curiosity, leaving behind only the spirit of Hope.
Ocram's Razor is one of only two boss-summoning items that use other boss-summoning items in its recipe. The other one is the  Old-gen console and 3DS-exclusive Suspicious Looking Skull.
Incidentally, the Suspicious Looking Skull is used to summon Ocram, the boss being referenced in this item.

title: Coin rain
content:
Coin rain is an event that can occur at the same time as Rain. During the event, Copper Coins, Silver Coins, and occasionally Gold Coins fall from the sky, and can be picked up by the player.


== Details ==
The chance for a Coin rain to occur is 1/25 (4%) when rain starts to fall.
The chance increases to 1/5 (20%) in worlds with the Celebration Mk 10 seed active but the For the Worthy seed inactive.
The chance increases with positive luck and decreases with negative luck. This depends on the player with the highest luck in the world.
The event cannot occur in worlds with the Remix or Mole people seeds active.
When the event occurs, the status message "Coins descend from the heavens!" appears in yellow text.
It ends when the total value of coins dropped has reached a hidden value based on world size:

It can also prematurely end when rain stops, a Thunderstorm begins, or when more than 391 item entities are active in the world.


== Contents ==
During the event, there is a 1/30 (3.33%) chance every tick for coins to fall from the sky, meaning on average it happens once every 0.5 seconds. Coins randomly appear within the upper 5% of the world, but cannot appear within 50 tiles of true left and right world borders. When coins are about to appear, there is a 1/2 (50%) chance for their horizontal starting position to be moved within 150 tiles to left or right of the closet player.
The table below shows the type and amount of coin that can fall, and the respective chance for them:

Therefore, the average amount of coins that fall each time is 29 Silver 92 Copper.


== Notes ==
Coins will not spawn if time is frozen in Journey Mode.


== Tips ==
Building a skybridge and using Conveyor Belts can help with collecting the coins.

Console 1.4.5: Introduced.

title: Carrot
content:
The Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Bunny that follows the player. If the player gets too far away from the bunny, it will fly at a fast speed while emitting a trail of smoke to catch up to the player. The color of the bunny's fur is defined by the shirt color chosen for the character, meaning the color can be changed using a Dresser. The Carrot is only available to players in the Terraria Collector's Edition and Terraria 15th Anniversary Collector's Edition, and will automatically appear in the inventory of any newly generated characters.


== Notes ==
It is only available to players who have purchased the Collector's Edition of Terraria – new characters created by them will spawn with it. While it can be obtained via trading or inventory editors, players who do not have the Collector's Edition will not be able to use it.
However, using an inventory editor, the user can apply the pet's buff, which makes the player spawn with the Bunny pet.
To avoid network incompatibility, and to make updates easier, the data corresponding to the Bunny pet is present in all  Desktop and  Mobile platforms, but only players identified as owning the Collector's Edition will spawn with a Carrot and be able to use it. This effectively makes it unobtainable and unusable on the  Mobile version.
The Carrot can be researched, but it will still have no effect without having bought the Collector's Edition.
The Bunny.exe file on the Collector's Edition disc can be used to activate the Bunny pet on any of either the Steam or GOG versions of the  Desktop version.
The color of the bunny pet can affect how dyes appear on it.


== Trivia ==
The publisher of the Collector's Edition requested an exclusive in-game feature, so as to motivate people to purchase the more expensive physical copy instead of the digital download version of the game. To avoid unbalancing the game, Redigit chose to comply with a relatively inconsequential feature.Verify
If the Carrot is equipped in the pet slot, the Bunny pet will appear in the character selection menu even if the player does not have the Collector's Edition (and thus cannot summon the pet in-game).


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.0.4: Fixed Collector's Edition Carrot overriding the Magic Mirror on a Journey Mode character.

Mobile 1.3.0.7: Introduced, but unobtainable and unusable.

title: Camera Mode
content:
Camera Mode is a special interface which allows taking screenshots of a Terraria world, providing controls to capture images of selected areas of the minimap or screen. Camera Mode is activated by pressing F4 or left-clicking the camera icon above the armor dye slots in the inventory, which replaces the gameplay interface with a specialized image capture interface. While Camera Mode is active, mouse control is used to frame the picture, and the player can neither build nor use items. Selecting an item on the hotbar, using the number keys, or pressing Esc will cancel Camera Mode.
Unrevealed sections of the world will not be uncovered by Camera Mode, represented as black swaths similar to ordinary unexplored areas on the minimap.


== Features ==


=== Screenshots ===
The most basic utility provided by Camera Mode, the screenshot, takes a full-size picture of the screen. The interface is hidden in screenshots taken using this function. The produced image is the same size as the viewable window, meaning that the size of produced images will change if the game window is resized.


=== Snapshots ===

The primary function of Camera Mode is its ability to capture selected areas of the screen by using the frame functions:

 Using Pin Frame, left and right clicking will set the two opposing corners of the rectangular capture area highlighted in white.
 Set Frame allows the player to drag the edges to expand the frame.
 Reset Frame removes the frame entirely.
Take Snapshot produces a complete image of the region inside the frame. Frames can also be set from the minimap, which can be accessed by pressing M or selecting the Open Map function.
A frame must be set before a snapshot can be taken. “You must first set a frame” will be shown when hovering over the snapshot button if no frame exists.


=== Open Folder ===
Both snapshots and screenshots are saved to the Captures folder and can be accessed by using the Open Folder function. This only functions in windowed mode.

On Windows Vista and later, %USERPROFILE%\Documents\My Games\Terraria\Captures
On Windows XP, %USERPROFILE%\My Documents\My Games\Terraria\Captures
On Mac, open Finder and press "Go" on the top. Then press "Go to folder...". Type in ~/Library/Application Support/Terraria/Captures
On Linux, $XDG_DATA_HOME/Terraria/Captures
This is typically ~/.local/share/Terraria


=== Settings ===

Prior to taking a picture, several options can be selected to modify the camera's output.

Image Packing: When taking a snapshot larger than the screen, Image Packing causes it to be compressed into a single continuous image, during which the completed image is "zoomed out". Disabling this feature instead produces a folder containing several exact replicas which the player will need to stitch together in an external image editor. This process is also slower to complete, but produces a 1:1 replica of the captured area.
Capture Entities: If disabled, the final image will not include the player, any pets, projectiles, minions, NPCs, or enemies.
Capture Background: If disabled, the final image will be presented on a transparent background.
Biome Pick: The thirteen biome icons at the bottom of the Settings menu allow for the changing of the displayed biome background and water color; for example, a picture of the Crimson could include the Hallow's bright purple water and pastel tree backgrounds. This background will be applied to the entirety of the image, even if it spans multiple biomes.


== Notes ==
The game is likely to crash if a too large snapshot with windy environment on is taken, particularly if there are more than 9000 tiles of a given type of dynamic tile (like pylons, relics, or tiles that react to wind) displayed at the same time.


== Trivia ==
Camera Mode was previously present in the  Mobile version of Terraria, although it was not fully functional – images were not stored anywhere and the game sometimes froze completely.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Camera Mode screenshots now only capture blocks that are fully on screen, which fixes some visual issues.
Certain visual effects that previously did not appear in Camera Mode snapshots now do appear if the entire snapshotted area is also on screen.
Camera Mode captures can now capture the Space sky and stars if the center of the capture is in Space.
Desktop 1.4.4.8: Biome Style buttons on the biome setting interface now have mouseover text showing what biome they represent.

The Tablet Fragment's sprite resembles a shard of the Mysterious Tablet. This is likely the case, considering the Cultists that must be killed to summon the Lunatic Cultist are seen worshipping it.
The Tablet Fragment even more closely resembles a Solar Tablet, as the same star symbol is visible on both sprites.
The Phantasmal Dragon's buff tooltip, "It keeps looking at the Moon", likely references the Mysterious Tablet's role in summoning the Moon Lord.

title: Creeper Egg
content:
The Creeper Egg is a Hardmode light pet-summoning item that spawns a Flickerwick to follow the player around. When active, it is similar to the Wisp in a Bottle, where it provides light wherever the player goes. The summoned Flickerwick has the same movement speed as the player, and cannot be left behind easily. The Creeper Egg is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/5 (20%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/10 (10%) chance during Tier 3. While equipped, light is produced not only around the pet, but also around the player.


== Trivia ==
This item is a direct reference to the "Flickerwick" pet/NPC in Dungeon Defenders 2.


== See also ==
Flickerwick at the Dungeon Defenders 2 Wiki

title: Shark Bait
content:
The Shark Bait is a pet-summoning item that summons a pet Shark Pup. When underwater, the Shark Pup swims around freely. When out of water, it is encased in a bubble. When the player is too far away, the Shark Pup will move swiftly toward them. The Shark Bait has a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Water Chests and a 1/10 (10%) chance of being found in Ocean and Seaside Crates.


== Trivia ==
The pet and the tooltip are a reference to the viral YouTube video and children's song "Baby Shark".
The pet sprite shares a similar visual to the Super Simple Songs version of "Baby Shark".
The sprite and name may be a reference to the 2003 American computer-animated movie Finding Nemo. The sprite resembles a clownfish, and "Shark Bait" is a nickname given to Nemo in the movie.

content:
The Bone Rattle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Face Monster that follows the player. title: Legacy:Guide:Brain of Cthulhu strategies
content:
The Brain of Cthulhu is a Pre-Hardmode boss. It is The Crimson counterpart of Eater of Worlds.


== Terrain Preparation ==

You'll want to set up a long platform in The Crimson, because it can only be summoned there. It can be summoned in caverns and above ground. It should be high enough so ground enemies can't jump up to you, but low enough that you don't accidentally go high enough to make it despawn.  It is similar to the Eater of Worlds in the way that it can be summoned and fought during day or night. An arena the size of your screen is preferred, since you can see the whole area in the middle, it is safe, and enemies can't go jumping in. It is suggested to place a Campfire in the center of the arena as it will grant a passive regeneration boost which can help you greatly. A Heart Lantern can accompany this if you already have 400 Health.
If you feel confident in the crimson, and don't mind the possibility of other crimson enemies barging in on your fight, you can set up a series of wooden platforms inside the large, circular hollows of the underground crimson.  These spaces are usually near 6-10 hearts, giving you a chance to kill 2 or 3 brains in a row using terrain prepared on-the-spot.  You can grapple up to wooden platforms, so you can space the platforms up or down more than your normal jumping range if you have a Grappling Hook, already. (Even when holding down, you fall faster with less platforms.)
Alternatively, you can also "box" the arena, by simply putting up a simple wall and ceiling in the big chasm the crimson usually forms, and using materials such as stone or even dirt. You can then set 2-4 wooden platform "floors" which you can then use to maneuver around the arena, and this will prevent other monsters from interfering in your fight. If there are multiple Demon Heart in the chasm, you can also use this arena repeatedly to fight in.
Keep in mind that the boss will spawn when you smash the third heart, setting you immediately into battle, not when you take your time getting to the arena. Have a path to your arena ready, and try to save any hearts close to your arena as the third heart to smash in a series unless you want to build more arenas every time you want to fight a new Brain. Alternatively you may try to destroy the hearts from a distance by using explosives.
If you have a world that has The Corruption, consider killing the Eater of Worlds for a Nightmare Pickaxe to mine crimstone and make getting to hearts and shaping terrain more easily. If you enjoy fishing, the Reaver Shark is very convenient for the same purpose.
The Brain Of Cthulhu is unique in the way it reacts when you die. Unlike every other boss, The Brain Of Cthulhu does not despawn upon your death, rather it keeps ramming into the spot you died. You can use this to your advantage by using Purification Powder to clear out a small area to make a basic house. Then if you place a bed inside, you have a respawn point in the main chamber. Now, there is virtually no consequence to dying in the fight, as you can keep respawning and continue the battle.


== Gearing up ==


=== Armor ===
If you want to stand a chance against the Brain of Cthulhu, you're going to need at least 
Iron or Lead armor. Lower armor can be used if you manage to get some defensive reforges on Accessories, but of course the better armor you have, the easier the fight will be. If you have access to Platinum armor, be sure to make it, as you benefit from it greatly.
On the Nintendo 3DS version, Bones drop from Skeletons, so Necro Armor can be used here.


=== Weapons ===
For melee users it is recommended to use The Rotted Fork or a Chain Knife if you didn't get a Rotted Fork from smashing crimson hearts.(Note for hardmode players the deathsickle is a good weapon for speed kills and quick harvesting for money)
For magic users, use a Water Bolt or Crimson Rod if you have one. Otherwise, use an Emerald Staff or better.
(Note the water bolt can be effective if in a enclosed arena)

For ranged users, use a Gold or Platinum bow with Jester's Arrows.


==== Ranged ====
Bows with Jester's or Unholy Arrows are good for their high damage. Because they are piercing weapons, both arrow types can hit multiple eyes. However, one can also use Flaming Arrows if they wish to. Recommended bows are the Platinum Bow/Gold Bow or Tendon Bow from the crimtane given from Eye of Cthulhu.
For guns, you might want to find an Undertaker from Demon Hearts, the equivalent to the Musket in The Corruption. Also make sure to buy plenty of bullets. If you have the extra meteorite or silver, you could craft bullets from them to give you an extra 2 damage per shot.


==== Consumables ====
In the beginning of the battle, Grenades are highly useful against the clumps of Creepers that form. Only a few are necessary to take many of the Creepers down.
For thrown, get lots of Shurikens or Throwing Knifes. Molotov Cocktails also works great because of the splash damage and the fire that hits multiple times keep the brain away in its second stage.
Also, the Harpoon seems to work great under its second stage, because of the great knockback. The harpoon is dropped from the goblins, so that means you will need to fight a goblin army first to get this.


==== Magic ====
As for the Magic users, find a Water Bolt, and get at least 100 mana if you don't want to continually run out and hope that one of the orbiting eyes drop another star. If you have already beaten the Queen Bee, the Bee Gun is useful to get rid of the Creepers. If you found a Floating Island, then make use of the equipment you get. If you're lucky, you can get the Starfury and make it an easy fight. If all else fails, you can use a Crimson Rod which is also found in the demon heart and will do constant damage over time, and only needs casting every 30 or so seconds.
If you already farmed a Meteorite crash site for Meteorite, you can use the excellent Space Gun with Meteor armor: its piercing ability will clear out the Creepers fairly easily, and it will cost no mana thanks to the set bonus of Meteor armor.
If you have access to a world with Corruption, the Vilethorn is tremendously potent against the eyes in the first half of the fight - the Vilethorn can penetrate infinite enemies, and has enough knockback to stun the whole crowd of Creepers, making the enemy evaporate.  It's also light on mana if you space your shots out.  (With 200 mana, you can regenerate all mana spent on the Vilethorn before the thorn effect, and its knockback, ends, giving you excellent juggling capabilities.)
The second phase of the boss is similar to the Eye of Cthulhu, but the teleportations can sometimes make the boss easier, as it tends to make the boss back off from the player a little.


==== Ranged ====
It may be best to switch to a weapon with higher one-target damage against the brain - you will likely be shooting at it from fairly close range, and there will only be one target, so your choice of weapon may change.  Fire arrows on the strongest bow you can bring, and The Undertaker will be more effective against the single, large target you face in the second half. If at all possible, defeat the Eye of Cthulhu first, then use the crimtane you get to make a Tendon Bow, then make fire arrows and watch in awe as the boss gets wiped out in about 2-3 minutes after it enters it's second stage.


==== Melee ====
For users who use melee, using a spear-type weapon can be effective on both the first and second stages of the battle. The Trident or The Rotted Fork are suggested, since a spear can hit multiple enemies multiple times with each attack. As well, it is highly suggested that, if you can, fight the Eye of Cthulhu first and make the Blood Butcherer from the crimtane dropped, it is likely the best sword you will have the ability to craft at this point, and using its sweeping overhead swing can help take down creepers quickly. If possible, use a Blade of Grass A flail type weapon such as the Ball O' Hurt or Chain Knife will also help in this fight since it let's you you keep a bit of distance, deliver reasonable knockback, and hit several enemies, as do Boomerangs on their return trip. Boomerangs can also deliver a decent amount of single target knock back and damage for the second phase.
A Katana is useful for its knockback and high chance of critical hits.
A Sawtooth Shark has enough knockback to keep the second stage of the BoC at bay, and just utterly chop it up but its low damage will mean that you will have to do this for several minutes. A safe and effective strategy but a slow one.


=== Multiplayer ===
If playing with someone, have one melee player who has a rotted fork or other spear to hit the creepers in the first stage, and have a ranged player off to the side with an undertaker, gold/platinum bow, or a gem staff. In the second stage, the melee player should use the fork/spear to keep the Brain from doing massive damage, and the ranged player should keep shooting it. If you have more than 2 people, have 1 melee and extra ranged players.


=== Potions ===
About 6 Lesser Healing Potions, 1 Ironskin Potion, 1 Regeneration Potion, and 1 Archery Potion. In case you use a magic weapon bring along some Lesser Mana Potions as well. Hunter Potions can also be useful if you are fighting the brain underground as you will immediately know where he has teleported.


=== Accessories ===
Any prefix that adds defense would be good if you are fighting him for the first few times, otherwise you are going to want movement speed or damage.
Spectre Boots -- Makes the fight far easier and lets you dodge around in both phases of the battle. Rocket Boots are still okay if you don't have the money for a Tinkerer's Workshop. Though fighting the Eye of Cthulhu 3 times should give enough money to purchase it.
Cloud in a Bottle -- Definitely helps with the lunges the Brain makes in phase 2. Combine with the Shiny Red Balloon if at all possible.
Band of Regeneration -- An extra heart every 40 seconds will help out.
Aglet -- Found easily, and provides moderately easier dodging. If possible, replace it with the Anklet of the Wind or Hermes Boots.
Frog Leg -- Found fishing in Ocean biome, a must for dodging Creepers and teleportation attacks.


== The Fight ==


=== Phase 1 ===
You want to get to the middle of your platforms and wait until the creepers and brain clump up together, then use any of your multi-target weapon. This can be your blood butcherer, flail, crimson rod, grenades, thrown weapons, or vilethorn. If you manage to get him in the open, this phase should go by very fast. The creepers will drop hearts and tissue. Do not collect these yet, if possible. You will need them in the second phase when the boss becomes more difficult.


=== Phase 2 ===
By now the brain will split, revealing a heart with an eye on the inside. In this phase, you should switch to your single target weapon and be prepared to dodge his attacks, the best way to do this is to either fall down platforms, or jump up platforms with the cloud in a Bottle. A good way to dodge its attacks is to use some ropes or jump on platforms. Alternatively, you could use a weapon with high knockback, stand in one place, and when the brain teleports to a new location, hit him, and he won't hit you, and will just teleport again. This method will deal with his second stage in less than a minute if you have a spear, like the rotted fork. A crimtane or iron bow with unholy or jesters arrows are good when your health goes down and other ranged weapons like the undertaker or minishark clear out the brain's second form relatively quickly.

title: Dryad
content:
The Dryad is an NPC vendor who sells various nature-themed items, including seeds, powders, and Planter Boxes. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:

There is an available vacant house.
The Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds, Brain of Cthulhu, or Skeletron has been defeated.
In addition to selling items, the Dryad can also report the percentages of Corruption/Crimson and Hallow that exist in the current world, which is based on the total number of blocks of each corresponding biome.
The Dryad will defend herself against nearby enemies by casting the Dryad's Ward, which summons two rotating circles of leaves around her, with the outer circle indicating the range of the attack. The attack lasts 10 seconds in total, however, if the Dryad takes damage when casting, the attack immediately ends. Counting from when the circles of leaves are summoned (and assuming the Dryad is uninterrupted), within the first 1.67 seconds, the radius of the Dryad's Ward is 18.75 tiles (300 pixels). The radius then generally increases to 37.5 tiles (600 pixels) over the course of 3.33 seconds, remains unchanged for another 3.33 seconds, after which the radius generally increases to 75 tiles (1200 pixels) over the course of 1.17 seconds before finally dissipating. 0.5 seconds after the circles of leaves are summoned, the Dryad's Blessing buff is granted to players and other town NPCs within its radius, while Dryad's Bane is inflicted on enemies with a clear line of sight inside its radius. Dryad's Blessing provides defense, health regeneration, and a thorns effect (similar to the Thorns Potion), while Dryad's Bane deals damage over time. See Dryad's Blessing page for details about the buff and debuff.


== Items sold ==


== World status ==
The Dryad will report the current percentage of Corruption/Crimson/Hallow coverage in the world with the “Status” option. The Dryad makes the distinction between Corruption and Crimson if they are present in the same world, and will list their percentages separately, though they both contribute to the overall total evil tile percentage in her final report.
The percentages of the respective biome is calculated by related tile count, with the following formulas:

Corruption = Corruption tiles ÷ Solid tiles × 100%
Crimson = Crimson tiles ÷ Solid tiles × 100%
Hallow = Hallow tiles ÷ Solid tiles × 100%
See below for a list of counted tiles.
If the world has no Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow, the And Good Riddance! achievement will be granted upon choosing the option.


=== Counting tiles ===
The following tiles will count towards the total tile count.


==== Corruption ====


==== Crimson ====


==== Hallow ====


==== Solid ====


== Joja Cola ==

When the player has a Joja Cola in their inventory, the Dryad will have special quotes hinting to the player to hold the Joja Cola. When the player is holding a Joja Cola, the “Status” option will be replaced with “Purify”. After choosing the option, the Joja Cola will be consumed as an animation of a Junimo jumping out of a star-shaped portal plays out. The Junimo then pulls out a Stardrop that the player can collect before disappearing.


== Living preferences ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Shimmered form ==

When submerged in Shimmer or sprayed with the Shimmer Gun, the Dryad will transform into her Shimmered form. This has no impact on gameplay or dialogue and is only a visual change. She can be returned to her classic look by submerging her in Shimmer again or spraying her with the Shimmer Gun again.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
For players creating housing for the Truffle, it would be beneficial to temporarily house the Dryad in or near a Glowing Mushroom biome where she will sell Mushroom Seeds.
It is not necessary to build a house, as a Queen Statue can be used to teleport her to a Glowing Mushroom biome.
Players can obtain items from both evils without using a different world by buying Corrupt or Crimson Seeds (Available while in the Graveyard minibiome) and making an artificial biome.


== Names ==
The Dryad may have any of the following names:
A world with both Celebration Mk 10 and Purify this enabled will spawn a shimmered Dryad named Lilith at game start. This is not a possible name for the Dryad under any other circumstances.


== Quotes ==


=== Interaction quotes ===


=== Happiness quotes ===


== Trivia ==
A dryad is a nature spirit from Greek mythology, generally depicted as a beautiful young woman. Fittingly, many of the Dryad's possible names take inspiration from either classical literature (e.g. Caelia, Elysia, Fae, Titania) or female celebrities.
This might be the reason that the Arms Dealer appears to flirt with her as shown in one of his quotes, but she states in one of her quotes that she wishes the Arms Dealer would stop pestering her. In the same quote she reveals that she is 500 years old.
According to Greek mythology, a dryad is a type of Nymph. This may be why Nymphs and the Dryad have a similar appearance.
The Dryad is depicted in a painting called Dryadisque, which itself is a parody of the 1814 real-world oil painting Grande Odalisque by Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres.
Her quote calling the Truffle a "fun guy" plays on the homophone “fungi”.

The quote “What's this about me having more 'bark' than bite?” is a pun on bark (the outermost layer on woody plants) and a possible joke about the fact that the Dryad is or was a tree.
This fact is shown in a credits cutscene.
This could also be a reference to her not cleansing the world evil herself despite claiming that she fought the Old One's Army.
One of the Dryad's quotes about the player's safety says "Terraria needs you", instead of "<Name of World> needs you". This is an oddity among the other quotes.
Her quote “I kissed a tree in the Jungle and I liked it.” is a reference to the Katy Perry song “I Kissed a Girl”.
Calista the Dryad is featured in the Terraria Comic Book from DC Comics.
The Dryad appears in the video game Dungeon Defenders 2 as a playable character. Her defenses include summoning World Trees, Moss Hornets, Harpies, Slimes, and Angry Nimbuses.
The Dryad's quote referencing her time in Etheria and her use of the Corruption against the Old One's Army is a reference to her ability in Dungeon Defenders 2 where she can become a corrupted version of herself. In her corrupt form, her abilities and defenses gain additional effects and/or deal more damage.
The Dryad's Shimmered form resembles her corrupted form from Dungeon Defenders 2.
 – According to the Terraria lore pages, an ancient race of Dryads once waged a large war with Cthulhu. Unable to defeat the beast, they managed to cripple it by ripping out its eyes, spine, and chunks of its brain. All but one of the Dryads were killed and the survivor (being the NPC encountered in-game) remains concealed for some time.
Despite this, like all NPCs, if she is killed and the spawn requirements are met, she will respawn. Re-Logic artist Jimmarn has speculated that she might be reincarnated.
The Guide's tip "You should prove yourself by defeating a strong monster. That will get the attention of a dryad." may or may not imply that there are still multiple concealed Dryads.
The name Celestia is a reference to the television series My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic, which features a princess of the same name.
The Princess has the chance to share the name Faye with the Dryad. In a world with both Celebration Mk 10 and Purify this enabled, the Zoologist has the chance to share the name Lilith with the Dryad.
The name Nissa comes from the planeswalker Nissa Revane from the collectible card game Magic: The Gathering.
According to Redigit, the Dryad "isn't actually wearing anything" and "the vines are a part of her body".
The Dryad is more likely to use the Stylist emote () than other emotes. It is unknown why this is the case.
In addition, the Stylist is also more likely to use the Dryad emote () than other emotes.
The internal name for the Junimo animation projectile is misspelled as "Jumino".
 The Bestiary entry for the Dryad: "The Dryad is the last of her kind. She is connected with nature and can analyze its purity worldwide. She sells seeds, too!"


== See also ==
Dryad at the Dungeon Defenders 2 Wiki


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: 
Dryad's Blessing defense bonus to other villagers increased from 6 to 10 in Classic difficulty, 10 to 15 in Expert and 14 to 20 in Master.
Defeating Queen Slime, Duke Fishron and Empress of Light now boost the damage of Dryad's Bane by 15% each (same as other Hardmode bosses).
Now sells all Planter Boxes regardless of game progression. Previously, the Dryad would only sell the Daybloom Planter Box after King Slime was defeated, the Blinkroot Planter Box after the Eye of Cthulhu was defeated, the Deathweed Planter Box after the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu was defeated, the Moonglow Planter Box after Queen Bee was defeated, the Waterleaf and Shiverthorn Planter Boxes after Skeletron was defeated, and the Fireblossom Planter Box after the Wall of Flesh was defeated.
Now also sells the Potted Forest/Jungle Cedar, Tree, Palm, and Bamboo in pre-Hardmode. These items were previously exclusively sold in Hardmode.
Now sells regular Torches during pre-Hardmode in worlds with both Vampirism and World is infected, as well as Corrupt or Crimson Torches, corresponding to the world's evil biome.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Now sells Guide to Environmental Preservation.
Can now purify Joja Cola.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Now sells Corrupt and Crimson Grass Walls, Flower Seeds, and Potted Trees. Also sells Crimson Seeds in Corruption worlds as well as Corrupt Seeds in Crimson worlds while in a Graveyard biome.
Desktop 1.3.0.6: Now sells Vicious Powder during a Blood Moon on Crimson worlds.
Desktop 1.3.0.5: Now properly increases the defense of other NPCs instead of decreasing it.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: 
Added Planter Boxes.
Added Dryad's Blessing buff.
Sprite updated. Old sprite was: .

Now sells Crimson Seeds during Blood Moon if in a Crimson world.
Now has Crimson specific dialogue for worlds with Crimson in them.
Improved Dryad's world status dialog.
Can now arrive following the defeat of the Brain of Cthulhu.
Fixed bug where Dryad would mention The Corruption in Purification Powder suggestion while in Crimson world.
Desktop 1.2.1: Now sells Pumpkin seeds along with her own clothes.
Desktop 1.2: Now sells Grass Walls and Flower Walls. Also sells Mushroom Grass Seeds when in a Glowing Mushroom biome.
Desktop 1.1.1: Now Corruption and Hallow status numbers are correct.
Desktop 1.1: 
Now has random name given to her on spawn. Her deaths will be reported with this name. Also other NPCs will use it in their quotes.
The Dryad will now tell the player the percentage of Corruption and Hallow in the game world.

title: Secret world seeds
content:
Secret world seeds are world creation modifiers that alter the created world in strange or unique ways.
Unlike regular world seeds, which only affect the usual world structure, secret seeds can produce worlds with characteristics that would not be attainable through normal world generation (i.e., they can affect the game's mechanics while playing in that world). For instance, they may change NPC shop inventories or permanently activate events. Compared to special world seeds, a similar feature, secret seeds generally have a more limited set of effects.
Secret world seeds are initially unavailable. They must first be "discovered" by entering their respective identifier in the seed input field in the world creation menu. Afterwards, they can be toggled on and off in a sub-menu of the world seed menu. There they can be combined both with each other and with all of the special world seeds.


== Overview ==
Seeds can be input with any capitalization or spacing, and special characters are skipped by the game. Therefore, for example, beammeup, bEam-me_Up, and beam me up all work for unlocking Beam me up. The list below separates them into words and adds punctuation for readability.
There is a total of 37 secret world seeds.


== While generating ==
The stars in the night background will start to slowly move towards the center of the screen. They will then start moving all over the place.


== Trivia ==
After the player discovers a secret world seed, the entered code is stored in plain text in the config.json file for displaying in the Seed Menu.
Combining all secret seeds as well as all special seeds (except for Skyblock) creates a world colloquially known as "True Zenith", which can be considered the highest world difficulty possible in Terraria.
Internally, the entered codes for secret world seeds are run through a non-reversible function (a cryptographic hash function) and are therefore impossible to determine by inspecting Terraria's source code. This means the codes can only be found out by trial and error, and as a result, it took an unusually long time to discover all of them. While most of the seeds introduced in 1.4.5.0 were found soon after release (January 27, 2026), certain ones proved to be particularly difficult to find:
double daring dangers was discovered on February 2, 2026, six days after release.
does that sparkle was discovered on February 5, 2026, nine days after release.
we don't even test for that was discovered on February 6, 2026, ten days after release. It was the last of the 35 secret seeds introduced in 1.4.5.0 to be discovered.


== Gallery ==

		
		


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Introduced Electric Boogaloo and Calm before the storm.
Desktop 1.4.5.5: All secret seeds in the seed selection menu now feature their own descriptions.
Desktop 1.4.5.4: Unlocked secret world seeds can now be toggled on and off via a new menu, accessed through the "Secret Seed" button.

title: Celebration Mk 10
content:
Celebration Mk 10 (also known as the Birthday World or Anniversary World) is a special world seed. It celebrates Terraria's tenth anniversary, on May 16, 2021.


== While generating ==
All generation descriptions and tips become pink-colored ( #FF69B4).
The Underground Hallow music will be played.


== World generation changes ==


=== Overall ===
The spawn point is changed to either Ocean in the world, implying most of the spawns usually happening in the inner third of the world will happen in the left or right sixth of the world.
Andrew the Guide, Whitney the Steampunker, Yorai the Princess, Amanda the Party Girl, and an Angora Town Bunny will also spawn there and a Party immediately starts.
A majority of the world is painted:
The Dungeon is in Deep Pink.
Living Trees, the Pyramid, and Clouds on Floating Islands are painted in Pink.
Jungle Temple tiles are painted in Purple, and walls are painted in Green.
All regular Sand Blocks, Sandstone Blocks, Hardened Sand Blocks, and ambient objects placed on or attached below these tiles are painted in Cyan. Unsafe regular Sandstone Walls and Hardened Sand Walls are also painted in Cyan.
Glowing Mushroom biomes are painted, with Giant Glowing Mushrooms painted in rainbow pattern and Mushroom grass painted in the same random color.
Half of the Underground Cabins have their tiles and walls replaced with Rainbow Bricks, and a half of the remaining ones are painted with a diagonal rainbow pattern.
Every tree generates as a vanity tree, except for Ebonwood and Shadewood trees (and their palm variants). All trees are painted in a rainbow pattern, including Ebonwood/Shadewood trees.
There are even more Living Trees than in a Drunk world.
Items in Chests always have a "best" modifier:
Accessories will have one of the +4 modifiers (Lucky, Menacing, Quick, Warding).
Weapons will have modifiers with the most stat increases, according to their damage type. The possible modifiers are:
Legendary, Godly, or Ruthless for melee weapons and whips
Unreal, Demonic, or Ruthless for ranged weapons
Mythical, Demonic, or Ruthless for magic weapons
Fabled, Eager, or Ruthless for summon weapons excluding whips
Over half of all moss is Neon Moss.
Gem trees are more common, similarly to the Drunk world.
All Floating Islands have Hallowed grass and a Hallowed Water Fountain.
Boulder traps have modified generation chances:
Bouncy Boulders' generation chance increased from 1/20 (5%) to 1/3 (33.33%).
Rainbow Boulders' generation chance increased from 1/25 (4%) to 1/7 (14.29%).
Life Crystal Boulders have a 1/4 (25%) chance to replace regular Boulders after all Boulders are generated.
Water pools near the Aether biome are replaced with Shimmer pools.
The number of Enchanted Sword Shrine placing attempts is doubled and the probability for an attempt to be skipped is halved. Additionally, the first attempt is never skipped, virtually guaranteeing at least one shrine.
The chances for a Lava Charm to be generated in a Chest is increased from 1/20 (5%) to 1/15 (6.67%).
The chances for Water Walking Boots to be generated in a Chest is increased from 1/10 (10%) to 1/7 (14.29%).
Rainbow Glowsticks replace Glowsticks in Chests.


=== Desert ===
The Desert generates without its usual entrance but with a single Pyramid.
The chest in the Pyramid always contains a Pharaoh's set in addition to its normal loot.
The caves of the Underground Desert are smaller.


=== Ocean ===
The Ocean cave will always be generated in the Ocean at the same side as the Dungeon.


== Other changes ==
Maximum size of Hardmode ore veins is increased.
Two unique enemies can be encountered in this seed:
The Jungle Mimic can spawn in the Hardmode Underground Jungle.
Golden Slimes can randomly spawn in place of a regular slime with a 1/180 (0.56%) chance.
Fairies have a higher spawn rate in the Cavern layer. All Fairies have a 5/6 (83.33%) chance to be a Pink Fairy. The latter effect does not apply when combined with a For the Worthy world.
Mimics have a higher spawn rate.
Coin rain is five times more likely.
When Hearts and Stars are dropped, they will randomly appear as normal variant or seasonal variant, with equal chance for each variant (1/3 (33.33%)).
All Fallen Star projectiles (including those from the Star Cannon, but not those from the Super Star Shooter) are pink.
The chance for a Blood Moon to occur is raised to 1/6 (16.67%) (from 1/9 (11.11%)) per night.
The chance for a Party to occur is raised to 1/7 (14.29%) (from 1/10 (10%)) per dawn.
The drop chance of the Rod of Discord is raised to 1/100 (1%) (from 1/500 (0.2%)).
Fireflies and Butterflies are more common.
The chance of obtaining a developer set from a Treasure Bag is doubled, from 1/16 (6.25%) to 1/8 (12.5%). Developer sets can still only be dropped from Hardmode bosses' Treasure Bags (except Queen Slime's), however.
The chance for a Starfall is increased from 1/10 (10%) to 1/5 (20%), and chance for a night to have an increased Fallen Star rate is increased from 1/3 (33.33%) to 1/2 (50%).
More clouds spawn in the background and more of them have a special shape.
The move-in criteria for the starting NPCs (Steampunker, Princess, Party Girl, Town Bunny) are removed. Should they be killed, they can respawn even if their conditions have not been fulfilled (e.g. the Steampunker can respawn even if no mechanical boss has been defeated). They do still require a vacant house in order to respawn, however.
The following bosses and boss servants are 50% smaller than normal:
These size changes does not apply if the For the Worthy seed is active.

The Traveling Merchant always sells 2 more items than normal.
The Princess sells rare items:
Slime Staff
Heart Lantern
Flask of Party
Sandstorm in a Bottle (while in the Desert)
Terragrim (during a Blood Moon)
Pirate Staff (after beating a Pirate Invasion in Hardmode, during the following moon phases:  )
Discount Card (after beating a Pirate Invasion in Hardmode, during the following moon phases:  )
Lucky Coin (after beating a Pirate Invasion in Hardmode, during the following moon phases:  )
Coin Gun (after beating a Pirate Invasion in Hardmode, during the following moon phases:  )
The Wizard Hat grants an additional minion slot.
The Tax Collector provides twice as much money.
The player explodes into confetti upon death, accompanied by one of the Don't Starve hurt sounds also heard in The Constant seed.
Palm trees drop 3 times as much wood on average (each tile of tree drops 2–4 corresponding wood).
Sand, Hardened Sand, and Sandstone Blocks will always be painted Cyan when placed.


== Notes ==
Due to the way certain invasion mechanics work, invasion events like Goblin Army will only take place near the initial beach spawn point. Unlike normal worlds, being near Town NPCs will not cause invasion enemies to spawn around the player.
Goblin Scouts and the King Slime will spawn a third of the world away from the beach spawn, which means they spawn around the middle of the world and the opposite ocean.


== Tips ==
Starting with the spawn at the Ocean may make the early game progression much harder if the player is on the Jungle side. However, starting on the Jungle side makes it easier to find the Aether.


== Trivia ==
The names of the four non-pet starting NPCs in the Celebration Mk 10 seed are the names of four members of Re-Logic: Redigit (Andrew), Cenx (Whitney), Yoraiz0r (Yorai), and Safeman (Amanda).
Unlike most of the other special seeds, the Celebration Mk 10 seed is interpreted as a number, so any number of 0s can be added in the front (e.g. 000005162011). In addition, there are numerous unintended strings that generate this special seed (due to the use of the CRC-32 algorithm), such as (case-sensitive):


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.0: Rainbow Glowsticks now replace Glowsticks in Chests.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Pre-Hardmode bosses and Queen Slime's Treasure Bags no longer yield developer items.
Now the Glowing Mushroom biomes are also painted in rainbow color.
Water pools near the Aether biome are replaced with Shimmer pools.
When generating, all texts become pink and the Underground Hallow music will be played.
The Party Girl spawned at world generation is now named "Amanda".
Probably other undocumented changes.
Desktop 1.4.2.3: Introduced.

title: Queen Bee
content:
The Queen Bee is a pre-Hardmode boss. Fighting her is not required for game progression, but defeating her rewards the player with useful items and weapons and allows the Witch Doctor to move into an available vacant house.
While the Queen Bee is alive, her exclusive music Queen Bee will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.


== Summoning and spawning ==
The Queen Bee spawns upon breaking a Larva found inside Bee Hives in the Underground Jungle.
She can also be summoned manually by using an Abeemination in the Jungle or Underground Jungle, at any time.


== Behavior ==
The Queen Bee has three distinct attack patterns:

The Queen Bee levels herself horizontally with the player before charging back and forth three times in an attempt to ram the player. Upon being summoned, she will always use this attack first.
The Queen Bee spawns Bees while hovering (which includes larger ones in Expert Mode), which pursue and attack the player. During this attack, she may spawn 6, 12, or 18 Bees.
The Queen Bee rapidly fires large yellow stingers at the player which visibly pulsate to indicate their location, similarly to Hornets. The stingers have a 1/3 (33.33%) / 100% chance of inflicting the Poisoned debuff for 10 / 2–20 / 2.5–25 seconds. During this attack, the Queen Bee alternates between hovering above the player and positioning herself to swoop in at the player from above.
In Expert Mode, the speed of these attacks increases as the Queen Bee's health lowers and her charges increase both in speed and number. At low enough health, the Queen Bee can perform up to six charges in a row before switching to a different attack. The Queen Bee's defense also increases up to a maximum of 28 depending on how much of her health has been depleted. Additionally, she will inflict the Poisoned debuff upon direct contact with the player for 2–8 / 2.5–10 seconds.
When fought outside of the Underground Jungle, the Queen Bee enrages, causing her movements to become more aggressive and firing stingers at a much faster rate. When fought in the surface Jungle or a different Underground biome, the Queen Bee still enrages, but this state is less aggressive than if the player were to fight her in any other surface biome.


== Aftermath ==
The Witch Doctor will be able to move in.
The Angler will be able to ask for Angelfish and Cloudfish if he could not already.
The Traveling Merchant will begin selling the Gray Zapinator if he was not already.
The Queen Bee emote  is unlocked.


== Notes ==
Unlike most other bosses, the Queen Bee does not despawn when far away from the player and charges towards the player instead.
This means if a player teleports, such as by using a Magic Mirror, the Queen Bee chases them across the map no matter the distance. If the player teleports outside of the Jungle, she will enrage and may kill the player.
In multiplayer, if all players fighting the Queen Bee die at the same time and any other players are alive at the time, the Queen Bee pursues the other players regardless of distance and will only swap aggro to a different player on the death of her current target.
The only way to properly despawn the Queen Bee outside of killing her is for all players in the world to die at once.
The Larva can be broken with any damaging weapon, similar to a Pot, so many actions such as the Orichalcum armor's set bonus or a Star Cloak can break the Larva, causing the Queen Bee to be unintentionally spawned.
This is especially common if there are remaining Larvae within the Jungle late into the game when it is possible to hit anything anywhere on the screen, even behind solid blocks. It is also possible early in the game if the player is using a whip, which can break things behind solid blocks.
Larvae are unaffected by the Guide to Environmental Preservation and its upgrades.
Bees spawned from Bee Hives, from mined Hive blocks, and from the Queen Bee herself will actively target other enemies and deal damage to them while also taking damage from them.
Bees do not drop Souls of Light, Souls of Night, or Biome Keys.
Occasionally, a Bee Hive may be large enough to possess two or more Larvae, especially in Drunk worlds. If a player is using bouncing weapons such as the Water Bolt, they must be wary of the additional Larvae, lest they be targeted by more newly summoned Queen Bees.
The amount of bees the Queen Bee can summon is not infinite, as 173 bees are the maximum amount of bees that can be alive at once.


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==

The Honey naturally found in Bee Hives can be used to craft Bottled Honey, provide passive health regeneration mid-fight, and help to negate the potency of being afflicted by Poisoned. However, standing in Honey will slow down the player significantly, so prolonged submersion is not recommended.
Equipping a Bezoar can help the player avoid taking large amounts of damage from being afflicted with Poisoned, especially in Expert and Master Mode due to its significantly extended duration, where it can reach upwards of 25 seconds.
The Bees do little damage, but can easily become an annoyance as they can push the player around. If the player does not have a Cobalt Shield or Obsidian Shield to avoid knockback, any grappling hook can be used to anchor the player to blocks.
In Classic difficulty, a spinning flail is sufficient to kill any incoming Bees before they can reach the player.
Bees will target other enemies if they are closer than the player and can thus be distracted with statue-spawned enemies or other trapped enemies.
In Expert and Master Mode, Bees are much tougher and can easily kill the player if ignored.
The Lightning Aura sentry summons and the Explosive Trap sentry summons can easily kill the bees if the player is near them.
The Queen Bee can be a viable source of money, dropping 5 Gold upon death and additional profit from her drops, as well as being comparably simple to summon.
The Obsidian armor is a great choice for summoners looking to focus on whips.
If the Shield of Cthulhu's dash is timed well, the damage of the Queen Bee's charging attacks can be blocked. However, this strategy will become less reliable over time due to the Queen Bee's speed ramping up significantly as her health is lowered.
For ranged players, any bow in combination with piercing arrows (such as Unholy or Jester's Arrows) can be a good choice for quickly dispatching the summoned Bees.


== Trivia ==

The Queen Bee has the largest number of drops of any pre-Hardmode boss in the game at 16. Furthermore, she has the second-most drops of any boss in classic mode, surpassed only by Plantera (a boss that is also spawned in the Underground Jungle), who has 17, and in expert mode or higher both are surpassed by Moon Lord, who has 20.
Because the Compass and Depth Meter reveal each tile to be 2 feet in length, judging by the Queen Bee's charging state, her body would be about 18′ 9″ (6.84 m) in length, and her wings would be about 10′ 7½″ (3.87 m) in length.
Although rare, it is possible to obtain the Yelets from the Queen Bee if she is defeated after one of the mechanical bosses has been killed.
The concept art of the Queen Bee from prior to her introduction looks vastly different than the sprite that was implemented. It bears resemblance to a Hornet.
 The Bestiary entry for the Queen Bee: "This highly aggressive monstrosity responds violently when her larva is disturbed; the honey-laden hives are her home turf."

title: Cool Whip
content:
The Cool Whip is a Hardmode whip. It has a 30% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

6 tag damage
Grants the A Nice Buff buff, creating a homing snowflake projectile that lasts for 3 seconds, which repeatedly deals 15 damage and has 30 armor penetration. The snowflake also applies the Cool Whip's tag damage to enemies it hits, like the whip itself. If a snowflake already exists, Cool Whip hits will refresh its duration instead of creating a new one.
Inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 4 seconds.
Its best modifier is Legendary.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The snowflake projectile applies 20 ticks of local invincibility frames upon hit, meaning it can hit for up to 3 times per second.
The snowflake projectile can home in on enemies within 25 tiles.
The snowflake is not affected by damage bonuses outside of banners, does not benefit from whip tag effects, and does not focus the player's prioritized target.


== Trivia ==
The Cool Whip and its tooltip, 'Let me have some of that cool whip', are a reference to the brand of imitation whipped cream of the same name.
The Cool Whip's tooltip is also a reference to "Barely Legal", the eighth episode of the fifth season of the American animated sitcom Family Guy, in which Stewie asks Brian for some Cool Whip, but pronounces it as "Cool Hwip."
The name of the Cool Flake's buff is a pun on the words nice and ice.
With perfect timing, it is possible to summon a snowflake at the same time the previous one is about to despawn, causing multiple snowflakes to exist at once.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.5.7: Fixed the Snowflake not properly syncing in multiplayer.
Desktop 1.4.4: 
Damage reduced from 50 to 45.
Now inflicts 6 Tag Damage.
Snowflake damage increased from 10 to 15, and now moves 50% faster.
Now inflicts Frostbite instead of Frostburn.
Desktop 1.4.1.2: 
Now inflicts Frostburn for a short duration on hit.
Increased the movement speed of the Snowflake minion by 50%.
Desktop 1.4.1: 
Range increased.
Damage penalty for each additional target hit per swing reduced from 33% to 30%.
Desktop 1.4.0.3: 
Fixed a bug where the Cool Whip's snowflake would not despawn when the player dies or quits.
The snowflake should no longer target critters and Target Dummies.

title: Reindeer Bells
content:
The Reindeer Bells are a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons the rideable Rudolph mount, which greatly speeds a player's movement and adds the ability to fly. The Reindeer Bells are dropped by the Ice Queen during or after wave 15 of the Frost Moon event with a 1.33%–2.22% / 6.67% chance depending on the current wave.
Similar to the Hoverboard, flight height can be constrained by holding the ▼ Down key in addition to the ↷ Jump key, so movement will be horizontal only.


== Notes ==
When the buff is active, fall damage is canceled.
Flying left or right allows Rudolph to climb to much greater heights than flying directly upwards.
The top running speed of Rudolph is 61 mph, reached after 2.222 seconds.
Rudolph's nose gives off a small amount of light.
Rudolph's maximum flight time is calculated according to the following formula: flightTime = 160 + xVelocity * 20. Under normal circumstances, Rudolph's maximum flight time can reach up to 6.67 seconds (400 ticks).Verify


== Achievements ==


== Tips ==
Rudolph allows the character to run and fly faster than the maximum speed attainable from accessory items, and also stacks with them. It is faster than most wings, even when running on the ground.
Riding Rudolph causes slightly inconsistent behavior when interacting with ground tiles. While on Rudolph, the player will still trigger player-activated pressure plates, but the player will not travel nearly as fast on asphalt as the player would unmounted. In order to obtain maximum speed, the player would have to run down an asphalt runway with movement speed buffs, such as the Panic! buff and Lightning Boots. The runway would transition into a Frozen Slime Block slide where the player could then mount Rudolph and retain the extra movement speed.


== Trivia ==
Rudolph was the first mount introduced to Terraria.
When standing still on it for between 15 and 25 seconds, it will start eating off the ground.
Rudolph and the Minecart are the only mounts available across all platforms for Terraria.
The Bee Mount comes the closest to being so, only missing from the Nintendo 3DS version. All other mounts are limited to certain versions.

title: Key of Night
content:
The Key of Night is a craftable item that spawns a Corrupt Mimic or a Crimson Mimic when placed in any slot of any empty Chest, depending on whether the world generated with The Corruption or The Crimson, respectively. The world must be in Hardmode and the only item inside the Chest must be a single Key of Night.
The Corrupt/Crimson Mimic is spawned as soon as the Chest is closed, consuming both the Key of Night and the Chest.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The drunk world seed has the potential to spawn either Mimic, depending on which world evil is active.
If utilizing Autopause, the Corrupt/Crimson Mimic will not spawn until the game is unfrozen again. On  Console, the Corrupt/Crimson Mimic will not spawn unless Autopause is disabled.
Placing a Key of Night in a storage item other than a chest (such as a Barrel) will not spawn the Mimic.
The Biome Mimic does not have to be spawned in The Corruption or The Crimson; it can be summoned anywhere.
Placing a Key of Night in a Chest without closing it and directly opening another inventory interface (which is only possible if Autopause is disabled), such as that of another Chest, will not spawn the Mimic.
A Key of Night pulled into a chest by Wiring will not spawn the Mimic.


== See also ==
Key of Light, the Hallow counterpart

title: Ocean
content:
The Ocean is a biome found at both left and right edges of a world. It consists of a sandy beach and a large body of water that extends toward the end of the world, with Shell Piles being occasionally generated in clumps. Palm trees grow on the surface, and can be cut down for Palm Wood. Seashells and Starfish are found commonly on the surface and underwater, and can grow over time. Corals also grow on the seabed. Usually, there will also be several Water Chests generated on the seabed.
Enemies in the Ocean include Crabs, Pink Jellyfish, and Sharks. Squids and Sea Snails rarely appear underwater, and respectively drop Black Ink and Purple Mucus. Critters in the Ocean include Dolphins, Seagulls, Seahorses, and Sea Turtles.
The player is considered in the Ocean biome if they are located less than 340 tiles from the left or right visible world border horizontally, and not lower than 40 tiles above the central line between surface border and Cavern border vertically.


== Contents ==


== NPC happiness ==
For more information, see NPC happiness.


== Notes ==
Like other enemies with Swimming and Jellyfish AIs, Ocean enemies will only detect and swim toward the player if they are in the water to a depth of at least one tile.
If the beach of an Ocean extends long enough towards inland, surface Desert enemies may spawn, but Desert plants will not grow in areas near water.
During Hardmode, Corruption/Crimson or Hallow can convert Sand Blocks into Ebonsand/Crimsand/Pearlsand, which can allow Corrupted/Crimson/Hallowed Desert enemies to spawn.
They can also spread to Sand Blocks out of the world's border.
For fishing in the Ocean, the game checks for the bobber's location instead of the player's location. The bobber has to be located in the Ocean biome and above surface to yield Ocean fishing catches.
Furthermore, the Ocean has to be pure, otherwise Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow fishing catches will override Ocean catches.
Ocean fishing catches are normally higher priority than Desert fishing catches, due to the Ocean naturally being a Desert. If the Ocean is Hallowed, Ocean fishing catches will no longer appear and Desert and Hallow catches each have a 1/2 (50%) chance to appear, due to the biome being a Hallowed Desert.
Sometimes, the sea bed can generate below the Surface layer, causing a bit of the Underground's background to appear and seaweeds to grow on Sand.
If the sea bed is low enough, it is possible to find Life Crystals, Desert Underground Cabins and Campsites on the Ocean floor.
The Ocean biome cannot be artificially created, nor can it be expanded.
While there are Underground Ocean backgrounds, the Underground Ocean spawns no unique enemies.


== Generation variants ==


=== Ocean cave ===

The Ocean on the same side of the world as the Dungeon has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of generating with a cave, which consists of a water-filled tunnel with a ceiling made of hardened sand beginning at the Ocean floor. This tunnel has an additional chance of generating Water Chests, which have equal chances of containing each primary item. It is decorated with long strands of Seaweeds growing from the sand floor.

When Remix is active, the generation chance of ocean caves is increased to 1/2 (50%).
When Drunk or Celebration Mk 10 is active, the ocean cave will always be generated.


=== Florida style ===

The world has a 1/4 (25%) chance to generate one of the Oceans as Florida style. This variant inverts the slope of the beach, with long beaches becoming steeper near the world edge.


== Tips ==

Players exploring the Ocean run the risk of drowning if not equipped with the proper accessories. In addition to plenty of healing potions, items and potions that aid breathing, such as the Breathing Reed and Gills Potion, a Magic Mirror for returning home quickly, and Flippers to aid swimming should be brought along. Hooks may also be of some help in returning to the surface for breath. The Neptune's Shell or any of its upgrades removes the need to breathe altogether.
Players may drain the Ocean by tunneling down to the Underworld, where water evaporates.
Another way of draining the Ocean is by making an air pocket, emptying a Lava Bucket in it and placing a background object (e.g. furniture) in the lava. Allowing water to flow in will cause it to disappear, as the object prevents Obsidian from being generated.
When attempting to preserve the Ocean biome from being infected in Hardmode, simply digging a horizontal gap under the seabed is insufficient because world data extends a little past the edge of the world. The gap must be created vertically along the beach of the Ocean to prevent the spread of Corruption/Crimson or Hallow.
The Oceans have a lot of space, making them good places for large-scale builds like arenas and farms.
While it is impossible to expand the Ocean biome further inland, the player may extend the watery area to the inner edge of the naturally spawning beach.


== Trivia ==
The Ocean Night theme used to be exclusive to the  Console version,  Old-gen console version, and Nintendo 3DS version before the 1.4.0.1(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) update.
It is possible for a Florida style Ocean to generate with a cave.


== Gallery ==


=== Backgrounds ===

		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		


==== Underground layer ====

title: Gills Potion
content:
The Gills Potion is a buff potion which grants the Gills buff when consumed. The buff prevents the player's breath meter from depleting and thus prevents drowning. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().
In addition to being crafted, Gills Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.


== Crafting ==


=== Recipes ===


== Notes ==
The Gills Potion will allow the player to survive while wearing a Fish Bowl.
In For the Worthy worlds, the player cannot breathe outside of water and honey while the Gills buff is active.


== Tips ==
Gills Potions are not needed for swimming in lava, as the player cannot drown in lava.
Swimming in lava can instead be aided by Obsidian Skin Potions (to avoid lava damage) and Flipper Potions or a Flipper (to allow unhindered movement).


== Trivia ==
The Gills Potion has the same crafting recipe as the Sonar Potion.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Stack limit increased from 30 to 9999.
Desktop 1.4.0.1: Duration increased from 2 to 4 minutes.
Desktop 1.3.0.1: Sprite updated.
Desktop 1.2: Gills Potions no longer cause the player to suffocate in air.
Desktop 1.0.6: Duration increased from 1 to 2 minutes.

title: Beetle Might
content:
Beetle Might is a buff granted to the player upon dealing melee damage with a full set of Beetle armor with the Scale Mail equipped. Damaging an enemy with the armor equipped will increase damage and melee speed by increments of 10%. This is increased to 20% and finally 30% if combat is continued for long enough. Each increase in strength causes an additional beetle to fly around the player. After the player stops doing damage, the beetles will disappear one by one, and their respective combat bonuses will be lost.


== Tiers ==


== Notes ==
The number of active beetles depends on a hidden value, beetleCounter, that increases in proportion to damage dealt to enemies. Every time an enemy is hit, beetleCounter is incremented by damage dealt * factor, where factor is 3 (if no beetles are active), 2 (if one beetle is active), or 1 (if two beetles are active).
The first beetle is earned when beetleCounter reaches 400, the second is earned when it reaches 1600, and the third is earned when it reaches 6200.
beetleCounter decreases on every game tick by 3 + ticks / 10, where ticks is the number of game ticks that passed since the wearer last dealt damage. This means that a minimum DPS of 180 is required to maintain beetleCounter at its current level. Due to this decay rate, it may also take a very long time (or even be impossible) to earn another beetle while using weak weapons against enemies with high defense.


== History ==

Desktop 1.4.4: Beetle's Might charges last about 33% longer, and it now takes slightly less time/damage to charge up to Beetle's Might tier 3.
Desktop 1.2.3: Introduced.

Console 1.07: Introduced.
